Song argues that full and rigorous self-governance of the Party must be pursued with "higher standards and more practical measures" during the 15th Five-Year Plan period, which the article treats as a critical stage for basically achieving socialist modernization. The author presents the speech's three "more" requirements as a coherent guide to action.

The article has three parts. The first explains why the 15th Five-Year Plan period raises the bar for Party governance. The second unpacks what "higher standards" and "more practical measures" mean. The third sets out how to apply the "three mores": implementing the Central Committee's major decisions more resolutely, confining power in an institutional cage more scientifically and effectively, and pursuing the fight against corruption more soberly and firmly.

Song argues that strengthening the Party's overall leadership requires three things of Party governance: carrying out the Central Committee's decisions as its first aim, controlling power through institutions as its key support, and anti-corruption work as an important task. Higher standards, in the author's reading, mean stronger political requirements, so that the whole Party acts in unison and avoids distorted understanding or diluted execution. More practical measures do not mean piling on pressure but making responsibility, supervision and enforcement tighter, more specific and verifiable, so as to avoid hollow responsibility and idle supervision. Together they mark a shift from experience-based responses to institutionalized governance.

For implementation, Song calls for political supervision tied to concrete tasks from the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee, such as modern industrial systems, new quality productive forces, common prosperity and local government hidden debt. The author also urges better rules and their rigorous enforcement, greater transparency and a sustained high-pressure anti-corruption stance with systemic governance. Read the original if you want to see how a Central Party School scholar presents official guidance on Party discipline and anti-corruption for the 2026–2030 planning period.
quoteEn: Higher standards and more practical measures reflect a deepening of the Party's approach to self-governance from experience-based responses to institutionalized governance, and an active grasp of how power operates under long-term governing conditions.
quoteZh: 更高标准、更实举措，体现的是治党方式从经验性应对向制度化治理的深化，是对长期执政条件下权力运行规律的主动把握。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A policy line associated with Xi Jinping since 2014 that stresses strict Party discipline, supervision and anti-corruption within the Communist Party.

glossary.en: confining power in an institutional cage
glossary.literal: lock power in the cage of institutions
glossary.explanation: A phrase used by Xi Jinping meaning that the exercise of power should be bound by rules, discipline and supervision.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for productivity growth driven by technological innovation and emerging industries.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all people, stressed in Party policy under Xi Jinping.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Upholding the Party's self-reform to lead social revolution
zh: 坚持以党的自我革命引领社会革命
paras: This is a newspaper report in China Social Sciences Today (20 January 2026) that gathers comments from Chinese academics on the formula "leading social revolution through the Party's self-reform". The formula appears in the Central Committee's recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan. The reporters open with Xi Jinping's speech to the Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection (12 January). The scholars' shared answer is that full and rigorous self-governance of the Party is the key guarantee for Chinese modernization.

The report draws on scholars from the CASS Academy of Marxism, the Central Party School, Renmin University, Nankai University, Jinan University and Wuhan University. It has three sections. The first reviews what the Party's self-reform achieved during the 14th Five-Year Plan period. The second explains how self-reform relates to social revolution. The third looks at the 15th Five-Year Plan period and the tasks it sets for the social sciences.

The interviewees say the 14th Five-Year Plan period saw rapid growth in intra-Party regulations, a campaign to implement the central Eight-point Regulation, and continued anti-corruption work. They credit these with cleaning up the Party's ethos and supporting development. Zhang Jian calls self-reform the "second answer" to the historical cycle of rise and decline. Chen Zhigang links self-reform to four capacities: political leadership, ideological guidance, mass organisation and social mobilisation. Zhu Jie describes self-reform as innovating in theory, institutions and practice. Zhang Xiaomeng says the Party's history is one of pursuing self-reform while advancing social revolution. The scholars treat the two as a dialectical unity: self-reform clears obstacles and provides political assurance, while social revolution sets new tasks that drive further self-reform.

Looking to the 15th Five-Year Plan period, the interviewees expect continued full and rigorous self-governance of the Party to turn organisational strengths into effective governance. They also call on philosophy and social science to support the Party's innovative theory, intra-Party regulations and long-term mechanisms for improving conduct. Dai Shengli adds a call to build a Party-governance theory "with Chinese characteristics" and to tell the story of Party self-reform to international audiences. The report ends by urging that the Party's overall leadership be upheld unwaveringly. Read the original if you want a sample of how Chinese scholars and the official press currently explain the link between Party-building and Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Self-reform is not revolution for its own sake; its fundamental purpose is to lead social revolution better.
quoteZh: 自我革命非为革命而革命，其根本目的在于更好地引领社会革命。

glossary.explanation: A Xi-era term for the Party's continuing effort to purify and improve itself through discipline, anti-corruption work and institution-building. Official texts present it as the Party's answer to the problem of how to avoid decline.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: The slogan for the Party-discipline and anti-corruption drive launched under Xi Jinping after 2012.
The official name for China's development path, which the Party says is led by the CPC and is distinct from Western modernization.
Rules issued in December 2012 to curb extravagance, bureaucratism and formalism among officials. They have since been repeatedly reinforced through campaigns.
Rules issued by the Party that govern Party organisations and members, such as the Disciplinary Regulations. They are separate from state law.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030, whose recommendations were adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee in 2025.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Leading high-level governance in emerging fields through high-quality Party building
zh: 以高质量党建引领新兴领域高水平治理
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 30 January 2026, asks how Party building can work in new economic organisations, new social organisations and new employment groups (the "two news" plus new workers). Chai Baoyong argues that these are the most active parts of society and a new frontier of governance. High-quality Party building there, in the author's view, can turn "variables" into "increments" of high-quality development and secure the Party's governing base in a mobile society.

The piece has three parts. It first sets out what is new about Party work in these fields, then what makes it difficult, and finally where it should be put into practice. It draws on Xi Jinping's call to strengthen the Party's appeal, cohesion and influence in emerging fields, and on examples such as platform firms and delivery riders.

Chai identifies novelty in organisational form (flat, decentralised, boundary-blurring networks rather than fixed workplace units), in function (a shift from mobilisation and management to guidance and service) and in content and carriers (from physical meetings to digital space). The difficulties are incomplete organisational coverage, a tension between platforms' profit-and-efficiency logic and the Party's political aims, and weak cohesion among workers facing unclear labour-relations status and patchy social protection. Chai's remedies are integrating Party organisations into corporate governance through "two-way entry and cross-appointment" and Party-building clauses in company charters, and steering algorithm design towards humane ends. Further remedies are service-first measures such as "Warm Station" rest stops, industry-wide Party structures, turning workers into part-time grid workers or "vanguard rider teams", and an "AI + Party building" approach.

Chai concludes that Party building should move from formal coverage to functional integration, turning those it serves into participants in governance and platform technology into social-governance capacity. The author presents this as building a shared governance community. Read the original if you want a concise official-academic statement of how Party organisation is being extended to platform firms and gig workers.
quoteEn: Party building cannot stop at "visible coverage"; it must also make the leap from organisational embedding to functional integration.
quoteZh: 党建工作不能止步于“有形覆盖”，更要实现从组织嵌入到功能融合的跨越。

glossary.zh: 新经济组织、新社会组织、新就业群体
glossary.pinyin: xīn jīngjì zǔzhī、xīn shèhuì zǔzhī、xīn jiùyè qúntǐ
glossary.en: new economic organisations, new social organisations and new employment groups
glossary.literal: new economic organisations, new social organisations, new employment groups
glossary.explanation: Official shorthand ("two news" plus new workers) for private and platform firms, newer non-state organisations, and flexible workers such as couriers and drivers. The Party has made building organisations among them a priority.
Service points offering rest, refreshment and assistance to couriers, drivers and other new-employment workers, often run with Party and local government support.
The practice of writing the role of the Party organisation into a company's articles of association.

t: The Party's conduct determines the success or failure of the cause of the Party and the state
zh: 党的作风决定党和国家事业成败
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in January 2026, asks why work style (zuofeng) matters so much in Party building. Zhang argues that the Party's conduct decides the success or failure of the cause of the Party and the state. The piece takes its starting point from Xi Jinping's treatment of work style as an entry point for full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.
The article is organised in three steps, each with its own heading. It links work style to Party spirit (dangxing), to popular support, and to the Party's capacity for long-term governance.

Zhang's central claim is that work style is the outward form and Party spirit the inner root. Lapses in conduct therefore signal weak Party spirit, damage the Party's image, its advanced nature and purity, and so its creativity, cohesion and combat strength. Seemingly small lapses, the author says, act like an invisible wall between the Party and the people and can cost the Party public support. If left unchecked, the problems reach the third stage: damage to long-term governing capacity and, eventually, to the Party's survival and the nation's cause. Zhang notes that in a long period of peace, complacency and sloth tend to recur in hidden, changing forms.

Zhang concludes that improving work style is a self-reform of the Party that demands persistence, lasting institutions and discipline placed ahead of law. The author presents this as the way to escape the historical cycle of rise and fall and keep the people's trust. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-school scholars link work style, Party spirit and regime survival.
quoteEn: Party spirit is the root, while work style and image are the form; only when Party spirit is strong and upright will the Party's work style and image be upright and good.
quoteZh: 党性是本，作风和形象是形，党性强和正，党的作风和形象才会正和好。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A Party-building policy line stressed since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering ideology, organisation, work style, discipline and anti-corruption.
The commitment, principles and loyalty expected of Party members, tied to belief in Marxism and communist ideals.
Efforts to improve the conduct, attitudes and everyday behaviour of Party members and officials, such as bureaucratism and sloth.

t: Experience and lessons of labour rule of law in the Central Soviet Area: a historical study based on Red China
zh: 中央苏区劳动法治建设的经验与启示——基于《红色中华》的历史考察
paras: Using the Soviet government's official newspaper Red China (founded December 1931) as its source, this short commentary asks what the labour law of the Central Soviet Area shows about early Party-led rule of law. Wang argues that the Labour Law of the Chinese Soviet Republic was a landmark of Party-led legislation, and that its making and enforcement left lessons that still apply.

The article describes the law's adoption at the First National Soviet Congress (November 1931), its entry into force on 1 January 1932 and its revision in October 1933. It sets out the law's two guiding ideas, its twelve chapters and 75 articles, its precedents in Soviet and regional legislation, and its enforcement as reported in Red China.

Wang identifies three practices: supervision by labour inspectors, special protection in judicial procedure through labour courts, and timely revision. According to the article, the original provisions exceeded local economic conditions, so employers resisted and some firms closed. The 1933 revision let employers negotiate wages with unions, cut employers' insurance contributions to 5–8 per cent and exempted small employers. Citing Red China, the author reports that wages rose in places such as Tingzhou and Ruijin.

Wang concludes that the experience yielded four lessons. These are Party leadership of rule of law, the principal position of the people, alignment with the Party's central tasks, and fit between law and economic and social development. For the last point the author cites Marx on rights never exceeding a society's economic structure. Read the original if you want a brief, source-based account of how the Party presents the origins of its labour legislation and its "red" rule-of-law tradition.
quoteEn: We must profoundly recognise that Party leadership is the most fundamental guarantee of socialist rule of law; only when rule-of-law building proceeds under Party leadership can its correct direction and institutional character be ensured.
quoteZh: 要深刻认识党的领导是社会主义法治最根本的保证，只有在党的领导下进行法治建设，才能确保法治的正确方向和制度属性

glossary.explanation: The main Communist-held revolutionary base in southern Jiangxi and western Fujian in the early 1930s. It was the seat of the Chinese Soviet Republic, proclaimed in 1931.

t: The establishment and improvement of the labour insurance system in the early years of the People's Republic of China
zh: 新中国成立初期劳动保险制度的建立与完善
paras: Jiang Yingchun, in a newspaper article published in Guangming Daily in January 2026, asks how the Chinese Communist Party built a labour insurance system in the early years of the People's Republic. The author argues that the Party drew on experience from Northeast China, adjusted benefit levels step by step to local conditions, and within a short time resolved labour-rights problems that had troubled modern Chinese society for a long time. In Jiang's account, the system played an important historical role in mobilising workers and driving economic and social development.

The article has three parts. The first traces the Northeast's pre-1949 experience and the national Labour Insurance Regulations of 1951. The second examines how the system was run, with trade unions and part-time insurance staff at its centre. The third explains the principle of enterprise responsibility and the shift from compensation after harm to prevention of injury and illness. Jiang draws on archival and published sources, including Party documents, People's Daily reports and trade-union handbooks.

Jiang first describes the Northeast's 1948 wartime regulations for state-run enterprises, which created two funds from a levy of 3 per cent of the wage bill. One was an enterprise-level relief fund, the other a regionally pooled welfare fund. Jiang cites a surplus of about 31 per cent of insurance income by the end of 1950 as evidence of success. Second, the author contrasts this with Western insurers, whose administrative costs, citing Li Lisan, reached 15 to 20 per cent of funds. Union management is presented as cheaper and as keeping insurance in workers' own hands. Jiang notes that about 200,000 insurance staff handled a growing caseload and also visited sick workers. Third, Jiang argues that placing responsibility on enterprises gave them an incentive to improve safety. Factory inspections, spending on safety equipment and staff who traced hazards led, by the article's figures, to fatal accidents falling 39.1 per cent in 1952 against 1951.

Jiang concludes that this enterprise-centred system, which aimed at comprehensive protection while taking concrete conditions into account, used the Party's leadership, organisational capacity and innovation. It encouraged the initiative of enterprises and workers, moved from after-the-fact compensation to prevention, and gave workers fairly good protection across life, old age, illness, injury and death. Read the original if you want a Party-history account of early PRC social insurance, with the archival and statistical sources behind it.
quoteEn: In sum, the enterprise-centred labour insurance system of the early People's Republic gave full play to the Party's leading, organising and innovative capacities, aiming at comprehensive protection while taking concrete circumstances fully into account.
quoteZh: 总之，新中国成立初期的以企业为中心的劳动保险体系，充分发挥党的主导力、组织力和创新力，以全面保障为目标但又充分考虑具体情况。

glossary.explanation: The early PRC system of workers' benefits covering injury, illness, maternity, old age and death, set out in the 1951 Labour Insurance Regulations. It was financed by enterprises and administered by trade unions.

t: Implementing the Party Central Committee's major decisions and plans more resolutely and effectively
zh: 更加坚决有力地贯彻落实党中央重大决策部署
paras: This commentary in Guangming Daily (28 January 2026) responds to Xi Jinping's call, at the Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection, to implement the Central Committee's major decisions and plans "more resolutely and effectively". Tang Junfeng argues that such implementation is a basic requirement for upholding the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership. The author presents it as a precondition for the Party to start the 15th Five-Year Plan period well and overcome difficulties.

The piece is organised under four headings. Each presents implementation as, in turn, the concrete form of the Two Upholds, the political guarantee for Chinese modernization, the first content of Party political discipline and rules, and a necessary demand of the continuing campaign against the "four undesirable work styles". It draws on Engels on authority, Xi's speeches, the Party Constitution and the Regulations on Disciplinary Actions.

Tang's first move is to tie implementation to political loyalty. The author holds that the Two Upholds must show in action, in job performance and in everyday conduct, and calls for "aligning" thought and behaviour with the Central Committee while opposing individualism, departmentalism, liberalism and localism. The second move treats implementation as a matter of discipline rather than a soft requirement. Tang cites the Party Constitution's rule that lower bodies carry out higher bodies' decisions and the disciplinary regulations' penalties for token compliance, and calls it an "iron rule" whose breach crosses a bottom line. Implementation is then linked to the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee's plans for the next five years, with local plans required to fit national ones while adapting to local conditions.

Tang concludes with proposals. These are education in political discipline, strict reporting systems, supervision and inspection tours, and assessment that makes implementation the primary political criterion, with accountability for those who do not carry decisions out. The author also calls for mechanisms to detect formalism and bureaucratism in disguised forms, for burden reduction at the grassroots, and for sustained work-style building. The author says that a minority of localities and cadres still show "deviation", "temperature differences" and "gaps" in implementation. Read the original if you want an example of how Party-discipline and Party-building discourse in early 2026 links central authority, supervision and the new five-year plan.
quoteEn: Implementing the Party Central Committee's major decisions and plans is not a soft constraint but an iron rule; failing to implement them resolutely violates Party discipline and crosses a bottom line.
quoteZh: 贯彻落实党中央重大决策部署，不是软约束，而是铁规矩；不坚决贯彻落实党中央重大决策部署，就违反了党纪、触犯了底线。

glossary.explanation: A formula from 2018 and 2019 requiring Party members to resolutely uphold Xi Jinping's core position on the Central Committee and in the Party as a whole, and the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.
The official term for China's path of modernization as defined by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022), presented as distinct from Western models.
Formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance. The Party has campaigned against them since the 18th Party Congress (2012), starting with the Eight-point Regulation.
The category of Party discipline concerning loyalty to the Party line and the Central Committee. Official texts rank it first among the Party's disciplines.

t: Doing more practical things for the people and raising the mass-organising capacity of primary-level Party organisations
zh: 更好为群众办实事解难题 不断提升基层党组织的群众组织力
paras: This short commentary, first published in People's Daily on 23 January 2026, asks how primary-level Party organisations can better organise, mobilise and unite ordinary people. Hou Xibao starts from the proposals of the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) and Xi Jinping's call to organise the grassroots masses. Hou argues that these organisations are the "last mile" in carrying out the Central Committee's decisions, and that raising their capacity to organise the masses bears on the Party's governing base and on modernising national governance.

The article is organised around three measures: education and guidance, Party building as leadership over grassroots governance, and technological empowerment. Hou draws on the Party's historical mass work, such as night schools for workers and literacy classes for women. Examples from the present include the "Fengqiao experience" of the new era, Datian County in Fujian, and Zhejiang's rural cultural halls.

Hou first argues that ideological and political education should run through every stage of grassroots governance and be tied to practical services and local culture. The second section concedes that some grassroots organisations still show a "cadres act, masses watch" pattern, and that some pile up paperwork while neglecting residents' urgent concerns. Hou's remedies are to tighten up weak and lax organisations, embed Party organisations in village collective economic bodies and cooperatives, and apply responsibility lists to reduce formalism. The third measure is to use big data and online platforms, such as a "smart hub" and "public-sentiment portraits", and to draw new forms of employment into "micro-governance".

Hou concludes that Party-led, technology-supported work of this kind can build a pattern of governance that is jointly built, jointly governed and shared by all. Read the original if you want a brief, official-style statement of how Party-building language links mass work, grassroots governance and digital tools in early 2026.
quoteEn: To raise the organisational function of primary-level Party organisations in connecting with and serving the masses, the key is to vigorously advance Party-building leadership over grassroots governance.
quoteZh: 提升基层党组织联系服务群众的组织功能，重在大力推进党建引领基层治理

glossary.explanation: A model of resolving disputes locally, relying on the masses and under Party leadership, which originated in Fengqiao, Zhejiang, in the 1960s. It is promoted today as a "new-era" approach to grassroots governance.
In Party discourse, work done for show, such as excessive paperwork and reports. Reducing its burden on the grassroots is an official aim.

t: Resistance in Northeast China: a heroic chapter of the anti-fascist war
zh: 东北抗战书写反法西斯英勇篇章
paras: This commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in January 2026, recounts the fourteen years of resistance by the people of Northeast China after the Japanese invasion of 1931. Sun argues that this struggle, led by the Communist Party of China, was an epic of unity and defence of sovereignty and national dignity, and an integral part of China's War of Resistance and of the world anti-fascist war.

The piece is organised in three thematic sections: the awakening of the Northeast population, the defence of resources and the right to survive, and the safeguarding of national integrity (minzu qijie). It draws on examples from mines, farms, forests, villages, schools and cultural life.

Sun describes a shift from spontaneous volunteer armies, said to exceed 300,000 by 1932, to the Party-led Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army of 1936. The author then shows resistance spreading through society: workers sabotaging mines and the Anshan ironworks, peasants hiding grain (puppet-regime data allegedly show collection often under 60 per cent of quota), and hidden mountain camps supporting the guerrillas. In culture, teachers used double textbooks, artists used coded imagery, and families kept traditional customs in defiance of colonial assimilation.

Sun concludes that the resistance, material and spiritual, weakened Japanese rule and displayed the Chinese nation's cohesion. The author calls for remembering it in order to carry forward this spirit, to keep to the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and to safeguard national sovereignty and security. Read the original if you want a brief, officially aligned account of how Northeast China's wartime resistance is presented in current Chinese commemorative writing.
quoteEn: The struggle of the people of Northeast China was an important part of the Chinese people's War of Resistance against Japan, and also a heroic chapter in the world anti-fascist war.
quoteZh: 东北人民的抗争是中国人民抗日战争的重要组成部分，也是世界反法西斯战争中的英勇篇章。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism, developed since reform and opening up in the late 1970s.
Guerrilla force formed in 1936 under Communist leadership by combining Communist-led units and remnants of volunteer armies in Northeast China.

t: Upholding the organic unity of governing the country according to law and governing the Party according to Party regulations
zh: 坚持依法治国和依规治党有机统一
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 16 January 2026, Zhou Yezhong examines the principle of "upholding the organic unity of governing the country according to law and governing the Party according to Party regulations". This principle is listed as the twelfth "upholding" in the core tenets of Xi Jinping's thought on the rule of law, as set out in the 2025 edition of its study outline. Zhou argues that it is an original contribution of that body of thought and a marker that separates the rule-of-law theory of socialism with Chinese characteristics from Western theories.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why the principle is an original contribution. The second explains its scientific connotation through four elements. The third lists four practical requirements for the new journey ahead. Zhou draws throughout on Xi Jinping's statements and on the 2024 Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee.

Zhou argues that the principle opens a new realm for full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and for law-based governance of the country. It also offers a new solution for the Party's long-term rule. Governing by law is presented as the institutional basis of "people's oversight", and governing by Party regulations as the legal tool of the Party's self-reform. The four elements are as follows. Party leadership and socialist rule of law are consistent, and "Is the Party or the law greater?" is called a false question, whereas "Is power or law greater?" is a real one. The Party governs the country by the constitution and laws, and governs itself by Party regulations, which are stricter than state law. Each system complements the other. The two are advanced together and built as one. In Zhou's account, this yields a "great rule of law" combining state law and Party regulations. The author says this is unique in world practice, breaks the "myth" of Western-centred rule of law, and goes beyond the Western assumption that law and political parties are separate.

For practice, Zhou calls for study of Xi Jinping's thought on the rule of law, for strengthening the Party Central Committee's centralised and unified leadership, and for firm confidence in the rule of law with Chinese characteristics, including rejecting the view that rule of law means only rule by statute. Zhou also proposes better mechanisms linking Party regulations with state laws. These would cover the Party Constitution and the state constitution, and run through drafting, review, filing, enforcement and supervision. Discipline and law enforcement would be aligned. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Chinese scholars present Party regulations as part of the legal system.
quoteEn: Upholding the organic unity of governing the country by law and governing the Party by regulations means forming a pattern in which state laws and Party regulations complement, promote and safeguard each other, so that their complementary roles are fully realised.
quoteZh: 坚持依法治国和依规治党有机统一，形成国家法律法规和党内法规制度相辅相成、相互促进、相互保障的格局，进而充分发挥两者的互补作用。

glossary.en: governing the Party according to Party regulations
glossary.explanation: The practice of managing the Communist Party through its internal regulations (党内法规) such as the Party Constitution and discipline rules. Since the 18th Party Congress (2012) it has been described as the Party's basic method of self-governance.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Official term for the Party's drive for discipline, anti-corruption and internal regulation since 2012.
Official term for the Party's efforts to correct itself, presented as the internal answer to the question of how to escape the historical cycle of rise and decline.

Rules issued by the Party, such as the Party Constitution and codes of conduct. They bind members and are distinct from state law, but are now counted within the socialist legal system with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.en: Xi Jinping's thought on the rule of law
glossary.literal: Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law
glossary.explanation: The body of Xi Jinping's statements on law, presented officially as a component of Xi Jinping Thought and consolidated at the 2020 Central Conference on Law-based Governance.

keywords: Xi Jinping's thought on the rule of law

t: Slogans and the Communist Party's shaping of opinion in the Great Revolution: the case of Workers' Path
zh: 从标语口号看大革命时期中国共产党的舆论动员——以《工人之路》为例
paras: How did the Communist Party use slogans to mobilise opinion during the Great Revolution of the 1920s? Tang Juan takes up this question through Workers' Path (Gongren zhi lu), launched in Guangzhou on 24 June 1925 and edited by Deng Zhongxia. Tang describes it as the first workers' daily under Party leadership. The article, a newspaper commentary, argues that its slogans effectively mobilised and guided workers in the Canton–Hong Kong Strike and left the Party with lasting propaganda experience.

The article has three parts. The first examines the form and content of the paper's slogans. The second sets out two mobilisation strategies. The third assesses how the slogans guided the workers' movement. Tang draws on the paper's issues, on Party documents including the resolution of the Fourth Party Congress, and on Deng Zhongxia's writings.

On form, Tang notes that from issue 20 (July 1925) large-type anti-imperialist slogans ran down the margins of page four. Small-type slogans closed articles, and cartoons paired image with text from issue 123. By Tang's own count, political slogans such as "Down with all imperialism" made up over 70 per cent of the total. The rest were economic, organisational (stressing unity and alliance) and other slogans. The two strategies are enlightenment of class consciousness and emotional mobilisation. Slogans such as "Down with imperialism" recast wage disputes and colonial aggression as class exploitation. Slogans of revenge for martyrs of the 7 February and 30 May incidents drew on grief and anger. Tang then identifies three kinds of guidance. Politically, the central slogans shifted from holding out in the strike to national liberation and then the Northern Expedition, which the paper promoted in issues 327 to 383. Organisationally, slogans of "great union of workers, peasants, merchants and students" countered union rivalries. In action, practical slogans such as suppressing strike-breakers and blockading the port followed Deng's call to replace grand slogans with useful ones.

Tang concludes that slogans were an intuitive, widely reaching tool of early Party political communication and made a lasting contribution to policy propaganda, mass mobilisation and building the ranks. As evidence of reach, Tang cites a peak circulation of 10,000 copies, roughly one for every four or five strikers. Read the original if you study the early Communist movement, propaganda history or the Canton–Hong Kong Strike and want a concise account of how one workers' paper used slogans.
quoteEn: Using colloquial, rhythmic slogans, Workers' Path combined Marxist theory with workers' real demands, won popularity among workers and played an important guiding role in the strike.
quoteZh: 《工人之路》借助口语化、韵律化的标语口号，将马克思主义理论与工人现实诉求相结合，受到工人群体欢迎，在罢工中发挥了重要引领作用。

glossary.explanation: The standard Chinese term for the 1924–1927 revolutionary period of Guomindang–Communist cooperation, which included the Northern Expedition.
A large anti-imperialist strike of 1925–1926 by workers in Guangzhou and Hong Kong, launched after the 30 May 1925 incident in Shanghai and the Shaji killings in Guangzhou.
The military campaign launched from Guangdong in 1926 by the National Revolutionary Army to defeat northern warlords and unify China.
The daily paper of the Canton–Hong Kong strike committee, edited by Deng Zhongxia, which the article presents as the first workers' daily under Communist leadership.

t: How Party newspapers and journals in the Yan'an period shaped the idea that labour is glorious
zh: 延安时期党报党刊对劳动光荣观念的塑造
paras: Zhang Yujie asks how the Communist Party used its press to cultivate the idea that labour is glorious during the Yan'an period. The short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in January 2026, argues that Party newspapers and journals became a key channel of opinion for this purpose. In Zhang's account, they did so by building recognition of labour's value, setting a moral orientation that honoured labour, and promoting positive attitudes to work.

The article is set in the Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia Border Region, where the Party launched the Great Production Movement to break the blockade and ease material hardship. Zhang draws on press reports from the Liberation Daily, Xinhua Daily, Liberation and other titles. These are organised under three headings: the several values of labour, the criticism of mistaken ideas, and the demonstration effect of labour heroes.

Zhang says the press presented labour as a way to escape poverty, a contribution to the revolution and the war effort, and a means of remoulding people's thinking, with the reform of idlers ("erliuzi") as an example. It criticised contempt for manual work, the view that women's participation in production was improper, and the habit of calling labour "suffering". Model workers such as Wu Manyou and Zhao Zhankui were reported as exemplars of dedication, mutual aid, hard work and innovation. The press also covered their honours and warned them against complacency.

Zhang concludes that this coverage spread the notion of glorious labour widely and strengthened participation in production. Read the original if you want a concise, source-based account of Yan'an-era Party journalism and ideological mobilisation around labour.
quoteEn: By building among the masses a recognition of labour's value, setting a moral orientation that takes pride in labour, and promoting positive attitudes to work, the Party newspapers and journals became an important arena of opinion for the Party's shaping of the idea that labour is glorious.
quoteZh: 党报党刊通过在群众中构建对劳动的价值认同、树立以劳动为荣的道德导向、倡导培育积极的劳动态度，成为党塑造劳动光荣观念的重要舆论阵地。

glossary.explanation: A campaign launched by the Communist Party in the Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia Border Region in the early 1940s. It mobilised civilians, officials and troops in farming and manufacturing to become self-sufficient under blockade.
Model workers and peasants publicly honoured in the border region for outstanding output and exemplary conduct. The Party used them as examples for others to follow.
A term used in the border region for idlers or loafers, often associated with gambling, vagrancy and petty theft. The Party ran campaigns to reform them through productive labour.

t: Women's cultural mobilisation in the Jin-Cha-Ji Daily during the War of Resistance
st: Literacy, winter schools and the press in the Jin-Cha-Ji border region
zh: 全民族抗战时期《晋察冀日报》的妇女文化动员
paras: This short newspaper article asks how the Jin-Cha-Ji Daily, the organ of the Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei border region government, helped mobilise women for the War of Resistance against Japan. Tian Jianping argues that, under Communist Party leadership, the paper's more than 900 reports on women played a leading role in promoting women's liberation and drawing rural women into the war effort. In Tian's account, cultural education was the necessary first step in that mobilisation.

The article is organised under three headings: mobilisation as ideological enlightenment, literacy as the basis of popularising knowledge, and winter schools as collective study in the agricultural off-season. It draws on editorials, news items and features from the paper (which ran as the Resist the Enemy News until November 1940), together with Party directives of 1939 and 1943 and the border region's 1938 resolution on culture and education.

Tian's central claim is that peasant women, confined to the household by feudal ethics and a small-peasant economy and overwhelmingly illiterate, had to be educated before they could take part in public affairs. The paper reported on literacy classes, people's schools, night schools and winter schools, covering policy, curricula, textbooks and teaching methods. Tian cites reports of Fuping women who studied despite hunger and parental opposition, and of winter-school systems adapted to guerrilla areas, such as scattered small-group study and disguised classes. Editorials such as that of March 1943 are presented as stating that women's liberation must be subordinated to national liberation and coordinated with the anti-Japanese struggle.

Tian concludes that the paper's work freed women from the constraints of feudal ethics and the small-peasant economy and began to establish a modern sense of independence. Women acquired basic literacy, a sense of family, country and nation, and an understanding of Party lines and policies, and many literacy-class students became cadres at various levels. Tian presents this as an important contribution to base-area construction and to final victory. Read the original if you want a brief overview of how the Communist press framed women's education and mobilisation in a wartime base area.
quoteEn: The cultural mobilisation of women in the Jin-Cha-Ji base area, represented by the Jin-Cha-Ji Daily, freed the broad mass of women from the oppression of the feudal system, feudal ethics and the confinement of the small-peasant economy, and began to establish a modern sense of independence among them.
quoteZh: 以《晋察冀日报》为代表的晋察冀根据地妇女文化动员工作，将广大妇女群众从封建制度、礼教束缚及小农经济禁锢的压迫下解放出来，初步树立起妇女独立自主的现代意识。

glossary.explanation: The Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei border region, one of the main anti-Japanese base areas led by the Communist Party behind Japanese lines during the War of Resistance (1937–1945). The article uses its name for the region and its newspaper.
A mass education campaign in the Communist-led base areas that used the agricultural off-season to run classes in literacy, political education and practical skills for villagers.
The most basic and widespread form of popular schooling in the base areas, including people's schools, night schools and anti-illiteracy classes.
Official term for the period of China's war against Japan from 1937 to 1945, stressing the mobilisation of the whole nation under the united front.

t: Using fine conduct to build cohesion and get things done
st: Xi Jinping's thinking on Party work style and the start of the 15th Five-Year Plan period
zh: 以优良作风凝心聚力真抓实干
paras: Published in People's Daily on 14 January 2026, this commentary asks how the Party's fine conduct (youliang zuofeng) can be sustained so that the first year of the 15th Five-Year Plan period gets a strong start. The authors answer that Party members and officials must study and apply Xi Jinping's statements on work style, turn changes in conduct into cohesion, and use down-to-earth practical work to drive high-quality development. The piece draws on Xi's speech of 12 January 2026 at the Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and on a Politburo democratic life meeting held at the end of 2025.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the content of Xi's remarks on fine conduct, grouped under its meaning, its significance, the key points of leverage, the practical path and the methods. The second reviews what the authors call the transformation of conduct since the 18th Party Congress (2012), starting with the eight-point regulation. The third proposes four ways to secure a strong start to the 15th Five-Year Plan period.

In the authors' account, Xi presents fine conduct as the Party's 'personality strength' that complements the strength of its truth, and as bound up with popular support and the Party's survival. They credit the campaign against formalism, bureaucratism, extravagance and hedonism with curbing unhealthy tendencies, tightening the Party's ties with the people and building rules intended to prevent relapse. They also say it has helped deliver poverty alleviation and technological breakthroughs. The authors cite poverty alleviation and efforts on key technologies as evidence that work style supports national goals.

For the new period, the authors call for four things: stronger theoretical study, so that the emphasis on practical work rests on Marxist ideas of practice; a problem-oriented approach based on investigation and on responding to people's urgent concerns; leadership by example from senior officials, described as a 'lead goose effect'; and regular, long-term institutional mechanisms, with accountability for inaction and misconduct. They close by urging officials to be doers who carry forward Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a typical official statement of how Party conduct is tied to the 15th Five-Year Plan and to Xi's discourse on self-governance.
quoteEn: Work-style building has only a present continuous tense, never a completed one; it is a decisive battle, but even more a protracted war.
quoteZh: 作风建设只有进行时，没有完成时；既是攻坚战，更是持久战。

glossary.explanation: A set of rules adopted by the Politburo in December 2012 to improve Party work style and close ties with the masses. It restricts extravagance, formalities and official perks, and is the starting point of the post-2012 work-style campaign.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030. 2026 is its first year.
The official term for China's path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models. The Party gives it as its central task for national rejuvenation.
The official term for a growth model that prioritises quality, innovation and efficiency over speed. It is now the stated main task of China's economic work.

t: Maintaining historical patience: methodological lessons from the CPC's long-term governance
zh: 保持历史耐心：中国共产党长期执政的方法论启示
paras: Zhou Jin's commentary in Guangming Daily takes up the concept of "historical patience" (lishi naixin) and asks what it shows about how the Communist Party of China (CPC) governs over the long term. Zhou argues that it is both a spiritual quality and a scientific method of thinking, forged over the Party's century-plus of struggle. The article presents it as a distinctive concept put forward by the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core, using a "big historical view". In Zhou's account it reflects a scientific grasp of the laws of Communist Party governance, socialist construction and human social development.

The piece has three parts. The first grounds historical patience in historical materialism and traces the idea through Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping, including Xi's 2013 remark on urbanisation at the Central Urbanisation Work Conference. The second runs through four periods: the New Democratic Revolution, the era of socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era. Examples include the protracted war, the household contract responsibility system, the graded opening of the economy, poverty alleviation, ecological protection and regional coordination. The third part sets out five practical requirements.

Zhou's central claim is that historical patience is not passivity. Referring to the Marxist view that the succession of social formations is a long "natural historical process", Zhou holds that the Party respects objective laws while exercising historical initiative. The five requirements are: following laws together with taking initiative; linking quantitative accumulation to qualitative leaps; combining long-range strategy with flexible tactics; matching the big historical view with a problem-oriented approach; and pairing "success need not be mine" with "success must have my contribution". Zhou says the last of these means taking a long-term view while acting responsibly in the present, and that it is shown in generations of successive struggle.

Zhou concludes that China's huge population, vast territory and complex conditions make development a long and arduous process. Zhou adds that the present period, with strategic opportunities alongside growing risks and uncertainties, calls for patience in particular. Goals such as the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, a modern socialist power and common prosperity are described as tasks achievable only through step-by-step accumulation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars present long-term governance and Xi-era concepts in official discourse.
quoteEn: Maintaining historical patience profoundly embodies the dialectical principle of the relation between quantitative and qualitative change, stressing that major strategic goals can be achieved only through long-term quantitative accumulation, which in continuous advance gives rise to a qualitative leap.
quoteZh: 保持历史耐心，深刻体现了量变和质变的辩证关系原理，强调重大战略目标的实现必须经过长期的量的积累，在持续推进中孕育质的飞跃。

glossary.explanation: A concept associated with Xi Jinping, who used it in 2013 on urbanisation. It stresses long-term, gradual progress towards strategic goals and resistance to haste.
A perspective promoted in Xi-era Party discourse. It urges analysing developments across long historical spans, the trends of the age and global change.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term national goal of the CPC, closely associated with Xi Jinping's leadership.
A stated goal of socialism with Chinese characteristics, given new emphasis under Xi Jinping. It refers to prosperity shared by all the people.
The policy launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping, introducing market-oriented economic reform and opening to the outside world.

t: Understanding the philosophical implications of the spirit of the Central Committee's eight-point decision
zh: 深刻领会中央八项规定精神的哲学意蕴
paras: This short commentary in Economic Daily asks what Marxist philosophy lies behind the Central Committee's eight-point decision on improving Party conduct, issued after the 18th Party Congress (2012). Chen argues that the decision, described as a 'golden calling card' of Party building in the new era, embodies Marxist standpoints, viewpoints and methods. Grasping them, the author says, matters for making conduct-building routine and lasting.

The article is organised around four philosophical themes: the ideological line of seeking truth from facts, the fundamental stance of putting the people first, the scientific method of systems thinking, and the practical character of upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground. Each section links a tenet of dialectical or historical materialism to the decision's content and implementation.

Chen contends that the decision reflects seeking truth from facts because it targets concrete, persistent problems with operable measures and supporting rules, shifting Party governance from lax to strict. It reflects the people-first stance because conduct is, in the author's view, a question of the Party's relationship with the masses, and combining popular oversight with the Party's self-reform is presented as the way to escape the historical cycle of rise and fall. Chen cites a 2024 National Bureau of Statistics survey in which 94.9 per cent of respondents endorsed its results. The decision also exemplifies systems thinking, since conduct and corruption are treated as intertwined and the rules are written into Party regulations, and it shows continuity from earlier Party traditions such as the 'Two Musts'.

Chen concludes that the decision, enriched since 2012, adapts widely and supplies a Chinese approach and wisdom for Party governance and anti-corruption efforts worldwide. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary ties Party discipline campaigns to Marxist philosophical categories.
quoteEn: The core of the conduct problem is the question of the Party's relationship with the people.
quoteZh: 作风问题的核心是党同人民群众的关系问题。

glossary.explanation: A set of rules adopted by the Politburo in December 2012 to curb formalism, bureaucracy, extravagance and waste among Party officials. It is widely treated as the starting point of Xi Jinping's conduct-building campaign.
An official concept presented as the Party's answer to how it can avoid decline during long-term rule, through continuous self-supervision and correction.

glossary.en: historical cycle of rise and fall
glossary.explanation: The idea, raised by Huang Yanpei in conversation with Mao Zedong in 1945, that regimes rise and then decline. Party discourse offers popular oversight and self-reform as ways to escape it.
Mao Zedong's 1949 call for Party members to remain modest and prudent and to keep up the style of hard struggle.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Understanding and grasping "strengthening the Party's political leadership capacity"
zh: 深刻理解和把握“增强党的政治领导力”
paras: This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 8 January 2026, explains one phrase from the Central Committee's Recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan: strengthening the Party's "political leadership capacity". Huang Gang argues that upholding and strengthening the Party's overall leadership means first of all upholding its political leadership. In the author's view, this is the fundamental guarantee for advancing Chinese modernization.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out the proposition that "the Party is the supreme political leadership force". The second traces the Party's long attention to "building the Party politically" through four historical periods. The third turns to how the Party's political leadership capacity can be strengthened on the new journey, through theoretical, strategic and institutional advantages.

Huang grounds the first proposition in a line of authorities. These run from Marx and Engels on the communist vanguard, through Lenin on Party leadership of all state work, to Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping on leadership as essentially political. Political leadership is said to consist mainly of leading major decisions on the Party's line, principles and policies. Its most important element is firmly upholding the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Party Central Committee. For the historical section, Huang cites the Gutian and Zunyi meetings, the wartime resistance line, the transition-period general line and the reform-era basic line. After the 18th Party Congress (2012), political building is described as the Party's foundational task, backed by the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds. On the new journey, Huang names three advantages to bring into play. The first is Marxist theory, especially Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The second is strategic capacity for setting direction and goals. The third is the institutional strength of the people's congress system, the "one blueprint" approach and successive five-year plans.

Huang concludes that the history of the Party is a history of upholding political leadership and forging its capacity. Provided the Party's overall leadership is upheld unwaveringly, the Party can handle complex situations and risks, and Chinese modernization can proceed in the right direction. The author calls for turning the distinctive institutional advantages of socialism with Chinese characteristics into effective governance. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how Party theorists now justify the Party's "supreme political leadership" and its link to the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: Upholding the Party's political leadership determines the essence and direction of the Party's overall leadership.
quoteZh: 坚持党的政治领导决定着党的全面领导的本质和方向

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, described as socialist modernization led by the Communist Party. It has been a central slogan since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A formula adopted in 2022 affirming Xi Jinping's position as the Party's core and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.

The requirement that Party members firmly uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions, presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.

One of four 'capacities' (with ideological guidance, mass organizing and social mobilizing) the Party aims to strengthen. It refers to the Party's ability to set political direction and make major decisions.

t: Carrying the Party's leadership through every aspect and the whole process of economic and social development
zh: 把党的领导贯穿经济社会发展各方面全过程
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 7 January 2026, He Yiting takes up the Party's leadership as the first principle in the Recommendations of the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) for the 15th Five-Year Plan period. He argues that Party leadership bears directly on the fundamental direction, fate and ultimate success of Chinese modernization, and must therefore run through every aspect and the whole process of economic and social development.

The commentary has two parts. The first sets out why Party leadership is the fundamental guarantee of Chinese modernization, casting the Party as its pioneer, theorist, rallier of forces and leader. The second sets out three sets of measures, each presented as a form of guarantee: political (centralised and unified leadership by the Central Committee), ideological (theoretical armament and innovation) and organisational (cadres and Party organisations). A closing section addresses full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and the Party's self-reform.

He's central claim is historical and structural. Late-Qing and later attempts to copy Western modernization failed, whereas Chinese modernization, led by the Party, is said to have overcome the inherent defects of modernization tied to the capitalist mode of production. As evidence he cites nearly 100 million rural people lifted out of poverty in eight years since the 18th Party Congress (2012). He then argues that unified leadership requires the Two Establishes, the Two Upholds, stronger implementation mechanisms and greater political capacity among cadres. Ideological work should consolidate Marxism's guiding position and continue the Two Integrations, while cadre selection should put political criteria first and give weight to practical performance.

He concludes that the Party's own discipline is the base of all these guarantees. He calls for steady enforcement of the Central Committee's eight-point rules, regular and long-term work on conduct, and strict use of intra-Party regulations. The spirit of reform and strict standards are described as complementary, and both are to be applied to Party governance. Read the original if you want a concise, authoritative statement of how Party-building is tied to the 15th Five-Year Plan and to Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: The reason Chinese modernization can create a new form of human civilization is precisely that it is socialist modernization led by the Communist Party of China.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化之所以能够创造人类文明新形态，就在于它是中国共产党领导的社会主义现代化

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path to modernization under Party leadership. It was developed in Party discourse from the 20th Party Congress (2022) onwards.
A formula from the 2022 Party resolution. It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the Party, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The requirement that Party members uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.
The principle of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party-discipline and anti-corruption drive pursued since 2012 under Xi Jinping.
An official concept for the Party's capacity to correct itself and renew its discipline, presented as the answer to the historical cycle of rise and decline.

t: Studying and implementing General Secretary Xi Jinping's important thinking on the Party's self-reform
st: Studying volume five of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China
zh: 深入学习贯彻习近平总书记关于党的自我革命的重要思想
zhSub: 深入学习《习近平谈治国理政》第五卷
authors: Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and National Supervisory Commission
paras: This People's Daily article, written in the name of the Party's top discipline and supervision organs, is a study piece on volume five of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China. It takes up Xi Jinping's thinking on \"the Party's self-reform\" as developed since the 20th Party Congress (2022). The authors argue that this thinking is a major theoretical innovation, a product of the Two Integrations, and the fundamental guide for pushing self-reform further. They call on discipline inspection and supervision bodies to grasp its meaning, significance and practical requirements.

The text has three parts. The first traces how the thinking grew out of the practice of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second sets out six areas of significance: theoretical, cultural, historical, contemporary, practical and international. The third reports what the discipline and supervision organs have done since the 20th Party Congress, in ten numbered areas, and cites statistics for several of them.

The authors argue that the thinking answers why, whether and how the Party should reform itself, and they summarise it in the \"nine requirements\" (九个以). They present it as enriching Marxist party-building theory, drawing on traditional Chinese culture as a model of the Two Integrations, and clarifying the relationship between the \"two great revolutions\": self-reform leads and secures the great social revolution, which is its ultimate purpose. They also claim it solves the \"worldwide problem\" of self-supervision. In their account, it combines self-supervision with supervision by the people and goes beyond Western parties' reliance on external checks such as multiparty rotation and separation of powers.

For practice, the article reports figures for the period since the 20th Party Congress. It cites 605,000 violations of the central Eight-point Regulation handled and 2.731 million people placed under investigation. It also cites six rounds of central inspections and the resolution of 3.918 million problems of public concern. It states that discipline organs will keep deepening Party governance, upholding the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, and will carry self-reform \"through to the end\". Read the original if you want an authoritative, official account of how the Party's anti-corruption and discipline apparatus presents its own theory and record at the end of 2025.
quoteEn: Xi Jinping's important thinking on the Party's self-reform upholds the dialectical unity of internal and external causes, stresses the decisive role of internal causes, goes beyond the path of Western parties that rely mainly on external oversight, and offers an important reference for ruling parties around the world in party governance and in meeting the tests of holding power.
quoteZh: 习近平总书记关于党的自我革命的重要思想，坚持内因外因辩证统一，突出内因决定性作用，超越了西方政党主要依赖外部力量监督的路径，为世界各国执政党开展政党治理、应对执政考验提供了重要借鉴。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping has stressed since the 18th Party Congress. It refers to the Communist Party's efforts to discipline, purify and improve itself from within, and is closely tied to the anti-corruption campaign.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the drive since 2012 to tighten Party discipline, conduct and organisation, including anti-corruption work.
The formula of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities (the first) and with China's fine traditional culture (the second).
A formula adopted in 2021 that affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of his thought.
The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party, and to uphold the authority and centralised leadership of the Central Committee.

Rules issued by the Central Committee in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism among officials. They are the base for the campaign against the "four undesirable work styles".

t: Steering the new journey of the 15th Five-Year Plan period with the Party's overall leadership
zh: 以党的全面领导领航“十五五”发展新征程
paras: Dai Lixing and Guo Wenjing write in response to the Recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025). That document makes "upholding the Party's overall leadership" the first principle for economic and social development in 2026–2030. The authors argue that this leadership explains the achievements of the 14th Five-Year Plan period and is the fundamental guarantee for the next plan period and for Chinese modernization.

The article, published in Sichuan Party Building in November 2025, has three parts. It first credits the 14th Five-Year Plan results to the leadership of the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core. It then explains why the Recommendations give Party leadership such prominence. Finally it sets out four sets of measures for putting that leadership into practice.

For the 14th Five-Year Plan period, the authors cite GDP rising towards about 140 trillion yuan in 2025, R&D spending above 3.6 trillion yuan in 2024, and a rise in the national innovation ranking from 14th to 10th. They attribute these results to centralised, unified decision-making, for example the September 2024 Politburo package of incremental policies, and to strategic steadiness in pursuing "one blueprint to the end". For the coming period they give three reasons for the priority: a world of accelerating change and uncertainty, the socialist character and direction of Chinese modernization, and the Party's role in rallying the people around common prosperity and whole-process people's democracy.

The proposed measures are: strengthening political guidance through Xi Jinping Thought and the Two Establishes and Two Upholds; deepening the Party's self-reform through supervision of "key minorities", stricter conduct and anti-corruption work; focusing on people's livelihoods in employment, education, health and elderly care; and improving institutions, including reporting and accountability systems for carrying out Central Committee decisions. Read the original if you want an official-line account of how Party leadership is linked to the 15th Five-Year Plan and of the measures the authors propose for it.
quoteEn: Party leadership determines the socialist character of Chinese modernization and ensures that modernization is always aimed fundamentally at meeting the people's growing needs for a better life.
quoteZh: 党的领导决定了中国式现代化的社会主义性质，确保现代化建设始终以满足人民日益增长的美好生活需要为根本目的

glossary.explanation: The official formulation of China's development path under the Party's leadership, promoted prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022). Official texts present it as socialist modernization with distinctive Chinese features.
A formula from 2021–22 affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.
An official goal of broadly shared prosperity, which Party documents present as an essential requirement of socialism and of Chinese modernization.
The official term for China's democratic model, which Party texts say involves popular participation at every stage of decision-making, not only at elections.
An official formulation describing the Party's continuous internal rectification as a means of staying capable of leading.

t: The historical standing of the CPC's independent and autonomous mountain guerrilla warfare during the War of Resistance against Japan
zh: 抗战时期中国共产党开展独立自主的山地游击战的历史地位
source: Journal of the Party School of the CPC Central Committee (National Academy of Governance), 2025 no. 4
paras: How did the Communist Party of China (CPC) keep its independence while building the broadest anti-Japanese national united front? He Husheng argues that the answer lay in "independent and autonomous mountain guerrilla warfare". In the author's account, this raised guerrilla tactics to a strategic policy, freed the Party from Comintern constraints, the Kuomintang's attempt to absorb but not tolerate the Communists, and erroneous views within the Party, and marked a major theoretical and strategic advance in armed struggle.

The article, published in 2025, has four sections. The first treats the background, ideological basis and theoretical innovation of the policy. The second treats its strategic significance for the united front and armed struggle, and how it fitted the military situation. The third follows its application, including the move from mountain to plain guerrilla warfare, and its contribution to victory. The fourth assesses its historical standing through a "grand view of Party history" with objective, dialectical and subjective dimensions.

He contends that the policy rested on adapting Marxism to the Chinese context, on Mao Zedong's analysis of the war (notably On Protracted War), and on the Party's own capacity for independent judgement. It twice surpassed earlier practice: from mobile warfare to guerrilla warfare, then from ordinary guerrilla tactics to a strategy centred on independence and Party command of the army. Its core was absolute Party leadership over the army and reliance on the people in a people's war. According to the author, it let the base areas behind enemy lines support the frontal battlefield, produced victories such as Pingxingguan, and expanded base areas that later underpinned the founding of the People's Republic.

In the fourth section the author reads the policy as historically inevitable, as an expression of the unity of opposites and of continuity and discontinuity, and as evidence of the Party's historical initiative. He links it to the unity of Party spirit and the people's character, to the Party's confidence in national rejuvenation, and to the Party's dual history as social revolution and self-reform. Read the original if you study CPC military history or how contemporary Party historians apply the grand view of Party history to the War of Resistance.
quoteEn: Independent and autonomous mountain guerrilla warfare gave guerrilla tactics a strategic character bearing on the whole situation, and was raised to the Party's strategic policy.
quoteZh: 独立自主的山地游击战赋予游击战术以全局性战略特征，并被提升为党的战略方针。

glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context
glossary.explanation: The idea, put forward by Mao Zedong in 1938, that Marxism must be applied according to China's particular conditions. It is the standard Party framing for theoretical innovation.
The CPC's policy of cooperation with the Kuomintang and other forces against Japanese invasion, adopted in the mid-1930s and operating from 1937.
A recent approach in Party historiography, derived from Xi Jinping's call for a "grand view of history", which examines Party history within long historical, epochal and global contexts.

t: A historical examination of the Communist Party of China's leadership of cultural construction during the War of Resistance against Japan
zh: 抗日战争时期中国共产党领导文化建设的历史考察
paras: He Juan asks how the Communist Party of China (CPC) led cultural construction during the War of Resistance against Japan (1937–45), and what that record offers for building a strong socialist cultural nation today. The article argues that the Party recognised victory could not be won without cultural mobilisation. In the author's account, this led it to develop New Democratic culture, build a "cultural army", pursue a Chinese philosophy and social science, orient literature and art towards the masses, and expand wartime education.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the historical background: Japanese militarism's cultural enslavement of occupied areas, the cultural autocracy and revivalism of the Kuomintang diehards, and the Party's growing cultural self-awareness. The second, the longest, describes five practical paths: the New Democratic cultural banner, the "cultural army" of intellectuals and organisations, the Sinicisation of Marxism in the humanities and social sciences, literature and art for the masses, and cadre, school and social education. The third part draws lessons for the present.

He's central claim is that the Party defined a cultural direction as "national, scientific and mass-oriented", which answered both cultural restorationism and wholesale Westernisation. The author presents the Party as combining a united front among cultural figures with ideological leadership by Marxism. Examples include the Anti-Japanese Association of Chinese Writers and Artists, Mao Zedong's call for a "cultural army", reformed traditional opera, new yangge works, and historical scholarship by Fan Wenlan and Guo Moruo. The article also cites Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region figures on schools, literacy groups and night schools to show the reach of education.

He draws five lessons: uphold Marxism's guiding position and the Party's cultural leadership; hold to a Chinese cultural standpoint, in line with the Two Integrations; value intellectuals and build the Party's cultural ranks; keep culture oriented to the people; and build an autonomous Chinese knowledge system in philosophy and social science. The author links these to Xi Jinping's cultural thought and Chinese modernization, and concludes that the Party's comprehensive leadership of cultural work is the fundamental guarantee for a strong socialist cultural nation. Read the original if you want a detailed, Party-history account of wartime cultural policy, organisations and works, together with the lessons drawn for today.
quoteEn: The Party's cultural construction during the War of Resistance against Japan unfolded within a complex international and domestic environment.
quoteZh: 党在抗日战争时期的文化建设是在复杂国际国内环境之下展开的。

glossary.explanation: Mao Zedong's concept, developed around 1940, of an anti-imperialist, anti-feudal culture described as national, scientific and mass-oriented. It was meant to guide culture in the revolutionary stage before socialism.

A phrase from Mao Zedong, who said that besides the armed forces the revolution needed a cultural force of writers, artists and scholars. It is used for intellectuals organised under Party leadership.
Official formulation of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. It was elaborated in Xi Jinping-era Party theory.
The official term for China's path of modernisation under Party leadership, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The Party's project of applying Marxism to Chinese conditions and giving it Chinese forms. The slogan became prominent in Mao Zedong's 1938 writings.

keywords: literature and art for the masses

t: The CPC's European organisation and its efforts to win over and struggle against anarchists, in the perspective of the international communist movement
zh: 国际共运视域下中共旅欧组织对无政府主义者的争取与斗争
source: Studies on the History of the CPC, 2025 no. 3
paras: Wang Qiaoshen asks how the Communist International's changing stance towards anarchists shaped the early Chinese communists in Europe. The article takes issue with Arif Dirlik's account of a 1922 'split' between Chinese Marxists and anarchists, which Wang says overlooks the Comintern side. Wang argues that the dispute between the CPC's European organisation and the Gongyu she (Spare-time Society), a group of Chinese anarchists in France, cannot be understood without tracing its texts back to Comintern debates, and that the Comintern first sought an alliance with anarchists and then moved to opposing them.

The article follows the polemic from 1922 to 1924, using the journals Shaonian (Youth) and Gongyu. Part one covers the argument over Soviet Russia, part two the argument over organisation (trade-union autonomy versus a vanguard party), and part three the Comintern's repositioning of anarchists within the united front. Wang compares the Chinese texts with their sources, including International Press Correspondence, speeches by Lozovsky and Trotsky, and French communist and syndicalist writings. The foreign anarchist sources include Freedom, Emma Goldman and Alexander Berkman.

Wang shows that the Chinese anarchist Ou Shengbai drew his claims of Russian failure and 'party dictatorship' from Western anarchist writings. Zhou Enlai's reply in Shaonian, in Wang's reading, drew on Comintern reporting and played down wartime communism's faults, stressing instead the peasants' narrow class outlook. The Chinese communists then borrowed from the Comintern's polemics against the French syndicalist Robert Louzon to argue that the party is the working class's 'brain'. Wang notes that Yin Kuan and Xue Shilun at times conflated the repressive function of proletarian dictatorship with the party's vanguard role. Following Lozovsky's notion of an 'anarcho-reformist front', Chinese writers moved towards class-based criticism. Wang judges some of it exaggerated, such as Ren Zhuoxuan's charges, and notes that Zinoviev's more conciliatory line left the Comintern's own position wavering.

Wang concludes that between the Comintern's first congress in 1919 and its fifth in 1924 the alliance with anarchists dissolved into opposition. The European Chinese communists criticised anarchism in order to build a common front against capitalism and the yellow trade-union international, not to eliminate it, but with little success. Anarchism then lost its revolutionary character and, after 1927, served as an ideological tool of Guomindang repression. For the Chinese communists, Wang argues, the struggle clarified the party's vanguard mission, and the CPC later found a path different from Soviet Russia's on leading the masses. Read the original if you study early CPC history, Sino-anarchist relations or the Comintern's united-front policy and want a text-by-text tracing of sources.
quoteEn: This relationship and its changes constituted a structural feature of the international communist movement in the 1920s.
quoteZh: 这种关系及其变化构成了20世纪20年代国际共产主义运动的结构性特征。

glossary.explanation: The Third International, founded in Moscow in 1919 to coordinate communist parties worldwide. It guided the early CPC until its dissolution in 1943.
Comintern policy from 1922 calling on communists to cooperate with other workers' organisations, including social democrats, syndicalists and anarchists, against capital.
The Leninist idea that the communist party is the conscious, organised leading section of the working class.

t: Motives, practice, lessons: a three-dimensional study of the Communist Party of China's political mobilisation during the War of Resistance against Japan
zh: 动因·实践·镜鉴:抗战时期中国共产党政治动员的三维探赜
paras: This article asks how the Communist Party of China (CPC) turned a divided and endangered nation into a force capable of sustained resistance to Japan between 1931 and 1945.
