zh: 全民族抗战时期党领导通信事业的建设成就
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 27 October 2025
paras: This short historical commentary asks how the Chinese Communist Party built and ran its communications system during the War of Resistance against Japan. Yuan argues that the Party treated communications as a priority and that a radio-centred network, supplemented by other means, secured the unified leadership of the Central Committee and the Central Military Commission over the Eighth Route Army, the New Fourth Army and guerrilla forces.

The article is organised around four areas: a management system for communications work, a wartime network centred on Yan'an, the training of technical personnel, and the procurement and manufacture of equipment. It draws on directives, organisational data and statistics on stations, staff and trainees.

Yuan points out that the base areas lay interlocked with enemy-held territory, so command depended mainly on radio. Mao Zedong's January 1938 directive is cited as stressing radio's role in guerrilla and mobile warfare. The author counts 50 central documents on the subject and describes the Military Commission's Third Bureau as the unified manager of units and personnel. Its radio networks grew from six to a Yan'an-centred system of eight stations and eight networks by 1940, alongside a local telephone network and long-distance wire lines. Trained operators rose to nearly 5,000, and radio stations from 34 in 1937 to nearly 700 in 1945. Equipment came from purchases, captures and self-reliant production at workshops such as the Yan'an communications materials factory.

Yuan concludes that this communications enterprise became a "red bridge" for passing information, supporting victory and informing central decision-making in a way the author calls irreplaceable. Read the original if you want a compact, data-rich overview of the organisation and growth of Communist communications in wartime Yan'an, as presented in Party-history writing.
quoteEn: During the War of Resistance, the Party-led communications enterprise centred on Yan'an became a \"red bridge\" for passing information in the struggle against the enemy.
quoteZh: 全民族抗战时期中国共产党领导的以延安为中心的通信事业，成为对敌斗争中沟通信息的“红色桥梁”

glossary.literal: Third Bureau of the Military Commission
glossary.explanation: The Communications Bureau of the Central Military Commission, which managed radio and telephone communications for the Party and the Communist-led armies during the war.
Communist-led army formed in 1937 from the Red Army in the north under the united front with the Nationalists.
Communist-led army formed in 1937 in south-central China, also under the united front.

t: Re-examining the Communist Party of China's role as the mainstay in the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression
zh: 对中国共产党在抗日战争中发挥中流砥柱作用的再认识
source: Renmin Luntan·Xueshu Qianyan (People's Tribune·Academic Frontier), 2025 no. 14
paras: Written for the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance and the World Anti-Fascist War (2025), this article asks why the Communist Party of China's role as the "mainstay" (zhongliu dizhu) of the war needs to be re-examined, and what that role consisted of. Zhu argues that the Party's leadership was decisive to the victory, and that the claim should be defended against what the author calls historical nihilism.

The article opens with Xi Jinping's statements of 2014 and 2020 on the Party's mainstay role, which Zhu treats as the guiding framework. It then gives a brief historiography. Early People's Republic accounts, in Zhu's view, undervalued the Kuomintang's frontal battlefield. After the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978) the Party corrected this. Zhu says a later wave of nihilism went to the opposite extreme. The main body sets out eight ways in which the Party played its role, and a short final section turns to present-day implications.

Zhu's eight points run chronologically. The Party was first to call for armed resistance after 1931, first to propose a national united front, and first to promote Kuomintang–Communist cooperation. It framed a comprehensive-war line and the protracted-war strategy of Mao Zedong's On Protracted War. It built up guerrilla forces and made the rear-area battlefield a main battlefield. It followed a policy of resistance, unity and progress, and it checked Kuomintang anti-Communist campaigns without breaking the united front. It built 19 anti-Japanese base areas, which the author says covered over a million square kilometres and about 100 million people. It also forged a wartime spirit through heroes such as Yang Jingyu and Zhao Yiman. Zhu contends that anyone respecting the historical facts can see this role, and that without the Party the war would have lacked a correct line, mass participation and moral support.

Zhu concludes that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the ideological situation has changed fundamentally, but that hostile forces at home and abroad will keep belittling the Party's wartime role in order to attack its legitimacy and the socialist system. The author calls for propagating the mainstay role, upholding a "correct view" of the war and answering nihilism with historical facts. The aim is to rally the people around the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core and advance the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want to see how a senior CASS historian presents the official case for the Party's wartime leadership and how it is tied to current ideological work.
quoteEn: Without the Communist Party of China, the War of Resistance would have lacked the guidance of a correct line, the participation of the broad masses and powerful spiritual support, and there would have been no genuine national independence or people's liberation.
quoteZh: 如果没有中国共产党，抗日战争将难以有正确路线的指引、广大民众的参与和强大的精神支撑，也不会有真正的民族独立和人民解放。

glossary.literal: a rock standing in the midstream
glossary.explanation: An idiom for a steadfast force holding firm in a crisis. In Party historiography it describes the CPC's leading role in the War of Resistance, a formulation Xi Jinping has stressed since 2014.
In official discourse, a label for interpretations that are said to deny or belittle the Party's revolutionary history and its leaders. Here it refers to claims that downplay the CPC's wartime role.
The alliance of the CPC, the Kuomintang and other forces against Japan, formally established after the 1937 Marco Polo Bridge Incident.
Territories behind Japanese lines governed by the CPC during the war, which served as bases for guerrilla warfare and for the Party's wartime policies.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central official goal of the Party under Xi Jinping: restoring China to a position of national strength and prosperity after the "century of humiliation".

t: Theoretical logic and focal points for strengthening the political and organisational functions of Party organisations in the new era
zh: 新时代增强党组织政治功能和组织功能的理论逻辑与着力方向
source: Renmin Luntan·Academic Frontiers (People's Tribune·Academic Frontier), 2025 no. 10
paras: Zheng Shipeng takes up a goal set out in the Decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform: strengthening the political and organisational functions of Party organisations. The article argues that this task is a key link in the Party's new great project of Party building, a lever for following the Party's mass line, and a safeguard for Party leadership of deepened reform. Zheng's thesis is that the two functions are internally coupled, with organisation serving politics, and that strengthening them is both a theoretical requirement and a practical programme.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the internal logic of the two functions, drawing on Marx, Engels, the 1922 Second Congress Party constitution and Xi Jinping's statements. The second explains why strengthening them matters. The third proposes four areas for action. Zheng also cites Party statistics for the end of 2023: 99.185 million members and 5.176 million primary-level organisations.

Zheng defines the political function as the Party organisation's basic function: expressing the interests of the great majority, formulating and implementing policy, and mobilising society. The organisational function is the foundation of Party building and serves the political function. Their coupling means political function gives organisation a people-oriented direction, while organisation builds unity and shared political will. The article gives three reasons for strengthening them. It enriches the Marxist theory of party building, it supports the Party's self-reform in leading social revolution, and it raises the quality of Party leadership over deepened reform. The four focal points are that the organisational line should serve the political line and be led by political building. Party organisations should move from formal coverage to effective coverage, including in new economic and social organisations. The mass line should be strengthened through people-centred work and social appeal. Supervision mechanisms, including digital supervision, should be integrated to build a capable cadre corps.

Zheng concludes that strengthening both functions will consolidate the Party's political and organisational foundations. They will help ensure that central decisions are carried out at every level and advance Chinese modernization alongside the new great project. The article identifies weak, hollowed-out and marginalised grassroots organisations, and trivialised organisational life, as problems that need regular rectification. Read the original if you want a systematic statement of current Party-building orthodoxy, with its concrete proposals on grassroots coverage and supervision.
quoteEn: The organisational function serves the political function and is the basis and precondition for its effective exercise; the political function is the main purpose and end point of the organisational function, providing it with value guidance and political safeguards.
quoteZh: 组织功能服务于政治功能，是保证政治功能有效发挥的基础和前提；政治功能是发挥组织功能的重要目的和落脚点，为组织功能提供价值引领和政治保障。

glossary.explanation: A term prominent under Xi Jinping for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself. The article presents it as the means by which the Party leads wider social revolution.
The official name for China's development path, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It serves as the overarching goal for the policies discussed.
A long-standing Party principle of working 'from the masses, to the masses' and keeping close ties with ordinary people. Xi Jinping calls it the Party's greatest political strength.

glossary.zh: 新时代党的建设新的伟大工程
glossary.pinyin: xīn shídài dǎng de jiànshè xīn de wěidà gōngchéng
glossary.en: the Party's new great project of Party building
glossary.explanation: An official formulation for Party building since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It covers political, ideological, organisational, stylistic and disciplinary building and anti-corruption work.

t: Academic research on the history of the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea, and the transmission of its spirit
zh: 抗美援朝史的学术研究与精神传承
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 24 October 2025
paras: This short commentary asks how scholarship on the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea is developing and how the war's memory should be passed on. Liu describes the war as a just war fought under extremely unequal conditions, and argues that research on it has a high academic value and an important value for transmitting the spirit of the war.

Liu notes that over seven decades the field has widened to take in logistics, social mobilisation, cultural construction and war memory, drawing more on local archives and oral sources. The article has two parts: a section on small-scale perspectives, mainly material life, and a section on three levels of cultural memory.

In the first part, Liu treats clothing, food, shelter and movement as windows onto the Chinese People's Volunteers' survival, the state's logistics and industrial capacity, and the Party's political work. Examples include the "fistful of fried flour, a fistful of snow" and the "glory tea". In Liu's reading, these ordinary hardships show patriotism, internationalism, revolutionary optimism and heroism. The second part divides memory into national memory (veteran care, martyrs' burials, commemoration), social memory (art, media, public education) and individual memory (veterans' recollections), which Liu says complement one another.

Liu concludes that the spirit of the war continues Chinese civilisation and the national awakening of modern times. Liu calls it a strong impetus for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and urges Chinese scholars to build a discourse of material life history that can take part in international dialogue. Read the original if you want a brief sample of how current Chinese scholarship links Korean War research to patriotic memory and commemoration.
quoteEn: Social memory, as the intermediary between national memory and individual memory, is spread and reproduced mainly through literary and artistic works, news media and public education.
quoteZh: 社会记忆作为国家记忆与个体记忆之间的中介，主要通过文艺作品、新闻媒体、公共教育等方式进行传播与再生产。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, closely associated with Xi Jinping, of restoring China's national strength and international standing after the "century of humiliation".

glossary.en: War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea
glossary.explanation: The official Chinese name for China's participation in the Korean War (1950–53), in which the Chinese People's Volunteers fought alongside North Korea.

t: The historical significance and contemporary value of the Resist America, Aid Korea Movement
zh: 抗美援朝运动的历史意义和当代价值
paras: Hou Songtao, in a newspaper commentary from October 2025, asks what the mass political movement that accompanied the Korean War meant for China then and now. The author defines the Resist America, Aid Korea Movement, launched on 26 October 1950, as a campaign to support the war materially and morally, running alongside it throughout. Hou argues that it carries deep historical significance and continuing value.

The article is organised in four parts: the movement as a pillar of victory in the war, as a driver of economic reconstruction, as a force for ideological integration, and as a source of spiritual wealth. It draws on the circumstances of 1950, the movement's organisational steps, and Xi Jinping's 2020 summary of the Resist America, Aid Korea spirit.

Hou stresses the imbalance between the two sides: the United States held, in the author's figures, two-thirds of the capitalist world's national product and 70 per cent of its gold reserves, while the new China was poor and poorly armed. Mobilisation through propaganda, enlistment, support for the front and donations, equal to the cost of 3,710 fighter aircraft, is said to have secured victory. By linking patriotic pledges and production drives to the policy of fighting, stabilising and building at once, the movement is said to have completed economic recovery on schedule by 1952. Hou also argues that it ended the 'sheet of loose sand' condition of Chinese society through the removal of imperialist influence, 'three-hatred' education against pro-American, worshipful and fearful attitudes, and patriotic education.

Hou concludes that the spirit forged in the war and tested in the movement drove wartime victory, reconstruction and ideological unity, and will keep inspiring the Chinese people against hardship and strong adversaries. Read the original if you want a brief, officially aligned account of how Chinese scholarship frames the home-front campaign of the Korean War.
quoteEn: It can be said that this state of ideological disunity, like a sheet of loose sand, was thoroughly changed precisely in the course of the Resist America, Aid Korea Movement.
quoteZh: 可以说，这种思想上的一盘散沙状态，正是在抗美援朝运动中才有了彻底改变。

glossary.literal: Resist America and aid Korea movement
glossary.explanation: The mass political campaign launched in China from late October 1950 to support the Chinese People's Volunteers in the Korean War through propaganda, donations, enlistment and production drives.

glossary.pinyin: biān kàng, biān wěn, biān jiàn
glossary.en: fighting, stabilising and building at once
glossary.explanation: A policy line of the early 1950s to advance the war effort, economic stability and reconstruction simultaneously.

glossary.literal: 'three views' education (hate, despise, look down on US imperialism)
glossary.explanation: An ideological campaign during the movement that sought to teach hostility, contempt and disdain towards the United States and to remove pro-American or fearful attitudes.

glossary.pinyin: wěidà Kàng Měi Yuán Cháo jīngshén
glossary.literal: great spirit of resisting America and aiding Korea
glossary.explanation: A set of values, summarised by Xi Jinping in 2020, comprising patriotism, revolutionary heroism, optimism, loyalty and internationalism.

t: The Northeast industrial base's important contribution to the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea
zh: 东北工业基地在抗美援朝战争中的重要贡献
paras: Han Han, writing in China Social Sciences Today (24 October 2025), asks how China's Northeast industrial base related to the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea. The author argues that victory would have been far harder without the Northeast as a strategic rear area, and that the war in turn spurred the region's later development.

The commentary first reviews the base's wartime role in production and in transport. It then considers what the region's industrial heritage means today, and ends with proposals for how that heritage should be presented.

Han describes the Northeast as the war's general logistics base. Factories in Shenyang, Anshan and Fushun produced and repaired weapons and equipment, and light industry supplied uniforms, shoes and food. The author cites Shenyang's No. 53 Factory, named a national model factory, and the railway network, including the 'Little Tiger' locomotive, the first train into Korea, and the Yalu River bridge at Tonghua. On this basis Han draws three lessons: mutual aid within the socialist camp, the dialectical unity of national construction and national security, and the shared origin of the fighting spirit and the self-reliant Daqing spirit.

Han holds that the Aid Korea spirit receives too little attention in Northeast heritage work. The author proposes brand building and storytelling, such as documentaries, oral histories and social-media projects, and immersive exhibitions and cultural products. These are meant to fill a gap in the heritage narrative and to contribute to the region's full revitalisation and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a short example of how Chinese heritage and memory discourse links the Korean War to Northeast industrial history.
quoteEn: Without national security, economic construction cannot even begin; without a strong industrial base, national security cannot be guaranteed, and industrial heritage is the material witness of this dialectical relationship.
quoteZh: 没有国家安全，经济建设无从谈起；而没有强大的工业基础，国家安全亦无法保障，而工业遗产是这一辩证关系的物质见证。

glossary.en: War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea
glossary.explanation: The official Chinese name for China's participation in the Korean War (1950–53), when the Chinese People's Volunteers fought alongside North Korea against US-led forces.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal of the Communist Party, associated especially with Xi Jinping, of restoring China to national strength and prosperity.

glossary.literal: spirit of resisting America and aiding Korea
glossary.explanation: An official term for the values attributed to the Chinese volunteers and home front in the war, such as courage, sacrifice and patriotism.
An official ideal of hard work and self-reliance, drawn from the development of the Daqing oilfield in the Northeast from the 1960s.

keywords: War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea

t: The great spirit of resisting US aggression and aiding Korea: timeless and ever fresh
st: Marking the 75th anniversary of the Chinese People's Volunteers' entry into the Korean War
zh: 伟大抗美援朝精神跨越时空历久弥新——纪念中国人民志愿军抗美援朝出国作战75周年
paras: Published in China Social Sciences Today on 24 October 2025, this commemorative press report marks the 75th anniversary of the Chinese People's Volunteers entering the Korean War. It asks how the 'great spirit of resisting US aggression and aiding Korea' can keep its force in the present. The reporters, drawing on scholars and museum staff, present the war as securing peace for the new People's Republic and the spirit as a resource to be passed on through oral history, education and further research.

The piece opens with the anniversary, the crossing of the Yalu River in October 1950 and the 1,007 days of fighting. It then moves through four sections: the war's strategic results, the rescue of veterans' memories, the spirit's role in the new era, and how historical research can support transmission. Interviewees include scholars from Central China Normal University, Harbin Normal University, Liaoning University and Liaodong College, and the deputy director of the Memorial Museum of the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea.

In the speakers' account, the victory of 'less steel but more spirit' over a stronger enemy broke the myth of American invincibility, raised China's international standing and gave the first Five-Year Plan a peaceful environment. Nationwide mobilisation also aided economic recovery. The article describes urgent oral-history work: a major National Social Science Fund project launched in 2023, student visits to 571 veterans since 2016, and a documentary series with over 700 interviewees. Interviewees propose immersive technologies, ideological and political education, and cross-disciplinary research with foreign archives to rebut historical nihilism. One scholar sets out a 'wide, detailed, deep' research agenda and a loop of historical interpretation, value transformation and practical empowerment.

The report concludes that, at a new historical starting point, the spirit remains a driving force. It calls on readers to unite around the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core and advance towards building a modern socialist country and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a snapshot of how Chinese academics and official institutions currently frame the memory, teaching and research agenda of the Korean War.
quoteEn: Strengthening research on the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea has important historical-source value and academic significance for enriching the history of the Party, of New China and of military affairs.
quoteZh: 加强抗美援朝战争研究，对于丰富党史、新中国史、军事史等具有重要的史料价值和学术意义。

glossary.en: the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea
glossary.explanation: The official Chinese name for China's participation in the Korean War (1950–53), in which the Chinese People's Volunteers fought alongside North Korea.
In Party discourse, a label for interpretations that are said to deny or distort the Party's and socialism's history. The article cites it as something to be countered through research.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: An official national goal, closely associated with Xi Jinping's leadership, of restoring China's strength and international standing.

t: Coordinating the great task of boosting consumption
zh: 统筹做好提振消费大文章
paras: This commentary, published in Economic Daily on 16 October 2025 and written by Ji Zhengju, Liu Minru, Liu Chengli and Wang Xiaorui, asks how China should consolidate and extend the gains made in boosting consumption. It holds that final consumption is the lasting driver of economic growth and that, under the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core, the strategy of expanding domestic demand has produced historic results, especially during the 14th Five-Year Plan period.

The piece has three parts. The first describes six features of changing consumption patterns: consumption's basic role in growth, the growth of household, government and production-related consumption, rural consumption, the rising share of improvement-oriented consumption, higher-quality services, and new consumption formats and scenarios. The second sets out four priority directions for boosting consumption, and the third lists concrete measures to put in place.

The authors cite figures to show progress. Consumption contributed 44.5 per cent of economic growth in 2024. From 2013 to 2024 rural consumption grew at about twice the urban rate and the Engel coefficient fell by 1.4 percentage points. Online retail sales also outpaced total retail sales growth. The authors nonetheless say that insufficient effective demand remains a prominent problem: household consumption's share of disposable income is falling and households are cautious. Their four priorities are raising consumption capacity (of households, government and enterprises), strengthening willingness to consume, promoting consumption upgrading, and improving the consumption environment.

For implementation the authors call for coordinated reforms: prioritising employment, reforming income distribution, adjusting taxation, easing urban settlement for migrant workers, improving social security, and raising government consumption spending by "investing in people". They also propose refining trade-in and equipment-renewal policies and the use of ultra-long special treasury bonds. They further call for stronger consumer rights protection, removal of restrictive measures in the consumption field, and better paid-leave arrangements. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of the policy agenda for domestic consumption at the close of the 14th Five-Year Plan period.
quoteEn: Final consumption is the lasting driving force of economic growth.
quoteZh: 最终消费是经济增长的持久动力。

glossary.explanation: A long-term national strategy to make domestic consumption and investment, rather than exports, the main source of growth. It has been repeatedly emphasised in Party and government planning in recent years.
China's national development plan covering 2021–2025.
The share of household spending devoted to food; a falling coefficient is used as an indicator of rising living standards.
Subsidy programmes encouraging households to replace old appliances, vehicles and other goods with new, more efficient ones.
Special central government bonds with very long maturities, issued from 2024 to fund major projects, large-scale equipment renewal and consumer trade-in subsidies.
A policy slogan calling for more public spending on education, health, social security and other services for people, rather than only on physical infrastructure.

t: The key to building a modern socialist country in all respects lies in the Party: studying Volume V of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China
zh: 全面建设社会主义现代化国家关键在党——学习《习近平谈治国理政》第五卷
authors: National Association for Party-Building Studies (Quanguo Dangjian Yanjiuhui)
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily on 23 October 2025 as the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee met in Beijing, is a study piece on Volume V of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China. It argues that the key to building a modern socialist country in all respects, and to national rejuvenation, is the Party. In the authors' reading, Xi Jinping's statements show that a strong country presupposes a strong Party and that a strong Party in turn aims at and rests on a strong country.

The text is organised around three questions. It first looks back at why the Communist Party can lead the Chinese people in building a modern country. It then identifies five major risks and challenges facing the Party on the new journey. Finally it asks what kind of 'the world's most powerful political party' is to be built and how to build it.

On the historical question, the authors trace the Party's role through the new-democratic revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era, and describe Chinese modernization as a path that breaks the equation of 'modernization = Westernization'. They cite a Party membership of 100.271 million and a comprehensive organisational system. The five challenges are the great changes unseen in a century; the task of high-quality development, where some cadres are said to lack ability or willingness to act; the internet as the 'biggest variable' in ideological struggle; separation from the people; and corruption, which they say has become more hidden and variable despite an 'overwhelming victory' in the anti-corruption struggle.

For strengthening the Party, the authors set out five pillars: resolutely achieving the Two Upholds and grasping the decisive significance of the Two Establishes; scientific theory, centred on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and the Two Integrations; a strong cadre and talent corps; firm organisation, including Party-building in new economic and social organisations and among new forms of employment; and the Party's self-reform through problem-orientation, innovation, strictness and institutions. The piece closes with a call for strategic resolve and unity around the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Party-building establishment frames Party leadership as the precondition of Chinese modernization, and the risks it names.
quoteEn: Modernization is a process of continually scaling peaks: the further one goes, the heavier the tasks, the more the tests, and the greater the difficulties.
quoteZh: 现代化是不断攀登高峰的过程，越往前任务越重、考验越多、困难越大。

glossary.explanation: The official term for the Party's model of modernization, presented as distinct from Western paths. It has become a central slogan since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A formula from the 2021 Party resolution affirming Xi Jinping's core position on the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The requirement that Party members uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised leadership of the Central Committee.
The principle of integrating Marxism's basic tenets with China's specific realities and with its fine traditional culture.
Official term for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself, presented as its second answer to the question of escaping the 'historical cycle' of rise and decline.
An official economic goal emphasising quality, innovation and efficiency over extensive growth; described since 2017 as the primary task of building a modern socialist country.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

keywords: Xi Jinping: The Governance of China

t: Persistently advancing the Party's work style building
zh: 锲而不舍推进党的作风建设
paras: This short commentary, published in the PLA Daily on 22 October 2025, argues that the Party's work style (zuofeng) bears on its image, on popular support and ultimately on its survival. Zhu Dayi, drawing on Xi Jinping, holds that bad styles are stubborn and recurrent, so good ones cannot be secured once and for all. Style building is therefore called a perennial theme of Party building and part of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

The piece first sketches the Party's historical record on style, citing the Central Soviet Area, the Yan'an period, the "Two Musts" before entering Beijing and the reform era. It then says the 18th Party Congress (2012) and the Xi era deepened understanding of the subject, and that the current stage of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation brings unprecedented risks. Three areas for action follow: Party spirit, Party–mass relations and leading by example.

Zhu's central claim is that style problems are at root problems of Party spirit, and that their core is the relationship between the Party and the people. On Party spirit, the author calls for lifelong cultivation, study of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and joint handling of Party conduct, discipline and corruption. On the masses, officials are urged to feel for ordinary people, listen to them and learn from them. On leadership, "key minority" cadres should set an example by taking on hard tasks, practising integrity, opposing privilege and maintaining a sound family ethos.

Zhu concludes that style building must become regular and long-term, with attention to the everyday, the detailed and the sustained. Good style is presented as a source of cohesion and a driving force for the Party's cause. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary frames Party conduct, discipline and leadership responsibility in 2025.
quoteEn: Problems of work style are, at root, problems of Party spirit.
quoteZh: 作风问题根本上是党性问题。

glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: Slogan of Xi Jinping's leadership since 2012 covering ideological discipline, anti-corruption and institutional rules for Party members and cadres.
The ideological commitment, discipline and political qualities expected of a Communist Party member.
Xi Jinping's term for leading cadres, whose conduct is said to set the tone for the wider Party and society.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation

t: Advancing the construction of an autonomous knowledge system for CPC history and Party building studies through academic innovation
zh: 以学术创新推动中共党史党建学自主知识体系构建
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily (17 October 2025), Zhao Nuo asks how the newly established first-level discipline of CPC history and Party building studies can build its own autonomous knowledge system. The author argues that the discipline, which studies the Party's history and the laws of its self-development, is among the most distinctively Chinese in the social sciences and should help build Chinese philosophy and social sciences with their own system. The answer offered is sustained academic innovation along three mutually dependent lines: knowledge, theory and method.

The piece opens with Xi Jinping's recent remarks on the National Education Conference and on Fudan University's 120th anniversary, which Zhao treats as the fundamental guidance for this task. It then has three sections, one for each type of innovation, and closes with a short summary of how they fit together. Examples come from the author's own research, from wartime diplomacy and from digital tools.

On knowledge innovation, Zhao calls for a closed loop from sources to concepts through "three connections": linking history and reality to find new materials (local archives, oral history, audiovisual records); linking the whole and the individual to reach new viewpoints (for instance, cadres' diaries showing that their perceptions of the situation drew on both Marxist classics and Neo-Confucian ideas of "form" and "momentum"); and linking Party history and Party building to create new concepts such as the Party's self-reform. On theory, the author holds that Marxism is the "soul", excellent traditional Chinese culture the "root", and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era the latest resource, with scholars expected to answer the questions of the times and the Two Integrations as the guide. On method, Zhao advocates interdisciplinary borrowing (institutional analysis, network analysis, political psychology) screened by a Marxist standpoint, plus digital humanities: text mining of cadres' writings, large databases and GIS reconstruction of revolutionary sites.

Zhao concludes that knowledge innovation is the foundation, theory innovation the core "beams and pillars", and method innovation the engine, and that together they form the basic path for building the system. The task is described as significant and demanding. Read the original if you want a brief statement of how a Peking University scholar proposes to operationalise the "autonomous knowledge system" agenda in Party history research, including its use of digital methods.
quoteEn: These three are interdependent and mutually reinforcing, and together they form the basic path guiding the construction of an autonomous knowledge system for CPC history and Party building studies.
quoteZh: 这三者相互依存、相互促进，共同构成了引领中共党史党建学自主知识体系构建的基本路径。

t: The contemporary significance of the Communist Party of China's strategic guidance in the War of Resistance against Japan
zh: 中国共产党抗战指导谋略的当代意义
paras: Published in Guangming Daily on 19 October 2025, this short commentary follows Xi Jinping's speech at the commemoration of the 80th anniversary of victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War. Zhao Weibo and Liu Siwei ask what the Communist Party of China's wartime strategic guidance can still teach today. They argue that the Party, acting as the "mainstay" of the resistance, combined a global outlook, coordination across several domains, innovative military strategy and flexible armed struggle, and that each of these yields lessons for current national security.

The article has four sections: using a global vision to coordinate national security; multi-domain coordination to build a winning combined force; continuous innovation in military strategic guidance; and resolute yet flexible military struggle. Each section first reviews the Party's wartime practice and then draws a lesson for the present. The wartime evidence includes the Party's declaration after the outbreak of the Pacific War in December 1941, the united front, base areas behind enemy lines, guerrilla tactics, the Hundred Regiments Campaign and Mao Zedong's 1938 writings on guerrilla warfare.

The authors argue that the Party set China's resistance within the global anti-fascist struggle, predicted that Britain and the United States would eventually join the anti-Japanese camp, and treated the Soviet Union as a reliable external ally. At home, the Party built a national united front through concessions such as reorganising the Red Army into the Eighth Route Army and the New Fourth Army, shifting to rent and interest reduction, and adopting the "three-thirds" system of government. Behind enemy lines it expanded base areas and turned their economic and social resources into military capacity through production campaigns and streamlined administration. Militarily, the authors credit the Party with making guerrilla warfare the main form of combat and with deliberately shaping the battlefield, in the manner of a game of go. They also credit it with shifting strategy as circumstances changed, combining guerrilla and mobile warfare, and seizing the initiative.

From this history the authors derive proposals for today. China should approach security with a global vision, mutual learning among civilizations, multilateralism and self-reliant development, and should build the capacity for total people's war and an integrated national strategic system. It should develop algorithmic, unmanned and cognitive warfare, pre-position in space, the deep sea, the polar regions and cyberspace, and conduct military struggle that is "not out of control, not showing weakness, not suffering loss", so as to safeguard territorial sovereignty and maritime rights. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese military-academic writers link the history of the War of Resistance to present-day security and military-strategy thinking.
quoteEn: Strategic guidance in war is not merely a matter of military command; more important is the comprehensive preparation and effective integration of the factors that decide victory or defeat, so that a combined advantage in strength can check and defeat a powerful adversary.
quoteZh: 战争战略指导并非单纯军事指挥问题，更重要的在于对影响战争胜负诸要素进行全面准备和有效整合，以综合力量优势制衡制胜强敌对手。

glossary.explanation: A principle of government in the anti-Japanese base areas under which Communists, left-progressives and middle-of-the-road figures each took roughly one third of the seats.

glossary.literal: anti-Japanese base areas in the enemy's rear
glossary.explanation: Territories behind Japanese lines, such as Jin-Cha-Ji, where the Party built armed forces, government and an economy during the war.
Mao Zedong's strategy of fighting by mobilising the whole population alongside regular and irregular forces. The article treats it as a continuing basis for modern warfare.

t: Accelerating the construction of a discourse system for the Communist Party of China's self-reform
zh: 加快构建中国共产党自我革命话语体系
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily, Liu Xianchun argues that the Party needs to build, quickly, a discourse system for its self-reform that has Chinese characteristics, style and manner. In Liu's view, the task enriches the Marxist theory of party building and deepens understanding of the laws governing the CPC's rule. It also helps consolidate the Party's long-term governing position and tell the Party's story abroad.

The short commentary sets out three guiding principles. They are: taking Xi Jinping's important thought on the Party's self-reform as the lead; orienting the work towards the problems unique to a large party; and drawing on resources from many disciplines.

On the first, Liu presents self-reform as the Party's second answer to the historical cycle of rise and decline, after Mao Zedong's 1945 answer of letting the people supervise the government. The discourse must explain the core content of Xi's thought and link it to the achievements of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012). On the second, Liu lists the tests and dangers the Party still faces, including ideological wavering, weak organisations, formalism and bureaucracy, and urges that discourse and practice advance together, including at the grass roots. On the third, Liu calls for politics, history, sociology, linguistics, communication studies and psychology to be combined, for example through a corpus of self-reform language in Party documents.

Liu concludes that the discourse system is both a theoretical task and a practical one, and should be political, practical and scholarly at once. It would give theoretical and discursive support to self-reform and, in Liu's words, offer Chinese wisdom and a Chinese approach to party governance worldwide. Read the original if you want a brief, official-register statement of how Party scholars frame the project of building self-reform discourse.
quoteEn: The Party's self-reform is not an abstract deduction of concepts, but a proactive revolution rooted in practice and aimed at solving problems.
quoteZh: 党的自我革命不是抽象的概念演绎，而是扎根实践、解决问题的主动革命。

glossary.explanation: A core concept in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse. It describes the Party's efforts to purify, improve, renew and strengthen itself, and is presented as the Party's answer to the historical cycle of rise and decline.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party-discipline and anti-corruption campaign pursued since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

glossary.pinyin: zhì luàn xīng shuāi lìshǐ zhōuqīlǜ
glossary.en: historical cycle of rise and decline
glossary.literal: historical cycle of order and chaos, rise and decline
glossary.explanation: A phrase from the 1945 Yan'an conversation between Mao Zedong and Huang Yanpei. It names the pattern of dynasties flourishing and then falling, which the Party says it has escaped.

glossary.en: problems unique to a large party
glossary.literal: difficulties unique to a big party
glossary.explanation: Official phrase for the challenges facing a very large ruling party, summarised as the "six how-to-always" questions, such as how to keep close ties with the people.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Grasping and conducting criticism and self-criticism scientifically and accurately through dialectical thinking
zh: 以辩证思维科学准确把握与开展批评和自我批评
paras: Chen Hexiang, a professor at the Shenzhen Party school, asks how Party members and officials can make criticism and self-criticism an effective tool rather than a blunt one. Writing in the People's Daily in October 2025, Chen argues that the answer lies in dialectical thinking, which the author presents as the basis of Xi Jinping's remarks on the subject since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The piece is framed by the call in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) to use this "weapon" to keep the Party's political ecology clean.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the multiple values of criticism and self-criticism. The second turns to methods and strategies, and the third to the "art" of turning opposition into unity. Xi's statements are quoted throughout. The text is tied to the current campaign of study and education on the central Eight-point Regulation, and to the aim of making improved work style routine and long-lasting.

In the first part, Chen identifies three functions. Epistemologically, criticism works as a "corrector" that exposes hidden contradictions and corrects cognitive bias within the cycle of practice and understanding. Dialectically, it is a "negative mediator" of sublation: a constructive negation that moves from negating the status quo to raising expectations of improvement and then reconstruction, in a cycle of unity–criticism–unity. In practice, its effects are twofold. Chen lists six criteria for telling constructive from destructive criticism, among them aim, object, attitude, content, communication and consequences. The second part pairs four methods, each of which should be balanced rather than chosen once and for all: inward and outward focus, fast and slow timing, public and private settings, and direct and indirect expression. The third part calls for balancing principle with flexibility, the whole with the part, and the present with the long term.

Chen concludes that the courage for self-reform is the Party's most distinctive quality and that criticism and self-criticism are central to preserving its vanguard character and purity. Chen calls on every Party member and official to use the tool often and well, until it becomes a habit, a sense of duty and a responsibility. The stated aim is to strengthen the Party's capacity for self-purification, self-improvement, self-renewal and self-advancement on the path to national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-school scholar applies Marxist dialectics to the practical conduct of internal Party criticism and to Xi Jinping's statements on it.
quoteEn: Criticism and self-criticism are a \"sharp weapon\" not because their content is pointed, but because of the dialectical logic within them: they both reveal contradictions and point to ways of resolving them.
quoteZh: 批评和自我批评之所以成为“锐利武器”，不在于其内容的尖锐性，而在于其内含的辩证逻辑：既揭示矛盾，又指出解决矛盾的方法。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing Communist Party practice of members openly criticising one another and examining their own faults, usually in meetings such as democratic life meetings. The Party describes it as a core method of internal discipline and a political strength.

Rules on work style adopted by the Central Committee in December 2012. They target formalism, bureaucracy, extravagance and waste among officials, and have been repeatedly reinforced through study and education campaigns.
The Hegelian and Marxist notion (Aufhebung) of negating something while preserving and raising its valuable elements to a higher level.
A term in Party discourse for the overall political climate within the Party, including its norms, culture and discipline. "Purifying" it is a stated aim of Party-building.

Official term, often rendered "the Party's self-reform", for the Party's claimed capacity to correct itself and rid itself of problems without outside pressure. It has been emphasised since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

t: Opening up a new realm of Party self-reform
zh: 开辟自我革命新境界
paras: This newspaper commentary, first published in Jiefang Daily on 30 September 2025, reads the fifth volume of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China through the chapter on upholding the Party Central Committee's centralised and unified leadership and carrying the Party's self-reform through to the end. Ding and Hao argue that the volume gives the Party's self-reform a systematic theoretical form, and that studying it deepens understanding of the laws of Communist Party governance.

The authors organise the chapter's material under three headings: the systematisation of Xi Jinping's ideas on self-reform, the identification of problems unique to a large party, and the building of a system of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. They cite specific speeches and articles collected in the volume for each.

On the first point, Ding and Hao describe Xi's January 2024 speech at the Third Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection as completing this systematisation. In their account it answers why the Party must, can and how it should carry out self-reform, and sets out a strategic approach of nine "takes" ("jiu ge yi"). On the second, they present the "six how-to-always" questions (Xi, January 2023) as the main factors affecting the Party's vanguard character and governing capacity, plus seven requirements for removing the soil in which corruption grows. On the third, they set out four "full" features of the approach and five systems to be improved: organisation, education, oversight, institutions and responsibility.

The authors conclude that mastering this theoretical system strengthens theoretical awareness and practical motivation to open up a new realm of self-reform. Read the original if you want a short, officially aligned guide to how the fifth volume of Xi's collected governance texts presents Party self-reform and its component formulas.
quoteEn: This constitutes two major principles: leading the great social revolution through the Party's self-reform, and escaping the historical cycle of rise and fall through self-reform together with supervision by the people.
quoteZh: 这就构成了以党的自我革命引领伟大社会革命、通过自我革命和人民监督跳出历史周期率的两大原理。

glossary.explanation: Official term for the Party's efforts to correct its own errors and combat corruption and misconduct. Xi Jinping has made it a central theme since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Official name for the comprehensive Party discipline and anti-corruption drive launched after 2012.

glossary.en: problems unique to a large party
glossary.literal: difficult problems peculiar to a big party
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's phrase, used since the 20th Party Congress (2022), for challenges said to arise specifically from the Party's size and long period in power.

glossary.en: Xi Jinping: The Governance of China
glossary.explanation: The official multi-volume collection of Xi Jinping's speeches and writings on governance, published in English by Foreign Languages Press.

t: Raising the digital competence of leading cadres
zh: 提升领导干部数字化胜任能力
paras: This short commentary, published in Study Times on 26 September 2025, asks how leading cadres can acquire the digital competence that the deepening construction of digital government requires. Qiu argues that, with big data, cloud computing, blockchain and artificial intelligence changing public expectations of government, the country needs cadres with strong digital awareness who can make digitalisation an effective tool of governance.

The article begins from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), which calls for a cadre corps able to lead modernization. It then moves through three steps: the digital mindset cadres need, the competence they must show across the digital economy, digital government and digital social governance, and the shortcomings Qiu sees at present. It ends with four proposals.

Qiu describes digitalisation as an intellectual revolution as well as a technical change, and divides digital thinking into three parts: sensitivity to data, use of data and technology to solve problems, and data-based decision-making that replaces reliance on experience. The article identifies gaps in four areas. Some cadres reduce digitalisation to technical tools, depend too heavily on outside technical providers, struggle with data sharing and security across departments, or follow a technology-first approach that neglects public needs.

Qiu proposes tiered, practice-oriented training; cross-departmental platforms and task forces to break down data silos; simulation platforms and training in algorithm oversight, data privacy and technical ethics, under the principle of technology as a tool and service as the foundation; and inclusion of digital competence in cadre evaluation, with measurable indicators and incentives that favour cadres combining governance thinking and technical understanding. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Party media frame digital skills training and assessment for officials.
quoteEn: Digitalisation is not merely a technological change but, more importantly, a revolution in thinking.
quoteZh: 数字化不仅仅是一场技术变革，更是一场思维革命。

glossary.explanation: Officials holding leadership posts in the Party, government and state institutions in China.
The use of digital technologies and data to reshape government administration and public services, a stated national construction goal in China.

t: The indelible historical memory of the Chinese nation
st: On the Red Flag Canal spirit
zh: 中华民族不可磨灭的历史记忆
paras: This short commentary in Study Times (26 September 2025) takes up the Red Flag Canal spirit, which Xi Jinping has called an indelible historical memory of the Chinese nation. Chen opens with Xi's remarks of 2011, 2019 and 2022, including the claim that the spirit is of one lineage with the Yan'an spirit. The author argues that these remarks affirm its lasting value and offer a basic guide for drawing wisdom and strength for overcoming difficulties.

The article first recounts how the spirit arose in Lin County (now Linzhou), Henan. It cites chronic drought, the 1959 crisis and the decision to draw water from the Zhang River. It then lists the construction achievements between 1960 and 1969, and the canal's foreign recognition. Four sections follow, one for each element of the spirit.

Chen takes the spirit's content as self-reliance, hard struggle, solidarity and cooperation, and selfless dedication. Self-reliance is called its essence, illustrated by the author's figures that local people made 77 per cent of the cement and that the state supplied 14.94 per cent of total investment. Hard struggle is shown through scarce food, improvised tools and inventions. Solidarity is presented as an institutional advantage of concentrating efforts on major tasks, with cadres sharing the workers' conditions. Selfless dedication is illustrated by county Party secretary Yang Gui, the worker Ren Yangcheng and the technician Wu Zutai.

Chen concludes that the spirit embodies the Party's nature and purpose and the people's historical agency. The piece serves as a Party-history primer on a model spirit. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated writers present the Red Flag Canal as a source of spiritual heritage in the new era.
quoteEn: Self-reliance is the essence of the Red Flag Canal spirit, showing the people's historical agency and their endogenous drive to rely on their own locality and strength.
quoteZh: 自力更生是红旗渠精神的精髓要义，彰显了人民群众的历史主体性和立足本地、依靠自身的内生动力。

glossary.explanation: A Party-promoted ethos drawn from the building of the Red Flag Canal in Lin County, Henan (1960–1969). It is summarised as self-reliance, hard struggle, solidarity and cooperation, and selfless dedication.
The Party's official term for the values associated with its Yan'an period (1935–1948), such as self-reliance, plain living and serving the people.

t: How the Party forged intellectual strength during the nationwide War of Resistance
zh: 全民族抗战时期党对知识力量的锻造
paras: This short commentary, drawing on documents held in the Central Archives, asks how the Communist Party of China treated intellectuals during the nationwide War of Resistance against Japan. Gao argues that the Party united, trusted and trained progressive youths and intellectuals who joined the revolutionary ranks, turning them into an important force in winning the war.

The article is organised under four headings: recruiting intellectuals in large numbers, valuing them, training and educating them, and their contributions to victory. It relies on directives such as "Recruit Large Numbers of Intellectuals" (1939), the 1941 instruction on specialists in the army and the 1942 instruction on intellectual cadres in the troops.

Gao shows how recruitment was justified by statements from Mao Zedong and Chen Yun that the war and the building of a new China required intellectuals. The Party promoted them, gave them responsibility according to their expertise, guaranteed material treatment and did not impose rigid political requirements on non-Party specialists. Local base areas issued their own measures to reward technical work. For training, Gao points to the Counter-Japanese Military and Political University and technical schools such as the Yan'an Natural Science Institute. The 1942 directive's formula of "tolerate, transform, use" is presented as an interconnected, dialectical whole.

Gao concludes that these policies won intellectuals' support for the Party's resistance and laid a solid basis for victory and for building the liberated areas. Their contributions included wartime propaganda, literary work and agricultural and military science, such as crop improvement at the Guanghua Farm. Read the original if you want a brief, archive-based account of the Party's wartime policy towards intellectuals and the documents behind it.
quoteEn: The crucible of war forged a powerful intellectual force.
quoteZh: 烽火熔炉锻造了强大的知识力量。

glossary.explanation: A three-part policy towards intellectuals in the army set out in a 1942 General Political Department directive. It means accepting them, changing their petty-bourgeois outlook, and assigning work suited to them.
A Communist-run cadre training school founded during the War of Resistance, known in short as Kangda. It trained political and military cadres, including many young intellectuals.

t: Strengthening day-to-day supervision by Party organizations
zh: 强化党组织日常监督
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 25 September 2025, asks how Party organizations can make their day-to-day supervision of Party members and cadres more effective. Zhang Lisi argues that such supervision is both an institutional constraint and a means of guidance and correction. In Zhang's account it is a key tool of the Party's self-reform and of making improvements in conduct routine and lasting.

The piece opens with Xi Jinping's call to strengthen daily supervision and increase its "penetrating power and effectiveness". It then sets out four areas of work: ideological foundations, supervisory skills, institutional safeguards and working style. The author refers throughout to the central Eight-point Regulation and the campaign against the "four undesirable work styles".

Zhang argues that Party organizations stand on the front line, know their members at close range and can intervene early, so that individual lapses do not become systemic risks. The author calls for theoretical study and discipline education, case-based training, and digital platforms with data comparison and early warning. Zhang also proposes five institutional measures: vertical coordination between levels, cross-department supervision led by discipline inspection organs, wider supervisory methods, deployment of supervisory strength to the grassroots, and clear responsibility lists. Without a solid working style, the author warns, even good systems become "armchair strategy".

Zhang concludes that improving supervision is a systemic task requiring coordinated effort, with the aim of full and regular coverage, a clean political environment and a good atmosphere for getting things done. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Central Party School scholar presents the practical agenda for Party supervision under full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.
quoteEn: Without a rigorous working style, even the most refined supervisory system and the most professional supervisory capacity will become mere "armchair strategy".
quoteZh: 缺乏过硬作风，再完善的监督制度、再专业的监督能力，也会沦为“纸上谈兵”。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping's leadership since 2012, covering Party discipline, ideology, organization and conduct, and anti-corruption work.
A formulation stressing that the Party must continually correct its own faults and combat corruption and misconduct through internal discipline and supervision.
Rules adopted by the Party leadership in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism among officials, for example on banquets, travel and meetings.
Formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, the four faults targeted by the Party's conduct-improvement campaigns.

t: Lessons from the Party's discipline building in the Xiangshan period
zh: 香山时期党加强纪律建设的经验启示
paras: Huang Xiaofang asks what experience the Communist Party's discipline building in the Xiangshan period offers today. This was the roughly six months in 1949 when the Central Committee was based at Xiangshan, Beijing, and, as the article describes it, carried out the march to the whole country, preparations for the new Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference and the founding of the new state. Huang argues that nationwide victory in the War of Liberation was inseparable from stronger discipline in the Party and army, and that this experience matters for full discipline building and the Party's self-reform today.

This short commentary draws three or four lessons from the period and sets each beside developments since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The sources are mainly directives, speeches and regulations from 1949 by Zhu De, Mao Zedong and the Central Committee, set beside Xi Jinping's statements and the Regulations on Disciplinary Actions of the Communist Party of China.

Huang's main points are that discipline must serve the Party's central task, rest on the people's interests, keep pace with changing conditions, and combine education with enforcement. In 1949 the central task was consolidating victory and shifting the Party's focus from countryside to cities. Rules on mass discipline, the "eight-point" proclamation protecting people's lives and property, and corrections to abuses during city takeovers, such as free entertainment for troops or seizure of capitalists' property, are presented as examples. Education before entering Shanghai and a system of rewards and punishments are also cited.

Huang concludes that the Party under Xi Jinping has followed the same lines. Mass discipline became one of six disciplines, with political discipline first. The Regulations were revised three times, and regular discipline education was linked to strict punishment of every violation. In Huang's view, these measures provide disciplinary support for Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party-history scholarship ties the 1949 period to current discipline policy.
quoteEn: Safeguarding the fundamental interests of the people is the starting point and foothold of all the Party's work, and also the core and foundation of the comprehensive strengthening of Party discipline since the new era began.
quoteZh: 维护人民群众的根本利益是党的一切工作的出发点和立足点，也是新时代以来全面加强党的纪律建设的核心和根本。

glossary.explanation: The official formulation of China's development path, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models of modernization.
An official term, prominent under Xi Jinping, for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself from within.
The months in 1949, from March to the founding of the People's Republic in October, when the Central Committee was based at Xiangshan in western Beijing.

glossary.zh: 中国共产党纪律处分条例
glossary.en: Regulations on Disciplinary Actions of the Communist Party of China
glossary.explanation: The Party's main internal code setting out violations and sanctions. The article says it was revised in 2015 and twice more since.

t: The logic of interaction between the Party's self-reform and social revolution
zh: 党的自我革命与社会革命的互动逻辑
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 11 September 2025
paras: Liang Haifeng asks how the Communist Party's internal renewal relates to the wider transformation of Chinese society. The article argues that the Party's self-reform and social revolution form a dialectical unity in which each strengthens the other. Self-reform supplies internal motive force and political leadership for social revolution, while the practical results of social revolution serve as the ultimate yardstick of whether self-reform is working.

This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today, first treats self-reform as the engine of social revolution and then social revolution as the external test of self-reform. It then turns to Party conduct (zuofeng) as the link between the two and lists current obstacles and remedies. Liang draws on Marx, Engels and Lenin, on Mao Zedong's and Deng Xiaoping's theories of Party building, and on the campaigns of the Xi Jinping era.

Liang reasons from the Marxist premise that the contradiction between productive forces and relations of production drives history, and that a proletarian party's revolutionary character makes self-reform its core dynamic. Social revolution then feeds back in three ways. Its achievements, such as the economy's size and the elimination of absolute poverty, are said to confirm the Party's self-reform. The problems it exposes, such as corruption, formalism and bureaucratism, mark where self-reform must aim. Its goals, including the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, modernisation of national governance and high-quality development, set the tasks of self-reform. Conduct building is the bridge, converting the Party's purity and advanced character into practical strength, though Liang says formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance still threaten it.

Liang proposes deepening conduct building through ideological education and Party-spirit training, firmer institutional constraints, regular supervision and "zero tolerance" for violations. The author concludes that persistence, summed up as making such work "regular" and "long-term", is needed to keep the Party's advanced and pure character and its role as the leadership core. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-building scholars at CASS connect self-reform with social transformation through the idea of Party conduct.
quoteEn: Conduct building works like a hub, converting the purity and advanced character forged by self-reform into a powerful practical force driving social revolution, so that the two connect and reinforce each other.
quoteZh: 作风建设如同枢纽，将自我革命锻造的纯洁性、先进性，转化为推动社会革命的强大实践力量，使两者相互贯通、协同促进。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping has stressed since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It refers to the Party's efforts to discipline, purify and improve itself, including through anti-corruption work.
Efforts to improve officials' work style and behaviour. It targets formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, together called the "four undesirable work styles" (四风).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term national goal associated with the Chinese Dream, stressed by Xi Jinping since 2012.
The official economic development goal that emphasises quality, efficiency and balance over speed of growth alone.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Strict supervision and discipline enforcement as a sharp tool of the Party's self-reform
zh: 从严监督执纪是党的自我革命的利器
paras: Gai Yixin takes up Xi Jinping's statement that strict supervision and discipline enforcement is "a sharp tool of the Party's self-reform". The article, published in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2025, argues that this practice is both a means of punishing corruption and correcting conduct and a pillar for keeping the Party from changing its nature, colour or flavour. Gai presents it as a key measure of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party in the new era.

The piece has three parts. The first traces strict supervision and discipline enforcement to Marxist party theory and to more than a century of Party history. The second describes what it contributes to self-reform since the 18th Party Congress (2012): firm discipline, punishment of corruption and rectification of work style. The third sets out how to strengthen it further.

In the first part Gai argues that the Party's vanguard character is not innate or permanent. Citing Marx and Lenin on party discipline, and episodes from the Jinggangshan period, Yan'an, the early People's Republic and reform and opening up, Gai holds that long-term rule exposes the Party to the erosion of power, capital and personal ties. Gai says the Party therefore needs routine, institutionalised supervision. In the second part, Gai credits the "four forms" of supervision and discipline enforcement, the revised disciplinary regulations, the anti-corruption drive of "no forbidden zones, full coverage, zero tolerance" and the campaign against the "four malpractices". Gai nonetheless describes the anti-corruption situation as still severe and complex.

Gai calls for three measures: a coordinated supervision system joining intra-Party and popular supervision; stronger day-to-day supervision by Party organisations, with closed-loop management of problems found; and joint investigation and handling of unhealthy work styles and corruption, through investigation, case-based reform and prevention. Gai concludes that supervision can only be strengthened, never weakened. Read the original if you want a representative statement of how Party theorists in 2025 link discipline enforcement to the Party's self-reform and to the Party's own account of its history.
quoteEn: The fundamental purpose of routine supervision is to ensure that the Party's line, principles and policies are implemented; it must not be confined to the surface of operational work and must show a high degree of political acuity and discernment.
quoteZh: 日常监督的根本目的在于保障党的路线方针政策得到贯彻落实，不能局限于业务工作的表象，必须具备高度的政治敏锐性和鉴别力。

glossary.explanation: Official term, prominent under Xi Jinping, for the Party's efforts to discipline, purify and renew itself. It is presented as the Party's answer to the problem of how to escape the historical cycle of rise and decline.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Policy line since the 18th Party Congress (2012) covering ideology, organisation, work style, discipline and anti-corruption within the Party.

A graded approach to handling violations: criticism and talks as the norm; light disciplinary sanctions or organisational adjustment; heavy sanctions; and criminal referral for serious cases. It is written into Party regulations.
Formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, targeted since the Central Committee's eight-point rules of 2012.

glossary.pinyin: bù gǎn fǔ, bù néng fǔ, bù xiǎng fǔ
glossary.en: no forbidden zones, full coverage, zero tolerance
glossary.explanation: The article cites two related slogans. The three-part formula (dare not, cannot, do not want to be corrupt) is a Party anti-corruption framework combining deterrence, institutional constraint and moral awareness. The phrase rendered here is a separate slogan on the scope of the anti-corruption campaign (无禁区、全覆盖、零容忍).

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Regulating the exercise of power as a requirement of anti-corruption work
st: Institutions, supervision and the ideological foundation of exercising power for the people
zh: 理论资源导航
paras: Starting from Xi Jinping's statement that "anti-corruption must regulate the exercise of power", Wang Daguang and Wu Tongge argue that corruption is at root the abuse of power for private gain, and that fighting it therefore means tightening supervision and restraining power. The piece, published in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) in 2025, presents this as guidance for the new era and for carrying the Party's self-reform through to the end.

The authors organise the argument in three parts. The first concerns key links in the chain of power: authorisation, use and restraint. The second concerns building a comprehensive, multi-layered system of power supervision. The third concerns consolidating the ideological base of holding and using power for the people. Throughout, they quote Xi Jinping's remarks and cite Party documents such as the decisions of the Third and Fourth Plenums of the 19th Central Committee.

In the first part the authors say that the anti-corruption situation remains "severe and complex", with existing corruption not yet cleared and new cases still arising, so rules must keep pace. They call for scientific authorisation (a division of decision-making, executive and supervisory powers, with power lists, negative lists and responsibility lists), procedural discipline for decision-making, approval and law enforcement, and transparency so that power works "in the sunshine". In the second part they stress enforcing rules rigidly, applying democratic centralism fully, with leading officials setting an example, and building two defences: early warning and precise correction, the latter using the "three distinctions" to tell error from wrongdoing while keeping officials motivated. In the third part they urge officials to hold a correct view of power and to stand in awe of the people, the organisation and Party discipline and law.

The authors conclude that institutional constraint, supervision and moral-political cultivation must advance together, in line with the formula of not daring, not being able and not wanting to be corrupt. Officials are told to treat power as service and responsibility, accept organisational supervision, observe the Eight-point Regulation and act under the law, never above it. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official Party-building writing in 2025 links anti-corruption institutions with the ideological education of cadres.
quoteEn: The vitality of institutions lies in their enforcement.
quoteZh: 制度的生命力在于执行。

glossary.pinyin: bù gǎn fǔ, bù néng fǔ, bù xiǎng fǔ
glossary.en: not daring, not being able and not wanting to be corrupt
glossary.explanation: A formula in Party anti-corruption policy describing three mutually reinforcing aims: deterrence through punishment, institutional barriers, and moral-ideological conviction. It has been widely used since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
Official term for the Party's efforts to discipline and purify itself, stressed in Xi Jinping's speeches. In official usage it covers anti-corruption and Party-building work.
The Party's fundamental organisational principle, combining internal discussion with unified decisions and discipline binding on all members.
Rules adopted by the Central Committee in December 2012 to curb formalism, extravagance and bureaucratic style among officials. The article treats them as a long-term, binding standard.
A guideline for handling cadre mistakes that distinguishes error from misconduct, for example by looking at motive, intent and consequences. It aims to protect officials who act in good faith.

t: Advancing self-reform requires strengthening the foundation and Party spirit
st: Five requirements for enhancing Party spirit among Party members and cadres
zh: 推进自我革命必须固本培元、增强党性
paras: Zhang Hao's commentary, published in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2025, takes up Xi Jinping's statement that advancing self-reform requires strengthening the foundation and Party spirit (dangxing). Zhang argues that Party spirit plays a central role in the Party's self-reform and that its enhancement must be put into practice so that Communists keep the Party's advanced and pure character. The piece reads as a study of Xi's formulation rather than an independent theoretical inquiry.

The article follows the five requirements in Xi's wording: firm ideals and convictions, loyalty to the Party, deep feeling for the people, sound moral character, and honesty and integrity. Each requirement gets its own section, and each section is divided into three practical routes or demands addressed to Party members and cadres. Zhang draws on Xi's speeches, classical Chinese sayings, Marx and examples of model Communists such as Jiao Yulu and Zhang Fuqing.

On ideals, Zhang argues that conviction rests on mastering theory, above all Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, on grasping the laws of historical development, and on concrete work in one's post. On loyalty, the article treats the Two Establishes as the decisive political achievement of the new era and calls for turning that consensus into the Two Upholds. It also asks cadres to keep the "matters of national importance" in mind and to observe discipline, political discipline above all. On the people, moral character and integrity, Zhang holds that Party spirit and the people's nature are unified, and urges cadres to rely on the masses and learn from them. Zhang also urges them to draw on traditional Chinese culture and on heroic models, and to use criticism and self-criticism. Finally, they should cultivate reverence, wariness and bottom lines against corruption.

Zhang concludes that Party spirit is the basis of a Communist's conduct and career, and that the Party's self-reform depends on cadres continually cultivating it in these five respects. The text is a normative, exhortatory guide rather than an analysis of cases or institutions. Read the original if you want a clear example of how Party-school-style writing in 2025 turns Xi Jinping's formula on Party spirit into concrete expectations for cadres.
quoteEn: In essence, upholding Party spirit means upholding the people's nature, and upholding the people's nature means upholding Party spirit; strengthening Party spirit requires cultivating deep feeling for the people.
quoteZh: 从本质上说，坚持党性就是坚持人民性，坚持人民性也就是坚持党性，增强党性必须厚植为民情怀。

glossary.explanation: The set of political qualities, loyalty and discipline expected of Communist Party members. Official texts treat its cultivation as a core task of Party building.
