An official concept, prominent since the 18th Party Congress (2012), for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself and to address problems such as corruption.
Official formula adopted in 2021–22 affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of his thought.
Official requirement that Party members uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the Central Committee's authority.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.

glossary.literal: the big things of the country
glossary.explanation: A phrase used by Xi Jinping asking officials to keep the Party and state's most important interests and priorities in view in their work.

t: The practical power and lessons of the Party's strategy for governing Tibet in the new era
zh: 新时代党的治藏方略的实践伟力和经验启示
paras: Marking the 60th anniversary of the Tibet Autonomous Region, this commentary in Red Flag Manuscripts (2025, no. 16) takes up Xi Jinping's call of 20 August 2025 to implement fully the Party's strategy for governing Tibet in the new era. Wang Hongxiao argues that the strategy, formed after the 18th Party Congress (2012), has produced historic change in Tibet and yields lessons for achieving long-term stability and high-quality development there.

The article has three parts. The first traces the strategy's lineage from Mao Zedong's Tibet policy through Deng Xiaoping's stress on economic development to the 1990s formulas of "long-term construction of Tibet" and handling development and stability together. It then presents the strategy's content, summarised as the "ten musts" set out at the Seventh Central Symposium on Tibet Work. The second part reviews achievements in stability, economy, livelihoods, ethnic and religious work, culture, ecology and border consolidation. The third draws seven lessons.

In Wang's account, the strategy rests on the thesis that "to govern the country, one must govern the borders; to govern the borders, one must first stabilise Tibet", and on the four major tasks of stability, development, ecology and strengthening the borders. Wang cites figures: regional GDP of 276.5 billion yuan in 2024, 628,000 people lifted out of poverty, rural per capita disposable income of 21,578 yuan against 5,698 in 2012, and public cultural facilities said to cover 100% of localities. Wang describes religious freedom as fully protected and reports that the sense of security among residents is above 99%.

The lessons are: uphold Party leadership; put the people at the centre; balance development and security; pursue high-quality development; forge a strong sense of community of the Chinese nation; govern Tibet by law; and treat the whole country as one chessboard, combining central support with counterpart assistance. Wang also calls for guiding Tibetan Buddhism to adapt to socialist society and for promoting the common national language. Read the original if you want an official-line overview of Tibet policy, with the Party's own statistics and its framing of governance principles, as presented in a central Party journal in 2025.
quoteEn: Tibet is a frontier ethnic region, and it is necessary to further forge a strong sense of community of the Chinese nation and advance the building of that community.
quoteZh: 西藏是边疆民族地区，必须进一步铸牢中华民族共同体意识、推进中华民族共同体建设

glossary.pinyin: xīn shídài dǎng de zhì Zàng fānglüè
glossary.en: the Party's strategy for governing Tibet in the new era
glossary.explanation: The official framework for Tibet policy, consolidated at the Seventh Central Symposium on Tibet Work (2020) and summarised in ten "musts". It combines Party leadership, regional ethnic autonomy, stability, development, ecology and border security.

glossary.zh: 治国必治边、治边先稳藏
glossary.pinyin: zhì guó bì zhì biān, zhì biān xiān wěn Zàng
glossary.en: to govern the country, one must govern the borders; to govern the borders, one must first stabilise Tibet
glossary.explanation: A strategic formula associated with Xi Jinping that treats Tibet as the key to border security and thus to national governance.

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: forge a strong sense of community of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A policy goal prominent since 2017 that stresses shared national identity across all ethnic groups, pursued through education, common language and inter-ethnic exchange.
The official goal of shifting from fast growth to growth emphasising quality, innovation, ecology and welfare.

t: The Communist Party of China's external relations during the War of Resistance against Japan
zh: 抗战时期中国共产党的对外交往工作
paras: Li Zhongjie examines how the Communist Party of China conducted contacts with foreign countries and peoples during the War of Resistance against Japan (1937–1945). Li argues that this work, which the Party's own 1944 directive called "semi-independent diplomacy", introduced the Party and the anti-Japanese struggle to the world and promoted a world anti-fascist united front. In Li's account it marked the Party's first steps onto the international stage and laid a foundation for the diplomacy of the People's Republic.

The article is a historical narrative in three parts. The first traces how the Party opened a window to the outside world, from the reception office at Yan'an and the visits of Edgar Snow, Agnes Smedley, Norman Bethune and others to the US Army Observation Group of 1944. The second covers the push for an international anti-fascist united front, including the work of the Southern Bureau in Chongqing, the 1941 Yan'an conference of Eastern peoples and intelligence cooperation with the Soviet Union and the Allies. The third deals with China's rise to great-power status and the Party's role at the founding of the United Nations.

Li's central claim is that the Party combined internationalism with patriotism and independence with the pursuit of foreign support, under the line of "publicise abroad and win over". Li stresses the 1944 Directive on Diplomatic Work, which set a national standpoint, rejecting both xenophobia and deference to foreigners, and tied diplomacy to the united front. Among the evidence cited are the reception of over 7,000 guests between 1938 and 1941, the impact of Snow's Red Star Over China and the Party's warning to Moscow of the German attack in 1941. Li also recounts how Zhou Enlai and US pressure secured a Communist delegate, Dong Biwu, a place in China's delegation to the 1945 San Francisco conference.

Li concludes that the Party's wartime diplomacy broke the blockade around it, won international recognition and contributed to China's first entry into the ranks of the great powers since the modern era, including a permanent seat on the UN Security Council. Li reads the signing of the UN Charter with a Chinese brush as a symbol that the Chinese people's contribution to the anti-fascist war had been recognised. Read the original if you want a concise, officially oriented account of the Party's early foreign relations and the episodes the Party historiography emphasises.
quoteEn: This kind of contact was characterised as a form of \"semi-independent diplomacy\" and is an important part of the history of the Communist Party of China during the War of Resistance.
quoteZh: 这种交往被定性为一种“半独立性的外交”，是中国共产党抗战历史的一个重要组成部分

glossary.explanation: A description used in the Central Committee's August 1944 directive on diplomatic work. It referred to the Party's external contacts, conducted while it was not yet a national government.
A wartime guideline for external work: spreading the Party's views abroad and winning foreign sympathy and support.
A Party strategy of building alliances with other forces against a main enemy. Here it refers to the domestic and international anti-Japanese and anti-fascist alliances.

glossary.literal: Southern Bureau of the CPC Central Committee
glossary.explanation: The Party's secret organ stationed in Chongqing, the Nationalist wartime capital, led by Zhou Enlai, which handled contacts with foreign diplomats and journalists.

t: The Communist Party of China leads in forging and promoting the great spirit of resistance against Japanese aggression
zh: 中国共产党引领弘扬伟大抗战精神
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in September 2025, asks how the Communist Party of China shaped the great spirit of resistance against Japanese aggression. He and Xue argue that the Party was the mainstay of the nation-wide War of Resistance and, through its political programme, firm resolve and exemplary conduct, led the forging of that spirit.

The article follows the war from the September 18th Incident (1931) to the later stages of the conflict. It organises the Party's role under four headings: raising the banner of national salvation, mobilising the whole people, fighting on the front line, and upholding independence and unity.

In the authors' account, the Party was first to call for armed resistance and a united front, citing the August 1st Declaration, the December 9th Movement and the peaceful settlement of the Xi'an Incident. They say it put national interest above past enmity with the Kuomintang. They credit it with a line of all-out, protracted resistance and with heroes such as Yang Jingyu and Zuo Quan. They describe the victory at Pingxingguan, the Hundred Regiments Offensive and guerrilla warfare in the enemy's rear, and state that by the war's later stage Party-led forces fought about 60 per cent of Japanese troops and 95 per cent of puppet troops. They also say the Party combined alliance with struggle against Kuomintang anti-communist moves and sustained the base areas through the production campaign.

The authors conclude that the Party's independence, commitment to unity and sacrifice instilled an unshakeable belief in victory, which became a shared national resolve. They quote Xi Jinping on the Party's consistent stance for resistance, unity and progress. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-history scholarship in 2025 presents the Party's wartime leadership and the spirit of resistance.
quoteEn: With the interests of the nation and state as its highest value, the Communist Party of China, in practice, raised the patriotic tradition that 'everyone bears responsibility for the fate of the nation' into a shared will to resist foreign aggression and save the nation, inspiring all Chinese to stand united in the national crisis.
quoteZh: 中国共产党以民族国家利益为最高依归的价值取向，用实践将“天下兴亡，匹夫有责”的中华民族爱国传统升华为抵御外侮、救亡图存的共同意志，鼓舞了全体中华儿女众志成城、共赴国难。

glossary.explanation: The wartime alliance of the Communist Party, the Kuomintang and other groups against Japan, formed in the late 1930s after the Second Kuomintang–Communist cooperation. The Party presents it as a central strategy.

The December 1936 detention of Chiang Kai-shek by Zhang Xueliang and Yang Hucheng, which pressed for ending the civil war. Its peaceful settlement paved the way for renewed Kuomintang–Communist cooperation.
A large 1940 offensive by the Eighth Route Army against Japanese-held rail lines and positions in North China.

glossary.en: great spirit of resistance against Japanese aggression
glossary.explanation: A Party formulation for the patriotic, heroic and persevering qualities attributed to the Chinese people during the 1931–1945 war against Japan.

t: The Communist Party of China as the mainstay of the nation's war of resistance
zh: 中国共产党是全民族抗战的中流砥柱
paras: This short commentary, published in 2025 in the China Social Sciences Today, argues that the Communist Party of China was the "mainstay" (zhongliu dizhu) of the whole nation's War of Resistance against Japan. Wang describes the war as the longest, largest and costliest national liberation struggle in modern Chinese history, and the first to end in complete victory. In Wang's account, the Party stood on the front line and carried the nation's hope of survival.

The piece is organised under three headings: the Party as vanguard of resistance, the Party as guide of the war's direction, and the Party's sacrifices and contributions. It runs chronologically from the Mukden Incident of 1931 to the anti-Japanese bases of 1945, citing Party declarations, Mao Zedong's wartime writings and figures on enemy forces tied down and destroyed.

Wang's central claims are that the Party was first to issue calls for resistance, after the Nationalist government's "non-resistance" policy, and that it built the anti-Japanese national united front, from the 1935 August First Declaration to the second Nationalist–Communist cooperation of 1937. Wang adds that the Party proposed an international anti-fascist front and, through Mao's On Protracted War, supplied a strategy of protracted war and independent guerrilla warfare. After 1938, Wang says, the bases behind enemy lines became the main battlefield. The article cites the tying down of more than two thirds of Japanese forces in China and 1.714 million Japanese and puppet troops killed.

Wang concludes that the Party forged the great spirit of resistance and calls on the whole Party and people to carry it forward in advancing national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a compact example of the current official Party narrative of the Anti-Japanese War, with its key dates and figures.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China's anti-Japanese banner was always the most distinct, its attitude the most resolute, and its actions the most active.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的抗日旗帜始终是最鲜明的，抗日态度始终是最坚决的，抗日行动始终是最积极的

glossary.explanation: A Chinese idiom for a stabilising force that holds firm amid turbulence. In Party historiography it expresses the claim that the CPC was the decisive force in the War of Resistance.
The broad alliance of the Communist Party, the Nationalist Party and other groups against Japan, formally established in 1937 around the second Nationalist–Communist cooperation.
The official name for the Party's path to modernization, set out in the 2020s as distinct from Western models.

t: Five-year plans (guihua) as an important way for the Communist Party of China to govern the country
zh: “五年规划”：中国共产党治国理政的重要方式
paras: Following Xi Jinping's remarks in April 2025 that the scientific formulation and successive implementation of five-year plans is an important Party experience and a political advantage of socialism with Chinese characteristics, this commentary asks how that practice should be understood. Tang and Qian argue that the five-year plan (renamed "planning" in 2006) is a mature, institutionalised way for the Party to govern, which relays China's modernisation from one period to the next and embodies the strengths of the system.

The piece is a short newspaper commentary in three parts. It first sketches the history from the First Five-Year Plan (1953) to the 14th Five-Year Plan; it then lists three institutional advantages the plans display; finally it examines how the plans coordinate government, market and society. It draws mainly on Xi Jinping's statements and on examples such as the consultation for the 14th Five-Year Plan.

In the authors' periodisation, the first five plans built an independent and fairly complete industrial system, including the Third Front construction. After the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978), the plan came to cover social development and became more standardised, with mid-term evaluation and central–local coordination. Since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Xi has personally led the drafting groups and pushed for a unified planning system and a national development planning law. The three advantages they name are the Party's centralised and unified leadership, which they say avoids the mutual obstruction and policy reversals of Western multiparty systems; a people-first orientation, illustrated by seven symposiums and over a million online messages for the 14th plan; and the ability to concentrate resources on major undertakings. The plan is then presented as the expression of a proactive government, an effective market and a vibrant society: it gives the market a clear direction, remedies market and social failures, and channels public participation.

The authors conclude that scientifically formulating and continuously implementing five-year plans produced the "two miracles" of rapid economic growth and long-term social stability and a path of modernization with universal significance. They place this in the context of the coming 15th Five-Year Plan, stressing scientific, democratic and law-based decision-making, and building a high-standard socialist market economy and a unified national market. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars present the five-year plan as a governance institution ahead of the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: The five-year plan is a mode of governance that our Party has continually explored and brought to maturity in the practice of socialist modernization, and it concentrates the institutional advantages of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 五年规划是我们党在社会主义现代化建设实践中不断探索并成熟定型的治国理政方式，集中体现了中国特色社会主义制度优势。

glossary.explanation: The official description of China's economic system since the 1990s, combining public ownership's leading role with market allocation of resources.
The official name for the Party's theory, path and system since the reform era.
A programme from the mid-1960s to the 1970s that built industrial and defence facilities in China's interior for war preparedness.
A term in official discourse for a government that actively intervenes in development, together with an "effective market".

t: How to understand Party spirit
zh: 怎样理解党性
paras: This short commentary, published in Qiushi in 2025, asks what Party spirit (dangxing) is, how it should be understood, and why it matters. Zhang defines it as the Party's inherent essential attribute as embodied in each member: the Party's ideals, stance, purpose, discipline and work style made concrete in a member's thinking, speech and conduct. Citing Xi Jinping, Zhang argues that Party spirit is what determines what kind of Party member a person is, and that it must be forged throughout one's life.

The article moves in three steps. It first traces the concept from Engels and Lenin, who tied it to class standpoint, through Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and other earlier leaders, who stressed common nature, unity of action and discipline. It then explains why Party spirit matters today, setting out the international situation, the demands of long-term governance and the failings Zhang sees among some members and cadres. Finally it names three relationships to be handled in cultivating Party spirit.

Zhang lists the criteria of strong Party spirit: firm ideals and convictions, loyalty to the Party, a people-centred standpoint, honesty and integrity, and self-discipline. Zhang says that in the new era, with the world undergoing what the article calls changes unseen in a century and the country advancing Chinese modernization, the Party needs members of strong Party spirit. Failings such as superstition, vanity projects, putting self above the organisation and corruption are traced mainly to internal causes, namely insufficient self-cultivation, rather than to weak supervision or the social environment alone. The three relationships are these. Party spirit and the people's character are said to be unified, so upholding one means upholding the other. Public and private interest is the "ruler" of Party spirit, and legitimate personal interests are acknowledged but distinguished from selfishness. Individuality must be subordinated to Party spirit, with Mao's distinction between creative and destructive individuality used to show that creative individuality is compatible with it.

Zhang concludes that Party spirit is not innate and is never secured once and for all, but needs rigorous inner-Party political life and tests in hardship. The text offers the example of a village Party secretary who died saving villagers in the Beijing floods of July 2025. It links the argument to full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and to the Party's long-term ruling position. Read the original if you want a concise, official Qiushi statement of how Party spirit is currently defined and what leading cadres are expected to do about it.
quoteEn: Party spirit, in the final analysis, is a question of standpoint.
quoteZh: 党性说到底就是立场问题。

glossary.explanation: The qualities of loyalty, discipline, ideological commitment and class standpoint expected of a Communist Party member. The term goes back to Lenin's idea of partiinost' and is a staple of Party-building discourse.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Official formula, prominent since the 18th Party Congress (2012), for strict discipline, anti-corruption work and institutional Party-building.
The official name for China's path of modernization, which Party documents present as distinct from Western models.

t: Patriotic fervour and fighting spirit in New Fourth Army literature
zh: 新四军文学中的爱国热情与战斗精神
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 3 September 2025
paras: Huang Xiaojuan, in a short newspaper essay, asks what patriotic and martial spirit is carried by the literature of the New Fourth Army, a Communist-led anti-Japanese force in central China. The author argues that this literature is an inseparable part of War of Resistance literature. It joins feelings of attachment to homeland with a determination to fight to the end for national independence.

The essay first defines New Fourth Army literature as one strand of the army's wider artistic activity, which also included music, art, drama and singing. Huang identifies three sources: works by writer-soldiers such as Qiu Dongping, Wu Qiang, Nie Gannu and Chen Yi; works from occupied and Nationalist-held areas that depict the army; and memoirs written after the army's designation was abolished in 1947. It then turns to geographical perception and to poetry.

Huang first reads Chen Yi's 1939 reportage Spring in Jiangnan during the War of Resistance. Soldiers who at first cursed the Maoshan rainy season later see the landscape transformed, which the author takes as a sign of changing circumstances and of the trust between army and people. Huang then argues that a "complex of attachment to the land" fuelled resistance, and reads Chen Yi's classical poems and the poet Lu Mang's verse in this light. Wu Qiang's account of the actress Li Ming, killed by Japanese fire, is paired with Chen Yi's poem on her dying words, "revolution sheds blood, not tears".

Huang concludes that the New Fourth Army's sacrifice and its literature, which fuses love of home with fighting spirit, make it an outstanding representative of red culture. The unyielding drive for national independence is presented as an important component of revolutionary and red culture. Read the original if you want a brief overview of how Chinese scholars frame New Fourth Army writing within red culture and War of Resistance literature.
quoteEn: The spirit of fighting resolutely to the end for national independence is an important element of New Fourth Army literature, and also an important component of revolutionary culture and red culture.
quoteZh: 义无反顾为民族独立战斗到底的精神是新四军文学蕴含的重要内涵，也是革命文化与红色文化的重要组成部分。

glossary.explanation: A term for the cultural heritage of the Chinese Communist revolution, including its literature, songs, sites and the spirit attributed to them. It is widely used in official discourse on history and patriotic education.

A Communist-led force formed in October 1937 from guerrilla units in southern China, nominally within the Nationalist army. It fought the Japanese in central China, and its designation was abolished in 1947.

t: Developing new forms of employment requires stronger legal safeguards
zh: 发展新就业形态须强化法治保障
authors: Office of the Social and Legal Affairs Committee of the National Committee of the CPPCC
paras: The article, a policy commentary reprinted from Qiushi, asks how China should support and regulate platform-based \"new forms of employment\" such as food-delivery riders, couriers, ride-hailing drivers and online streamers. Its answer is that the central problem is institutional: rules have lagged behind practice, so the authors call for law-based means to support and regulate this work and so promote high-quality development.

The text has three parts. It first presents new-form workers as an important force for development. It then sets out the main problems that need attention, and it closes with four sets of legal and institutional measures. It draws on Xi Jinping's remarks praising these workers as \"hardworking little bees\", on survey figures and on a list of recent State Council and ministerial policy documents.

The authors cite the 2023 national survey of the workforce, which counted about 402 million workers, of whom 84 million (21 per cent) are in new forms of employment, mostly under 35. They credit this work with expanding job options and incomes, including for low-income and rural migrant workers. They then identify three problems: algorithmic management by platforms with monopoly power and information advantages, weak rights protection (long hours, and pension and medical insurance coverage of only about 50 per cent for flexible workers), and labour, labour-contract, employment-promotion and dispute-mediation laws that predate the digital economy. They note that over 80,000 first-instance civil cases involving new forms of employment were concluded in 2024.

The authors call for four measures. First, innovative regulation: platform duties on working hours and minimum pay, more transparent and fair algorithms, and coordinated enforcement. Second, rights protection through differentiated, category-specific policies, wider occupational injury insurance after the pilots begun in 2022, and legal aid. Third, care and services through Party building, training, trade-union consultation and participation in grassroots governance. Fourth, revision of the main labour laws, when conditions are ripe, to define the nature and criteria of new-form labour relations in national legislation. Read the original if you want an official Party-journal statement of how the Chinese state frames platform labour, with its figures and its proposed legislative agenda.
quoteEn: The problems in the development of new forms of employment lie fundamentally in institution-building lagging behind practice.
quoteZh: 新就业形态发展中的问题，根本上在于制度建设滞后于实践。

glossary.explanation: Official term for work organised through internet platforms, such as delivery, ride-hailing and livestream marketing. It is characterised by flexible labour relations and often unclear employment status.
A Party-state slogan, prominent since 2017, that stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over pure growth speed.
Work to establish and strengthen Party organisations and their influence, here extended to platform-economy workers and enterprises.
The Chinese Communist Party Central Committee's flagship theoretical journal, published twice a month.

t: Qiushi commentator: Dealing more effectively with prominent problems of formalism
zh: 《求是》杂志评论员：更加有效整治形式主义突出问题
paras: This commentary by a Qiushi commentator (Qiushi, 2025 no. 17) takes up the Party's campaign against formalism and for easing burdens on grassroots officials. It argues that formalism is alien to the Party's nature and fine style of work and obstructs the implementation of Central Committee decisions. In the commentary's account, removing it is necessary to keep policy delivery open and the Party close to the people.

The text opens with the Regulations on Rectifying Formalism and Reducing Burdens on the Grassroots, issued in full in August 2025 by the General Offices of the Party Central Committee and the State Council. The commentary calls them the first Party regulation on grassroots burden reduction. It then reviews results, lists persistent forms of formalism, analyses their causes and sets out what must be done.

The commentary says formalism is stubborn, recurrent and prone to mutation, and gives examples: training for its own sake, fact-finding tours with rehearsed interviews, notices and reports standing in for real work, and new formalism produced by burden-reduction itself, such as demands to backfill three years of paperwork. It traces the causes to a distorted view of performance, lack of responsibility, insufficient ability among some cadres, and assessment and supervision systems that push targets downward and make grassroots officials fear blame.

The author calls for treating symptoms and root causes together, targeting the grassroots' pain points, and stressing that reducing burdens does not mean reducing responsibility. Proposals include lowering the weight of reports and ledgers in assessments, favouring real results and public evaluation, and building a workable system for tolerating and correcting errors. Persistent effort and a correct view of performance are also urged. Read the original if you want an official statement of how the Party frames formalism and the 2025 grassroots burden-reduction rules.
quoteEn: It must be made clear that reducing burdens does not mean reducing responsibility or the readiness to take on tasks.
quoteZh: 需要明确的是，减负不是减责任、减担当。

glossary.explanation: In Party discourse, a style of work that stresses outward appearances, paperwork and procedure over practical results. It is paired with bureaucratism as a target of Party conduct campaigns.

glossary.literal: lighten the load for the grassroots
glossary.explanation: A policy aimed at cutting excessive meetings, paperwork, assessments and tasks imposed on township, village and community-level officials.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Improving the study system of the theoretical study groups of Party committees
zh: 完善理论学习中心组学习制度
paras: This short commentary, published in Study Times on 29 August 2025, asks how the study system of the theoretical study groups (中心组) of Party committees and Party leadership groups can be improved. Dou argues that the system is an important means of strengthening the Party itself and of keeping strategic clarity. The decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) called for its improvement, and Dou holds that what matters now is implementation.

The article opens with a brief history, from the study system and the General Study Committee set up in Yan'an, through reform and opening up, to the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It then sets out four areas of work, drawing repeatedly on the Rules on the study groups: collective study and discussion, annual study plans, the link between study and investigation, and the responsibility of the leadership.

Dou's central claim is that the system's value lies in its application, so it needs operable rules and measurable results. Collective discussion should be the main form of study, with rules on how often groups meet and members speak, and members should read original works. Annual plans should follow central tasks and give a "first item" slot to Xi Jinping's latest important speeches and instructions. Each member should carry out at least one thematic investigation a year and write a high-quality report, as a guard against formalism and bureaucratism.

Dou concludes that Party secretaries, as the first persons responsible, should treat the system as a political duty. They should set an example and build a system of reporting on study and of assessment, linked to Party-building evaluation. The aim is model learning-oriented organs. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official institutional requirements for leading cadres' theoretical study in the current period.
quoteEn: The life of a system lies in its implementation.
quoteZh: 制度的生命在于落实

glossary.explanation: Study bodies in Party committees and Party leadership groups, made up of leading members and heads of departments, which meet to study Party theory and policy collectively.
A practice of placing study of Xi Jinping's latest speeches and instructions first on the agenda of meetings.
The top leader of a unit, such as the Party secretary, who bears primary responsibility for its work.

glossary.pinyin: dǎng de èrshí jiè sān zhōngquánhuì
glossary.en: Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
glossary.explanation: The plenary session of July 2024 that adopted a decision on further deepening reform comprehensively.

t: Advancing the deep integration of Party building and business in free trade port parks
zh: 推进自贸港园区党建与业务深度融合
paras: This commentary, published in Study Times on 27 August 2025, asks how Party building and business operations can be integrated in the industrial parks of the Hainan Free Trade Port. Liu and Wang argue that three principles resolve the problem of Party work and business running as "two skins": guidance by belief, linkage of interests and integration of sentiment. They hold that the three reinforce one another and supply lasting momentum for high-quality development.

The piece is organised in three sections, one per principle. Each pairs a short statement of rationale with examples of mechanisms said to be in use in the parks, and the authors present these as existing practice rather than proposals.

On belief, the authors say Party organisations in the parks put political building first and make studying the Party's theory a priority. Tools include a "first agenda item" study system, "Party member shock teams" and a three-tier organisational structure, so that an "organisation chain" drives the industry, talent and innovation chains. On interests, citing Marx on the link between ideas and interests, they describe Party-run channels for firms' demands, such as service officers, government–business forums and Party-member responsibility zones, plus Party-guided benefit-sharing among government, enterprises and research bodies. On sentiment, they describe a 24-hour service hotline, pairing of Party members with foreign and skilled staff, cultural events and the parks' response to Typhoon Yagi ("Moji"), which they say turned emotional identification into practical capacity.

The authors conclude that belief supplies direction, interests supply drive and sentiment supplies cohesion, so that Party leadership is built into enterprise services throughout. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party media describe grassroots Party-building practice in Hainan's free trade port parks.
quoteEn: Guidance by belief provides fundamental direction for business, the linkage of interests is the basic driver of practical work, and the integration of sentiment is the deep adhesive that builds consensus.
quoteZh: 信仰引领为业务航向提供根本指引，利益联结是驱动实干的基本动能，情感融合是凝聚共识的深层黏合剂

glossary.explanation: A official economic goal since 2017 that prioritises quality, innovation and efficiency over speed of growth.
The Communist Party's work of strengthening its organisations, discipline, ideology and membership, here applied inside business parks.
A special economic zone on Hainan island, with policy plans announced by the central government in 2018 and 2020, that has liberalised trade and investment rules.
A Party system under which meetings begin by studying the latest speeches and instructions of Xi Jinping.

t: "Demeanour: People and events in the Party's work-style building" published
st: Xinhua notice of a new book from the Party History and Literature Research Institute
zh: 《风范——党的作风建设中的人与事》出版发行
paras: This is a short Xinhua news notice, dated 26 August 2025, announcing the publication of a book titled Fengfan (roughly "Demeanour"): People and Events in the Party's Work-Style Building. The notice reports that the Central Institute of Party History and Literature compiled the volume to put into practice the spirit of the Central Committee's eight-point regulation, promote the Party's glorious traditions and fine work style, and use Party history as a guide to the present.

According to the notice, the book was issued by the CPC History Press. It collects 83 articles totalling 170,000 characters, and it tells short stories to convey larger principles. The stories feature veteran revolutionaries, heroes and model figures.

The notice says these stories illustrate several fine habits: linking theory with practice, staying close to the masses, criticism and self-criticism, hard work and plain living, and seeking truth and being pragmatic. It presents the book's central message as the view that the Party's work style is the Party's image, that it bears on whether the people support the Party, and that it determines the success or failure of the Party's and the country's cause.

The notice concludes that the book will help Party members, cadres and the public study the history of work-style building. It says the book should help carry good traditions into the new journey and promote good work style in the new era. It adds that new results in work-style building will give strong backing to the advance of Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a brief example of how official media present Party-history publications and the way they link work-style building to current Party goals.
quoteEn: The book collects 83 articles, 170,000 characters, using small stories to tell big truths.
quoteZh: 该书收录文章83篇,17万字,用小故事讲述大道理
keywords: Central Institute of Party History and Literature

t: The Communist Party of China as the mainstay of the War of Resistance against Japan
zh: 中国共产党是抗日战争的中流砥柱
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily shortly before the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japan, asks what role the Communist Party of China played in that war. Liu Zhipeng argues that through political leadership, strategic planning, exemplary military action and moral integrity, the Party played an irreplaceable part and was the "mainstay" (zhongliu dizhu) of the war.

The article moves through five areas: the Party's early call for resistance and the anti-Japanese national united front; its line of total resistance and the protracted-war strategy; the opening of the battlefield behind enemy lines; the spirit of hard struggle; and the sacrifice and national integrity of Party members. Evidence includes the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army, the 1935 August First Declaration, the Wayaobao meeting, the Xi'an Incident, the reorganisation of the Red Army into the Eighth Route Army and New Fourth Army, and Mao Zedong's 1938 On Protracted War.

Liu contrasts the Party's people's war, which relied on mobilising the masses, setting up democratic governments and reducing rent and interest behind enemy lines, with what the article calls the Nationalist Party's one-sided resistance that relied on government and army. Liu credits guerrilla tactics and the behind-the-lines front with forcing Japan to fight on two fronts, and says that this front became the main battlefield in the stage of strategic stalemate. Liu also cites Yan'an's production campaign and the deaths of commanders such as Zuo Quan and Yang Jingyu as proof of the Party's spirit.

Liu concludes that the Chinese people and history chose the Party through this war, and that grasping this conclusion matters today for promoting the resistance spirit, uniting the nation and achieving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official Party narrative of the anti-Japanese war's leading role is currently presented in the mainstream press.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China initiated and upheld the anti-Japanese national united front, formulated and carried out the line of total resistance and the protracted-war strategy, opened up and firmly led the battlefield behind enemy lines, and most steadfastly promoted and practised the great spirit of resistance; the Party was the mainstay of the War of Resistance against Japan.
quoteZh: 中国共产党是抗日民族统一战线的发起者和维护者，是全面抗战路线和持久战战略的制定者与执行者，是敌后战场的主要开辟者和坚强领导者，是伟大抗战精神最坚定的弘扬者和践行者，中国共产党是抗日战争的中流砥柱。

glossary.literal: a rock standing in the midstream
glossary.explanation: An idiom for a steadfast force that holds firm in a crisis. In Party historiography it is used to describe the CPC's role in the War of Resistance against Japan.
The broad alliance of the CPC, the Nationalist Party and other forces against Japanese invasion, formed in the mid-to-late 1930s and centred on Nationalist–Communist cooperation after 1937.
Mao Zedong's 1938 strategy, set out in On Protracted War, which held that China would win a long war in three stages: strategic defence, stalemate and counter-offensive.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal of the Party since the 2010s, referring to restoring China's national strength and international standing.

t: Writing a new chapter for our times in Party conduct building on the new journey
zh: 书写好新征程党的作风建设的时代新篇
paras: Writing in 2025, Sun Mingzeng takes up the question of why improving the Party's conduct (zuofeng) remains essential and how it should be advanced on the "new journey". The article is tied to the study and education campaign on thoroughly implementing the central Eight-point Regulation, which a Politburo meeting in April 2025 and Xi Jinping's inspection in Henan in May called for. Sun argues that conduct-building is a lasting theme of Party building and a safeguard for Chinese modernization.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out why conduct matters to a Marxist party, drawing on theoretical, historical and practical logics. The second reviews achievements since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third proposes four or five lines of work for the period spanning the end of the 14th Five-Year Plan and the drafting of the 15th.

Sun's central claim is that conduct expresses a party's nature, purpose, programme and line, so neglecting it risks losing popular support and power. The article traces this through the Party's history, from wartime traditions and rectification campaigns to reform-era campaigns. It credits the post-2012 period with deeper understanding of conduct as a question of Party spirit and of the Party's relationship with the people, a better political ecology, a fuller system of Party regulations, and a purer Party style. For the future, Sun calls for stronger ideological and political foundations through study. Other measures are targeted rectification combined with the promotion of good practice, and leading cadres setting an example. Sun also urges treating unhealthy work styles and corruption together, using big data to find leads, and building a closed loop of investigation, governance, supervision and education.

Sun concludes that conduct-building has no end point and calls for "genuine and strict, long-term and strict" management, with responsibility assigned at every level of Party organisation. The aim, in the article's terms, is to ensure the Party never changes in nature, colour or flavour and to secure Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a representative statement of the official 2025 framing of the Eight-point Regulation campaign and the policy measures it emphasises.
quoteEn: Conduct building is not an expedient or a one-off measure; it has no final note.
quoteZh: 作风建设，不是权宜之计、一时之举，没有休止符。

glossary.explanation: A set of rules adopted by the Politburo in December 2012 to curb extravagance, bureaucracy and formalism among officials. It has since served as a benchmark for Party discipline campaigns.
The official description of China's development path, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

t: Strengthening the Party's overall leadership over urban work
zh: 加强党对城市工作的全面领导
paras: Taking its cue from the recent Central Urban Work Conference, which stated that building modern people's cities requires stronger Party leadership over urban work, this commentary argues that the Party's overall leadership is the fundamental guarantee of good urban work. Fu Gaosheng draws on Xi Jinping's statements on urban work to set out the theoretical and practical significance of this principle.

The piece, published in Guangming Daily on 26 August 2025, has three parts. It first reviews how Party leadership has served urban work since 1949, then explains how leadership should be exercised, and finally turns to the capabilities required of Party members and cadres.

Fu says Party leadership gives urban work its direction, notably through the "people's city" concept advanced since the 18th Party Congress (2012), its planning (five-year plans and five central urban work conferences) and its organisational base, including four-tier Party organisations from street to building. Leadership, Fu argues, must be comprehensive, systematic and holistic: it should cover the whole life cycle of a city, treat urban work as a subsystem linked to rural work and to economic, political, cultural, social and ecological construction, and build a governance community of Party committees, government, market and residents in line with whole-process people's democracy.

Fu calls on cadres to study Xi's urban-work remarks, to adopt a correct view of performance that makes benefiting the people the greatest achievement rather than focusing only on GDP or large projects, and to improve their work style with patience and consistent plans across changes of leadership. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party commentary links urban governance to Party leadership.
quoteEn: Party leadership is comprehensive, systematic and holistic.
quoteZh: 党的领导是全面的、系统的、整体的。

glossary.explanation: An urban-development concept associated with Xi Jinping, who in 2019 said that cities are built by the people and for the people. It is used to stress people-centred planning and governance.
An official concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2019. It describes the Chinese political system as one in which citizens take part in every stage of decision-making, not only in elections.
A high-level Party and state meeting that sets national policy on urban development. The article says five have been held, the latest in 2025.

t: Strengthening the conscious commitment of Party and government organs to leading by example in living a frugal life
zh: 增强党政机关带头过紧日子的自觉性
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 26 August 2025, responds to the revised Regulations on Practising Economy and Opposing Waste in Party and Government Organs, recently issued by the CPC Central Committee and the State Council. Ruan Dongbiao argues that the revision tightens the institutional bolts on Party and government organs' pledge to "live a tight life", and that officials must take up frugality as a matter of conscious commitment.

The piece moves from cultural tradition to Party history, then to current practice. It cites classical sayings on thrift, recalls the Jinggangshan and Yan'an periods and figures such as Jiao Yulu and Gu Wenchang, and then turns to the revised rules on funding, travel, official receptions, vehicles, meetings, office space and resource saving.

Ruan contends that thrift is a Party tradition and follows from the Party's purpose: the Party and government live frugally so that ordinary people can live well. Savings are said to free funds for innovation, rural revitalisation, ecology, education and health, and to support high-quality development; examples are Daliangshan in Sichuan and Dingxi in Gansu, where 15 rural water projects reportedly reached 1.22 million people. The author also credits an anti-waste rules system with curbing "corruption on wheels" and wasteful banqueting, and describes layered supervision and big-data platforms, including a national asset-sharing platform that, according to the article, saved over 40 million yuan.

Ruan concludes that thrift must be built into the work style of Party and government organs through stricter oversight and risk control, and that the revision shows Party conduct-building is always "on the road". Party members and officials are urged to be self-disciplined and to set an example in hardship. Read the original if you want a brief example of official Party-media framing of the 2025 anti-waste regulations and the central rules on conduct.
quoteEn: The Party and government lead in living a tight life so that ordinary people can live good lives; this is determined by the Party's purpose and nature.
quoteZh: 党和政府带头过紧日子，目的是让老百姓过好日子，这是我们党的宗旨和性质所决定的。

glossary.literal: take the lead in living tight days
glossary.explanation: A slogan calling on Party and government bodies to cut spending and practise frugality, so that public funds go to priority and livelihood areas.
An official economic goal since 2017 that stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.

t: The Communist Party of China's role as the mainstay was the key to victory in the Chinese people's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression
zh: 中国共产党的中流砥柱作用是中国人民抗日战争胜利的关键
paras: Lu Yi takes up Xi Jinping's formulation that the Communist Party's role as the mainstay (zhongliu dizhu) was the key to victory in the War of Resistance against Japan. The article, a commentary published in the People's Daily in August 2025, argues that this is a scientific conclusion drawn from a full review of the 14-year war and a settled historical verdict. Lu presents the victory as the first complete victory over foreign invasion in modern Chinese history and a turning point towards the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article is organised around four areas in which the Party is said to have played an irreplaceable role: political guidance through the anti-Japanese national united front, social mobilisation through the total-resistance line, strategic guidance in military affairs, and Party building. It draws on Mao Zedong's wartime writings, Party documents from 1935 to 1945, and recent remarks by Xi. It also cites observers outside the Party: Liang Shuming, Chen Jiageng, a Nationalist propagandist, the US Army Observation Group in Yan'an and Japanese military histories.

Lu argues that the Party first proposed, then promoted and finally defended the united front, from the 1935 August 1st Declaration through the Xi'an Incident to the formal Nationalist–Communist cooperation of 1937. The Party is said to have kept the front intact through three anti-Communist upsurges by pursuing both unity and struggle. Lu contrasts the Party's line of mobilising the whole people with the Nationalists' government- and army-centred line, and credits the Party's guerrilla strategy, set out in On Protracted War, with moving the enemy-rear battlefield to the centre of the war. Party building, in Lu's account, supplied the capacity for this through Mao Zedong Thought, the Yan'an Rectification, a consolidated leadership and the Party's style of work, which Lu sums up in the 'three magic weapons' of united front, armed struggle and Party building.

Lu concludes that the Party that saved the nation in wartime is also the core of leadership for national rejuvenation today. The author calls for firmly upholding the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, studying Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and applying the Party's historical experience and the spirit of resistance. Lu also urges the Party's self-reform and a new great project of Party building. Read the original if you want a concise example of the official People's Daily account of the Party's wartime leadership, and of how that history is tied to current Party-building themes.
quoteEn: History fully proves that without the Communist Party of China there would have been no anti-Japanese national united front, without the united front there would have been no nationwide resistance, and the Party was the well-deserved mainstay and political leadership core of the War of Resistance.
quoteZh: 历史充分证明，没有中国共产党就没有抗日民族统一战线，没有抗日民族统一战线就没有全民族抗战，中国共产党是抗日战争当之无愧的中流砥柱和政治领导核心。

glossary.explanation: An idiom for a steadfast force that holds firm amid turbulence. Xi Jinping uses it to describe the Party's role in the War of Resistance.
The broad coalition of parties, armies and social groups, centred on Nationalist–Communist cooperation, formed against Japan in 1937.
A Party formula, adopted in 2021–22, that affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–18.
The Party-wide rectification campaign of 1942–45, aimed at dogmatism and at securing Mao Zedong's ideological leadership.
An official term for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself, a major theme since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

t: Carrying forward the great founding spirit of the Party to speed up building a strong agricultural country
zh: 弘扬伟大建党精神 加快建设农业强国
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today on 21 August 2025, asks how the great founding spirit of the Party can inform the drive to build a strong agricultural country. Liu argues that carrying forward this spirit has real practical significance for that goal and for building a modern socialist country, on the premise that a strong country first needs strong agriculture.

The piece takes the four components of the founding spirit in turn: upholding truth and ideals; staying true to the original aspiration and mission; fearing no sacrifice and fighting bravely; and being loyal to the Party and faithful to the people. Each section sketches the Party's historical record on that theme, then links it to the present task.

In Liu's account, each component answers a specific need. Upholding truth and ideals calls for using the Marxist stance, viewpoint and method, together with Xi Jinping's statements on agriculture, rural areas and farmers, to find a Chinese path of agricultural and rural modernization suited to a large country of small farms. The original aspiration and mission turns the Central Committee's two-step plan into responsibility: basic agricultural modernization by 2035 and a strong agricultural country by mid-century. Liu names weak agricultural foundations, low efficiency, resource constraints, weak competitiveness and the urban–rural income gap as the difficulties that require struggle.

Liu concludes that loyalty to the Party and service to the people keep the effort on course. The author calls for raising farmers' incomes, treating food security as a matter of national importance, advancing rural revitalization, and achieving self-reliance in agricultural science and technology. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-building discourse is tied to agricultural policy in 2025.
quoteEn: For the nation to be rejuvenated, the countryside must first be revitalized.
quoteZh: 民族要复兴，乡村必先振兴。

glossary.en: great founding spirit of the Party
glossary.explanation: A formula set out by Xi Jinping in 2021 for the Party's centenary. It sums up the Party's founding values as upholding truth and ideals, staying true to its original aspiration, fearing no sacrifice, and being loyal to the Party and the people.
A standard shorthand in Chinese policy for agriculture, the countryside and farmers, treated as a single policy field.
A national strategy announced in 2017 to promote the comprehensive development of rural industry, ecology, culture, governance and living standards.
A policy goal of building a country with strong agricultural supply, technology, equipment, industry and competitiveness. Official plans set it for the middle of the twenty-first century.

t: Bringing the Party's leadership advantages into play to promote scientific and technological innovation vigorously
zh: 发挥党的领导优势 大力推进科技创新
paras: This commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today on 21 August 2025, argues that the Communist Party's overall leadership is the precondition for high-level scientific and technological self-reliance and for building China into a leading science and technology power. Wei Rong places this in a world of accelerating great changes, in which international competition increasingly centres on high technology. The article cites the 20th Party Congress (2022) goal of becoming a science and technology power by 2035.

The piece first reviews the Party's science policy from the founding of the People's Republic to the present, then explains why innovation matters to the Party's mission, and finally sets out four ways to use the Party's leadership advantages.

In Wei's account, the Party has adjusted its science policy to each period's needs: the 1956 call to "march on science", the 1978 formula that science and technology are productive forces, the 1985 reform decision, the strategy of invigorating the country through science and education, and the innovation-driven development strategy of the new era. Wei argues that innovation serves the Party's founding mission and is a necessary condition for Chinese modernization. It also strengthens national security, which requires a new type of whole-nation system and solutions to "chokepoint" problems. The four proposals are centralised Party leadership with full-chain planning and stronger basic research, integrated education, science and talent under the principle that the Party manages talent, deeper reform that makes enterprises the main innovators, and self-reliance combined with open international cooperation.

Wei concludes that China's own innovation path depends on turning the Party's political and institutional advantages into driving force for innovation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars link Party leadership to the science and technology agenda.
quoteEn: The leadership of the Communist Party of China is the greatest strength of the socialist system with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的领导是中国特色社会主义制度的最大优势。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's development path, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models of modernisation.
An official term for mobilising state, market and social resources under Party leadership to achieve major scientific and technological goals.

glossary.en: strategy of invigorating the country through science and education
glossary.explanation: A national strategy announced at the 1995 national science and technology conference. It puts science and education at the centre of economic and social development.
A Party principle that the Party leads talent selection, training and deployment through its organisation departments.

t: Grasping in depth that problems of work style are essentially problems of Party spirit
zh: 深刻把握作风问题本质上是党性问题
paras: This commentary, published in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) in 2025, takes up Xi Jinping's statement that problems of work style are essentially problems of Party spirit. Xu Mei argues that whether Communists can resolve style problems is a key measure of their faith in Marxism, their belief in socialism and communism, and their loyalty to the Party and the people. The author calls on Party members and cadres to link self-cultivation of Party spirit with style building, as a way of consolidating the results of the study and education campaign on the Central Committee's eight-point regulation.

The article has three parts. The first sets out what it means to say that style is a matter of Party spirit. The second reviews the Party's history of style building, from its founding through the Gutian Conference (1929), the Yan'an rectification, the 1950s campaigns, the post-1978 Party rectification and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third turns to practical requirements for the new journey.

Xu's central claim is that Party spirit is internal and style is its outward expression: wavering belief, a lost sense of purpose or discarded Party spirit will inevitably show up in conduct. The author names the distinction between public and private interest as the "fundamental yardstick" of Party spirit, and traces formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance to distorted worldviews, ideals and views of power. For this reason, Xu argues, correcting style cannot treat each incident in isolation; it must look through style to Party spirit and solve the underlying problem. The historical survey is used to show that the Party has consistently treated Party spirit as the root of style building, citing documents such as the 1941 decision on strengthening Party spirit and Liu Shaoqi's writings.

For practice, Xu proposes three measures: firm ideals and convictions, sustained through regular ideological self-checks; serious intra-Party political life, including democratic life meetings, criticism and self-criticism and the "three meetings and one lesson"; and a spirit of the Party's self-reform, with zero tolerance for breaches of the eight-point regulation and use of the "four forms" of discipline. The aim, the author says, is to provide a strong style guarantee for building a strong country and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want an example of how official Party-building commentary links ideology, discipline and the Party's own history in the campaign on work style.
quoteEn: Party spirit is internalised in the heart; work style is externalised in conduct.
quoteZh: 党性内化于心，作风外化于行。

glossary.explanation: The qualities of principle, loyalty and ideological commitment expected of a Communist Party member. In Party discourse it is the standard against which members' conduct is judged.
The Party's campaigns to improve the conduct and working methods of members and cadres, aimed at problems such as formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance.
Rules adopted by the Politburo in December 2012 to curb extravagance, bureaucratic practices and formalism among officials, covering matters such as meetings, travel and official hospitality.
An official concept for the Party's claimed capacity to examine and correct itself without external pressure.
A graded approach to discipline in which minor problems are handled by criticism and talks, and only serious or criminal violations lead to heavier sanctions or prosecution.
The official name for the Party's development path and goal, presented as distinct from Western models.

t: The Communist Party of China and the nationwide War of Resistance through the eyes of Western eyewitnesses
zh: 西方亲历者视域下的中国共产党与全民族抗战
paras: Zhang Deming asks how Western journalists, diplomats, officers and doctors who visited the anti-Japanese base areas under Communist leadership described the Communist Party of China (CPC) after the nationwide War of Resistance began in 1937. The short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in August 2025, argues that these outside observers, through their own accounts, confirm the Party's role as the "mainstay" (zhongliu dizhu) of the nationwide resistance.

Zhang organises the material under three headings: the line of all-out resistance, the consolidation of the Anti-Japanese National United Front, and guerrilla warfare behind enemy lines. The witnesses quoted include Edgar Snow's contemporaries and others such as Agnes Smedley, Theodore White, Evans Carlson, John S. Service, Israel Epstein, Rewi Alley-era visitors like Anna Louise Strong, the Austrian doctor Jakob Rosenfeld, and the German journalist Hans Shippe. Their statements are set beside passages from Mao Zedong, Peng Dehuai and Party documents such as the 1937 Luochuan Conference decisions.

Zhang's central move is to read these testimonies as evidence for the Party's own account. On the all-out resistance line, observers described mass mobilisation, village self-defence units and close army–people ties, in contrast with what Zhang calls the Kuomintang's one-sided reliance on government and army. On the united front, they noted the Party's persuasion of other forces, the "three-thirds" system of government and moderate rent reduction that protected landlords' interests. On guerrilla warfare, they recorded tactics such as tunnel and mine warfare, the role of militias, and the fact that Communist-led forces pinned down most Japanese and puppet troops, which Zhang says rebuts Kuomintang charges that Communist forces "roamed but did not fight".

Zhang concludes that the Western eyewitnesses saw the Party's political leadership and strategy at first hand and that their writings helped present a positive international image of the CPC. Some observers, such as Epstein, expected the Party to become China's dominant force. Zhang treats the Party's account of the Southern Anhui Incident of 1941 and of Kuomintang friction as settled, relying on the quoted witnesses as external confirmation. Read the original if you want a compact sampler of Western wartime testimony on the CPC as it is used in current official Party-history narrative.
quoteEn: Through observing the combat practice of the Eighth Route Army and the New Fourth Army, Western eyewitnesses came to see that the strong support of the broad masses in battle, which produced a true unity of army and people, was a powerful guarantee of the Party's growth, again confirming the correctness of the all-out resistance line.
quoteZh: 西方亲历者通过观察八路军、新四军的作战实践认识到，在作战中广大群众大力支持，真正实现了军民一体，是中国共产党得以发展壮大的有力保障，再次印证了全面抗战路线的正确性。

glossary.explanation: A standard Party-history description of the CPC's role in the War of Resistance, evoking a rock that stands firm against the current.
The broad alliance, centred on Kuomintang–Communist cooperation, formed after 1937 to resist Japan and joined by other parties, groups and overseas Chinese.
A system of base-area government in which Communists, non-Party progressives and middle-of-the-road figures each held about one third of seats.

t: Inheriting and promoting the spirit of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army
zh: 传承与弘扬东北抗联精神
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in the year of the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance (2025), Li Shujuan, a professor at Harbin Normal University, takes up the history and meaning of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army (the Northeast Anti-Japanese Allied Forces). Li argues that, under Communist Party leadership, its fourteen years of struggle from 1931 to 1945 produced a distinctive spirit. In Li's account this spirit embodies the wider spirit of the War of Resistance and forms an important part of the Chinese Communists' spiritual lineage.

The short commentary has three parts. It first recounts the army's hardships: the Japanese military build-up, the forced "collective hamlets", blockades, hunger, clothing shortages and extreme cold. It then assesses the army's historical standing, and finally turns to the moral qualities of individual commanders and fighters. Li draws on Japanese and Soviet sources, letters and reports by commanders such as Zhou Baozhong and Feng Zhongyun, and recollections of veterans.

Li's central claim is that the Northeast was the starting point and the longest-running theatre of the Eastern anti-fascist war. The article argues that the army tied down large Japanese forces, citing figures for Japanese military spending and Kwantung Army casualties. In this reading, it delayed both Japan's "northward" and "southward" advances and indirectly supported the Soviet Union. It also helped Soviet forces in 1945 through reconnaissance and by serving in the Soviet 88th Independent Rifle Brigade, and it prepared the ground for the Party's later takeover of the Northeast. The spirit itself is illustrated through loyalty to the Party despite long lost contact (Zhao Shangzhi, Feng Zhongyun), patriotic sacrifice (Zhao Yiman, Xu Chengshu, the twelve martyrs of Xiaogushan), and the unyielding resistance of Yang Jingyu.

Li concludes that research on the army's history has important academic and practical value in 2025. The author calls for study based on a correct view of the Second World War history and on empirical historical methods. Such work would cover the army's course of struggle, its conditions, its contributions and the contemporary value of its spirit, and would offer international scholarship a further angle on China's war. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army is presented in official commemorative writing, with the sources it cites.
quoteEn: The spirit of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army, as the bearing and ideological character shown in the war by the army under Communist Party leadership, is a concrete embodiment of the great spirit of the War of Resistance, a precious spiritual asset of the Chinese people, and an important part of the spiritual lineage of Chinese Communists.
quoteZh: 东北抗联精神作为中国共产党领导的东北抗联在战争中表现出来的精神风貌和思想品格，是伟大抗战精神的具体体现，是中国人民弥足珍贵的精神财富，是中国共产党人精神谱系的重要组成部分。

glossary.explanation: Communist-led guerrilla forces in Manchuria, formed from 1936 by reorganising the Northeast People's Revolutionary Army, which fought Japanese occupation until 1945. It is commonly abbreviated as Dongbei Kanglian.

t: Understanding the significance of "work style building is always on the road"
zh: 深刻理解“作风建设永远在路上”的重大意义
paras: Huang Qisong takes up Xi Jinping's formulation that "work style building is always on the road" and asks why it matters for a Marxist party. Writing in a Guangming Daily commentary of August 2025, Huang argues that Party conduct is not a peripheral matter but the foundation of the Party's governing position and of popular political identification with it. The thesis is that the formulation reflects an objective law of long-term rule and deepens Marxist party theory.

The piece has three numbered sections. The first links work style to the Party's governing base and political identity, drawing on the Communist Manifesto, Lenin's vanguard party and Mao Zedong's Yan'an-era statements. The second presents the formulation as the "deep code" of the Party's vitality over a century. The third treats it as a deeper understanding of how parties are built, including a comparison with Western party politics.

Huang first contends that the vanguard character of a proletarian party is not given in advance but must be forged through continuous self-construction, above all in work style. Bureaucratism, formalism, hedonism and extravagance are described as products of a distorted view of power that weaken the Party's close ties with the people. Second, bad work styles are said to be stubborn, recurrent and tied to their era, from the "sugar-coated bullets" of the early People's Republic to the market logic of the reform period and the "four tests" and "four dangers" today. Hence work style building must be sustained, and it is presented as the key entry point for the Party's self-reform, through the anti-corruption struggle, the eight-point rules and campaigns against the "four undesirable work styles". Third, Huang places this in a line from the Yan'an rectification and the Three-Antis and Five-Antis campaigns to full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, as an answer to the historical cycle of rise and fall. Huang describes Western party politics as periodic "political performance" and a struggle for power whose difficulties are almost insoluble, and contrasts this with the Chinese approach.

Huang concludes that continuous work style building gives long-term Party rule a political guarantee and offers a new approach to Marxist party building. In Huang's account it also underpins Chinese modernization and carries world-historical significance as a Chinese solution for party politics. Huang calls for work style building to run through the whole of the new great project of Party building. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party-building discourse in 2025 justifies permanent work style campaigns and frames them against Western party systems.
quoteEn: Work style problems are by no means trivial details; they are fundamental questions of principle bearing on the Party's nature and purpose and on its very survival.
quoteZh: 作风问题绝非细枝末节，而是攸关党的性质宗旨、生死存亡的根本性、原则性问题。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's development path, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western modernization.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping-era slogan for tightening Party discipline, anti-corruption work and internal supervision.
Rules adopted by the Politburo in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism among officials, such as limits on banquets, travel and meetings.
Formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, the targets of the Party's work style campaigns since 2012.
Official concept stressing that the Party must keep purging itself of corruption and wrong tendencies without external pressure.

glossary.en: historical cycle of rise and fall
glossary.explanation: The idea, raised by Huang Yanpei in conversation with Mao Zedong in 1945, that regimes flourish and then collapse; the Party presents self-reform and popular supervision as its way out.

t: Studying and thoroughly grasping the latest achievements of the Party's theoretical innovation
st: A reading of volume five of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China
zh: 学深悟透党的创新理论最新成果
paras: This short newspaper commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in August 2025, introduces volume five of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China. Chen describes the volume as the authoritative and systematic record of the latest results of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The author argues that it shows the Party's practice in high-quality development, deeper reform and the building of a modern socialist country, and that it should guide Party members and the public in studying the Party's theoretical innovation.

The article is organised around three themes drawn from the volume. The first is advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization, with the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) as the volume's opening. The second is the Two Integrations as the route of theoretical, institutional and cultural innovation. The third pairs new quality productive forces with the Global Civilization Initiative and the Global South as contributions to a community with a shared future for mankind.

On modernization, Chen reports the volume's claim that Chinese modernization overturns the equation of modernization with Westernization, offers developing countries another path, and is a new form of human civilization. Chen says it requires the Party's overall leadership, high-quality development as the first task, and deeper reform, citing the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). On the Two Integrations, the author presents the first as keeping Marxism abreast of the times and the second as giving it Chinese character, and calls the second a fresh liberation of thought. On productive forces, Chen summarises Xi's January 2024 definition: innovation-led, high-tech, high-efficiency, high-quality advanced productive forces. The author adds Xi's caution against blind rushes and a single model, and his call to tailor development to local conditions.

Chen presents the Global Civilization Initiative, proposed in March 2023, as a third pillar alongside the Global Development and Global Security Initiatives. The author also cites Xi's statements from 2023 and 2024 on the collective rise of the Global South as a major historical event. Chen concludes that the volume offers new answers to major questions of reform, governance and foreign affairs, and serves as an action guide for studying the Party's theory. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned overview of how volume five of The Governance of China is presented to Party cadres and the public.
quoteEn: The "first integration" stresses adapting Marxism to the needs of our times, keeping it at the forefront of the era and forever advanced; the "second integration" stresses adapting Marxism to the Chinese context, giving it Chinese spirit, Chinese style and Chinese character, so that it takes firm root in China.
quoteZh: “第一个结合”注重马克思主义的时代化，使马克思主义不断走在时代前列，永葆先进性；“第二个结合”注重马克思主义的中国化，使马克思主义具有中国气韵、中国气派、中国风格，从而牢牢扎根中国。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
The official name for China's path of modernization, elaborated at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
The formula of integrating Marxism with China's concrete realities and with excellent traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added in 2021–2023.
A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023 and elaborated in January 2024. It refers to innovation-driven productive forces based on advanced technology.
The official economic goal since about 2017, stressing quality, innovation and efficiency over speed of growth.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, which the Party promotes as a vision of shared global development and security.
A term for developing and emerging countries, which Chinese official discourse uses to place China among them.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream and the second centenary target of 2049.

keywords: Xi Jinping: The Governance of China
community with a shared future for mankind

t: A study of the positive interaction between the Party's theoretical innovation and practical innovation in the new era
zh: 新时代党的理论创新与实践创新良性互动探析
paras: Che Zongkai asks how the Communist Party of China's theoretical innovation and practical innovation have interacted in the new era, and why this matters for understanding and extending Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The article argues that this body of thought is the product of a "positive interaction" (liangxing hudong) between the two kinds of innovation under Party leadership. It also holds that the same interaction supplies a method for advancing theory on the basis of practice in the new journey ahead.

The article has three parts.
