The first sets out the dialectical relationship between theory and practice, drawing on Marx, Lenin and Mao Zedong and tracing it through the Party's history, from Mao Zedong Thought to Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents and the Scientific Outlook on Development. The second applies this to the new era, covering the changed principal contradiction, the major questions of the era, and the Party's summaries of experience. The third looks ahead to national rejuvenation and Chinese modernization.

Che's central argument is that practice is both the source and the driving force of theory, while theory guides practice and is in turn tested and developed through it. For the new era, the author reads the "Ten Clarifications" as original theoretical conclusions drawn from practice and the "Fourteen Commitments" as the basic strategy for applying theory in work. The "thirteen areas of achievement" summarised in the Party's third historical resolution are presented as practical verification of the theory. The author also holds that the "six musts" in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) contain the stance, viewpoint and method behind this interaction. They are: putting the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, a problem-oriented approach, a systems approach, and a global vision.

Looking forward, Che calls for continued interaction in the face of two pressures: the strategic overall picture of national rejuvenation and "changes unseen in a century" in the world. The author proposes advancing theory through the Two Integrations, combining Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. Che also argues that the practice of Chinese modernization, including deepening reform after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), is a rich source for further theoretical innovation. Read the original if you want a systematic, official-line account of how Party theorists frame the theory–practice relationship in Xi-era ideology and the structure of its core formulations.
quoteEn: This positive interaction between the Party's theoretical innovation and practical innovation means that theoretical innovation always reflects and meets the real demands of practical development, and that practical innovation always has correct theoretical guidance and ideological leadership, giving the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times a lasting driving force.
quoteZh: 党的理论创新与实践创新之间的这种良性互动，使党的理论创新始终能够反映和符合实践发展的现实要求，也使党的实践创新始终具有正确的理论指导和思想引领，赋予马克思主义中国化时代化以持续的动力保证。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
The formula of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added to official discourse in 2021–2023.
The official name for China's path of modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress in 2022. It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A ten-point summary of the core tenets of Xi Jinping Thought, adopted at the 19th Party Congress (2017) and later revised.
The 19th Party Congress's list of fourteen basic principles for upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era.

t: Mao Zedong's original contributions to constructing Chinese Marxist philosophy in the Yan'an period
zh: 延安时期毛泽东对构建中国马克思主义哲学的原创性贡献
source: Mao Zedong Studies (Mao Zedong yanjiu), 2025 no. 2
paras: Zhao Zihan asks what Mao Zedong originally contributed to building a Chinese Marxist philosophy, and argues that existing studies still need to answer this from the standpoint of the unity of worldview and methodology. The article holds that in the Yan'an period (1935–1948) Mao inherited the basic categories of Marxist philosophy and enriched them in light of Chinese conditions, producing the first typical result of Chinese Marxist philosophy.

The article first sets out the conditions that made this possible: Mao's world outlook, which combined Chinese and Western sources, and his Chinese sensibility, which linked tradition and modernity. It then traces how Mao treated three categories in turn: practice, labour and reality. Finally it assesses his contributions under four headings: ontology, worldview, methodology and values.

Zhao argues that Mao did not make 'matter' his sole starting point, as Soviet philosophical textbooks did. Mao instead moved the emphasis to practice and contradiction, in works that became On Practice and On Contradiction, and treated labour as the basic form of practice for organising the masses. Matter and practice then converge in the category of 'reality', which Zhao reads as an ontology that sidesteps the later dispute between material and practical ontology. Mao called the Marxist worldview a 'cosmology' and held that worldview and methodology are one thing, with materialist dialectics as the core. In Zhao's reading, Mao also recast the traditional Chinese relation of knowing and acting as a unity of the two, and made the people the subject of history and the point of departure and destination of value.

Zhao concludes that Mao activated Marxist principles and Chinese practice in both directions and brought traditional Chinese culture into dialogue with Marxist philosophy. The article links this to the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called for an independent knowledge system in Chinese philosophy and social sciences. It presents the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as a continuation of Mao's unified approach. Read the original if you study Mao Zedong Thought, the philosophy of the Yan'an period, or the Chinese debate over practical versus material ontology.
quoteEn: By interpreting worldview and methodology as one, Mao Zedong activated the basic principles of Marxism and Chinese practice in both directions, and brought China's fine traditional culture and Marxist philosophy together in dialogue.
quoteZh: 毛泽东通过对世界观和方法论的一体性诠释实现了马克思主义基本原理与中国实践的双向激活，使中华优秀传统文化与马克思主义哲学在对话中相结合。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

The years from October 1935, when the Party leadership reached northern Shaanxi, to March 1948, when Mao and others crossed the Yellow River. The article treats it as the time when Mao's philosophical thought took shape.
Mao Zedong's 1937 essay on the relation of knowledge and practice, which the article treats as a core Chinese Marxist statement on epistemology.
Mao Zedong's 1937 essay on the universality and particularity of contradiction, central to his version of materialist dialectics.

t: Research on the CPC's War of Resistance against Japan from the perspective of holistic history: a conference report
st: Review of an academic symposium held in Shenzhen, 16 November 2024
zh: “整体史视野下的中共抗战史研究”学术研讨会综述
source: Studies of CPC History (Zhonggong dangshi yanjiu), 2025 no. 2
paras: This is a report on the symposium "Research on the CPC's War of Resistance against Japan from the Perspective of Holistic History", held on 16 November 2024 at the Shenzhen campus of Harbin Institute of Technology. It was co-organised by the editorial office of Studies of CPC History and the university's School of Marxism, ahead of the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance. More than 30 scholars from universities, Party schools, military academies, research institutes and journals took part. The report says the field is shifting from a single-track political and military history towards a more multidimensional holistic history.

The meeting combined commentary on eight selected papers with roundtable thematic speeches. The papers covered North, Central and South China and addressed military strategy, mobilisation, social life, weaponry, Kuomintang–Communist relations and international factors. The report groups the discussion into several areas: the holistic and international framing; regional, social and cultural history; renewed work on traditional military, political and economic topics; methods; and sources.

On framing, participants called for placing the CPC's resistance within the world anti-fascist war and comparing it with responses to aggression in Europe, America, Asia, Africa and Latin America. One scholar urged treating the War of Resistance and the War of Liberation as one continuous line, and others urged viewing the frontal and enemy-rear battlefields together. Participants identified gaps in work on Northeast China before August 1945, on the Central Plains, Central China and Shandong afterwards, and on the Rear Area. They proposed more attention to women, film, medical care, veterans, emotions and human relationships, and to cultural-relic protection. Proposals on traditional fields included technological history of base-area arms industries, quantitative work on base-area economies and a longer time frame for studying the councils. Methodological suggestions included global history, fieldwork, virtual-reality reconstruction, maps, interdisciplinary work and critical borrowing from Western and Japanese scholarship. On sources, participants urged collecting foreign archives, Japanese and Russian materials, grassroots diaries, local inscriptions and technicians' notebooks, and treating memoirs with caution to avoid "survivor bias".

The report concludes that future research should widen its scope to topics such as war and the ecological environment, social security, education and law, integrate methods across disciplines, and pursue "heterogeneity" by looking for what is changing and distinctive. It expects deeper disciplinary integration to make the field more comprehensive and to link it to Chinese and world history. Read the original if you want a map of current research agendas, gaps and source suggestions in Chinese-language scholarship on the CPC and the anti-Japanese war.
quoteEn: Participating scholars held that the collection and use of sources on several new topics should be strengthened, with particular attention to grassroots sources.
quoteZh: 与会学者认为，要加强若干新议题的史料挖掘和利用，特别要注重其中的基层史料。

glossary.en: the CPC's War of Resistance against Japan
glossary.literal: history of the CPC's resistance war
glossary.explanation: The history of the Chinese Communist Party's role in the 1937–1945 war against Japan, known in China as the War of Resistance (14 years if counted from 1931). It is a major sub-field of Party history research.
An approach that places a topic within wider international, social and cultural contexts rather than treating it as only political or military history.
The wartime territory in south-west and north-west China under Nationalist control, away from the front, where the CPC also conducted work.

t: Empowering the dissemination of the Party's innovative theory with generative AI
zh: 以生成式人工智能赋能党的创新理论传播
paras: This short commentary in Guangming Daily asks how generative AI can help spread the Party's innovative theory when communication is shifting from broad coverage to precise reach. Zhang argues that AI can build detailed audience profiles and tailor content to each group. In Zhang's account, this addresses the "last mile" problem of moving audiences from knowing a theory to endorsing and practising it.

The article proceeds in five steps: building audience profiles with intelligent technology; keeping a people-centred orientation; explaining theory in language audiences know; delivering it through the right channels and at the right times; and forming a communication–feedback–iteration loop. It ends with a short assessment of what this represents.

Zhang says profiles draw on explicit data, such as registration and reading time, and implicit data, such as social-media topics and sentiment, and are updated continuously. On this basis, content can be adapted: anime-style material for young people, case-based reports for entrepreneurs, and picture-and-text items on local change for older people. Scene-specific content is another example, such as short videos for teachers. Zhang adds that AI can match platforms and timing to groups, and can assess behavioural, emotional and cognitive feedback to simplify or reformat material. Zhang presents building profiles as a way of listening to the people, in line with a people-centred approach.

Zhang concludes that such tailored communication is a new exploration of popularising the Party's innovative theory in the intelligent age. It does not negate traditional methods but makes them more precise and vivid. Zhang holds that adhering to communication for the people while innovating through technology will strengthen the theory's guiding and cohesive power. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party-school scholars frame AI-assisted ideological communication and audience targeting.
quoteEn: It is not a negation of traditional modes of communication, but a way of using new technical means to make theory communication more precise, more vivid and more considerate.
quoteZh: 它不是对传统传播方式的否定，而是通过新的技术手段让理论传播更精准、更生动、更贴心。

glossary.explanation: The Party's officially sanctioned latest theoretical achievements, centred on Xi Jinping Thought, which are to be studied and publicised among Party members and the public.
The long-standing aim of making Marxist and Party theory accessible and acceptable to ordinary people through plain language and relevant examples.

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A principle emphasised in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse that work should start from the needs and views of the people.
A common expression for the final stage of delivery, here the step from communicating theory to audiences actually accepting and applying it.

t: Responding to global challenges and advancing a multipolar world order
zh: 应对全球性挑战推动世界格局多极化
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War (2025), this newspaper commentary asks what the wartime alliance offers a postwar order now under strain. Feng argues that promoting a multipolar world, institutional equality and shared governance is a practical response to today's global challenges.

The piece moves in three steps. It first recalls anti-fascist cooperation, citing the Chinese united front, the Soviet–American meeting on the Elbe in 1945 and Mexico's declaration of war on Germany. It then turns to the establishment of multilateralism through the UN Charter and the agencies that followed. Finally it surveys present-day multipolarity.

Feng contends that states with different systems and cultures proved able to cooperate on the basis of shared justice, an experience the author links to the Chinese idea of harmony in diversity (hé ér bù tóng). The 1945 UN Charter, with sovereign equality and one vote per state in the General Assembly, is presented as the institutional result. The 1951 San Francisco conference, which excluded China and was boycotted by the Soviet Union, is described as a deviation that hardened into structural injustice. Today, the author says, BRICS states, the Global South, the European Union and the Belt and Road Initiative are strengthening multipolarity.

Feng concludes that multipolarity does not harm any country's interests but ends unilateralism and builds a fairer order of joint governance, which the author calls tianxia gongzhi. Developing powers and traditional powers should both take part in reforming global governance. Read the original if you want a brief example of how a Chinese academic frames the anti-fascist war's legacy in support of multipolarity and multilateralism.
quoteEn: Promoting a multipolar world by no means weakens any country's interests; rather, it breaks the shackles of unilateralism and establishes a fairer, more just, cooperative and win-win global order.
quoteZh: 推动世界多极化，绝非削弱任何一国利益，而是要打破单边主义桎梏，建立更加公平、正义、合作、共赢的全球秩序。

glossary.explanation: A term for developing and emerging countries, mostly in Asia, Africa and Latin America. Chinese official discourse uses it to describe a collective group of states.
An infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.
A classical Chinese idea that differences can coexist in harmony. The author treats it as a civilisational basis for international cooperation.

glossary.literal: joint governance of all under heaven
glossary.explanation: The article's term for a vision of shared global governance. It draws on the traditional Chinese notion of tianxia, 'all under heaven'.

t: Inheriting and promoting the great spirit of resistance against Japanese aggression in the new era
zh: 在新时代继承和弘扬伟大抗战精神
paras: Published in the China Social Sciences Today on 15 August 2025, this commentary asks where the "great spirit of resistance against Japanese aggression" came from, what it consists of, and how it should be carried on today. Pu Duanhua argues that the spirit is a concentrated expression of the Chinese national spirit in the War of Resistance. In Pu's view it has lasting value that must be cherished and promoted.

The piece has three parts. The first traces the spirit's origins. The second sets out its four defining qualities, using President Xi Jinping's formulation. The third draws four lessons for the present drive to build a strong country and achieve national rejuvenation. Pu supports the account with episodes from the war, such as the death of Yang Jingyu, the "Five Heroes of Langya Mountain" and the "Eight Hundred Heroes", and with the figure of more than 35 million Chinese military and civilian casualties.

Pu locates three sources of the spirit: the bloody struggle of the Chinese people after the 1931 Mukden Incident, the sublimation of the Chinese national spirit, and the firm leadership of the Communist Party of China. Pu stresses the Party's role as the "mainstay" of the war. In Pu's account, the Party raised the banner of armed resistance, upheld the anti-Japanese national united front and put forward the strategy of protracted war. The four qualities are patriotism ("everyone is responsible for the fate of the nation"), moral integrity in the face of death, heroism in fighting to the end, and unshakeable confidence in victory. Pu presents patriotism as the decisive factor in the victory.

Pu concludes that building a strong country and achieving national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization is a relay race requiring the same spirit. Pu calls for four things: stronger consciousness of following the Party; unity through patriotism, national unity and the unification of the motherland; self-reliance and self-strengthening; and a readiness to struggle against risks and challenges. Pu ties the first of these to upholding the authority of the Party Central Committee. Read the original if you want an example of how a military-academy leader links the memory of the anti-Japanese war to current Party leadership and national rejuvenation themes.
quoteEn: It can be said that victory in the War of Resistance was not only the recovery of the nation's land and rivers, but also an elevation of the Chinese national spirit for its era and a vivid manifestation of it.
quoteZh: 可以说，抗日战争的胜利，不仅是山河光复，更是中华民族精神的时代升华和生动彰显。

glossary.en: great spirit of resistance against Japanese aggression
glossary.literal: great spirit of the War of Resistance
glossary.explanation: A formulation used in official discourse, notably by Xi Jinping, for the values said to have emerged from China's 1931–1945 war against Japan. It names patriotism, moral integrity, heroism and confidence in victory.
The official name for China's path of development, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

glossary.literal: great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China to strength and prestige after what Party discourse calls the 'century of humiliation'. Xi Jinping has made it central to his political agenda.
The wartime alliance between the Communist Party and the Nationalist Party, together with other groups, against Japan's invasion. It was formed in the late 1930s.
A phrase used in Party historiography, and by Xi Jinping, to describe the Communist Party's role in the War of Resistance.

t: Carrying the building of Party conduct through to the end
zh: 将作风建设进行到底
paras: Fang Wenhao, writing in the China Social Sciences Today in August 2025, argues that the Party's conduct (zuofeng) is its calling card and bears on its image, popular support and survival. The commentary holds that the building of Party conduct must be carried on without letup, because the core of conduct problems is the relationship between the Party and the people.

The piece opens with the Central Committee's eight-point regulation, adopted after the 18th Party Congress (2012), and its campaign against formalism, bureaucracy, hedonism and extravagance. It then moves through historical models of good conduct, from the Central Soviet Area and the Long March to Yan'an and figures such as Gu Wenchang, Jiao Yulu and Yang Shanzhou, before turning to practical measures.

Fang treats the distinction between public and private as the basic yardstick of correct conduct. In this reading, vanity projects, cliques and nepotism all come down to self-interest, and public funds and public power must never be used privately. Because conduct problems are really problems of Party spirit, the author calls for education in Party spirit, ideals and convictions, and systematic theoretical study. Fang also urges institutional rules that are targeted, enforceable and equally binding, with no exceptions or "hidden doors".

The author further calls for tackling the main contradiction within each of the four undesirable work styles and watching for their new variants. Leading cadres, the "key minority", are asked to set an example in self-discipline and in family conduct. Read the original if you want a compact statement of how Party-building commentary in 2025 links the eight-point regulation to the public–private distinction and to institutional discipline.
quoteEn: The fundamental yardstick for measuring whether the Party's conduct is correct or not lies in two words: public and private.
quoteZh: 衡量党的作风正与不正的根本尺子在于公、私二字。

glossary.explanation: A set of rules adopted by the Central Committee's Political Bureau in December 2012 on improving work style and keeping close to the masses. It restricts official banquets, travel, meetings and perks.

glossary.zh: 形式主义、官僚主义、享乐主义和奢靡之风
glossary.pinyin: xíngshì zhǔyì, guānliáo zhǔyì, xiǎnglè zhǔyì hé shēmí zhī fēng
glossary.explanation: The four undesirable work styles, often abbreviated as the "four winds", which the Party has targeted since 2012.
A phrase used in Party discourse for leading cadres, whose conduct is held to shape the behaviour of the Party and society as a whole.
The qualities of loyalty, discipline and commitment to the Party's aims expected of members, often treated as the root of conduct problems.
The Party's ongoing effort to improve the work style and ethical conduct of members and cadres.

t: Upholding political principle is a fundamental requirement of a Marxist party
zh: 讲政治是马克思主义政党的根本要求
paras: Lu Jie takes up the Party's call to "talk politics" (jiang zhengzhi), meaning to stand firm on political principle. The commentary argues that this is a defining feature of Marxist parties and a consistent political strength of the Communist Party of China. Party members and officials, Lu says, should grasp it through theoretical, historical and practical logic.

The short piece first sets out the theoretical basis in the nature of a Marxist party and its organisational principle. It then turns to history: the Paris Commune, Lenin and the Bolsheviks, the Soviet collapse, and the Chinese Party's stages from Mao Zedong to Xi Jinping. It closes with what officials should do in the new era.

Lu contends that Marxism gives the proletarian party its direction, so political discipline keeps the Party on the people's side and unites its members under democratic centralism. Historically, Lu reads the Paris Commune's fall as a lack of centralisation and authority, and the Soviet collapse as a party that stopped talking politics and became a privileged stratum. For the present, the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds are presented as the main political outcomes and markers of this principle. Lu lists five requirements for officials: theoretical study, the "three political capacities" of judgement, understanding and execution, a people-first stance, a sound view of performance, and self-discipline with integrity.

Lu concludes that the Party's strength rests on strict organisational discipline and unified will and action. In practice, Lu says, this means upholding the authority of the Party Central Committee, carrying out its political line and observing its political discipline, so that it becomes a "truly iron-like organisation". Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars present political loyalty as a Marxist requirement.
quoteEn: Talking politics is not abstract but concrete and real.
quoteZh: 讲政治不是抽象的，而是具体实在的。

glossary.explanation: A Party expression for keeping political awareness, loyalty to the Party line and discipline at the forefront of work. Here it is rendered as standing firm on political principle.
A formulation from the 20th Party Congress (2022) affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Party Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.
A Party formulation for political judgement, political understanding and political execution, which officials are asked to build.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Party, combining discussion with binding unity of action under higher bodies.

t: Showing the world a vibrant Red China
st: Chinese Communists as seen by British and American journalists in China during the War of Resistance
zh: 向世界展现一个生机勃勃的红色中国
zhSub: 全民族抗战时期英美在华记者眼中的中国共产党人
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in August 2025, asks how British and American journalists who reached Yan'an and other anti-Japanese base areas during the War of Resistance (1937–1945) portrayed the Chinese Communists. Zhong argues that these reporters broke the Kuomintang's news blockade, gave the world a complete and truthful picture of the Communists, and supplied further evidence that the Communist Party was the mainstay of the nation's resistance.

The article draws on the accounts of Gunther Stein, Harrison Forman, James Bertram, Agnes Smedley, Theodore White, Nym Wales, Freda Utley and Israel Epstein. It is organised in four thematic sections: whether the Communist-led armies actually fought, mass mobilisation, the democratic practices of the base areas, and comparisons between the Communists and the Kuomintang.

Zhong's first move is to present the journalists' testimony as a rebuttal of Kuomintang claims that the Eighth Route and New Fourth Armies resisted without fighting. The author cites Stein's figures of 115,120 engagements between 1937 and March 1945 and Forman's remark that "we saw with our own eyes that the Eighth Route Army fights". The second move is to read the reporters' descriptions of organised and armed villagers, wall slogans, theatre and local elections as evidence of the Party's mass line and of working democracy. White, for example, saw the Party's strength in its tie to the peasantry. Finally, the author notes that many reporters had first stayed in Chongqing, so they compared the two parties. White judged that the Communists shone by contrast, and reporters described the leaders as frugal and selfless.

Zhong concludes that these first-hand reports changed domestic and international opinion of the Communists. In the author's account, the observers saw the Yan'an model as showing China's direction and the Party as the leader of China's future, and history has borne out those judgments. The piece is a brief, affirmative use of foreign eyewitness sources to support the Party's wartime narrative. Read the original if you want a concise example of how current Chinese Party-history writing uses Western journalists' testimony, and which names and quotations it selects.
quoteEn: In sum, the first-hand reports of British and American journalists in China during the War of Resistance broke through the Kuomintang's blockade of opinion, showed the world a vibrant Red China, and greatly changed domestic and international perceptions of the Communist Party.
quoteZh: 总而言之，全民族抗战时期英美在华记者的第一手报道，冲破了国民党的舆论封锁，向世界展现了一个生机勃勃的红色中国，极大地改变了国内外舆论对中国共产党的认知。

glossary.explanation: A Communist Party principle, associated with Mao Zedong, of drawing on the views of the people and relying on them in leadership and policy implementation.
The name given to the Communist-led Red Army in North China after it was nominally placed under the national government's command in 1937.
A Communist-led army formed in 1937 in central China from guerrilla forces left in the south, operating in the lower Yangtze region.

t: Strengthening the rule-of-law foundations of the unified national market
zh: 夯实全国统一大市场的法治根基
paras: Writing in the Economic Daily in August 2025, Hu Ming asks how law can help push forward the building of a unified national market, which the article presents as a major strategic decision of the Party Central Committee. Hu argues that the rule of law should lead, regulate and safeguard this effort, and that it should focus on remaining difficulties.

The commentary notes recent legal and policy steps, including the Fair Competition Review Regulations and the 2025 negative list for market access. It cites the sixth meeting of the Central Financial and Economic Affairs Commission, which set out the requirement of "five unifications and one opening". The text is organised under three headings: the boundary between government and market, basic market institutions, and reform of factor markets.

Hu first argues that law should define the line between government and market. Hu says the market should handle what it can, and government should address what the market cannot manage, while local protectionism and inconsistent enforcement are corrected. Next, Hu calls for stronger property protection, a single national negative list, bankruptcy and exit rules, and social credit legislation. Finally, Hu proposes deeper market-oriented reform of factor markets: revising laws and hukou rules for a unified urban-rural labour market, and data legislation to build a nationally integrated data market.

Hu concludes that unified rules, consistent enforcement and open factor flows, all anchored in law, are needed to deepen the unified national market. Hu also links this to aligning domestic rules with high international economic and trade standards. Read the original if you want a concise official-line statement of the legal measures proposed for market unification in 2025.
quoteEn: To better combine an efficient market with a capable government, the boundary between government and market should be drawn by the rule of law.
quoteZh: 推动有效市场和有为政府更好结合,应以法治来划定政府和市场的边界。

glossary.explanation: A policy goal, stressed by the Party leadership since 2022, of removing regional barriers and local protectionism so that goods, services and production factors move freely across China.

A formula from the sixth meeting of the Central Financial and Economic Affairs Commission. It calls for unified basic market rules, infrastructure, government conduct, regulation and enforcement, and factor markets, plus continued opening at home and abroad.
A list of sectors where investment is prohibited or restricted. Activities not on the list are open to all, which is the principle of "if not prohibited, then permitted".
China's household registration system, which ties access to public services to place of registration and affects labour mobility between city and countryside.

t: Comprehensive thinking: the methodology of the Communist Party of China in the new era
zh: 全面性思维：新时代中国共产党的方法论
paras: Wu and Ding take up a methodological question: how can thought grasp reality well enough to guide practice, and what mode of thinking does the Communist Party of China rely on to do so? They argue that "comprehensive thinking" (quanmianxing siwei) has grown from a summary of experience into a methodology with Chinese characteristics, and that it is the core thinking method of the Party in the new era. The piece appeared in China Social Sciences Today in August 2025.

The article begins with the frequency of the word "comprehensive" (quanmian) in the reports to the 19th (2017) and 20th (2022) Party Congresses, which it counts at 96 and 109 occurrences. It then places comprehensive thinking within Marxist epistemology and the traditional idea of the unity of knowing and doing. Next it relates it to the specific thinking methods Xi Jinping has put forward, and it ends by assessing its practical necessity today.

The authors make two main moves. First, they argue that comprehensiveness should not be treated as a mere sub-feature of dialectical thinking, as the standard triad of connection, development and comprehensiveness has it. In their view, dialectical thinking centres on principal contradictions, whereas comprehensive thinking attends to the whole system of contradictions, secondary ones included, and so avoids either-or metaphysics. Second, they hold that the "five" and then "six" thinking methods (strategic, historical, systemic, rule-of-law, bottom-line, people-centred and innovative thinking) each have limits. Comprehensive thinking, they say, integrates them through multi-angle analysis, multi-means verification and multi-party coordination, working at the cognitive, practical and value levels. They present Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as a model case, citing the five-sphere integrated plan, the Four-pronged Strategy and a community with a shared future for mankind.

The authors conclude that comprehensive thinking answers three needs. It offers a way to resolve the "development paradox" of unbalanced and inadequate development. It is a strategic choice for a changing world, in which they say it goes beyond zero-sum Western-centrism. It also supports building an autonomous Chinese system of knowledge. They expect it to keep guiding the drive towards the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a short example of how Party-affiliated scholars frame a thinking method as a distinct methodology within Xi Jinping's theory.
quoteEn: The essence of comprehensive thinking is to achieve an organic integration of specific thinking methods through the methodological principle of \"taking overall charge and coordinating all parties\".
quoteZh: 全面性思维的本质是通过“总揽全局、协调各方”的方法论原则，实现对具体思维方法的有机统摄。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept associated with Xi Jinping since about 2012. It calls for shared responsibility and cooperation in global governance.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term national goal of restoring China's power and standing by the mid-twenty-first century.

A strategic framework announced by Xi Jinping in 2014–15. Its four elements are building a moderately prosperous society, deepening reform, governing by law and strictly governing the Party. The English rendering varies; official sources also use "Four-Pronged Comprehensive Strategy".
The overall plan adopted at the 18th Party Congress (2012). It coordinates economic, political, cultural, social and ecological development.

t: The meaning of "whole-process supervision of the exercise of power"
zh: “全过程监督权力运行”的内涵阐释
paras: This short commentary in Guangming Daily explains a formulation Xi Jinping put forward at the 21st collective study session of the Political Bureau of the 20th Central Committee: "whole-process supervision of the exercise of power". Zhao presents it as a summing-up of the Party's experience of supervising power, and as a result of innovation in theory, practice and institutions for full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. The author argues that it gives guidance for the Party's self-reform.

Zhao first lists reasons for studying the formulation, including improving the rules system for self-reform, keeping close ties with the people, solving problems unique to a large party, and modernizing national governance. The article then reads the formulation through four dimensions drawn from Xi's 2023 speech: full coverage of content, of objects, of responsibility chains and of institutions.

On content, Zhao holds that such supervision is essentially political supervision. It covers implementation of the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, central decisions, correct operation of power under democratic centralism, and corruption that mixes political and economic problems. On objects, it reaches Party organisations, members, cadres and all public officials, with leading cadres as the focus, through disciplinary, supervisory, resident-inspection and inspection tours. On responsibility chains, supervision runs through authorisation, use and restraint of power, or before, during and after the event, as in budget review, execution and audit. On institutions, Party regulations, state law, mass and media supervision, and the chain of responsibilities must be linked.

Zhao concludes that the formulation shows the Party's deepening understanding of checking power. The author calls for stricter enforcement of rules, full democratic centralism, coordination among supervising bodies, technology to remove blind spots, and focus on key areas and the "key minority". Read the original if you want a brief official-style outline of how Party theorists frame power supervision within Party-building.
quoteEn: The three links of authorisation, use and restraint of power depend on and reinforce one another as an organic whole, and together make up the full cycle of procedures for supervising the exercise of power.
quoteZh: 授权、用权、制权三个环节相互依存、相互促进有机统一，共同构成权力运行监督程序的全周期。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the 2022 Party resolution, affirming Xi Jinping's core position in the Party and the guiding role of his thought.
The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised leadership of the Central Committee.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's drive for discipline, anti-corruption and rule-building, prominent since 2012.
An official concept stressing that the Party must rectify itself, mainly through internal supervision and discipline.
The Party's organisational principle combining internal discussion with unified discipline and obedience to higher bodies.

t: The Communist Party's comprehensive construction of the rural base areas in North China
zh: 中国共产党对华北农村根据地的全面建设
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in August 2025, asks how the Communist Party turned the rural areas behind Japanese lines in North China into a foundation for victory in the War of Resistance. Huo Hongwei argues that, by mobilising the masses and rebuilding the traditional countryside in politics, the economy and culture, the Party organised scattered human and material resources and laid a solid basis for final victory.

The piece opens with the situation after the Lugouqiao (Marco Polo Bridge) Incident, when Japan's full-scale invasion and the Nationalists' rapid retreat left the nation, in Huo's words, at its most dangerous moment. It then takes the three fields in turn: the building of democratic government, the improvement of the rural economy, and cultural work. The Jin-Cha-Ji border region serves as the main example.

On politics, Huo describes mass semi-governmental bodies giving way to border-region governments chosen by democratic election, down to village level. These were organised on the "three-thirds system" and, the author says, combined a united-front character with people's democracy. Turnout in the 1940 elections is given as over 70 per cent, and above 90 per cent in core areas, with women voting for the first time. On the economy, rent and interest reduction, mass mobilisation for production and mutual-aid cooperation raised productivity and moved scattered peasant households towards cooperative forms the author calls socialist in character. On culture, winter schools, night schools, literacy classes, wall newspapers and the arts were all, Huo says, tied to the single task of defeating Japan.

Huo concludes that this all-round construction aroused national consciousness and patriotic enthusiasm, drew Japan's forces into a "sea" of people's war, and produced villages of a New Democratic character that served as a basis for the founding of New China. Read the original if you want a concise, officially framed account of how Party history presents the North China base areas' political, economic and cultural work.
quoteEn: Cultural construction in the base areas, whether in education, propaganda or literature and art, was without exception organised around one central task: defeating Japanese imperialism and winning final victory in national liberation.
quoteZh: 根据地的文化建设，无论教育、宣传、文艺，无不围绕一个中心任务，即打败日本帝国主义，赢得民族解放的最终胜利。

glossary.explanation: A power-sharing arrangement in the anti-Japanese base areas, under which Communists, non-Party progressives and centrists each held about one third of government and representative posts. It was promoted by the Party from about 1940 as part of the united front.

A Party policy during the War of Resistance that cut tenant rents (the "25 per cent reduction") and loan interest (to one fen per month) rather than confiscating land. It aimed to ease peasant burdens while preserving the united front.
Mao Zedong's concept of a transitional stage of Chinese revolution, led by the proletariat and joined by several classes, before socialism. It also names the associated politics and culture.

t: Forging a high-calibre contingent of grassroots cadres
zh: 锻造高素质基层干部队伍
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in August 2025, asks how to build a high-calibre body of grassroots cadres at a time when grassroots tasks are heavy and demanding. Xu Dongtao argues that the Party should clearly signal that it values, cares for and protects grassroots cadres, and should work on five fronts at once.

The article is organised around five "emphases": Party spirit and ideological grounding, the original aspiration and mission (closeness to the masses), practical needs, scientific and professional competence, and a results-based incentive system. Each section names a shortcoming Xu sees among some cadres and then lists measures that localities could try.

On the first two fronts, Xu calls for selecting cadres by "both ability and integrity, with integrity first", for lectures on Party spirit by exemplary young cadres, and for short videos of their stories. Against superficial home visits, Xu proposes "people's-feelings diaries", regular analysis meetings at village, township and county levels, and periodic service weeks. On the third and fourth fronts, Xu criticises a "one mould for all" approach to training and proposes local surveys of development, reform and public needs, alongside annual rotational training and secondments to developed regions. The fifth front concerns incentives, with special recruitment drives for grassroots cadres, two-way secondments between grassroots and higher levels, and wider exchanges across prefectures and the province.

Xu concludes that these measures together would strengthen Party spirit, mass awareness, practical orientation, professional ability and motivation among grassroots cadres. The proposals are framed as options for local trial, mentioning new quality productive forces and the modernization of governance as targets. Read the original if you want a concise inventory of the concrete cadre-training and selection measures currently proposed for grassroots governance in China.
quoteEn: Grassroots work is, in the end, about serving the people; in practice we need to carry out a "thorough survey of the conditions of the people and enterprises" around the themes of curbing formalism and relieving burdens on the grassroots.
quoteZh: 基层工作，说到底就是为人民服务，在具体工作中我们需要围绕整治形式主义和基层减负的议题，开展“民情企情大摸底”活动

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological innovation and emerging industries.
Party and government officials working at village, township, street and county levels, who deal directly with the public.
An official goal of improving China's system and capacity for governance, usually linked to the Party's reform agenda.

t: Integrating the consciousness of the Chinese nation as a community into legislation in ethnic minority areas
st: Strengthening forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation through local legislation
zh: 推动铸牢中华民族共同体意识融入民族地区立法
paras: Feng Zhidong's short commentary (China Social Sciences Today, 6 August 2025) asks how local legislation in ethnic minority areas can serve the task of forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation, which the author calls the main theme of the Party's ethnic work in the new era. Feng argues that since the 2015 revision of the Legislation Law, such areas have produced locally suited laws, but that "legislative formalism", meaning omnibus and repetitive legislation, limits their effect.

The piece sets out four lines of improvement, framed by the principle of national legal unity and the guidance of the 20th Party Congress (2022) on scientific, democratic and law-based legislation. It closes with a note that it is an interim result of a Gansu provincial social science project on local legislation in the province's ethnic areas.

Feng's first two proposals concern who leads. Party committees in ethnic areas should put legislative planning on their agendas and focus on gaps and conflict points in local law. People's congresses, not government departments, should lead drafting, so as to contain the risk of "departmental interests becoming law"; provincial congresses should review annual plans and refuse approval to repetitive or omnibus projects. The third and fourth proposals concern craft: precise topic selection (for example rural environmental problems), workable content that balances national legal unity with legitimate local interests, and concise texts, citing Xi Jinping's advice to enact only as many articles as needed. Coordinated legislation among neighbouring areas, through joint meetings, would reduce imitation and duplication.

Feng concludes that coordination can only resolve differences between adjacent areas. The deeper problem of legislative formalism, in the author's view, requires a change in how ethnic areas understand legislative values, concepts and, above all, performance goals. Read the original if you want a concise, Party-line view of how local lawmaking in ethnic regions is meant to support national unity policy.
quoteEn: Coordinated legislation can only resolve some of the differences between the local legislation of geographically adjacent ethnic areas.
quoteZh: 协同立法只能解决部分地理位置相邻民族地区地方立法之间的差异性

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: firmly forge the consciousness of the Chinese nation as a community
glossary.explanation: A slogan that became the theme of Party ethnic policy after the 19th Party Congress (2017). It stresses a shared national identity over separate ethnic identities.
The author's term for local lawmaking that favours appearance over substance, such as omnibus laws that copy other regions' texts.
Regions with autonomous governments for ethnic minorities, including autonomous regions, prefectures and counties, which hold special local legislative powers.
Joint or coordinated lawmaking among different localities on similar matters, without changing their territorial scope or powers.

t: "For the Party and the people, promote the good and expose the bad, value both ear and eye": Xi Jinping on journalism and public opinion work in Zhejiang
st: Tracing his remarks and practice on news and public opinion work during his time in Zhejiang
zh: “为党为民、激浊扬清、贵耳重目”
paras: Zhao Yu and Chen Peihao review what Xi Jinping said and did about news and public opinion work while he worked in Zhejiang (the speeches cited date from 2002 to 2006). They argue that these remarks produced a three-part requirement: work "for the Party and the people", work that promotes the good and exposes the bad (jiluan yangqing), and work that "values ear and eye", meaning fact-finding by listening and looking. In their view, tracing these remarks systematically helps in understanding today's changes in the media landscape, in discourse, and in the balance between offence and defence. The article first appeared in the People's Daily in August 2025.

The article is organised in eight sections, each built around a phrase from Xi's Zhejiang speeches. They cover the Party principle in journalism, news work as a special ideological task, the line of "unity, stability and encouragement" with mainly positive coverage, the people's standpoint, the internet as a new front, innovation, the mass line in reporting, and the building of the journalist corps. Most evidence comes from Xi's addresses to Zhejiang media officials, to Party propaganda meetings and to central media staff based in the province.

The authors argue that Xi tied journalism's political character to professional demands. Media must remain the mouthpiece of the Party and the people, with the Party managing both media and cadres. Journalism is described as a special ideological field, where "a single guiding ideology" should steer diverse social currents. The authors present positive coverage as a way to build consensus and keep the public mood steady, and they say reporting must unify promoting Party positions with reflecting popular concerns. Xi's call to make the internet a "new position, new channel and new carrier" and his remark that blocking wrong ideas is not enough, because the main theme must be sounded, are presented as early responses to the digital age. The authors also report his demands for innovation, for journalists to go to the grassroots, to avoid fake news and hype, and to build a corps that is politically strong, professionally skilled, disciplined and upright.

The authors conclude that the Zhejiang experience offers lessons for the systemic reform of mainstream media in the new era. They list five: take a firm political stand and unify Party spirit with people-centredness; lead media trends through innovation; rely on investigation and the masses; build a full-media communication system; and invest in talent. They add a wider aim of a "big propaganda" pattern in which the whole Party takes part. Read the original if you want a concise, officially framed account of how Xi's Zhejiang-era statements on media are now being presented as a basis for Party media policy.
quoteEn: These important statements link the essence of news and public opinion to the professional requirements placed on those who do the work, fully reflecting an organic unity and close fusion of political character and professionalism.
quoteZh: 这些重要论述将新闻舆论的本质与新闻舆论工作者的职业要求关联起来，充分体现了政治性与专业性的有机统一和高度融合。

glossary.explanation: A Party term for the management of news media and the guidance of public opinion. It treats journalism as part of the Party's wider propaganda and ideological work.
The doctrine that news media must uphold the Party's leadership and line. It is regarded in Party discourse as the basic principle of journalism.

glossary.zh: 团结稳定鼓劲、正面宣传为主
glossary.pinyin: tuánjié wěndìng gǔjìn, zhèngmiàn xuānchuán wéizhǔ
glossary.literal: unity, stability, encouragement, with positive propaganda as the mainstay
glossary.explanation: A longstanding Party guideline for media work. It stresses mainly positive coverage that builds cohesion and morale.
A Party method of work that stresses learning from ordinary people and returning to them ('from the masses, to the masses'). Here it is applied to reporting.

t: Understanding the contemporary significance of Party conduct building
zh: 深刻领会党的作风建设的时代意蕴
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in August 2025, reads Xi Jinping's statements on Party conduct building (zuofeng jianshe) as both a theory of what conduct problems are and a practical system for tackling them. Liu Li links the piece to the 2025 campaign of study and education on the spirit of the Central Committee's eight-point regulation. The author argues that this body of thought raises the Party's understanding of conduct work to a new level and gives it an ideological weapon for the new era.

The article moves through seven of Xi's formulations, each paired with a classical Chinese saying and a call for "a high degree of consciousness". They cover conduct as a matter of the Party's survival, conduct as a question of Party spirit, the relationship with the people, the eight-point regulation, the "four undesirable work styles", the "critical few" of leading cadres, and long-term mechanisms.

Liu's central claims are that conduct problems are never minor but bear on the Party's survival and on popular support. They are rooted in weak Party spirit and a fading sense of purpose, and at core they concern the Party's relationship with the people. The author presents the eight-point regulation as a rigid, long-term rule, noting that it replaced "in general" with "without exception" and carries no "trial" label. Liu adds that formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance must be treated as the principal contradiction and that leading cadres must set the example. Institutionalisation is presented as the route from treating symptoms to treating causes.

Liu concludes that conduct building must advance in step with the Party's and the people's cause, and calls for full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and the Party's self-reform to be sustained on the path of Chinese modernization. Theoretical clarity and rigid institutions are said to ensure political firmness and conscious action. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars present Xi's conduct-building discourse in 2025.
quoteEn: Conduct building cannot be accomplished in one stroke or settled once and for all; it must be integrated into daily work and pursued constantly.
quoteZh: 作风建设不可能一蹴而就、一劳永逸，必须融入日常、抓在经常。

glossary.explanation: A set of rules adopted by the Politburo in December 2012 to curb bureaucratic practices, extravagance and formalism among officials. It is a core instrument of the Party's conduct and anti-corruption campaigns.
The Party's effort to shape officials' working style and behaviour, with the aim of keeping the Party close to the people.
Formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, named as the main conduct problems targeted since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Official term for the strict Party discipline and anti-corruption governance promoted since 2012.
A concept stressing that the Party must correct itself and eliminate its own problems through internal discipline, promoted under Xi Jinping.
Xi Jinping's phrase for leading cadres, whose example is said to shape the conduct of Party members and society at large.
The official term for China's development path as defined by the Party since 2021.

t: Rural mutual aid and cooperation in the Central Soviet Area as a demonstration of the Party's wisdom
zh: 中央苏区农村互助合作彰显党的智慧
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 4 August 2025
paras: This short commentary examines the mutual aid and cooperation that the Communist Party of China led among peasants in southern Jiangxi and western Fujian during the Central Soviet Area period. Zhang argues that the movement was both a strategic answer to wartime economic hardship and an early experiment in changing rural relations of production. In Zhang's account it supported the revolutionary war, restored farm output and consolidated Soviet power.

The article moves from causes to organisation to results. It first explains how the fragility of smallholder farming after land reform, together with the Nationalist blockade and encirclement campaigns, created demand for cooperation. It then describes the system of cooperatives, its operating principles and its regulatory documents, and ends with the movement's effects.

Zhang reports that the Party worked on the principle of voluntariness and mutual benefit, opposed coercion, and measured labour exchange in work points. Cooperatives covered circulation (consumer, purchasing, marketing, grain and credit societies), agriculture (field-tilling teams, labour mutual-aid societies, plough-ox cooperatives) and handicrafts. The author cites figures such as 1,206 labour mutual-aid societies in Xingguo County by April 1934 and more than 500,000 cooperative members across the area. Zhang credits the movement with higher grain harvests, better allocation of labour and support for the preferential treatment of Red Army families.

Zhang concludes that these experiments showed early Party wisdom in leading collective economy. The author names centralised, unified Party leadership, respect for peasants' wishes and interests, and gradual, realistic methods as the main lessons. The article treats the period as a source of the Party's later rural work methods. Read the original if you want a concise, officially framed account of cooperative organisation in the Jiangxi–Fujian base areas, with local statistics and policy documents.
quoteEn: The exploratory practice of mutual aid and cooperation in the Central Soviet Area demonstrated the early wisdom of the Communist Party of China in leading peasants to develop a collective economy.
quoteZh: 中央苏区互助合作的探索实践，彰显了中国共产党领导农民发展集体经济的早期智慧。

glossary.explanation: The main Communist-held revolutionary base area of the 1930s, centred on southern Jiangxi and western Fujian, with Ruijin as its capital. The Chinese Soviet Republic was founded there in 1931.
Cooperatives in which peasants pooled funds or draught animals so that members could share ploughing oxen, which were scarce in the base areas.
Peasant associations for exchanging labour, building on traditional seasonal labour exchange; work was recorded in work points and settled at year-end.

t: Historical experience of the century-old Party in rectifying formalism and bureaucratism
zh: 百年大党整治形式主义官僚主义的历史经验
paras: Wang Maosen asks what the Communist Party of China has learned over more than a century of fighting formalism and bureaucratism. The commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in July 2025, argues that these experiences are important for strengthening Party conduct in the new era and for eliminating the two problems effectively.

The piece follows the Party's record from the democratic revolution through the early People's Republic to the reform era. It cites Mao Zedong's condemnation of bureaucratism, the Yan'an rectification movement, the Common Programme, the early campaigns to rectify Party style and Party organisations, and the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978).

Wang organises the record into three pairs of lessons. The first combines a protracted, sustained struggle with targeted campaigns on specific problems. The second pairs the "lead goose effect" of leading cadres, who set an example, with stronger supervision by the masses. The third pairs political education, which builds ideological awareness, with institution-building, which Wang describes as tightening the "cage of rules". Wang treats the two evils as twins that both stem from subjectivism detached from reality.

Looking ahead, Wang calls for using big-data supervision, "smart Party building" and "Internet plus supervision" to raise effectiveness and widen public participation. Wang also calls for improving the system of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, so that Party conduct work becomes regular, long-term and institutionalised in support of building a modern socialist country. Read the original if you want a short, official-style summary of how Party history is used to frame current campaigns against formalism and bureaucratism.
quoteEn: Practice has proved that combining a protracted war with focused decisive battles on key points is a very important experience of our Party in rectifying formalism and bureaucratism.
quoteZh: 实践证明，坚持打持久战与突出重点打攻坚战相结合，是我们党整治形式主义官僚主义的一条非常重要的经验。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping's leadership since 2012. It refers to strict discipline, anti-corruption work and institutional rules within the Party.
A metaphor for leading cadres setting an example, as the lead goose guides the flock. It is used in Party discourse to stress that officials must model good conduct.
Official terms for empty, show-oriented work and for officials detached from the people and practical conditions. The Party treats them as persistent faults in its working style.
A Party-wide campaign from 1942 in the Yan'an base area to correct subjectivism, sectarianism and "stereotyped Party writing". It is treated as a model for later campaigns on Party conduct.

t: Understanding and grasping "upholding the Party's cultural leadership" in depth
zh: 深刻认识把握“坚持党的文化领导权”
paras: Yang Hongyuan takes up one of the core elements of Xi Jinping's thought on culture: upholding the Party's cultural leadership. In this commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 31 July 2025, Yang argues that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Central Committee has treated the question as strategically vital to the fate of the Party and state. In Yang's account, it has answered what cultural leadership is, why it must be upheld, and how to uphold and consolidate it.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out what cultural leadership means. The second explains why cultural subjectivity makes it necessary, given the tasks of national rejuvenation and the current international environment. The third lists practical requirements: theory, innovation, and concrete institutional leadership over propaganda, ideological and cultural work.

Yang defines cultural leadership as, in essence, leadership over ideological work, covering the powers of leadership, management and discourse. Yang treats ideological leadership as the foundation of all Party leadership, alongside political and organisational leadership, and holds that a rising class must win cultural leadership to take the initiative in making history. The Party exercises its leading role through ideological guidance, core socialist values, international discourse power and cultural reform. Yang cites new technologies such as mobile internet and artificial intelligence, a more diverse range of ideas, and what the author calls hostile forces' ideological infiltration as reasons why this leadership matters more. Consolidating cultural subjectivity, citing Xi Jinping, is presented as the basis of cultural confidence and of any culture's capacity to lead and radiate influence.

Yang calls for arming the whole Party and educating the people with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and for building popular identification with it. Yang also asks for cultural innovation grounded in practice, paired with adherence to the correct direction. Leadership must be made concrete through centralised, unified Party leadership over propaganda, ideology, media and the internet, and through unifying Party spirit with the people's interests. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of how Party theorists explain the concept of cultural leadership and its practical implications.
quoteEn: The Party's cultural leadership is not abstract but concrete, and the Party's comprehensive leadership over propaganda, ideological and cultural work must be put into effect.
quoteZh: 党的文化领导权不是抽象的而是具体的，必须把坚持和加强党对宣传思想文化工作的全面领导落到实处。

glossary.explanation: The Party's authority over ideology and culture, which the article treats as equivalent to leadership over ideological work. The Chinese term also echoes the Gramscian idea of cultural hegemony.
A body of ideas on culture and ideology attributed to Xi Jinping and formally presented in 2023 as part of Xi Jinping Thought.
A nation's conscious sense of its own culture and its initiative in cultural creation. Xi Jinping presented it as the basis of cultural confidence.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.
A twelve-word official set of values, promoted since 2012, covering national, social and individual levels.

t: Putting the requirements of the Party's self-reform in the new era more fully into effect
zh: 把新时代党的自我革命要求进一步落实到位
paras: This commentary responds to Xi Jinping's speech at the 21st collective study session of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee. Xi called for the Party's self-reform to be implemented more fully in five areas: understanding, Party spirit, regulation of power, strict supervision and discipline, and responsibility for Party governance. Hu Guoxi argues that these five requirements form a closed loop of top-level design that gives strategic guidance and a practical path for carrying self-reform through to the end.

The piece is short and takes the five requirements in turn, treating each as a link in one chain. It draws on Xi's formulations throughout and adds images such as power's 'revolution' and 'rotation', and the Party organisation's unsheathed blade.

Hu's central claims run as follows. Self-reform is first an ideological revolution, so mistaken views must be rejected, including that it is troublesome, excessive or 'none of my business'. Party spirit must be tempered, because the author holds that weak Party spirit leads to degeneration. Hu argues that corruption is at root the use of power for private gain, so self-reform must focus on governing power by making it operate transparently and traceably under institutional constraints. Hu also notes that cases are more often dug up passively than uncovered proactively, and calls for routine supervision and joint investigation of misconduct and corruption.

On responsibility, Hu calls for a performance outlook in which running Party affairs well counts as the greatest achievement, and for a complete chain of responsibilities, accountability and assessment. Hu concludes that this will build an atmosphere of strictness and integrity and advance full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary presents the Party's self-reform agenda and its rhetoric.
quoteEn: The Party's self-reform places its emphasis on governing power.
quoteZh: 党的自我革命重在治权。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping has stressed since the 18th Party Congress (2012), describing the Party's efforts to discipline, purify and improve itself without external pressure.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: The official slogan for the Party-building and anti-corruption drive under Xi Jinping, covering ideology, organisation, conduct, discipline and institutions.
The qualities of loyalty, discipline and commitment expected of Party members, which the Party treats as the basis of members' conduct.

t: Making better use of the rule of law in further deepening rural reform
zh: 更好发挥法治在进一步深化农村改革中的作用
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in July 2025, Zhang Zhenli takes up the question of how legal tools can support further rural reform after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). Zhang argues that rule-of-law thinking and methods must be used to handle the major issues of rural reform, so that law "consolidates the foundation, stabilises expectations and benefits the long term". The piece is a short commentary that follows recent Party and State Council documents on rural reform and the comprehensive revitalisation of the countryside.

The article is organised in three parts. The first addresses the relationship between farmers and land, which Zhang, citing Xi Jinping, calls the main line of rural reform. The second covers integrated urban–rural development, and the third covers effective rural governance. Each part lists the relevant statutes, such as the Land Management Law, the Civil Code, the Rural Land Contracting Law, the Rural Revitalisation Promotion Law and the 2024 Law on Rural Collective Economic Organisations, and then sets out tasks for the present.

On land, Zhang holds that the basic rural operating system rests on four elements: collective land ownership, the foundational role of household operation, stable contracting relations, and the improved "three rights separation" arrangement. Zhang describes how legislation has strengthened the legal standing of collective owners and households, and calls for better contract management, orderly pilots extending second-round contracts by thirty years, and respect for farmers' wishes in land transfer. On urban–rural integration, Zhang urges collective economic development that benefits members, a unified urban–rural construction land market, priority fiscal support and the extension of basic public services to all permanent residents. On governance, Zhang calls for Party-led village self-governance combining self-rule, rule of law and moral governance, along with stronger grassroots Party organisations, public legal services and village rules to change social customs.

Zhang concludes that law must be used to protect farmers' rights and keep reform on a legal footing, while ensuring Party leadership in rural governance. The piece is largely a policy-oriented survey of existing legislation with proposals for its application. Read the original if you want a concise official-style overview of how Chinese legal scholarship links rural land, urban–rural integration and village governance to the current rural revitalisation agenda.
quoteEn: To deepen rural reform further, we must make better use of the rule of law as a safeguard that consolidates the foundation, stabilises expectations and benefits the long term, and keep using rule-of-law thinking and methods to handle a series of major rural reform issues properly.
quoteZh: 进一步深化农村改革，必须更好发挥法治固根本、稳预期、利长远的保障作用，坚持运用法治思维和法治方式妥善处理农村改革一系列重大问题。

glossary.explanation: A rural land arrangement that separates the collective's ownership right, the household's contracting right and the operator's land-management right, so that land use can be transferred while contracting rights stay with farm households. It became national law through the 2018 revision of the Rural Land Contracting Law.
The policy goal of the rural revitalisation strategy launched in 2017, covering rural industry, ecology, culture, governance and living standards.
A phrase in Party discourse asking officials to handle reform, development and disputes according to law. Xi Jinping has stressed that major reforms should have a legal basis.
The system built on household contract operation within a two-tier structure combining collective and household management, with land collectively owned.

t: Bringing red culture into Party-spirit education
zh: 发挥红色文化在党性教育中的作用
paras: Writing in a newspaper commentary of July 2025, Wei Min asks how red culture can be used in Party-spirit education for Party members and cadres. Against the background of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, Wei argues that this is both an innovative application of Marxist cultural theory and an important route to strengthening members' Party-spirit cultivation. Local red culture, in Wei's view, is a concrete way of passing on the red gene.

The piece draws on the experience of the Heilongjiang Provincial Party School, where Wei works. It first sets out the theoretical fit between red culture and Party-spirit education, then describes how the school uses Heilongjiang's red resources for ideals and convictions and for service to the people. It ends with regional cooperation and digital empowerment.

Wei holds that, on Marxist cultural theory, advanced culture shapes group values and gives spiritual guidance, so red culture's collectivism and revolutionary idealism match the aims of Party-spirit education. Heilongjiang's core symbols are the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army spirit and the Great Northern Wilderness spirit. Wei cites Zhao Shangzhi and Yang Jingyu as models of conviction, and the transformation of the wilderness into farmland of 11.38 million hectares as an illustration of serving the people and the mass line. Sites such as the Northeast Martyrs' Memorial and a 'red family tradition' classroom serve as immersive teaching. Wei adds that linking Heilongjiang's spirit with Yan'an and Jinggangshan through themed study routes would help members grasp the continuity of the Party's history.

Wei concludes that the school should keep developing local red resources, encouraging teachers to research and publicise them, and turn them into high-quality teaching material. The article is brief and descriptive, and the digital side of the title's argument is only lightly developed. Read the original if you want a short example of how a provincial Party school presents local revolutionary heritage as a tool of Party-spirit education.
quoteEn: Integrating Heilongjiang's red culture into Party-spirit education is, in essence, a way of using cultural carriers to give Marxist ideology a concrete, tangible form of dissemination.
quoteZh: 将黑龙江红色文化融入党性教育，本质上是通过文化载体实现马克思主义意识形态的具象化传播

glossary.explanation: Training for Party members and cadres aimed at strengthening political loyalty, ideals and discipline. It is a core task of Party schools.
The culture, sites, stories and spirit associated with the Chinese Communist Party's revolutionary, construction and reform history.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Official term for the Party's drive to tighten discipline and internal management, prominent since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
The spirit attributed to Communist-led guerrilla forces that fought Japanese occupation in northeast China in the 1930s–40s.
The spirit attributed to settlers who reclaimed the wilderness of Heilongjiang for farming from the 1950s onward.
A Party principle of drawing on and serving the masses in its work, developed under Mao Zedong.

t: Party building as leadership in resolving governance problems of county-level modernization
zh: 付伟、党建引领化解县域现代化的治理问题
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in July 2025, asks how grassroots governance can be modernized so that it supports county-level modernization. Fu argues that Party building as leadership (党建引领) is the key lever for doing so. The piece takes its cue from the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called for a grassroots governance system led by Party organizations.

The article first sets out the new demands that county modernization places on grassroots governance, then draws on the experience of Jiangyin city, as seen by a Peking University research team, to propose three directions for improvement.

Fu describes a rise in both the quantity and the quality of governance tasks, which leaves grassroots bodies overburdened ("a small horse pulling a big cart"). The author attributes this to fragmentation between functional lines and territorial levels, low popular participation ("cadres act, the masses watch") and weak mechanisms for involving social forces. The remedies are to strengthen Party coordination across departments and relieve village and community organizations of top-down tasks and assessments; to build precise, responsive services through grid-based management, digital platforms and "smart" government; and to mobilise residents through a new-era mass line, illustrated by Jiangyin's "1+10+N" system linking Party members with households.

Fu concludes that high-quality grassroots governance, led by Party organizations, is what advances county modernization. Fu also calls for ending "one-assessment-decides-all" practices and for giving grassroots bodies more room to experiment. Read the original if you want a brief statement of how Party-building and grassroots governance are linked in current policy discourse on counties.
quoteEn: The simultaneous rise in the quantity and quality of grassroots governance tasks inevitably adds to the burden on the grassroots governance system, and this is an important reason for the "small horse pulling a big cart" problem.
quoteZh: 基层治理任务的质量齐增，也不可避免地加重基层治理体系的治理负担，这也是导致“小马拉大车”的重要原因。

glossary.explanation: A policy formula in which Party organizations take the lead in coordinating local governance, services and mobilisation. It is widely used in official discussion of grassroots work.
A Chinese Communist Party working method, associated with Mao Zedong, of going among the people, drawing on their views and mobilising them. The article calls for a "new-era" version of it.

glossary.en: fragmentation between functional lines and territorial levels
glossary.explanation: A description of the Chinese administrative system, in which vertical functional departments (条) and local territorial governments (块) overlap and often fail to coordinate.

t: Thoroughly implementing the spirit of the Central Committee's eight-point regulation: polishing the Party's golden calling card of conduct building
st: Summaries of expert presentations at the forum "Theory and Practice of Ruling-Party Building"
zh: 深入贯彻中央八项规定精神 擦亮党的作风建设金色名片
