paras: This is a report on a forum, "Theory and Practice of Ruling-Party Building", jointly held by the Academy of Marxism of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, Jiangxi Normal University and the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences. Its theme was the spirit of the Central Committee's eight-point regulation and the Party's conduct building (zuofeng jianshe). The editors present abridged remarks from several participants, held while a Party-wide study and education campaign on implementing the regulation was under way.

Speakers came from research institutes, universities and Party schools. They include Zhu Xiaoli (Jiangxi Normal University), Deng Chundong (formerly of the Academy of Marxism), Liu Jianhui (formerly of the Central Party School), Liu Jingbei (formerly of the China Pudong Cadre College), Liu Honglin (Fudan University), Ding Junping (Wuhan University), Song Jin (East China Normal University) and Zang Xiuling (Shandong University).

The speakers largely agree that the regulation is a starting point rather than an end. Deng describes conduct building as the premise of all Party building, a determinant of the Party's political advantages and the most basic factor in its long-term rule. Liu Jianhui and Song stress that the regulation is a basic requirement and a first step, linked to the claim that conduct building is never finished. Ding finds the spirit of the regulation centred on integrity and self-discipline, thrift, practical efficiency and close ties with the masses. Liu Honglin asks how to strengthen the enforcement of intra-Party regulations, and Zhu and Liu Jingbei call for systematic study of Xi Jinping's statements on conduct. Zang draws on Chen Yun's example of ideals, Party spirit, seeking truth from facts, plain service and diligent study.

The participants conclude that conduct building should be made regular and long-term, and that full and rigorous self-governance of the Party should be deepened. Several link the campaign to the Party's long-term rule and to Chinese modernization, and Liu Jianhui presents it as part of the Party's self-reform. Zhu proposes three research priorities: systematising Xi's discourse, theorising the results and experience since the 18th Party Congress (2012), and studying the historical experience of the Party's century. Read the original if you want a compact view of how Party-affiliated scholars frame the eight-point regulation, its theory and its place in Party discipline.
quoteEn: Conduct building has only a starting point and no end point, only a continuous tense and no completed one; it is by no means an expedient measure but an eternal task.
quoteZh: 作风建设只有起点，没有终点，只有进行时，没有完成时，绝不是权宜之计，而是永恒的课题。

glossary.explanation: A set of rules on official conduct adopted by the Politburo in December 2012, shortly after the 18th Party Congress. They curb formalism, bureaucratism, extravagance and waste, and the practice of officials' privileges.
The Party's term for efforts to shape the working style and everyday behaviour of Party members and officials. It is treated as one part of overall Party building.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A strategy adopted under Xi Jinping that stresses strict Party discipline, anti-corruption work and intra-Party regulations.
An official concept holding that the Party can keep its vitality by rectifying its own problems through internal discipline and supervision.
The official name for the Party's path of modernization, set out in 2022. It is presented as distinct from Western models.
Formal rules issued by the Party to govern its organisation and members' behaviour. They are distinct from state law.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Consolidating the rule-of-law foundation of high-standard opening up
zh: 夯实高水平对外开放的法治根基
paras: This commentary from the Chinese Social Sciences Today (28 July 2025) asks how high-standard opening up can proceed on a rule-of-law track. Yang Song argues that the key lies in the rule-of-law dimension of institutional opening up (制度型开放). Citing the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and Xi Jinping's remarks at a Politburo study session in November 2023, Yang holds that law accompanies opening, so foreign-related rule of law must advance with each step of opening.

The piece has three parts. The first traces how institutional opening up entered Party documents, from the 2018 Central Economic Work Conference through the 19th Central Committee's Fourth and Sixth Plenums, the 14th Five-Year Plan and the 20th Party Congress (2022) to the 2024 Third Plenum. The second sets out a system of six "theories" of institutional opening up. The third turns to the broader consequences for China's place in the world.

In the core of the argument, Yang describes institutional opening up as aligning rules, regulations, management and standards with international norms. The six components are institutional alignment, opening, inclusiveness, standards, competition and security. Alignment means actively matching high-standard trade rules such as CPTPP and DEPA. Opening refers to measures such as pre-establishment national treatment with a negative list and the new Foreign Investment Law. Inclusiveness is tied to the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind and to opposing unilateralism. Standards means that China's institutions should "go out", gaining rule-making power in a global order that Yang says developed countries still dominate. Competition covers institutional rivalry with the US and the West, to which Yang says China responds with the Belt and Road Initiative, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and the BRICS bank. Security treats institutional security as the baseline and the cornerstone of the holistic approach to national security, with rule of law as its guarantee.

Yang concludes that China should align domestic rules with international standards, raise the competitiveness of its economic legal institutions, uphold inclusiveness and an economic-security bottom line, and push its standards abroad. This calls for inclusive, open, breakthrough and innovative thinking in building a new system of an open economy. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese legal scholars frame institutional opening up and foreign-related rule of law in terms of official policy.
quoteEn: Having institutions \"go out\" is in essence having standards \"go out\"; only when the standards China advocates go abroad can the influence and acceptability of China's economic institutions rise and China play a leading role in international markets.
quoteZh: “制度走出去”实质是“标准走出去”，只有我国提倡的标准走出国门，才能提升我国经济制度的影响力和可接受程度，才能在国际市场上发挥我国的主导作用。

glossary.explanation: Opening that goes beyond tariffs and market access to align rules, regulations, management and standards with international norms. The term was first used at the 2018 Central Economic Work Conference.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept of international relations stressing shared interests, multilateralism and mutual benefit. It is used in official texts as a guiding idea for global governance.
Xi Jinping's framework, introduced in 2014, which treats security as spanning politics, economy, culture, technology and other fields and links internal with external security.
China's infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

t: Using digital-intelligence technology to improve the quality and effectiveness of intra-Party supervision
zh: 以数智技术助力提升党内监督质效
paras: This newspaper commentary (Guangming Daily, 28 July 2025) asks how big data, cloud computing and artificial intelligence can be built into intra-Party supervision while guarding against risks. Liang argues that such "digital-intelligence" supervision can become a new engine for improving the quality and effectiveness of supervision and for strengthening efforts against misconduct and corruption.

The piece is organised around three tasks: building a digital-intelligence supervision platform, improving the mechanisms that govern it, and raising the digital-intelligence skills of those who carry out supervision.

On the platform, Liang proposes a chain of linked components (inspection, evaluation and feedback, risk warning, problem handling, information release). The author calls for Party committees to coordinate funding, technology and personnel, for data barriers to be broken down, and for platforms to be merged, for example by combining tax, transport, property and finance data so that discipline inspection bodies can spot problems early. On mechanisms, Liang calls for Party regulations that set the scope and limits of technology use, give discipline inspection organs lawful access to data, and guard against misuse, privacy breaches and leaks. Supervision should sit within a system led by Party committees, with discipline inspection and supervisory commissions coordinating and cooperating with audit, accounting and statistical supervision.

On skills, Liang says supervisors must change traditional thinking, and that digital-intelligence competence should be assessed and linked to evaluation, promotion and appointment. Training, through Party schools and cadre education institutions with added technology courses, should address concrete problems in applying technology to supervision. Liang presents these steps as moving supervision from reliance on experience and after-the-fact response towards combining experience with technology and acting in advance. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how official Party-building discourse frames the use of big data in discipline inspection and supervision.
quoteEn: If technology is used in ways that depart from its basic aims and leads to incidents that harm information security or personal privacy, or to leaks, this goes against the original purpose of applying it.
quoteZh: 如果技术使用脱离了基本目标，出现了危害信息安全和个人隐私、泄密等事件，就背离了技术应用的初衷。

glossary.explanation: The system by which the Communist Party oversees its own organisations and members, led by Party committees and discipline inspection bodies.

t: The string of self-reform must be drawn tighter
st: Commentator's article in Qiushi
zh: 《求是》杂志评论员：自我革命这根弦必须绷得更紧
paras: This commentary in Qiushi (2025, no. 14) takes up Xi Jinping's remarks at the 21st collective study session of the 20th Political Bureau, held before 1 July 2025, on making the eight-point regulation and the long-term mechanism against the "four undesirable work styles" more effective. It argues that the string of the Party's self-reform must be drawn tighter and that work-style building cannot be relaxed.

The commentary looks back at the period before the 18th Party Congress (2012), when, in its account, bad work styles and corruption spread. It then turns to current conditions, to misunderstandings among some cadres, and to four requirements: strengthening Party spirit, regulating the exercise of power, strict supervision and discipline, and layered responsibility.

The author presents the eight-point regulation as a small opening that drove a wider transformation of work style, and calls self-reform the Party's second answer to the historical cycle of rise and fall. Because Chinese modernization and deeper reform face heavy tasks and external risks, the author holds that the Party cannot slacken, and cites officials who broke rules during the current study campaign as a warning. The author rejects the views that self-reform harms the Party's image or obstructs economic growth, and argues that it removes obstacles and restores vitality. Work-style problems are traced to a lapse in Party spirit.

The commentary calls on Party members to study Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and to temper themselves in practice. It also calls for transparent, traceable systems that put power "in the cage of institutions", joint supervision, and the investigation of work-style and corruption cases together. Leading cadres, as the "key minority", are urged to shoulder responsibility for Party governance. Read the original if you want an example of how official Party media frame the continuing campaign for full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.
quoteEn: Self-reform is by no means self-harm to the Party's image; by curing illness, healing wounds and removing rot to promote new growth, it better establishes the Party's image and authority and unites the hearts of Party members and the people.
quoteZh: 自我革命绝不是自损形象，而是通过祛病疗伤、去腐生肌，更好树立形象威信、凝聚党心民心

glossary.explanation: An official concept from the Xi Jinping era. It describes the Party's efforts to discipline itself and remove corruption and bad work styles from within.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official slogan for the Party's drive to tighten discipline, supervision and anti-corruption work across the whole organisation. It has been central since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
Rules adopted in December 2012 that restrict officials' extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism, for example on banquets, travel and meetings.
Official shorthand for formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance among Party members and officials.
The official term for China's development path under Party leadership, promoted since 2021–22 as the Party's central task.

t: The threefold meaning of "maintaining historical patience"
zh: “保持历史耐心”的三重意蕴
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in July 2025, examines Xi Jinping's repeated call to "maintain historical patience" (baochi lishi naixin). It opens with Xi's remarks in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) and at the Central Urban Work Conference of 14 July 2025, where he warned against rushing urbanisation and industrialisation. Sun Laibin argues that the phrase has three layers of meaning: a dialectical character, a strategic rationale and practical requirements for pursuing Chinese modernization.

The piece is organised under three headings. The first defines historical patience and explains its dialectical qualities. The second sets out why it matters strategically, drawing on Party history, the "two overall situations" and the demands of development. The third lists what the principle requires in practice. Sun draws on Xi's speeches throughout, together with examples such as the C919 airliner, the ten-year Yangtze fishing ban and the Xiong'an New Area.

Sun defines historical patience as a long-term view, steady strategic planning and composed temperament, grounded in grasp of historical laws. In this reading it combines respect for objective laws with initiative, so it is not passive waiting, and it balances speed and slowness and long-term planning with present action. Strategically, Sun presents it as a lesson from the Party's successes and from mistakes such as the Great Leap Forward, which the article attributes partly to impatience. Sun also ties it to the "two overall situations" and to high-quality development, which the article treats as a long and arduous task requiring a shift from quantity to quality.

For practice, Sun calls for a "grand view of history", including the balance between progress and setbacks on the path to socialism, and a correct view of performance that puts serving the people ahead of showy achievements. Sun also calls for a fighting spirit, directed at corruption through full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and at external pressure on China's sovereignty and development. The article presents patience as compatible with, and supported by, firmness and sustained effort. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars interpret Xi Jinping's "historical patience" and link it to Chinese modernization, governance and anti-corruption.
quoteEn: Maintaining historical patience does not mean passive waiting or doing nothing; it means taking a responsible attitude towards history and acting actively and seizing momentum on the basis of grasping the laws and broad trends of historical development.
quoteZh: 保持历史耐心，并不意味着消极等待、无所作为，而是要本着对历史负责的态度，在把握历史发展规律和大势的基础上积极作为、乘势而上。

glossary.explanation: A phrase Xi Jinping has used since the 18th Party Congress (2012), urging steady, gradual progress on long-term tasks such as modernization instead of hasty, short-term results.
The official term for China's path to modernization, presented by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
Official formulation referring to the strategic overall situation of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and to profound changes unseen in a century in the world.
Official economic goal, stressed since 2017, of shifting from rapid growth in scale to growth centred on quality, efficiency and innovation.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Official term for the strengthened Party discipline and anti-corruption drive promoted since 2012.
A term Xi uses for analysing events within long historical, epochal and global perspectives.

t: The theoretical contributions and contemporary value of the Seventh Party Congress
zh: 党的七大的理论贡献与时代价值
paras: Writing in a newspaper commentary, Yang Na takes up the Seventh Party Congress, held at Yang'jialing in Yan'an in spring 1945, when China faced the question of where it was heading. Yang argues that the Congress built a complete theoretical system covering guiding ideology, political line and Party organisation. In the author's account, this system carried through revolution and governance and still offers guidance today.

The article is organised in three parts: the Congress's theoretical landmarks, its historical echoes in practice, and its relevance in the new era. It draws on the new Party constitution, Mao Zedong's report On Coalition Government, and later events from the civil war to the early People's Republic.

Yang reads the Congress as doing three things. It wrote Mao Zedong Thought into the Party constitution as the guide for all work. It set a political line aimed at a New Democratic China and a coalition government. It also made serving the people wholeheartedly the Party's fundamental purpose, refined democratic centralism, and distilled the Party's three styles of work. Yang traces its later effects: the blueprint was realised within four years, its ideas on people's congresses and a mixed economy shaped the early state, and its stress on work style fed the multi-party cooperation system. For the new era, Yang links the Congress to the Two Integrations, to a people-centred development philosophy and to full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

Yang concludes that the Congress's method, popular standpoint, historical initiative and work style continue to support Chinese modernization and the Party's self-reform. Achievements in poverty alleviation, technology and diplomacy are presented as evidence of this continuity. Read the original if you want a brief example of how current Party scholarship links the 1945 Congress to Xi Jinping-era themes.
quoteEn: The historic contribution of the Seventh Party Congress lies in building a complete theoretical system covering guiding ideology, strategy for action and organisational principles, laying the cornerstone for winning the revolution.
quoteZh: 党的七大的历史性贡献，在于构建起涵盖指导思想、行动方略、组织原则的完整理论体系，为夺取革命胜利奠定基石。

glossary.explanation: A formula in Xi-era Party theory: integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Official name for the Party-discipline and anti-corruption drive prominent since 2012.
An official concept describing the Party's efforts to correct its own faults and maintain discipline.
Mao Zedong's theory of a transitional stage after the anti-imperialist, anti-feudal revolution, led by the Party with a multi-class alliance, before socialism.

t: Advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance by starting with Party conduct
zh: 从抓作风入手推进全面从严治党
paras: An Yufeng takes up Xi Jinping's statement that starting with Party conduct to advance full and rigorous self-governance of the Party is an important lesson of the Party's self-reform in the new era. Published in Guangming Daily on 24 July 2025, the commentary argues that conduct is the Party's image, bears on public support, and decides the success of the Party's and the country's undertakings. An holds that the eight-point regulation adopted after the 18th Party Congress (2012) opened up the whole field of conduct building.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out why conduct building matters. The second turns to methods and requirements. The third describes practical paths for carrying it forward. It draws on the Yan'an-era contrast between the Yan'an and Xi'an styles, on Xi's remarks about the eight-point regulation, and on a list of Party education campaigns since 2012.

An argues that conduct problems are in essence problems of Party spirit, and that their core is the Party's relationship with the people. The author therefore ties conduct to ideals and convictions, to serious inner-Party political life, and to the mass line. On method, An calls for linking the rectification of conduct, the enforcement of discipline and the fight against corruption, and for making these efforts routine and long-term through institutions. The author also proposes strict management systems and a framework to make officials unwilling, unable and afraid to be corrupt. On practice, An urges rigorous implementation of the eight-point regulation and sustained correction of the “four undesirable work styles” (formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance). Leading officials are to set an example, including in family conduct, so that good Party conduct lifts social and popular customs.

An concludes that conduct building must be sustained and pursued from the top down, with leaders acting as a “lead goose”. Local bodies are to treat public satisfaction as the measure of improvement. The author also calls for a healthy political ecology and “amicable yet clean” relations between government and business. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of how Party-affiliated scholars present conduct building within Party self-governance.
quoteEn: Problems of conduct are, in essence, problems of Party spirit.
quoteZh: 作风问题本质上是党性问题。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A policy slogan since the 18th Party Congress (2012) for stricter Party discipline, anti-corruption work and internal supervision, and one of the 'Four Comprehensives'.
A term in Xi Jinping-era discourse for the Party's claimed capacity to correct its own faults and tackle corruption without outside pressure.
Rules adopted by the Politburo in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism among officials, covering matters such as meetings, travel and receptions.
Formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, targeted by the Party's campaign against improper conduct since 2012.
A Party working method, rooted in the Mao era, of drawing ideas from the people and returning them as policy; the Party describes it as its lifeline.

glossary.pinyin: bù gǎn fǔ, bù néng fǔ, bù xiǎng fǔ
glossary.en: unwilling, unable and afraid to be corrupt
glossary.literal: dare not, cannot, do not want to be corrupt
glossary.explanation: An official three-part anti-corruption formula combining deterrence, institutional constraint and moral-ideological education.

t: The distinctive contributions of women delegates to the CPC's Seventh National Congress during the War of Resistance against Japan
zh: 党的七大女性党代表在抗战中的独特贡献
paras: Zhuang Qiuju, in a short piece for the Chinese Social Sciences Today (July 2025), asks what the women delegates to the Seventh National Congress of the Communist Party of China (1945) contributed to the War of Resistance against Japan. The author argues that, despite differing ages, origins and schooling, these women played an important role on every front of the war.

The article opens with a profile of the 52 women delegates, 18 of them alternate delegates, who made up 6.9 per cent of all delegates. Zhuang gives their average age as 33, notes that they came from 14 provinces, that about 37 per cent had peasant family backgrounds and that 52 per cent had secondary schooling. It then treats their work under two headings: strengthening the fight against the Japanese, and promoting national unity in resistance.

On the first, Zhuang describes women who fought at the front, built base areas and guerrilla units, and joined anti-"mopping-up" campaigns, citing Li Zhen, Liu Yaxiong and An Jianping. Others gathered intelligence and moved funds and supplies underground, such as Wei Gongzhi, who helped bring a large sum raised by the Communist International from Shanghai to Xi'an. On the second, Zhuang says the delegates ran propaganda, mobilised workers' groups and united influential figures in the united front. They paid particular attention to women: according to the author's incomplete count, 44 of the 52 worked in women's organisations.

Zhuang concludes that the women delegates acted as an independent force in the resistance, whose contributions to fighting, base-area construction and final victory are indelible. The piece is a stage result of a National Social Science Fund project on the history of the Party's marriage policy. Read the original if you want a concise, example-rich account of how Chinese scholarship presents women Party delegates' wartime roles and the biographical details behind it.
quoteEn: The women delegates to the Seventh Congress acted as an independent force in resisting the Japanese invaders.
quoteZh: 七大女性党代表作为抗击日寇的一支独立力量

glossary.explanation: The wartime policy, promoted by the CPC after 1931, of uniting different classes, parties and groups against Japanese aggression.

t: The Seventh Party Congress and the building of the Party's work style
zh: 党的七大与党的作风建设
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 24 July 2025
paras: Zhou Liangshu, a professor at Peking University's School of Marxism, argues in this newspaper commentary that the Seventh Party Congress (1945) was a milestone in the history of the Communist Party's work style. In Zhou's account, the "three major work styles" that Mao Zedong summed up and established there laid a foundation for victory in the new-democratic revolution. They also pointed the way for building a Marxist ruling party after that victory.

The piece first explains why the Congress met in 1945, 17 years after the Sixth. It traces the delay to war and then to the Yan'an rectification movement and the study of the Party's history, which produced the first "historical resolution". It then shows how the Congress combined review of the past with a forward-looking line, and finally turns to the three work styles and Mao's plain-language formulation of them.

Zhou identifies three points on which the Party leadership had reached consensus about Party building: democratic centralism, unity among comrades, and leading by example, especially in self-criticism, where Mao criticised his own mistakes before the Congress. The three work styles are integrating theory with practice, maintaining close ties with the masses, and criticism and self-criticism. The Congress wrote them into the Party constitution for the first time. Mao also put them in everyday terms as telling the truth: "no stealing, no pretending, no boasting", meaning no plagiarism, no feigned knowledge and no inflated reports.

Zhou concludes that Mao both summarised and practised these styles, citing his calls for modesty, prudence and wholehearted service to the people, and his Foolish Old Man story. On this basis Zhou holds that the Seventh Congress marks a boundary stone in the history of Party work style. Read the original if you want a short, officially aligned account of how the 1945 Congress is presented in Party-history writing on work style.
quoteEn: The "three major work styles" are the concentrated expression of the nature and purpose of the Chinese Communist Party and a distinctive mark separating it from other parties.
quoteZh: “三大作风”是中国共产党性质和宗旨的集中体现，是党区别于其他政党的显著标志。

glossary.explanation: The Party's traditional style of work: integrating theory with practice, close ties with the masses, and criticism and self-criticism. They were written into the Party constitution at the Seventh Congress in 1945.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Communist Party, combining discussion and democratic input with unified decisions and discipline.
A Central Committee resolution that gives an authoritative verdict on Party history. The first, in 1945, was the Resolution on Certain Questions in the History of Our Party.
A campaign launched in Yan'an from 1941–42 to unify the Party's thinking, criticising subjectivism and sectarianism.

t: Reform and innovation to drive high-quality development of state-owned enterprises
zh: 改革创新推动国企高质量发展
paras: This short commentary, published in Economic Daily in July 2025, asks how deeper reform and innovation can push state-owned enterprises (SOEs) towards high-quality development. Fan and Chen argue that SOEs are a material and political foundation of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and that strengthening them is necessary for serving Chinese modernization.

The authors take as their basis the Decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which calls for stronger, better and bigger state capital and SOEs. They note that reforms since the 18th Party Congress (2012) have improved layout, innovation capacity and efficiency, but identify remaining problems: incomplete modern enterprise systems, weak asset structures and unfinished upgrading. They propose three areas of action.

First, the authors call for improving the modern enterprise system: clearer powers and responsibilities among governance bodies, Party leadership built into every stage of corporate governance, flatter and more market-responsive management, reformed incentives and tolerance-of-error rules, and smarter supervision. Second, they urge SOEs to focus on their main business and to concentrate state capital in the "three concentrations": national security and the economic lifeline, public services, and forward-looking strategic emerging industries. Third, they argue SOEs should be the main force in scientific and technological innovation, acting as hubs and "chain leaders" that integrate resources, fund basic and frontier research, and act as patient capital.

The authors conclude that these measures would strengthen supply-chain security, raise SOEs' core competitiveness and support a modern industrial system and a technologically strong country. They also support cooperation between SOEs and private firms through industrial alliances. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official policy agenda for SOE reform after the Third Plenum.
quoteEn: SOEs are the main force in scientific and technological innovation.
quoteZh: 国企是科技创新的主力军。

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation of China's development path, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022), which stresses features such as a huge population, common prosperity and peaceful development.
An official goal, emphasised since 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to growth driven by innovation, efficiency and better structure.
The official name for China's political and economic system since the reform era, combining Party leadership, public ownership as the mainstay and a socialist market economy.
A policy formula from the Third Plenum Decision directing state capital towards national security and key sectors, public services and strategic emerging industries.

t: Party conduct and image-building of the Communist Party during the nationwide War of Resistance
zh: 全民族抗战时期党的作风建设与形象展示
paras: Yue Kui asks how the Communist Party of China built up its own conduct and public image during the nationwide War of Resistance against Japan (1937–45), and what this achieved. The newspaper commentary argues that, faced with Japanese aggression, Nationalist die-hards' anti-communism and prejudice abroad, the Party strengthened its self-construction, especially its conduct (zuofeng). In Yue's account, this raised its cohesion, appeal and fighting capacity and produced rapid growth in its strength.

The piece is organised in four sections. They cover the Party's people-centred orientation and its political and organisational character; legal and democratic construction in the Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region; discipline and clean governance; and the united front, military struggle and propaganda at home and abroad. It draws on Party documents, Mao Zedong's writings and episodes from Yan'an, and cites a US Army observer's remark about the Communists.

Yue's central claim is that conduct and image reinforced each other. The author points to the Party's self-definition from 1935 as the vanguard of both the proletariat and the whole nation, the rectification campaign against subjectivism, sectarianism and Party formalism, and the Yan'an hospital and epidemic-prevention campaigns as evidence of serving the people wholeheartedly. Border-region legislation, universal suffrage for adults over eighteen, the "three-thirds" system and assemblies are presented as guarantees of people's democratic rights. Strict discipline is illustrated by the executions of Huang Kegong and Xiao Yubi, which Mao said served to educate the Party. Yue adds that newspapers such as Xinhua Daily and Liberation Daily, an international propaganda committee and visits by foreigners to the border region spread this image.

Yue concludes that the Party became the mainstay (zhongliu dizhu) of national resistance and presented itself as hardworking, resolute, united with the masses, democratic and progressive. In the author's reading, this image demonstrated strong governing capacity and vitality, gave hope for national salvation and won international support. Read the original if you want a concise example of how current Party-history writing presents wartime conduct, discipline and propaganda as sources of the Party's authority.
quoteEn: The Party vigorously strengthened its own construction and established the image of a party that was hardworking, resolute, united with the masses, democratic and progressive, demonstrating strong governing capacity and vitality.
quoteZh: 我们党大力加强自身建设，树立起艰苦奋斗、坚韧不屈、团结大众、民主先进的政党形象，展现出强大的执政能力和生命力

glossary.explanation: A Party term for cultivating members' and cadres' style of work and behaviour, such as honesty, closeness to the masses and discipline. It is a long-standing part of Party building.
An idiom, used in Party historiography, for the Communist Party's claimed leading role in the resistance to Japan. Mao Zedong used it in 1938.
The cooperation between the Communists, Nationalists and other groups against Japan, formed after the Xi'an Incident of 1936. The Party also used it as a general strategy of alliance-building.
A power-sharing arrangement in the anti-Japanese base areas. Communists, non-Party progressives and middle-of-the-road figures each held about one third of seats in government bodies.
The Party-wide ideological campaign launched in Yan'an in the early 1940s against subjectivism, sectarianism and Party formalism.

t: Passing the Long March spirit down the generations
zh: 让长征精神代代相传
paras: Du Fanding, who led the drafting of the Long March National Cultural Park plan, takes stock of the park's first six years. Writing as the 90th anniversary of the Long March's victory approaches, Du argues that the project has begun to deliver results. In the author's account, it preserves the physical carriers of the Long March spirit, interprets them vividly and uses them for Party-style education.

The newspaper commentary is organised in three parts: protection of resources, interpretation of the spirit, and red education. It draws on examples from provinces along the route, which the 2021 plan brought together across 15 provincial-level units. It describes the park as the only one of the five national cultural parks built around a revolutionary spirit.

On protection, Du reports that the number of immovable Long March relics has grown from over 1,600 to 2,000. The newly recognised sites include historic road remains, and relics are now identified as a group around major events, as at the Xiang River battle site. Du also cites the 2022 designation of "red grasslands" to give the crossing of the grasslands a material basis. On interpretation, the article lists research publications, a museum alliance, stage dramas, digital exhibitions and documentaries. On education, it points to Party schools, cadre academies and "Great Ideological and Political Course" classes, plus study routes where students make straw sandals and carry stretchers. Du says one Yibin county project has received 220,000 visitors since 2021.

Du concludes that future work should be cautious yet innovative and should seek methods that suit current needs. The aim is a protection, display and transmission system that reflects national will, standards and image and enjoys international esteem. Du presents this as the way to keep the Long March spirit a lasting source of motivation. Read the original if you want an insider's overview of how a flagship heritage and red-education project is being implemented, with concrete local examples.
quoteEn: In future, we must still uphold the principle of being proactive yet prudent and pioneering, and explore construction methods that meet the needs of the times.
quoteZh: 未来，仍需秉持积极稳妥、开拓创新的理念，探索符合时代需求的建设方法

glossary.explanation: A state-planned heritage zone linking relics and cultural resources along the Red Army's Long March route across 15 provincial-level units. It is one of five national cultural parks, and its plan was issued in 2021.
The Party's term for the values it attributes to the Red Army's Long March of 1934–36, such as firm ideals, sacrifice and reliance on the people. It is regularly invoked in Party history education.
Education that uses revolutionary history, sites and memorials to instil Party ideals and patriotic values.
An initiative to extend ideological and political education beyond classrooms by drawing on social practice and local resources, including red heritage sites.

t: Cultivating the Communist's "learning of the mind" begins with firm ideals and convictions
zh: 修炼共产党人“心学”首在坚定理想信念
paras: This short commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in July 2025, takes up Xi Jinping's call for Party members to cultivate a Communist "learning of the mind" (xinxue), unifying study, thought and practice, and knowledge, belief and action. Chen Yanbo argues that this cultivation starts with firm ideals and convictions, which steady the will, temper resolve and raise fighting spirit.

The piece is organised in three steps, each borrowing a concept from the Ming thinker Wang Yangming. It treats ideals as the "first-rate matter" of a Communist, firmness of conviction as "training through affairs", and fighting spirit as the "unity of knowledge and action".

Chen contends that the Party differs from other parties in being organised around shared ideals rather than shared interests, so joining it means making those ideals one's own life priority. On this reading, the Party's survival of setbacks rests on its lofty aims, and the Communists who founded New China held firm to the aim of saving the nation through Marxism. Firm conviction, the author says, is never spontaneous or permanent. It must be renewed over a lifetime, and the anti-corruption cases of recent years show to Chen that political, economic, moral and lifestyle degeneration begins with loss of ideals. The author links firm conviction to loyalty and strong Party spirit, and describes it as the "special material" that resists corruption.

Chen concludes that, facing growing risks, Communists with firm convictions will recognise their historical mission, stay confident in communism and in socialism with Chinese characteristics, and develop the capacity to struggle. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party-building writing draws on Neo-Confucian heart-mind philosophy to discuss ideological discipline.
quoteEn: Firm ideals and convictions do not arise spontaneously, are not achieved in one stroke, and are certainly not settled once and for all: being firm in the past does not mean being firm now, and being firm now does not mean being firm in the future.
quoteZh: 坚定的理想信念不是自发产生的，也不是一蹴而就的，更不是一劳永逸的，过去坚定并不意味着现在坚定，现在坚定并不意味着将来坚定。

glossary.explanation: A school of Neo-Confucian thought associated with Wang Yangming, stressing self-cultivation and the unity of knowledge and action. Xi Jinping has used the term for the inner discipline expected of Party members.
A principle from Wang Yangming holding that true knowledge is inseparable from practice. It is used in Party discourse to urge that belief be matched by conduct.

t: Grasping the distinctive features of the system of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
zh: 把握全面从严治党体系鲜明特征
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in July 2025, asks how to understand the system of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Li presents it as a dynamic system that is rich in content, fully equipped, scientific and efficient, and as a product of theoretical, practical and institutional innovation in Party building in the new era. The author argues that it must be read through systems thinking, by identifying the features of each of its five sub-systems.

The article takes its structure from Xi Jinping's speech at the 15th collective study session of the Political Bureau of the 20th Central Committee. That speech named five components: organisational, education, oversight, institutional and responsibility systems. Li devotes one section to each and pairs each with two features.

Li assigns rigour and connectedness to the organisational system, citing coverage of central, local and grassroots levels, of new economic and social organisations and of new employment groups, and the use of digital tools. Continuity and integration describe the education system, with its regular and intensive study and its mechanisms such as the "three meetings and one lesson". Guidance and coordination mark the oversight system, in which intra-Party supervision is linked to the Party's self-supervision and to supervision by the people. Wholeness and effectiveness describe the institutional system, and clarity and layering the responsibility system. Li reads the last as a closed loop of assigning, performing, questioning and pursuing responsibility, which is meant to stop pressure from weakening as it passes down the hierarchy.

Li concludes that these paired features together make up the systemic character of the whole and that each sub-system must be understood through its own practical requirements. The article is a brief interpretive gloss on Xi's speech rather than an empirical study. Read the original if you want a compact, official-style outline of how Chinese Party scholars classify the components of Party-building policy.
quoteEn: Effectiveness is the key yardstick for judging how an institutional system is operating, and an important indicator for guiding its further development and improvement.
quoteZh: 实效性是评价制度体系运转状态的关键尺度，也是引导制度体系实现进一步发展完善的重要指标。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: A policy line associated with Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It covers discipline, anti-corruption, ideological education and institutional rules for Party members and organisations.
A basic system of Party branch life: regular branch meetings, branch committee meetings, small group meetings and Party lectures.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: The history of the War of Resistance as a living "great ideological and political course"
zh: 抗战史是生动的“大思政课”
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 22 July 2025, Shen Youhong takes up Xi Jinping's recent call, made during a visit to the Hundred Regiments Offensive memorial hall in Shanxi, to tell the story of the War of Resistance well and pass the great spirit of resistance down the generations. Shen's thesis is that the history of the war is itself a living "great ideological and political course" for young people, and that this spirit should shape a new generation able to shoulder national rejuvenation.

This short commentary, timed to the 80th anniversary of victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War, first describes the war and the spirit it produced. It then sets out three tasks in education: deepening historical understanding, elevating patriotic feeling, and turning the spirit into practice.

On historical understanding, Shen cites the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army, the Pingxingguan victory and the Hundred Regiments Offensive, and proposes red cultural resources and VR reconstructions to teach the Communist Party's pivotal role and the spirit's world significance. On values, Shen holds that patriotism is the core of the spirit, that it echoes the core socialist values, and that young people should move from "historical memory" to "value consciousness". On practice, Shen points to the united front and tactical innovations such as tunnel and mine warfare as examples of practical wisdom.

Shen concludes that young people should carry on a practical, hard-working spirit, take initiative and innovate in reform and development, and so contribute to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the memory of the anti-Japanese war is framed in Chinese official education discourse in 2025.
quoteEn: The history of the War of Resistance is in itself a living "great ideological and political course".
quoteZh: 抗战史本身就是一堂生动的“大思政课”

glossary.explanation: A slogan for ideological and political education that extends beyond the classroom to social practice and real-world resources such as history and memorial sites. It is promoted in Chinese education policy.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping and the Chinese Dream.
A set of twelve values promoted officially since 2012, covering the national, social and individual levels, including prosperity, democracy, patriotism and integrity.

t: Grasping the interactive logic between the Party's self-reform and social revolution
zh: 把握党的自我革命与社会革命的互动逻辑
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in July 2025, asks how the Party's self-reform and social revolution relate to each other. Liang Haifeng argues that the two are dialectically unified and mutually reinforcing, and that together they drive the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Liang presents a "double revolution" in dynamic balance as a strategic requirement for keeping the Party vital.

The article first treats self-reform as the Party's key instrument for leading social revolution, citing Xi Jinping and the campaigns of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party since 2012. It then argues that the results of social revolution are the ultimate test of self-reform. Finally it turns to Party conduct as the link between the two, and to the problems still facing it.

Liang cites economic scale, manufacturing capacity and poverty alleviation, including the lifting of nearly 100 million people out of poverty, as evidence that self-reform works. In the other direction, Liang says problems in social development, such as formalism and bureaucratism, expose weaknesses in Party building that self-reform must address. Conduct building is described as a hub: it purifies the Party and turns that purity into practical strength for social revolution, including a closer bond with the people.

Liang concludes that formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance still erode the Party's credibility and the popular base of social revolution. The author calls for conduct building to be pursued with persistence over the long term, supported by stronger institutions. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party-building scholarship currently links internal discipline to national development goals.
quoteEn: Conduct building acts as a hub, turning the purity and advanced nature forged by self-reform into a powerful practical force for social revolution, so that the two connect and reinforce each other.
quoteZh: 作风建设如同枢纽，将自我革命锻造的纯洁性、先进性转化为推动社会革命的强大实践力量，使两者相互贯通、协同促进。

glossary.explanation: A term stressed under Xi Jinping for the Party's efforts to correct its own faults, fight corruption and maintain discipline without outside pressure.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the campaign, pursued since 2012, to tighten Party discipline, combat corruption and improve Party conduct.
Used here for the broad transformation of society and the building of socialism under Party leadership, rather than an overthrow of the existing order.
Party campaigns to improve cadres' work style and behaviour, aimed at problems such as formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Applying and governing artificial intelligence in basic education
zh: 人工智能在基础教育领域的应用及治理
paras: Wang Jia asks how artificial intelligence (AI) can serve fair, high-quality basic education while its ethical, privacy and security risks are kept in check. Opening with Xi Jinping's calls to integrate AI deeply with education and to teach AI at every school stage, the article argues that basic education, as the starting point of talent cultivation, offers real opportunities but needs early, deliberate governance. It is a short commentary from Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao), 2025, no. 13.

The piece has three parts. The first describes what AI changes in basic education: ideas and models of teaching, the structure and ecology of education, and the balance of resources. The second sets out three risks: over-reliance on AI, misleading values, and the dissolution of the educational community. The third proposes five governance strategies, from legislation to international exchange.

On benefits, Wang says AI tools can personalise learning content, shift goals from transmitting knowledge to building overall capacities, help teachers and parents through diagnostic reports, and carry top teachers' courses to remote mountain areas. Predictive analysis of enrolment and teacher needs, and multimodal generation for deaf students, are said to advance educational equity. On risks, Wang argues that stress on AI literacy may crowd out other capacities, and that students may lose independent and critical thinking. Algorithms may carry developers' value preferences and create "information cocoons", particularly in education on national conditions and political identity. More human–machine interaction may weaken the teacher's role, and opaque algorithms may endanger minors' data and privacy.

Wang calls for specific legislation on AI in basic education, building on the Interim Measures for Generative AI Services and the Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online, plus ethical guidelines. Wang also proposes multi-level content review involving platforms, third-party bodies and education authorities, AI training for teachers and age-graded AI literacy courses for pupils, and pilot demonstration zones under inclusive and prudent regulation. Finally, China should take part in setting international rules and standards and offer "Chinese solutions" to raise its influence. Throughout, the article holds that AI must serve the basic questions of whom to train, how and for whom. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Central Party School scholar frames AI in schooling in Party-policy terms, with a list of regulatory measures.
quoteEn: AI has injected new momentum into the reform and development of basic education, continually driving innovation and restructuring of the educational ecosystem and bringing unprecedented opportunities, but because the development and application of technology cuts both ways, it inevitably faces many risks and challenges.
quoteZh: 人工智能为基础教育的改革与发展注入了新动力，通过赋能教、学、评、研、管等教育场景，持续推动教育生态的创新与重构，带来前所未有发展机遇，但由于科技发展应用的双刃性，也不可避免地面临诸多风险挑战。

glossary.explanation: A Party-theory journal published under the Qiushi Journal group, carrying commentary on policy and ideology.
A term for the narrowing of a user's information intake by personalised recommendation algorithms, so that they meet only reinforcing content.
An official regulatory approach that tolerates experimentation with new technologies and business models while monitoring risks.

glossary.zh: 培养什么人、怎样培养人、为谁培养人
glossary.pinyin: péiyǎng shénme rén, zěnyàng péiyǎng rén, wèi shéi péiyǎng rén
glossary.en: whom to train, how and for whom
glossary.literal: what kind of people to train, how to train people, for whom to train people
glossary.explanation: A formula used by Xi Jinping for the fundamental questions of education: what kind of people to cultivate, how to cultivate them and in whose service.

t: Telling the story of whole-process people's democracy in practice
zh: 讲好全过程人民民主实践故事
paras: This short commentary argues that vivid stories of the Communist Party's democratic practice can make the breadth and effectiveness of whole-process people's democracy tangible. Zhou holds that such storytelling helps break Western dominance of democratic discourse, strengthens the international voice and image of Chinese democracy, and offers what the article calls Chinese wisdom to developing countries seeking their own democratic paths.

The piece is organised around three claims: that whole-process people's democracy is the most broad, the most genuine and the most effective democracy. Each section ties one quality to a question (democracy of whom, what kind of democracy, what democracy is for) and ends with suggestions for how the story should be told in the new era.

On breadth, Zhou says the model rejects elite-led democracy and covers all people regardless of ethnicity, occupation, region or class, with rights running through elections, consultation, decision-making, management and oversight. On authenticity, the article describes a closed loop from expressing demands to policy and evaluation, so that popular consent becomes continuous rather than a momentary grant at elections. On effectiveness, Zhou presents democratic centralism as converting institutional strengths into governance capacity, citing consultative decision-making, crisis mobilisation and grassroots governance.

Zhou proposes legal clarification of participation rights, digital channels, blockchain-based traceability, big-data analysis of public opinion, constitutional safeguards and a theory of democratic effectiveness. The conclusion is that institutional innovation, technological empowerment and cultural cultivation should advance together. Read the original if you want a concise example of how this democratic model is framed for international communication in Chinese academic writing.
quoteEn: The breadth of whole-process people's democracy is rooted in the essential Marxist attribute of 'people-centredness'.
quoteZh: 全过程人民民主的广泛性，植根于马克思主义“人民性”这一本质属性。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2019 and promoted since as the defining feature of China's socialist democracy. Official accounts stress that democracy extends beyond elections to consultation, decision-making, management and oversight.
The organisational principle of the Communist Party and state organs, combining discussion with unified decision and discipline. The article presents it as a source of governance effectiveness.

t: What kind of self-cultivation Communists need
st: Revisiting Liu Shaoqi's "How to Be a Good Communist"
zh: 共产党人要有什么样的修养
zhSub: 重温刘少奇《论共产党员的修养》
paras: Why should Communist Party members still read Liu Shaoqi's 1939 lecture on self-cultivation, and what does it ask of them? This short commentary, first published in Study Times in July 2025, revisits the text and argues that it remains relevant to Party members and cadres today. Ding Junping contends that it can help them keep the Party's purpose in mind and settle questions of worldview, outlook on life and values.

The lecture was delivered in July 1939 at the Marx-Lenin Institute in Yan'an and is included in the first volume of Liu's Selected Works. Ding cites Xi Jinping's remark that it enriched Party-building theory and educated generation after generation of Communists. The commentary follows the lecture in three steps: why cultivation is necessary, what its content is, and how Marxism-Leninism should be studied. It closes with lessons for the present.

Ding reports that Liu begins from historical materialism: people change nature and so change themselves, and Communists, as the most advanced revolutionaries, must reform themselves while reforming society. Cultivation matters most in times of success, Liu warns, since some members become arrogant, bureaucratic and corrupt after victory. Its content covers theory, political and strategic ability, moral character, discipline, work style, ties with the masses and general knowledge. It must not be abstract or detached from practice, and its only aim is to serve the people and the revolution. Ding stresses Liu's view that theoretical study and cultivation of a proletarian standpoint depend on each other. Liu criticises reciting phrases and conclusions, and calls for combining universal truth with the concrete practice of the country's revolution.

Ding concludes that, under full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and the new great project of Party building, every member still needs to strengthen their training and cultivation. The author calls for serious study of the Party's innovative theory, especially Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and for unity of knowing, believing and doing. Members should do their own jobs conscientiously and so contribute to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a brief, official-style account of how Liu's text is presented in current Party-building discourse.
quoteEn: Revisiting this text yields many insights.
quoteZh: 重温这篇文献，能够获得诸多启示。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: A Party-building policy associated with Xi Jinping since 2012. It stresses discipline, anti-corruption work and ideological training within the Communist Party.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The official name for China's path of modernization, which the Party presents as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A long-term national goal that the Party has stressed since the early 2010s, often tied to the Chinese Dream.

t: Small matters and minor details as the "touchstone" for testing Party spirit
zh: 小事小节是检验党性的“试金石”
paras: Liu Junjie, in a commentary first published in Study Times in July 2025, takes up a question of Party discipline: why do so many violations of discipline and law begin with matters that officials dismiss as trivial? Citing Xi Jinping's remark that small matters reflect character and style and contain Party spirit, principle and personality, Liu argues that holding the line on discipline is both a requirement of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and a basic guarantee of the Party's vanguard character and purity.

The article is organised around the functions Liu assigns to the "red line" of discipline. It is first the foundation of the Party's work style, then the first barrier against lawbreaking, then a means of cutting the chain of corruption, and finally the "guardian" of public trust. It draws heavily on Xi's statements, including his address to the Fourth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection on 6 January 2025, and ties its closing section to the current study and education campaign on implementing the central Eight-point Regulations.

Liu's central claim is that decline is gradual. Neglected small matters weaken Party spirit and produce a "broken windows" effect. The author describes a three-stage path from breaking discipline to breaking the law (weak discipline awareness, then chancing a breach of the red line, then total collapse) and a parallel path from lax style to power-for-rent-seeking to systemic corruption. Against this, Liu defends the principle that discipline must be stricter than law and come before it, since Party discipline is a high standard and law a bottom line. Liu proposes combining deterrence ("dare not"), institutions such as power lists and conduct rules ("cannot"), and cultivated conviction through Party-spirit education ("do not want"). Liu also urges investigating and addressing style problems and corruption together.

Liu concludes that officials should treat small matters as the touchstone of Party spirit, oppose formalism and bureaucratism, avoid extravagance and waste, and so build the first line of defence against corruption and degeneration. The stated aim is to ensure that central decisions take root at the grassroots and to secure public trust and the Party's governing base. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party media present the link between everyday conduct, discipline inspection and anti-corruption policy in 2025.
quoteEn: The red line of discipline is both a "firewall" against problems of work style and a "sluice gate" that cuts off corrupt conduct.
quoteZh: 纪律红线既是作风问题的“防火墙”，也是腐败行为的“截流闸”。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping's leadership since 2012, covering Party discipline, anti-corruption and Party-building. It is one of the "Four Comprehensives".
A figure for the limits of conduct set by Party rules and discipline, which members must not cross.

glossary.pinyin: jì yán yú fǎ, jì zài fǎ qián
glossary.en: discipline must be stricter than law and come before it
glossary.literal: discipline stricter than law, discipline ahead of law
glossary.explanation: A principle in Party discipline work that Party members are held to standards higher than the law, so that violations are dealt with before they become legal offences.
Rules adopted by the Central Committee's Political Bureau in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism among officials.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Improving investigation and research requires attention to methods
zh: 改进调查研究应重视方式方法
paras: This newspaper commentary argues that investigation and research (diaocha yanjiu) is the Party's "family heirloom" and a basic skill for all work, and that its methods and style need to be improved. Zhao Yong notes that Xi Jinping has stressed the practice since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and that the first of the Central Committee's eight-point regulations concerns improving it. The author holds that deepening it serves Party conduct, leadership capacity and long-term governance.

The piece has three parts. The first concerns problem awareness and a problem-oriented approach. The second concerns a systematic outlook and scientific methods. The third concerns improving work style and avoiding formalism.

On the first, Zhao says the task is to establish the facts, identify the real problem and put forward practicable countermeasures. Conclusions should follow investigation, the principal contradiction should be addressed first, and findings should be turned into concrete measures and then tracked and assessed. On method, the author calls for unity of "going in person" and "engaging the mind", of field and online investigation (big data, sampling surveys), and of investigation and analysis. On style, Zhao rejects showcase-style research. The author urges precise topic selection rather than following trends, and unannounced visits under the "four no's, two straight" approach so that officials hear real views. The author also urges travelling light with fewer accompanying staff and simpler reception.

Zhao concludes that research done this way will produce reliable information and workable policies, and that officials should learn from the people. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style statement of how Party cadres are expected to conduct investigation and research in the Xi Jinping era.
quoteEn: Investigation is the premise and foundation of research, and research continues and deepens investigation; the purpose of investigation is to enable better research, and research is for solving problems better.
quoteZh: 调查是研究的前提和基础，研究是调查的继续和深化；调查的目的是更好地进行研究，研究则是为了更好地解决问题。

glossary.explanation: A method of fieldwork and analysis associated with Mao Zedong's "no investigation, no right to speak". The Party treats it as a core working method for cadres and policy-making.
Rules on official conduct adopted by the Politburo in December 2012. They aim to curb formalism, extravagance and bureaucratism, and the first concerns improving investigation and research.
In Party discourse, a style of work that stresses appearances and procedure over practical results, such as staged site visits.
A method of unannounced inspection: no prior notice, no briefing, no reception arrangements and no accompanying officials. Inspectors go directly to the grassroots and directly to the problem site.

t: The string of self-reform must be drawn tighter
zh: 自我革命这根弦必须绷得更紧
paras: This newspaper commentary takes up Xi Jinping's remark, made at the 21st collective study session of the 20th Politburo, that the Party's tasks are heavy, its governing environment is exceptionally complex, and the string of self-reform must be drawn tighter. Wang argues that this reflects the Party leadership's historical responsibility and sense of risk, and that continuous self-reform is the Party's defining trait and greatest strength.

The piece first recalls that the Party has corrected its course through self-reform at each major historical juncture. It then sets out the pressures of the present: the tasks of Chinese modernization and a turbulent international and domestic environment. It closes with four practical measures and a reference to the current campaign to study and implement the central Eight-point Regulation.

Wang's central claim is that the Party's spirit, leadership and governing capacity bear directly on whether Chinese modernization succeeds. Whether the Party passes this test depends on its willingness to purify, improve, renew and strengthen itself. Since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the author says, full and rigorous self-governance of the Party has resolved many problems, but solving the difficulties peculiar to a large party is long-term work with no room for fatigue.

The proposed measures are to consolidate ideological foundations through theoretical education, perfect institutions that restrain and supervise power, keep up a high-pressure stance against corruption with zero tolerance, and motivate officials, including through tolerance of error and correction mechanisms. Wang concludes that the Party must keep the strict tone for the long term so that it remains the core of leadership for socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary justifies sustained Party discipline in 2025.
quoteEn: Ideological development is the Party's foundational work and the master switch of self-reform.
quoteZh: 思想建设是党的基础性建设，是自我革命的总开关。

glossary.explanation: A term Xi Jinping stresses for the Party's ability to correct itself, purge corruption and renew itself without outside pressure. It is presented as a defining feature of the Communist Party of China.
The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, promoted prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official label for the Party-discipline and anti-corruption drive intensified since 2012, covering ideology, organisation, conduct and institutions.
Rules adopted by the Central Committee in December 2012 to curb officials' extravagance, bureaucratism and formalism. Periodic campaigns of study and education are built around them.

t: Party building leading the construction of modern people's cities
zh: 党建引领现代化人民城市建设
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 17 July 2025
paras: Responding to the 2025 Central Urban Work Conference, this newspaper commentary asks how modern people's cities should be built. Yang argues that Party building is the fundamental guarantee: only by upholding the Party's overall leadership and a performance outlook that puts the people first can urban construction keep a clear direction and draw on co-building, co-governance and sharing.

The piece has three parts. It first sets out the people's-city concept as the guiding direction, then identifies current problems in urban development and governance, and finally lists measures for strengthening Party leadership over urban work.

Yang names three challenges: fragmented governance and weak coordination between departments, grassroots bodies overburdened and under-resourced, and poor cooperation between government and society, with limited institutional channels for participation. In the author's view, these can be solved only through Party building, all the more so as urbanization shifts from large-scale expansion to improving existing urban stock. The proposed measures include a Party-committee-led governance system, a three-tier street–community–grid structure of Party organizations, "smart Party building plus smart city" tools, whole-process people's democracy at the grassroots, and revised cadre evaluation that rewards residents' sense of gain, happiness and security rather than growth speed.

Yang concludes that Party leadership must run through every field and stage of urban planning, construction and governance so that policy is not distorted. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars link urban governance reform to Party building after the 2025 conference.
quoteEn: Party leadership is the fundamental guarantee and greatest strength of building people's cities, and it must run through every field and the whole process of urban construction.
quoteZh: 党的领导是人民城市建设的根本保证和最大优势，必须贯穿城市建设的全领域全过程。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2019 describing China's democracy as covering every stage of decision-making, not only elections.
An urban-development concept associated with Xi Jinping's statement that "cities are the people's cities, built for the people", stressing the people's principal role in urban development.

glossary.literal: jointly build, jointly govern, jointly share
glossary.explanation: An official formula for social governance in which multiple actors jointly build and govern and share the results.
A grassroots governance method that divides a locality into small grid units, each with assigned staff responsible for services and problem-solving.

t: Persistently strengthening the Party's work style
zh: 锲而不舍加强党的作风建设
source: China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News, 17 July 2025, p. 5
paras: Writing in July 2025, after Xi Jinping's remarks at the 21st collective study session of the Political Bureau, Zhu Lingjun and Shan Boya ask how the Party's work style (zuofeng) should be built up and kept up. They argue that the Party's self-reform is the "second answer" to the question of how to escape the historical cycle of rise and fall. In their account, starting from work style is an important experience of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party in the new era. The piece appeared in the China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News and is a short commentary.

The authors organise the discussion in three parts. The first traces the theoretical sources of the concept: classical Chinese ideas of "wind" (feng) as custom and moral influence, remarks by Marx, Engels and Lenin on the habits of proletarian parties and on bureaucratism, and the statements of Chinese Party leaders from Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping to Xi Jinping. The second reviews historical experience under six headings, running from ideological style to discipline. The third describes the practice of the new era since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

The core claim is that work style has been a continuous thread in the Party's history and a mark of its nature and purpose. Its historical forms, in the authors' account, include seeking truth from facts, linking theory with practice, close ties with the masses, honesty and integrity, plain living and hard struggle, appointing people on merit under democratic centralism, and discipline as a guarantee. For the new era, Zhu and Shan describe a sequence of measures that began with the eight-point regulation of the Central Committee in December 2012. The measures include leadership by example, concentrated education campaigns, immediate rectification, institutional reform, and strict standards. They say these were aimed at formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance (the "four undesirable work styles"), and that results were published monthly for 141 consecutive months up to June 2025.

The authors conclude that work-style building must be made routine and long-term, so that the cycle of "tighten and it improves, relax and it rebounds" is broken. They call for continued study of Xi's statements, a persistently strict tone, and the current education campaign on the eight-point regulation. Read the original if you want a concise official account of how Party scholars link work-style rectification to Chinese tradition, Marxist classics and the post-2012 anti-formalism campaign.
quoteEn: Making work-style building routine and long-term requires stable institutions and mechanisms built on strict standards, and a constant signal that discipline enforcement grows stricter over time.
quoteZh: 推进作风建设常态化长效化，需要以严的标准形成稳定的体制机制，不断释放越往后执纪越严的信号。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan of the Xi Jinping era for a campaign of stricter Party discipline, anti-corruption work and internal supervision.
A formulation stressing that the Party should correct its own errors and problems without external pressure. Xi Jinping presents it as an answer to the historical cycle of rise and decline.
Rules adopted by the Political Bureau in December 2012 on improving work style and ties with the masses. They limit official meetings, travel, receptions and extravagance.
The four faults targeted by the post-2012 campaign: formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance.
A principle associated with Mao Zedong and reaffirmed by Deng Xiaoping in 1978, treated as the core of the Party's ideological line.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Party, combining discussion and decision-making by members with unified discipline and subordination to higher bodies.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Letting the Jinggangshan spirit radiate new light for our times
zh: 让井冈山精神放射出新的时代光芒
source: China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News (Zhongguo jijian jiancha bao), 17 July 2025, p. 8
paras: Written in the year of the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japan (2025), this newspaper commentary asks how the Jinggangshan spirit, formed in the revolutionary struggle of the late 1920s, should be carried forward in the present. Luo argues that it is a lasting asset in the Communist Party's "spiritual genealogy" and that it must be given new meaning under today's conditions.

The piece opens by linking the Party's role in the anti-Japanese war to a lineage of spirits that begins with the great founding spirit of the Party. It then moves through three sections: how the Jinggangshan struggle produced the spirit, where the spirit sits in the genealogy, and four practical requirements for the new era. The commentary was published in the Party's discipline inspection newspaper in July 2025.

In the first section Luo traces the spirit to four sources. These are firm ideals and convictions after the failures of 1927, when Party membership fell from nearly 60,000 to just over 10,000, and a seeking of truth from facts that led to a rural-centred revolutionary road despite doubts from the Comintern and Stalin. The other two are hard struggle under blockade, and reliance on the masses. In the second section Luo presents the spirit as inheriting the founding spirit and shaping the Soviet Area, Long March, Yan'an and anti-Japanese war spirits. The same section extends the line to the Dazhai, Daqing, reform and opening up and poverty-alleviation spirits.

For today Luo calls for four things: holding to communist ideals and the common ideal of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and keeping to one's own path guided by seeking truth from facts. Luo also calls for continued Party conduct building under the Central Committee's eight-point regulations, and a people-centred approach built on the mass line. Luo says conduct building has produced marked results over more than ten years but must continue. Read the original if you want an example of how Party-school and discipline-inspection commentary links revolutionary-era memory to current Party-building tasks.
quoteEn: The Jinggangshan spirit is a great revolutionary spirit that the Party formed through struggle by combining the basic principles of Marxism with the concrete realities of the Chinese revolution.
quoteZh: 井冈山精神是我们党把马克思主义基本原理与中国革命具体实际相结合，在斗争中孕育而成的伟大革命精神。

glossary.zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系
glossary.explanation: A list of named revolutionary and construction-era "spirits" (such as the Jinggangshan, Long March and Yan'an spirits) that the Party presents as a continuous heritage. The first batch was set out by the Central Publicity Department in 2021.

The Party's name for the values attributed to the Jinggangshan base area struggle of 1927–1929, summarised by Xi Jinping as firm conviction, hard struggle, seeking truth from facts, daring to blaze new trails, and reliance on the people.
