Rules on official conduct adopted in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucracy among Party officials.
A Party principle, associated with Mao Zedong, of drawing on the views of ordinary people and relying on them in policy and work.
A core element of the Party's ideological line, stressing that policy should proceed from actual conditions rather than dogma.

t: Classic translation and the paths of theory dissemination in the Yan'an period
zh: 延安时期的经典翻译与理论传播路径
paras: Liu Shuo asks how the translation of Marxist classics in Yan'an (the Party's wartime base) worked as a means of theory dissemination. The article argues that this was not mere linguistic conversion but a composite process joining text production, dissemination and practical guidance. In Liu's account it moved Marxism from the study to the battlefield and set the principle of linking theory with practice for the Party's news and communication work.

The short piece, published in the China Social Sciences Today in July 2025, covers three mechanisms: organised translation and editing, popularised communication, and the practical conversion of theory. It then turns to localisation, to mass participation in theory study, and to the international reach of the "Yan'an experience". It closes with lessons for the present.

Liu describes an institutional system: a translation and editing department at the Marxist-Leninist Institute (1938), a Military Commission translation office, and a 1939 Central Committee directive on propaganda and printing. Dissemination used Party newspapers, publishers, and also yangge operas, wall newspapers and leaflets that rendered class theory as colloquial slogans. Liu holds that converting terms such as "working class" into peasant-centred expressions, and recasting the city-centred path as "encircling the cities from the countryside", marked a shift from literal translation to problem-oriented communication.

Liu concludes that Yan'an translation was a successful exploration of how the Party used communication to secure ideological leadership. For the era of all-media, Liu draws three lessons: theory should address Chinese problems, rest on popular participation and dialogue, and pursue mutual learning among civilisations. Liu also urges online and offline study, new-media lectures, and multilingual translation of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era under the Belt and Road Initiative. Read the original if you want a brief, official-line view of Yan'an translation as a model for present-day theory communication.
quoteEn: Translation practice in the Yan'an period proved that the vitality of theory dissemination lies in its deep integration with the local context.
quoteZh: 延安时期的翻译实践证明，理论传播的生命力在于与本土语境的深度融合。

glossary.explanation: A China-led international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative announced by Xi Jinping in 2013.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

t: The theoretical implications of grasping the "critical few"
zh: 抓住“关键少数”的理论意蕴
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily on 16 July 2025, asks what theoretical significance lies in Xi Jinping's repeated call to "grasp the critical few" (关键少数), meaning leading cadres. Zhang argues that this body of statements is an innovation in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and that it displays the distinctive theoretical features of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The piece is a short theoretical commentary, not an empirical study.

The article begins with the 20th Party Congress (2022) report, which links the "critical few" to the Central Committee's eight-point regulation, the correction of the "four undesirable work styles" and the fight against privilege. It defines the group and then proceeds in two parts. The first part sets out five ways the idea advances Marxist theory. The second part identifies five features of Xi Jinping Thought that it displays: being of its time, people-centred, systematic, dialectical and practical.

On the first part, Zhang says the idea refines the historical-materialist view of the relation between the masses and leaders, defines the group concretely (senior cadres, "top leaders" of each unit, and county Party secretaries), and extends Marxist thinking on power through power lists, accountability and supervision. It also enriches methods of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Zhang reads Xi's formula of managing "all" Party members while concentrating on senior cadres as an application of Marxist contradiction analysis, combining the "emphasis on key points" with the "two-sided view". On the second part, the author links each feature to Xi's statements, for example the "people-centred" quality to the claim that cadres come from the people and serve them. The author also says the approach draws on traditional Chinese governance ideas such as "leading from above" and "governing the state begins with governing officials", as an instance of the Two Integrations.

Zhang concludes that grasping the "critical few" means grasping the key point of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and of national governance, since "the Party must govern itself, beginning with its cadres". The author calls for action on political development, strict selection and appointment, better assessment and a fuller supervision system, so that cadres set an example in advancing Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party theory presents cadre discipline and leadership responsibility as a Marxist, Xi Jinping Thought-based method.
quoteEn: The Party must govern itself, and the first task is to manage its cadres well; the key to full and rigorous self-governance of the Party is strict management of officials.
quoteZh: 党要管党，首先是管好干部；全面从严治党，关键是从严治吏。

glossary.explanation: Phrase used by Xi Jinping for leading cadres, especially senior officials and top leaders of units, whose conduct is held to shape that of the wider Party and society.

t: A deep understanding of the value of upholding the Party's cultural leadership
zh: 深刻理解坚持党的文化领导权的价值意蕴
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 15 July 2025, Zhang Beiping takes up Xi Jinping's statement that the "most essential feature" of the path of socialist cultural development with Chinese characteristics is upholding Party leadership. The article argues that upholding the Party's cultural leadership (wenhua lingdaoquan) is a core element of Xi Jinping's thinking on culture and a necessary requirement of the Party's mission in the new era. Zhang's thesis is that its strategic significance and value can be understood in four dimensions.

The commentary is organised in four numbered sections: strengthening cultural confidence by safeguarding the Marxist "soul" and the "roots" of Chinese civilisation; consolidating the cultural foundation by serving people's livelihood and winning hearts; building cultural security through confrontation and defence; and displaying the value of civilisation through exchange and integration. It ends with a short summary stating that Party cultural leadership is the fundamental guarantee for building a socialist cultural power.

In the first section Zhang links cultural confidence to cultural subjectivity, which the article presents as strengthened by the Two Integrations, and calls for an autonomous Chinese body of knowledge to dispel the myth that "Westernisation equals modernisation". The second section argues that no modern state or party can lead effectively without a value system that unites people. It points to public cultural provision and mass events such as "village evening galas" and the "Village Basketball Association", as well as digital technologies. The third section claims that Western powers hold "cultural hegemony" and use "colour revolutions" to undermine governments. Zhang proposes three responses: upholding fundamental principles while innovating, telling China's story well, and strengthening discursive struggle against what the article calls the "China threat" and similar narratives. The fourth section rejects ranking civilisations and presents online exchanges between Chinese and American users, and a foreign influencer's tour of China, as examples of two-way cultural empowerment.

Zhang concludes that only by upholding the Party's cultural leadership can socialist culture become the shared values and ideological base of the whole nation and a force for national rejuvenation. The author presents this as enabling China to take on a new cultural mission and to contribute to a new form of human civilisation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party commentary in mid-2025 links cultural leadership to cultural confidence, ideological security and international communication.
quoteEn: Upholding the Party's cultural leadership is the fundamental guarantee for building a socialist cultural power.
quoteZh: 坚持党的文化领导权是建设社会主义文化强国的根本保证。

glossary.explanation: The Party's authority over cultural and ideological work. The term echoes Gramsci's idea of hegemony and is used in Chinese Party writing for Party leadership over culture.
Xi Jinping's formula of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. The second integration was added in 2023.
A slogan promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012), meaning confidence in the value and vitality of China's own culture. It is often counted as part of the Four-sphere Confidence.
The official goal of building China into a country with strong cultural influence and soft power. It was set as a target for 2035 by the 20th Party Congress.

t: The Communist Party of China as the mainstay of the nation-wide War of Resistance
zh: 中国共产党是全民族抗战的中流砥柱
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japan, Zhang Taiyuan asks in what sense the Communist Party of China (CPC) was the "mainstay" (zhongliu dizhu) of the whole nation's resistance. The article argues that the victory was a victory of the entire nation and, above all, one in which the CPC played this pivotal role. It was published in the Party journal Red Flag Manuscripts in 2025.

The piece is organised in four sections, each ending with a lesson for the present. They cover the Party's line and strategy of protracted war, its promotion and defence of the anti-Japanese national united front, its guerrilla warfare and base areas behind enemy lines, and the spirit of resistance forged by its members and fighters. Zhang draws on Party declarations from 1931 to 1937, Mao Zedong's writings, military statistics and accounts of individual martyrs and heroes.

Zhang contends that the Party gave the resistance its direction through the line of all-out resistance set at the Luochuan Meeting (1937) and the strategy in Mao's On Protracted War (1938), which held that mobilising the people was the root of victory. The Party then initiated and upheld the united front with the Kuomintang, even after the Southern Anhui Incident, and so held the alliance together. On the military side, the article cites figures for the Eighth Route Army, the New Fourth Army and the Party-led base areas: the Party-led rear-area battlefields are said to have faced 58–62 per cent of Japanese forces in the stalemate stage, and over the war to have eliminated about 1.714 million Japanese and puppet troops and established 19 base areas. The article presents these results as the concrete form of the Party's pivotal role. It also describes the courage of figures such as Yang Jingyu, Deng Yufen and the Five Heroes of Langya Mountain, presented as expressions of patriotism, unyielding integrity and conviction of victory.

Zhang concludes that history teaches the need to uphold the Party's overall leadership, to consolidate the broadest patriotic united front, to rely on and mobilise the people, and to treat the great spirit of resistance as a resource for national rejuvenation. The article links these lessons to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and to Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want an example of how a Central Party School historian presents the CPC's role in the War of Resistance in the official narrative of 2025, with its figures and chosen examples.
quoteEn: Without the Communist Party there would have been no nation-wide anti-Japanese united front, and without the anti-Japanese national united front there would have been no nation-wide resistance.
quoteZh: 没有中国共产党就没有全民族的抗日统一战线，没有抗日民族统一战线就没有全民族抗战

glossary.explanation: An idiom for a steadfast force that holds firm amid turmoil. Party historiography uses it to describe the CPC's role in the War of Resistance, and Mao Zedong used it in a 1941 inner-Party directive.
The broad alliance, centred on CPC–Kuomintang cooperation, that was formally established in 1937 to resist Japan. Official history credits the CPC with initiating it.
Mao Zedong's 1938 strategy, set out in On Protracted War, which foresaw three stages: strategic defence, stalemate and counter-offensive.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since it was written into the Party Constitution in 2017.

t: Resolving prominent problems of work style with the spirit of self-reform
zh: 以自我革命精神解决作风方面突出问题
paras: Tang Junfeng takes up the Party-wide study and education campaign on thoroughly implementing the spirit of the Central Committee's eight-point regulation, launched in 2025. The article argues that the campaign should be carried out in the spirit of the Party's self-reform, and that tackling work-style problems, which Xi Jinping calls an important historical lesson, is a way of advancing full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

The piece is a commentary built in three parts and draws heavily on Xi Jinping's statements. The first part explains how the eight-point regulation, issued after the 18th Party Congress (2012), enriched the means of self-reform. The second sets out how to conduct the current campaign. The third discusses how to make work-style building a regular and lasting task.

In the first part, Tang identifies four features of the regulation: it is an iron rule with no "trial" label, it relies on leadership by example from the Political Bureau downwards, it combines tough enforcement with long-term persistence, and it keeps close ties with the people. According to the author, before 2012 lax Party governance allowed formalism, bureaucracy, hedonism and extravagance to persist, and the regulation curbed practices once thought impossible to stop. The second part calls for tempering Party spirit, since work style is at root a matter of Party spirit. It also calls for rectifying the "four undesirable work styles", observing discipline and practising honest, pragmatic action. The third part proposes integrating study, self-examination and rectification, handling Party spirit, work style and discipline together, and combining individual self-discipline with oversight by Party organizations and the masses.

Tang concludes that the campaign is time-limited but that implementing the regulation has no end point. Tang calls for turning external requirements into inner motivation and for building regular, long-term mechanisms. Work style is presented as a question of the Party's bond with the people and of its long-term rule. Read the original if you want a representative example of how Party-school commentary presents the eight-point regulation and the 2025 campaign in terms of self-reform.
quoteEn: The core of the work-style problem is the relationship between the Party and the people.
quoteZh: 作风问题的核心是党同人民群众的关系问题。

glossary.explanation: A set of rules adopted by the Political Bureau in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucracy among officials. It covers matters such as meetings, official travel, receptions and contact with the public.

A concept in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse for the Party's continuous correction of its own failings. It is presented as the second answer to the question of how to escape the historical cycle of rise and decline.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the campaign to tighten Party discipline and anti-corruption efforts, promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
The official shorthand for formalism, bureaucracy, hedonism and extravagance, the targets of the Party's work-style rectification campaigns.

t: Continuously achieving the Party's self-purification and self-renewal
zh: 不断实现党的自我净化和自我革新
paras: Writing in Beijing Daily (14 July 2025), Li Zhongjie reflects on more than a century of Party conduct building (zuofeng jianshe) in the Communist Party of China. Starting from Xi Jinping's warning that Party style bears on the Party's image, on public support and on its very survival, Li argues that such work is a permanent task through which the Party achieves self-purification and self-renewal.

The short commentary is organised as five "reflections". They deal with Party style as an expression of the Party's nature, the need to treat style as a matter of survival, the open-ended character of the work, the answer to the historical cycle of rise and fall, and the balance between purity and vitality.

Li defines Party style as the Party's observable image and a "barometer" of its nature, purpose and relationship with the people. Good style signals vigour; bad style signals disease. Citing Xi that style problems are stubborn and recurrent, Li holds that work on them is always "on the road". Li presents two historic answers to the question of how to escape the historical cycle: Mao Zedong's "new path of democracy", with the people supervising government, and Xi's Party self-reform, which the 20th Party Congress (2022) tied to the claim that anti-corruption is the most thoroughgoing self-reform.

Li concludes that full and rigorous self-governance of the Party must purify the Party without making it lifeless. Quoting Xi, Li says the aim is a healthy political ecology in which people get things done, so that society is both orderly and vibrant. Persistent work on Party style is said to let the Party keep the initiative under any conditions. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official rationale for Party conduct building, as presented by a senior Party historian.
quoteEn: The Party's style is the Party's image.
quoteZh: 党的作风，就是党的形象。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since 2014, covering discipline, anti-corruption and Party conduct. It is presented officially as a comprehensive system of Party management.

glossary.en: historical cycle of rise and fall
glossary.explanation: The pattern in which dynasties and regimes flourish and then decline. It is associated with a 1945 exchange between Mao Zedong and Huang Yanpei.
Efforts to improve the Party's work style, including study, writing, meetings, leadership and personal conduct.

t: The mission and path of comprehensively deepening reform in social science work at universities
zh: 高校社科工作全面深化改革的使命与路径
paras: This commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today on 14 July 2025, asks how university social science work should respond to the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which set out the direction for further comprehensively deepening reform and advancing Chinese modernization. Li Xiaobing argues that universities must take Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as their guide and uphold the Two Integrations, so as to move philosophy and social sciences to a new level.

The piece is organised under three headings: consolidating theoretical foundations and building a knowledge system; engaging in social practice to serve national development; and cultivating new-era talent while inheriting and renewing culture. Each contains several concrete tasks for university social scientists.

On the first, Li holds that the Two Integrations supply the methodological guidance: researchers should keep Marxism as the "soul" while drawing on excellent traditional Chinese culture as the "root". Li also calls for building an autonomous Chinese knowledge system by balancing "upholding fundamental principles" and innovation, and for interdisciplinary work. On the second, Li urges stronger think tanks and a "government, industry, academia, research and application" collaboration mechanism, deeper use of big data and artificial intelligence (for example through humanities labs), and reformed evaluation that rewards quality, contribution and integrity.

On the third, Li calls for teaching that integrates theory and practice, produces socialist builders and successors, and strengthens cultural confidence through cultural exchange. Li concludes that such work should supply intellectual support for building a community with a shared future for mankind and serve national strategy. Read the original if you want a short example of how a university Party leader frames the tasks of social science work after the Third Plenum.
quoteEn: In building an autonomous knowledge system, university social science workers must correctly handle the dialectical relationship between "upholding fundamental principles" and "innovation".
quoteZh: 高校社科工作者要在构建自主知识体系中正确处理“守正”与“创新”的辩证关系

glossary.explanation: A formulation in Party theory: combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture. It was prominently stated in Xi Jinping's 2021–2023 speeches and the 20th Party Congress report.
The official name for China's path of modernization, presented since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng

glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, stressing shared interests and joint global governance.

glossary.en: government, industry, academia, research and application
glossary.explanation: An official model of collaborative innovation linking government bodies, enterprises, universities, research institutes and end users.

t: The victory in the War of Resistance against Japan as a great victory of the national spirit with patriotism at its core
zh: 抗日战争胜利是以爱国主义为核心的民族精神的伟大胜利
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of the victory in the War of Resistance against Japan, this commentary in Qiushi, attributed to the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, takes up Xi Jinping's statement that the victory was a great victory of the national spirit with patriotism at its core. It argues that this spirit was the decisive factor in the war and that the Communist Party of China turned popular patriotic feeling into a historical force.

The text has three parts. The first traces how patriotism, described as the heart of the Chinese national spirit, was awakened after the Opium War of 1840 and reached a new height after the September 18th Incident of 1931. The second examines the Party's role in the war. The third sets out how the spirit should be promoted today through publicity, education, the internet and scholarship.

The core argument in the second part holds that without a vanguard party, simple patriotic feeling could drift into narrow nationalism or blind xenophobia. According to the article, the Party gave patriotism a new content by making national independence and liberation its first task. It was the first to call for armed resistance in 1931 and to declare war on Japan in 1932. It also promoted the Anti-Japanese National United Front, leading to the second Kuomintang–Communist cooperation. The article further credits the Party with relying on and mobilising the people, through the idea of protracted war and guerrilla warfare, so that the conflict became a true people's war, which it calls the fundamental reason for victory. Communist-led forces are said to have fought at the front at great sacrifice, and the article cites a figure that they tied down 58–75 per cent of Japanese forces in China after the stage of strategic stalemate began.

The article concludes that the spirit must be carried forward. It calls for publicity on the Party's pivotal role and on China's contribution as the main Eastern theatre of the world anti-fascist war. It urges patriotic education that focuses on young people and links the war's history with Party history, and says new media should be used. It also calls on philosophy and social science to build a Second World War discourse system and to rebut distortions of history. This effort is tied to national rejuvenation under Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want an authoritative Party-journal statement of how the war's history and spirit are framed for patriotic education and historical research in 2025.
quoteEn: The victory in the War of Resistance was not only the recovery of the land but also the recovery of hearts and the remoulding of the spirit; its history is not only a history of war but also a history of the spirit and of the heart.
quoteZh: 抗日战争的胜利，不仅是河山光复，更是人心光复、精神重塑；抗日战争的历史，不仅是战争史，更是精神史、心灵史。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path of modernisation, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). The article links patriotic unity to advancing it.

glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: An official goal of restoring China's strength and standing after the 'century of humiliation'. The article presents the anti-Japanese war as a turning point on the way to it.
The broad alliance of parties and social groups formed against Japan in the 1930s, including the second Kuomintang–Communist cooperation.
The 1931 incident at Shenyang that led to Japan's occupation of Northeast China, treated in China as the start of the 14-year resistance war.

t: Keeping secrets is a glorious tradition and fine work style of the Party
zh: 保守秘密是党的光荣传统和优良作风
source: Chinese Discipline Inspection and Supervision News, 10 July 2025, p. 8
paras: Zhang Jianjun's commentary, published in the Chinese Discipline Inspection and Supervision News on 10 July 2025, argues that protecting Party and state secrets is both a concrete expression of Party discipline and a glorious tradition and fine work style of the Party. It is prompted by the revised Law on Guarding State Secrets, which took effect on 1 May 2024. Zhang holds that recalling how Mao Zedong, Zhou Enlai, Deng Xiaoping and other older revolutionaries practised secrecy helps carry that tradition forward today.

The piece is a short historical-exemplary essay organised under three headings, each introduced by a quotation from Xi Jinping: firm ideals and absolute loyalty to the Party; strict observance of confidentiality discipline; and leading by example so that secrets are kept safe. Each section is built from anecdotes and recollections about Mao, Deng Xiaoping, Ren Bishi, Chen Yun, Deng Yingchao, Zhou Enlai and Liu Shaoqi. A brief closing passage turns to present-day tasks.

In the first section, Zhang recounts the narrow escapes of Mao and Deng during underground work in the 1920s, and Ren Bishi's refusal to reveal his identity under torture in 1929. Zhang presents these as proof that such figures valued protecting Party secrets above their own lives. The second section cites Chen Yun's writings on Party discipline, Deng Yingchao's account of Zhou Enlai telling her nothing before leaving to lead the Nanchang Uprising, and Mao's telegrams ordering secret documents burned before the Southern Anhui Incident and during the Huaihai Campaign. The third section shows leaders enforcing secrecy within their own households: Liu Shaoqi's rule of not saying, asking or reading what one should not, even in front of his children, and Chen Yun's refusal to tell his wife in advance of a price change in 1962 or 1963.

Zhang concludes that, facing a broader and more complex national security environment, the Party should apply the holistic approach to national security and promote high-quality development of confidentiality work. In Zhang's view, this work bears on the Party's long-term governing position, national security, people's wellbeing and national rejuvenation, and should contribute to building a strong country through Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a sample of how official Party media use revolutionary-era anecdotes to teach confidentiality discipline to cadres.
quoteEn: Through long years of struggle, the older generation of revolutionaries came to understand the extreme importance of strict discipline, above all the Party's confidentiality discipline, and held to strictness first and unflagging caution.
quoteZh: 老一辈革命家经过长期斗争实践,深知严守纪律特别是严守党的保密纪律的极端重要性,坚持严字当头、慎密不怠。

glossary.en: the holistic approach to national security
glossary.explanation: A security concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2014 that treats security as covering politics, economy, culture, society, technology and other fields together.
An official slogan, prominent since 2017, for a growth model stressing quality, efficiency and innovation over speed alone. Here it is applied to confidentiality work.
The official term for the Party's path of national development, set out in the 20th Party Congress report (2022).
Official shorthand for the goal of restoring China to a strong and prosperous position, usually phrased as the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

t: Furthering comprehensively deepening reform in the spirit of historical initiative
zh: 以历史主动精神进一步全面深化改革
source: China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News (Zhongguo jijian jiancha bao), 10 July 2025, p. 5
paras: He and Xue take up the question of how the Communist Party of China can carry reform further after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). Their answer is that the Party must keep up what they call the spirit of historical initiative, a distinctive ideological strength of Marxist parties. They argue that this spirit is the key to deepening reform and advancing Chinese modernization.

The piece, a commentary in a Party discipline newspaper, has three parts. It first traces historical initiative through the new-democratic revolution, socialist construction, reform and opening up, and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It then sets out the internal logic by which this spirit guides reform. Finally it draws practical requirements for the new journey.

The central move is a three-part account of the spirit's content. Historical self-awareness, meaning accurate knowledge of laws, stages and trends, supplies theoretical initiative and answers where initiative is heading. A clearly identified historical subject, the people, supplies practical strength and answers who realises it. Historical responsibility supplies spiritual drive and answers how it is realised. The authors present reform and opening up as the Party's active "breaking of the deadlock" and the post-2013 comprehensively deepening reform as active "construction". On this reading, historical initiative reached a new height in the new era.

The authors make three proposals. The Party should grasp the trend of the times, anchoring reform to the overall goal of improving socialism with Chinese characteristics and modernizing national governance. It should also keep its political foundation by strengthening Party leadership, fostering a fighting spirit and pursuing the Party's self-reform. Finally it should hold to the people's standpoint, uniting Party leadership with the people's principal role and combining top-level design with grassroots exploration. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party commentary links the concept of historical initiative to the reform agenda set out in 2024.
quoteEn: The spirit of historical initiative is the ideological driving force with which the Communist Party of China grasps the situation and plans scientifically at major historical junctures, and a powerful weapon for turning crises into opportunities and overcoming hardships.
quoteZh: 历史主动精神是中国共产党在重大历史关头把握时势、科学谋划的思想驱力，也是化危为机、攻坚克难的强大武器。

glossary.explanation: A concept in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse describing the Party's capacity to grasp historical laws and trends and act on them proactively. It was prominent in the 2021 Party resolution on history and later speeches.
The official name for the Party's model of modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022) as the path to national rejuvenation.
Official term for the Party's efforts to purify, improve and renew itself, presented as the Party's answer to the problem of historical cycles of rise and decline.

t: Continually dusting off the mind
zh: 不断掸去思想上的灰尘
paras: This short commentary asks how Party members and cadres should deal with the ideological problems behind misconduct. Yue starts from Xi Jinping's remark that the Party's prominent problems are, at root, problems of thinking. The article argues that the current campaign of study and education on the central Eight-point Regulation is a chance for self-examination and correction, so that cadres can dust off their thinking and correct deviant behaviour.

The piece is a brief exhortatory essay in a Party journal, apparently written as part of that campaign. It moves from diagnosis, which covers where ideological 'dust' comes from, to two remedies: inner steadfastness and regular criticism and self-criticism. It draws on classical Chinese sayings, an anecdote about the Yuan-dynasty scholar Xu Heng, and a passage from Mao Zedong.

Yue holds that formalism, bureaucratism, shirking responsibility and the hidden, mutated forms of the 'four undesirable work styles' all come down to wavering ideals, weak awareness of the Party's purpose, distorted values and the influence of subjectivism, utilitarianism and hedonism. The first remedy is resolve of the kind Xu Heng showed in declining to pick pears from an ownerless tree: 'the pear tree has no owner, but my heart has one'. The second is criticism and self-criticism, which Yue presents, following Mao, as sweeping and washing away dust, and which calls for openness to sharp criticism.

Yue concludes that style problems are at bottom problems of Party spirit. Party spirit and moral standing, in Yue's view, do not improve automatically with age, length of service or promotion, so members must keep up self-cultivation, self-restraint and self-reform. They should measure themselves against Party style, Party spirit and Party discipline to keep the political character of Communists. Read the original if you want a short example of how Party journals frame ideological self-cultivation within the Eight-point Regulation campaign.
quoteEn: Problems of work style are, in essence, problems of Party spirit.
quoteZh: 作风问题本质上是党性问题。

glossary.explanation: A set of rules on official conduct adopted by the Party's Political Bureau in December 2012. They aim to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism among officials.
A Party term for formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance. It was prominent in the mass-line campaign launched after 2012.
A long-standing Party method of internal correction in which members point out one another's faults and examine their own.
The ideological and moral qualities expected of a Party member, including loyalty to the Party's principles and discipline.

t: The CPC-led resistance behind enemy lines as seen in Japanese private sources
zh: 日本民间资料所见中国共产党领导的敌后抗战
source: China Social Sciences Net / Chinese Social Sciences Today, 9 July 2025
paras: This short commentary asks what privately held Japanese records reveal about the Chinese Communist Party's leadership of the war of resistance behind Japanese lines. Zhang argues that regimental and battalion histories, veterans' memoirs and wartime interviews show how Japanese officers themselves explained their failure, and that they placed the Party's mobilisation of the people at the centre.

The article draws on Japanese military and private materials, including an internal army document titled The Operations of the Chinese Army, statements by staff officers such as Inomoto Kumao and Matsumura Tomokatsu, the memoir of Tokutsu Junichi, a regimental history, and a lecture by Prince Mikasa. It moves from Japanese misjudgements of Chinese resistance, to the role of the敌后 (behind-the-lines) front, to the contest for popular support.

Zhang reports that Japanese officers widely believed China was a divided nation lacking national consciousness, and expected a short war. According to the sources cited, the Japanese army later conceded that events followed the Communist account of a three-stage protracted war, and that occupied land became 'Communist territory'. Zhang stresses accounts attributing Communist strength to ties with the people: a North China Area Army estimate of at least 500,000 unarmed civilians aiding the Communist forces, Tokutsu's 'fish and water' image, and Prince Mikasa's contrast between Communist discipline and Japanese plunder.

Zhang concludes that these Japanese sources, read as the opponents' own testimony, show that winning popular support decided the outcome and that the Party-led resistance behind enemy lines changed the course of the war. Read the original if you want a brief overview of the Japanese-language testimony that Chinese historians now use in studying the anti-Japanese war.
quoteEn: In practice the Japanese army gradually came to realise that the contest for popular support was the key to deciding victory or defeat in the war.
quoteZh: 日军在实践中逐渐认识到，民心的争夺是决定战争胜负的关键。

t: The Communist Party of China's role as the mainstay was the key to victory in the Chinese people's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression
zh: 中国共产党的中流砥柱作用是中国人民抗日战争胜利的关键
authors: Party School of the CPC Central Committee (National Academy of Governance) Committee
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression, this commentary from the Central Party School's governing committee takes up Xi Jinping's formulation that the Communist Party's role as the mainstay (zhongliu dizhu) was the key to victory. It also treats victory as the Party's own triumph in that role. The authors present this as a settled historical conclusion and as a basis for upholding the Party's overall leadership today.

The text is organised in five sections, each naming one source of the Party's decisive role. These are political leadership and sound strategy, the anti-Japanese national united front, the great spirit of resistance, standing on the side of justice and human progress, and Party building. Each section ends by drawing lessons for the present. These are tied to the Two Establishes, the Two Upholds and Chinese modernization.

The authors argue that the Party first identified the contradiction with Japanese imperialism as the principal one. It then developed the strategy of protracted war and opened the battlefields behind enemy lines. They cite figures: Party-led forces fought over 125,000 engagements, wiped out 1.714 million Japanese and puppet troops, and built 19 base areas with nearly 100 million people. They say the Party promoted peaceful resolution of the Xi'an Incident and the second Kuomintang–Communist cooperation. It held to "resist, unite, progress" against three anti-Communist high tides. In their account, patriotism-centred national spirit, a "cultural army" and the Party's internationalist stance connected China's front to the global anti-fascist war. They add that the Yan'an rectification movement and the Party-building "great project" of 1939 made the Party cohesive enough to lead.

The authors conclude that the Party's leadership is the most essential feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics and its greatest institutional advantage. They call for the Party to keep strengthening its political leadership and the united front, to carry forward the spirit of resistance, and to reject distortions of Second World War history and hegemonism. They also call for continued full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, which they say has found a "second answer" to the historical cycle of rise and fall. Read the original if you want an authoritative example of how Party-school theorists link the memory of the anti-Japanese war to current claims about Party leadership and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
quoteEn: The War of Resistance was a contest of material strength, and even more a confrontation of spirit.
quoteZh: 抗日战争是物质的角力，更是精神的对垒。

glossary.literal: the pillar standing in the midstream
glossary.explanation: A metaphor for a force that stays firm amid turbulence. In Party historiography it describes the Communist Party's claimed role in the anti-Japanese war, a formulation Xi Jinping has repeated.
A formula adopted in 2022 that affirms Xi Jinping's position as the Party's core and the guiding status of Xi Jinping Thought.
The political requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Party and the authority and centralised leadership of the Central Committee.
The official name for China's development path, described by the Party as distinct from Western models. It has been central to Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The broad alliance of parties, classes and groups against Japan. Its core was the second Kuomintang–Communist cooperation, formed in 1937.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The campaign since 2012 to tighten Party discipline and fight corruption.

t: Party conduct in the new era, seen through the victory of the "Yan'an style" over the "Xi'an style"
zh: 从“延安作风”打败“西安作风”看新时代党的作风建设
paras: Wang Yongjie takes up Xi Jinping's remark that Mao Zedong and other older revolutionaries in Yan'an defeated the "Xi'an style" with the "Yan'an style". The commentary asks what this history means for Party conduct today. Wang's thesis is that the eight-point regulations of the Central Committee (2012) continue the Yan'an style while adapting it to new conditions, and that both keep the Party's close ties with the people.

The article, a newspaper commentary published in Guangming Daily in July 2025, has three parts. The first recounts Mao's 1940 conversation and sets out four features of the Yan'an style. The second presents the eight-point regulations as the new era's version of that tradition, and the third turns to institution-building and long-term practice. Wang links the piece to the current Party-wide study and education campaign on the eight-point regulations.

Wang defines the Yan'an style as honest and clean government, close links with the masses, and theory tied to practice, and contrasts it with the Kuomintang's "Xi'an style" of extravagance, pleasure-seeking and detachment from the people. The four features are a firm political direction, the fundamental purpose of serving the people wholeheartedly, the ideological line of emancipating the mind and seeking truth from facts, and self-reliance with hard struggle. For the present, Wang argues that a people-centred stance requires curbing formalism, bureaucracy, hedonism and extravagance, which Xi likens to a wall between Party and people. Wang also argues that leading cadres, the "critical few", must set the example, and that unhealthy conduct and corruption share roots and must be investigated and handled together.

Wang concludes that Party conduct must be made routine and lasting, because such problems recur and resist change. Wang calls for firm, long-term enforcement, rigid institutions, cultivation of Party spirit, conduct and discipline together, and good family discipline among officials so that Party style lifts social customs. Wang presents this as a safeguard for national rejuvenation and for full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Read the original if you want an official Party-school account of how current conduct campaigns are tied to the Yan'an legacy.
quoteEn: The spirit of the Central Committee's eight-point regulations continues the "Yan'an style" of eighty years ago in the new era, preserving its core while innovating.
quoteZh: 中央八项规定精神是对80年前“延安作风”在新时代的赓续传承和守正创新

glossary.explanation: A set of rules adopted by the Central Committee in December 2012, shortly after the 18th Party Congress, to curb officials' extravagance, bureaucratic habits and formalism. They are the base of the Party's anti-"four undesirable work styles" campaign.
The Party's conduct in its Yan'an base in the 1930s–40s, described as frugal, honest and close to the masses. Mao Zedong contrasted it with the Kuomintang's "Xi'an style".
A phrase for leading cadres, who are held to set the tone for Party and social conduct through their example.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's drive since 2012 to tighten discipline, fight corruption and improve internal governance.

t: Party discipline and conduct building of the Communist Party of China during the full-scale War of Resistance
zh: 全面抗战时期中国共产党的纪律和作风建设
orig: China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News, 3 July 2025
source: China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News, 3 July 2025, p. 5
paras: Jin Minqing, writing in the Party discipline newspaper China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News (July 2025), asks what the Communist Party of China learned about discipline and conduct (zuofeng) during the full-scale War of Resistance against Japan (1937–45). The author argues that the Party's explorations in this period helped forge it into a politically, ideologically and organisationally mature Marxist party able to lead national resistance, and that these experiences still offer lessons today.

The article is built in three parts. The first treats discipline as the guarantee of the political line and of the authority of the Party Central Committee. The second treats close ties with the masses as the core of conduct building, with the Yan'an Rectification Movement as its main example. The third covers the harsh punishment of corruption and crime, and the way the Party summed up its experience in theory and institutions. Cases include the Wang Ming affair, Huang Kegong and Xiao Yubi.

Jin's central claims are as follows. First, discipline serves the line: the author cites Mao Zedong's formulas that discipline is the guarantee of carrying out the line and that the line is the 'kingly way' and discipline the 'hegemonic way', both indispensable. Discipline in turn means upholding central authority and unified leadership, which the author illustrates with the removal of Wang Ming's Yangtze Bureau and with the 1942 decision on unified, 'integrated' Party leadership in the base areas. Second, conduct building combined work on a 'critical few', senior cadres who set an example, with the 'vast majority'. The author describes this through the Yan'an rectification, the 1943 decision on leadership methods (the mass line) and the 1941 decision on investigation and research. Third, the executions of Huang Kegong and Xiao Yubi, both veterans, show that no special persons were exempt, and Jin says they consolidated the bond with the people.

Jin concludes that the Party turned this experience into theoretical and institutional innovation. Mao set out the content of Party conduct and the three fine styles (integrating theory with practice, close ties with the masses, self-criticism). The Sixth Plenum documents set out the 'four obediences', and the Seventh Congress (1945) Party constitution wrote discipline into its general programme as an organisational foundation. Jin presents the joint handling of conduct, discipline and anti-corruption as an enduring method of Party building. Read the original if you want a concise official-academic account of how wartime Party history is used to frame discipline and conduct building today.
quoteEn: The practice of coordinating and jointly advancing the rectification of conduct, the enforcement of discipline and the fight against corruption, first formed during the full-scale War of Resistance, has through long development and enrichment become an important working method of Party building.
quoteZh: 全面抗战时期初步形成的这种正风肃纪反腐相互协同、一体推进的工作做法，经过长时间的发展和丰富，已经成为党的建设的重要工作方法。

glossary.explanation: A Party-wide ideological education campaign launched in 1941–42 in the Yan'an base area under Mao Zedong. It targeted subjectivism, sectarianism and 'Party formalism' (stereotyped writing).

The Party's working method of gathering the views of the masses, concentrating them into policy and returning to the masses to test them. The 1943 decision on leadership methods gave it its classic formulation.
A term for leading cadres whose example is held to shape the conduct of the whole Party. It is used here with the image of the 'lead goose' effect.
The principle, set out in a 1942 decision, that in each base area a single Party committee leads the army, government and mass organisations.
Basic organisational rules of the Party: individual to organisation, minority to majority, lower level to higher level, and the whole Party to the Central Committee.

glossary.literal: three great fine styles of work
glossary.explanation: Mao Zedong's formulation at the Seventh Congress (1945): integrating theory with practice, close ties with the masses, and self-criticism.

t: Accurately grasping the scientific methods of investigation and research
zh: 准确把握调查研究的科学方法
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in July 2025, asks how Party members should conduct investigation and research (diaocha yanjiu) in order to carry out the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and advance Chinese modernization. Feng and Jia argue that investigation is the basis of all sound decision-making and that it must follow five scientific principles.

The article moves through five requirements in turn: seeking truth from facts, a systems approach, the mass line, a problem orientation, and keeping pace with the times. It draws on Marx and Engels's own investigative work, Party experience from the revolutionary period to poverty alleviation, and the 20th Party Congress report (2022).

The authors present these principles as a working method. Cadres should visit both successful localities and troubled ones, and should listen to unwelcome views as well as welcome ones. Research should be "deep, practical, detailed, accurate and effective". The authors hold that its worth is judged by whether problems are actually solved and findings turned into institutions and policy, not by the scale of a survey or the quality of its report. They also call for updating methods, such as conferences, fieldwork and village-based investigation, with networked information, modern technology and several disciplines, and for combining qualitative and quantitative analysis.

The authors conclude that investigation is the source of sound judgement and is needed for both policy-making and implementation. They treat Xi Jinping's speeches on the subject as the basic guide for a Party-wide drive to revive it. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official methodology of investigation and research as presented in Party-school and Party-building writing.
quoteEn: The fundamental purpose of investigation and research is to solve problems.
quoteZh: 调查研究的根本目的是解决问题。

glossary.explanation: The official Party-state concept of China's own path to modernization, promoted prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A core principle of the Party's ideological line, associated with Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping, requiring policy to start from actual conditions.
The Party's method of work, developed under Mao Zedong, of gathering the views of ordinary people, refining them into policy and testing them in practice.

t: Opening up a better future through unity and struggle
zh: 用团结奋斗开辟美好未来
paras: Qu Qingshan takes up Xi Jinping's 2022 statement that unity and struggle is the only way for the Chinese people to create great historic achievements. The article, a study-and-interpretation piece in Qiushi (2025 no. 13), presents this as a major thesis that answers who creates China's historic undertakings and how. Qu argues that it has both theoretical and practical weight as the country faces a changing international environment, intense great-power rivalry and demanding domestic tasks.

The article has three parts. The first treats unity and struggle as the most distinctive spiritual mark of the Chinese people and the Communist Party. The second reviews four historical dimensions: the development of the Chinese nation, the history of the Party, the history of the People's Republic, and the history of reform and opening up. The third turns to the present and sets out what unity and struggle require on the new journey.

In the core argument, Qu holds that the Chinese nation's spirit combines creativity, struggle, unity and dreams, with patriotism at its core. Qu links it to the Party's "spiritual lineage", which runs from the Jinggangshan spirit to the poverty-alleviation and anti-epidemic spirits. The historical survey then credits each period's achievements to unity and struggle. These include the victory of the new-democratic revolution, socialist transformation and construction, the reforms after 1978, and, since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the elimination of absolute poverty for nearly 100 million rural people. Qu concludes that all of the Party's and people's successes are the result of unity and struggle.

Looking ahead, Qu says that unity built around a clear goal, the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, is the firmest kind. The goal is to be pursued through Chinese modernization and the two-step strategy to 2035 and the middle of the century. Qu calls for four commitments: upholding Party leadership, including the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds; putting the people first; daring and being skilled in struggle; and maintaining the broadest patriotic united front. Read the original if you want an authoritative example of how the Party leadership presents its history, national spirit and current tasks under a single slogan.
quoteEn: All the achievements won by the Party and the people are the result of unity and struggle, and unity and struggle is the only way for the Chinese people to create great historic achievements.
quoteZh: 党和人民取得的一切成就都是团结奋斗的结果，团结奋斗是中国人民创造历史伟业的必由之路。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formula for China's own path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A formula from the 2022 Party resolution on history. It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralized, unified leadership.
The Party's strategy of building alliances with non-Party groups and forces. It is treated as a key instrument of the Party's political work, historically and today.
The Party's official catalogue of named "spirits" tied to historical episodes and models, from the Jinggangshan spirit to the Beidou spirit. It begins from the founding spirit of the Party.
The policy course launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978. It shifted the Party's focus to economic development and opened China to the outside world.

t: Forging the vanguard of the era, showing the strength of a great Party
zh: 锻造时代先锋 展现大党伟力
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 4 July 2025, takes up the milestone that Party membership has passed 100 million. According to the latest Organisation Department figures cited by Zheng Qi, the Communist Party of China had 100.271 million members at the end of 2024, a net rise of 1.086 million (1.1%) over 2023. Zheng argues that this scale shows the Party's attractiveness and vitality, but that quality, not number, must remain the foundation of its strength.

The piece has three sections. The first traces the principle of 'quality first' through Marx and Engels in the Communist League and the First International, Lenin, Mao Zedong and Xi Jinping. The second reads the Party's size as evidence of its appeal and of rising quality since 2013. The third sets out measures for consolidating the numerical advantage while raising quality.

Zheng's central claim is that quantity is the carrier of strength and quality its soul, and that a large membership does not automatically become a quality advantage. As evidence of quality, the article cites an average of 20.627 million applicants and 2.377 million new members a year in 2013–2024, a selection ratio of 8.7 to 1. It also reports that more than 80% of new members each year since the 18th Party Congress (2012) were aged 35 or under, that members with college education or above have exceeded 50% since 2019, and that frontline workers have made up over half of new recruits for eight years. Zheng contrasts this with the 'marginalised' membership and 'hollowed-out' organisations of some Western parties.

To turn scale into quality, Zheng calls for three things. Education and management should be strengthened through Party schools, the 'three meetings and one lesson', and a digital 'smart Party building' system. Discipline should be tightened through full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, in the spirit of the Party's self-reform, with zero tolerance for corrupt members. Members should be tested in practice through 'dual reporting', Party responsibility zones and shock teams. Zheng presents this as the way for a Party of over 100 million to lead Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise official-line statement of how Party-building scholars link membership growth to quality control, with the recruitment statistics cited.
quoteEn: Quantity is the carrier of strength and quality is its soul; scale lays a magnificent foundation, while quality lifts the cause to its height.
quoteZh: 数量是力量的载体，质量是力量的灵魂；规模构筑了宏伟根基，质量擎起了事业高度。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping's leadership since 2012, covering discipline, anti-corruption and organisational management within the Party.
An official formulation stressing that the Party must continually correct itself and purge its own problems without relying on outside supervision.
The official name for the Party's development path, presented since 2021–22 as a distinctive route to modernity led by the Party.
The regular branch-level Party routine of branch meetings, branch committee meetings, small group meetings and a Party lesson.
A system under which Party members register both at their workplace Party branch and at the community where they live, to take part in local service work.

t: Grasping the original contributions of the Party's organizational line for the new era
zh: 深刻把握新时代党的组织路线的原创性贡献
authors: Beijing Municipal Association for Party Building Research
paras: This commentary, written collectively by the Beijing Municipal Association for Party Building Research and carried in the People's Daily in July 2025, sets out what it regards as the original theoretical contributions of the Party's organizational line for the new era. The line was first put forward by Xi Jinping at the national organization work conference in July 2018 and elaborated at a Politburo study session in 2020. The authors argue that it is a landmark result of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and a distinctive concept of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

The article is organised around five contributions: the first definition of the content of an organizational line; the first statement of a basic layout for organizational work; the joining of ideological and organizational Party building; the shift towards systematic construction; and the political criteria for selecting officials. It closes with the line's purpose of serving the political line. Historical references run from Marx, Engels and Lenin through the 1928 Sixth Party Congress, the Gutian Conference and the Yan'an rectification to the post-1978 period and the 18th Party Congress (2012).

The authors contend that the classics stressed organization but never named an organizational line. In their account, the Chinese Party introduced the term in 1928 yet for decades left its content undefined, and organizational work was often equated with cadre work or with grassroots branch building. The new-era formulation is said to resolve this by setting a basic layout of one focus and two emphases: building the organizational system, cultivating high-calibre cadres and attracting talent. It pairs this with Xi's image of organization as the 'form' and ideas as the 'soul', so that theoretical armament underpins organizational strength. The article also presents the stress on integrity first, with both integrity and ability, as a concrete form of the traditional principle of appointing people on merit.

The authors conclude that the line serves the Party's political line and, in their words, provides a strong organizational guarantee for upholding the Party's overall leadership and socialism with Chinese characteristics. They call for linking ideological and organizational Party building, strengthening the organizational system, and carrying the Two Upholds through to every level of the Party. Read the original if you want an authoritative Party-press statement of how the organizational line is now officially framed and periodised in Party-building theory.
quoteEn: A correct organizational line serves and safeguards a correct political line, and at the same time has a positive influence on how the political line is formulated and carried out.
quoteZh: 正确的组织路线服务保证正确政治路线，同时对政治路线的制定和执行产生积极影响。

glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding principles for organizational work, covering structures, cadres and talent. The term first appeared in a 1928 Party Congress resolution; Xi Jinping gave it a formal definition in 2018.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's claim to develop Marxism through Chinese practice and conditions.
The requirement to uphold the core position of the General Secretary and the authority and centralized, unified leadership of the Central Committee.

glossary.literal: appoint people by virtue and merit alone
glossary.explanation: A traditional Chinese principle of selecting officials by virtue and ability, adopted by the Party as its cadre line in 1938.

t: Addressing Party spirit, Party style and Party discipline together as an effective path to self-reform
zh: 党性党风党纪一起抓是实现自我革命的有效途径
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in July 2025, takes up the 20th Party Congress (2022) instruction to "address Party spirit, Party style and Party discipline together". He argues that handling the three together is an effective route to the Party's self-reform, because each performs a distinct function that must be linked to the others.

The article is organised around two principles. The first is systems thinking, which treats the three as an organic whole. The second is strategic thinking, which aims at a long-term mechanism. Between them the author considers the three elements both jointly and one by one.

He describes Party spirit as the foundation, Party style as its outward expression and Party discipline as the guarantee. In his view the three are complementary rather than rivals, and strengthening one strengthens the others. He also gives each its own role. Breaches of style and discipline, he says, usually begin with wavering Party spirit, so cultivating it is the root-level remedy. Party style shapes the political ecology and public support. Party discipline is a rigid constraint, and he calls for combining discipline education with disciplinary punishment.

For the long term, He calls for routine Party-spirit education as a lifelong task, because Party spirit does not grow automatically with seniority or rank. He also calls for a sustained educating role for Party style and for steady improvement of discipline, under the requirements that rules exist, are followed, are enforced strictly and that violations are pursued. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-building commentary in China explains the relationship between the three concepts.
quoteEn: Party spirit is the foundation, Party style is its manifestation, and Party discipline is the guarantee.
quoteZh: 党性是根本，党风是表现，党纪是保障。

glossary.explanation: The ideological conviction, principles and loyalty expected of a Communist Party member. Party documents treat it as the basis of a member's conduct.
The conduct and work style of Party organisations and members, including their relations with the public and their integrity.
The rules and disciplinary regulations that bind Party members, enforced through internal sanctions.
A concept stressed under Xi Jinping. It refers to the Party's efforts to correct its own problems, including corruption and misconduct, through internal discipline and supervision.

t: Forging the spiritual backbone of Chinese Communists with the great founding spirit of the Party
zh: 以伟大建党精神铸牢中国共产党人精神支柱
paras: This short commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in July 2025, asks where the great founding spirit of the Party comes from and why it should anchor the spiritual backbone of Chinese Communists. Wang Zhongru argues that this spirit expresses the Party's advanced character and gives fundamental guidance for fulfilling its nature, purpose and historical mission under new conditions.

The piece traces the spirit to three sources and then turns to the present. These are Marxist theory, traditional Chinese culture, and a firm stand with the people. It adds a fourth strand, the Party's historical consciousness and initiative, before linking the argument to the goals set by the 20th Party Congress (2022).

Wang argues that the Party's century-long fidelity to truth and ideals rests on loyalty to Marxism, especially in its sinicised form. The author presents the willingness to sacrifice and fight as an inheritance from classical Chinese ethics, citing poetic lines on duty and martyrdom, and says the Party's mission of seeking the people's happiness and national rejuvenation is borne out by poverty alleviation, pollution control and welfare gains since the new era began. In Wang's reading, the Party's historical initiative, shown in the War of Resistance, the founding of the new China and reform and opening up, is the key support of the spirit.

Wang concludes that, to meet risks on the new journey, the Party must use the great founding spirit to forge its members' spiritual backbone and gather strength for advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party School scholars link founding-spirit rhetoric to Marxism, tradition and current policy goals.
quoteEn: The great founding spirit of the Party is a vivid summation of Chinese Communists' high degree of historical consciousness and initiative.
quoteZh: 伟大建党精神，是中国共产党人高度的历史自觉和主动精神的生动概括。

glossary.en: the great founding spirit of the Party
glossary.explanation: A formulation stated by Xi Jinping in 2021 for the Party's centenary: upholding truth and ideals, staying true to the original aspiration and mission, fearing no sacrifice and fighting bravely, and being loyal to the Party and the people.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term goal of the Party, presented as restoring China's national strength and international standing.
The official term for China's development path, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

t: Common traits of the spiritual genealogy of Chinese Communists
zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系共同特质
source: China Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 1 July 2025
paras: This short commentary asks what the great spirits in the "spiritual genealogy of Chinese Communists" share, despite their different content. Liu Ronggang argues that these spirits, which the Party formed through revolution, construction and reform, have ten common traits. The author notes that the first batch of spirits was officially published in September 2021, after approval by the Central Committee.

The article is a list-based survey. It sets out ten traits in turn and gives for each a few examples drawn from named spirits, such as the spirit of founding the Party, the Long March spirit, the Jinggangshan spirit, the Yan'an spirit, the special economic zone spirit and the Silk Road spirit. It closes with an account of why the genealogy has these common features.

Liu's ten traits are firm ideals and convictions, loyalty to the Party, living up to the original aspiration and mission, seeking truth from facts, serving the people, pioneering innovation, hard work, daring to struggle, dedication and sacrifice, and solidarity and cooperation. Each is tied to quoted wording from individual spirits and described as a basic requirement or strength of the Party. On causes, Liu says the genealogy comes from practice, continues the spirit of founding the Party, and carries forward the Chinese national spirit.

Liu presents these traits as the shared core of the Party's spiritual wealth and as a call to keep the original aspiration and mission in a new era. Seeking truth from facts is described as the Party's ideological line, to be applied by studying Marxism and its adaptation to China. Read the original if you want a compact official-style summary of how Party historians classify the spirits in the genealogy.
quoteEn: Serving the people is the distinguishing mark that sets the Communist Party of China apart from other parties, and it is the lifeline and an important family heirloom through which the Party keeps its youthful vitality and fighting strength.
quoteZh: 为人民服务是中国共产党区别于其他政党的显著标志，是我们党永葆青春活力和战斗力的生命线和重要传家宝。

glossary.zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系
glossary.explanation: An official list of named "great spirits" (for example the Long March spirit and the Yan'an spirit) said to have arisen in the Party's revolutionary, construction and reform practice. The first batch was published by the Central Publicity Department in September 2021.
A Party slogan, stressed under Xi Jinping, for the Party's founding purpose of seeking happiness for the Chinese people and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
A principle presented as the Party's ideological line, associated with Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping, that policy should rest on actual conditions rather than dogma.

t: Deepening research on the spiritual genealogy of Chinese Communists
zh: 深化中国共产党人精神谱系研究
paras: Wang Binglin, writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today (1 July 2025), argues that research on the spiritual genealogy of Chinese Communists, which takes the great founding spirit of the Party as its source, needs to be deepened. In the author's view, promoting this genealogy supplies spiritual impetus for socialism with Chinese characteristics, nourishes Party building and provides resources for training a new generation. Wang adds that such research has real academic value for the Party's innovative theory and for building the discipline of CPC history and Party building.

The short commentary has three parts: the precise meaning of the concept, the need for scholarly rigour and seriousness, and directions for further research. Wang treats the concept as an innovation in discourse introduced by the Party Central Committee under Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

On the concept, Wang explains the stress on 'Communists' rather than 'the Communist Party'. People create and pass on the spirits, the genealogy is a large system of many individual spirits, and some spirits were not formed by the Party alone: the great spirit of resistance was forged by the whole nation, and the Yimeng and Saihanba spirits by the people together with Communists. On rigour, Wang calls for combining history and theory, with claims resting on solid historical sources. Research should be based on the first batch approved by the Central Committee. Wang urges caution in re-defining revolutionary spirits and in raising local spirits arbitrarily. Wang also holds that general work-style requirements such as a spirit of unity or struggle should not be placed in the genealogy, lest its seriousness be diluted.

Wang proposes further work on how the genealogy formed, viewed through the Two Integrations; on its contribution to Chinese modernization; on its function within the discipline of CPC history and Party building; and on its shared values in a global perspective. Read the original if you want a brief view of how a Party historian sets conceptual limits on what counts as part of the official spiritual genealogy.
quoteEn: We must prevent every requirement containing the word 'spirit' from being placed in the spiritual genealogy, which would dilute its role and in turn affect its seriousness and scientific character.
quoteZh: 要防止把带有“精神”字样的各种要求都纳入精神谱系，从而淡化精神谱系的作用，继而影响精神谱系的严肃性和科学性。

glossary.zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系
glossary.explanation: An official term for the connected series of revolutionary and other exemplary 'spirits' (such as the Yan'an spirit or the Lei Feng spirit) that trace back to the founding of the Party. A first batch was approved by the Central Committee in 2021.
The official summary of the values of the Party's founders, announced in 2021 around the Party's centenary, and treated as the source of the later spirits.
Official formula for combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
The official name for the Party's path of national development, set out prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A first-level academic discipline established in China to study Party history and Party building together.

t: Forging the cause of national rejuvenation with the great founding spirit of the Party
zh: 以伟大建党精神铸就民族复兴伟业
paras: Writing in the China Social Sciences Today in July 2025, Mao asks what role the "great founding spirit" of the Communist Party of China plays in the effort to achieve the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The author argues that this spirit is the Party's winning formula over more than a century and the ideological core guiding the national cause, and calls for more scholarly study of it.

The short commentary opens with Xi Jinping's remarks at the Party's centenary in 2021 about the Party's spiritual lineage. It then traces how successive spirits arose in each period: the Red Boat spirit at the Party's founding, the Jinggangshan, Long March and Yan'an spirits in the revolution, the Daqing and Red Flag Canal spirits after 1949, and the reform-era and post-2012 spirits such as poverty alleviation and the fight against Covid-19.

Mao makes three moves. First, the founding spirit is said to embody the Party's original aspiration and mission through a people-centred historical materialism, a firm belief in lofty ideals and a readiness for "great self-reform". Second, it is said to steer national rejuvenation by keeping to the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics and avoiding both the "old path" and the "evil path". Third, Mao calls for distilling each era's spirit scientifically and for refuting historical nihilism, which the author says underlies attacks on these spirits and on model figures.

Mao concludes that the founding spirit is never "completed" and will keep being enriched as the Party leads the people towards rejuvenation. The author urges firm rebuttal of erroneous currents of thought and deeper propaganda and education work that is integrated into the overall cause of the Party and state. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-school scholarship presents the Party's spiritual lineage as a source of legitimacy and guidance.
quoteEn: The continued inheritance of the great founding spirit has no \"completed tense\".
quoteZh: 伟大建党精神的接续传承没有“完成时”

glossary.explanation: A formulation endorsed in 2021 for the Party's centenary, summarising the founders' ideals and commitment. It is treated as the source of the Party's later spirits.
The official term for the series of named "spirits" (such as the Long March spirit and the Yan'an spirit) that the Party presents as drawn from its history and descended from the founding spirit.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official term for the national goal of restoring China's strength and standing, central to Party discourse since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
The Party's name for its path of socialist development since reform and opening up.
A term stressing the Party's capacity for self-criticism and internal reform, emphasised under Xi Jinping.
In official usage, a label for views that question or negate the Party's official account of its history and its leaders.

t: Building a strong and powerful Marxist governing party
zh: 建设坚强有力的马克思主义执政党
paras: Published in Guangming Daily around the Party's anniversary on 1 July 2025, this short commentary asks what it takes to build a strong Marxist governing party. Xiao Guiqing argues that the Communist Party of China, born in a period of national crisis, has tied its own development to the fate of the Chinese nation. In Xiao's account this has produced a Marxist governing party that leads the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, enjoys popular support and is willing to undertake self-reform.

The article has three sections. The first traces the growth of Party membership and organisation through four historical stages: the revolutionary period, the early socialist period, reform and opening up, and the new era. The second turns to building a united and disciplined membership. The third deals with the vanguard and exemplary role of individual Party members. Xiao draws repeatedly on Xi Jinping's statements.

Xiao contends that growth in size matches the Party's historical position and mission.
