paras: Zhao Xiuhua examines the requirement, set out by Xi Jinping in July 2024 at the Second Plenary Session of the 20th Central Committee's Third Plenum and repeated in January 2025, to "govern the Party with a reform spirit and strict standards". The article argues that this is an essential part of Xi Jinping's thinking on Party building. In Zhao's account, a reform spirit and strict standards together keep the Party vital and sustain its full and rigorous self-governance.

The article has four parts. It first presents the reform spirit as a historical lesson of Party building across the revolutionary, socialist-construction, reform-and-opening and new-era periods. It then discusses problem-oriented self-assessment, and innovation in ideas, methods and institutions. The last part sets out what it means to apply strict standards in terms of criteria, content and process. A short conclusion follows.

Zhao holds that the reform spirit supplies three things to Party governance: awareness of the times, new approaches and measures, and internal motivation. The author cites examples including the Yan'an rectification movement, the campaigns against corruption and bureaucracy in the 1950s, and today's digital tools such as big-data inspection and online Party building. Self-assessment is to be made against three yardsticks: external and domestic challenges, the demands of new technologies and organisational forms, and people's rising aspirations for a better life. Strictness is then specified in five standards (political, ideological, organisational, conduct and work style). It also covers every area of Party building and every Party member, with "key minorities" singled out, and runs through the whole process from admission to accountability.

Zhao concludes that the secret of the Party's lasting vitality is advancing its own building in a reform spirit, and that self-reform with strict requirements keeps its original mission fresh. The author argues that long-term governance amid what the text calls great changes unseen in a century depends on this approach, which is presented as a fundamental guarantee for Chinese modernization and national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a systematic, officially aligned exposition of how Party-building theory links the reform spirit to disciplinary and institutional measures after the Third Plenum.
quoteEn: Advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance in a reform spirit can effectively prevent the Party from drifting away from the masses and from reality, helps to draw on the people's wisdom and gather their strength, and provides a solid foundation for full and rigorous self-governance.
quoteZh: 以改革精神推进全面从严治党，能够有效防止党内出现脱离群众、脱离实际的现象，有利于吸收群众智慧、凝聚群众力量，为全面从严治党提供坚实基础。

glossary.explanation: A concept in Xi Jinping's discourse that presents the Party as able to correct itself through criticism, discipline and institutional reform. The article uses it for the Party's internal reform.
The official term for China's path of modernization, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Advancing the broad, multi-level and institutionalised development of consultative democracy
zh: 推进协商民主广泛多层制度化发展
paras: Writing in the Study Times (Xuexi Shibao) in June 2025, Zhang Shuhua takes up Xi Jinping's call to advance the broad, multi-level and institutionalised development of socialist consultative democracy. Zhang argues that this form of democracy is a distinctive institutional feature and political strength of Chinese-style democracy. The article presents consultation as the practical meaning of "people's democracy" in China: matters of common concern are discussed by the people, in order to find the greatest common denominator of society's wishes.

The piece has three parts. The first explains why consultative democracy matters, the second describes how it has operated across the system of national governance since the 18th Party Congress (2012), and the third sets out measures to make institutionalisation "take effect on the ground". It is a short commentary and cites no external scholarship. Its evidence is drawn from Party regulations, the work of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) and local practice.

Zhang gives three reasons for the system's significance. It embodies Party leadership and the Party's public-minded governing outlook, particularly through consultation between the Party and the democratic parties under the new type of party system. It promotes social integration by seeking the "greatest common denominator" of interests and uniting respect for the majority with care for minorities. It also promotes democratic oversight, which the author says helps correct errors and makes decisions more responsive to public opinion. On practice, Zhang lists seven institutional platforms: party, people's congress, government, CPPCC, people's organisation, grassroots and social-organisation consultation. Party and CPPCC consultation are described as the main channels. Zhang cites regulations on united front work and political consultation, the CPPCC's input into medium- and long-term plans including the 14th Five-Year Plan, and local forums such as democratic heart-to-heart talks and villagers' deliberation councils.

Zhang concludes that the system already has a clear framework running from the centre to localities, and calls for it to be made more effective. The proposals include mechanisms for informing participants and feeding results back, treating institutionalisation as part of political structural reform, an open consultative atmosphere fostered by the ruling Party, and stronger consultative capacity among the democratic parties. Zhang ties this to the project of national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official rationale for consultative democracy and its institutional channels as presented by a leading Chinese political scientist.
quoteEn: The essence of consultation is to seek the intersection of interests and the greatest "common denominator", to take account of all parties' interests, and to draw the largest concentric circle with fundamental interests as its centre.
quoteZh: 协商的本质是寻求利益交集，寻求最大“公约数”，照顾各方利益，以根本利益为圆心画出最大同心圆。

glossary.explanation: A form of democracy in which different groups discuss major issues before and during policy implementation, under Party leadership. Official discourse treats it as a distinctive Chinese form alongside electoral and representative institutions.
The official name for China's path of modernisation, set out by Xi Jinping and the 20th Party Congress (2022), which is said to differ from Western models.
The official description of China's system of multi-party cooperation and political consultation under Chinese Communist Party leadership, involving the eight democratic parties.
A national and local advisory body that brings together the Party, the democratic parties, non-Party figures and social groups. It is officially treated as a main channel of consultative democracy.

t: Comprehensively strengthening the Party's conduct to open a new realm of leading national governance through Party governance
zh: 全面加强党的作风建设开辟以治党引领治国新境界
paras: Writing in Study Times (23 June 2025), Deng Maosheng argues that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core has used the improvement of Party conduct, beginning with the eight-point regulations of the Central Committee, to open a new realm in which governing the Party leads governing the country. In Deng's account, the Party must be governed well first, so that it can lead the people in governing the state.

The commentary has three parts. The first describes the changes attributed to the eight-point regulations, including a transformed political climate, and notes problems that remain. The second sets out the political logic linking Party building and national governance, and the role of conduct building within full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. The third identifies three long-term problems that conduct building must address.

Deng claims the regulations changed China's political ecology in four respects: clear politics, clean officialdom, a prosperous country and secure people. Deng contrasts this with what the article calls political polarisation and social tearing in many Western countries. Drawing on past deviations, Deng argues that politics and economic development cannot be separated, and that disorder in politics undermines growth, citing the "middle-income trap" as an example. Party conduct is presented as a key lever, with the stress on officials, especially leaders, since strict governance of the Party is above all strict governance of officials. Deng presents the anti-corruption campaign as the Party's most thorough self-reform and says its scale has no precedent in the dynastic histories. Deng also asks officials to accept tighter discipline so that ordinary people can feel at ease.

Deng concludes that three problems need sustained attention: separation from the masses after taking power, corruption once in office (especially under market-economy conditions, where power can be exchanged for wealth), and spiritual complacency after a long period of peace. Deng calls for conduct building to become regular and long-term, and for the Party to keep using its self-reform to lead social revolution, in service of Chinese modernization and national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a senior Party policy researcher presents the link between Party conduct and national governance.
quoteEn: Full and rigorous self-governance of the Party is not a slogan but real action; it is not an expedient that is tightened for a while and then relaxed, but a strategic undertaking.
quoteZh: 全面从严治党不是口号,而是实实在在的行动;不是抓一阵松一阵的权宜之计,而是战略之举

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A Party-building policy promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012), combining discipline, anti-corruption work, ideological education and institutional rules for Party members.
Rules issued by the Politburo in December 2012 to curb formalism, bureaucratism, extravagance and waste among officials. They are treated as the starting point of Xi Jinping-era conduct building.
A term for the Party's efforts to correct its own problems, including corruption, without outside pressure. The article links it to the idea of leading wider social revolution.
The official name for the Party's path of development, said to differ from Western modernization in features such as a large population and common prosperity.

glossary.literal: great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, usually dated to the mid-twenty-first century.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Attending to military–political relations in the war zones during the War of Resistance against Japan
zh: 关注抗战时期的战地军政关系
source: Journal of CPC History Studies (Zhonggong dangshi yanjiu), 2025 no. 1
paras: Chen Mo argues that the relationship between stationed armies and local governments in the war zones is an important but under-studied topic in research on the War of Resistance against Japan (1937–45). Defining 'war-zone military–political relations' as the interaction between garrison forces and provincial, district and county governments, excluding the central-level Nationalist–Communist relationship, the author sees it as a Chinese case of civil–military relations. The article is a research agenda rather than a finished study: it maps what scholars have found and what remains unresolved.

The article is organised around four questions: the position of military power in the war-zone power structure; the role of military commanders in local administration; military–political friction; and the separate efforts of the Nationalists (Guomindang) and the Chinese Communist Party (CPC) to manage these relations. For each, Chen sets out existing scholarship and then lists cases, mechanisms and comparisons that still need study, on both the Nationalist front and the CPC-led base areas behind Japanese lines.

Chen holds that both parties raised the status of armies and officers in rebuilding local power. On the Nationalist side, the author cites figures showing that of 67 wartime provincial chairmen, 77.6 per cent had military backgrounds (70 per cent in war-zone provinces), a pattern linked to Chiang Kai-shek's preference for the army over the Party. In the base areas, armies founded governments and, from 1938, military leaders often headed joint military–political committees. Friction arose over personnel, finance and especially grain requisition, as in the Eastern Hubei incident, and also inside the base areas, where Mao Zedong and He Long criticised overbearing army cadres. Chen contends that Chiang usually sided with the military, leaving the underlying tensions unresolved. The CPC, by contrast, is said to have eased the problem through unified leadership from September 1942, rectification, the campaign against warlordism and the 'support the government and cherish the people, support the army and give preferential treatment to military families' campaign, a far more successful approach in Chen's account.

Chen concludes that all four areas leave room for further work, including year-by-year and regional quantitative studies of power shifts, commanders' practical solutions (for example Chen Cheng's grain rationing in Hubei and Luo Ronghuan's sea-salt trade in Shandong), the reasons some armies and governments cooperated under shared hardship, and the long-term effect of the two parties' divergent approaches, to be analysed with political science and sociology. Read the original if you work on wartime Chinese history, Nationalist or CPC institutions, or civil–military relations and want a detailed list of sources, cases and open questions.
quoteEn: As far as coordinating military–political relations in the war zones is concerned, the CPC was far more successful than the Nationalists.
quoteZh: 就协调战地军政关系而言，中共较国民党要成功得多。

glossary.explanation: A CPC policy adopted in September 1942 that placed Party committees in authority over military, government and mass organisations in each base area, replacing the earlier military–political committees.
Joint bodies of army and local Party and government leaders set up in many CPC base areas from 1938, often chaired by the commanding officer, until replaced by Party committees.

glossary.en: support the government and cherish the people, support the army and give preferential treatment to military families
glossary.explanation: A CPC campaign launched in the base areas after 1942 to improve relations between armed forces, local governments and civilians.
A term in CPC criticism for army cadres who disregard local Party and government authorities and place military power above all else.
A dispute around 1941 in which the Nationalist Fifth War Zone pressed the Hubei provincial government to hand over control of local administration in eastern Hubei.

t: An analysis of the Communist Party of China's military leadership in the period of the New Democratic Revolution
zh: 新民主主义革命时期中国共产党的军事领导力探析
source: China Leadership Science (Zhongguo lingdao kexue), 2025 no. 2
paras: Ma and Yi ask how the Communist Party of China forged, and kept strengthening, the military leadership that let a weak revolutionary army defeat much better-equipped opponents between 1927 and the Korean War. Their thesis is that this leadership rested on three principles: the Party commanding the gun, unity between officers and soldiers, and people's war. All three, they argue, depended on valuing and cultivating people.

The article opens with an introduction that uses Mao Zedong's analysis of the balance of forces to explain how strength and weakness can be reversed in war. Three substantive sections follow, one for each principle, and a conclusion closes the piece. The evidence is drawn from the failed Nanchang, Autumn Harvest and Guangzhou uprisings, the Sanwan reorganisation, the Gutian Conference, the War of Resistance against Japan, and comparisons with the Kuomintang army.

On the first principle, the authors argue that early Red Army units kept the habits of old mercenary armies and often collapsed. Mao's response was to place Party committees at battalion level and above, branches in companies, and groups in squads and platoons, which in the authors' account turned military command into collective Party decision-making. They add that the company is the basic unit of combat and daily life, and so the right place for a Party branch. On the second principle, officer–soldier equality and the "three major democracies" (political, military, economic) are said to have produced class feeling, self-management and initiative, in contrast with the Kuomintang's reliance on money and coercion. On the third, the authors describe a three-tier armed system of main forces, local guerrillas and militia, rooted in land reform and discipline toward civilians, which they credit with large-scale guerrilla war behind Japanese lines and with five specific effects on Japan's war effort.

Ma and Yi conclude that Party organisation at the grass roots, military democracy and fusion with the masses together made up the Party's military leadership, and that each rested on a Marxist concern with the human being. They cite the peasant origins of most of the 1,614 founding-era generals, and the remoulding of former Kuomintang units, as evidence that Party leadership can turn ordinary people into capable soldiers. Read the original if you want a Party-affiliated scholarly account of how Chinese military leadership principles are explained and justified, including its use of leadership-science and psychological arguments.
quoteEn: The Party's command of the gun laid the organisational foundation for building the army politically, ensuring that the people's army could stay united and obey the Party in a brutal environment, avoiding disintegration or becoming the private force of a warlord.
quoteZh: 党指挥枪奠定了政治建军的组织基础，确保人民军队能在残酷的环境中保持团结、听党指挥，避免解体或沦为军阀私人武装。

glossary.explanation: A principle formulated by Mao Zedong that the armed forces are subject to the absolute leadership of the Communist Party, and that the gun must never command the Party.
Mao Zedong's military doctrine of mobilising the masses, especially the peasantry, in protracted guerrilla and regular warfare backed by rural base areas.
Political, military and economic democracy in the Red Army, including soldiers' committees that took part in management and supervised officers.

t: Lessons from building a Chinese autonomous knowledge system of Xinhai Revolution history
zh: 建构中国自主的辛亥革命史知识体系的启示
source: Social Science Digest (Shehui kexue wenzhai), 2025 no. 2
paras: Ma Min takes up a task he describes as pressing for Chinese historians: accelerating the construction of an autonomous Chinese knowledge system of historical studies. He argues that research on the 1911 (Xinhai) Revolution, and the way its own autonomous knowledge system took shape, is a model case that offers several lessons for that wider project.

The article has three parts. It first traces more than 70 years of Xinhai Revolution scholarship in the People's Republic in three stages: emergence (1949–1966), flourishing (1978–1989) and deepening (1990 to the present). It then identifies five defining features of the resulting knowledge system. Finally it looks ahead to how the field might be extended.

For the historical account, Ma holds that the early stage, guided by historical materialism, established the 'bourgeois revolution' thesis through class analysis and a mass-centred view of history. In the 1980s, he says, mainland scholars refined this thesis in debate with Taiwan scholars' 'revolution of the whole people' view and overseas scholars' 'gentry movement' view. Since the 1990s, social history, the modernization paradigm and postmodern approaches have broadened the field. The five features are: historical materialism as the 'soul'; historical sources as the 'foundation'; academic-system building, meaning concepts, theories and findings, as the 'core'; major monographs as the visible 'form'; and institutions and journals as the 'network'. Ma stresses that the system is open: it drew on Western, Japanese and Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan scholarship, so 'autonomy' must not exclude sensible borrowing.

Ma proposes widening the field's horizons in time, space and society. In time, he follows Zhang Kaiyuan's 'three hundred years' idea and urges study of links between the Hundred Days' Reform, the late-Qing New Policies, the Xinhai Revolution, the May Fourth Movement and the founding of the Communist Party, within the larger frame of national rejuvenation and Chinese modernization. In space, he calls for Asian and global perspectives and for regional studies. In society, he advocates combining revolutionary and social history, with finer empirical work such as local, visual and individual-experience studies. Ma sees this as a 'new revolutionary history' of renewal. Read the original if you want a Chinese historian's account of how the field's paradigms developed and of the research directions he proposes for it.
quoteEn: Therefore, the formation of an autonomous knowledge system is in fact the result of interaction between indigenous and foreign knowledge; while stressing 'autonomy', one must not overlook reasonable 'borrowing'.
quoteZh: 因此，自主知识体系的形成，其实是本土知识与域外知识互动交流的结果，在强调“自主”的同时，切不可忽略合理的“借鉴”。

glossary.explanation: The mainland view that the 1911 Revolution was a bourgeois-democratic revolution arising from the growth of national capitalism and class conflict in the late Qing.
Marx's theory of history, in which material production and class relations shape social development. Chinese historiography treats it as its guiding method.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, prominent in Party discourse since the 2020s.
A central theme of Party discourse, presenting modern Chinese history since the Opium War as a path from decline to renewal of the Chinese nation.

t: The spiritual genealogy of Chinese Communists in the perspective of historical progress: theoretical picture and practical significance
zh: 历史进步视野中的中国共产党人精神谱系：理论图景与现实意义
paras: Xing Yunwen and Yan Manqing ask how the spiritual genealogy of Chinese Communists should be located within the long course of human history, and what its significance is today. They argue that the question comes down to a prior one, how spirit takes part in historical progress, and that Marx and Engels's historical materialism gives the theoretical route for answering it. On this basis, the authors present the genealogy as an important spiritual driving force of historical progress.

The article has three parts. The first reviews how Marxist views of historical progress reconsidered the place of spirit, from Hegel's teleological account to Marx and Engels's reinterpretation. The second examines how the genealogy was formed and developed, along three lines: the value of putting the people first, the complex movement of social contradictions in different periods, and the dialectic between objective historical laws and the subjective spirit of historical agents. The third sets out the genealogy's significance for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, world socialism, human civilization and the free and all-round development of every person.

In the authors' reading, Hegel treated history as the self-development of Absolute Spirit, which left spirit without a real subject. Marx and Engels, citing The German Ideology and Engels's late letters, located history in the practice of real individuals and rejected the reduction of historical materialism to economic determinism. Progress, on this view, results from the combined force of economic base and superstructure, practice and spirit. The authors apply this to the Party. They hold that the great spirit of Party founding is the source of a genealogy whose branches include the Jinggangshan, Xibaipo and Yan'an spirits. Its inner core is the value of putting the people first, and its growth comes from respecting historical laws while exercising historical initiative.

The authors conclude that the genealogy supplies lasting spiritual momentum for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and strengthens the Chinese nation's sense of community. They also hold that it leaves a distinctive mark on the world socialist movement, offering other socialist countries a spiritual example, and that it is a resource for civilizational progress that draws on both traditional Chinese culture and Marxism and challenges Western-centric notions of civilizational superiority. They further argue that its "sublime" value orientation enriches the human-liberation perspective of all-round human development. Read the original if you want to see how Party-history spirit studies are grounded in Marxist philosophy of history and tied to claims about Chinese modernization and world socialism.
quoteEn: The history of the formation and evolution of the spiritual genealogy of Chinese Communists is the Party's stirring history of growth, from immaturity to maturity and from a "single spark" to a "prairie fire".
quoteZh: 中国共产党人精神谱系的生成演进史就是中国共产党从幼稚走向成熟、由“星星之火”发展成“燎原之势”的峥嵘成长史。

glossary.zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系
glossary.explanation: An official designation, used since the early 2020s, for the series of named "spirits" the Party says it formed in different periods, such as the Jinggangshan, Yan'an and Xibaipo spirits. It is presented as a unified lineage that begins with the spirit of Party founding.
A formulation put forward officially in 2021 around the Party's centenary. It is described as the source of the later spirits in the genealogy.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China's national strength and standing, closely linked to the Chinese Dream and Xi Jinping's leadership.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

t: Making the Party's innovative theory take root among the people in the digital age
zh: 数字时代推动党的创新理论深入人心
paras: Writing in the China Social Sciences Today (25 June 2025 posting of a 20 June article), Zhang Weizhou takes up the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee's (2024) call to build a system that arms the whole Party, educates the people and guides practice with the Party's innovative theory. Zhang argues that digitalisation has reshaped communication and created three tensions: depth of content against breadth of reach, theoretical height against audience reception, and system completeness against innovation in carriers. The proposed answer is a "three-dimensional architecture" of systematic research, scenario-based communication and coordinated advancement.

The commentary is built around three practical pathways, each illustrated with examples from Xi'an, where the author works in the municipal publicity department. These are a people-centred communication model, technological innovation in the delivery system, and a collaborative communication ecosystem. Zhang cites Xi Jinping's remarks on news communication, on systematising theory and on integrated media development as support for each section.

On the first pathway, Zhang holds that one-way indoctrination yields diminishing returns online, so theory must be adapted to audiences through cognitive fit, scenario embedding and emotional resonance. Xi'an's "Runli Xi'an" project, with live-streamed Q&A, online volunteer communicators and a points system, is presented as moving learning from "I speak, you listen" to co-creation. On the second, Zhang describes a converged network of smart platforms (such as the Learning Powerhouse app), social media and offline VR/AR or holographic exhibitions, while warning of information cocoons, privacy disputes and over-personalisation. Zhang proposes a framework of "values as substance, technology as function", with safeguards such as weighting mainstream values, data desensitisation and human review. On the third, Zhang outlines a feedback loop of communication, feedback, assessment and optimisation, and a three-tier city, district and community network.

Zhang concludes that bringing the theory into ordinary homes consolidates the Party's governing foundation and gathers strength for national rejuvenation. This requires correct political, opinion and value orientations and innovation in concepts, content, forms and mechanisms, so as to open the "last kilometre" of theoretical arming. Xi'an's practice is offered as a model of three shifts: from content supply to shared meaning-making, from technology as tool to ecosystem, and from one-way governance to multi-party cooperation. Read the original if you want a concrete local example of how Party propaganda departments plan digital theory communication, including Xi'an's platforms and mechanisms.
quoteEn: When academic depth and real-world warmth are deeply fused, theory is transformed from abstract concept into concrete identification.
quoteZh: 当学术深度与现实温度深度融合，理论便从抽象概念转化为具象认同。

glossary.explanation: Official term for the Party's latest theoretical achievements, centred on Xi Jinping Thought, which Party organs seek to study and spread.
The author's own framework combining systematic research, scenario-based communication and coordinated advancement in theory dissemination.
The idea that algorithmic personalisation traps users in narrow streams of information matching their existing preferences.
A Party-run mobile learning platform launched in 2019 that carries Party theory, news and study content.
Official goal of restoring China's strength and standing, usually called the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

t: Building the enforcement capacity of intra-Party regulations as the concrete form of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
zh: 党内法规执行力建设是全面从严治党的具体化
paras: This short commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in June 2025, asks how the Party's self-reform can be secured institutionally. Huang Tianhong argues that strengthening the enforcement capacity of intra-Party regulations is the concrete form of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, and that such regulations are indispensable to a long-term mechanism of self-reform.

The piece first explains why institutional guarantees matter: they turn good working styles formed in self-reform into norms, support mechanisms for finding and solving problems, and help restrain power. It then sets out the roles of intra-Party regulations, headed by the Party Constitution, as a basis, a code of conduct, a standard for supervision and a source of values. The second half proposes four routes to better enforcement.

Huang's core argument is that enforcement itself should embody the spirit of self-reform. The four routes are: improving the scientific quality and consistency of drafting (clear wording, no overlap or conflict between rules, alignment with the Constitution and law, timely revision with Party and public input); raising the integrity and professional competence of those who enforce; fostering rule-consciousness among all Party members and cadres; and strengthening supervision. On supervision, Huang calls for accountability mechanisms, links between Party and state, democratic, judicial, public and media oversight, performance assessment, and a mechanism that tolerates honest error while separating it from deliberate wrongdoing.

Huang concludes that periodic campaigns of cleansing are necessary, but that long-term purity and vanguard status depend on reform and institutions. Pursuing self-reform scientifically and systematically is presented as a distinctive advantage of the Party. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official rationale and policy measures for improving the implementation of Party regulations.)
quoteEn: For the Party to keep its vanguard character and purity for ever, concentrated sweeping and cleansing is necessary, but over the long term it must rely on reform and institutions.
quoteZh: 党要永葆先进性和纯洁性，集中性地打扫、洗涤很有必要，从长计议还得靠改革、靠制度。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: A Party slogan since the 18th Party Congress (2012) for tightening discipline, anti-corruption work and internal regulation of the CPC.
A formulation in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse for the Party's continuous internal self-correction and purification, presented as its way of avoiding decline.
The formal rules issued by the CPC to govern Party organisation and members' conduct, headed by the Party Constitution and enforced through Party discipline.

t: Resolutely fighting the anti-corruption struggle as a tough battle, a protracted war and an all-round campaign
zh: 坚决打好反腐败斗争攻坚战持久战总体战
source: China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News, 19 June 2025, p. 5
paras: Zhou Xinqun's commentary, first published in the Party discipline newspaper China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News in June 2025, explains Xi Jinping's call at the Fourth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection to fight corruption as a tough battle (gongjianzhan), a protracted war (chijiuzhan) and an all-round campaign (zongtizhan). Zhou argues that the formulation reflects a scientific reading of the situation and the laws of anti-corruption work. The author treats it as a political struggle the Party cannot afford to lose.

The article is organised around three questions: why the three-part fight is needed, why the Party can win it, and how to advance it. The first section analyses the current situation. The second lists the Party's advantages. The third sets out five practical tasks.

On the first question, Zhou holds that corruption remains serious, stubborn and recurrent. The author points to stock not yet cleared, new cases still emerging, collusion between officials and business, corruption among top leaders and in sectors such as finance, state enterprises and energy, and more concealed forms. The tough battle answers the difficulty of the task. The protracted war answers its long-term nature, which Zhou illustrates with dynastic decline and with lingering feudal and capitalist-influenced cultures of privilege. The all-round campaign answers its complexity, requiring the Party to advance the three-sphere approach of not daring, not being able and not wanting to be corrupt, and to draw in the whole society. On the second question, Zhou cites a firm leadership core, scientific theory, popular support, an improved system of rules and supervision, and a rich set of preventive tools.

For the third question Zhou proposes five tasks: strengthening the Party Central Committee's centralised and unified leadership, keeping up high-pressure punishment, tightening checks on power, investigating and tackling unhealthy work styles and corruption together, and continuously cleaning up the political ecology through Party life and a culture of integrity. The three battles are presented as one integrated whole, not a sequence. Read the original if you want an authoritative Party-press account of how the post-2012 anti-corruption campaign is framed, including its current priorities and policy vocabulary.
quoteEn: The essence of corruption is the abuse of power.
quoteZh: 腐败的本质是权力滥用。

glossary.pinyin: bù gǎn fǔ, bù néng fǔ, bù xiǎng fǔ
glossary.en: not daring, not being able and not wanting to be corrupt
glossary.literal: dare not be corrupt, cannot be corrupt, do not want to be corrupt
glossary.explanation: The official three-part anti-corruption approach combining deterrence through punishment, institutional constraints, and moral and ideological education.

t: Carrying forward the Red Boat Spirit and keeping all undertakings in the front rank
zh: 传承红船精神 推动各项事业走在前列
paras: Marking the 20th anniversary of the Red Boat Spirit (proposed in 2005), this commentary from Study Times (18 June 2025) asks how the spirit has driven the development of Jiaxing, the Zhejiang city where the Party's founding congress ended on a boat. Hu argues that the three components of the spirit have turned spiritual strength into material strength, and that the same spirit must guide Jiaxing's future path towards Chinese modernization.

The piece opens by defining the spirit's three elements: pioneering initiative, firm ideals and perseverance, and selfless dedication to the Party and the people. It then reviews Jiaxing's record over two decades in five areas: economic growth, integrated urban-rural development, technological innovation, reform, and green and harmonious development. The final sections set out plans and requirements for the coming period, including economic, reform, innovation and Party-building tasks.

Hu's central evidence is a set of statistics, which the author attributes to the Red Boat Spirit. Regional GDP is reported to have risen from 116.6 billion yuan in 2005 to 756.95 billion in 2024, and the urban-rural income ratio to have fallen from 2.02 to 1.51. Jiaxing is also said to rank first or second in Zhejiang on several innovation and digitalisation indicators. Looking ahead, Hu says the city will follow the "Eight-Eight Strategy", make high-quality development its first task, and aim at narrowing the "three major gaps". It will also deepen reform and opening up, build a manufacturing-innovation city, develop new quality productive forces, and pursue green and low-carbon transition. Hu also calls for strengthening Party building, with a cadre corps that is loyal, pragmatic and clean, and for continued anti-corruption work and study of the Central Committee's eight-point regulation.

Hu concludes that Jiaxing got where it is through spirit and must rely on spirit to move forward, and that the Red Boat Spirit remains its main source of inner motivation. The city is to become an important centre of the Yangtze River Delta urban cluster and to write a new Jiaxing chapter of Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a local example of how Party commentary links the Red Boat Spirit to economic indicators, development plans and Party-building tasks.
quoteEn: Jiaxing has reached today through spirit and must rely on spirit to move into the future; the Red Boat Spirit remains a powerful spiritual pillar and inner driving force for the road ahead.
quoteZh: 嘉兴靠精神走到今天，更要靠精神走向未来，红船精神依然是激励我们走向未来的强大精神支柱与内在动力。

glossary.explanation: A Party-defined spirit named after the boat on Jiaxing's South Lake where the First Party Congress (1921) concluded. Xi Jinping, then Zhejiang Party secretary, formulated it in 2005 as pioneering initiative, struggle and dedication.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, which the Party presents as distinct from Western models.
A set of eight strategic measures for Zhejiang's development, put forward in 2003 by Xi Jinping when he led the province.
A concept promoted since 2023 that stresses technology-driven, innovation-led productive capacity as the basis of high-quality development.
The official guiding aim of economic policy since 2017, emphasising quality, innovation and sustainability over speed of growth.

t: Treating both symptoms and root causes: sustaining Party work-style building
zh: 标本兼治持之以恒推进作风建设
paras: This newspaper commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 19 June 2025, asks how the Communist Party of China can make improvement of its work style (zuofeng) a lasting, routine undertaking. Liu Zhiming argues that building a good work style is a decisive source of the Party's strength, that the problem is stubborn and recurrent, and that only an approach treating both symptoms and root causes (biaoben jianzhi) can consolidate results.

The piece is built in three parts. It first reviews the Party's history of work-style building, from Mao Zedong's rectification campaigns and the Yan'an style through Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao to the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It then argues that the work remains unfinished, citing current problems. Finally it sets out three practical lines of effort.

Liu's core argument is that work-style problems are at root questions of Party spirit and of the Party's relationship with the people. The author lists persisting problems: wavering ideals, breaches of the eight-point regulation, formalism and bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, and disguised variants of these. Liu cites a 2024 National Bureau of Statistics survey in which 97.4 per cent were satisfied with the Party Central Committee's implementation of the eight-point regulation, but warns that old habits could rebound. The three remedies are to keep reinforcing the eight-point regulation, to strengthen Party-spirit cultivation (using the image of a pathogen that can relapse if the 'master switch' of worldview is wrong), and to build comprehensive institutions, because many apparent style problems are in fact institutional ones.

Liu concludes that work-style building has a starting point but no end point, and that it must advance in step with the stage reached by the Party's and the people's cause, including further comprehensive deepening of reform and Chinese modernization. Proposed institutional measures include long-term mechanisms to reduce burdens on grassroots officials, revised performance appraisal, incentive and error-tolerance mechanisms, and checks on the allocation and exercise of power. Read the original if you want a concise official-style statement of how Party theorists frame the continuity and institutionalisation of work-style campaigns in the Xi Jinping era.
quoteEn: Building a good work style ultimately depends on institutions.
quoteZh: 抓作风建设，根本上还是要靠制度。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing Party term for efforts to improve the conduct, attitudes and working methods of Party members and officials, often through campaigns and rules.
Rules adopted by the Politburo in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism among officials, such as limits on banquets, travel and meetings.

glossary.en: treating both symptoms and root causes
glossary.literal: treat both the branch and the root
glossary.explanation: A principle of tackling both the visible manifestations of a problem and its underlying causes, widely used in anti-corruption and discipline discourse.
The official term for China's path of modernization, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

t: Grasping the root and foundation of work-style building
zh: 抓住作风建设的根与本
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in June 2025, asks how the Communist Party of China should deepen its campaign to improve the conduct of its members, known as work-style building. Li Kunpeng argues, following Xi Jinping, that work-style problems are at root problems of Party spirit. Weak Party spirit produces distorted conduct, such as formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance.

The article proposes three lines of effort: building an ideological foundation, holding firm to ideals and the Party's purpose, and enforcing rules and moral self-cultivation. It draws on Xi's statements, the Party's history (including the "two musts" of the Xibaipo period) and the Central Committee's eight-point regulation.

Li holds that cadres should arm themselves with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era through study that is systematic, prompt, reflective and tied to practice. The author says the "four undesirable work styles" are only surface symptoms, and that the real cause is departure from the Party's purpose of serving the people. The commentary links firm ideals to a people-centred approach and to the mass line. It also calls for updating Party regulations to cover hidden variants of the four work styles, naming "electronic red envelopes" and gifts sent by courier, and for strict implementation.

Li concludes that combined ideological education, institutional constraint and moral cultivation will carry work-style building further and help build a Marxist governing party. The author calls on senior cadres to lead by example, drawing on traditional Chinese culture, revolutionary family traditions and discipline over relatives and staff. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official Party-building view that work style is rooted in Party spirit.
quoteEn: Work-style problems are in essence problems of Party spirit.
quoteZh: 作风问题本质上是党性问题。

glossary.explanation: A long-running Party campaign to correct the conduct of Party members and cadres, such as bureaucratism and extravagance. It is treated as part of Party building.
The political character, loyalty and discipline expected of Party members. Official discourse treats it as the basis of correct conduct.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sixiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions from 2017–2018.
Formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, named by the Party as targets of rectification after the 18th Party Congress (2012).
Rules adopted by the Central Committee in December 2012 to curb official extravagance and bureaucratic practices and to improve cadres' conduct.
The Party's traditional method of working, taking ideas from the people and returning them as policy. It stresses close ties with ordinary people.

t: The dialectical logic of building the Party's cultural leadership in the new era
zh: 新时代党的文化领导权建设的辩证逻辑
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education (Sixiang lilun jiaoyu), 2025 no. 5
paras: Wang Yan and Liu Yang take up the concept of "the Communist Party of China's cultural leadership" (cultural hegemony in Gramsci's vocabulary), which Xi Jinping put forward in June 2023. The article asks why building it is necessary, what it consists of, how it should be carried out and what it is for. Its thesis is that cultural leadership building in the new era rests on a set of dialectical relations, which the authors say show the Party acting with initiative and practical rationality.

The article has four parts. The first treats the "ought" of this work as drawn from history, driven by present needs and oriented to the future. The second sets out its core meaning. The third turns to the practical layout. The fourth discusses its value. The authors trace Party practice from the new-democratic revolution through socialist construction and reform and opening up to the present, and they draw on Gramsci, Marx and Engels, and Xi's speeches.

In the authors' account, cultural leadership has three core dimensions: building a power system aimed at ideological leadership, a political practice that fosters national identity, and a governance strategy covering cultural production, management and communication. These are said to be mutually supporting. The practical layout rests on three unities: Party spirit with people-centredness, systematic design with targeted measures, and innovation with critique. The authors argue that creation opens cultural space while struggle against capital-driven alienation, Western-centrism and historical nihilism protects cultural security. They cast Western cultural influence, including "universal values" and consumerist commercial products, as a threat to cultural security that this leadership must counter.

The authors conclude that the work brings value on three levels. It consolidates cultural subjectivity, notably through the Second Integration of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture. It supports spiritual independence for the Chinese nation's modernization. It offers developing countries a "Chinese wisdom" for resisting Western cultural hegemony. They call for effectiveness to be judged by whether Party aims fit popular needs, whether overall planning is matched by precise measures, and whether cultural progress is matched by cleaning up cultural disorder. Read the original if you want a systematic Party-theoretical account of how cultural hegemony is conceptualised in current Chinese ideological work.
quoteEn: By holding innovation and critique together as its method, the Party's cultural leadership building in the new era uses innovation to open up cultural space and critique to safeguard cultural security, building through simultaneous demolition and construction a system of cultural development with both drive and resilience.
quoteZh: 新时代党的文化领导权建设坚持创新性与批判性相统一的方法策略，是以创新开拓文化空间，以批判维护文化安全，在破立并举中构建兼具驱动力与抵御力的文化发展体系。

glossary.explanation: Chinese rendering of the idea close to Gramsci's cultural hegemony. Xi Jinping introduced the formula "the Party's cultural leadership" at the June 2023 symposium on cultural inheritance and development.
The Party's formula, put forward in 2023, for combining the basic principles of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture. It is the second of the Two Integrations.
The idea that a nation's culture has its own independent standpoint and agency. Xi Jinping stressed it in 2023, and the article ties it to the Party's leadership in culture.

t: On the Communist Party of China's capacity for modernization in the new era: components, logic of formation and integrated pathway
zh: 论新时代中国共产党的现代化建设能力：构成要素、生成逻辑与集成路径
paras: Following the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called for comprehensively raising cadres' capacity for modernization, and Xi Jinping's later demand to raise the whole Party's Marxist level and modernization capacity, Hu Hongbin asks what this capacity actually is, how it forms in practice and how it can be fully raised. Using systems thinking, the article argues that the Party's modernization capacity is an organic whole made up of several types of element. Hu contends it can be raised only by integrating those elements through a systematic pathway.

The article has four parts. It first defines the capacity and its functions in the deepening of Chinese modernization. It then sets out the capacity's components, explains the mechanism and modes by which it forms, and ends with a three-stage pathway for improvement. Hu draws on Marx, Engels and Xi Jinping to ground systems thinking as a method.

Hu sorts the components into three groups. Foundational elements are theoretical (Marxist modernization theory and the theoretical system of Chinese modernization) and historical (the Party's long exploration from Mao Zedong to Deng Xiaoping and after). Operational elements are executive (strategic, policy and reform execution) and social (the public's recognition of and participation in the Party's agenda). Safeguarding elements are organisational, institutional and personnel-related, with a high-quality cadre corps as the key. Because these elements come from different actors, Hu identifies three generative modes: "endogenous" construction by the Party, "exogenous" assistance from social actors, and collaborative "symbiosis" between the two.

The proposed integrated pathway improves the elements at three points: construction and input, integration and adjustment, and output after practical conversion. At the centre is a comprehensive, digital "one-stop" Party-building platform that breaks down administrative and information barriers. It would be paired with dynamic coordination and practice-conversion mechanisms, followed by feedback and evaluation mechanisms. Hu also calls for stronger cadre training, wider channels for social participation and a summary of the people's experience of modernization. Read the original if you want a systems-theory account of how Party-building scholarship frames capacity-building for Chinese modernization, including its proposals for platform design and evaluation mechanisms.
quoteEn: The Party's capacity for modernization in the new era is an organic whole composed of multiple elements.
quoteZh: 新时代党的现代化建设能力是由多重要素构成的有机整体。

glossary.explanation: Official concept of a modernization path led by the Communist Party and described as distinct from Western models. It has been elaborated in Party documents since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
Service and governance platforms, increasingly digital, set up by Party organisations to share information and integrate resources for Party work and ideological-political work.

A method that analyses objects as wholes with interconnected parts, stressing overall, structural, open and dynamic features. The author presents it as part of Marxist epistemology and Party working methods.

glossary.pinyin: Dǎng de èrshí jiè sān zhōng quánhuì
glossary.en: Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
glossary.explanation: The July 2024 plenary meeting of the Party's Central Committee, which adopted a decision on further deepening reform and advancing Chinese modernization.

t: Methodology for advancing the systematization and academic grounding of the Party's innovative theory
zh: 推进党的创新理论体系化学理化的方法论
paras: Chen Jinlong takes up Xi Jinping's call, made at the sixth group study session of the 20th Politburo, to "vigorously advance the systematization and academic grounding" of the Party's innovative theory. The article defines that theory as Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Systematization means starting from the texts and revealing their structure and internal relations. Academic grounding means using the theories and methods of different disciplines to bring out their underlying reasoning. Chen argues that this work follows a methodology with three parts: a holistic perspective, academic expression and the recognition of laws.

The article is organised in three sections, one for each part. The first treats the theory as a whole: its formation, content, features and historical standing. The second works through levels of academic expression: signature concepts, original concepts, basic categories, propositions, principles, and worldview and methodology. The third identifies the laws of Communist Party governance, socialist construction, human social development and the Party's own theoretical innovation.

On the holistic perspective, Chen lists five conditions behind the theory's formation: theoretical sources, practical foundation, cultural heritage, the conditions of the age, and subjective conditions. Chen proposes organising its content under fifteen headings, from the Party's overall leadership to Chinese modernization, and assesses its standing across long historical spans. On academic expression, Chen names four signature concepts (socialism with Chinese characteristics, Chinese modernization, full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation). Chen also names original concepts such as whole-process people's democracy, new quality productive forces and a community with a shared future for mankind. Chen says these should be explained with disciplinary tools, for example political science for democracy and Marxist political economy for productive forces. On laws, Chen holds that the theory has deepened understanding in four areas, citing the Two Integrations and the Party's self-reform as principle-level results.

Chen concludes that systematization and academic grounding are distinct but mutually supporting: grounding rests on systematization, and systematization relies on grounding. Chen calls the task practical as well as theoretical, one that requires the whole Party and especially scholars, who must master the concepts and methods of their disciplines. Chen also links it to building an independent system of Chinese philosophy and social science knowledge, which the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) placed within cultural reform. Read the original if you want a detailed account of how Chinese academics are told to frame, categorise and explain Xi Jinping Thought as a scholarly system.
quoteEn: Advancing the systematization of the Party's innovative theory focuses on interpreting its system and structure; advancing its academic grounding focuses on interpreting its scholarly and theoretical substance.
quoteZh: 推进党的创新理论体系化，侧重对党的创新理论的体系、结构的诠释；推进党的创新理论学理化，侧重对党的创新理论的学术、学理的诠释。

glossary.explanation: In this article, a term for the Party's theory of the new era, identified with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.
Xi Jinping's formulation for the task of exposing the structure of the Party's theory and explaining its content with academic concepts and methods.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017.
The formula of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's drive to tighten discipline and strengthen Party building.
Official term for the Party's efforts to correct itself and resolve internal problems. It is presented as the second answer to the historical cycle of rise and fall.
The Party's official account of China's path to a modern socialist country.
The official description of China's democracy, which stresses participation across all stages of decision-making.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for innovation-led, high-technology advanced productive forces.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept of a world of lasting peace, common prosperity and openness.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's long-term national goal, used as the central theme of its historical mission.

t: Understanding that the core of the style-of-work problem is the Party's relationship with the people
zh: 深刻理解作风问题核心是党同人民群众的关系问题
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2025, no. 7), Chen Li takes up the Party-wide study and education campaign on thoroughly implementing the Central Committee's eight-point regulation. Chen's thesis, drawn from Xi Jinping's statements since the 18th Party Congress (2012), is that the core of the problem of work style (zuofeng) is the relationship between the Party and the people. On this reading, work-style building must centre on keeping the Party's flesh-and-blood ties with the masses, upholding the Marxist mass viewpoint and applying the Party's mass line.

The article has four parts, each arguing that focusing on this relationship has a different kind of basis: theoretical, practical, realistic and policy-based. The first part goes through Marx and Lenin. The second covers the Party's history from 1919 to the present. The third turns to current conditions and tasks. The fourth sets out the deployment of the campaign and five practical requirements.

Chen's central move is to derive the point from historical materialism. Marx's view that the masses make history, and the Communist Manifesto's description of the proletarian movement as that of the immense majority, are presented as the basis for how a Marxist party must treat the people. Chen reads Lenin as adding that a party's strength comes from the masses and that bureaucracy is a major source of popular discontent, so improving work style is necessary. Chen then argues that Chinese Communist experience confirms this, citing Mao Zedong's "bastion of iron" remark, the Central Soviet Area ditty on cadres, and the "half a quilt" story. Under present conditions, the author says, Chinese modernization and a turbulent international environment require reliance on the people. Chen adds that problems of impure thinking, organisation and work style persist and that the Party faces the "four tests" and "four dangers".

Chen calls for five things: strengthening ideals and convictions through Marxist historical materialism and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era; practising the mass line and addressing people's pressing concerns; targeted action against formalism, bureaucracy and disguised variants of the "four undesirable work styles", with joint investigation of misconduct and corruption; enforcing discipline, including mass discipline; and persistence, since work-style problems recur. The aim is to make work-style building regular and long-term and to maintain the Party's vanguard character. Read the original if you want an example of how a senior Party historian presents the theoretical lineage and official rationale for the 2025 campaign on the eight-point regulation.
quoteEn: The most important thing in strengthening work-style building is to grasp the core issue of maintaining the Party's flesh-and-blood ties with the people and to persevere until results are achieved.
quoteZh: 加强作风建设最重要的是抓住保持党同人民群众的血肉联系这个核心问题，持之以恒抓出成效

glossary.explanation: A set of rules on officials' conduct adopted by the Politburo in December 2012, shortly after the 18th Party Congress. It curbs formalism, bureaucracy, extravagance and similar practices.
A Party principle, associated with Mao Zedong, of working "from the masses, to the masses". Cadres are to gather popular views and turn them into policy.
Official shorthand for formalism, bureaucracy, hedonism and extravagance. It has been the target of work-style campaigns since 2012.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The official name for China's path of modernization. It is presented as distinct from Western models and was elaborated at the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: A cultural banner raised high in the fires of the War of Resistance against Japan
st: The cultural resistance led by the Communist Party of China and its great significance
zh: 抗日烽火中高擎的文化旗帜
zhSub: 中国共产党领导的文化抗战及其伟大意义
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 18 June 2025, Wang Jiping argues that the cultural resistance led by the Communist Party of China was an integral part of the Chinese people's War of Resistance against Japan, alongside its military, political and economic dimensions. In Wang's account, it repelled Japanese imperialism's cultural aggression and enslavement, defended Chinese national culture, lifted morale and gathered the spirit of the nation.

The article is organised in three parts. The first presents cultural resistance as a struggle to defend Chinese culture against Japanese policies in occupied areas. The second sets out the Party's role as the mainstay of that effort, covering united-front organisations, the press, literature and art, music, academic work, science and education. The third turns to the significance of cultural resistance for national spirit and for the development of Chinese culture.

Wang describes Japanese cultural policy as destruction of institutions and books, persecution of intellectuals, slogans such as the "New Order in East Asia", and enslaving education. Against this, the article says, Party-led patriotic cultural workers built a broad cultural united front, from the 1936 declaration signed by Lu Xun, Guo Moruo and Mao Dun to the 1938 founding of the All-China Anti-Aggression Association of Literary and Art Circles in Wuhan. Wang cites works such as the Yellow River Cantata and the March of the Volunteers, the founding of Marxist history, philosophy and economics, and cadre-training schools in the base areas. Drawing on Mao Zedong, Wang holds that because the new culture after the May Fourth Movement was proletarian-led New Democratic culture, cultural resistance had to be led by the Party.

Wang concludes that the Party's leadership carried forward the great spirit of resistance, opposed Kuomintang cultural dictatorship and feudal or capitulationist currents, and advanced the adaptation of Marxism to Chinese conditions. In this reading, it moved Chinese culture from bourgeois new culture to New Democratic culture and opened a new stage in cultural development. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-state scholarship frames wartime culture as Party-led and as a foundation for later Marxist scholarship in China.
quoteEn: The cultural resistance led by the Communist Party of China was in fact a battle to defend the culture of the Chinese nation.
quoteZh: 中国共产党领导的文化抗战，实际上是中华民族的文化保卫战

glossary.explanation: The extension of the Party's united-front strategy to writers, artists and intellectuals of differing political views who were willing to support resistance to Japan.
Mao Zedong's term from around 1940 for an anti-imperialist, anti-feudal culture of the people under proletarian leadership, which he distinguished from both bourgeois culture and socialist culture.

glossary.en: adaptation of Marxism to Chinese conditions
glossary.explanation: The Party's formula for applying Marxism to China's concrete circumstances and history, associated with Mao Zedong's writings of the late 1930s and 1940s.
The 1919 student and intellectual movement for national renewal. Party historiography treats it as the point at which Marxism entered China and new culture became proletarian-led.

t: Deepening the joint investigation and joint handling of unhealthy work styles and corruption
zh: 深入推进风腐同查同治
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 18 June 2025, takes up the instruction that the Party should deepen the joint investigation and joint handling of unhealthy work styles and corruption. Tao Yuanhao notes that Xi Jinping raised the point at the Fourth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection, and that the session's communiqué called for a mechanism to push the correction of work styles and the fight against corruption forward as one. Tao argues that this approach reflects a higher level of understanding of the regularities of Party conduct and anti-corruption work in the new era.

The article has three sections. The first sets out why the approach is a major strategic consideration for keeping the Party healthy. The second explains why work-style problems and corruption share one root, and describes two directions of inquiry. The third sets out practical measures for building a clean political ecosystem.

On the theory, Tao draws on the formula that Party spirit, Party conduct and Party discipline form an organic whole, with Party spirit as the foundation, conduct as its expression and discipline as its safeguard. The article presents the approach as a summary of practice since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and as a requirement of the Party's self-reform. In Tao's account, bad work styles and corruption are two faces of one problem: both stem from wavering ideals and convictions, and corruption often begins with a dinner, a gift or a red envelope. "Investigating corruption through work style" follows such clues to hidden bribery and power-for-money deals. "Correcting work style through corruption cases" examines the extravagance and indulgence behind corrupt officials.

Tao proposes that joint investigation should punish cases where the two problems intertwine, by enforcing the eight-point regulation, pursuing new and hidden forms of corruption, and investigating bribe-givers together with bribe-takers. Joint handling should remove common roots through Party-spirit education, institutional improvements such as multi-department supervision of the "four unhealthy tendencies", and strict discipline. Tao also calls for stopping small problems early and for using big data to find leads. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of the rationale and the working methods behind current Party discipline campaigns.
quoteEn: Unhealthy work styles and corruption differ in how they appear, but in fact they are two sides of one problem, sharing the same root and origin.
quoteZh: 不正之风和腐败问题的表现形式有所不同，但二者实则互为表里、同根同源。

glossary.pinyin: fēng fǔ tóng chá tóng zhì
glossary.en: joint investigation and joint handling of unhealthy work styles and corruption
glossary.literal: investigate and handle work style and corruption together
glossary.explanation: A Party discipline principle that treats unhealthy work styles and corruption as linked problems to be investigated and addressed together. It was written into the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).
An official term for the Party's efforts to correct its own faults and maintain its character, frequently used in Xi Jinping-era discourse.
Rules adopted in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism among officials. They are seen as the opening step of the new-era campaign on Party conduct.
The official shorthand for formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, the work-style problems targeted by Party discipline.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Accelerating the transformation of scientific and technological achievements in the new era
zh: 加快新时代科技成果转化
paras: Qu Dacheng takes up the problem of getting scientific and technological achievements out of the laboratory and into production, a step the article treats as the link between science and application. Qu argues that accelerating this transformation is a priority for China as states compete for the commanding heights of a new technological and industrial revolution. The piece is a policy commentary that follows the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called for deepening reform of the mechanisms for transforming scientific and technological achievements and strengthening the national technology transfer system.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why transformation matters: for high-level scientific and technological self-reliance, for forming new quality productive forces, and for industrial innovation. The second names four key elements, namely technology, people, finance and markets, and discusses the science base, education and talent, and financial backing. The third proposes new pathways, drawing on quotations from Xi Jinping and on the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference.

In Qu's account, transformation is the point where innovation chains meet industrial chains, and its weakness is the so-called "valley of death", where many results remain idle in laboratories. Qu holds that the new-type whole-nation system should be used to strengthen enterprises as the main body of innovation, speed up work on key core technologies and deepen industry–university–research integration. The concrete measures cover government guidance and top-level design, shared pilot-scale testing platforms, and institutional reform such as granting researchers rights over职务 service-related results through an "empowerment + transfer + agreed income" model. They also include training professional technology managers and building a science-and-technology finance system with insurance, risk-compensation funds and long-term government guidance funds.

Qu concludes that a combination of state guidance, enterprise leadership, talent development, supportive law and policy, and finance suited to innovation can turn more original and frontier technologies into real productive forces. The article presents this as raising China's position in global industrial and value chains and supporting high-quality development. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official policy agenda on technology transfer and its reform measures as presented in a Party theoretical journal.
quoteEn: The transformation of scientific and technological achievements is an \"incubator\" linking technological innovation with industrial development, and above all an important \"gateway\" for seamlessly connecting the innovation chain and the industrial chain.
quoteZh: 科技成果转化是衔接科技创新和产业发展的“孵化器”，更是促进创新链和产业链无缝对接的重要“关口”。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by innovation, high technology and high efficiency, in contrast to traditional growth models.
An official goal since the late 2010s that shifts emphasis from fast growth to quality, efficiency and innovation in the economy.
An official term for mobilising state, market and social resources nationwide to achieve major scientific and technological goals.
Professionals who evaluate, market and broker technologies between research institutions, enterprises and investors.

t: Strengthening the protection and use of revolutionary cultural relics
zh: 加强革命文物保护利用
paras: Gao Yifan takes up how revolutionary cultural relics should be protected and put to use in the new era. Opening with Xi Jinping's statements that such relics carry the Party's and the people's history and that protecting them is a shared responsibility of the whole Party and society, Gao argues for a combined programme. It rests on scientific protection, activation of the relics' contemporary value, wider social reach and durable institutional mechanisms.

The article, published in Red Flag Manuscript, is organised in four parts. The first deals with building a scientific protection system; the second with activating the relics' value today; the third with expanding their social influence; and the fourth with long-term mechanisms. Gao cites figures from the National Cultural Heritage Administration: over 36,000 registered immovable revolutionary relics and more than one million movable items or sets. Many sites, Gao notes, still suffer from disrepair and inadequate protection.

Gao's core argument is that protection and use must move together under the principle of 'upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground' (shouzheng chuangxin). On protection, Gao calls for grading by historical value, degree of endangerment and difficulty of conservation, not only by administrative level. Gao also wants detailed classification, stronger technology such as 3D scanning, virtual reconstruction and AI, and dedicated regulations following the revised Cultural Relics Protection Law of 2024. On use, Gao proposes integration with cultural tourism and rural revitalisation, while warning that this must not become mere 'sightseeing with a plaque'. Gao also proposes adding relics to the national education system, including the 'large-scale ideological and political course', and building a short-video and new-media communication matrix. Social coordination and international exhibitions are meant to raise cultural soft power and international discourse power.

Gao concludes by proposing long-term mechanisms. These include a national coordinating body, giving revolutionary relics more weight in the 15th Five-Year Plan for cultural heritage, a special central fund with local budget lines and social capital, and performance supervision of spending. Gao also calls for interdisciplinary training that combines conservation skills with Party history, Marxist theory and communication studies, and for a professional qualification system. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-affiliated researcher sets out current policy priorities for 'red heritage' work, from legal and technological protection to education, tourism and overseas outreach.
quoteEn: Integrating revolutionary relics with cultural tourism is by no means simple 'sightseeing with a plaque'; it must be pursued with reverence for history and culture, balancing tourism development with relic protection, holding the safety bottom line and cherishing the spiritual wealth the relics contain.
quoteZh: 革命文物与文旅融合绝非简单“挂牌观光”，必须秉承敬畏历史、敬畏文化之心，统筹好旅游发展和文物保护，筑牢安全底线，珍视革命文物蕴含的精神财富。

glossary.explanation: Sites and objects connected with the Chinese Communist Party's revolutionary history, such as former headquarters, documents and personal items. They are treated in official discourse as a core part of 'red' heritage.

glossary.en: upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground
glossary.explanation: A formula stressed by Xi Jinping, including in his June 2023 speech on cultural inheritance. It asks that work stay true to core ideals and orientation while adopting new methods.
A policy concept that extends ideological and political education beyond the classroom into society, museums and real-life settings.
China's medium-term national planning cycle. The article refers to the planning round for 2026–2030 and to the evaluation of the preceding 14th Five-Year Plan.

t: Establishing and improving a long-term mechanism for building socialist cultural and ethical progress
zh: 建立健全精神文明建设长效机制
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Economic Daily in June 2025, takes up Xi Jinping's recent instruction on spiritual civilization work. The instruction calls for stronger organisational leadership, deeper reform and innovation, and broad social mobilisation, so as to form a long-term mechanism in which all parties share responsibility. Sun Cunliang argues that this requirement both distils historical experience and answers present-day conditions, and that it points the way to high-quality development of spiritual civilization work.

The article opens with the Dragon Boat Festival activities run through New Era Civilization Practice Centres, then proceeds in three parts. The first reviews the Party's experience from the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978) onwards, citing resolutions of the Sixth Plenum of the 12th Central Committee and the Sixth Plenum of the 14th Central Committee, the later leadership system, and measures since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second explains why such a mechanism fits the era. The third sets out three practical directions.

Sun's central claim is that spiritual civilization is a systemic, long-term task that cannot be left to cultural departments or to campaign-style governance. The author gives three grounds: the people's expectations have shifted with the change in the principal contradiction, the work cuts across every field and requires coordination among Party committees, government, enterprises, social organisations and citizens, and shaping people's thinking is gradual and faces the long-term, complex influence of Western ideology. Institutional mechanisms are presented as the way to overcome the 'gust of wind' effect of campaigns. Sun then proposes strengthening Party leadership through a 'single chessboard' approach and performance assessment, deepening innovation through the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) reforms and digital technologies, and mobilising enterprises, charities and volunteers.

Sun concludes that institutional innovation, coordination among actors and pooling of resources will let civilization practice endure and supply ideological guarantees and moral nourishment for national rejuvenation. Spiritual and cultural needs are linked to common prosperity in the realm of spiritual life.
