Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Party theorists present the institutional logic behind spiritual civilization work and its link to Xi Jinping Thought on Culture.
quoteEn: Building a long-term mechanism of joint management for spiritual civilization means using institutional mechanisms to overcome the 'gust of wind' effect of campaign-style governance, so that the work is sustained and achieves results.
quoteZh: 构建齐抓共管的精神文明建设长效机制，就是以制度机制克服“运动式”治理导致的“一阵风”现象，推动精神文明建设久久为功、善作善成。

glossary.explanation: A Party-state term, prominent since the 1980s, for efforts to cultivate morality, ideals, culture and social etiquette alongside material development.
Grassroots centres, set up across urban and rural areas, that organise volunteer services, education and cultural activities promoting official values.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all, here extended by the author to spiritual and cultural life.

t: Fundamental guidelines and practical paths for building a strong education nation in the new era
zh: 新时代教育强国建设的根本遵循与实践路径
paras: This commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in June 2025, asks how China should build a strong education nation (jiaoyu qiangguo) and answers by interpreting Xi Jinping's September 2024 speech at the National Education Conference, his Qiushi article "Accelerating the Building of a Strong Education Nation" and the 2024–2035 outline for the goal. Chen Junjing argues that these texts provide the fundamental guidelines and the practical path for the task.
The article has three parts: the political direction and value coordinates of the effort; the practical path to a high-quality education system; and the supporting systems needed to sustain it.

On direction, Chen stresses the Party's overall leadership, Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education. Chen also calls for a people-centred approach that narrows urban–rural gaps, and for a global outlook that contributes Chinese educational wisdom to a community with a shared future for mankind. On the path, Chen proposes integrating education, science and technology, and talent, with universities reforming disciplines, training models and evaluation. Chen also proposes strengthening original innovation, and opening education to the outside world through a cycle of input, integration and output.

For support, Chen calls for institutional reform, deeper integration of AI and digital tools, a stronger teaching force guided by the spirit of educators, and industry–education integration across the education, talent, industry and innovation chains. Chen concludes that educational strength should become talent, scientific and development strength, underpinning Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese academics are presenting official education policy in 2025.
quoteEn: Building a strong education nation in the new era is a systematic and historic undertaking: institutional innovation should release vitality, the digital revolution should reshape the ecosystem, and a global vision should open up new horizons.
quoteZh: 新时代教育强国建设是一项系统性、历史性工程，要以制度创新释放活力，以数字革命重塑生态，以全球视野开拓格局。

glossary.explanation: A policy goal of making China a world leader in education by 2035, set out in the 2024–2035 outline issued by the Party Central Committee and the State Council.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions.
The official fundamental task of Chinese education: cultivating moral character alongside knowledge and skills.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept of international relations, promoted since the early 2010s as a framework for global cooperation.
The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models.

t: Improving the comprehensive internet governance system
zh: 健全网络综合治理体系
paras: This commentary in Guangming Daily takes up the call of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) to improve the comprehensive internet governance system. Zeng Runxi argues that this system is now an important part of China's national governance system and that building it is a complex systems project. It requires, the author says, grasping the laws of internet development and applying systems thinking so that governance becomes more effective and the online environment "clearer and more orderly".

The article is organised under four headings: upholding the Party's overall leadership; deepening reform of the internet management system; maintaining a healthy online ecosystem; and coordinating development and security. Each section draws heavily on statements by Xi Jinping on cyberspace work and turns them into practical tasks for Party committees, officials, government departments, companies and users.

On leadership, Zeng argues that the Party must keep control of the internet and that responsibility for online ideological work must be fully enforced. The author also calls for Party building to be integrated with business operations in internet firms and online social organisations, and for better online skills among leading cadres. On management, Zeng proposes integrating governance actors, levels, institutions and tools, and covering the whole process from prevention to feedback. A pattern of Party leadership, government management, corporate responsibility, social oversight and netizen self-discipline is to be built, with the cyberspace administration coordinating across departments.

On content and security, Zeng calls for strengthening mainstream ideas and opinion, building the Party's innovative theory into the common ideological foundation, countering mistaken trends and harmful information, and improving the supply of online content. The author also urges legal safeguards, continued "Clear and Bright" campaigns and protection of minors. On generative artificial intelligence, Zeng proposes tiered and classified management, a regulatory sandbox, traceability rules and domestic core technologies. The article ends by urging international cooperation and a community with a shared future in cyberspace, offering "Chinese wisdom and Chinese solutions". Read the original if you want a concise statement of how the Party's current policy line on internet governance is being explained in the official press.
quoteEn: The Party's overall leadership over cyberspace and informatization work is the essential feature of the Chinese approach to governing the internet.
quoteZh: 党对网信工作的全面领导，是中国特色治网之道的本质特征。

glossary.explanation: A policy concept for governing cyberspace through coordinated Party, government, corporate, social and technical means. The Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) called for improving it.

glossary.literal: clear and bright series of special actions
glossary.explanation: Recurring special campaigns run by the cyberspace authorities against illegal or harmful online content and behaviour.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future in cyberspace
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's extension of the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind to internet governance, stressing international cooperation and shared governance.
A controlled setting in which new technologies can be tested under regulatory supervision before wider rules are applied.

t: Continuing to make work-style building regular and long-term
zh: 持续推进作风建设常态化长效化
paras: This short commentary, published in Beijing Daily in June 2025, asks how work-style building (zuofeng jianshe) should be pursued so that it becomes a regular and lasting feature of Party life. Wang and Wang argue that work style is a decisive entry point for full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, and that it must be sustained through the eight-point regulation of the Central Committee rather than treated as a passing campaign. The authors link the issue to the Party's survival in power.

The piece opens with the March 2025 notice calling for a Party-wide study and education campaign on implementing the eight-point regulation, and with Xi Jinping's remarks in Henan on that campaign. It then has three parts: the essential requirement and core problem of work-style building; why work style is the key entry point for full and rigorous self-governance of the Party; and three directions for opening up new prospects. Historical examples from the revolutionary period are used as illustrations.

Wang and Wang contend that work-style problems are at root problems of Party spirit (dangxing), and that the core issue is maintaining close ties between the Party and the people. Departing from the masses is, in their words, the greatest danger for a Marxist party in power. They argue that the eight-point regulation works as a small opening that can set the whole effort in motion: tackling the "four malpractices", especially formalism and bureaucratism and their covert variants, while exposing linked corruption. Their three directions are to trace problems to their root by strengthening ideals and convictions; to lead from the top, with senior leaders setting the example, citing Mao Zedong and Zhu De; and to keep work style tied to the Party's central tasks, handled constantly and in detail.

The authors conclude that using the eight-point regulation as the entry point, and letting work-style building drive full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, is an important response to the great changes unseen in a century. They call for perseverance in rectifying Party conduct and enforcing discipline, so that the effort supports Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party theorists in 2025 frame the eight-point regulation campaign and its links to Party spirit and mass-line ideas.
quoteEn: Work-style building has only a continuous tense, never a completed one; it is always on the road.
quoteZh: 作风建设只有进行时,没有完成时,永远在路上。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: Slogan associated with Xi Jinping since 2014, covering Party discipline, anti-corruption and internal Party management.
Rules adopted in December 2012 on officials' conduct, such as simplifying meetings, reducing formalities, curbing banquets and perks, and improving investigation and research.
Formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, named in Party campaigns as the main work-style failings.
The qualities of loyalty, discipline and commitment to the Party's purpose expected of members.
Official term for the Party's path of national development, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: The moral content of the spiritual lineage of Chinese Communists
zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系的道德内涵
paras: Wei Jianguo asks what moral content lies inside the "spiritual lineage of Chinese Communists", the series of revolutionary spirits that begins with the great founding spirit of the Party. The article argues that this lineage and the lofty morality of Chinese Communists are essentially the same thing. It therefore treats the lineage as a direct source for moral construction in the new era, and says that distilling its moral values is an important task for contemporary Marxist ethics in China.

The piece is a short commentary first published in Guangming Daily in June 2025. It has three parts: the lineage as bearer of a high moral spirit; the lineage as a "textbook" of moral cultivation across the Party's history; and its role in supporting citizens' moral construction today. Wei draws on remarks by Xi Jinping and discusses the Lei Feng spirit and the Jiao Yulu spirit as examples.

Wei first lists over twenty values in the lineage, such as seeking truth, self-sacrifice, hard struggle, selflessness, collectivism and integrity. Wei then condenses them into ten moral requirements: holding to ideals, seeking truth from facts, fearing no sacrifice, serving the people, hard struggle, daring to blaze new trails, selfless dedication, collectivism, patriotism, and self-reliance. These are said to have stayed constant from the New Democratic Revolution to the new era, even as their expression changes. Patriotism, for example, once meant resisting foreign invasion and now means striving for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Wei argues that named spirits such as Lei Feng and Jiao Yulu serve as moral exemplars, in line with the Party's long reliance on model-setting. Wei adds that the lineage's moral spirit matches "advanced socialist morality" in content and so feeds citizen moral education.

Wei concludes that Marxist ethics should systematically uncover the moral genes, spirit and requirements in the lineage and summarise Communists' virtues. This would enrich the socialist moral value system and guide moral practice, so as to build a moral system that matches Chinese modernization. Party members and cadres are urged to honour loyalty to the Party, public virtue that benefits the people, and self-discipline. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese ethics scholars link Party spirit to moral education and citizen morality.
quoteEn: There is no essential difference between the spiritual lineage of Chinese Communists and the lofty morality of Chinese Communists.
quoteZh: 中国共产党人精神谱系和中国共产党人崇高道德之间没有本质区别。

glossary.zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系
glossary.explanation: An official term for the series of named spirits (for example the Long March spirit, the Yan'an spirit, the Lei Feng spirit) said to have been formed in the Party's history. It was formalised from 2021, starting with the founding spirit.

A formulation Xi Jinping put forward in 2021. It sums up the founders' qualities as upholding truth and ideals, fulfilling the original mission, fearing no sacrifice, and being loyal to the Party and the people.
The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, set out as a core Party theme since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The official long-term national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, closely tied to the Chinese Dream.
A term in official moral-construction discourse for the higher tier of morality expected of Party members and exemplary citizens, as distinct from basic norms for all.

t: Promoting understanding through action: making Party members' pledges and their fulfilment real
zh: 以行促知做实党员承诺践诺
paras: This short commentary, published in Study Times on 16 June 2025, argues that grassroots Party building should stress not only learning in order to act but also acting in order to know, so that practice deepens understanding. Liu Qiangjin, writing from the Suzhou Municipal Tobacco Monopoly Bureau (Company) in Anhui, presents the bureau's practice of Party members' pledges and their fulfilment as a vehicle for this. The author claims that such practice unifies study, reflection and application, and makes ideological and political education reach members' minds and hearts.

The article sets out a management scheme the bureau calls the 'seven haves': specific items, a certain weight, an environment and atmosphere, actual action, process supervision, application of results, and safeguard mechanisms. Each element is described with concrete requirements, ending with a note on the Party's share of the workforce and the regulations on Party work in state-owned enterprises.

Liu's core argument is that pledges must avoid empty, formalistic declarations. Pledges should be tied to the unit's development goals, to the member's own weaknesses and to social responsibility. They should be challenging, targeted, feasible and measurable, with quantified targets and deadlines rather than vague words such as 'improve'. They are to be declared publicly at Party meetings, displayed on notice boards, desk plates and short videos, and reported monthly. Each is overseen by a supervisor, normally the branch secretary or a committee member, who vets quality, checks progress at least quarterly and assesses completion, with roughly 10 and at most 20 members each. Results feed into democratic life meetings, 'two excellents and one pioneer' selection, cadre assessment and talks with members, but are not used directly for annual performance appraisal, so that members are encouraged to set demanding pledges.

Liu concludes that the scheme, with a single A4 page per pledge, flat supervision and closed-loop management, helps integrate Party building with business operations. The article states that Party members make up about 50 per cent of the bureau's staff. The author claims the practice has deepened members' ties with the public, strengthened their political, ideological, theoretical and emotional identification with the Party, and raised their sense of achievement, mission and ability. Read the original if you want a detailed, practice-level example of how a grassroots Party organisation in a state-owned enterprise operationalises member pledges and their supervision.
quoteEn: Party members' pledges must avoid the formalism of empty declarations.
quoteZh: 党员承诺切忌空泛化表态的形式主义

glossary.literal: Party members' making and fulfilling of pledges
glossary.explanation: A grassroots Party-building practice in which members publicly commit to concrete tasks or self-improvement goals and are then checked on fulfilling them.
The bureau's own framework of seven requirements for managing the pledge process, from specific items to safeguard mechanisms.
The Party's regular commendation of outstanding Party members, outstanding Party workers and advanced grassroots Party organisations.
Regular Party branch meetings in which members review their conduct and engage in criticism and self-criticism.

t: Easing burdens, empowering cadres, encouraging responsible action
zh: 减负赋能激励担当作为
source: China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News, 16 June 2025, p. 3
paras: This short commentary, first published in the Party's discipline-inspection newspaper in June 2025, asks how the campaign against formalism and bureaucracy can lighten the load on grassroots cadres without weakening their sense of responsibility. Yang argues that relief from burdens must be built into the Party-wide study and education drive on the spirit of the Central Committee's eight-point regulation, so that cadres can act with fewer encumbrances.

The piece opens by recalling Xi Jinping's instructions on easing grassroots burdens: clarify powers and duties, set no unrealistic targets, and avoid meetings and documents without substance. It credits local authorities with trimming documents and meetings and standardising inspections and assessments. It then notes that problems persist, and ends with measures on mechanisms and incentives.

Yang's central claim is that formalism and bureaucracy are stubborn and recurrent and keep reappearing in new forms. Examples include vanity projects, padded reports, mechanical process management and digital tools that become a "fingertip burden". Yang urges targeted investigation, moving from solving single problems to solving whole categories of them, and standing mechanisms such as meeting-free weeks, merged meetings and shared research data. Yang adds that burdens that show up at the grassroots often originate higher up, so Party organisations at every level must take responsibility. Burden reduction, in this account, does not mean reducing responsibility.

Yang proposes better cadre appraisal that rewards practical results and commitment to the grassroots. Discipline inspection organs should keep up routine supervision and apply the "four forms" of accountability precisely, combining strict management with care. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party media frame the link between combating formalism and motivating grassroots cadres.
quoteEn: Reducing burdens does not mean reducing responsibility or the willingness to take it on. It means letting the grassroots shed burdens they should not bear and shoulder the duties they should, so they can settle in and focus on solving problems and doing practical things for the people.
quoteZh: 减负不是减责任、减担当，而是让基层卸下不该承担的负担，担起该担之责，沉下心沉下身，集中精力为群众解难题办实事。

glossary.explanation: A set of rules on official conduct adopted by the Politburo in December 2012. They target extravagance, bureaucratic practices and formalism among Party officials.
Party term for work done for show, such as excessive paperwork, meetings and inspections, and for officials detached from the people. The Party treats them as persistent faults to be corrected.
A campaign to cut the paperwork, meetings, assessments and tasks that higher levels pass down to township and village cadres.
A graduated approach to discipline. It runs from criticism and warnings, through light and heavy sanctions, to criminal investigation for the most serious cases.

t: The most important thing in building a good work style is to "be serious"
zh: 抓作风建设最重要的是“讲认真”
paras: Lin Xueqi takes up Xi Jinping's statement that the most important thing in building a Party work style (zuofeng) is to "be serious" (jiang renzhen). Without seriousness, Lin argues, cadres drift into perfunctory work, overlook problems in front of them, and fall back on formalism. The commentary, published in Guangming Daily, presents this principle as the basic guide for the current study and education campaign on thoroughly implementing the central Party's eight-point regulation and for making that regulation take root.

The piece has three parts. It first traces "being serious" as a long-standing tradition of Party governance, citing Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin, Hu Jintao and then Xi Jinping. It then explains why seriousness is intrinsic to deepening work-style building. Finally it sets out four areas of practice: political clarity, deepening rectification, handling work style and corruption together, and cultural cultivation.

Lin's core claim is that work-style building is long-term and prone to relapse. Good style is, in Lin's words, hard to repair once damaged, and bad practices regrow "like leeks after cutting", as Xi put it, because their stubbornness and recurrence were underestimated. Seriousness therefore means persistence, attention to detail and institutional arrangements that tackle problems at source, in the "nail-driving" spirit. Lin also argues that corruption among cadres often begins with style problems and that each feeds the other. Investigating corruption through style problems and correcting style through corruption cases should therefore proceed together, to reduce existing corruption and curb new cases.

Lin concludes that the Party must keep to the conviction that seriousness matters most, and must treat work-style building as always "on the road". Concrete proposals include combining concentrated campaigns with routine governance, field research into hidden variants of the "four undesirable work styles", and stronger integrity-culture education that draws on classical sources about upright officials. Lin says a sound Party style will lift government, social and popular conduct and gather strength for Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-school commentary presents the eight-point regulation campaign and the rhetoric of work-style discipline.
quoteEn: The difficulty of correcting bad work styles lies in preventing a rebound.
quoteZh: 纠风之难，难在防止反弹。

glossary.explanation: A set of rules adopted by the Politburo in December 2012 to curb formalism, bureaucracy and extravagance among officials, covering matters such as meetings, travel and official hospitality.
The Party's long-standing term for improving the conduct, attitudes and methods of Party members and officials, treated as a matter of Party spirit and discipline.
Formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, the four problems targeted by the Party's work-style campaigns since 2012.
The official formulation of China's development path, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models of modernization.

t: Leading social revolution through the Party's self-reform: internal logic, spiritual strength and practical orientation
zh: 以党的自我革命引领社会革命：内生逻辑、精神伟力与实践指向
source: Study and Practice (Xuexi yu shijian), 2025 no. 2
paras: Taking up the formulation advanced by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), Zhang Li asks why the Communist Party of China can lead profound social change by reforming itself. The article argues that leading social revolution through the Party's self-reform is a distinctive dynamic of Chinese modernization, rooted in historical materialism. It is presented as the Party's key historical experience and a precondition for further comprehensively deepening reform.

The article has three main sections, followed by a short conclusion. The first examines the internal logic of the idea in terms of value, history and practice. The second turns to the spiritual strength that sustains it, organised around historical consciousness, initiative and creativity. The third sets out the practical orientation in five areas: theoretical innovation, political stance, spiritual will, institutional norms, and reform and innovation. Zhang draws on Marx and Engels's Communist Manifesto, on Xi Jinping's statements, and on the Party's history from the 1920s to the present.

In the first section, Zhang argues that historical materialism gives the Party a people-centred value stance, the goal of the free and all-round development of the individual, and a method of advancing in stages. The Party's social revolution is therefore said to share the same subject, direction and process as its self-reform. The second section holds that the Party's historical awareness is shown in its three historical resolutions (1945, 1981, 2021), and that it awakens the people's initiative through the Party's own pioneering and fighting spirit. The third section presents the Party's self-reform and the social revolution as reinforcing each other. Self-reform aims to lead the revolution, and the revolution is judged by whether it succeeds. In turn, the revolution depends on self-reform as its fundamental guarantee.

Zhang concludes that willingness to reform itself is what distinguishes the Party from other parties. The author calls it a "mission-driven" party, set apart from what the article describes as the self-interested, power-seeking and task-oriented parties of the West, and sees this as a major development of modern party theory and practice. The proposals include adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, keeping a people-centred stance and strengthening full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Read the original if you want a detailed account of how Party-building scholarship in China links the Party's self-reform to historical materialism and to the project of national rejuvenation.
quoteEn: Being bold in self-reform is the distinctive mark that sets the Communist Party of China apart from other parties, and the spirit of self-reform is the spiritual support that keeps the Party vital and vigorous.
quoteZh: 勇于自我革命是中国共产党区别于其他政党的显著标志，自我革命精神是党永葆生机活力的精神支撑

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed since the 18th Party Congress (2012), presented by Xi Jinping as the Party's second answer to the question of how to escape the historical cycle of rise and fall. It refers to the Party's efforts to discipline, purify and improve itself.
The official name for China's path to modernization, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party-discipline and anti-corruption drive carried out since 2012, which stresses institutions, supervision and accountability at every level.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: An official formula for the ongoing project of fitting Marxist theory to China's conditions and to contemporary circumstances.

t: Strengthening Party building in the "three new" sectors in the new era: logic and optimised paths
zh: 新时代加强“三新”党建的逻辑理路与优化路径
paras: The 20th Party Congress report (2022) was the first to speak of Party building in the "three new" sectors: new economic organizations, new social organizations and new employment groups such as couriers, food-delivery riders, ride-hailing and truck drivers, and livestreamers. Liu and Wang ask why such Party building is needed, what it is, and how it should proceed. They argue that it follows from a theoretical, a historical and a practical logic, and they propose three paths to strengthen it.

After a literature review that finds existing studies too propagandistic, too macro-level and too short on historical comparison, the article sets out its three logics in turn. It then traces the evolution from "one new" to "two new" to "three new" Party building in four stages from 1978 to the present. The final section turns to practice. It draws on official statistics, Party documents and speeches by Xi Jinping, and cites Marx, Engels, Lenin and Mao Zedong.

The theoretical logic rests on the principle that "where there are masses, there is the Party", which the authors trace from Marx, Engels and Lenin through Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin, Hu Jintao and Xi Jinping. The historical logic describes a shift from simply founding Party organizations, to making them effective, to strengthening their political and organizational functions. The practical logic holds that the "three new" sectors are a weak link in grassroots Party building. The article cites 174 million new economic entities in 2023, 881,000 social organizations and 84 million platform workers. In the authors' account, full and rigorous self-governance of the Party requires comprehensive coverage in content, targets, responsibility and institutions, so it requires strengthening Party building in these sectors.

The authors propose three paths. First, secure the Party's leadership through a coordinated management system, writing Party building into company and organization charters, and cross-appointment of Party members and management. Second, integrate Party building with business development through "Party building plus" activities and service centres for workers. Third, build the "three new" Party organizations themselves with a reformist spirit and strict standards, across political, ideological, organizational, disciplinary, institutional and anti-corruption work. Read the original if you want a systematic official-academic account of how Party building in the private, social-organization and platform-labour sectors is justified and organized, with statistics and a chronology of Party documents.
quoteEn: Strengthening Party building in the "three new" sectors and upholding the Party's comprehensive leadership over "three new" organizations and groups is a concrete requirement, and an important arena, for carrying full and rigorous self-governance of the Party into every "nerve ending" in the new era.
quoteZh: 加强“三新”党建，坚持党对“三新”组织和群体的全面领导，成为新时代全面从严治党落实到每一根“末梢神经”的具体要求与重要场域。

glossary.literal: Party building in the three new
glossary.explanation: Shorthand introduced in the 20th Party Congress report (2022) for Party building in new economic organizations, new social organizations and new employment groups.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping-era approach to Party discipline and organization, spanning political, ideological, organizational, conduct, disciplinary and institutional work and anti-corruption efforts.
Non-public-sector economic entities such as private and foreign-invested enterprises and self-employed businesses.
Workers in platform and internet-based forms of employment, such as couriers, delivery riders and ride-hailing drivers.

glossary.zh: 哪里有群众哪里就有党
glossary.pinyin: nǎlǐ yǒu qúnzhòng nǎlǐ jiù yǒu dǎng
glossary.en: where there are masses, there is the Party
glossary.explanation: A principle of Party building that Party organizations should be established wherever people work and live.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Knowledge, ideas and values in the discipline of CPC history and Party building
zh: 论中共党史党建学中的知识、理念与价值观
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2025 no. 3
paras: Writing about the newly designated first-level discipline of CPC history and Party building, Shang asks what its content should consist of as China builds an autonomous knowledge system in philosophy and the social sciences. The article's thesis is that the discipline needs three interlocking components: knowledge, ideas and values. Shang presents these as dialectically united and as the basis on which the discipline performs its functions.

The article opens with Xi Jinping's call to build an autonomous knowledge system, and argues that the discipline should be understood as self-directed, as marked by Chinese characteristics, and as strongly political and ideological. It then takes each component in turn: knowledge, then ideas and values together. It ends by examining how the three relate and by illustrating the relationship with the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea, before offering practical requirements.

Shang defines knowledge as the discipline's foundation, with two tasks: establishing facts and explaining underlying principles. Such knowledge is said to be objective, truthful, systematically complete and publicly credible. Ideas express the subject's opinions and attitudes, since people can disagree about the same facts. The Party's leadership is the example of an idea. Values are the guiding stance the discipline instils in its audience. They are not stated separately in textbooks but are embedded in the ideas and knowledge. The three differ in the subject–object relation: in presenting knowledge the subject respects the object, in forming ideas both count, and in guiding values the subject leads. Shang uses the Korean War to illustrate: troop numbers and campaigns are knowledge, judgements on why the war began and its justice are ideas, and the Great Anti-US Aggression Spirit is the value orientation. The aim is to avoid both mechanical materialism and subjective idealism.

Shang concludes that the discipline can secure its place only if knowledge, ideas and values are developed together. The author proposes four practical requirements: study Party history seriously, grasp the Party's practice within Chinese modernization, understand Party building and the Party's self-reform, and firmly trust the Party's leadership. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese scholar defines the content and ideological function of this new discipline and how the discipline links its scholarly claims to political guidance.
quoteEn: Knowledge, ideas and values are internally connected and dialectically unified. They are an indispensable part of the discipline's content, and the basic reliance and fundamental support through which it fulfils its functions.
quoteZh: 知识、理念与价值观，三方面内在联结、辩证统一，既是中共党史党建学学科内容不可或缺的重要组成部分，更是中共党史党建学实现学科功能、发挥学科作用的基本依赖和根本支撑。

glossary.explanation: A goal for Chinese philosophy and social sciences stressed by Xi Jinping since 2022. It calls for building theory and concepts rooted in China's own experience rather than following Western frameworks.
A first-level academic discipline in China, recently established, that studies the history of the Communist Party of China and its organisational development.
The official name for China's path of development under Party leadership, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official term for the Party's efforts to purify and improve itself, including anti-corruption and discipline, stressed under Xi Jinping.

t: Putting the people's city concept into practice in urban development during the 15th Five-Year Plan period
zh: 在“十五五”城市发展中践行人民城市理念
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily in June 2025, asks how Chinese cities should carry out the people's city concept when drawing up their plans for the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030). Deng Zhituan argues that the principle that the people's city is built by the people and for the people, set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), gives the basic direction. Cities should become more liveable, innovative, smart, green, humane and resilient, giving residents a greater sense of gain, happiness and security.

The article has two parts. The first reviews what cities achieved during the 14th Five-Year Plan period in five areas: economic momentum, cultural heritage and digitalisation, livelihood provision, governance, and ecological transition. It then names pressures at home and abroad, including technological competition, the climate crisis, population concentration alongside hollowing-out in some cities, and commercial pressure on historic preservation. The second part sets out several relationships to be balanced in the coming period.

Deng's core argument is that these relationships must be handled with dialectical thinking, and the article gives each a set of practical measures. They include serving national strategy while fixing a city's own position; balancing long-term goals against short-term growth; combining high-quality development with a high quality of life; and pairing digital with green and low-carbon transformation. Deng also covers organic urban renewal with cultural continuity, deeper reform with higher-level opening up, and high-quality development with high-level security. Proposals include a three-tier transmission mechanism from national strategy to local implementation, a 'green GDP' accounting system, '15-minute living circles', small-scale 'embroidery-style' renewal of historic districts, institutional opening-up pilot zones, and a broad security governance system with early-warning mechanisms. The article presents Xi Jinping's work in Xiamen in the 1980s as an example of the people-centred, forward-looking planning it recommends.

Deng concludes that, in the 15th Five-Year Plan period, cities should seize the historical initiative and uphold a people-centred approach, so that the people's city concept is embedded in the key fields of urban construction. The article is a programmatic piece that mixes a review of recent achievements with policy proposals, and it gives little supporting evidence or data. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary on urban planning in 2025 links the people's city concept to concrete planning tools and to the framing of the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: A full-chain mechanism of "decoding cultural genes – protection and use – innovative expression" should be established.
quoteZh: 要建立“文化基因解码—保护利用—创新表达”全链条机制

glossary.explanation: A concept associated with Xi Jinping, who used it in Shanghai in 2019, holding that cities are built by the people and for the people. The 20th Party Congress report (2022) repeated it as a principle of urban development.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030, being drafted in 2025. Provinces and cities prepare their own plans in step with it.
A planning standard under which residents can reach basic services such as education, healthcare, elderly care and shopping within a 15-minute walk of home.
The official policy theme since 2017, which stresses quality, innovation and sustainability over speed of growth.

t: Making the cultivation of Party spirit a lifelong task for Communists
zh: 把锤炼党性作为共产党人的终身课题
paras: This short commentary, first published in Guangming Daily in June 2025, asks how Party members and cadres can build a sound work style. Xu Jian argues that style problems are at root problems of Party spirit (dangxing), so cultivating it must be treated as a lifelong task. The author turns to the Marxist classics to support this and ties the argument to the Central Committee's eight-point regulations.

The article draws on Marx, Engels and Lenin in three sections. The first treats Party spirit as the distinguishing mark of proletarian parties. The second links firm Party spirit to firmness in theory. The third presents practice as the test of Party spirit.

In Xu's reading, Lenin held that "non-partisanship" is a bourgeois product that obscures class contradictions, while strict Party spirit turns class struggle into a conscious, principled one. Engels's criticism of German "absolute socialism" and Lenin's claim that philosophy is partisan lead Xu to argue that theory must align with the proletariat's fundamental interests. Study of theory therefore trains Party spirit, and Xu names Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as the first thing to study. Citing Marx on the Blanquists and Lenin on active participation in Party work, Xu holds that Party spirit shows in conduct, not only in attitude.

Xu concludes that Party spirit is not innate but forged through study and practice. Cadres should keep correcting their political direction, strengthen their commitment to the masses and take responsibility, helped by strict inner-Party life, discipline and the Party's self-reform. Xu says this is how the eight-point regulations can curb the "four undesirable work styles" and problems such as hedonism and inaction. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party-building writing in 2025 draws on Marxist classics to justify work-style campaigns.
quoteEn: Party spirit is not innate; it is forged through constant study and reflection.
quoteZh: 党性不是与生俱来的，而是在不断学习、思考中锤炼出来的。

glossary.explanation: A concept of Party-mindedness, drawn from Lenin's idea of partisanship. In current Chinese usage it means the political stance, discipline and commitment expected of Communist Party members.
Rules on official conduct adopted by the Politburo in December 2012 to curb extravagance, bureaucracy and formalism among officials.
Official shorthand for formalism, bureaucracy, hedonism and extravagance, which Party campaigns since 2012 have targeted.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions.
An official term for the Party's efforts to correct its own problems and maintain discipline, stressed in Party-building discourse since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

t: The meaning of "people-centredness" for deputies to the people's congresses
zh: 人大代表的“人民性”意涵
paras: This commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today on 13 June 2025, asks what the "people-oriented character" (renminxing) of deputies to the people's congresses means and how law secures it. Liu Xiaomei argues that it has two components: putting the people at the centre, and the "Two Linkages". The occasion is the fourth revision of the Deputies Law, adopted by the National People's Congress on 11 March 2025, the first revision made by the full NPC.

The article moves in four steps. It first sets out the value goal of people-centredness, then the principle that deputies keep close ties with the people, with a historical sketch from Mao Zedong through the 1979, 1982 and 1992 laws to documents of the 20th Party Congress (2022) and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). It then discusses how voters' interests relate to the interests of the people as a whole, and ends with the institutional guarantees.

Liu's central claim is that the revised law now requires deputies to be people-centred, to practise whole-process people's democracy, to stay in close touch with the public, to represent the people's interests and will faithfully and to accept supervision. The "Two Linkages" are ties between state organs and deputies and between deputies and the public. Citing Marx, Liu holds that deputies depend on voters' trust and can be recalled, so faithfully reflecting voters' interests is a deputy's first duty. Because the people's interest is not the simple sum of voters' interests, Liu says deputies must reconcile the two. They do so by looking beyond their own constituency to broader and longer-term interests, and by ensuring that the full body of deputies, including every ethnic group, represents the whole people.

Liu identifies three institutional guarantees: elections together with the part-time deputy system, which keeps deputies in their own workplaces and communities; the liaison system, including "deputy liaison stations" and grassroots legislative contact points; and supervision, with recall as the last and strictest means. In Liu's account, moving from elections to recall closes the loop of safeguards for deputies' people-oriented character. Read the original if you want a concise official-line account of the 2025 revision of the Deputies Law and of how Chinese scholars link deputy representation to whole-process people's democracy.
quoteEn: Faithfully reflecting voters' interests and will is a people's congress deputy's primary duty and an important expression of deputies' "people-oriented character".
quoteZh: 忠实地反映选民的利益和意志，是人大代表的首要职责，也是人大代表“人民性”的重要体现。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2019 to describe China's democracy as covering every stage of political life, not only elections. Official sources present the people's congress system as its main institutional vehicle.
The requirement to strengthen ties between state organs and people's congress deputies and between deputies and the people. The 2025 Deputies Law revision expands the mechanisms for both.

t: Writing a new chapter for our times in Party conduct building on the new journey
zh: 书写好新征程党的作风建设的时代新篇
paras: Writing in mid-2025, Sun Mingzeng asks what Party members and cadres must understand and do to strengthen the Party's conduct (zuofeng) at a critical juncture between the 14th and 15th Five-Year Plans. The commentary was written in the context of the campaign of study and education on implementing the Central Committee's eight-point regulation, called for by the Politburo in April 2025. Sun's thesis is that Party conduct bears on the survival of a Marxist party, that the new era has produced significant results, and that further work is needed to guarantee Chinese modernization.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why conduct matters, on theoretical, historical and practical grounds. The second surveys achievements since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third proposes five lines of action for the new journey. Sun draws on statements by Mao Zedong and Xi Jinping, and on the Party's history from the revolutionary years through the reform era.

Sun argues that conduct is the concrete expression of a party's nature, purpose, programme and line, and that a ruling party which tolerates unhealthy tendencies risks losing popular support and power. Citing the Party's history of rectification campaigns, Sun presents attention to conduct as a 'family heirloom' that sustains the Party's vitality. The achievements listed are a deeper understanding of how conduct work operates (drawing on Xi's remarks), an improved political ecology within the Party, a more complete system of Party regulations, and a purified Party image. For the future Sun proposes strengthening ideological foundations through study, targeted correction of problems that anger the public alongside the cultivation of good examples, and leading by example from senior cadres. Sun also calls for tackling unhealthy practices and corruption together, using big data to detect leads, and a strict, sustained system of responsibility at every level.

Sun concludes that conduct building is never a stopgap and has no end point. It must be pursued with the 'Four Malpractices' (formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance) held in check and with 'real and long-lasting strictness'. The result, in Sun's account, would be to ensure the Party never changes its nature. Read the original if you want a representative example of how official Party-school writing frames conduct building, the eight-point regulation campaign and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party in 2025.
quoteEn: Conduct building is not an expedient or a one-off measure; it has no final note.
quoteZh: 作风建设，不是权宜之计、一时之举，没有休止符。

glossary.explanation: A set of rules adopted by the Politburo in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucracy among officials, covering matters such as meetings, travel and official hospitality. It became a signature measure of Xi Jinping's Party-discipline drive.
The Party's shorthand for formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, which the post-2012 conduct campaigns target.
The official name for the Party's model of development, presented as a path distinct from Western modernization.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The slogan for the Party's drive since 2012 to tighten discipline, combat corruption and strengthen internal oversight.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: CPC leadership as the fundamental feature of China's new-type party system
zh: 中国共产党领导是中国新型政党制度的根本特征
paras: Zuo Peng takes up Xi Jinping's call, made on 20 January 2025 at a Spring Festival gathering with non-Party figures, to firmly grasp CPC leadership as the fundamental feature of China's new-type party system. The article argues that this leadership is what lets the system of multi-party cooperation and political consultation under the CPC function as a basic political institution. In Zuo's account, it is a political creation that grew from Chinese soil and compares favourably with Western party-political models.

The commentary, from a journal of the Party's theoretical press, is organised in three parts. Each part names one thing that CPC leadership "ensures": representation of the fundamental interests of the people, unity around shared goals, and institutionalised, procedural collection of opinions for decision-making. Zuo supports these points with a historical sketch running from the united front of the revolutionary period and the founding of the People's Republic through the post-1978 period to the present.

Zuo's core claim is that the system combines ruling and participating, leadership and cooperation, consultation and supervision. The CPC is presented as having no special interests apart from those of the nation and people. It is said to integrate the specific interests of the groups the democratic parties represent into the people's fundamental interests, seeking the "greatest common denominator". Zuo contends that this avoids two defects: a single party lacking supervision, and competing parties taking turns in office with vicious rivalry. Leadership is also said to make the system's three channels work. These are party consultation, participation in political affairs and democratic supervision, which Zuo describes as ways of improving the scientific and democratic quality of decisions and of correcting errors.

Zuo concludes that the system has historical inevitability, creativity, superiority and vitality. It is said to embody the essence of fine traditional Chinese culture and the requirements of socialism, to play an irreplaceable part in modernising national governance, and to contribute to human political civilisation. Maintaining and improving it is described as bearing on the Party's long-term rule and the country's lasting stability. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official Party-line justification for the party system, including its historical narrative and its stress on the Party's leading role.
quoteEn: On the basis of democratic centralism, China's new-type party system seeks common ground while reserving differences, forming a mechanism for discovering and correcting errors and reducing mistakes.
quoteZh: 中国新型政党制度在民主集中的基础上求同存异，形成发现和改正错误、减少失误的机制。

glossary.explanation: The official description of China's arrangement of CPC leadership alongside eight non-ruling "democratic parties" and non-affiliated figures. Official discourse, notably Xi Jinping since 2018, presents it as distinct from both one-party and multi-party competitive systems.

glossary.zh: 多党合作和政治协商制度
glossary.pinyin: duōdǎng hézuò hé zhèngzhì xiéshāng zhìdù
glossary.explanation: The formal name of the basic political institution under which the CPC rules and the democratic parties take part in consultation and advisory roles. It is written into the Constitution.
The eight non-Communist parties that exist in China and accept CPC leadership. Officially they are defined as "participating parties", not opposition parties.
The CPC's long-standing strategy of building broad alliances with non-Party groups and social forces to pursue its political goals.

t: The "ontology," analytical paradigm and basic map of the concept system of CPC Party-building studies
zh: 中共党建学概念体系的“本体论”、分析范式与基本图谱
paras: With the History and Party Building of the CPC newly established as a first-level discipline under law, Liu Honglin asks how its concept system should be built. The article argues that Party-building studies must start from concepts: they must take the Communist Party of China as their object, treat the advanced nature of Marxist parties as the foundation, and draw core concepts from Marxist party theory and the Sinicised theory of Party building, while also using a comparative view of world parties.

The article has three parts. The first treats the "ontology" of the field (its object of study) and sets out four principles for building the concept system. The second discusses the essential attributes of Marxist parties, drawing on the Communist Manifesto, Lenin and Party leaders' statements, and compares rival analytical paradigms. The third sets out a hierarchy of basic, core, theory-identifying, important and general concepts, and lists examples of each.

Liu holds that the object of study should be understood through a "big Party-building outlook" rather than a narrow one: Party leadership, Party building, Party affairs work and intra-Party regulations together. The four principles are seeking truth from facts, combining policy language with scholarly language, layered and systematic structure, and stability combined with openness. Liu argues that advanced nature, a unity of political, practical and theoretical advancement, is the essential attribute of Marxist parties and the "meta-concept" and basic analytical paradigm. Liu judges the "mission-oriented party" and "party-centrism" paradigms less comprehensive, since the Party's mass character, representativeness, responsibility and mission all derive from its advanced nature. Basic concepts, such as party organisation, discipline and party politics, are treated as neutral and comparable across countries, so Liu says they should not count as core concepts. Core concepts are anchored in advanced nature and fall into three levels: the overall level (full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, the Party's self-reform, democratic centralism), the institutional level (such as the Party congress system and inspection tours), and the middle level (such as the mass line and rectification campaigns). Negative phenomena such as formalism and bureaucratism are excluded from the core.

Liu calls for three urgent tasks: set scientific criteria for classifying concepts, so that basic concepts are not mistaken for core ones; adopt a world vision and the big Party-building outlook to fix basic concepts and the framework; and keep ontology, epistemology, methodology and axiology united while extracting core and identifying concepts from Party theory according to advanced nature. Read the original if you want a detailed taxonomy of concepts in the emerging discipline of Party-building studies and the author's reasoning for placing advanced nature at its centre.
quoteEn: Advanced nature should always be the "meta-concept" and the overall theory-identifying concept of Marxist party theory, the most fundamental "analytical paradigm" for studying Marxist parties, and the benchmark and basic yardstick for anchoring the core concepts of Party-building studies.
quoteZh: 先进性应该始终是马克思主义政党理论的“元概念”与总的理论标识性概念，应该成为马克思主义政党研究的最根本的“分析范式”，应该成为锚定党建学核心概念的基准点与基本标尺。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A policy line promoted under Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012), stressing strict discipline, institutional rules and anti-corruption work within the Party.
A formula in Xi Jinping-era discourse describing the Party's efforts to correct its own problems and maintain its purity and vitality.
The author's term for viewing Party building broadly, as linked with Party leadership and the Party's cause, rather than only as the Party's internal self-construction.
The organisational principle of the Communist Party, written into its Constitution, combining internal discussion with unified decision-making and discipline.
The quality attributed to Marxist parties of being the vanguard in politics, practice and theory. Official discourse treats it as the essential attribute of the Communist Party.
A Party working method associated with Mao Zedong: drawing ideas from the masses, refining them, and returning them as policy, in order to maintain ties with the people.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Shaping the image of the Communist Party of China as a major party in the new era
zh: 新时代中国共产党大党形象的塑造
source: Journal of East China University of Science and Technology, 2025 no. 1
paras: Hu Guosheng and Guo Qian ask how the image of the Communist Party of China (CPC) has been built in the new era, and what that image consists of. Starting from the Central Committee's call to "tell the story of the Party's governance well", they argue that the Party's "big party" image rests on four positioned identities: a centenarian party, the largest party, a ruling party and a world party. They contend that these identities show historical self-confidence, courage in self-reform, a people-first stance and a global outlook, and that shaping them helps the state secure control over how the Party and country are portrayed abroad.

The article is organised in four sections, each matching one dimension of image-building: historical accumulation, Party building, governing philosophy and international contribution. Each section breaks the dimension into three or four sub-images, drawing mainly on Xi Jinping's speeches, Party Congress reports and the 2021 historical resolution. A short conclusion places the argument in the context of great changes unseen in a century and the need to build international communication capacity.

In the first two sections the authors link historical self-confidence to historical consciousness (summing up achievements, the Party's spirit and traditional culture, including the Two Integrations) and to historical initiative (grasping laws of history, shouldering missions, opening new horizons). As the largest Marxist ruling party, they say, the CPC faces problems peculiar to its size, which it answers through self-reform: purifying the political ecology through the Central Committee's eight-point rules and the anti-corruption campaign, tightening Party rules and discipline, updating outdated ideas, and raising the quality of cadres through education campaigns.

The later sections present a people-first ruling party that applies the mass line, reduces poverty and pursues common prosperity, and a world party that proposes a new form of human civilization and a community with a shared future for mankind. The authors cite peacekeeping, pandemic assistance and climate commitments as evidence. They conclude that this image makes China's international profile fuller and more accurate and helps foreign audiences hold a "correct view" of the CPC and China. Read the original if you want a systematic account of how Chinese scholarship frames the Party's image-building and its official rationale.
quoteEn: Historical consciousness is the conscious expression of historical self-confidence.
quoteZh: 历史自觉是历史自信的意识表征。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities (the first integration) and with China's fine traditional culture (the second integration).

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for global governance and international relations based on cooperation and shared interests, now written into Party and state documents.
An official goal of shared wealth for all, emphasised under Xi Jinping as a defining feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
A long-standing Party method of drawing ideas from the people and returning them as policy, treated as a "lifeline" of Party work.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: An intellectual-history study of how the concept of the "Communist Party" spread in China
zh: “共产党”概念在中国传播的思想史考察
source: Scientific Socialism (科学社会主义), 2025 no. 1
paras: Xiao Chunbai asks how the term and idea of the "Communist Party" entered China, and how history came to "choose" one party out of many that used the name. The article argues that this was a gradual and winding process: Marxism was accepted first, then various organisations called themselves communist parties, and only later did the party led by Chen Duxiu and Li Dazhao prevail. Xiao presents the study as useful for developing Party-building discourse with Chinese characteristics and for understanding the laws governing Communist Party rule.

The article has four sections. The first traces early circulation of the Communist Manifesto, from partial translations by Chinese students in Japan (1907–08) to Chen Wangdao's full Chinese translation of 1920, and notes the 1912 newspaper notices announcing a "Chinese Communist Party". The second explains why early Party groups were called "socialist" rather than "communist". The third reconstructs how the name "Communist Party of China" was fixed, including the rival groups claiming it. The fourth draws lessons.

Xiao argues that the name "Communist Party" became universal only gradually: German, Russian, French and other parties began as social-democratic or socialist parties, and the Russian party renamed itself in 1918. In China, Xiao says, the socialist label was more influential, and early organisers used "socialist party" and "communist party" almost interchangeably. The reasons given include the large anarchist presence among early members, nationalists seeking national revival, doubts that China's small working class was ready, and the founders' own earlier democratic or reformist backgrounds. Xiao reports that Chen Duxiu consulted Zhang Shenfu and Li Dazhao, and that after Voitinsky's advice the name Chinese Communist Party was chosen. Xiao adds that at the Third Comintern Congress in 1921 five groups claimed to represent Chinese communism. The article concludes that a party's fate depends on its turning points, not its starting point.

Xiao concludes that the naming process shows the Party's goals were tiered from lower to higher, while its highest ideal never wavered, citing Xi Jinping on communism as the Party's founding ideal. The short naming period meant limited theoretical preparation and mixed membership, so the author treats ideological Party-building as a lasting tradition. The early spread of Marxism is read as a scattered form of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, which became conscious only after the First Congress in 1921. Read the original if you want a detailed, source-rich account of the early Chinese communist groups and the debate over "socialist" versus "communist" naming, written from an official Party-history perspective.
quoteEn: A party's fate depends not on its historical starting point but on its turning points.
quoteZh: 政党的命运不取决于历史的起点而取决于转折点。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for fitting Marxist theory to China's conditions and to each era. The article applies it retrospectively to the scattered early spread of Marxism.
The Party tradition of strengthening the Party through ideological education and struggle over its members' thinking, stressed by Mao Zedong in the 1940s.

t: Developing whole-process people's democracy is a systematic undertaking
zh: 发展全过程人民民主是一项系统工程
paras: Yang Xuedong, writing in the Party School newspaper Study Times, asks how whole-process people's democracy, a concept still new as a theoretical category, can be developed further. The commentary argues that it is a systematic undertaking. In Yang's account, it needs deeper theory, better summing-up of practice, stronger international explanation and closer coordination among all actors in state governance.

The piece first traces the concept from Xi Jinping's 2019 visit to a legislative liaison point in Shanghai through its 2021 entry into law and Party documents. It ends with the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called whole-process people's democracy an essential requirement of Chinese modernization. Yang then names three shortcomings and sets out five tasks.

The three shortcomings are limited academic definition and comparison with other democratic types, insufficiently refined practical experience, and far more domestic publicity than external explanation, including inconsistent foreign-language renderings. Yang's tasks include building a theory that turns political discourse into academic discourse. Western-led democratic theory, centred on competitive elections, is described as facing serious challenge. Others include applying the concept within existing institutions, above all the people's congress system, and mobilising every level and department of governance.

Yang also proposes an index system for measuring democratic governance that differs from Western-led measures and can be operationalised and compared. The author concludes that this would help to explain China's approach to the world and strengthen confidence in Chinese-style democracy. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese political scientist sets out the research and institutional agenda for this official concept.
quoteEn: Whole-process people's democracy is an "all-round" democracy, in which every level, every department and every actor in the state governance system should take an active part.
quoteZh: 全过程人民民主是一种“全方位”的民主，是国家治理体系中每个层级、每个部门、每个主体都应该积极参与的事情

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2019 and the Party now presents as the core of socialist democracy in China. It stresses people's participation across the whole cycle of elections, consultation, decision-making, management and oversight.
The official name for the Party's path of national development, set out since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

China's fundamental political system, in which people's congresses at each level, topped by the National People's Congress, exercise state power. The Party describes it as the main institutional vehicle for democracy.

t: Advancing the "dual integration, dual creation" drive to do well in Party building in emerging fields
zh: 深入推进“双融双创”做好新兴领域党建文章
paras: Tian Hongjian, head of the Binzhou (Shandong) municipal Party committee's social work department, reports on how the city has carried out the "dual integration, dual creation" campaign in Party building. The article, a practice-oriented commentary, starts from Xi Jinping's call to strengthen Party building in new economic organisations, new social organisations and new employment groups. Tian's thesis is that systematised Party building, three-dimensional integration and durable safeguards can tie Party work in these fields to economic development and social governance.

The article is organised around three headings, each with three measures: a "three-dimensional linkage" Party-building structure, a "three-chain" development ecosystem, and a "three-force" support system. It draws on figures from Binzhou for the first half of 2025 and for 2024.

On structure, Tian describes quarterly reporting by county Party secretaries, a "two lists and one table" mechanism covering 114 annual practical items and 157 key tasks, and extension of social work bodies to all 98 township-level units. On integration, Tian says Party committees set up in 11 industrial chains, 1,823 Party-building instructors were sent to firms, and 38.6 billion yuan in new credit and financing was arranged for enterprises. The article also cites 200-plus high-level technology talents recruited in 2024, as well as a "Sunflower" brand for delivery riders and similar workers, which handled over 750 cases such as schooling and medical insurance.

Tian concludes that these measures give emerging-field Party building a firm organisational basis and add "new momentum" to urban development. Read the original if you want concrete local examples and figures of how Party organisations are being built into private firms and platform-economy workforces in a Chinese prefecture-level city.
quoteEn: Integrate Party building in emerging fields into enterprise management, industrial development and sector governance, so as to achieve both strong Party building and strong development.
quoteZh: 将新兴领域党的建设融入企业管理、产业发展、行业治理，着力实现党建强、发展强。

glossary.explanation: A Shandong campaign slogan: Party building should merge with economic development and with social governance, in order to create new economic space and a new governance pattern.
Workers in new forms of employment such as delivery riders, couriers and ride-hailing drivers, a focus of recent Party outreach.
Officials sent to firms, especially non-public ones, to help set up and run Party organisations.

t: Fully recognising the real harms of the hedonistic and extravagant outlook on values
zh: 充分认识享乐奢靡价值观的现实危害
source: China Discipline Inspection and Supervision, 2025 no. 10
paras: Ren Jie, a researcher at the Academy of Marxism, argues that hedonism and extravagance remain a live danger for the Chinese Communist Party and must be treated as a problem of values and Party spirit, not merely of conduct. The commentary starts from the proverb that extravagance marks the beginning of decline. It notes that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Central Committee has listed these tendencies among the "four undesirable work styles" and that Party and public conduct have improved. In Ren's account, such problems are recurrent and stubborn, so they must be cured at the source by strengthening ideals and convictions.

The piece, published in China Discipline Inspection and Supervision (2025, no. 10), has two main sections. The first sets out three ways in which a hedonistic and extravagant outlook corrodes Party spirit: it departs from the Party's nature and purpose, it conflicts with Party discipline, and it departs from the Party's goals. The second section argues that the spirit of hard struggle never goes out of date, and answers doubts about whether thrift is still needed. Ren draws on Xi Jinping's statements and on examples of revolutionary martyrs and contemporary "model figures".

Ren contends that, as Xi Jinping has said, style problems are fundamentally problems of Party spirit, rooted in incorrect views of the world, of life and of values. Left unchecked, extravagance damages the Party's image, turns the "fish-and-water" bond with the people into one of "oil and water" (a pun on perks), weakens cohesion and fighting capacity through disregard for discipline, and saps inner drive once ideals fade. Ren sets the austere lives of Peng Pai and Fang Zhimin, and of Liao Junbo and Huang Wenxiu in the new era, against officials who indulge in luxury. On consumption, Ren says that pursuing a better life is not the same as extravagance, and that encouraging consumption should be distinguished from waste, given the emphasis on green, low-carbon living within Chinese modernization.

Ren concludes that at a critical stage of building a strong country through Chinese modernization, with greater risks and challenges, cadres must reject hedonism, keep up hard struggle and thrift, and keep public and private interests clearly separate. They should clear their minds of stray thoughts, correct deviations in conduct and strengthen their defences against corruption. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-discipline journals link frugality campaigns to Party spirit, ideals and the case for continuing thrift in an affluent period.
quoteEn: Pursuing a better life is absolutely not the same as extravagance and waste.
quoteZh: 追求美好生活，绝对不等同于奢靡浪费。

glossary.explanation: Formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, targeted in a Party campaign launched after the 18th Party Congress in 2012 and tied to the eight-point rules on conduct.
The ideological and moral qualities expected of Party members, including loyalty to the Party's principles and purpose. Official discourse treats work style as an expression of it.
The official concept of China's own path to modernization, advanced by Xi Jinping and the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A long-standing Party ethos of austerity, diligence and perseverance, associated with the revolutionary period and still promoted as a virtue of cadres.

t: New understandings and driving forces in building an ecological civilization
zh: 生态文明建设的新认知与发展动力
paras: Zhang Yunfei asks what is new in the Party's thinking on ecological civilization since the 20th Party Congress (2022). The article argues that the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core has deepened its answers, producing great achievements and enriching Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization. In Zhang's view, this amounts to an innovative development of contemporary Chinese Marxism and twenty-first-century Marxism on ecological civilization. The piece appeared in China Social Sciences Today in June 2025.

The article is organised in four parts: new understanding of the laws governing ecological civilization construction; a broadened path of construction; the new focus of ecological civilization institutional reform; and new driving forces for future development. It draws mainly on Xi's 2023 speech at the national conference on eco-environmental protection, the 19th and 20th Party Congress reports, and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).

First, Zhang presents the "five major relationships" from the 2023 speech: high-quality development and high-level protection, key-problem tackling and coordinated governance, natural recovery and artificial restoration, external constraints and internal drivers, and the "dual carbon" commitments and autonomous action. Zhang reads them as an organic whole embodying an "ecological dialectics". Second, Zhang holds that Chinese modernization is a modernization of harmony between humanity and nature, which builds ecological civilization into modernization from the start. This, the author says, distinguishes it from the Western pattern of "pollute first, clean up later", from Western ecological modernization, and from eco-capitalism and eco-imperialism, and offers the Global South a new option. Third, Zhang sees new impetus in green and smart technology, in Xi's claim that new quality productive forces are "green productive forces", and in a "digital ecological civilization" as the technological prospect of civilization's evolution.

On institutional reform, Zhang calls for focusing on building a Beautiful China, with more systematic integration across the "five-sphere integrated plan". Proposed measures include improving market systems for environmental governance, compiling an ecological environment code, using ecological culture, and combining rule of law with moral governance and policy with science. Zhang concludes that the Party has clarified the direction of reform and improved its top-level design, enriching the ecological theory of the new era. Read the original if you want a concise Party-theory account of how current official ecological civilization discourse links the "five major relationships", Chinese modernization and green technology.
quoteEn: Productive forces are the actual capacity to realise the metabolism between humanity and nature, and must not be regarded as humanity's capacity to conquer and transform nature.
quoteZh: 生产力是实现人与自然之间物质变换的实际能力，不能将之视为人类征服自然和改造自然的能力。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese official concept for a form of civilization built on harmony between humans and nature. It has been a national goal in Party documents since the early 2010s and is part of the 'five-sphere integrated plan'.
The Party's term for China's own path of modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress in 2022. Official texts list features including harmony between humanity and nature.
A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023–24, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation. Official discourse links it to high-quality development.
A term for developing countries, used in Chinese official discourse to frame China's solidarity and development offerings.
The Party's overall plan for advancing economic, political, cultural, social and ecological civilization construction together, formalised at the 18th Party Congress in 2012.

keywords: Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization

t: Accelerating the deep integration of culture, science and technology, and industry during the 15th Five-Year Plan period
zh: “十五五”时期应加快推动文化、科技和产业深度融合
paras: Hou Yanquan, deputy director of a strategic planning institute at the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology's Industrial Culture Development Center, argues in this commentary (Guangming Daily, 11 June 2025) that the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030) should see faster deep integration of culture, science and technology, and industry. Hou presents this as an objective trend in the cultural economy and a key task for building a culture-strong, science-and-technology-strong and manufacturing-strong country. The piece claims that great-power competition is shifting from "technology plus industry" to "technology plus industry plus culture".

The article has two parts. The first sets out the inner logic of the integration by taking each of the three elements in turn as a starting point. The second diagnoses present obstacles, namely an incomplete policy system, a shortage of composite talent and slow growth of new business forms, and then offers four recommendations. Hou draws on Xi Jinping's writing on building a culture-strong country, a 2025 policy document on high-quality cultural development, and the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).
