Hou's central claim is that technology and industry already form a two-dimensional system, and that culture adds a "software" upgrade that turns it into a three-dimensional structure supporting high-quality development. Starting from culture, the article sees value guidance, talent support and creative vitality flowing into innovation; starting from technology, it sees the cultural sector becoming a main arena for developing new quality productive forces through digital, networked and intelligent change, including artificial intelligence; starting from industry, it sees culture and technology jointly upgrading traditional industries and nurturing emerging and future ones. Hou summarises the goal as a cycle of "cultural empowerment, technological drive, industrial upgrading" in which the three reinforce one another.

The four recommendations are: build a policy mechanism, with a special project, a multi-department coordination body and a dedicated fund; develop new cultural business forms through both "industry acquiring culture" and "culture becoming industry", for example digital collectibles, digital cultural tourism and metaverse experiences; train cross-disciplinary talent through integrated education, technology and talent policy; and build platforms, including cultural-technology parks, demonstration bases and laboratories in national high-tech zones. Hou presents this as laying a foundation for Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official-adjacent policy writing links cultural industries, technology policy and the coming Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: The integration of culture and technology ultimately lands in industry.
quoteZh: 文化与科技的融合,最终落点在于产业。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, emerging industries and innovation rather than traditional resource-heavy growth.
The official name for China's path of modernization, presented by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
An official goal, in place since 2017, that stresses quality, innovation and efficiency over speed of growth.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030, in preparation when the article was written.
An official goal, set for 2035, of building China's cultural influence, cultural industries and public cultural life.

t: The well-deserved mainstay: the status and role of the Communist Party of China in the War of Resistance against Japan, revisited
st: Revisiting the Communist Party of China's status and role in the War of Resistance against Japan
zh: 当之无愧的中流砥柱
zhSub: 再谈中国共产党在抗日战争中的地位与作用
paras: Writing for the 80th anniversary of victory in 2025, Xu Zhimin takes up historical nihilism in the study of the War of Resistance against Japan. Xu says this tendency repeats Kuomintang diehard slanders, such as that the Communist Party "fought guerrilla war but not the enemy" or put "seven parts into expansion, two into coping, one into resisting Japan". Xu argues that the Party was the mainstay of the war (zhongliu dizhu), and that scholars should uphold a correct view of the war's history.

The article is a short newspaper commentary built around several headed sections. They cover the Party as vanguard of resistance, its leading role in the national united front, the line of all-out resistance and protracted war, the rear-area battlefield, the mobilisation of international anti-fascist forces, and the forging of the spirit of resistance. It ends with three requirements for research on the war in the new era.

Xu's central move is a chronological record of Party initiatives. These include its declarations after the 18 September 1931 Incident, the 1932 declaration of war on Japan, the call for a united front, and its role in forming the Second United Front after 1937. Xu says the Party held the "leading core" even after the Southern Anhui Incident of January 1941, when it chose to struggle without breaking the alliance. Xu also presents Mao Zedong's On Protracted War as the guide to strategy, with guerrilla warfare dominant in the stalemate phase. Citing the Hundred Regiments Offensive of 1940 and Japanese shifts of effort towards the base areas, Xu holds that the rear-area battlefield became the main battlefield, working with the frontal one. Xu adds that the Party built links with anti-fascist forces abroad, such as the 1941 Yan'an conference of Eastern nations.

Xu concludes that denying the Party's contribution distorts memory and obstructs the transmission of the spirit of resistance. Xu proposes three principles for research: guidance by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, a correct view of the war's history, and drawing on history to build the future and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Chinese historiography currently defends the Party's wartime role against revisionist claims.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China is the well-deserved mainstay of the War of Resistance against Japan; to discuss the history of China's resistance and the building of its autonomous knowledge system apart from this easily falls into the rut of historical nihilism.
quoteZh: 中国共产党是抗日战争当之无愧的中流砥柱，脱离这一点谈中国抗战史及其自主知识体系构建，就容易陷入历史虚无主义的窠臼。

glossary.explanation: In official Chinese usage, a label for interpretations that deny or belittle the Party's historical record and revolutionary achievements. It is widely used in Party discourse since the 2010s.

glossary.literal: pillar standing firm in the midstream
glossary.explanation: An idiom for a steadfast force that holds up under pressure. Chinese official narratives apply it to the Party's role in the war against Japan.
The wartime alliance between the Communist Party and the Kuomintang, formally formed in September 1937. It is also called the Second United Front.
The guerrilla theatre in Japanese-occupied areas, run by the Communist-led Eighth Route Army and New Fourth Army. Official narratives contrast it with the Kuomintang-led frontal battlefield.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Party, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: An official national goal, tied to the Chinese Dream and to a strong, modernised China by mid-century.

t: Firmly grasping the distinctive orientation of improving the system of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
zh: 牢牢把握健全全面从严治党体系的鲜明指向
paras: This short commentary asks what orientation should guide efforts to improve the system of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, a requirement set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). Liu argues that the system rests on four linked features: strengthening Party leadership, comprehensive coverage, strictness in everything, and governance in the sense of treating problems. The author presents these as the system's defining direction and as evidence of the central leadership's resolve to deepen Party building.

The article is organised in four sections, one for each feature, and closes with a brief summary. Liu draws heavily on Xi Jinping's statements and on the record of campaigns since the 18th Party Congress (2012), including the mass line education campaign, the "Three Stricts and Three Honests" education and the "Two Studies, One Action" learning drive. It is an exposition of official positions rather than a comparative or empirical study.

Liu's central claim is that Party leadership is both the purpose and the guarantee of rigorous self-governance. Hence Party committees must bear primary responsibility, discipline inspection commissions must carry out supervision, and the authority of the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core must be upheld. Coverage must be "comprehensive" in three senses: everyone in the Party is both agent and object of governance, the campaigns have moved from the "critical few" leading cadres towards ordinary members, and political, ideological, organisational, conduct, anti-corruption and institutional work must be treated as one systematic project. Strictness must be real, courageous and lasting, so that it does not become a passing campaign. Governance, in the author's reading, means both managing and curing: it is problem-oriented, driven by a sense of vigilance about future risks, and marked by a willingness to take responsibility.

Liu concludes that the system is a dynamic whole, rich in content, complete in function and efficient in operation. Improving it requires implementing the general requirements for Party building in the new era and sustaining overall Party leadership. The "comprehensive" requirement, the "strict" tone and the "governance" concept should be built into the system, with greater institutionalisation, standardisation and scientific rigour. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-school scholars present the official logic of Party discipline and self-governance.
quoteEn: The system of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party is a dynamic system with rich content, complete functions, scientific standards and efficient operation.
quoteZh: 全面从严治党体系是一个内涵丰富、功能完备、科学规范、运行高效的动态系统。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan and policy line promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering discipline, anti-corruption and Party building. It is part of the "Four Comprehensives" strategy.
The Communist Party of China's National Congress held in October 2022. Its report called for improving the system of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.
Official term for leading cadres, who are treated as the decisive group in Party discipline and governance campaigns.

A 2014–2015 Party education campaign for leading cadres. It stressed being strict in self-cultivation, power use and self-discipline, and honest in conduct, in starting a career and in dealing with people.
A 2016 education drive for all Party members. It involved studying the Party constitution and Xi Jinping's speeches, and acting as a qualified Party member.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Coordinating integrated reform of the systems and mechanisms for education, science and technology, and talent
zh: 统筹推进教育科技人才体制机制一体改革
paras: Qiu Rui, a professor at the Beijing Municipal Party School, takes up a policy question set by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024): how to reform education, science and technology, and talent as one system. This short commentary, first published in Guangming Daily in June 2025, argues that the three are inseparable parts of the national innovation system. Integrated reform, Qiu contends, should raise the system's overall effectiveness and underpin new quality productive forces.

The article first explains why integration matters, then examines three strands of reform in turn. These are comprehensive reform of higher education, reform of the science and technology system, and reform of talent development mechanisms. It draws on the Plenum decision and the Outline Plan for Building a Leading Education Country (2024–2035).

Qiu holds that science and technology innovation depends on talent, talent on education, and education in turn supplies talent for scientific progress. Universities are described as the key meeting point of the three. Qiu calls for subject planning driven by national strategic needs, an independent system for training top innovative talent, and closer ties between universities, national laboratories and leading firms. For science and technology, Qiu proposes a collaborative platform in which the government guides, high-tech industry leads, and universities, research institutes and financial bodies support. Government is urged to respect market rules and tolerate failure. For talent, Qiu stresses evaluation reform, "breaking the five onlys" and setting new standards, and long-cycle support for young researchers.

Qiu concludes that integrated reform is a complex, long-term task requiring systems thinking and joint research, decision-making and implementation. It should remove blockages across the education, talent, innovation, technology and industry chains. Read the original if you want a concise Party-school statement of how current policy links education, science and talent reform.
quoteEn: Talent is the foundation of innovation, and innovation-driven development is in essence talent-driven development.
quoteZh: 人才是创新的根基，创新驱动实质上是人才驱动。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted since 2023 by Xi Jinping, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation rather than traditional resource-heavy growth.

glossary.pinyin: Dǎng de èrshí jiè sānzhōng quánhuì
glossary.en: the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
glossary.explanation: A July 2024 plenary meeting of the Communist Party's Central Committee that adopted a decision on further deepening reform.
A reform slogan to end evaluation based solely on papers, titles, diplomas, awards and student admissions.

t: Inheriting and carrying forward the fine tradition of the Xunwu Investigation
zh: 继承和弘扬《寻乌调查》的优良传统
paras: Marking the 95th anniversary of Mao Zedong's investigation in Xunwu, Wang Junwei argues that the Xunwu Investigation remains a model for how Party members should conduct investigation and research, which the article calls the Party's family treasure. Wang links the text to the revolutionary road of "encircling the cities from the countryside", to adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions and to the "living soul" of Mao Zedong Thought. The piece appears amid the Party-wide study and education campaign on the eight-point regulations, in which improving investigation and research is one task.

The article opens with the background: in 1930 Mao produced a cluster of rural investigations and the essay Oppose Book Worship, after the Red Fourth Army was criticised by superiors for "circling around" instead of expanding towards central cities. Wang then describes the May 1930 investigation in Xunwu, with its meetings lasting over ten days, visits to shops and markets, and the later 80,000-character report. The remainder draws lessons under two headings: what makes an investigation "correct", and what the Party style it embodies requires today.

Wang identifies several features of a "correct investigation": a clear problem and purpose, a representative "sparrow" to dissect, informants who speak truthfully, a focus on the principal contradiction (urban commerce and old land relations), and the ability to draw general conclusions from raw material. Wang says the report's detailed figures, such as the 23 forms of exploitation in three categories, supplied evidence for the land-revolution line and for urban policy. The second theme is style: Wang quotes Mao on becoming a pupil of the people and quotes Xi Jinping's examples of the Bazhazhan strategy in Zhejiang and cycling in Zhengding. Wang also repeats Xi's warnings against formalist research, such as "dragonfly-skimming" visits, "imperial envoy" tours, staged visits and visiting only successful places.

Wang concludes that the Party's work has advanced when investigation was valued and has suffered when it was neglected. Leading cadres are urged to go to difficult and complicated places, hear the truth, avoid snap decisions on arrival, and use the Party's innovative theory to study new problems. Wang presents this as serving scientific decision-making and the Party's governing capacity in the new era. Read the original if you want an official Party-history account of how Mao's Xunwu method is being used to frame current campaigns against formalism in research.
quoteEn: Investigation and research are a means; the aim is to solve problems.
quoteZh: 调查研究是手段，目的是解决问题。

glossary.explanation: A social survey Mao Zedong carried out in Xunwu county, Jiangxi, in May 1930, written up in 1931. The Party treats it as a model of rural and commercial fact-finding.
Rules on Party work style issued in December 2012 to curb formalism, extravagance and bureaucracy among officials. A 2025 study and education campaign is built around them.

glossary.en: encircling the cities from the countryside
glossary.explanation: The revolutionary strategy associated with Mao in which the Party built rural base areas before taking the cities.
In Party discourse, work that focuses on appearances and procedures rather than results. It is a recurring target of official campaigns.

t: High-quality Party building must lead high-quality development
zh: 必须坚持以高质量党建引领高质量发展
paras: This commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in June 2025, takes up a point Xi Jinping made when joining the Jiangsu delegation at the third session of the 14th National People's Congress: economically large provinces must "shoulder the main load" and should use high-quality Party building to lead high-quality development. Sui Guorong argues that high-quality development is the first task of building a modern socialist country in all respects, and that Party building is its fundamental political guarantee.

Sui stresses that high-quality development covers all areas of Party and state work, not only the economy, and is required of every region, not just developed ones. The article is organised around six dimensions of Party building, each introduced as a way of supporting development: political, ideological, organisational, conduct (work style), disciplinary and institutional building. A short closing paragraph draws the strands together.

The central move is to link each dimension of Party building to a specific contribution to development. Political building supplies direction: Sui calls the Party's overall leadership the "sea-calming needle" of the cause, citing the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, and credits the Party with enabling China to complete in decades an industrialisation that took Western countries centuries. Ideological building provides theoretical armament through Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Organisational building, in Sui's account, embeds Party organisations in new economic and social organisations and among new groups of workers, selects cadres willing to take responsibility, and attracts talent so that organisational strength becomes productive strength. Conduct, discipline and institutions are treated as conditions: opposing formalism and bureaucratism, promoting investigation and research, advancing the three-part aim of not daring, not being able and not wanting to be corrupt, fostering a "clean and amicable" relationship between government and business, and revising Party regulations so they are simple, workable and enforced.

Sui concludes that Party members should rally around the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core, strengthen the political and organisational functions of Party organisations, and find the point where improved Party building meets development, "focusing on development when doing Party building and doing Party building to promote development". Cadres are urged to take on heavy responsibilities with a pragmatic and clean image. Read the original if you want a compact example of how current Party-building discourse in China ties the Party's internal construction to economic development goals.
quoteEn: High-quality development is the primary task of building a modern socialist country in all respects, and Party building is the fundamental political guarantee of high-quality development.
quoteZh: 高质量发展是全面建设社会主义现代化国家的首要任务，而党的建设是高质量发展的根本政治保障。

glossary.explanation: An official formulation, prominent since the 19th Party Congress (2017), that shifts the emphasis of development from speed of growth to quality, efficiency and sustainability.
A formula from the 2021 Party resolution on history, affirming Xi Jinping's position as the Party's core and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

t: Promoting the all-round development of workers
zh: 促进职工全面发展
paras: This newspaper commentary takes up Xi Jinping's call, made at the meeting marking the 100th anniversary of the All-China Federation of Trade Unions, for a worker-centred orientation of work and for promoting workers' all-round development. Ma Yuna argues that, amid a new round of technological revolution and industrial change, such development is needed to produce high-quality employment and to feed high-quality development.

The piece has three parts. It first sets out why the task matters, then names the requirements of the present period, and finally lists conditions that would favour it. Ma writes in the register of Party commentary and draws throughout on Xi's speeches.

On significance, Ma presents workers' all-round development as the labour-sphere expression of Marx's theory of human development, as a requirement of further comprehensively deepening reform, and as part of the people-centred approach to development. Ma holds that workers' demands are shifting from survival needs to development needs, such as pay, skills, rights protection and participation in management. The requirements include integration into Chinese modernization, adaptation to a modern industrial system through lifelong learning and innovation incentives, and recognition of workers' own agency, supported by the model-worker, labour and craftsman spirits.

Ma's proposed conditions are the Party's overall leadership, with Party building and ideological work among workers; guiding workers to serve national strategies; a worker-centred orientation covering employment support, aid to workers in difficulty and democratic management in enterprises; and coordinated action among government, industry, enterprises and society, supported by digital service platforms. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary links trade-union work to Chinese modernization and high-quality development.
quoteEn: Labourers are the most active and dynamic factor within the productive forces, and only by giving full play to their agency can workers' all-round development be better promoted.
quoteZh: 劳动者是生产力中最活跃、最积极的因素，发挥好其主体性作用才能更好促进职工全面发展。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formulation of China's path to modernization, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models and is tied to goals such as common prosperity.
An official economic policy goal, stressed since 2017, that favours innovation, efficiency and sustainability over speed of growth alone.

glossary.zh: 劳模精神、劳动精神、工匠精神
glossary.pinyin: láomó jīngshén, láodòng jīngshén, gōngjiàng jīngshén
glossary.literal: model-worker spirit, labour spirit, craftsman spirit
glossary.explanation: A trio of values promoted officially to encourage diligence, honest labour and pursuit of skill, modelled on national model workers.

t: Building digital oral-history archives for the discipline of CPC history and Party building
zh: 中共党史党建学口述历史数字档案建设论略
source: Teaching and Research (教学与研究), 2025 no. 2
paras: Lü Xiaoying asks how digital oral-history archives can be built as a new documentary foundation for the discipline of CPC history and Party building, a new first-level discipline. Writing against the background of the national strategy of cultural digitization, the author argues that combining digital technology with oral history changes the form of historical sources. Such archives, Lü contends, support the construction of an autonomous knowledge system for the discipline.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the value of building such archives. The second defines the concept and its scope: essential attributes, features, forms and classification. The third lays out an operating procedure for collecting and processing the material, organised by a "whole life cycle" approach in three stages: preparation, execution and post-collection care.

Lü defines a digital oral-history archive as a record of the discipline's development, narrated by those who took part in or heard of events, collected by standard methods, and generated and stored in digital form. The author claims it complements official archives, which are often notices, summaries and reports. It also draws on history, film and media studies, archival science and sociology, and it supports Party history study and education. The archive keeps the primary-record character of traditional archives, takes multimodal forms (text, audio, video, virtual reality, holograms), and is classified into personal, event and composite types. These can be subdivided by generation of interviewee, institution, discipline and region. The operating rules cover interview lists and outlines, authorisation documents, a cataloguing scheme for describing each record, a mutually respectful interview in which the interviewee speaks freely, and transcription that combines AI with manual checking. They also cover editing by people with Party-history expertise and encrypted storage of sensitive data.

Lü concludes that following this procedure can produce scientific, institutionalised and standardised technical norms for the archives. In the author's view, digital technologies are a "double-edged sword" that needs methodological guidance, and collecting and studying these archives is integral to building the discipline's autonomous knowledge system. Read the original if you want a practical, discipline-specific framework for oral-history archiving in Chinese Party history research, including the author's typology and its references to technical standards.
quoteEn: Collecting, organising and studying the discipline's digital oral-history archives is inherent in accelerating the construction of an autonomous knowledge system for CPC history and Party building.
quoteZh: 开展学科口述历史数字档案的采集、整理与研究，是加快构建中共党史党建学自主知识体系的题中之义。

glossary.literal: Discipline of CPC history and Party building
glossary.explanation: A first-level academic discipline in China that studies the Communist Party's history and its organisational development, under Marxist guidance. The article treats it as an emerging discipline in the Chinese philosophy and social sciences system.
A goal in Chinese academic policy of building a body of concepts and theories rooted in Chinese practice rather than relying on Western frameworks.
The article's term for archival records of spoken testimony by participants or witnesses, generated and stored with digital equipment.
A Party-wide campaign to study the Party's history, launched in 2021. The article says the archives can help make it routine and long-term.

t: On the distinctiveness of the theoretical development of the Communist Party of China
zh: 论中国共产党理论发展的独特性
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2024 no. 9
paras: Cao Fengqi asks what is distinctive about the way the Communist Party of China (CPC) has developed its theory. The author argues that this theoretical development is dynamic, historically conscious and self-initiated, and that it combines upholding fundamental principles with innovation. Cao also contends that the Party's innovative theories are underrated in the West, because of ideological constraints and deliberate efforts to discredit them.

The article examines the Party's theoretical development through four philosophical dimensions: ontology, axiology (value theory), epistemology and methodology. Each dimension is illustrated by tracing the main theoretical achievements in turn: Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development, and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The evidence is mainly quotation from Party leaders and from their key texts.

Cao assigns one distinctive feature to each dimension. Ontologically, the Party's theory is a development of Marxism and not of any other doctrine, so that upholding fundamental principles while innovating (shouzheng chuangxin) is its first principle. In terms of value, it is defined by the people-centred stance (renminxing), including respect for the people's initiative. Epistemologically, it is defined by seeking truth from facts (shishi qiushi), which Cao treats as the thread running through Marxism's practical theory of knowledge in China. Methodologically, it is defined by the Two Integrations, which the author presents as the fundamental method of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Cao notes that epistemology and methodology are easily confused, and distinguishes them by treating the former as the guiding insight and the latter as the principle for putting theory into practice.

Cao concludes that the Party's theoretical development is a continuing process of opening new horizons for Marxism in China, and of pursuing and practising truth. Cao holds that understanding this helps grasp the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought, and calls for applying the "Six Upholds" in advancing Party theory. The author also presents the approach as useful for systematic and scholarly study of the Party's theory and for telling China's story well. Read the original if you want a systematic, officially aligned account of how Party theorists frame the continuity from Mao Zedong to Xi Jinping.
quoteEn: In the ontological sense, the Communist Party of China's theoretical development is precisely the upholding of fundamental principles and innovation in Marxism, and this is the first principle of the Party's theoretical development.
quoteZh: 在本体论意义上，中国共产党的理论发展就是对马克思主义的守正创新，这是中国共产党理论发展的第一性原理。

glossary.explanation: Formula stressed by Xi Jinping in 2021: integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with its fine traditional culture. It is presented as the core method of adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official phrase for the continuing process of applying Marxism to Chinese conditions and updating it for each era.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology, written into its constitution in 2017, associated with Xi Jinping.
Classical Chinese phrase adopted by Mao Zedong in 1941 and later made the core of the Party's ideological line, meaning that policy should proceed from actual conditions.
Theory associated with Jiang Zemin, stating that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the vast majority.
Theory associated with Hu Jintao, stressing people-centred, comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable development.

glossary.literal: guarding what is correct and innovating
glossary.explanation: Formula for preserving Marxism's core principles while developing theory and practice.

keywords: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context

t: A powerful ideological weapon for full and rigorous self-governance of the Party in the new era
st: Studying General Secretary Xi Jinping's important thinking on the Party's self-reform
zh: 新时代全面从严治党的强大思想武器
zhSub: 深入学习习近平总书记关于党的自我革命的重要思想
paras: Qu Qingshan presents Xi Jinping's thinking on the Party's self-reform as a theoretical resource for full and rigorous self-governance of the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The article contends that this body of thought distils the Party's century-plus of experience and answers why the Party must, can and how it should carry out self-reform. Qu treats self-reform as the "second answer" to the historical cycle of rise and decline, and as an integral part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

The piece, which appeared in Qiushi in late 2024, has three parts. The first assesses the theoretical significance of the thinking for Marxist party-building doctrine. The second reviews how it has guided Party governance in the new era. The third sets out how the "nine uses" (jiu ge yi), the practical requirements Xi has laid down, should drive further work on the new journey.

In the first part, Qu argues that the thinking results from the Two Integrations. It draws on the critical and revolutionary nature of dialectical materialism, citing Marx, Engels, Lenin, Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping, and on classical Chinese ideas of renewal and self-examination. Qu also claims it offers a path to the problem of self-supervision by a ruling party, and says it refutes the notion that multi-party rotation or separation of powers is needed to correct a governing party. In the second part Qu describes rigour in ideology, Party management, discipline, cadre management, conduct (including the eight-point regulations) and anti-corruption. Qu reports an "overwhelming victory" against corruption and says the Party has found the second answer to the historical cycle. The third part elaborates the nine requirements: centralised leadership as the fundamental guarantee, leading the great social revolution as the purpose, Xi's thought as the guide, escaping the historical cycle as the strategic goal, and solving problems unique to a large party as the main focus. The remaining requirements are a full system of Party governance, strong organisation and cadre ranks, improved conduct, discipline and anti-corruption work, and combining self-supervision with supervision by the people.

Qu concludes that the nine requirements form a coherent whole, combining strategy and deployment, epistemology and method. Qu calls on the Party to study the thinking thoroughly and implement it so that the Party remains the leading core of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want an authoritative statement of how the Party's leadership presents its self-reform doctrine, its theoretical sources and its practical agenda for the new journey.
quoteEn: Self-supervision is a worldwide problem, the Goldbach conjecture of national governance.
quoteZh: 自我监督是世界性难题，是国家治理的哥德巴赫猜想。

glossary.explanation: A concept central to Xi Jinping's Party-building discourse. It denotes the Party's continuous self-purification, self-improvement and self-renewal as a way to remain in power without degenerating.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official slogan, since 2012–2014, for strict discipline, anti-corruption work and institutional building within the Chinese Communist Party.

glossary.en: historical cycle of rise and decline
glossary.explanation: The pattern of dynastic rise and fall, raised by Huang Yanpei in conversation with Mao Zedong in 1945. Mao's answer was democracy and Xi's second answer is the Party's self-reform.
The formula of combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
Nine practical requirements for the Party's self-reform, each beginning with 以, from centralised leadership to combining self-supervision with public supervision.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: The core meaning of building a high-standard socialist market economy
zh: 构建高水平社会主义市场经济体制的核心要义
paras: Zhao Feng and Duan Yuchen ask what a high-standard socialist market economy system means in theory and how it should be built. They argue that, with the principal contradiction in society changed and socialism with Chinese characteristics in a new stage of development, it is a key goal of economic reform for further liberating productive forces and achieving high-quality development.

The short article, published in Chinese Social Sciences Digest (2025, no. 3), identifies four interdependent components: strong market entities, a unified and efficient large domestic market, a dialectical unity of an efficient market and a capable government, and smooth flows of factors between domestic and foreign markets. It then treats four tasks in turn.

First, the authors call for the Two Unwaverings: consolidating public ownership, deepening state-enterprise reform, and widening space for private firms after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). Second, the market must play the decisive role in allocating resources, which requires modern property rights, fair competition, a credit system and factor-market reform. Third, government must do better, through the Party's comprehensive leadership, a stronger macroeconomic governance system and greater governance capacity. Fourth, they urge high-standard opening up: institutional opening, a focus on western and north-eastern regions and free trade zones, and high-quality Belt and Road cooperation.

The authors conclude that the task is to combine the socialist system with the market economy more closely. They describe it as a complex systemic project that needs coordination among institutions, and as an ongoing exploration whose content will change with practice. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official policy framework for market-economy reform as presented in 2025.
quoteEn: Building a high-standard socialist market economy system ultimately means combining the socialist system with the market economy more closely, and bringing the strengths of both into fuller play.
quoteZh: 构建高水平社会主义市场经济体制，归根结底就是要将社会主义制度与市场经济更加紧密地结合起来，更好地将二者的优势发挥出来。

glossary.explanation: A Party formula calling for unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
An official economic goal, stressed since 2017, that favours efficiency, innovation and quality over speed of growth.

glossary.zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.explanation: The official description of China's economic system since the early 1990s, combining public ownership as the mainstay with market allocation of resources.

t: Taking institution-building as the main thread to lead further comprehensively deepening reform
zh: 以制度建设为主线挈领进一步全面深化改革
paras: Wang Puqu takes up one of the basic principles set out in the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further comprehensively deepening reform and advancing Chinese modernization: that institution-building should be the main thread of reform. Wang argues that this principle both sums up the historical experience of reform in the new era and serves as a guide to action for the new journey. The article is a research article published in Political Science Research.

The article has two main parts. The first sets out what institution-building means for comprehensively deepening reform. The second turns to the implementation paths for leading further reform through institution-building. Between them, Wang lists the functions institution-building performs, from the Two Integrations to risk prevention.

In the first part, Wang argues that institution-building is driven by the development of the basic and principal contradictions of society. It adjusts interest relations and the relations between power and rights, and it amounts to supply-side structural reform of institutions in the building of a modern state. Wang describes it as embodying a philosophy of "breaking and establishing" together, with establishing first. Its leading functions include realising the Two Integrations, further liberating productive forces (including new quality productive forces), and serving as an authoritative lever for regulating interests. It is also described as the main track of modern state-building, a vehicle for core socialist values, and a safeguard against major risks in a period of great global change.

On implementation, Wang calls for stronger Party leadership over institution-building, including full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, and for a people-centred approach: institutions built for the people, reformed in their service and innovated with their support. Wang adds that institution-building should be organised around the overall goal of reform, led by economic restructuring and pursued through rule-of-law thinking. It should uphold fundamental principles while innovating, favour systematic integration, key priorities and practical effect, and be assessed by its effectiveness in advancing Chinese modernization. Wang holds that the basic criterion for assessment is for whom institutions are built, whom they serve and on whom they rely. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese academic exposition of how institution-building is framed as the organising logic of the post-2024 reform agenda.
quoteEn: The fundamental criterion for assessing institutions and institution-building lies in for whom, in service of whom, and relying on whom.
quoteZh: 评估制度和制度建设的根本标准在于为了谁、服务谁、依靠谁。

glossary.explanation: The official formulation of China's development path, elaborated by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models of modernization.
Official formula for combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation and emerging industries.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Official term for the Party's drive since 2012 to strengthen discipline, supervision and anti-corruption work within its ranks.

t: Advancing the Party's governing capacity through new results in improving conduct
zh: 以作风建设新成效推进党的执政能力建设
paras: Zheng Haixiang's commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in June 2025, takes up the Party-wide study and education campaign on the central Eight-point Regulation, which the Central Committee ordered from the 2025 National People's Congress and Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference sessions until July. Zheng argues that better Party conduct should be tied to building a strong governing capacity, as a guarantee for further comprehensively deepening reform and for Chinese modernization.

The piece first defines "strong governing capacity", then sets out three tasks: developing the Party's governing theory, improving its leadership and governing institutions, and raising its overall capabilities through institution-building and cadre work.

Zheng describes governing capacity as the Party's ability, grounded in full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and the Party's self-reform, to run state power and manage public affairs in an institutionalised way. In this account leadership is the political precondition of governing, and effective governing is the basis of effective leadership. Governing theory should rest on the question of for whom, by whom and how the Party governs, with a people-centred outlook and the Two Integrations. Institutionally, Zheng calls for refining leadership systems, optimising relations between Party and state, mass, inter-party and intra-Party structures, and strengthening whole-process people's democracy and the socialist legal system.

Zheng calls for a stronger system of Party regulations built around the Party Constitution and democratic centralism, along with reform of cadre selection and regular training. The aim is to combine governing-capacity building with the modernization of national governance. Read the original if you want a short example of how Party-building scholarship links the conduct campaign to governing capacity and Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: The Party performs the dual political functions of leading and governing: leadership is the political precondition of governing, governing is the concrete way the Party realises leadership, and effective governing is the political basis of effective leadership.
quoteZh: 党发挥领导与执政双重政治功能，领导是执政的政治前提，而执政是党实现领导的具体方式，有效执政则是实现有效领导的政治基础。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's development path, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A Party slogan since 2014 for strict discipline, anti-corruption work and institution-building within the Party.
An official term for the Party's efforts to correct its own problems and keep itself pure and capable.
Xi Jinping's formula of combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
The official description of China's democratic system, promoted by Xi Jinping since 2019.

t: The value concepts of China's diplomacy in the new era
zh: 新时代中国外交的价值理念
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 5 June 2025
paras: Gao Xiaolin takes up a phrase from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): the Communist Party of China seeks "progress for humanity and a world of great harmony". The article argues that this aim is the distinctive value concept of Xi Jinping's diplomatic thinking and an integral part of promoting lasting peace, prosperity and progress worldwide. Gao presents it as grounded in Marxism, rooted in Chinese tradition, drawn from the Party's historical experience and suited to a changing world.

This short commentary, published in a Party-affiliated newspaper, is organised in four sections. The first covers the Marxist Party's value pursuit, the second the inheritance of fine traditional Chinese culture, the third the historical experience of "keeping the whole world in mind", and the fourth the Party's conscious response to global change. The historical section runs from the New Democratic Revolution through the founding of the People's Republic and the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978) to the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Gao argues first that Marx's theories of human emancipation and world history supply the foundation: communism means the free and all-round development of the individual, and growing global interdependence lets the Party treat humanity as an organic whole and move beyond narrow nationalism. Second, Gao finds cultural sources in the traditional ideals of "great harmony" under heaven, peaceful coexistence, and "harmony in diversity", which are said to explain why China seeks mutual learning among civilizations rather than cultural hegemony and does not impose its values. Third, Gao reads the "great changes unseen in a century" as both opportunity and risk, citing the collective rise of emerging economies, scientific breakthroughs, unilateralism, protectionism and hegemonism, and presents the Party's value pursuit as its Chinese approach to these changes.

Gao concludes that the Party stands on the side of historical progress and human civilization, and contributes Chinese wisdom and solutions to global problems and to building a community with a shared future for mankind. The piece is a statement of the official framing of Chinese diplomacy and does not engage rival interpretations. Read the original if you want a concise sample of how a Chinese Marxist academic links Marx's world-history theory, traditional culture and Party history in explaining foreign-policy values.
quoteEn: That the Communist Party of China has always kept the whole world in mind is an important guarantee that the Party and people remain invincible, and the fundamental driving force behind the continued success of their cause.
quoteZh: 中国共产党始终坚持胸怀天下，是党和人民始终立于不败之地的重要保证，是党和人民事业不断成功的根本动力

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept associated with Xi Jinping since the early 2010s, used to frame China's vision of international relations based on shared interests and cooperation.
The official body of ideas on foreign affairs attributed to Xi Jinping, treated as part of Xi Jinping Thought.

glossary.en: great changes unseen in a century
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for the current global transformation, referring to shifts in the balance of power, technology and the international order.

glossary.en: keeping the whole world in mind
glossary.literal: holding the world in one's heart
glossary.explanation: A phrase from traditional Chinese thought, used in Party discourse for a global outlook; it is listed among the Party's historical experiences.
A classical Chinese ideal of a harmonious society in which the world is shared by all, invoked in Party texts alongside the Marxist goal of communism.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind
great changes unseen in a century

t: Exploring Party building at the CPC's Seventh National Congress and its historical lessons
zh: 中共七大加强党的建设的探索及其历史启示
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in June 2025, Xue Lin asks what the Seventh National Congress of the Communist Party of China, held in Yan'an from April to June 1945, can teach the Party about strengthening itself today. The author's thesis is that the Congress marked the Party's maturity politically, ideologically and organisationally, and that its work on Party building offers wisdom for resolving the "unique problems of a large party". The piece is a short newspaper commentary, a stage result of a National Social Science Fund project on Yan'an's exploration of those problems.

Xue opens with the Congress's context: more than 1.2 million members, nearly a million troops and leadership over almost 100 million people. The article then moves through five themes, each closing with a lesson for the present: the Party's nature and purpose, the leading core, ideological unity, the capacity to govern, and the Party's "three styles of work". Evidence is drawn from the 1945 Party Constitution, speeches by Mao Zedong and Liu Shaoqi, and a Liberation Daily editorial, with Xi Jinping's 2022 assessment of the Congress as a milestone.

Xue's central claim is that the Congress answered "what the Party is and what it is for" by defining it as the vanguard of the working class that represents the interests of the nation and people, with serving the people wholeheartedly as its fundamental purpose. Mao Zedong Thought was established as the guiding ideology, summarised in nine aspects, and written into the Constitution. The Congress also elected a new Central Committee under Mao and, in Xue's account, achieved unity through intra-Party democracy and the discipline of "keeping in line with the Centre". Finally, Xue stresses the three styles of work: integrating theory with practice, close ties with the masses, and self-criticism, which Mao treated as a mark distinguishing the Party from others.

Xue concludes that today's Party members must strengthen their awareness of the Party's purpose, oppose privilege, accept supervision by the people, and uphold the authority of the Central Committee and its centralised, unified leadership. The author also calls on members to study the Party's innovative theory, raise their ability to govern and to struggle, and use criticism and self-criticism to keep the Party's political life clean and vital. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese Party scholarship draws present-day Party-building lessons from the 1945 Yan'an Congress.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China is great not because it makes no mistakes, but because it never hides its ailments for fear of treatment, and can face problems with a serious attitude, analyse them with a truth-seeking style and solve them with firm resolve.
quoteZh: 中国共产党之所以伟大,不在于它不犯错误,而在于它从不讳疾忌医,在于它能以郑重的态度直面问题、以求真的作风分析问题、以坚定的决心解决问题。

glossary.en: unique problems of a large party
glossary.literal: problems unique to a big party
glossary.explanation: A phrase in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It refers to the governance challenges said to arise from the Party's size and long period in power.
A formulation from the Seventh Congress (1945) summarising the Party's good traditions: integrating theory with practice, close ties with the masses, and self-criticism.
The Party's official ideology, regarded as the adaptation of Marxism-Leninism to Chinese conditions. The Seventh Congress wrote it into the Party Constitution as the guiding ideology.
A long-standing Party practice of openly assessing members' and organisations' faults, presented officially as a method of self-correction and discipline.

glossary.literal: serve the people with one's whole heart and mind
glossary.explanation: The Party's official fundamental purpose, associated with Mao Zedong and written into the 1945 Constitution.

t: Winning the people's trust and support through new results in improving Party conduct
zh: 以作风建设新成效不断赢得人民群众信任拥护
paras: Writing during the Party-wide study and education campaign on implementing the spirit of the Central Committee's eight-point regulation, Pan Xihua asks what Party conduct work should focus on and how it should proceed under current conditions. The commentary argues that Party members and officials must hold a stance rooted in the people, keep a presence anchored in the heart, and treat their conduct as an examination ground, so that Party conduct yields new results and the Party keeps its advanced and pure character.

The piece is organised in three numbered sections. The first treats the people's stance as the Party's fundamental political position. The second concerns the mindset of officials, namely reverence for the people and identification as their servants. The third sets out internal discipline and external popular supervision as complementary requirements.

Pan argues that the question of whom a party serves and relies on is the test of its nature, citing the Communist Manifesto and Xi Jinping to say that Party conduct is a barometer of public support. Left uncorrected, bad conduct becomes an invisible wall between the Party and the people. Officials should therefore revere the people, take popular opinion as the best yardstick, and exercise power for the people, fairly, lawfully and honestly. The author adds that conduct outside working hours is also an examination, calling for self-discipline in private life, and that the people should be the final judge of results, through open channels for suggestions, criticism and supervision.

Pan concludes that conduct building is a protracted effort that cannot be completed in one stroke. The eight-point regulation should become an internalised habit, in order to consolidate the Party's popular base, keep it the leading core of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and support Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a short example of how official commentary links Party conduct, the mass line and the current eight-point regulation campaign.
quoteEn: The key to conduct building lies in internalising it in the heart and externalising it in action.
quoteZh: 作风建设贵在内化于心、外化于行

glossary.explanation: A set of rules on official conduct adopted by the Party leadership in December 2012, aimed at curbing formalism, bureaucracy, extravagance and hedonism among officials.
The official name for China's current path, theory and system of socialism, developed since reform and opening up.
The official term for China's path to modernization, set out by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

t: The logical path to consolidating the Party's cultural leadership in the new era
zh: 新时代筑牢党的文化领导权的逻辑进路
paras: This short commentary from the Chinese Social Sciences Today (29 May 2025) asks how the Party can consolidate its cultural leadership in the new era. The authors argue that since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the Central Committee has put forward "upholding the Party's cultural leadership" as a defining task. They hold that it must be strengthened along four logical lines.

The piece is organised as four "logics": theoretical, historical, realistic and practical. Each is tied to a concrete requirement, ranging from Marxist guidance and the people's standing as the main body of culture to international discourse power and the Two Integrations.

On the theoretical line, the authors say Marx and Engels grounded culture in practice and stressed spreading socialist ideas among the working class. They present the Party's cultural leadership as an innovative development of that theory. On the historical line, they review the Party's record from the New Democratic Revolution to reform and opening up. They conclude that the people's standpoint and the unity of Party spirit and people's character are the basic principles. On the realistic line, they describe Western states as trying to infiltrate culture with hegemonism and weaken the Party's ruling base. They therefore call for stronger international communication, telling China's stories well, and export of film, animation and games.

The practical line rests on the Two Integrations within Chinese modernization. The authors propose surveying local cultural needs, building rural cultural brands and urban cultural venues, putting classics into curricula, and using modern technology for cultural platforms. Their conclusion is that these steps will strengthen cultural leadership and advance the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Party-affiliated scholars frame cultural leadership in current official terms.
quoteEn: The people's standpoint is the fundamental standpoint for upholding the Party's cultural leadership, and the unity of Party spirit and people's character is the basic principle for doing so.
quoteZh: 人民立场是坚持党的文化领导权的根本立场，党性和人民性相统一是坚持党的文化领导权的基本遵循。

glossary.explanation: Chinese rendering of the idea of cultural hegemony (cf. Gramsci). In Party discourse it means the Party's guiding authority over culture and ideology.
Formula stressing the integration of Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
Official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: Official national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, central to Xi Jinping's political language.

t: Deepening Party conduct building in the new era
zh: 纵深推进新时代党的作风建设
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in May 2025, asks how the Party's work on conduct (zuofeng jianshe) should be pushed further. Kan Daoyuan argues that the Party's conduct is its image, bears on popular support and decides the success of its cause. In Kan's view, the effort must be made routine and long-lasting through a firm grounding in Party spirit.

The article opens by defining conduct, which covers ideological, work, leadership and lifestyle styles as well as styles of study, writing and meetings. It then turns to the continuing correction of the "four undesirable work styles", the role of leading cadres as the "critical few", the base in Party spirit, and the institutional and mass mechanisms needed for lasting results.

Kan holds that ideological conduct is the fundamental layer, since solving it resolves the others, and that Party conduct sits at the core of social and popular customs while also being shaped by them. The eight-point rule of the Central Committee is presented as the "first cut" of the Party's self-reform, used to tackle formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance. Kan warns that these problems are stubborn and may return in hidden forms. Leading cadres must set an example, because problems often show up below but originate above. Conduct is ultimately a matter of Party spirit, measured by the distinction between public and private interest.

Kan calls for stronger ideals and convictions, a correct view of public and private, and a combined approach to Party spirit, conduct and discipline, with joint investigation and joint treatment of conduct and corruption problems. Kan also proposes institutional supervision, performance appraisal and cadre selection tied to conduct, and a dense supervision network that relies on the masses. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars present conduct building and the eight-point rule in 2025.
quoteEn: Problems of conduct are in essence problems of Party spirit.
quoteZh: 作风问题本质上是党性问题。

glossary.explanation: A set of Central Committee rules adopted in December 2012 to curb extravagance, bureaucratic habits and formalism among officials. It is treated as the starting point of Xi Jinping-era campaigns on Party conduct.
Formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, the four styles that Party campaigns since 2013 have targeted.
A phrase for leading cadres, whose example is said to shape the conduct of the Party as a whole.
The qualities of loyalty, principle and discipline expected of Party members, often framed as ideological and moral cultivation.
Official term for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself from within, central to Xi Jinping-era Party discourse.

t: Grasping the distinctive advantages of whole-process people's democracy from the dimension of practice
zh: 从实践维度把握全过程人民民主的显著优势
paras: This short commentary, first published in Guangming Daily, asks how the distinctive advantages of whole-process people's democracy can be understood through practice. Zhang and Feng argue that it is the most broad, genuine and effective form of socialist democracy. In their account it supplies momentum and institutional guarantees for deepening reform and advancing Chinese modernization.

The article has three parts. It first traces the Party's century of democratic exploration, from the border-region councils of the revolutionary period through the 1954 constitution and the reform era to the new era. It then describes the system's institutional procedures and participatory practice. Finally it assesses the practical value of the model.

The authors identify the institutional supports as the Party's leadership system, the people's congress system, the new type of party system, and grassroots self-governance. They say that democratic election, consultation, decision-making, management and oversight form a complete closed loop of practice. They also argue that the model extends democracy beyond politics into the economy, culture, society and ecological civilization. In their view it surpasses Western-style democracy by attending to both process and result, procedure and substance, and representation and participation.

Zhang and Feng conclude that whole-process people's democracy has distinct Chinese features while reflecting a shared human pursuit of democracy. They present it as a contribution of Chinese wisdom and a Chinese approach to democratic development worldwide. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars present the history, institutions and comparative claims of whole-process people's democracy in 2025.
quoteEn: Whole-process people's democracy links democratic election, consultation, decision-making, management and oversight, forming a complete closed loop in the chain of democratic practice.
quoteZh: 全过程人民民主将民主选举、民主协商、民主决策、民主管理、民主监督等环节贯通，形成了民主实践链条的完整闭环

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping first used in 2019. It describes China's democracy as covering every stage from election to oversight, and the Party presents it as an alternative to Western electoral democracy.
The official name for China's development path, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It stresses Party leadership, a large population, common prosperity and peaceful development.
The official description of China's system of multi-party cooperation and political consultation under Communist Party leadership. The Party contrasts it with Western competitive party systems.
China's fundamental political system, in which congresses at each level are the organs of state power. It was established formally in 1954.

t: The Communist Party of China as the mainstay of the nation's War of Resistance
zh: 中国共产党是全民族抗战的中流砥柱
paras: Writing in Economic Daily in May 2025, ahead of the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japan, Cao Ziyang argues that the Communist Party of China (CPC) was the mainstay (zhongliu dizhu) of the whole nation's resistance. In Cao's account, the Party's leadership was decisive in four areas: political and ideological guidance, organisation and mobilisation, strategy and tactics, and military struggle.

The commentary is organised chronologically and thematically in four sections. It first traces the CPC's early armed resistance from the Mukden Incident (1931) through the Xi'an Incident (1936) to the outbreak of full-scale war in 1937. It then turns to the Party's role in building and defending the anti-Japanese national united front, its general line and strategy for protracted war, and the rise of the rear-area battlefield behind Japanese lines.

Cao's central claims run as follows. The Party issued the earliest calls for armed resistance, led guerrilla forces in the north-east, dropped the slogan of opposing Chiang Kai-shek in favour of pressing him to resist Japan, and helped bring about the peaceful resolution of the Xi'an Incident and the second Kuomintang–CPC cooperation. When the Kuomintang turned to passive resistance and anti-communism after the stalemate stage began, the Party adopted a policy of both uniting with and struggling against it, and a line of developing progressive forces, winning over the middle and opposing the diehards. On strategy, Cao credits the Luochuan Conference (1937) and Mao Zedong's 1938 works, including On Protracted War, with setting out a comprehensive people's war line and the three stages of the war. Cao concludes that the Party-led rear-area battlefield became the main battlefield, citing about 1.32 million regular troops, over 2.6 million militia and 19 liberated areas by war's end.

Cao concludes that without the CPC and the base-area forces and people it led, complete victory could not have been won, and presents the victory as the turning point from national crisis towards the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The Party, Cao says, will remember this history and lead the people toward building a strong country and national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official Party-history narrative of the CPC's leading role in the War of Resistance is currently presented, with its chronology and key documents.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China held high the banner of the anti-Japanese national united front, resolutely upheld, consolidated and developed it, and persisted in independence and unity in resistance, safeguarding the overall situation; it was the well-deserved core of united resistance.
quoteZh: 中国共产党高举抗日民族统一战线的旗帜，坚决维护、巩固、发展统一战线，坚持独立自主、团结抗战，维护了团结抗战大局，是当之无愧的团结抗战核心。

glossary.literal: a rock standing in the midstream
glossary.explanation: An idiom for a steadfast force that holds firm in a crisis. Official Party-history writing uses it to describe the CPC's role in the War of Resistance.
The wartime alliance policy of the CPC, which sought cooperation with the Kuomintang and other social groups against Japan, formalised after 1937 as the second Kuomintang–CPC cooperation.
The December 1936 detention of Chiang Kai-shek by Zhang Xueliang and Yang Hucheng to press him to end the civil war and resist Japan. Party history credits CPC mediation with its peaceful settlement.

The guerrilla theatre behind Japanese lines, led by the CPC, as distinct from the frontal battlefield where Kuomintang forces fought. Party historiography presents it as the main battlefield of the war.
Mao Zedong's 1938 strategic theory that China's resistance would pass through strategic defence, stalemate and counter-offensive, with guerrilla warfare given strategic importance.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, often described as the CPC's historical mission.

t: Raising the "new quality combat power" of state security organs through new results in Party conduct
zh: 以作风建设新成效提升国家安全机关新质战斗力
paras: Writing in Study Times (28 May 2025), Chen Yixin, identified as Party secretary and minister of the Ministry of State Security, asks how work on Party conduct can strengthen the fighting capacity of China's state security organs. He argues that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Central Committee's campaign on conduct, which began with the eight-point regulations, has changed Party, government and social ethos. In his account, the security organs are now applying this through the current study and education campaign on the spirit of those regulations, in order to raise what he calls "new quality combat power".

The article is a programmatic report organised under eight headings: political leadership and loyalty; investigation and research; innovation; practical combat readiness; cutting paperwork and meetings; thrift; Party self-reform and supervision; and a fighting spirit. Each section opens with a statement by Xi Jinping and then lists measures the ministry's Party committee says it has taken. Chen gives some concrete details, such as weekly, monthly and quarterly follow-up on Xi's directives, a first batch of 10 observation points for reducing burdens on grassroots units, and falls in several categories of spending in 2024.

Chen's central claim is that the security organs' political character comes first, since he calls them the "knife handle" of the Party and people, so their conduct and their operational strength cannot be separated. He describes institutional measures: a revised set of detailed rules on the eight-point regulations, a supervision system to promote the Three Forms of Non-corruption, tighter accountability, and a ban on disguised or mutated violations. He pairs these with operational reforms: "virtual institutions, substantive operation and integrated mechanisms" without changing organisations or staffing, technology-driven methods, and combat teams. Cutting formalism and waste is presented as freeing up personnel and resources for the main tasks.

Chen concludes that the officers should develop a "daring to fight, good at fighting" spirit and become a loyal, pure and capable force. He lists five fronts to be won: counter-subversion, counter-hegemony, counter-separatism, counter-terrorism and counter-espionage. He also says they must hold firm on questions of sovereignty, security and development interests. Read the original if you want a first-hand view of how the security leadership links Party conduct campaigns to institutional reform and operational goals, and of the vocabulary it uses.
quoteEn: State security organs are the "knife handle" of the Party and the people; their political attribute is their first attribute, and they must always uphold political guidance, stay under the Party's absolute leadership, and adhere to the centralised, unified leadership of the Party Central Committee.
quoteZh: 国家安全机关是党和人民的“刀把子”，政治属性是第一属性，必须始终坚持政治引领，将国家安全机关置于党的绝对领导之下，坚持党中央集中统一领导

glossary.explanation: A set of rules on official conduct adopted by the Politburo in December 2012. They restrict extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism among officials, and later campaigns refer back to them.
A phrase modelled on "new quality productive forces". Here it refers to the enhanced operational capacity of the state security organs.
An anti-corruption formula meaning officials should not dare, not be able to, and not want to be corrupt. It combines deterrence, institutional constraint and moral education.

t: Understanding the methodology of strengthening Party conduct in the new era
zh: 深刻理解新时代加强党的作风建设的方法论
source: China Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 28 May 2025
paras: Writing as the Party-wide study and education campaign on the spirit of the Central Committee's eight-point regulation gets under way, Cai Wencheng, a professor and dean at Lanzhou University, asks how the Party's work on conduct (zuofeng) in the new era should be understood methodologically. The commentary, published in a newspaper in May 2025, argues that Xi Jinping's statements on Party conduct answer three questions: why to take it up, what to take up, and how. Cai presents these statements as providing a sound internal Party environment for advancing national strength and rejuvenation through Chinese modernization.

Since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Cai notes, the Central Committee has treated conduct as a key lever of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. The piece is organised around six paired relationships, each presented as dialectical: root and form, large and small, strictness and substance, top and bottom, governance and institutions, and regularity and long-term effect.

Cai argues that firm ideals and convictions are the root of good conduct, so formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance are traced to a loosened ideological "master switch". The eight-point regulation is described as a small entry point, seemingly about a mooncake or a meal, that drives the larger strategy of Party discipline. Strict self-cultivation must go with practical action, and leading cadres, the "critical minority", set the example while ordinary members push upward. Institutions must be tightened and enforced through law-based means, so that improvement is standardised and lasting.

Cai concludes that conduct-building has a starting point but no end, and that Party committees and their top officials must bear responsibility consistently and over the long term. The eight-point regulation is described as a lasting iron rule, and Cai holds that good Party conduct should in turn lead social and popular customs. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how the official discourse frames Party conduct campaigns as a set of dialectical working methods.
quoteEn: Through the mutual inclusion and coexistence of "governance" and "institutions", conduct-building can have rules to follow and address both symptoms and root causes.
quoteZh: 通过“治”与“制”的互摄共生，推动作风建设有规可依、标本兼治。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A policy line associated with Xi Jinping since 2012, covering discipline, anti-corruption and Party-building efforts.
Rules adopted by the Politburo in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism among officials, such as limits on banquets, meetings and official travel.
The Party's efforts to shape the working style and behaviour of its members and cadres, usually targeting the "four undesirable work styles".
A phrase used for leading cadres, whose conduct is held to set the pattern for the whole Party.
The official name for China's development path, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

t: Promoting high-quality development of trade union work in the new era and on the new journey
zh: 推动新时代新征程工会工作高质量发展
paras: Wang Dongming, chairman of the All-China Federation of Trade Unions (ACFTU), offers a study-and-implementation commentary on Xi Jinping's speech of 28 April 2025. Xi spoke at the ceremony marking the ACFTU's 100th anniversary and honouring national model workers. Wang argues that the speech answers fundamental questions of direction and strategy for the Party's labour movement. In Wang's account, it also enriches Xi's body of statements on the working class and trade union work and provides the guiding principles for union work on the new journey.

The article is organised as six sections, each headed by a call to grasp a theme of Xi's speech. These are: the Party's leadership as the basis of a century of labour movement; the status of the working class and unions; the path of trade union development with Chinese characteristics; the labour movement's theme in the new period; the meaning of the model-worker, labour and craftsman spirits; and the unions' duties and mission. Each section summarises Xi's points, adds historical illustration, and ends with what unions "must" do.

Wang's central claim is that the Party's leadership is the fundamental guarantee of the labour movement's success, from the First Party Congress's resolution on workers' work to the post-2012 period. The article restates Xi's judgement that the working class's position, the policy of wholeheartedly relying on the working class, and the nature and functions of unions "must not be shaken". It presents the "six adherences" as the content of a trade union development path with Chinese characteristics, part of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The labour movement's theme is tied to the Party's central task of advancing Chinese modernization, with high-quality development as the first priority. Wang sketches model workers from the revolutionary years to the present, and names new challenges: weak grassroots foundations, insufficient coverage and limited appeal of unions amid new technologies and new forms of employment.

Wang calls on unions to uphold the Party's leadership and the Two Establishes, strengthen ideological and political work among workers, and run labour and skills competitions and mass innovation activities. They should also build a knowledgeable, skilled and innovative industrial workforce, improve a "universal plus special" system of rights protection and services, and reform to strengthen their political, advanced and mass character. Wang also asks for stronger Party building within the union system. Read the original if you want an authoritative statement of how the ACFTU leadership frames the union's tasks after its centenary, and of the official vocabulary used for them.
quoteEn: The position and role of China's working class and the nature and functions of China's trade unions are determined by the nature of our Party and our country's socialist system, and can never be shaken or changed.
quoteZh: 我国工人阶级的地位作用和我国工会的性质职能，是由我们党的性质、我们国家的社会主义制度所决定的，任何时候都不能动摇、不能改变。

glossary.explanation: A formula adopted in 2021–22 affirming Xi Jinping's core position in the Party and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought. It is used in official texts to stress political loyalty.
The official term for China's path of modernization, elaborated by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as the central task of the Party and country.
An official economic goal that emphasises quality, innovation and efficiency over speed of growth. It was put forward in the late 2010s.
The official name of the Party's theory and system since the reform era, combining Marxism with China's conditions.
