Six principles Xi Jinping set out in 2025 as the core of the trade union development path, covering Party leadership, reliance on the working class, serving central tasks, the unions' character, serving workers and acting by law and statute.

t: Upholding the dialectical unity of breaking and establishing to make further comprehensive deepening of reform take root
zh: 坚持破和立的辩证统一 推动进一步全面深化改革走深走实
paras: Zheng Shanjie, writing as head of the National Development and Reform Commission, takes up Xi Jinping's instruction that further comprehensively deepening reform should centre on institution-building and should stress "breaking and establishing together, establishing before breaking". The article presents this as the fundamental guide for handling the relation between breaking the old and establishing the new, and sets out how the Commission will apply it to economic reform.

The piece has three parts. The first explains the theoretical and practical significance of the dialectical unity of breaking and establishing. The second sets out how to understand it completely and accurately in the current reform drive. The third lists the Commission's planned measures in five areas: the socialist market economy, a modern industrial system, coordinated urban-rural and regional development, a more open economy, and people's livelihoods together with green and low-carbon development.

Zheng argues that the principle draws on the Two Integrations: Marxism combined with Chinese realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture, citing ideas such as "getting rid of the old to bring in the new". It is traced through the stages of revolution, socialist transformation, and reform and opening up. Breaking, in the article's account, is the means and establishing is the purpose. Breaking without establishing leaves an institutional vacuum, while establishing without breaking leaves reform incomplete. Zheng adds that the direction of any break or establishment must be set by the overall goal of improving socialism with Chinese characteristics and modernizing national governance, under Party leadership. Reform measures should be carefully assessed and sequenced so that timing and intensity strike a balance.

In the third part, Zheng gives concrete commitments. They include a high-standard socialist market economy, the Two Unwaverings, a unified national market, the cultivation of new quality productive forces and future industries, and institutional opening up. They also include extending the second round of land contracts by 30 years in pilot areas, expanded employment and social-security support, and carbon-market and carbon-accounting systems. The article presents these as the Commission's way of carrying out the Third Plenum's reform agenda. Read the original if you want an official statement of how this reform method is turned into planned economic policy tasks.
quoteEn: Breaking is the means; establishing is the purpose.
quoteZh: 破是手段，立是目的。

glossary.pinyin: pò lì bìngjǔ, xiān lì hòu pò
glossary.en: breaking and establishing together, establishing before breaking
glossary.literal: break and establish simultaneously; establish first, then break
glossary.explanation: A reform method stressed by Xi Jinping, meaning that new institutions should be put in place before or alongside the removal of old ones, to avoid a vacuum.
Official formula for combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture.
Official policy line of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
A concept promoted since 2023 for advanced productivity driven by technological innovation, such as digital technology, new energy and future industries.

glossary.zh: 国家发展和改革委员会
glossary.explanation: A State Council body responsible for macroeconomic planning, major reform tasks and development policy.

t: China–Russia High-level Think Tank Forum (2025) opens in Beijing
st: Report on the opening session, 30 May 2025
zh: 中俄智库高端论坛（2025）在北京召开
paras: This news report, originally from People's Daily Online, covers the opening on 30 May 2025 of the China–Russia High-level Think Tank Forum in Beijing. The theme was "China and Russia: Cooperation in the New Era", and the forum marked the 80th anniversaries of victory in the World Anti-Fascist War and of the founding of the United Nations.

The forum was co-hosted by the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and the Russian International Affairs Council. The CASS Institute of Russian, EEast European and Central Asian Studies and a CASS think tank on China–Russia strategic coordination organised it. According to the report, more than 100 delegates from governments, think tanks, universities and business attended. They were to discuss three topics: defending genuine multilateralism and promoting multipolarity, practical cooperation and joint development, and cultural exchange and mutual learning among civilizations.

Four speakers gave opening addresses: CASS President Gao Xiang, Russian International Affairs Council head Igor Ivanov, and the Chinese and Russian ambassadors, Zhang Hanhui and Igor Morgulov. Gao called on both countries to uphold UN authority, advance multipolarity and the democratisation of international relations, link the Belt and Road Initiative with the Greater Eurasian Partnership, and expand cultural exchange. Ivanov stressed the need to recall the causes of the Second World War and oppose historical revisionism. He said the May 2025 joint statement on global strategic stability could also offer a framework for cooperation among the major nuclear powers. Zhang described the leaders' joint statement as top-level design for cooperation. Morgulov said China had been Russia's largest trading partner for 15 consecutive years, while Russia ranked fifth for China.

The report notes that the forum, held since 2018, is described as the highest-level, broadest and most influential think tank exchange platform between the two countries. Read the original if you want a brief official record of who spoke, what themes were set and how Chinese and Russian officials framed bilateral relations at this event.
quoteEn: Since it was first held in 2018, the forum has become the highest-level, broadest and most influential think tank exchange platform between China and Russia, making an active contribution to deepening and developing the China–Russia comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination for a new era.
quoteZh: 自2018年举办至今，论坛已成为中俄两国间层次最高、覆盖面最广、影响力最大的智库交流平台，为深化和发展中俄新时代全面战略协作伙伴关系做出了积极贡献。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese foreign-policy and infrastructure initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013 to expand connectivity and trade across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

t: Building a strong education nation around the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education
zh: 围绕立德树人根本任务建设教育强国
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in May 2025, takes up Xi Jinping's remarks on education since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Huang argues that building a strong education nation depends on the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education (lide shuren), which means strengthening Party leadership and ideological and political work in schools.

The piece moves through three areas: Party leadership over education, the priority development of education together with the quality of ideological and political theory courses, and the building of the teaching force for those courses. It draws on official formulations and offers no case studies.

Huang presents Party leadership as the basic guarantee of good education and says Party building in schools must not be formalistic. The author describes hostile forces seeking to Westernise and divide China and targeting young people, and calls for control of ideological work, filtering of ideas circulating among students, and continued adherence to Marxism. Higher education, in this reading, must serve the people, the governance of the country and socialism with Chinese characteristics. Huang also sets out six requirements for teachers of ideological and political courses: firm politics, deep commitment, fresh thinking, broad vision, strict self-discipline and upright character.

Huang concludes that ideological and political education is a distinctive strength of Chinese universities, which must strengthen it and keep it running through the whole of education. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated education officials present the link between education, ideology and Party leadership.
quoteEn: Ideological and political education in universities is both a distinctive feature and a strength of China's universities.
quoteZh: 高校思想政治教育既是我国高校的特色，也是我国高校的优势。

glossary.explanation: A formula for the fundamental task of education in Party documents: moral and political formation of students comes first, alongside knowledge and skills.
Compulsory courses in Marxism and Party doctrine taught from school to university. The Party treats them as a main channel of political education.
A national goal, set out in Party and State planning for 2035, of making China a leading country in education.

t: Understanding the rich meaning of "turning good conduct into custom"
zh: 深入理解“化风成俗”的丰富意蕴
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in May 2025, appears while the Party is running a study and education campaign on the spirit of the Central Committee's eight-point regulations on conduct. Su and Guo take up Xi Jinping's phrase "huà fēng chéng sú" (turning good conduct into custom) and argue that it is the key term of Party work-style building. In their reading, the phrase expresses the Party's grasp of how work-style problems recur and provides the direction for reform in the new era.

The article has three parts. The first defines the term, drawing on classical Chinese ideas of feng (prevailing ethos, imposed from above by example) and su (custom, habit widely accepted and practised by ordinary people). The second sets out three shifts the concept requires. The third discusses how to sustain the effort, citing Xi's remarks, including those from his March 2025 inspection in Guizhou and Yunnan.

The authors argue that work-style problems are stubborn and prone to rebound, citing Xi's remark that "tighten up and it improves, relax and it bounces back". They say hedonism, extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism persist, and that undesirable practices take new, concealed forms because the root causes of the "four undesirable work styles" have not been removed. Genuine change therefore means three transformations: from strict observance of rules to habit, from outward compliance to inner conviction, and from improving the Party's own conduct to shaping social conduct. For the last, they cite Mao Zedong's Yan'an-era claim that the people would learn from a Party with a fully upright style.

On how to persevere, the authors call for three measures. The first is strengthening ideals and Party spirit, since work-style problems are at root problems of Party spirit. The second is a problem-oriented approach that watches for rebound and for hidden variants of misconduct. The third is strategic resolve, making the effort routine and long-term through laws, regulations and institutions, and through combining punishment with accountability. They conclude that only this will break the cycle of improvement and relapse and make good conduct a lasting custom. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary explains the Party's work-style campaign and Xi's phrase "turning good conduct into custom".
quoteEn: Work-style problems are in essence problems of Party spirit; one must look through work style to Party spirit, and resolve the problem of Party spirit on the basis of resolving work-style problems.
quoteZh: 作风问题本质上是党性问题，必须透过作风看党性，在解决作风问题的基础上解决好党性问题。

glossary.explanation: Rules adopted by the Politburo in December 2012, shortly after the 18th Party Congress. They restrict officials' banquets, travel, meetings, extravagance and bureaucratic practices, and they anchor the Party's work-style campaigns.
A phrase Xi Jinping uses for the long-term goal of work-style building. Good Party conduct is meant to become everyday habit among officials and then a social norm.
Formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance. These are the targets of the Party's work-style campaign since 2012.
The Party's term for efforts to improve the conduct and discipline of Party members and officials, and their ties with the public.

t: Building broad consensus for further deepening reform comprehensively
zh: 广泛凝聚进一步全面深化改革共识
paras: This short commentary, published in Beijing Daily in May 2025, takes up Xi Jinping's remark that building broad consensus and mobilising all positive factors is very important for the smooth advance of reform. He Husheng and Fang Liang argue that, at a critical period for advancing national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization, consensus is both a safeguard and a necessary path for further deepening reform comprehensively.

The article is organised in three parts. The first explains why consensus matters, the second sets out what the consensus must contain, and the third proposes how to build it. It draws on Xi's speeches and on the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform.

The authors say consensus does three things for reform. It lays an ideological foundation by turning perceptual understanding into rational conviction. It resolves practical problems, since reform has reached a stage in which, in Xi's words, only hard bones remain to be gnawed, and these involve complex interests. It also gathers a strong joint force, which the authors describe as a political strength of the Party. They then divide the content of consensus into three dimensions. Leadership consensus rests on the Party's leading role. Ideological consensus rests on the theoretical innovations of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, notably Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Interest consensus requires cadres and citizens to develop a sense of the overall situation and to treat adjustments of interests and personal gains and losses correctly.

For practice, the authors call for three measures. The first is upholding the Party's overall leadership and the authority of the Central Committee, so that reform decisions are carried out. The second is deepening institutional reform to coordinate social interests, balance fairness and efficiency, handle distribution and address the concerns people feel most directly. The third is strengthening ideological work, guiding public opinion on reform, promoting positive publicity and keeping Marxism in its guiding position. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars present consensus-building as part of the reform agenda after the Third Plenum.
quoteEn: Upholding Party leadership is the fundamental requirement for advancing further comprehensive deepening of reform, and affirming the Party's core leading position in reform and development is the practical expression of building leadership consensus in contemporary China.
quoteZh: 可以说，坚持党的领导是推动进一步全面深化改革的根本要求，明确党在改革发展中的领导核心地位就是当代中国领导共识凝聚的现实表达。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path of modernization, promoted by the Party leadership especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for combining Marxist principles with Chinese conditions, traditional culture and contemporary developments.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017.
The reform agenda adopted at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee in July 2024, set out in a decision linking reform to Chinese modernization.

t: Mastering investigation and research as a basic skill
zh: 掌握好调查研究这个基本功
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 26 May 2025, asks how Party members and cadres can master investigation and research (diaocha yanjiu) as a basic work skill. Li Xiuduo, an associate professor at a university school of Marxism, argues that it is the foundation of sound decisions and a 'family heirloom' of the Party that must be carried forward.

The piece opens by citing the emphasis placed on it since the 18th Party Congress (2012), including the first of the Central Committee's eight-point regulations, and Xi Jinping's statements that research must be regular and go to the masses and into practice. It then sets out four requirements: seeking truth, putting findings into practice, using scientific methods, and learning from the people.

Li argues that research must establish real problems and real facts, guided by seeking truth from facts, and avoid staged or perfunctory visits. It must be done in person through the 'four withouts and two directs' approach, including in places with many complaints and complicated contradictions, rather than by demanding forms and data from grassroots units. Li also calls for varied methods, combining micro and macro, qualitative and quantitative analysis, and for hearing minority and opposing views. Finally, research is presented as the mass line in action, drawing on Mao Zedong and the Third Plenum decision of the 20th Central Committee (2024).

Li concludes that good research findings should be turned promptly into decisions and concrete measures, so as to solve problems and support the further comprehensively deepening of reform. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party commentary presents research methods and the mass line to cadres.
quoteEn: Investigation and research does not mean sending documents to the grassroots to demand materials, still less passing down orders level by level for data and 'filling in forms'.
quoteZh: 调查研究不是给基层发文件索要材料，更不是层层下派要数据、“填表格”。

glossary.explanation: A Party method, associated with Mao Zedong, of drawing ideas from the masses, refining them and returning them as policy, requiring cadres to stay close to ordinary people.
Rules on Party work style adopted by the Politburo in December 2012. The first requires improving investigation and research.
A fieldwork approach of making visits without prior notice, formal briefings, accompanying officials or set receptions, and going directly to grassroots sites and problems.
A principle of Chinese Marxism associated with Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping, stressing that policy should rest on actual conditions.

t: Party leadership as the fundamental guarantee for further comprehensively deepening reform
zh: 党的领导是进一步全面深化改革的根本保证
paras: Taking its cue from the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), this article argues that Communist Party leadership is the fundamental guarantee for further comprehensively deepening reform and advancing Chinese modernization. Wang presents this as a study of the Plenum's guiding principle, drawing heavily on Xi Jinping's speeches. The author holds that the principle sums up the experience of reform and opening up and explains why it has succeeded.

The article is a short Party-theory piece in three parts. The first treats Party leadership as historically inevitable, running through the periods of new democratic revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era. The second presents Party leadership as the root cause of the achievements of comprehensively deepening reform since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third presents it as the "sea-calming needle" that lets reform withstand risks and challenges.

Wang's first move is historical. After the Opium War China became semi-colonial and semi-feudal, and in the author's account no class or political force, from peasants to bourgeois reformers and revolutionaries, could change this. The Communist Party emerged from the union of Marxism-Leninism and the workers' movement, and Wang credits it with national independence, the socialist system, the shift to a socialist market economy and the nation's rise. Second, the author points to new institutions such as the Central Commission for Comprehensively Deepening Reform, led by Xi, as the means by which the Party drove reform from local experiments to systematic integration, with mature institutions and modernised governance. Third, citing the 20th Party Congress (2022) warning about "black swan" and "grey rhino" events, Wang contends that deep reform will touch entrenched interests and meet unpredictable risks. Only the Party's overall leadership, in this view, keeps reform's stance and direction secure.

Wang calls for the Party to uphold its overall leadership without wavering, and for full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, including the Party's self-reform, anti-corruption work and selection of reform-minded cadres. The author also urges study of the Two Establishes and practice of the Two Upholds, together with awareness of risk, a fighting spirit and bottom-line thinking. The article concludes that these will let reform consolidate its gains and open new prospects amid crisis. Read the original if you want an example of how Party-theory journals present the link between Party leadership and the reform agenda after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee.
quoteEn: Looking back at history, one basic conclusion can be drawn: the leadership of the Communist Party of China is historically inevitable, and without it China's revolution, construction and reform could not have advanced successfully.
quoteZh: 回望历史，可以得出一个基本结论，中国共产党的领导是历史发展的必然，如果没有中国共产党的领导，我国的革命、建设和改革就不可能成功推进

glossary.explanation: A formula from the 6th Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and of the whole Party, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A requirement that Party members uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the whole Party, and uphold the Central Committee's authority and its centralised, unified leadership.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A Party-building slogan since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It covers discipline, anti-corruption and institutional rules within the Party.
A concept stressing that the Party must correct its own problems through internal supervision and discipline. It is emphasised in Xi-era Party-building discourse.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership. It is presented as distinct from Western models.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978.

t: Leading social customs and popular mores with a good Party style
zh: 以优良党风引领社风民风
paras: This short commentary, originally published in Guangming Daily on 22 May 2025, responds to Xi Jinping's article in issue 10 of Qiushi on persistently implementing the spirit of the Central Committee's eight-point regulation. Zhang Tai, an associate research fellow at Shandong University, argues that a good Party style is a force that unites Party and people and sets the tone for wider social customs. Zhang presents Xi's call to persist for twenty or thirty years as a mark of the Party's determination.

The piece moves from the value of a good Party style, through a historical sketch from the Party's founding, the early People's Republic and reform and opening up to the period after the 18th Party Congress (2012), to current tasks. It cites one local example and closes with recommendations for continued work.

Zhang contends that when Party members and cadres work for the people and practise thrift and hard work, they set an example that improves society and raises cohesion. As evidence, Zhang describes Haikou's enterprise service officers, in which local heads act as one-to-one service staff to counter formalism and bureaucratism, and notes that the clean-plate habit and green consumption are spreading. Zhang sees these as a positive interaction between Party style and social style.

Zhang calls for leading cadres, the "key minority", to lead by example and for Party members to cultivate Party spirit and accept popular supervision. Zhang also urges organisations to improve cadre selection and to build on documents such as the opinions on integrity culture. Because style problems recur and persist, Zhang says, the effort must be sustained with a nail-driving spirit. Read the original if you want a brief example of how official commentary frames the eight-point regulation and the current Party study campaign on it.
quoteEn: Problems of work style are recurrent and stubborn, and cannot be solved at one stroke.
quoteZh: 作风问题具有反复性和顽固性，不可能一蹴而就。

glossary.explanation: A set of rules on Party and official conduct adopted by the Political Bureau in December 2012, shortly after Xi Jinping became General Secretary. It curbs extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism.
An expression used by Xi Jinping for leading cadres, whose conduct is said to shape that of the wider Party and society.

t: Grasping the historical, theoretical and practical logic of the Party's work style building
st: Studying Xi Jinping's important statements on strengthening the Party's work style
zh: 深刻把握党的作风建设的历史逻辑、理论逻辑和实践逻辑
zhSub: 学习习近平总书记关于加强党的作风建设的重要论述
source: China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News (Zhongguo jijian jiancha bao), 22 May 2025, p. 5
paras: Ouyang Song's commentary, first printed in the Party's discipline-inspection newspaper in May 2025, takes up the study and education campaign on thoroughly implementing the central Party's eight-point rules, then under way across the Party. Ouyang argues that Xi Jinping's statements on work style (zuofeng) can be understood through three connected logics, historical, theoretical and practical. Grasping them, the author says, will help the campaign take root and give work style building new results.

The piece is organised around those three logics. The historical section traces work style from the Party's founding through the Yan'an period, the early People's Republic, the opening of reform and opening up, and the years since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The theoretical section sets out why style is at bottom a question of Party spirit. The practical section lists concrete tasks for the present.

On the historical side, Ouyang presents a continuous line from the Yan'an style that defeated the Xi'an style, through Mao Zedong's warnings against bureaucratism, to Deng Xiaoping's 1979 view that correcting the Party's style was decisive. The eight-point rules of 2012 are cast as the opening move that revitalised the whole effort. Theoretically, the author argues that style is the personal force of a Marxist ruling party, determines the success of its cause, centres on relations with the people, and drives the Party's self-reform. The author therefore says the remedy is to address Party spirit so that officials do not dare, cannot and do not want to deviate. Practically, Ouyang calls for handling Party spirit, style and discipline together, and for leading by example from the top. The author also urges persistent correction of formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance. Further calls are to investigate misconduct and corruption jointly, to build lasting rules and institutions, and to let the Party's style lift social customs.

Ouyang concludes that work style building bears on Chinese modernization and on leading a great social revolution through a great self-reform, so it must be "always on the road". The author asks for sustained effort in being constant and long-lasting, strict and practical, and deep and detailed. Read the original if you want an official-line account, by a former head of the Party history office, of how the eight-point rules are placed in Party history and theory.
quoteEn: The core of the work style question is the relationship between the Party and the people.
quoteZh: 作风问题核心是党同人民群众的关系问题。

glossary.explanation: A set of rules adopted by the Politburo in December 2012 to improve officials' conduct, covering research visits, meetings, and similar matters. They have since been the basis of campaigns against extravagance and bureaucratism.
The Party's term for efforts to shape officials' conduct and their relationship with the public. It is treated as part of Party building.

A concept that the Party must continually purge its own problems. It is presented officially as the second answer, alongside popular oversight, to the question of escaping the historical cycle of rise and fall.
The official description of China's development path, presented as distinct from Western modernization. It is a central theme of Party discourse since 2021.

t: Advancing the effective empowerment of consultative democracy by digital technology
zh: 推进数字技术有效赋能协商民主
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in May 2025, asks how digital technologies such as big data, cloud computing and artificial intelligence can strengthen consultative democracy in China. Sun argues that digital technology opens broad space for consultative practice, but only if its risks are managed and it is treated as a tool rather than an end.

The piece first describes consultative democracy as an important component of whole-process people's democracy, with cultural, theoretical, practical and institutional foundations. It then sets out three areas of action: bridging the digital divide, breaking out of information cocoons, and safeguarding data security.

Sun contends that digital technology fits the practical stages of consultative democracy more closely than it fits electoral democracy. In the author's view it can lower the cost of building consensus and turn institutional strengths into governance effectiveness. Digital empowerment must rest on a people-centred approach that joins humanistic orientation with technological governance. On the digital divide, Sun calls for more investment in infrastructure, extension of resources to grassroots and less developed areas, and better digital literacy among participants. On information cocoons, platforms should improve recommendation algorithms, and consultative actors such as members of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) should use e-mail, WeChat and Weibo to be reachable. On data security, Sun proposes full-process data management, anonymisation of personal data, stricter platform rules and a fuller legal framework.

Sun concludes that these measures would better realise the principle of consultation "with the people and for the people" while keeping digital empowerment safe and reliable. Read the original if you want a brief statement of official-academic thinking on digital governance and consultative democracy in China.
quoteEn: It should be recognised that digital technology is only a tool for stimulating the effectiveness of consultation, not its substance; the root of digital empowerment lies in releasing human vitality and achieving people's free and all-round development.
quoteZh: 应当看到，数字技术只是激发协商效能的工具而非本体，数字赋能的根本在于释放人的活力、实现人的自由而全面发展。

glossary.explanation: A form of democratic practice in China in which Party, government, CPPCC and social actors deliberate on policy before decisions are made. Official discourse presents it as a distinctive feature of China's political system.
A concept advanced by Xi Jinping from 2019 describing China's democracy as covering the full cycle of elections, consultation, decision-making, management and oversight.
A national and local advisory body bringing together representatives of the Communist Party, other parties, and social groups. It is a main venue for consultative democracy.
Unequal access to, and ability to use, digital infrastructure and technologies across regions and social groups.
A term for the narrowing of a person's information environment when algorithms feed them only content matching existing preferences.

t: Experience and lessons from the Communist Party of China's work on improving its conduct
zh: 中国共产党作风建设的经验和启示
authors: Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee
paras: This Qiushi article, written by the Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee, asks what the Party's long record of work on its conduct (zuofeng jianshe) teaches for the present. Opening with Xi Jinping's statement that Party conduct bears on the Party's image, popular support and survival, it argues that four historical lessons should guide the continuing campaign to study and implement the Central Committee's eight-point regulations.

The text moves chronologically through each of four lessons, citing episodes from the 1921 founding programme, the Jiangxi Soviet and Yan'an periods, the early People's Republic and reform and opening up, and then the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Each section pairs quotations from Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, Zhou Enlai, Chen Yun and Xi with examples. Each ends with a paragraph of lessons for the "new journey".

The first lesson is that Party spirit (dangxing) is the root of conduct problems, resting on ideals and convictions. The second is that conduct centres on the Party's flesh-and-blood ties with the people, kept up through the mass line. The third is that improvement must come from the top down, starting with the "critical few" of leading cadres, and the article presents the eight-point regulations as the Politburo setting that example. The fourth is that conduct work must combine establishing and eliminating: promoting exemplary models and fostering healthy norms, while correcting the "four undesirable work styles" and fighting corruption. The author treats unhealthy practices and corruption as sharing one root.

The article concludes that, amid what it calls great changes unseen in a century and the critical period for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, the Party must keep implementing the eight-point regulations without relaxation. It calls for a strong conduct guarantee for Chinese modernization. Specific proposals include treating Party-spirit cultivation as a lifelong task, advancing "not daring, not being able and not wanting to be corrupt" together, and having leaders fight privilege. Read the original if you want an authoritative statement of how the Party leadership currently summarises its conduct-building history and the historical examples it uses to support it.
quoteEn: Conduct reflects image and quality, but what plays the decisive role is Party spirit, and the strength of Party spirit in turn depends on whether ideals and convictions are firm.
quoteZh: 作风反映的是形象和素质，但起决定作用的是党性，而党性强弱又决定于理想信念是否坚定。

glossary.explanation: The qualities, stance and discipline expected of Communist Party members. Party documents treat it as the foundation of correct conduct.

Rules adopted in December 2012 after the 18th Party Congress. They restrict official extravagance, banquets, lavish travel and formalistic meetings, and are the basis of the Party's anti-formalism campaigns.
A Party working method, associated with Mao Zedong, of drawing ideas from the people and returning them as policy. It is presented as a way to keep the Party close to ordinary people.
Xi Jinping's term for leading cadres, whose example is said to shape the conduct of the whole Party.
Formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, the four faults targeted by conduct campaigns since 2012.
The official name for China's current development path, set out under Xi Jinping as distinct from Western models of modernization.

t: The inherent logic and practical requirements of deepening reform of the Party-building system
zh: 深化党的建设制度改革的内在逻辑与实践要求
paras: This commentary asks why the Party's institutional arrangements for its own building need further reform and what that reform should involve. Writing after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), Ni argues that deepening reform of the Party-building system is both a component of and a guarantee for further comprehensively deepening reform. In Ni's account, it provides firm support for advancing Chinese modernization.

The piece is organised in three parts. The first sets out why the reform matters, drawing on the classics and on the record since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second identifies the key priorities and the points of leverage for reform. The third lists six practical measures for making the reform effective.

Ni's central argument is that institutions must change with the times. Citing Marx on institutional change as an interaction between productive forces and relations of production, Ni treats Party-building institutions as part of the superstructure, which must adapt as the economic base is reformed. The reform is also presented as the way to solve the "six 'how to always' problems", the difficulties said to be unique to a large party, through the principle of using institutions within the Party to govern the Party. On priorities, Ni calls for motivating Party members and officials to drive reform, building long-term mechanisms for study and discipline education, and reforming cadre personnel management so that officials can be promoted or demoted, and mistakes tolerated and corrected. Ni also stresses strengthening the political and organisational functions of Party organisations.

Ni concludes that the reform should convert the Party's political, organisational and institutional strengths into governance effectiveness, so that "Party governance" leads "China's governance". The six measures include improving the Party's leadership system, integrating Party building across its different dimensions with the fight against corruption, making the organisational system effective from top to bottom, normalising the promotion and demotion of cadres, and regular training. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Party-building reform agenda after the Third Plenum is framed in official-academic discourse.
quoteEn: Deepening reform of the Party-building system is ultimately meant to convert the Party's political, organisational and institutional strengths into governance effectiveness, so that "Party governance" leads "China's governance".
quoteZh: 深化党的建设制度改革，归根结底是为了将党的政治、组织、制度优势转化为治理效能，以“政党之治”引领“中国之治”。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, set out prominently from the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as the Party's central task for national development.

glossary.literal: problems unique to a big party
glossary.explanation: A formula from the 20th Party Congress era describing difficulties said to be specific to a very large ruling party, such as how to maintain its original aspirations and its bond with the people.

glossary.literal: able to go up, able to go down
glossary.explanation: A principle that officials should be promoted or removed according to performance, rather than holding posts indefinitely.

t: Solving development problems through reform
zh: 以改革的办法破解发展难题
paras: Zheng Xinli, a former deputy director of the Central Policy Research Office, argues in this People's Daily commentary that reform remains the means of resolving China's development difficulties. As reform deepens it touches sharper conflicts of interest, so Zheng holds that it must combine systematic design with continued bold experiment.

The piece first credits the past four decades of reform with economic, poverty-reduction, social and ecological achievements, citing figures such as GDP passing 130 trillion yuan in 2024 and manufacturing at about 30 per cent of global value added. It then turns to the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and its roadmap for Chinese modernization, and ends with three problem areas for reform.

Zheng's central claim is that "top-level design" and "crossing the river by feeling the stones" must be used together, a principle he presents as an application of historical materialism. Top-level design supplies coordinated goals that are adjusted over time, while stone-feeling means pilot projects whose lessons are generalised once proven. He sets out three areas for reform. Insufficient effective demand calls for better macroeconomic coordination. Agricultural and rural modernization lags behind industry and cities, and Zheng sees the countryside as the greatest source of future growth. Technological innovation requires integrated reform of education, science and talent systems and use of the new whole-nation system.

Zheng concludes that the plenum's more than 300 reform measures will only take effect with clear responsibilities, tracking of results and policies pointing the same way. He ties this to the goal of basically realising socialist modernization by 2035. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a senior policy figure presents the reform agenda after the 2024 plenum.
quoteEn: Crossing the river by feeling the stones means feeling out the laws of development; whether a reform measure is feasible can only be known through testing in practice.
quoteZh: 摸着石头过河就是摸规律，改革措施是否可行，通过实践检验才能知道。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formulation of China's own path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
Centralised, overall planning of reform goals and paths by the leadership, used alongside local experimentation.

glossary.en: crossing the river by feeling the stones
glossary.explanation: A phrase associated with the reform era, describing gradual, pilot-based experimentation when the path is not yet clear.
An official term for mobilising state and national resources in a coordinated way to achieve breakthroughs in key technologies.

t: Strengthening the Party's overall leadership: multi-dimensional exploration and practice in Yunnan
zh: 加强党的全面领导立体化探索与实践
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in May 2025, asks how the Party's leadership and Party building can be strengthened in Yunnan, a border province with many ethnic minorities. Zhang and Zhao take Xi Jinping's instructions during his inspection tour of Yunnan as their starting point. They argue that Party leadership is the fundamental guarantee of development and that the quality of a locality's "political ecology" is a key test of its Party building.

The article is organised as a five-part programme: political leadership at the core, the purification of political ecology, long-term mechanisms for improving work style, organisational innovation in building the cadre corps, and grassroots Party organisations as fortresses for border governance. Under each heading the authors set out what Yunnan should do and cite local practices already tried, including the "first-line work method", the "project work method" for rural revitalisation and a "political health checklist".

Zhang and Zhao's central move is to treat political construction as the guiding thread that is then turned into concrete mechanisms. They call for tracking systems and supervision to ensure central decisions are carried out locally, loyalty education drawing on Yunnan's revolutionary sites, and a regular, quantified assessment of political ecology with an "assessment–rectification–improvement" loop. They also propose a cadre system that rewards actual performance and tolerates and corrects mistakes, training for fields such as the digital economy and green transition, and Party-building models differentiated by sector.

The authors conclude that Yunnan's experience shows the Party's leadership must be merged with local conditions and pursued systematically, so that a healthier political ecology and high-quality development reinforce each other. They urge Yunnan to keep a systems mindset, address new problems and convert the strengths of Party building into governance effectiveness in support of Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-building doctrine is translated into provincial-level policy measures in a border region.
quoteEn: Yunnan's exploration and practice in strengthening Party leadership and Party building fully show that only by deeply integrating Party leadership with local realities, and systematically advancing political leadership, innovation in work style and organisational empowerment, can a virtuous interaction between an improved political ecology and high-quality development be achieved.
quoteZh: 云南在加强党的领导和党的建设方面的探索实践充分表明，唯有将党的领导与地方实际深度融合，系统推进政治统领、作风革新、组织赋能等，才能实现政治生态优化与高质量发展的良性互动。

glossary.explanation: A Party term for the overall political climate within a locality or institution, covering officials' integrity, work style and the health of Party discipline. It is used as a measure of how well Party building is going.
The official name for China's development path under Party leadership, promoted prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official policy goal that stresses quality, efficiency and sustainability of growth rather than speed alone.

t: Adhering to bottom-line thinking to prevent and defuse risks and challenges
zh: 坚持底线思维 有效防范和化解风险挑战
paras: Han Yu's article, a Party-theory commentary published in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) in 2025, asks how Party members and officials should apply Xi Jinping's statements on "bottom-line thinking" (底线思维) to prevent and defuse risks. Han argues that bottom-line thinking is a scientific concept, a mode of thought and a working attitude that rests on dialectical materialism. The author holds that it should guide efforts to balance development and security and so support high-quality development.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the meaning of bottom-line thinking and its philosophical logic. The second explains its present-day value, tracing it to traditional Chinese culture, the Party's historical experience and current strategic needs. The third lists practical requirements for putting it into practice.

Han defines the bottom line as the lowest limit and the critical point at which a thing changes in quality. Bottom-line thinking means setting minimum goals, starting from the worst case, preparing fully and aiming for the best outcome. Han describes it as risk-preventive, problem-oriented and proactive, and reads it as an application of dialectical pairs: favourable and unfavourable factors, quantitative and qualitative change, and subjective initiative and objective law. The author cites Mao Zedong's call to "base estimates on the most difficult conditions", Deng Xiaoping's remarks on preparing for major risks and Xi Jinping's repeated instructions. Han also argues that the Party faces both strategic opportunities and risks, citing "great changes unseen in a century", external suppression and "black swan" and "grey rhino" events. The author says the ability to use bottom-line thinking is a standard for judging leading cadres.

Han proposes four practical steps. These are to raise awareness of hardship and build risk monitoring and early warning; to improve institutions for risk research, assessment, coordination and accountability, with emergency plans and training; to strengthen responsibility so that officials guard their own areas and act at each stage of a risk; and to cultivate a fighting spirit that confronts problems directly. The aim, in Han's account, is to keep affairs above the bottom line while reaching for higher goals. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party writing presents the philosophy and cadre-training uses of risk prevention.
quoteEn: Bottom-line thinking is not a passive, hidebound and indolent way of thinking, but a proactive, enterprising one, with achieving better results as its core value orientation.
quoteZh: 底线思维不是消极被动、墨守成规的怠惰思维，而是积极作为、主动干事的进取思维，以取得更好结果为核心价值取向。

glossary.explanation: A method of thought stressed by Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It means assuming the worst case, setting minimum goals and preparing fully to avoid crossing critical limits.
An official economic goal that emphasises quality, efficiency and sustainability over speed of growth. It has been central to Party policy since about 2017.

glossary.zh: 世界百年未有之大变局
glossary.en: great changes unseen in a century
glossary.literal: great changes in the world unseen in a century
glossary.explanation: A phrase used in Chinese official discourse to describe a period of shifting global power and instability, including tensions with the West.
A Party term for readiness to confront difficulties and opponents directly. Xi Jinping has urged cadres to develop it as part of their ability to handle risks.

t: Never relaxing the strict tone
zh: 始终坚持严的基调不放松
source: China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News, 21 May 2025, p. 3
paras: This short commentary, published in the Party's discipline-inspection newspaper in May 2025, responds to Xi Jinping's article in Qiushi on implementing the Central Committee's eight-point regulation (中央八项规定). Li Juan argues that, with the new journey bringing heavy tasks of reform, development and stability, the Party must keep a strict tone on conduct without relaxation, so that improved work style opens a new phase of high-quality development.

The piece describes the eight-point regulation as a landmark measure of Party governance in the new era and a move to build credibility. It reviews more than a decade of enforcement, cites recent figures and a recent case, and then sets out what must be done going forward.

Li's central reasoning is that strictness has been the regulation's guiding principle from the start, citing Xi's remarks that the rule is rigid and carries no "trial" label. The author points to monthly published data on violations, now in its 139th consecutive month, and to the campaign against the "four undesirable work styles", with no exceptions for anyone. Asked whether enforcement can pause, Li answers with 16,994 cases and 22,547 people criticised or punished in March 2025, and with ten officials in Luoshan County, Xinyang, Henan, who broke the rules during a study-and-education campaign. Because bad practices can revive, Li calls for resisting arguments such as "minor matters" or "harm to development", and for severe punishment of disguised violations.

Li concludes that the regulation is a long-term hard rule and that persistent, strict implementation will gradually produce clean conduct and a clean political environment. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party media frame continuing work-style discipline in 2025.
quoteEn: Sustaining a strict tone, strict measures and a strict atmosphere over the long term is an inevitable requirement for achieving new results in work-style building.
quoteZh: 把严的基调、严的措施、严的氛围长期坚持下去，是推动作风建设取得新成效的必然要求。

glossary.explanation: Rules adopted by the Party Central Committee in December 2012 to curb bureaucracy, extravagance and formalism among officials, covering matters such as meetings, travel, hospitality and official publicity.
The Party's term for formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, which the eight-point regulation campaign targets.
An official formulation since 2017 that stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.

t: The practical value of strengthening integrity culture in the new era
zh: 新时代加强廉洁文化建设的实践价值
paras: Lin Guoqing's commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Journal in May 2025, asks what practical value the Party's drive to build an "integrity culture" (lianjie wenhua) has in the new era. It starts from the 20th Party Congress (2022) report and the Fourth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection, which called for a three-year action plan for 2025–2027. Lin argues that grasping the significance of this work is a precondition for understanding its place in a comprehensive "all-out war" against corruption.

The piece is organised under four headings. Each names one area of value: carrying forward fine traditional Chinese integrity culture, building a clean political ecosystem, stimulating the people's pursuit of truth, goodness and beauty, and displaying the political character of a Marxist party. Lin draws throughout on Xi Jinping's remarks, and on Confucian, Daoist and Legalist sources.

Lin first presents the current effort as a "creative transformation and innovative development" of a long tradition. As examples, Lin cites the writing of "integrity in the family" into the Party's integrity and self-discipline code, the inclusion of opposition to privilege in intra-Party regulations, and local research centres and campaigns that take integrity education into enterprises, schools and families. Lin then links integrity culture to the goal of cultivating a "do not want to be corrupt" consciousness, tied to shame and value rejection, and to popular support. Leading cadres' family conduct is said to set a model for Party and government style. Finally, Lin places the effort in a Marxist lineage running from the Communist Manifesto and the Paris Commune to Lenin's campaign against bureaucracy and the CPC's own record. The author claims that international comparison shows other developing countries falling into the "middle-income trap" through party corruption, while the CPC's integrity culture secures political, cultural and spiritual guarantees for Chinese modernization.

Lin concludes that integrity culture cannot be built in one campaign. It must be sustained over the long term, like the eight-point regulations the Party has said it will keep in force. Lin holds that the work has no end point and no shortcut, and that it should become a spiritual pillar of national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars present integrity culture as a link between tradition, Marxist party-building and anti-corruption policy.
quoteEn: Strengthening integrity culture in the new era has no end point, only ceaseless striving; it has no shortcut, only down-to-earth effort.
quoteZh: 加强新时代廉洁文化建设，没有终点，只有永不停歇的奋进，没有捷径，只有脚踏实地的耕耘

glossary.explanation: A term for values, norms and educational activities that promote official probity and oppose corruption. It is promoted as part of the Party's anti-corruption work and draws on traditional Chinese ideas of incorruptibility.
Part of a three-stage anti-corruption formula: officials should be unable to, dare not and not want to be corrupt. The third stage stresses moral and cultural self-discipline.
The official name for the Party's path of national development, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
Rules adopted in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism among officials, and treated as a cornerstone of Party conduct reform.

t: Opening a new phase of high-quality development through new results in improving Party conduct
zh: 以作风建设新成效开创高质量发展新局面
paras: This short commentary in Study Times (21 May 2025) takes up the link between Party conduct and economic development. Chen Peng argues that the Party's conduct is its image, bears on popular support and decides the success of Party and state undertakings. Citing Xi Jinping's remarks at a Politburo meeting, the author holds that the study and education campaign on the spirit of the Central Committee's eight-point regulation should produce results that open a new phase of high-quality development.

The piece is built in two parts. The first reviews the Party's history to show that good conduct is both fighting strength and productive force: the Yan'an period, the early People's Republic, the reform era and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second sets out practical measures for making conduct-building serve development.

Chen's central claim is that good conduct builds cohesion, morale and creativity, and so converts into productivity. The author cites the Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region's "ten nots" and the saying that "Yan'an conduct defeated Xi'an conduct" as evidence from the revolutionary period. For the present, Chen says conduct-building has become a variable affecting the depth of reform and the quality of development. It should therefore be embedded in solving development problems, target formalism and bureaucratism, and promote practical work and willingness to take responsibility.

Chen calls for perseverance and for institutional safeguards: closing loopholes that breed unhealthy tendencies, writing gains into rules and enforcing them strictly. Party members and cadres should use good conduct to lift social customs and public morale. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party media link Party discipline campaigns to economic work in 2025.
quoteEn: Good conduct is fighting strength, and even more a productive force.
quoteZh: 好作风是战斗力,更是生产力。

glossary.explanation: An official economic goal since 2017, stressing quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth alone.
Rules adopted by the Politburo in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism among officials. They are the base of the Party's conduct-building campaigns.
The Party's term for efforts to improve officials' working style and discipline, including opposing formalism and bureaucratism.
Party terms for superficial, box-ticking work and for officials who are detached from the public and unwilling to take responsibility.

t: Promoting the Long March spirit and advancing the construction of the Long March National Cultural Park
zh: 弘扬长征精神 推进国家文化公园建设
paras: This short commentary from the Chinese Social Sciences Today (19 May 2025) takes up the Long March National Cultural Park, one component of China's system of national cultural parks. The authors argue that summing up the experience of building the park and planning its future direction is both the core of raising construction effectiveness and a precondition for making better use of what has already been built. Their thesis is that construction is now shifting from 'building well' to 'using well' and 'developing well'.

The piece has three parts. It first lists achievements, drawing on provincial examples from Jiangxi, Fujian, Guizhou, Gansu and Shaanxi. It then sets out four guiding principles for construction and development. It closes with five concrete proposals for the 'living utilisation' (活化利用) of the park. The authors describe the park as an outcome of implementing Xi Jinping's thought on culture and upholding the Party's cultural leadership.

On achievements, the authors report that key projects have largely been completed and have produced a spatial layout linking a core exhibition park, distinctive exhibition sites and concentrated exhibition belts. They cite provincial frameworks such as Fujian's 'three parks, six belts and many sites' and Guizhou's '1+3+8' project system. They also say the park has boosted red tourism and serves as a means of promoting rural revitalisation. The four principles are: coordinating construction with development; unifying theory and practice; matching capital input with returns, including market-based operation; and combining scientific protection with living utilisation, in which digital protection and a database of Long March red cultural resources play a part.

The authors propose an efficient coordination mechanism, supported by relevant laws and regulations and by cross-disciplinary approaches. They also call for a unified Long March brand built on a 'history-based' design concept, and for 'Long March+' cultural-tourism products supported by price-compensation for red study tours. Further proposals are to integrate park resources into universities' 'big ideological and political course' and to use metaverse and immersive digital experiences that, in their words, foster positive political identification among the public. Read the original if you want a concise overview of how Chinese scholars frame the policy goals, market logic and ideological-education uses of the Long March National Cultural Park.
quoteEn: The Long March National Cultural Park is a public cultural product that ultimately must rely on market mechanisms to make its operation sustainable, and it therefore requires integrated planning, systematic advancement and coordinated operation.
quoteZh: 长征国家文化公园属于公共文化产品，最终需要依靠市场机制实现其运营的可持续化，因此需要统筹融合、系统推进、协同运行。

glossary.explanation: A state-led initiative begun around 2017 to protect and showcase major cultural heritage routes, including the Great Wall, the Grand Canal, the Yellow River and the Long March. The parks combine heritage protection, education, tourism and research.
A body of ideas on culture and ideology attributed to Xi Jinping and promoted as an official doctrine since 2023. It stresses the Party's leadership over cultural work.
An official strategy, launched in 2017, to develop rural economies, society and governance. Red tourism is one of the means it promotes in former revolutionary areas.
Tourism to sites linked to the Chinese revolution and Party history. The state promotes it for both economic and ideological education purposes.
A policy concept for ideological and political education that extends beyond the classroom into social practice and field sites, with a link between schools of different levels.

t: Four long-term mechanisms are needed to keep reducing burdens on the grassroots
zh: 持续为基层减负应健全四项长效机制
paras: Su Yongxiang takes up the problem of formalism and bureaucratism that weigh on grassroots cadres in China. Writing in the Guangming Daily in May 2025, Su draws on Xi Jinping's call to keep reducing burdens on the grassroots and on the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which asked for long-term mechanisms to this end. The author's thesis is that burden reduction will only be lasting if four mechanisms are put in place: list management, linkage and coordination, technological empowerment, and assessment and incentives.

This is a short policy commentary organised in four numbered sections, one for each mechanism. It quotes Xi Jinping repeatedly and refers to the 2025 Government Work Report, the national meeting of Party and government secretaries-general on 24 April, and the central "Several Provisions on Rectifying Formalism to Reduce Burdens on the Grassroots". Su also links the effort to the Central Committee's eight-point regulation on conduct and to Party discipline education.

Su argues that burdens originate above the grassroots, so reform must start with higher-level organs. The first mechanism uses lists: powers-and-responsibilities lists for grassroots and higher authorities, plus a negative list of tasks that may not be passed down, so that "outside the list there is no power". The second builds Party-led coordination across levels and departments, for example by letting township and subdistrict Party committees call in departments and by merging approval and enforcement forces. The third applies digital tools such as a single unified reporting form, a unified online management network and smart governance platforms, with a warning that technology must not itself become a new burden. The fourth reforms assessment by cutting duplicate inspections, shifting from checking paperwork to checking results, and combining stronger accountability for formalism with rewards and tolerance for error among cadres who take responsibility.

Su concludes that these four mechanisms would free grassroots cadres from formalism and bureaucratism and release their initiative, providing organisational and stylistic backing for building a strong country and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The author stresses that lighter burdens should not mean lower standards or less responsibility. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned summary of the current Chinese policy toolkit for grassroots burden reduction and its vocabulary.
quoteEn: Excessive burdens show up at the grassroots, but their root lies at the top.
quoteZh: 基层负担过重的问题，表现在基层，根子在上头。

glossary.explanation: A set of rules on Party and official conduct adopted by the Central Committee in December 2012. It targets extravagance, excessive meetings and formalistic working styles.

Official terms for work styles in which form, paperwork and ritual displace practical results, and officials are detached from the public. The Party treats them as persistent problems to be corrected.
The lowest levels of the Party and government system, such as townships, subdistricts and villages or communities, where cadres deal directly with residents.

t: A new layout: fresh thinking on improving the institutional system of whole-process people's democracy
zh: 新布局：健全全过程人民民主制度体系新思路
paras: This short commentary reads the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) as setting out a "new layout" for improving the institutional system of whole-process people's democracy. Xu Yaotong argues that the Plenum's Decision offers a systematic approach. It rests on Party leadership, a people-centred stance, upholding fundamental principles while innovating, and institution-building as the main thread.

The article takes the Decision's formulations in turn and treats each as a task. They are: strengthening the Party's overall leadership; making institution-building the main thread; strengthening the institutions through which the people run the country; improving consultative democracy; improving primary-level democracy; and refining the broad united front work pattern. It is written for a newspaper readership and mostly paraphrases and elaborates the Decision's wording.

Xu's core claim is that the Party's leadership system comes first in the structure of the whole-process people's democracy system. In this account, Party leadership supplies top-level design, political direction and exemplary inner-Party democracy, which Xu says will empower people's democracy. On institution-building, Xu names three requirements: making existing rules sound, innovating to fill gaps, and reforming outdated provisions, with attention to detail so that mechanisms actually work. Xu gives the people's congress system the highest place among institutions for popular self-rule and asks deputies to act as a "window" and "bridge" to the public. Consultative democracy is described as a distinctive strength, to be advanced chiefly through the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference. Primary-level democracy is called the most direct and basic form, linked to the higher-level institutions. Xu reads the Decision's separate listing of the united front as raising its importance rather than changing its consultative nature.

Xu concludes that the Decision's seven institutional directions for the united front form a complete system. They cover the new type of party system, non-Party representatives, forging a sense of community among the Chinese nation, religious affairs, intellectuals and new social strata, the non-public economy, and Hong Kong, Macao, Taiwan and overseas Chinese work. Xu presents these as strengthening the Party's ability to unite people and as a further sign of whole-process people's democracy. Read the original if you want a concise official-line reading of how the Third Plenum's democracy provisions fit together, as a Party-school scholar presents them.
quoteEn: Consultative democracy is a unique strength and distinctive feature of whole-process people's democracy.
quoteZh: 协商民主是全过程人民民主的独有优势和鲜明特色。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2019 to describe China's socialist democracy. Official texts present it as covering electoral, consultative, decision-making, management and oversight processes.
Official term for democratic practice through broad consultation before and during decision-making, institutionally centred on the CPPCC and the Party-led consultation system.

A Party-led advisory body bringing together non-Party figures, parties and social groups. Official texts describe it as the main channel of consultative democracy and an organisation of the patriotic united front.

The Third Plenum Decision's phrase for a wider united front effort. The united front is the Party's work of building alliances with non-Party groups, ethnic and religious communities, and overseas Chinese.

t: Putting strictness first in strengthening discipline building
zh: 严字当头加强纪律建设
source: China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News, 19 May 2025, p. 6
paras: This short commentary, first published in the China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News in May 2025, describes how the discipline inspection and supervisory commissions of Zhen'an County, Shaanxi, carry out Party discipline building. Yu Hongsong, the county's discipline inspection chief, takes his cue from the Fourth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection. That session called for turning external constraint into self-discipline among Party members and cadres. Yu presents the county's practice as a way to consolidate Party discipline study and education and to deepen full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

The article is a local work report organised under three headings: discipline education, strict enforcement of discipline, and the balanced use of policy and tactics. Each heading lists concrete measures taken in the county.

On education, Yu describes regular, long-term mechanisms. These centre on Xi Jinping's statements on discipline and on the Regulations on Disciplinary Actions. They include differentiated training for "top leaders", young and newly promoted cadres and new members, and use of a local warning-education base and local cases. On enforcement, the commissions stress political discipline and the Two Upholds, and they supervise the "key minority" through accountability reports by top leaders and monitoring of conduct outside working hours. They investigate undesirable work styles and corruption together. On policy, Yu describes applying the "four forms" of supervision and discipline and the "three distinctions", which tolerate honest errors and clarify the facts when officials are falsely accused, so that strict control goes together with encouraging officials to take responsibility.

Yu concludes that discipline building is continuous work that must be done with strictness and persistence. Cases should lead to institutional reform, through supervisory recommendations and "problem lists", so that power, matters and people are managed by institutions. Read the original if you want a concrete, official example of how county-level discipline inspection organs describe putting Party discipline policy into practice.
quoteEn: Dealing with problems early and when small, preventing them from growing, while also severely investigating serious violations of discipline, creates deterrence and strengthens Party members' and cadres' reverence for discipline.
quoteZh: 既抓早抓小、防微杜渐，又严查严重违纪行为，形成震慑，增强党员干部对纪律的敬畏

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping's leadership since 2012. It covers anti-corruption work, discipline enforcement and Party building.

A political requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position on the Party Central Committee and in the Party as a whole, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and its centralised, unified leadership.
A graded approach to handling violations. It runs from criticism and talks, through light and heavy disciplinary sanctions, to investigation of serious violations.
A guideline for distinguishing honest mistakes made in reform and exploration from deliberate violations. It underpins policies to tolerate error and protect officials who take initiative.
A Party-wide campaign in 2024 centred on study of the revised Regulations on Disciplinary Actions.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: The normative guidelines the whole Party must strictly follow in politics
st: The "political principles" stressed by General Secretary Xi Jinping
zh: 全党在政治上必须严格遵循的规范准则
zhSub: 习近平总书记强调的“政治原则”
paras: This short commentary, first published in Study Times in May 2025, asks what "political principles" are and how General Secretary Xi Jinping has defined them since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The authors define a political principle as a basic political requirement and norm that guides all fields of social life. They contend that such principles express the will, interests and values of the ruling class, and that studying Xi's statements helps the Party uphold its overall leadership and raise its political leadership capacity.

The article proceeds chronologically through six occasions on which Xi addressed the subject: the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection plenums of January 2013 and January 2016, the national conference on propaganda and ideological work (August 2013), the conference on Party building in state-owned enterprises (October 2016), a training class at the Central Party School (September 2021), and the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). Each section summarises Xi's remarks and the requirements he attached to them.

The authors present a set of named principles. Staying consistent with the Party Central Committee in thinking, politics and action is a major political principle, and the authors list prohibited conduct such as diluting central policy, leaking secrets or spreading political rumours. Party leadership of state-owned enterprises is another, described as embedding Party organisations in corporate governance. Ideological work must keep Party control and a combative stance on questions of right and wrong. Xi also criticises cadres who avoid conflict and act as \"good old boys\", and argues that Party spirit requires struggle. The highest principle, per the 20th Party Congress report, is the Central Committee's centralised and unified leadership.

The authors conclude that safeguarding the authority of the Central Committee is the first task of Party political building, and that its most critical element is upholding Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and of the whole Party. They link this to Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and to the Two Upholds. They also list five major principles for dealing with deep-seated contradictions in reform, development and stability. Read the original if you want a compact chronological digest of Xi's formulations on political principles, political discipline and Party leadership, as they were presented in Party media in 2025.
quoteEn: Upholding the Party Central Committee's centralised and unified leadership is the Party's highest political principle and a fundamental requirement that a mature Marxist party must adhere to; it must never be blurred or shaken, at any time or in any circumstance.
quoteZh: 坚持党中央集中统一领导是党的最高政治原则，是一个成熟的马克思主义政党必须坚持的根本要求，任何时候、任何情况下都不能含糊和动摇。

glossary.explanation: A Party formula, prominent since 2018, calling on members to firmly uphold Xi Jinping's core position on the Central Committee and in the whole Party, and the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, set out in the 20th Party Congress report (2022) as the route to national rejuvenation.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's leadership.
The Party's rules requiring members to stay politically aligned with the Central Committee, including limits on public speech that contradicts Party decisions.

t: The spirit of resisting US aggression and aiding Korea: daring to struggle and skilled in struggle
zh: 抗美援朝精神：既敢于斗争又善于斗争
paras: This short commentary, published in Study Times on 16 May 2025, takes up the spirit forged in the war to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea (1950–53). Starting from Xi Jinping's October 2020 speech marking the 70th anniversary of the Chinese People's Volunteers' entry into the war, Yan Hui argues that this spirit grew out of China's modern history of national salvation and gives guidance today for facing risks and challenges, daring to struggle and being skilled in struggle.

The article first sketches the origins of the spirit: national awakening, a tradition of struggle and wartime practice. It then briefly describes the course of the war, with eight months of mobile warfare followed by a two-year-and-one-month stalemate in which the Chinese side fought while negotiating. The main body takes in turn the five components named in Xi's speech: patriotism, revolutionary heroism, revolutionary optimism, revolutionary loyalty and internationalism.

Yan treats patriotism as the foundation, citing patriotic pacts signed by over 80 per cent of residents in cities such as Beijing, Tianjin and Shanghai by October 1951, and production campaigns among workers and peasants. Heroism is called the essence and is illustrated by the Changjin Lake battle, Shangganling and the "three disbelieves" of Yang Gensi. Optimism is described as the most distinctive core, loyalty as the underlying base, and internationalism as an organic part, rooted in Mao Zedong's view of the duty to a neighbour in danger and in the Volunteers' conduct toward Korean civilians.

Yan concludes that the spirit is a precious asset that will inspire the Chinese people and nation to overcome all difficulties and defeat any powerful enemy. In this account the war made the Chinese nation truly stand among the nations of the world. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Party press presents the Korean War spirit and its contemporary relevance.
quoteEn: The spirit of patriotism is the foundation of the spirit of resisting US aggression and aiding Korea.
quoteZh: 爱国主义精神是抗美援朝精神的根本。

glossary.explanation: The name of the Chinese forces that entered the Korean War in October 1950. They were formally volunteers, though organised from the People's Liberation Army.
A Party term for courage and readiness for self-sacrifice in the revolutionary cause. It is one of the five components of the Korean War spirit.
A Party term for steadfast confidence in the eventual victory of a just cause, even in severe hardship.

t: Shaping a fine work style through strong Party spirit
zh: 以坚强党性塑造优良作风
paras: Zhang Hao asks how the Communist Party of China can shape a fine work style in the new era, and answers that style must be tackled through Party spirit. Writing in a Chinese Social Sciences Today commentary (May 2025), Zhang takes up the line, stressed by the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core since the 18th Party Congress (2012), that one should "see Party spirit through work style" and resolve Party-spirit problems on the basis of resolving style problems. Party spirit is internalised in the heart; work style is its outward expression in conduct.

The short piece has three parts. The first argues that Party spirit is the essence of style problems. The second sets out five features of strong Party spirit. The third presents Party-spirit education as a required course and lists five habits to cultivate.
