It draws on official formulations about the Party's founding spirit, the mass line and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

Zhang's central claim is that Party spirit is the inner basis of style: firm Party spirit yields fine style, and impure Party spirit yields impure style. Zhang acknowledges that since the Eight-point Regulation was introduced, Party conduct has improved markedly, but says the "four undesirable work styles" persist. In the article's account their roots are a distorted view of achievements, lack of responsibility, wrong values and swollen material desire, which are essentially defects of Party spirit. Style work therefore cannot treat each case in isolation. Strong Party spirit is said to show in firm ideals and convictions, solid theoretical grounding, a sincere commitment to the people, a spirit of responsibility and strict discipline. Zhang names the people's standpoint as the fundamental content of Party spirit.

Zhang concludes that cadres, especially leading ones, must temper their Party spirit through five habits: tempering the will to forge ahead, cultivating the virtue of governing, keeping close to the people, maintaining reverence for the Party, the people and law and discipline, and reflecting on the harm of greed. Zhang says Party spirit does not rise automatically with seniority or rank and requires self-discipline, self-reform and acceptance of supervision. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-building commentary in 2025 links personal moral cultivation to the Party's campaign on work style.
quoteEn: Party spirit is the inner basis of work style: whatever kind of Party spirit one has, that is the kind of work style one will show.
quoteZh: 党性是作风的内在依据，有什么样的党性，就有什么样的作风。

glossary.explanation: The political character and moral qualities expected of a Communist Party member, including loyalty to the Party's ideals, discipline and service to the people. Cadres are urged to cultivate it continuously.
The conduct and manner in which Party members and cadres carry out their work and relate to the public. Official discourse treats it as a gauge of the Party's character.
Formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, targeted by Party campaigns since 2012.
Rules adopted in December 2012 on cadres' work style, including curbs on extravagance, banquets and bureaucratic practices. They launched the post-18th Party Congress drive on Party conduct.
The Party's working method of relying on and learning from the people. It is described officially as the Party's fundamental line of work.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.

t: Safeguarding high-quality development with new results in full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
zh: 以全面从严治党新成效护航高质量发展
source: China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News, 15 May 2025, p. 6
paras: This commentary, first published in the China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News in May 2025, responds to Xi Jinping's call at the Fourth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection to use new results in full and rigorous self-governance of the Party to support Chinese modernization. Fu argues that discipline inspection and supervision bodies should serve Chinese modernization and high-quality development through political supervision, work on conduct and corruption, and support for officials' initiative.

The piece is organised in three parts. Each sets out how supervision can build a particular development environment: one in which orders are carried out, one that is clean and upright, and one that rewards practical action. Fu draws on examples from Zhejiang.

On political supervision, Fu calls for supervision that is specific, precise and routine. This means focusing on concrete entry points, checking whether responsibility and work style are real, and using mechanisms such as monthly reports and closed-loop handling of problems. On conduct and corruption, Fu urges sustained work in key sectors such as finance, state-owned enterprises, energy and construction. Fu also urges joint investigation, analysis, handling and prevention of the two problems, and continued action against misconduct affecting ordinary people. Zhejiang's four-year campaign on bidding and tendering is cited as an example.

On officials' initiative, Fu proposes reducing formalism at the grassroots, as in Zhejiang's campaign against "formalism at the fingertips". Fu also proposes strict management combined with care: early warnings, clarifying false accusations, precise accountability and follow-up education for disciplined cadres. Fu presents these measures as ways to protect modernization. Read the original if you want a practitioner's account of how a provincial discipline commission turns national anti-corruption policy into working methods.
quoteEn: Problems of misconduct and corruption undermine fairness and justice, damage the business environment and disrupt economic order; they are "roadblocks" and "stumbling blocks" on the way to Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 风腐问题破坏公平正义、损害营商环境、扰乱经济秩序，是实现中国式现代化的“拦路虎”“绊脚石”。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A Party-building slogan prominent since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It covers discipline, anti-corruption and the Party's internal supervision.
The official term for China's path to modernization, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
An official economic-policy concept that stresses quality, innovation and efficiency over speed of growth. It is described as the primary task of building a modern socialist country.
Supervision by discipline inspection bodies of whether Party organisations and officials carry out the Central Committee's decisions and directives.
In Party discourse, work done for show, such as excessive meetings, paperwork and inspections. The Party treats it as a burden on grassroots officials.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Vigorously promote the model worker spirit, the labour spirit and the craftsmanship spirit
zh: 大力弘扬劳模精神、劳动精神、工匠精神
paras: This short commentary by Qiushi Online's commentators responds to the meeting held in the Great Hall of the People on 28 April 2025. The meeting marked the 100th anniversary of the All-China Federation of Trade Unions and honoured national model workers and advanced workers. The commentary relays Xi Jinping's call to promote the model worker spirit, the labour spirit and the craftsmanship spirit, and argues that these spirits are an essential moral force for national tasks.

The piece first recalls the history of model-worker recognition. It notes that 17 national meetings have been held since 1950 and names earlier exemplars such as Zhao Zhankui, Wu Yunduo and Wang Jinxi. It then describes the latest honourees, who include workers in farming and manufacturing, heritage craftspeople and workers in new occupations such as delivery riders. Finally it sets out practical measures for promoting the three spirits.

The commentary defines each spirit by its qualities: dedication and striving for excellence for model workers, honest and diligent labour for the labour spirit, and focus and perfectionism for craftsmanship. It presents them as embodiments of the core socialist values, of the national spirit centred on patriotism and of the spirit of the times centred on reform and innovation. The commentary argues that the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation needs spiritual as well as material strength. It says that, amid what it calls great changes unseen in a century, this spirit is needed to build consensus and to mobilise workers' initiative.

The commentary calls for a social climate in which labour is honoured, for more stories about model workers, and for labour education across the whole of talent training. It also calls for better employment and working conditions, aligned with high-quality development and the new round of technological and industrial change, so that workers gain a stronger sense of fulfilment. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party commentary links labour values, ideological education and national development goals.
quoteEn: The fine dreams of the human world can be realised only through honest labour; the various difficulties of development can be solved only through honest labour; and all the glories of life can be forged only through honest labour.
quoteZh: 人世间的美好梦想，只有通过诚实劳动才能实现；发展中的各种难题，只有通过诚实劳动才能破解；生命里的一切辉煌，只有通过诚实劳动才能铸就。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, popularly tied to the Chinese Dream, of restoring China's national strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.
The official economic priority since about 2017, stressing innovation, efficiency and sustainability over speed of growth.
A set of twelve values promoted by the Party since 2012 at the national, social and individual levels, including prosperity, democracy, patriotism and integrity.
The ideal of dedication, striving for excellence and selfless contribution, associated with the national model workers honoured by the state since 1950.
A term promoted by the Party for focus, meticulousness and the pursuit of excellence in one's craft or occupation.

t: Tightening the "master switch" of conduct, forging an honest "fresh force"
st: On conduct building among young cadres and the eight-point regulation
zh: 拧紧作风“总开关” 锻造清廉“生力军”
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 15 May 2025, asks how young Party cadres should build a sound work style and personal integrity. Xiao argues that conduct building is a permanent task and a compulsory course for young cadres. It is also a safeguard for keeping their political character. The piece ties this to the Party-wide study and education campaign on the eight-point regulation of the Central Committee, then under way.

The article opens with remarks by Xi Jinping on conduct building, including his Ningde-period warning about lifelong integrity and his 2021 speech at the Central Party School. It then sets out four requirements: theoretical study, strict self-discipline in daily life, integrity combined with responsibility, and persistence over the long term.

Xiao holds that belief is the root of conduct, so young cadres, whose worldview is not yet fully formed, must arm themselves with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and study the history of the eight-point regulation. The author reads cases of imprisoned young cadres as showing that violations begin with indifference to "small privileges" and petty bureaucratism, so problems must be stopped early and small. Xiao also calls for self-examination as an opportunity for the Party's self-reform, and for turning external constraint into inner conviction. Integrity, in this view, goes together with practical work for national development.

Xiao concludes that conduct problems are recurrent and stubborn, so the effort must be sustained and never a passing campaign. Young cadres are called on to keep the mindset of sitting an examination, and to keep burnishing the eight-point regulation as a "golden calling card", so that their improved conduct contributes to Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party commentary frames discipline and conduct for the younger generation of cadres.
quoteEn: Integrity and self-discipline are unified with taking responsibility and getting things done.
quoteZh: 廉洁自律是与担当作为相统一的。

glossary.explanation: A set of rules adopted by the Central Committee's Political Bureau in December 2012 to curb formalism, bureaucratism, extravagance and waste among Party officials. It has since been a central reference for Party conduct campaigns.
A term in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse for the Party's efforts to correct its own problems and maintain discipline, presented as a means of avoiding corruption and decay.
The official name for China's path of modernization, set out by Xi Jinping and the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.

t: Implementing the spirit of the eight-point regulation: what comes next?
zh: 落实八项规定精神接下来怎么干?
paras: This short commentary, excerpted from a longer piece by Dai Lixing and published in the Party journal Xianfeng in 2025, asks how the Party should carry forward the eight-point regulation on Party conduct. Dai argues that the current round of study and education signals a consistent commitment to implementing the regulation's spirit, addressing new problems inside the Party, and pursuing full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and the improvement of Party conduct through to the end.

Dai first recalls the origin of the regulation: the Political Bureau adopted it in December 2012, when, in the author's account, laxity and softness in Party building had left many inside and outside the Party worried about its future. The text then sets out three tasks for the present stage, concerning new challenges, new technology-driven forms of misconduct, and shortfalls in capacity and method.

Dai contends that the regulation began with the practices the public most detested and that most damaged the Party's image, and that this small entry point changed the overall pattern of Party governance and reversed laxity and softness. For the new stage, the author says study should focus on newly promoted, young and key-post cadres, who are vulnerable to corruption if they neglect this "compulsory political course". Dai also notes new variants of the "four undesirable work styles" such as virtual-currency red envelopes, livestream tipping as bribery, and e-gift cards, and argues that the Party must not "carve a mark on the boat to find a sword".

Dai calls for deeper use of data resources and for digital technology to be built into Party-discipline and supervision work, giving the examples of blockchain tracing of official spending and big-data monitoring of official vehicle use. Read the original if you want a brief, official-style statement of how Party-building scholars link the eight-point regulation to digital supervision and cadre education.
quoteEn: Party building must keep pace with the times and continually achieve innovation.
quoteZh: 党的建设要与时俱进，不断实现创新。

glossary.explanation: A set of rules on official conduct adopted by the Political Bureau in December 2012, aimed at curbing formalism, bureaucracy, extravagance and related practices among Party officials.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: Official slogan, prominent since the 18th Party Congress (2012), for strengthened discipline, anti-corruption work and internal Party management.
Formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, the Party-conduct problems targeted by the eight-point regulation.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: The great spirit of resistance against Japanese aggression as a precious asset for national rejuvenation
zh: 伟大抗战精神是砥砺复兴的宝贵财富
paras: Zhou Junjie asks how the spirit forged in the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression (1931–1945) can serve China today. The article argues that this "great spirit of resistance" is a precious spiritual asset that should be promoted now, when China is at what the author calls a critical stage in realising the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Zhou urges that it be used to sustain a fighting posture and to carry the country "from victory to new victory".

The commentary, published in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2025, has three parts. The first explains how the war produced the spirit. The second sets out why it is a valuable heritage, covering patriotism, revolutionary heroism and values shared by all humanity. The third turns to the present and names three uses for it. Zhou draws repeatedly on Xi Jinping's statements about the spirit.

In the first part, Zhou traces the spirit to three sources. One is national peril, described through Japanese atrocities and the author's figures of 100 billion US dollars in direct and 500 billion in indirect economic losses. Another is Communist Party leadership, illustrated by the united front, protracted war and Mao Zedong's On Protracted War (1938). The third is hardship, including fighting with inferior weapons against a large share of Japanese and puppet forces. The second part gives examples of mobilisation and sacrifice by home and overseas Chinese, and of military heroes. Zhou presents revolutionary heroism as a creative fusion of the Marxist view of heroes and the Chinese tradition of sacrificing life for righteousness. The author also says the victory spread values of freedom, justice and peace and shook the colonial system.

Zhou then calls for the spirit to be used in three ways. First, it should consolidate unity, so that people remember the Party's role as the "mainstay" of the war, trust it, and channel patriotism into Chinese modernization. Second, it should help overcome difficulties, which means vigilance against risks, bottom-line thinking and a readiness to struggle in a world of great changes. Third, it should defend peace, which Zhou argues must be won through struggle and strength, including readiness to act when core national interests are harmed and the building of a world-class military. Read the original if you want an example of how a military-affiliated Party theorist ties war memory to current themes of national rejuvenation, struggle and national defence.
quoteEn: Peace is not obtained by praying for it; it must be won through struggle and defended with strength.
quoteZh: 和平不是靠祈求得来的，而是要靠斗争去争取，靠实力去捍卫。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China to national strength and international standing after the "century of humiliation". It has been closely associated with Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream.
The official name for China's path of development under Party leadership. It is presented as distinct from Western models and as the means of achieving national rejuvenation.

glossary.literal: great spirit of the War of Resistance
glossary.explanation: Official term, used prominently by Xi Jinping, for the patriotism, heroism and determination attributed to the Chinese people in the war against Japan. It is counted within the Party's spiritual lineage.
Mao Zedong's 1938 text arguing that China would win the war against Japan through a long, staged struggle. Party histories treat it as the strategic guide of the resistance.

t: The core of the problem of work style is the Party's relationship with the people
zh: 作风问题核心是党同人民群众的关系问题
source: China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News, 13 May 2025, p. 8
paras: This commentary, first carried in the Party discipline newspaper China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News in May 2025, argues that the core of Party work style building is keeping flesh-and-blood ties between the Party and the people. Hong and Yang contend that the Party's greatest political strength is its close connection with the masses and that its greatest danger in office is becoming divorced from them.

The piece moves in three steps. It first restates the people's role as the source of the Party's strength, with examples from the revolutionary years. It then turns to the Party's tradition of serving the people, citing exemplary cadres such as Jiao Yulu and Kong Fansen. Finally it sets out measures for the long term.

The authors draw on the Marxist view that the people are the creators of history and argue that good work style has been vital to the Party's growth. They say that under reform and opening up, a market economy and long-term rule, the risk of detachment has grown. They name formalism, bureaucracy, hedonism and extravagance, the "four undesirable work styles", as an invisible wall between Party and people. In their account the eight-point rules have reshaped the Party's image, but work style problems recur and need sustained effort.

Hong and Yang propose theoretical education, a revival of the spirit of hard struggle, and long-term mechanisms: practical services for the people, regular investigation and research, and continuous work style building. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party School scholars link work style, the mass line and institutional measures in official discourse.
quoteEn: The more we pursue reform and opening up, develop the socialist market economy and remain in power for a long time, the more prominent the various work style problems within the Party become, and the more we must strengthen work style education and building.
quoteZh: 越是改革开放，越是发展社会主义市场经济，越是长期执政，党内形形色色的作风问题越是突出，我们越是要加强作风教育和作风建设。

glossary.explanation: The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China in 1978.
A Party principle, developed under Mao Zedong, that cadres should take ideas from the people, refine them and return them as policy, staying close to ordinary people.
Formalism, bureaucracy, hedonism and extravagance, which the Party has campaigned against since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
Rules adopted by the Central Committee in December 2012 to curb bureaucratic practices and extravagance among officials.

t: Beware of old problems of formalism in new guises
zh: 警惕形式主义老问题新表现
paras: This short commentary, published in Study Times in May 2025, argues that formalism remains a stubborn problem in the Party's conduct despite a decade of campaigning. Xu holds that formalism is incompatible with the Party's nature and purpose and is an enemy of its original mission. Although the "four forms of decadence" have been largely tackled since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Xu says they have not been eradicated, and formalism keeps mutating like a stubborn skin complaint.

Xu first recalls the Party's long opposition to formalism: Mao Zedong's remark that formalism is deadly, his use of rectification campaigns, and Deng Xiaoping's treatment of it as an issue for reforming Party and state leadership institutions. The piece then examines three new variants, named after parts of the body: formalism "at the fingertips", "at the toes" and "at the pen tip". It closes with a general call for sustained effort.

For each variant Xu names the symptom and then a remedy. Fingertip formalism means app check-ins and instant replies in work chats that tie grassroots cadres to their screens; Xu says its root lies in the head, in a distorted view of performance, and calls for cutting such tasks so cadres can go among the people. Toe formalism means staged inspection tours that show only highlights; Xu calls for going deep, being practical and judging research by results. Pen-tip formalism means reports that inflate achievements, play down shortcomings and pad data; Xu traces it to lazy governance and wants cadres to stop treating "traces" as achievements.

Xu concludes, citing Xi Jinping, that improving Party conduct is never finished and must be pursued relentlessly, with constant pressure and deterrence. The author argues that lasting results require turning persistence into routine and building long-term institutions. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party media frame the current campaign against formalism and bureaucratism at the grassroots level.
quoteEn: The form lies in the "fingertips", but the root lies in the "head".
quoteZh: 形式在“指尖”,根子却在“脑袋”。

glossary.explanation: The Party's term for formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance. It was the target of the Party's conduct campaign launched after the 18th Party Congress in 2012.
In Party discourse, a style of work that stresses outward show, paperwork and procedure over real results. It is treated as a core fault of Party conduct.

t: The question that determines the Party's survival and development
st: Xi Jinping's emphasis on "political direction"
zh: 关系党生存发展第一位的问题
zhSub: 习近平总书记强调的“政治方向”
paras: This short commentary, originally in Study Times (12 May 2025), takes up the question of why "political direction" matters for the Communist Party of China. Yao defines it as a party's basic stance, goals and trajectory on core questions such as the state system and social structure. The article contends that whether it is correct bears directly on the Party's future and on the success or failure of its cause.

The piece works through five statements by Xi Jinping on keeping to the correct political direction since the 18th Party Congress (2012). They date from 2012, 2013, 2018, 2020 and 2024, and each is tied to a different setting: the constitution anniversary, propaganda and ideological work, Party discipline, Politburo democratic life meetings, and reform.

Yao's central move is to treat political direction as something rooted in history and practice rather than subjectively set. It is said to be embodied in the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, in the Party Constitution as its institutionalised form, and in Party leadership over ideology and reform. For officials, the author calls for political acuity, systemic thinking and dialectical method, so that political problems are spotted early. On reform, the article argues that comprehensive Party leadership keeps reform serving the people and aimed at common prosperity.

Yao concludes that firmness on political direction underpins Chinese modernization and keeps Party members aligned with the Central Committee with Xi at its core. The text is a study-guide style exposition of Xi's remarks rather than an independent analysis. Read the original if you want a compact overview of how Party media present Xi's statements on political direction across 2012–2024.
quoteEn: Whether the political direction is correct or not directly determines the success or failure of reform and the course of national development.
quoteZh: 政治方向的正确与否，直接决定着改革的成败和国家发展的走向。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's model of socialism since the reform era. It is presented as Marxism adapted to China's conditions.
The Party's official formulation of China's path to modernity, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official goal of shared wealth for all, emphasised under Xi Jinping as a defining feature of socialism.

t: The great significance of strengthening Party conduct in the new era
zh: 新时代加强党的作风建设的重大意义
source: Chinese Party and Government Cadres Forum (中国党政干部论坛), 2025 no. 4
paras: Jin Minqing asks why strengthening the Party's conduct (dang de zuofeng jianshe) matters so much in the new era. The article argues that it is a decisive guarantee for the Party's task of advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. In Jin's account, the Party faces unprecedented risks, so it must govern itself with a spirit of reform and strict standards and sustain work on conduct.

The article is built around three claims, each developed in its own section. Conduct-building is described as a weapon for preserving the Party's advanced and pure character, as a key measure for consolidating the foundation of long-term governance, and as an important guarantee for achieving the Party's central task. Jin draws throughout on Mao Zedong's writings and on Xi Jinping's statements on conduct, the Party's self-reform and the mass line, and traces the historical record from the Jinggangshan base area and the Yan'an period to the post-1949 rectification campaigns.

First, Jin follows Xi in treating problems of conduct as fundamentally problems of Party spirit. Conduct expresses the Party's nature and purpose of serving the people wholeheartedly, and it also drives the Party's self-reform. In the new era, Jin says, formalism and bureaucratism have become entangled with corruption, which makes conduct a political problem. Second, popular support is presented as the Party's ultimate legitimacy. Jin argues that conduct-building helps the Party escape the historical cycle of rise and decline. Mao's answer was letting the people supervise government, and Xi's second answer is self-reform. Jin adds that conduct-building addresses the problems unique to a large party. Third, Jin argues that Party leadership is the defining feature of Chinese modernization. Cadres' conduct is therefore how that leadership is made concrete, and it is how the mass line is applied and how common prosperity is advanced.

Jin concludes that the Party's conduct and image are part of its strength, its moral force alongside the force of truth, and that they partly determine the success or failure of Chinese modernization. The author calls on Party committees, especially at city and county level, to treat unhealthy tendencies and corruption near ordinary people as a regular task. Cadres are urged to keep a people-centred stance. Read the original if you want a representative Party-theory account of how current official discourse links conduct, legitimacy, self-reform and modernization.
quoteEn: The Party's conduct is an important component of the Party's strength and an important embodiment of its personal moral force.
quoteZh: 党的作风是党的力量的重要组成部分，是党的人格力量的重要体现。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's path to modernization under Party leadership, stressing features such as huge population size, common prosperity and peaceful development. It is presented as an alternative to Western modernization.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's overarching national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, linked to the 'second centenary goal' of 2049.
Xi Jinping's term for the Party's continuous self-purification, self-improvement and self-renewal. It is presented as the second answer to the problem of the historical cycle.
The Party's traditional method of work, which holds that the Party must draw on the masses and serve them, and must stay in close contact with them.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, presented as a defining feature of socialism and of Chinese modernization.

t: Promoting the spirit of educators and nurturing outstanding teachers for a great country in the new era
zh: 弘扬教育家精神 培育新时代大国良师
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in May 2025, asks how the "spirit of educators" can guide the building of a high-quality teaching force. Zhu argues that this spirit supplies core value guidance for teachers and should shape what a good teacher in the new era is expected to be.

The piece opens with the national commendation of model workers, which included teachers in western universities, rural schools and special education. It then links the theme to the Outline for Building a Leading Education Country (2024–2035), which calls for an action to "forge the soul and strengthen teachers" through the spirit of educators. This is to run through teacher training, teaching, research and social practice.

Zhu organises the argument around three qualities of a good teacher for a great country. The first is great virtue: teachers should hold firm ideals, serve the people and the Party's governance, and act as moral exemplars in fostering virtue and cultivating people. The second is great wisdom: teachers should unite professional skill with moral cultivation, being both teachers of classics and teachers of character, and should respect the laws of education. The third is great vision, built on benevolent love, with the Guangming Daily's example of the headmaster Zhang Guimei, and on a sense of mission that extends to promoting the common values of all humanity.

Zhu concludes that carrying out the action to forge the soul and strengthen teachers will root this spirit in teachers' hearts and help gather strength for building a leading education country. Read the original if you want a brief example of how official discourse describes the ideal teacher and links teacher ethics to the education-power agenda.
quoteEn: Education is a undertaking of "benevolence and love for others"; love is the soul of education, and without love there is no education, so love is also the foundation of the spirit of educators.
quoteZh: 教育是“仁而爱人”的事业，爱是教育的灵魂，没有爱就没有教育，因此热爱也是教育家精神的底色。

glossary.explanation: A set of qualities expected of teachers, including ideals, moral character, wisdom, benevolence and a commitment to teaching. It was articulated in official statements in 2023 as a guide for the teaching profession.
A national goal of building China into a country with a leading education system, set out in the 2024–2035 outline. It is often described as supporting wider national rejuvenation.
The official fundamental task of education in China: moral education and the shaping of students' character alongside knowledge.

t: Strengthening Party-building leadership to support innovation in community governance
zh: 强化党建引领 助力社区治理创新
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today on 9 May 2025, asks how Party building can lead innovation in urban community governance. Wang argues that grassroots governance is the foundation of national governance and that the community is its basic unit, the "last mile" linking the Party and government to residents. The author's answer is three mutually supporting paths: organisational leadership, resource-guarantee leadership and service leadership.

The piece opens with the 20th Party Congress report (2022) and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which call for Party-building leadership of grassroots governance. It draws on the author's field investigations of communities in various places, and moves through the three paths in turn before presenting them as one system.

On organisation, Wang observes that grassroots Party organisations are weakening and need better structures: Party general branches and branches set by Party-member numbers, clear divisions of labour with residents' committees and supervisory committees, deliberation rules, and a weighing of the pros and cons of concurrent posts. On resources, Wang describes community foundations, charity supermarkets and public-interest markets that pool internal and external resources, with Party building supplying mobilising power. On services, the author calls for needs-oriented work, assessing residents' needs through observation, home visits, focus groups and joint community meetings.

Wang concludes that the three paths form a systematic project running from building organisations to delivering services. The stated aims are better governance mechanisms, mobilised resources, improved services and residents' greater sense of gain, which would modernize grassroots governance systems and capacity. Read the original if you want a brief, practice-oriented account of how Chinese scholars frame Party-led community governance.
quoteEn: Party-building leadership of community governance becomes a systematic project, beginning with building the organisational system and ultimately resting on services.
quoteZh: 党建引领社区治理成为一项系统工程，即从构建组织体系开始，最终落实到服务

t: Advancing Party conduct building from the standpoint of serving the Party's overall work
zh: 从服务党的工作大局的高度推进作风建设
paras: This short commentary, published in Study Times in May 2025, asks how the Party's work on conduct (zuofeng jianshe) should be understood and pursued. Zhu Peilei argues, following Xi Jinping, that such work serves the Party's overall work and is not an isolated task. Improving conduct, in this reading, should be the same process as carrying out the Party's theory, line and policies and advancing reform and opening up and socialist modernization.

The article first sets out the historical record, from the Yan'an rectification movement, which established standards such as linking theory with practice, to the correction of the "four undesirable work styles" in the new era. It then turns to the present, when the Party's size, time in power and environment make conduct problems more complex. It closes with practical directions for 2025, the final year of the 14th Five-Year Plan.

Zhu contends that conduct building has gone beyond disciplinary tidying-up and become a key variable in the depth of reform, the quality of development and governance effectiveness. The author traces a continuing line from the "two musts" to the "three musts" and from the Eight-point Regulation to the current study and education campaign on it, and describes a system covering thinking, study, work, leadership and cadres' private life. Two tasks are stressed. One is to improve conduct through close ties with the people, curbing formalism and bureaucratism and exposing "lying-flat" cadres. The other is to temper conduct in complex conditions, citing China–US trade friction, technology blockades and geopolitical conflict, so that cadres become more pragmatic and efficient.

Zhu calls on the whole Party to use the study and education campaign on the Eight-point Regulation, and to link it with implementing central decisions and with the work on Party integrity and anti-corruption. The aim is to produce new results in conduct building and a new phase of high-quality development. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party media in 2025 link conduct building to economic and national tasks.
quoteEn: Conduct building is not only a key step in putting the Party's purpose into practice and purifying its style, but also a practical means of rallying Party members and cadres to work together and get things done.
quoteZh: 作风建设不仅是践行宗旨、纯洁党风的关键之举，更是推动党员干部凝心聚力、干事创业的务实之功。

glossary.explanation: The Party's long-running effort to shape the thinking, working methods and daily behaviour of its members and cadres. It is often presented as a means of maintaining the Party's ties with the people.
Formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, named as targets of the campaign launched after the 18th Party Congress (2012).
Rules adopted by the Central Committee in December 2012 to curb extravagance, bureaucracy and formalism among officials, covering matters such as meetings, travel and receptions.
Mao Zedong's 1949 call to keep to a modest and hard-working style. In 2022 Xi Jinping added a third ("three musts"), on daring to struggle.
Official terms for cadre habits of putting on a show of work and of being detached from the public and from practical results.
The official goal for China's economy since about 2017, stressing quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.

t: Conduct building should aim to turn good practice into lasting custom
zh: 作风建设重在化风成俗
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in May 2025, Liu Ziyi and Wu Fulai ask how the Party's work on conduct (zuofeng jianshe) can be made durable. Their answer is the idea of "turning conduct into custom" (huafeng chengsu): improved practice should settle into habit and conscious commitment rather than remain a campaign result. They present it as a key phrase in Xi Jinping's remarks on the Central Committee's eight-point regulation, including his March 2025 inspection tour of Guizhou and Yunnan, where he spoke of loosening in some places and a rebound of bad habits.

The article is a short commentary tied to the Party-wide study and education campaign on implementing the spirit of the eight-point regulation. It is organised in three parts: the idea as an expression of the Party's self-awareness as a Marxist party; its roots in the Party's history from the revolutionary years to the new era; and three practical requirements for the present.

On the first point, the authors read the Han Shu line on rulers shaping "wind" and the people's "custom". They define "wind" as phased results of top-down education and correction, and "custom" as a lasting good climate in which cadres' norms and values are internalised. They describe this as a dialectical shift from quantity to quality, which opens a new stage rather than ending the work. For the present, they set out three requirements. The first is to combine targeted correction with treatment of root causes, since the "four undesirable work styles" (formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism, extravagance) reappear in disguised forms, such as "digital traces" replacing meeting overload; corruption and misconduct should be investigated and addressed together. The second is to join external constraint, through Party regulations, with inner conviction, through ideological education. The third is to align Party and government conduct with social and popular customs, with leading cadres setting the example.

The authors conclude that conduct building has no end point and must be kept up consistently until good conduct becomes habitual. In their account, this supports the Party's long-term governance and provides a safeguard for further deepening reform and advancing Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party-building discourse in 2025 frames the long-term institutionalisation of the eight-point regulation and its historical lineage.
quoteEn: The idea of turning conduct into custom shows that Party conduct building is not the work of a single moment or a single matter. Only by persevering and sustaining the effort can improving conduct become a habit, a conscious commitment and a responsibility across the whole Party.
quoteZh: 化风成俗的理念，深刻揭示了党的作风建设不是一时一事之功，只有锲而不舍、久久为功，才能使改进作风在全党成为一种习惯、一种自觉、一种责任

glossary.explanation: A phrase Xi Jinping uses for conduct improvements that become lasting habit. The authors derive it from the Han Shu line about rulers shaping "wind" and the people's "custom".

Rules adopted by the Politburo in December 2012, shortly after the 18th Party Congress, to improve officials' work style and curb extravagance and bureaucratism. They have been the basis of the Party's conduct campaigns since.
Formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, the practices targeted by the Party's conduct campaigns since 2012.
The official term for China's development path, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: University functional league organisations should strengthen the "three attributes" and raise the "three capacities"
zh: 高校功能型团组织要增强“三性”提升“三力”
paras: This short commentary asks how functional league organisations in universities should define their identity and make their education of students effective. Xu and Gu argue that these units must hold to three attributes, namely political character, mass character and precision, and that doing so raises three corresponding capacities: ideological guidance, organisational cohesion and service.

The authors begin with the revised regulations on grassroots Communist Youth League work in regular universities, issued jointly by the League's Central Committee and the Ministry of Education. These call for functional league organisations built on student self-governing bodies such as student unions and clubs, or on groups formed around a task. The article then takes each attribute and capacity in turn.

On political character, Xu and Gu hold that it is the essential attribute of the League. Functional organisations sit mostly in informal, interest-based groups, which have strong cohesion but must not trade away political character to win participation. The authors link mass character to advanced character as a dialectical unity: the vanguard role needs a mass base, and mass activity needs political direction. They call for managing student self-governing bodies, promoting role models and building online communities, so that students can find the League. On precision, they cite Xi Jinping's call to solve practical problems for young people, and propose campus culture, festival-themed activities and innovation and entrepreneurship competitions as the vehicles.

The authors conclude that functional organisations can extend League coverage, strengthen the grassroots and join the first and second classrooms. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party-youth work in Chinese universities frames organisational reform.
quoteEn: Functional league organisations absolutely must not sacrifice their political attribute in order to win the participation and support of young university students.
quoteZh: 功能型团组织绝对不能牺牲政治属性来换取青年大学生的参与与支持

glossary.explanation: The Communist Youth League of China is the Party's youth organisation for people roughly aged 14 to 28. It operates in schools, universities and workplaces.

Grassroots League units set up on the basis of student self-governing bodies, clubs or task groups, rather than formal departments or classes. They supplement the traditional organisation-based (entity-type) League branches.
A common term in Party youth work for shaping the political beliefs and values of young people.
The first classroom means formal teaching in the curriculum. The second classroom means extracurricular activities such as practice, culture and competitions.

t: Making a concerted effort to strengthen the system of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
zh: 着力加强全面从严治党体系建设
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today on 8 May 2025, responds to the 15th collective study session of the Political Bureau of the 20th Central Committee, which discussed improving the system of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Du argues that such a system is the key to preserving the Party's vanguard character and purity within the Party's self-reform, and sets out how it should be strengthened.

The article is organised around five tasks: consolidating the foundations through ideological and Party-spirit education; building a tightly organised structure; raising the effectiveness of supervision; improving the system of intra-Party regulations; and pooling the efforts of Party organisations and members through clear responsibilities.

Du proposes concrete measures under each heading. On organisation, the author calls for a closed-loop mechanism of decision, execution, supervision and feedback, tracking platforms for implementing central decisions, and Party organisations in new fields such as internet and logistics firms. On supervision, Du stresses political supervision centred on the Two Upholds, power and responsibility lists for top leaders, and the combination of intra-Party supervision with public reporting, supported by big-data analysis. On responsibility, Party committees, discipline inspection commissions, committee secretaries and individual members are each assigned defined duties.

Du concludes that the task is long and arduous and requires sustained effort across the Party, providing a political and organisational guarantee for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned summary of the practical measures commentators link to the 2025 Politburo study session on Party self-governance.
quoteEn: Improving the system of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party is a long and arduous task that requires the whole Party to work together with sustained effort.
quoteZh: 健全全面从严治党体系是一项长期而艰巨的任务，需要全党上下齐心协力、久久为功。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012) covering discipline, anti-corruption, ideology and organisation within the Communist Party of China.
An official concept in which the Party presents itself as capable of correcting its own problems through internal discipline and supervision.
The requirement to uphold General Secretary Xi Jinping's core position in the Party and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: An official national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, associated with the Chinese Dream.

t: Practising whole-process people's democracy: implementing and improving the people's supervisor system
zh: 践行全过程人民民主落实和完善人民监督员制度
paras: Writing in Study Times in May 2025, Ying Yong, head of the Supreme People's Procuratorate, argues that implementing and improving the people's supervisor system is an important way for procuratorates to put whole-process people's democracy into practice. Under this system, citizens drawn from many walks of life oversee how procuratorates handle cases. Ying presents it as a means of ensuring that prosecutorial power is exercised for the people, subject to the people's supervision and satisfactory to the people.

The article has three parts. The first explains why the system matters, noting that the Supreme People's Procuratorate began exploring it in 2003 and that Party documents from the 18th Party Congress (2012) onward ordered its deepening, including a 2015 reform plan. The second reviews progress in selection, supervisory effectiveness and support for supervisors, with figures. The third sets out four requirements for further work.

Ying's core reasoning is that the system serves three purposes. It widens orderly citizen participation, in line with the constitutional principle that all power belongs to the people. It adds external oversight to internal procuratorial controls, so that those who supervise others also accept supervision. It also helps test cases against public perceptions of fairness. As evidence, Ying cites the 'separation of management and use' mechanism, under which judicial administrative bodies select and manage supervisors while procuratorates organise their work. The article reports 25,000 supervisors nationwide, 740,000 case-handling activities supervised since 2015, 470,000 opinions offered and an 89.3 per cent adoption rate.

Ying calls for upholding Party leadership, including the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, and for accepting supervision more consciously by inviting supervisors to take part wherever possible. Ying also urges closer cooperation between procuratorates and judicial administrative bodies, and for the supporting mechanisms to be completed. The article names gaps in linking the system with other external checks and in guaranteeing supervisors' ability to perform their duties. Read the original if you want an official procuratorial account of how citizen oversight of prosecutors is institutionalised in China, with statistics and the rules governing it.
quoteEn: The ones who experience fairness and justice are the people, not the judicial personnel; it is not enough for them to declare themselves fair. The people's feelings must come first, and their satisfaction is the highest standard.
quoteZh: 对公平正义感受的主体是人民群众，不是司法人员自己说公正就公正了，要以人民群众感受为第一感受，以人民群众满意为最高标准。

glossary.explanation: A concept associated with Xi Jinping, which the Party presents as a form of democracy covering every stage of governance and not only elections. It has been used in official discourse since the late 2010s.
A system in which citizens chosen from various backgrounds observe and give opinions on procuratorial case handling. The Supreme People's Procuratorate began trialling it in 2003.
A mechanism under which judicial administrative bodies select and manage the supervisors, while procuratorates only arrange their participation in cases. It is meant to keep supervision neutral.
A Party formulation affirming Xi Jinping's status as the core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought. It was adopted in 2021–22.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Party and the authority and centralised leadership of the Central Committee.

keywords: Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law

t: The journal The Communist and the building of the Party's mobilisation capacity during the War of Resistance
zh: 《共产党人》杂志与抗战时期党的动员能力建设
paras: Wang Fengqing, writing in Guangming Daily (7 May 2025), asks how the Party journal The Communist (Gongchandang ren) helped the Chinese Communist Party build its capacity to mobilise the population during the War of Resistance against Japan. The journal was an internal theoretical publication of the Central Committee. It ran from October 1939 to August 1941, for 19 issues, a period of Guomindang anti-communist policy and a serious setback for the anti-Japanese united front. Wang argues that the journal gave timely, practical guidance to Party organisations and members, and so played a historical role in gathering strength for national victory.

The short article treats the war as a contest for popular support as well as a military one. It is organised around three themes in the journal's content: the vanguard and exemplary role of Party members, the flexible use of mobilisation methods, and the timely summing up of useful experience. Wang draws on articles by Yang Shangkun, Zhang Wentian, Li Weihan and Yang Song, on field reports from villages and army units, and on directives of the Central Propaganda Department.

On the first theme, Wang reports that the journal's authors insisted that Party members set an example, whether by keeping the Party distinct from ordinary masses and expelling opportunists, or by befriending even die-hard and middle elements in the united front. Under the "three-thirds" system of government, Party members were to win over non-Party people by exemplary work. Local reports described branches that made leading by example part of Party education. On the second theme, the journal advised tailoring propaganda to its audience: enemy troops, the army's own soldiers, international opinion and young people. Youth work, it said, should be lively and sincere rather than recite resolutions. Central directives on writers, on propaganda against the enemy and puppet regimes, and on agitation among the masses asked for vivid, popular language tied to people's immediate concerns.

Wang concludes that the journal's guidance was both theoretical and practical, and that its habit of summarising experience, a tradition he describes as a political strength of the Party, helped spread successful practice. Examples include women's work in Wan County, Hebei, and a grain-collection committee in Yan'an in which 18 of 27 representatives were non-Party and the grain quota was exceeded. Wang judges that this had a positive effect on mobilisation work. Read the original if you want a brief overview of how a wartime Party journal is presented in current official historiography as a tool for training and mobilising cadres.
quoteEn: The Communist journal promptly summarised and scientifically distilled the practices and experience of Party organisations and members at all levels in strengthening mobilisation capacity, and this had a positive influence on advancing that work.
quoteZh: 《共产党人》杂志对各级组织和党员加强动员能力建设过程中的做法与经验进行及时总结与科学归纳，对推进动员能力建设产生了积极影响。

glossary.explanation: A principle for anti-Japanese base-area governments, set out in 1940, under which Communists, left-wing progressives and middle-of-the-road figures each held roughly one third of seats. It was meant to broaden the united front.
The wartime cooperation between the Chinese Communist Party and the Guomindang and other groups against Japan. It came under severe strain from 1939 as the Guomindang pursued anti-communist policies.
The Party doctrine that Party members must lead and set an example for the masses in work and conduct. The article follows Mao Zedong's 1938 formulation of it.
The Chinese name for the war with Japan of 1937–1945, treated in Chinese historiography as part of the wider anti-fascist war.

t: A major milestone in the history of the Party
st: Commemorating the 80th anniversary of the Seventh Party Congress
zh: 在党的历史上具有重要里程碑意义
zhSub: 纪念党的七大召开80周年
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of the Seventh National Congress of the Communist Party of China, held in Yan'an from April to June 1945, Li Rong argues that the congress was a landmark in Party history. In Li's account it summed up more than two decades of the new-democratic revolution, set the line, programme and tactics, and wrote Mao Zedong Thought into the Party constitution as the guiding ideology. The congress went down as a "congress of unity and victory", and Li draws five lessons from it for the present.

The article has three parts. The first describes the long preparation: the 17-year gap since the Sixth Congress (1928), the repeated postponements, the election of delegates, their dangerous journeys to Yan'an, and their participation in the Yan'an rectification movement. The second narrates the congress itself, including Mao's opening speech, his political report "On Coalition Government", the reports by Zhu De, Liu Shaoqi and Zhou Enlai, the new constitution, the first secret-ballot election in a Party congress, and the First Plenum of the Seventh Central Committee. The third part moves from the victory of 1949 to the five lessons.

Li presents the rectification movement and the 1945 resolution on questions of Party history as what produced ideological unity among delegates, who were examined on dogmatism and empiricism and asked to criticise themselves. From the congress, Li draws five requirements. The Party must maintain unity and its position as the leading core, which Li links to the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds. It must innovate in theory, from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. It must follow the mass line and serve the people wholeheartedly. It must carry out criticism and the Party's self-reform. And it must stay alert to danger and be ready to struggle, as Mao listed 17 difficulties in 1945.

Li concludes that the congress showed the Party's political, ideological and organisational maturity, and that its lessons bear directly on full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and on building a strong modern socialist country. Li calls for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation to be pursued through Chinese modernization with heightened vigilance. Read the original if you want an official Party-history reading of the Seventh Congress and of how it is used today to support Party unity, leadership and self-reform.
quoteEn: The greatness of the Communist Party of China lies not in making no mistakes, but in never shying away from treating its own ailments, daring to face problems, being bold in self-reform, and having a very strong capacity for self-repair.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的伟大不在于不犯错误，而在于从不讳疾忌医，敢于直面问题，勇于自我革命，具有极强的自我修复能力。

glossary.explanation: A formulation from the 2022 Party resolution on history, affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold the authority of the General Secretary as the core and the centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and presented as the latest result of adapting Marxism to China.
A Party term for its own continuing correction of errors and rectification of its ranks, emphasised in Xi-era discourse.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A policy line since 2014 that stresses strict discipline, anti-corruption work and Party-building.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: An official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, central to Party narrative since the early 2010s.
The official name for the Party's path of national development, presented as distinct from Western models.

t: Taking up the mission the Party has assigned to the Communist Youth League in the new era and on the new journey
zh: 担起新时代新征程党赋予共青团的使命任务
authors: Secretariat of the Central Committee of the Communist Youth League of China
paras: Written by the Secretariat of the Communist Youth League (CYL) Central Committee and published in Qiushi in 2025, this programmatic commentary asks how the League should carry out the tasks the Party has set for it. It takes as its basis Xi Jinping's speech at the League's 19th National Congress and his talk with the new League leadership in June 2023. The authors argue that the League must remain the Party's assistant and reserve force, and that its work should follow the Party's central tasks.

The text is organised around six "how" questions: how to hold to the League's fundamental position, how to nurture new-era youth, how to serve the overall agenda, how to be a bridge to young people, how to energise League organisations, and how to govern the League strictly. Each section first reviews achievements since 2023 and then sets out tasks for the new journey. The authors give figures and examples, including the 390,000-plus League branches in the theme education campaign, "Youth Post Houses" for graduates, and the Western China volunteer programme.

The core claim is that political character is the League's first attribute, so that "where the Party's flag points, the League's flag follows". The authors say the League must become a political school guiding young people's thinking, a vanguard force for long-term struggle, a firm bridge between the Party and youth, and an advanced organisation. They report that League organisations in new fields grew from under 100,000 five years earlier to over 700,000. They also describe efforts on youth employment, mental-health services and grassroots reform. Alongside this, the authors stress that young people are exposed to varied social currents and to hostile forces, which makes ideological guidance harder.

The authors conclude that the League should deepen reform at the grassroots, expand organisational coverage, and apply full and rigorous self-governance of the Party's logic to League cadres and members through discipline, training and tighter admission. They call for mobilising young people to contribute to Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want an official account of how the League's leadership frames its priorities, achievements and tasks under Xi Jinping.
quoteEn: We bear in mind that political character is the League's first attribute, and that heeding the Party and following the Party has always been the political lifeblood the League upholds.
quoteZh: 我们牢记，政治性是共青团的第一属性，听党话、跟党走始终是共青团坚守的政治生命

glossary.explanation: The Party's youth organisation for people roughly aged 14 to 28, which describes itself as a school of communism and the Party's reserve force.
The official name for China's path of development, set out by Party leaders since the early 2020s as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: A Party-building policy launched under Xi Jinping, stressing discipline, anti-corruption and stricter supervision of members and cadres. Here it is extended to the League.

t: Making great efforts to improve political capability
zh: 着力提高政治能力
authors: Central Party School (National Academy of Governance) Committee
paras: This article, issued in the name of the Central Party School (National Academy of Governance) committee and published in Qiushi in 2025, takes up the question of how Party members and officials should raise their political capability. It argues that, at a critical period for building a strong country and advancing national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization, political capability is the first among the abilities cadres need. It presents this as a response to Xi Jinping's repeated calls to speak plainly about politics and to place political cultivation first in Party-spirit cultivation.

The text is organised as eight tasks, each introduced by a short heading: strengthening political loyalty; keeping to the correct political direction; serving the political big picture; strictly observing political discipline and rules; strengthening political responsibility; preventing and defusing political risks; continually purifying the political ecosystem; and cultivating sound political ethics. Each section combines statements by Xi Jinping, references to Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and model cadres such as Jiao Yulu, and practical demands on officials.

The argument rests on a few moves. First, loyalty to the Party is treated as the primary political quality, and the article says it must be anchored in the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, including upholding the authority of the Party Central Committee. Second, direction, the overall interest and discipline are linked: officials are told to put local and sectional interests beneath the national whole, to treat political discipline as the foremost of the Party's six disciplines, and to report major matters as required. Third, the article stresses risk and conduct: it calls for vigilance against political risks, including those it attributes to hostile Western forces, for resistance to cliques and 'one-man rule', and for the cultivation of personal and official virtue.

The article concludes that officials should turn political requirements from external demands into inner conviction, so that they become politically firmer and more mature. It calls on them to take up responsibility in priority areas such as high-quality development, to practise full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, and to build a clean political ecosystem. Read the original if you want an authoritative statement of the Party-school line on what 'political capability' demands of cadres in the Xi Jinping era.
quoteEn: Political discipline is the fundamental guarantee for safeguarding the Party's unity and solidarity; it is a red line that Party members and officials must not cross and a bottom line they must hold.
quoteZh: 政治纪律是维护党的团结统一的根本保证，是党员、干部不可逾越的红线、必须坚守的底线。

glossary.explanation: A formula adopted in the Party's 2021 historical resolution: establishing Xi Jinping's position as core of the Central Committee and of the whole Party, and establishing the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.

The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Party and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Party Central Committee. The article calls it the Party's highest political principle.
The official term for China's path to modernization under Party leadership, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party-discipline and anti-corruption campaign pursued since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
An official metaphor for the overall political climate within the Party, including its culture, norms, and the state of discipline and corruption.

t: How the Communist Party of China won the "two historical initiatives"
zh: 中国共产党何以赢得“两个历史主动”
paras: This commentary, published in Study Times on 5 May 2025, interprets Xi Jinping's speech at the Fourth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection. Chen Li asks how the Party has won what the speech calls two "historical initiatives": keeping the Party from changing in quality, colour or flavour, and uniting the people behind the building of a strong country and national rejuvenation. Chen's answer is that the Party has led social revolution through self-reform and has pursued the fight against corruption on a sustained, systematic basis.

The article is organised in four parts. It first treats the anti-corruption struggle as a long-term political task of the Party's self-reform. It then sets out three strands of the approach: deterrence through high-pressure punishment, restraint through institutions and supervision, and moral and ideological cultivation. Throughout, Chen draws on Xi's formulations and on the record since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

In Chen's account, the Party leadership has repeatedly judged the situation to be "still severe and complex", moving from the "three persistents" of 2013 to the "two stills" of the latest plenum, which note that existing corruption has not been cleared and new cases keep emerging. The central method is to advance in an integrated way the aims that officials should not dare, not be able and not want to be corrupt. Chen describes zero tolerance, no "restricted zones" and no quotas for investigations, and cites 2024 figures: 2.175 million leads handled, 877,000 cases filed and 889,000 people disciplined, including 58 centrally managed cadres. The article presents institutional measures as the root remedy: power lists, tighter procedures, Party regulations, discipline placed ahead of law, inspection tours with full coverage, and a full and rigorous self-governance of the Party system. It adds ideological education, a correct view of power, and a healthier political culture within the Party.

Chen concludes that the struggle must continue, with the Party fighting a decisive, protracted and all-round battle against corruption. The article presents this as essential to Chinese modernization and to escaping the historical cycle of rise and fall. Read the original if you want an example of how official Party commentary explains the anti-corruption campaign and its link to the Party's self-reform.
quoteEn: Corruption eats away at the Party's body, undermines fairness and justice and harms relations between cadres and the masses; it is the biggest malignant tumour threatening the Party's vitality and fighting capacity, and a "stumbling block" that must be removed to advance Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 腐败侵蚀党的肌体，破坏公平正义，影响干群关系，是危害党的生命力和战斗力的最大毒瘤，是推进中国式现代化必须着力清除的“拦路虎”“绊脚石”。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed by Xi Jinping: the Party's capacity to correct its own problems and purify itself through rigorous internal discipline. It is presented as the basis of its governance.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: A strategic principle since the 18th Party Congress (2012) covering Party discipline, conduct, organisation and anti-corruption work.
The official name for China's path of modernization, set out by Xi Jinping and the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

glossary.pinyin: bù gǎn fǔ, bù néng fǔ, bù xiǎng fǔ
glossary.en: not dare, not be able and not want to be corrupt
glossary.literal: dare not, cannot, do not want to be corrupt
glossary.explanation: The official three-part formula for anti-corruption: deterrence by punishment, prevention through institutions, and moral self-discipline through education.

t: Adhering to the path of cultural development with Chinese characteristics
zh: 坚持中国特色社会主义文化发展道路
paras: This short commentary, published in Economic Daily on 30 April 2025, asks how China should keep to the path of cultural development with Chinese characteristics. Li Yuanyuan argues that Party leadership is the most essential feature of this path and the organisational and ideological guarantee for building a culture-strong country.

The piece first recalls the principle that the Party manages propaganda and ideology, and says the Party has led cultural work through the revolutionary, construction and reform periods. It then credits the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012) with a fundamental turn in the ideological field and stronger cultural confidence. Li sets out three tasks for the present.

The first is to uphold Marxism's guiding position in ideology. Li holds that Marxism is a guide to action, not dogma, and that it fits Chinese civilisation closely. Li calls for the Two Integrations to be applied so that theoretical, institutional and cultural innovation continues. The second is to improve cultural governance in the information age: strengthen internet management according to law, guard against online ideological risks, reform mainstream media and build a multi-level communication matrix. The third is to let the core socialist values guide cultural work. Li lists their incorporation into law, textbooks, the "two benefits" standard for cultural output and citizen moral-building programmes.

Li concludes that only by making the core socialist values everyday, concrete and lived can they become the people's shared pursuit and secure the cultural foundation for national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style statement of how Party-school scholarship frames Party leadership, ideology, media governance and values education in cultural policy.
quoteEn: Upholding the Party's leadership is the most essential feature of the path of cultural development with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 坚持党的领导，是中国特色社会主义文化发展道路最本质的特征。

glossary.explanation: A formula in Party theory for combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's specific realities and with its fine traditional culture. The second integration was added in official discourse in 2021–2023.
A set of 24 characters in twelve values, at national, social and individual levels, promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012) as the official moral and ideological foundation.
The official standard that cultural products should be judged by both social benefit and economic benefit, with social benefit given priority.
A stated goal of building China into a country with strong cultural influence and soft power, set out in Party documents.

t: Putting political cultivation first in Party-spirit cultivation
zh: 把政治修养摆在党性修养的首位
paras: Published in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2025, this commentary takes up a directive Xi Jinping gave at a Politburo democratic life meeting in December 2024: that political cultivation (zhengzhi xiuyang) must come first in the cultivation of Party spirit (dangxing). Shi Xu places the directive within the current Party-wide study and education campaign on implementing the central Eight-point Regulation. The author's thesis is that forging Party spirit and raising ideological awareness requires putting political cultivation first, so that cadres steadily improve their political judgement, political understanding and political execution.

The article has three sections. The first sets out why the priority is necessary, the second argues that political cultivation is the most fundamental form of cultivation for Party members and cadres, and the third describes how cadres should pursue it as a lifelong task. Shi draws throughout on Xi Jinping's statements and on the reports to the 19th Party Congress (2017) and the 20th Party Congress (2022).

On necessity, Shi gives three reasons. Political development is said to lead the Party's overall building, so cultivation must follow that order. Fulfilling the tasks of Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is said to require politically reliable cadres. And the "unique challenges of a large party" can be met only by looking at problems politically. On primacy, Shi contends that political attributes are a party's first attribute, that political cultivation underpins the Party's vanguard character and purity, and that it sets the direction and effect of theoretical, moral, cultural, professional and disciplinary cultivation alike. If political cultivation goes astray, the author says, the other kinds lose their meaning.

For practice, Shi proposes three tasks: tempering political character through loyalty to the Party, which the author describes as unconditional and tied to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era; building political ability through political experience; and strengthening political responsibility, including a correct view of performance that values both visible and long-term achievements. The author concludes that cultivation never ends and must continue "to the end of one's life". Read the original if you want to see how current Party-building commentary links Party spirit, political loyalty and cadre conduct to Xi Jinping's recent directives.
quoteEn: Political cultivation is the core of Party-spirit cultivation and determines its direction and effectiveness.
quoteZh: 政治修养是党性修养的核心，决定着党性修养的方向和效果。

glossary.explanation: The ongoing self-training of Party members to strengthen their loyalty, discipline and ideological commitment to the Party. It is a long-standing theme in Chinese Communist Party building.
In this article, the process by which Party members and cadres train themselves to raise their political awareness and the quality of their political thinking.
A set of rules on cadre conduct adopted by the Politburo in December 2012, aimed at curbing formalism, bureaucracy and extravagance. Study campaigns on it were launched in 2025.

glossary.en: unique challenges of a large party
glossary.explanation: A phrase Xi Jinping used to describe problems he says are specific to a very large governing party, such as maintaining unity, governing capacity and a clean political environment.
The official term for China's path of modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022) as the route to national rejuvenation.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal of the Party, presented as restoring China's national strength and international standing by the middle of the twenty-first century.

t: The contemporary value of promoting the Bandung Spirit
zh: 弘扬万隆精神的时代价值
paras: Marking the 70th anniversary of the 1955 Bandung Conference, this newspaper commentary asks what the Bandung Spirit offers the world today. Luo Jianbo argues that, as the "Global South" rises collectively while unilateralism, protectionism and bullying grow, the spirit's core elements of independence, solidarity and cooperation, and seeking common ground while shelving differences have a new value. In Luo's account, China contributed decisively to the conference and will make new and greater contributions to the common interests of the Global South.

The piece opens with a reference to Xi Jinping's recent signed article in Malaysian newspapers, which called for promoting the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence and the Bandung Spirit. It is then organised in three sections, each pairing one element of the spirit with a present-day task: independence and international fairness, solidarity and Global South development, and seeking common ground and exchange among civilizations.

On independence, Luo recalls that the 29 Asian and African participants opposed colonialism and imperialism and adopted ten principles of international relations, and that China's delegation helped make anti-imperialism a core part of the spirit.
