Today, the author says, hegemonic and zero-sum thinking persist, so states should uphold equality, mutually beneficial cooperation and consultation, oppose "decoupling" and defend the World Trade Organization-centred trading system. On solidarity, Luo cites UN-agency figures that about 35.4 per cent of the world's population, and 64.8 per cent in Africa, cannot afford a healthy diet. The author describes the Global South as a collective identity and says South-South cooperation has shifted from national liberation to mutual benefit in pursuit of modernization. China's zero-tariff treatment for the least developed countries and the Belt and Road Initiative are presented as examples.

On seeking common ground, Luo credits Zhou Enlai's delegation with bridging divisions at Bandung and treats the approach as a Chinese contribution to international relations that rejects bloc division by ideology. The author links it to the common values of all mankind, a community with a shared future for mankind, and partnership without alliance. Luo concludes that greater Chinese influence in building international consensus and in civilizational exchange is an inherent requirement of that community. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese official scholarship presents Bandung as a basis for China's Global South diplomacy.
quoteEn: The "Global South" is not merely a geographical concept but in essence a collective identity, which carries shared historical memory and reflects shared practical needs, and therefore has a special sense of belonging, identification and mission.
quoteZh: “全球南方”不只是一个地理概念，在本质上是一种集体身份认同，不仅承载着共同的历史记忆，也反映了共同的现实需要，因此有着特殊的归属感、认同感和使命感。

glossary.explanation: The set of principles associated with the 1955 Asian-African Conference in Bandung, Indonesia, including anti-colonialism, solidarity and peaceful coexistence. Chinese official discourse often cites it as a foundation for South-South cooperation.
A term for developing countries, used in current Chinese diplomacy to stress shared development interests and identity.
Principles of mutual respect for sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference, equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful coexistence, promoted by China since the 1950s.

glossary.en: seeking common ground while shelving differences
glossary.explanation: A approach associated with Zhou Enlai at Bandung: cooperating on shared aims while setting aside disagreements.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2013 as the aim of China's foreign policy and vision of global governance.
A Chinese initiative launched in 2013 for infrastructure and economic cooperation across Asia, Africa, Europe and beyond.

t: Grasping the distinctive features of the Party's cultural leadership
zh: 深刻把握党的文化领导权的鲜明特质
paras: This short commentary takes up Xi Jinping's proposition, advanced at the symposium on cultural inheritance and development, of the "cultural leadership" of the Communist Party of China. Wang Yan argues that understanding its distinctive features is required for studying Xi Jinping's thought on culture and is a precondition for giving the building of a strong cultural nation a firm political guarantee. The article identifies five features: advancement, political character, contemporary relevance, popular character and systemic character.

Writing in the framework of the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Wang devotes one short section to each feature. The sections move from the Party's grasp of the laws of cultural development, through ideological work, responses to new conditions at home and abroad, and service to the people, to the Party's overall coordination of cultural work.

On advancement, Wang says the Party has summarised three sets of laws: those of socialist cultural construction, which proceed from the interaction of economic base and superstructure; those of traditional Chinese culture, guided by the Two Integrations; and those of human civilisation, involving exchange and mutual learning. On political character, Wang holds that cultural leadership is in essence leadership over ideological work, since a regime's collapse often begins in the realm of ideas. Wang points to the system of Marxism's guiding role, ideological responsibility systems and Party study mechanisms. On contemporary relevance, the article describes opposition to cultural hegemonism, historical nihilism and "universal values", and the Party's self-reform.

Wang adds that the people-centred character appears in meeting diverse spiritual needs and equalising basic public cultural services. Systemic character is said to cover leadership over propaganda and public opinion, cultural innovation, and the management of cultural organisations. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style statement of how Party theorists currently define the Party's cultural leadership.
quoteEn: The Party's cultural leadership is in essence leadership over ideological work.
quoteZh: 党的文化领导权实质上是意识形态工作领导权。

glossary.explanation: The term, related to Gramscian 'cultural hegemony', is used in Party discourse for the Party's leading role over cultural and ideological affairs. Xi Jinping put it forward at the 2023 symposium on cultural inheritance and development.
The principle of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
An official term for the Party's efforts to discipline itself and fight corruption, prominent since the 18th Party Congress.
A system assigning Party committees and leaders formal responsibility for ideological work in their areas, introduced in 2015.
An official goal of building China's cultural strength and soft power, set as a national objective for 2035.

t: The significance and practical requirements of establishing a mechanism for delivering high-quality cultural resources directly to the grassroots
zh: 科学把握建立优质文化资源直达基层机制的重大意义和实践要求
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao, 2025 no. 7), Zhou Qin takes up a reform measure set out in the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and repeated in the 2025 government work report: establishing a mechanism that delivers high-quality cultural resources directly to the grassroots. Zhou argues that the mechanism matters for meeting the people's cultural needs and for building a culture-strong nation. The article also sets out what must be done to put it into practice.

The piece has three parts. The first explains why the mechanism is significant. The second identifies its key tasks around three questions: whether the resources are good, whether they reach the grassroots, and whether the supply mechanism is flexible. The third proposes practical paths. Zhou draws throughout on Xi Jinping's statements and on Party documents from the 19th and 20th Party Congresses and the 14th Five-Year cultural development plan.

Zhou's core argument is that the main tension in cultural supply has moved from whether there is enough to whether it is good and refined. In Zhou's account, uneven allocation between town and country and between regions still leaves gaps in high-quality supply. Zhou proposes defining quality by the depth, breadth and influence of a cultural resource. The author links the mechanism to common prosperity in spiritual life and to strengthening grassroots cultural confidence as a foundation of the culture-strong nation.

On practice, Zhou calls for three things. The first is better content, through a people-centred orientation in creative work, talent incentives, grassroots amateur arts teams and the participation of non-public cultural enterprises. The second is moving resources downward, through urban support for rural culture, tilting resources towards old revolutionary areas, ethnic minority and border regions, and services for older people, minors, disabled people and migrant workers. The third is service innovation, through digital platforms offering order-based, menu-based and appointment-based services, and a main-branch library and cultural centre structure. Zhou presents these as parts of a systematic reform. Read the original if you want to see how a Party theoretical journal turns the Third Plenum's cultural-service reform into concrete policy tasks.
quoteEn: At present, the main contradiction in China's cultural supply is no longer whether there is a shortage or enough, but whether it is good and refined.
quoteZh: 当前，我国文化供给的主要矛盾已经不是缺不缺、够不够的问题，而是好不好、精不精的问题。

glossary.explanation: A Party goal of raising China's cultural capacity and influence, set out in Party congress documents and tied to national rejuvenation.
A Party goal of shared wealth for all, here extended to spiritual and cultural life.

glossary.pinyin: dǎng de èrshí jiè sān zhōngquánhuì
glossary.en: Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
glossary.explanation: The 2024 Party plenary session that adopted a decision on further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization.

t: Studying and implementing the spirit of the Central Economic Work Conference and putting the Party Central Committee's decisions into effect
zh: 深入学习贯彻中央经济工作会议精神 扎实推动党中央决策部署落地落实
authors: Party Leadership Group of the National Development and Reform Commission
paras: This article, a study-and-implementation piece by the Party leadership group of the National Development and Reform Commission, takes up Xi Jinping's speech at the Central Economic Work Conference of December 2024. The authors argue that the speech reviews 2024, assesses the current situation and sets out the work for 2025. They call on officials to unify thinking and action around it, put work first, and use high-quality development to advance the building of a strong country and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The text has four parts. It begins with an account of the progress made in 2024. It then weighs the challenges and opportunities facing the economy, followed by an explanation of the "regular patterns" of economic work that Xi's speech distils. It ends with a list of tasks for putting the Central Committee's decisions into effect in 2025. The first part cites figures on growth, industry, consumption, employment, innovation, trade, grain output, debt and incomes.

On the outlook, the authors apply a "two-sided" method. They set external pressures against favourable factors, and weak domestic demand against what they call a stable base, many advantages, strong resilience and great potential. They cite political guarantees such as the Two Establishes, institutional strengths, supply and demand potential, and stronger macro policy. In the third part they present Xi's guidance as five relationships to be balanced: an effective market and an enabling government, total supply and total demand, new and old growth drivers, increments and existing stock, and quality and total volume. They place the Party Central Committee's centralised and unified leadership as the fundamental guarantee of economic work.

The final part lists tasks for 2025. These are more proactive fiscal policy and moderately loose monetary policy, measures to boost consumption and investment, and faster development of new quality productive forces with a modern industrial system. They also include a unified national market, further opening up, containing risks in property, local debt and small financial institutions, coordinated urban–rural development and better livelihoods. The authors conclude that these steps will keep the economy recovering and lay the groundwork for the 15th Five-Year Plan period. Read the original if you want an official summary of the economic priorities, policy language and data the Party leadership used to frame 2025.
quoteEn: Expanding domestic demand bears on both economic stability and economic security; it is not an expedient measure but a strategic one.
quoteZh: 扩大内需既关系经济稳定，也关系经济安全，不是权宜之计，而是战略之举。

glossary.explanation: The official development goal since the late 2010s. It stresses efficiency, innovation and balance rather than growth speed alone.
A formula adopted in 2022. It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023. It refers to productivity driven by technological breakthroughs, emerging and future industries, and the upgrading of traditional ones.
An annual meeting of top Party and state leaders, held in December. It reviews the year's economy and sets the next year's policy direction.

t: Drawing the strength of cultural confidence from red culture
zh: 从红色文化中汲取文化自信的力量
paras: Zhao Yongfu asks how red culture, the culture created under Communist Party leadership, can serve as a source of cultural confidence. Opening with Xi Jinping's March 2025 remarks in Guizhou on using regional red and ethnic cultures to strengthen cultural confidence, the author argues that red culture both underpins that confidence and should be actively transmitted and renewed. The context is the drive for national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization.

The commentary has three parts. The first sets out why red culture gives cultural confidence its foundation. The second discusses how to draw strength from it through inheritance and dissemination, in Party training, school ideological education and public storytelling. The third turns to innovation: technology, red tourism and international communication. Examples come mainly from Guangxi, where the author works.

Zhao defines red culture as advanced culture created by the Party and the people in revolution, construction and reform. In this account it results from combining Marxism with China's circumstances and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The article says it carries forward traditional ideals such as benevolence, people-centredness and national integrity, and that the Party's "spiritual lineage" runs from the Jinggangshan and Long March spirit to the poverty-alleviation and lunar-exploration spirits. For transmission, Zhao points to Party history study rules, integrated ideological education from primary school to university, and storytelling, with the Xiang River battle and Guangxi's memorials as the example. For innovation, the author proposes AI presenters, VR and AR exhibitions, immersive live performances, themed red-tourism routes, and international storytelling with trained communicators and a discourse system foreigners can understand. The author also says new quality productive forces should empower the cultural industries.

Zhao concludes that protecting and using red resources, passing on the red gene and telling red stories are the way to firm cultural confidence, in line with Xi Jinping's directives. The author presents international dissemination as a way to help the world understand the Party and China and to raise national soft power. Read the original if you want to see how Party-history officials frame red culture, and what practical measures they propose, from cadre education to digital media and tourism.
quoteEn: International communication of red culture is not only an important way to pass on and promote the spirit of the Chinese nation, but also a bridge and link for mutual exchange and learning among civilizations worldwide.
quoteZh: 红色文化国际传播不仅是传承与弘扬中华民族精神的重要途径，也是促进全球文明交流互鉴的桥梁与纽带。

glossary.explanation: The revolutionary, socialist and reform-era culture created under Communist Party leadership, including its sites, stories and values. Official discourse treats it as a core part of China's advanced socialist culture.
A concept stressed by Xi Jinping since around 2014, adding confidence in China's culture to confidence in the path, theory and system of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The official name for China's development path, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
The official catalogue of named "spirits" (such as the Long March spirit and Yan'an spirit) formed in the Party's different historical periods, said to originate in the founding spirit of the Party.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productivity driven by technological innovation, used in policy to guide high-tech and industrial upgrading.

t: Lenin's approach to resolving problems within the Party and the Chinese Communist Party's self-reform
st: A textual study based on What Is to Be Done?
zh: 列宁解决党内问题的思路与中国共产党的自我革命
zhSub: 基于《怎么办？》的文本考察
source: Journal of the Party School of the Fujian Provincial Committee of the CPC (Fujian Academy of Governance), 2025 no. 1
paras: Guo and Yu ask what Lenin's What Is to Be Done? (1902) offers the Chinese Communist Party as it pursues the Party's self-reform. They argue that the book sets out a systematic method for dealing with internal problems that starts from members' ideas, and that the method still applies to the Party in the new era. The article opens with Xi Jinping's citation of Lenin on openly admitting mistakes.

The article has three parts. The first reconstructs Lenin's critical analysis of the Russian Social-Democratic Party's "confusion, disintegration and vacillation", including the roots and harms of "worship of spontaneity" and his rebuttal of the Economists' slogans. The second draws out Lenin's "scientific approach" in four elements: whom to win over, the form of struggle, the groundwork, and the channel. The third turns to five lessons for the Chinese Party.

On the authors' reading, Lenin traced the crisis to Economist ideology, which they describe as trade-unionist and bourgeois in class character. Lenin treated the Economists' "demagogues" as opponents, while winning over the young members they misled and training workers as professional revolutionaries. The struggle was to be theoretical rather than merely organisational, grounded in materialist analysis of major real-life problems, and carried out through an all-Russia political newspaper. The authors say the paper would give scattered local groups a common "plumb line" and real ties among them. They hold that today's world remains in the historical era Marx identified, so ideological erosion and temptation still threaten Party members. They link the "four dangers" and "seven haves" to weak theoretical grounding.

The authors draw five proposals. The Party should unify "curing the illness to save the patient" with high-pressure anti-corruption work. It should make criticism and self-criticism routine through discipline and leadership example. It should select a small number of readable, theoretically rigorous interpretive works as required reading, using central leadership, anonymous expert review and anonymous sampling of cadres' views. Finally, it should build a dedicated online platform for theoretical study and discussion among Party members, in the manner of Lenin's all-Russia newspaper. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Party-building study uses Lenin's text to justify ideological work and concrete study and discussion measures in the Party's self-reform.
quoteEn: To resolve problems within the Party thoroughly, the Party must focus its strength on resolving its members' ideological problems.
quoteZh: 要彻底解决党内问题，就必须要将党的力量聚焦到解决党员的思想问题上来

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed by Xi Jinping since the 19th Party Congress (2017): the Party's continuing effort to correct its own shortcomings and misconduct, including through anti-corruption work.
Lenin's term for the Economists' view that the workers' spontaneous movement is sufficient. He held that it leaves workers under bourgeois ideology.
A current in Russian Social-Democracy around 1900 that stressed economic struggle for workers' immediate demands over political struggle. Lenin attacked it in What Is to Be Done?

glossary.en: curing the illness to save the patient
glossary.literal: treat the disease, save the person
glossary.explanation: A long-standing Party principle for handling erring members: criticise and educate them rather than simply punish them.
The Party's formulation of four major dangers it faces: lack of drive, incompetence, detachment from the people, and passivity and corruption.

t: Understanding the true meaning of "upholding a worldwide vision"
st: What it means, why it is held, and how it is put into practice
zh: 深刻理解和把握“坚持胸怀天下”的思想真谛
paras: Xu Yanling takes up the principle of "upholding a worldwide vision" (jianchi xiongHuai tianxia), which the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021) listed among the Party's historical experiences. The 20th Party Congress (2022) report presented it as part of the stance, viewpoint and method of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Xu argues that it should be grasped on three levels: what it means, why the Party holds it, and how it is carried out.

The article follows this three-part structure. The first part sets out four components of the principle's meaning. The second traces its sources in Marxism, in traditional Chinese culture, in the Party's history from Mao Zedong to Xi Jinping, and in present-day global conditions. The third describes the practical path, summed up in four phrases: clarifying the great principle, creating great harmony, acting with great righteousness and taking the great way.

In Xu's account, the principle means broadening the world outlook and developing global thinking, and it means pursuing shared destiny and common development. It also means responding to widespread concerns through global governance and deepening exchange and mutual learning among civilizations. Xu argues that it rests on the Marxist aim of human emancipation and on the Chinese idea of "all under heaven as one family". It is also confirmed by the Party's record of supporting other peoples' struggles, opposing hegemonism and pursuing peaceful development. For the present, Xu says the principle is a correct choice for a turbulent world marked by Cold War thinking, because China's certainty can offset the world's uncertainty.

Xu holds that the practical path begins with shared human values: peace, development, fairness, justice, democracy and freedom. It continues with a community with a shared future for mankind, built at bilateral, regional and global levels. It also includes the Global Development, Global Security and Global Civilization Initiatives, the high-quality Belt and Road Initiative and a stronger voice for the Global South. Xu concludes that this is how the Party contributes Chinese wisdom, solutions and strength to human peace and development. Read the original if you want a compact, officially aligned account of how Chinese Party theorists link the Party's global outlook to Marxism, Chinese tradition and current foreign-policy initiatives.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China has always placed China's development within the coordinates of human development, closely linking its own destiny with that of the peoples of all countries.
quoteZh: 中国共产党始终把中国发展置于人类发展的坐标系中，把自身命运与世界各国人民命运紧密相连

glossary.literal: adhere to having the whole world in one's breast
glossary.explanation: One of the Party's "historical experiences" listed in the 2021 resolution on its history. It expresses the claim that the Party acts with concern for humanity as a whole and not only for China.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept of international relations, promoted since about 2013. It calls for common security, development and governance among states.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.
A term for developing countries, which Chinese official discourse presents as a group whose representation in global affairs should be increased.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sixiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Promoting the great spirit of the Chinese nation and building a shared spiritual home for the Chinese nation
zh: 弘扬中华民族伟大精神 构筑中华民族共有精神家园
paras: This short commentary, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in April 2025, takes up Xi Jinping's call to build a shared spiritual home for the Chinese nation as cultural support for building the Chinese nation as a community. The authors argue that grasping the internal link between the great spirit of the Chinese nation and this shared spiritual home is the core route to forging a strong sense of community of the Chinese nation.
The piece has two parts. The first sets out how the great spirit underpins the shared spiritual home. The second takes four components of that spirit in turn: creativity, struggle, unity and dream.

In the first part, Qiu and Fu present the great spirit as the core of the shared home and identify four links between them: shared spiritual content, the transmission of history and culture, the strengthening of national identity, and resonance of values. They name patriotism, collectivism and the core socialist values as the value basis that unites the ethnic groups within a pattern of "diversity in unity". In the second part they assign each component a role. Creativity energises innovation and cultural confidence. Struggle mobilises all ethnic groups for the Chinese Dream. Unity strengthens cohesion and is called the lifeline of the Chinese people. The dream spirit integrates personal and national aspirations and is described as the soul of the shared home.

The authors conclude that promoting these four aspects in the new era will strengthen identification with the Chinese nation and culture, and will keep the shared spiritual home vital. They also link this to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official ethnic-unity discourse ties the great spirit of the Chinese nation to nation-community building.
quoteEn: The great spirit of unity is the core force in building the shared spiritual home of the Chinese nation.
quoteZh: 伟大团结精神是构筑中华民族共有精神家园的核心力量

glossary.zh: 中华民族共有精神家园
glossary.en: shared spiritual home for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: the common spiritual homeland of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A concept in official ethnic-policy discourse, stressing a common cultural and spiritual base for all ethnic groups in China. It is presented as supporting the building of the Chinese nation as a community.

glossary.en: sense of community of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: consciousness of the Chinese nation community
glossary.explanation: A key term in Xi Jinping-era ethnic policy, referring to a shared sense of belonging to one Chinese nation. Officials call for it to be "forged firmly" (铸牢) among all ethnic groups.

glossary.en: great spirit of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A formulation in official discourse for the Chinese nation's enduring spiritual qualities. Xi Jinping has summarised them as the spirits of creativity, struggle, unity and dream.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central national goal in Party discourse since the 18th Party Congress (2012), often tied to the Chinese Dream.
A slogan introduced by Xi Jinping in 2012 that joins national rejuvenation with the well-being of the people.

keywords: great spirit of the Chinese nation

t: Grasping scientifically the stance and direction of the great struggle
zh: 科学把握伟大斗争的立场和方向
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily in April 2025, takes up a passage in which Xi Jinping says that risks and challenges threatening the Party's leadership, the socialist system, national sovereignty and security, core interests, the people's fundamental interests or the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation must be met with resolute struggle and victory. Chen Long argues that this passage settles the question of stance and direction in the "great struggle", and also sets basic requirements and methods for it.

The piece is short and has three sections. The first concerns the need for a clear understanding of the "fundamental questions" of struggle. The second deals with holding firmly to the people's stance. The third deals with upholding Party leadership and the socialist direction. Chen draws on Xi Jinping, Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping, and on the Party's history from the revolutionary period to reform.

Chen's first move is that leaders need clear heads about what banner to raise and what road to take, since in Xi's words a large country cannot make "subversive errors" on fundamental questions. Chen says this clarity comes from understanding the "new historical characteristics" of the struggle, namely a world of great change and the demands of national rejuvenation at home, and from a firm grasp of Marxism and the Party's innovative theory. Second, Chen presents the people's stance as the Party's fundamental political stance, rooted in Marxism's aim of human liberation and in the Party's purpose of serving the people wholeheartedly; the people are described as the Party's greatest support against risks. Third, Chen holds that reform and innovation must have a direction, neither rigid and closed nor a change of banner. The direction is the self-improvement of the socialist system, which Chen says depends on the Party's comprehensive leadership and, at its core, on upholding the authority of the Central Committee and its centralised, unified leadership.

Chen concludes that Chinese modernization requires standing firm on the people's stance, adhering to the socialist direction and maintaining Party leadership without wavering. Chen calls on Party members to grasp the decisive significance of the Two Establishes, strengthen the Four Consciousnesses, hold to the Four-sphere Confidence and carry out the Two Upholds. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars present the ideological basis of "struggle" in the Xi Jinping era, for study of official discourse.
quoteEn: Only with theoretical clarity can one be politically firm, and only then does one have confidence and strength in struggle.
quoteZh: 只有理论上清醒,政治上才能坚定,斗争起来才有底气、才有力量。

glossary.explanation: A phrase used in Party discourse under Xi Jinping for the Party's struggle against major risks and challenges on the path to national rejuvenation.
A formula adopted in 2022 affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and of the whole Party, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The requirement to uphold the core status of Xi Jinping and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Party Central Committee.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The official name for China's path to modernization under Party leadership, prominent in Party discourse since 2021–22.
An official requirement that Party members maintain political awareness, a sense of the big picture, of the core, and of alignment with the Party centre.

t: The anti-corruption struggle in the new era has won the Party the historical initiative
zh: 新时代反腐败斗争为党赢得历史主动
source: China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News, 24 April 2025, p. 5
paras: This commentary, first published in the China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News on 24 April 2025, interprets a judgement Xi Jinping made at the Fourth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection. Xi held that the new era's anti-corruption struggle has won the Party two forms of "historical initiative". The first is keeping the Party from degenerating in nature, colour or flavour. The second is uniting and leading the people in building a strong country and achieving national rejuvenation. Tian Peiyan argues that grasping this judgement strengthens confidence and clarity for pressing the struggle further, so that the Party's great self-reform can lead the great social revolution.

The article has three parts. The first sets the anti-corruption record in a lineage running from Marx, Engels and Lenin through the Party's early history. That history includes the 1926 notice on purging corrupt elements, the harsh Soviet-period and Shaan-Gan-Ning regulations, and the post-1949 campaigns, among them the execution of Liu Qingshan and Zhang Zishan. The second part sets out what the struggle has achieved since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third turns to how the struggle should continue.

In Tian's account, the new-era campaign carried forward the Party's tradition of resisting corruption and has raised its capacity to do so. The author credits Xi Jinping's thinking on Party building and on the Party's self-reform, and a mechanism that advances "not daring, not being able and not wanting to be corrupt" together. It has also created a deterrent momentum in which, the author says, there are no untouchable people or forbidden zones. The second initiative is shown through stronger Party leadership and political supervision, with 12,000 people disciplined for political violations in 2024. Tian also cites cleaner finance, state enterprises and livelihood sectors, a better business environment, and stronger public cohesion.

Tian warns that the situation remains "severe and complex", pointing to unremoved stock and new increments of corruption, collusion between officials and business, hidden new-type corruption, and incomplete supervision. The author rejects both complacent optimism and the view that anti-corruption harms growth. The article calls for strategic resolve, deeper work on the three "nots" through punishment, institutional reform and education, and combined effort by Party committees, discipline bodies, departments and the public, with Party-building work linked to the struggle. Read the original if you want an example of how official Party-discipline media present anti-corruption as a source of political legitimacy and a framework for next steps.
quoteEn: The anti-corruption struggle is both a \"barrier remover\" and a \"booster\" of economic and social development, and a guardian and promoter of social fairness and justice.
quoteZh: 反腐败斗争既是经济社会发展的“除障机”“助推器”，又是社会公平正义的守护者、促进者。

glossary.literal: historical initiative / taking the initiative in history
glossary.explanation: A phrase prominent in recent Party discourse for the Party acting on its understanding of historical trends so as to shape events rather than react to them.

Xi Jinping's term for the Party's capacity to purify and correct itself, presented as the means of avoiding the decay seen in other long-ruling parties. The official English rendering is "self-reform".

glossary.pinyin: bù gǎn fǔ, bù néng fǔ, bù xiǎng fǔ
glossary.en: not daring, not being able and not wanting to be corrupt
glossary.literal: dare not be corrupt, cannot be corrupt, do not want to be corrupt
glossary.explanation: The Party's formula for an integrated approach to corruption: deterrence through punishment, institutional constraints on power, and ideological and moral education.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Strengthening conduct building to energise a sound Party organisational system
zh: 加强作风建设为健全组织体系注入动力
paras: This short commentary, published in Study Times on 23 April 2025, asks how the Party's organisational system can be improved in quality and function as well as in coverage. Ming and Peng argue that work-style (conduct) building is the "soul-like bond" running through that system and an important guarantee of the vitality of Party organisations at every level.

The piece has two parts. The first sets out three effects of good conduct: greater cohesion and fighting strength, stronger leadership and execution, and greater appeal and influence in emerging fields. The second proposes three ways of building conduct into organisational development. Throughout, the authors illustrate their points with the work of the Henan Jiao Yulu Cadre College, where they appear to work, as the campaign to study and implement the central Eight-point Regulation is under way.

The authors argue that top-down, tier-by-tier conduct practice gives the system vertical reach, and that conduct building helps remove "paper implementation" so that central decisions are carried out in full. They note that 84 million workers in new forms of employment, 21% of the workforce, make Party building in emerging fields necessary, and they present flexible Party organisation and online branches as examples. Their practical proposals are three-tier theoretical study with dual assessment of study results and conduct; stricter requirements for the "key minority" of leaders, including a "top leader" project, negative lists and dynamic conduct files; and grassroots institutional measures such as star ratings for branches.

The authors conclude that conduct building and a sound organisational system reinforce each other, and that the current campaign should use conduct as a breakthrough point to optimise structure and upgrade function. They present the college's courses, case teaching and its teaching site in Lankao County as practical models. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party-school practice is linked to the official discourse on conduct building and organisational development.
quoteEn: Conduct building and the improvement of the organisational system are closely linked and mutually reinforcing.
quoteZh: 作风建设与健全组织体系紧密相连、相互促进。

glossary.explanation: A set of rules on officials' conduct adopted by the Politburo in December 2012. They curb formalism, bureaucracy, extravagance and hedonism among Party members and cadres.
The Party's campaign to improve the working style and behaviour of its members and cadres. It targets the "four undesirable work styles" of formalism, bureaucracy, hedonism and extravagance.
A term for senior leading cadres, whose conduct and example are held to shape that of the whole Party.

t: Upholding the mass line: key historical lessons from rule-of-law building in the Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region
zh: 坚持群众路线：陕甘宁边区法治建设的重要历史经验
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily (23 April 2025), Xu Shi argues that the mass line, described as the Party's lifeline and fundamental working line, has consistently guided the Party's leadership of legal construction. The commentary takes the Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region of the Yan'an period as its case. Xu contends that its legal system always put the people's needs and interests at the centre, and that this earned popular support and laid foundations for victory in the War of Resistance and the Liberation War and for legal construction in the People's Republic.

The piece is a short historical commentary that follows the legal process from legislation through adjudication and mediation to legal education and cadre discipline. Xu notes that in 13 years the Border Region government issued more than 1,000 laws, regulations and normative or programmatic documents. Evidence includes the Border Region's governing programmes, its regulations on human rights and property rights and on elections, and the judicial practice of Ma Xiwu and Xi Zhongxun's instructions to judicial personnel.

Xu's core argument is that the mass line was built into each stage. In legislation, Party policy set the direction, the Three-Thirds system and general elections broadened participation, and laws were issued only after investigation, consultation and majority agreement in the Border Council. In the courts, on-the-spot and circuit trials, oral complaints, waived fees and the 'Ma Xiwu method' of trial, illustrated by the 1943 Feng Pen'er marriage case, are presented as making justice accessible. Xu adds people's mediation committees, which drew on local custom, and legal education delivered through literacy classes, newspapers, drama and songs.

Xu stresses that the mass line also requires leading cadres to set an example and requires full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Examples cited include the 1937 death sentence on Huang Kegong, anti-corruption regulations, the rule that Communists who break the law are punished more severely, cadre training, and a right of citizens to accuse officials. Xu also cites the execution of the trade official Xiao Yubi after villagers reported him, and Lin Boqu's personal replies to more than a hundred complaint letters. Read the original if you want a brief, officially aligned account of how Yan'an-era legal practice is presented today as a model of the mass line in law.
quoteEn: Upholding the mass line is also the Party's consistent practice and an important lesson in leading the building of the rule of law.
quoteZh: 坚持群众路线，也是我们党领导法治建设的一贯做法和重要经验。

glossary.explanation: A Party working method, associated with Mao Zedong, of gathering views from the people, distilling them into policy and returning them to the masses. It is officially described as the Party's lifeline.
The Communist-led base area in northwest China, centred on Yan'an, that existed from 1937 to 1949. It served as the Party's wartime political and administrative centre.
A principle in the Border Region's wartime governance under which Communists, non-Party progressives and middle-of-the-road figures each held roughly one third of government seats.
A style of judging associated with the Border Region judge Ma Xiwu. It involved going to the locality, investigating on site, relying on local people and avoiding rigid formality.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A policy slogan of the Xi Jinping era stressing strict discipline and anti-corruption within the Party. The article applies it retrospectively to Yan'an-era practice.

t: A historical examination of the Party's organisational strength building during the War of Resistance against Japan
zh: 抗战时期党的组织力建设的历史考察
paras: Xiong Qiuliang asks how the Communist Party of China built up its organisational strength (zuzhili) during the War of Resistance against Japan, and what that experience offers today. Defining organisational strength as the Party's capacity to mobilise, organise and unite cadres and the masses to carry out its line, Xiong argues that the Party grew from small and weak to large and strong in this period and served as the mainstay of national resistance. This is a short commentary in Guangming Daily, supported by a major National Social Science Fund project on Party membership building.

The article is organised around four components of organisational strength, each linked to a wartime practice: a lofty organisational goal (leading capacity), a tight organisational system (cohesion), a well-built Party membership (combat effectiveness) and close ties with the people (power to call on the masses). Xiong draws on speeches and documents by Mao Zedong, Liu Shaoqi, Chen Yun and Peng Zhen, on Party resolutions, and on examples from the Yan'an centre and the base areas.

On leadership, Xiong stresses theoretical study and ideological education at Yan'an, together with Mao's On Protracted War and his theory of New Democracy, which are said to have given the Party and the people a clear sense of the revolution's course. On cohesion, Xiong cites the 1942 decision unifying leadership in the base areas under Party committees, democratic centralism, and the 'four subordinations' adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the Sixth Central Committee (1938), enforced through Party regulations and expulsions. On membership, Xiong describes the rapid expansion from 1938, reaching 800,000 members by 1940, and then the 1939 decision on consolidating the Party after 'sudden expansion' and campaign-style recruitment let in unqualified people. On mass work, Xiong argues that Party branches won support by meeting practical needs: rent and interest reduction, the production campaign, the 'three-thirds' system, elections and winter schools.

Xiong concludes that wartime experience shows organisational strength rests on firm ideals, strict structure and discipline, quality membership, and a livelihood-based bond with the people, and that it offers lessons for advancing the Party's 'great new project' of Party building in the new era. Read the original if you want a concise, officially framed account of how Party historians present wartime Party building, with references to the primary sources it cites.
quoteEn: The Party's organisational strength refers to its leading capacity, cohesion, combat effectiveness and power of appeal in mobilising, organising and uniting Party cadres and the people to carry out the Party's line, principles and policies in pursuit of its goals.
quoteZh: 党的组织力指的是党为了实现自己的目标，动员、组织和团结党员干部、人民群众以贯彻执行党的路线方针政策的引领力、凝聚力、战斗力和号召力等。

glossary.explanation: A term in Party-building discourse for the Party's ability to lead, unite, fight and mobilise through its organisations. The article breaks it into leading capacity, cohesion, combat effectiveness and mobilising appeal.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Party, combining internal discussion with binding obedience to higher bodies and the centre.
Principle set out by Mao Zedong in 1938: the individual to the organisation, the minority to the majority, the lower level to the higher level, and the whole Party to the Central Committee.
A wartime power-sharing arrangement in the anti-Japanese base areas, under which Communists, left-progressives and middle-of-the-road figures each took roughly one third of government seats.
Mao Zedong's theory, developed around 1939–40, of a transitional stage of Chinese revolution led by the proletariat before the move to socialism.
A campaign launched in the base areas in the early 1940s in which troops, officials and peasants raised output to ease economic hardship.

t: Grasping the inherent unity of Party discipline and getting things done
zh: 把握党的纪律和干事创业的内在统一性
paras: This newspaper commentary (Guangming Daily, 23 April 2025) takes up Xi Jinping's statement at a Politburo democratic life meeting in December 2024 that Party discipline both educates and constrains, and also protects and motivates, so that discipline and getting things done are inherently unified. Wu and Tang argue that the remark summarises experience from full and rigorous self-governance of the Party in the new era and gives guidance for strengthening discipline while encouraging officials to take initiative.

The authors first trace the Party's emphasis on discipline from the first programme of 1921 through Mao Zedong, the early People's Republic and Deng Xiaoping to the period after the 18th Party Congress (2012). They then set out the relationship between discipline and enterprise, and close with two practical directions for the new journey.

Wu and Tang contend that discipline works in two ways. It marks bottom lines and boundaries, acting as a safety barrier that keeps officials honest and on the right track. It also gives them freedom and space to act, since clear rules and a clean political ecology protect officials who want to and can get things done. Because the Party has long been in power, they say, officials without experience of severe trials may drift into comfort-seeking or confusion.

They therefore propose centring discipline education on the Party's central tasks, with struggle and responsibility education to lift officials' sense of mission. They also call for accurate use of the "four forms" of supervision and discipline enforcement and strict application of the "three distinctions", to address officials who act recklessly, fail to act, dare not act or act poorly. Read the original if you want a brief, official-line statement of how current Party discipline work is linked to calls for officials' initiative.
quoteEn: Party discipline and getting things done have never been a matter of one at the expense of the other; they are a unity that promotes and complements each other.
quoteZh: 党的纪律与干事创业从来不是顾此失彼的，而是相互促进、相辅相成的统一体。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A leading Party-building slogan since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering discipline, anti-corruption and internal supervision.

glossary.literal: four forms of supervision and discipline enforcement
glossary.explanation: A Party framework graduating responses to violations, from criticism and warnings as the norm through to serious punishment and criminal referral.
A guideline asking discipline bodies to distinguish honest mistakes in reform and exploration from deliberate violations, among other distinctions, in order to protect officials who take risks.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Understanding the centenary course, achievements and basic experience of Chinese trade unions under Party leadership
zh: 深刻领悟党领导的中国工会百年历程、成就和基本经验
paras: Marking the centenary of the All-China Federation of Trade Unions (ACFTU), founded at the Second National Labour Congress in Guangzhou on 1 May 1925, this commentary reviews what a century of Party-led trade unionism has meant. Liu Xiangbing, writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in April 2025, argues that Chinese unions have always rallied around the Communist Party and mobilised workers around its programme and the central tasks of each period. The author presents the history as a resource for carrying forward the workers' movement in a new era.

The article has three parts: the course of the unions' history, their achievements, and the experience drawn from them. The historical section follows the unions through the New Democratic Revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It opens with the Party's First Congress resolution of 1921 and the Secretariat of the Chinese Labour Union.

In Liu's account, the achievements include contributing to the founding of New China, consolidating the Party's governing base and state power, acting as the main force in economic development and modernization, supporting harmonious and stable labour relations, and promoting the spirit of model workers, labour and craftsmanship. The core argument lies in five lessons. Liu holds that Party leadership is the fundamental guarantee of union work, and that unions must serve the Party's central tasks, which in the new era means striving for the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation. Unions must act as a bridge and link between Party and workers and as an important social pillar of state power. They must also protect workers' legitimate rights and serve them wholeheartedly. Finally, they must keep reforming and innovating. Throughout, the author relies heavily on statements by Xi Jinping.

Liu concludes that these experiences are of lasting importance for union work and for developing a trade union path with Chinese characteristics. The author stresses that unions should safeguard workers' rights while also representing the overall interests of the people, and that their greatest danger is losing contact with workers. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official Party narrative on the role and history of the Chinese trade union movement.
quoteEn: The unions' greatest strength is close ties with workers, and their greatest danger is becoming detached from them.
quoteZh: 工会最大的优势是密切联系职工群众，最大的危险是脱离职工群众。

glossary.literal: great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream.
Slogan popularised by Xi Jinping from 2012, linking individual aspirations with national rejuvenation.
The policy course launched in 1978 that introduced market-oriented reforms and opened China to foreign trade and investment.
Mao Zedong's term for the Party-led revolution against imperialism, feudalism and bureaucratic capitalism, before the founding of the People's Republic in 1949.
Official description of mass organisations such as trade unions as connecting the Party with workers and other groups.

glossary.zh: 劳模精神、劳动精神、工匠精神
glossary.pinyin: láomó jīngshén, láodòng jīngshén, gōngjiàng jīngshén
glossary.en: the spirit of model workers, labour and craftsmanship
glossary.explanation: A trio of official values promoted by the Party and unions, honouring exemplary workers, dedication to labour and skilled craft.

t: Linking up the correction of work styles, the enforcement of discipline and the fight against corruption
zh: 把正风肃纪反腐贯通起来
source: New Xiang Review (Hunan Provincial Party Committee), 2025 no. 7; reprinted in Qiushi, 2025/08
paras: This short commentary, published in 2025, takes up the Party's current campaign on conduct and discipline. Xin argues that correcting work styles (zhengfeng), enforcing discipline (suji) and fighting corruption must be treated as one connected task rather than three separate ones. The piece follows the launch of a Party-wide study and education drive on the spirit of the Central Committee's eight-point regulations and Xi Jinping's call, made during inspections in Guizhou and Yunnan, to link the three together.

The commentary is built in four steps. It first sets out why work style matters to popular support, then explains the internal link between improper work styles and corruption. It next reviews the record since the 18th Party Congress (2012), and finally turns to the Party's present responsibilities and what Party organisations at all levels should do.

Xin's central claim is that improper work styles and corruption share the same root and feed each other. In this reading the "four undesirable work styles" run counter to the Party's nature and purpose, while corruption erodes its governing foundation. Handling them together, by investigating corruption through work-style problems and correcting work style through corruption cases, is said to cut the chains of interest that bind the two. Xin acknowledges that in some places the problems have rebounded and that blind spots remain, so the effort must be sustained.

Xin concludes that a Marxist governing party of more than 99 million members and over 5 million primary-level organisations needs systems thinking to advance Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The proposals include mechanisms for jointly investigating and handling work-style and corruption cases, attention to Party spirit, work style and discipline together, and a focused, practical study and education drive. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party media currently frame the link between work style, discipline and anti-corruption.
quoteEn: Improper work styles are a hotbed for breeding corruption.
quoteZh: 不正之风是滋生腐败的温床。

glossary.explanation: A set of rules on official conduct adopted by the Central Committee's Political Bureau in December 2012. They aim to curb formalism, bureaucracy, extravagance and waste among officials.
A Party term for formalism, bureaucracy, hedonism and extravagance. It has been the main target of work-style campaigns since 2012.
The official name for the Party's path of modernization, presented as distinct from Western models. It is linked to the goal of national rejuvenation.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal of the Party, associated with the Chinese Dream, of restoring China's national strength and international standing.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: The people's congress system as an important institutional vehicle for realising whole-process people's democracy in China
zh: 人民代表大会制度是实现我国全过程人民民主的重要制度载体
paras: Taking its cue from Xi Jinping's speech marking the 70th anniversary of the National People's Congress (NPC), this article from Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao, 2025 no. 6) argues that the people's congress system is an important institutional vehicle for realising whole-process people's democracy. Wang Haifeng holds that the system must be upheld under Communist Party leadership and that an institutional framework must secure the people's position as masters of the country.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out the theoretical and practical significance of whole-process people's democracy. The second explains why the fundamental political system carries it. The third lists measures to uphold, improve and operate the people's congress system so that it performs this role.

Wang presents whole-process people's democracy as an original concept of Xi Jinping that enriches the Marxist theory of the state, and as an essential requirement of Chinese modernization. In the article's account, it links democratic election, consultation, decision-making, management and oversight into one chain, and unites process and outcome, procedural and substantive democracy, direct and indirect democracy, and the people's democracy and the will of the state. The people's congress system carries this, Wang argues, in three ways. Its design embodies the constitutional principle that all power belongs to the people, and the executive, supervisory, judicial and procuratorial organs are created by, answerable to and supervised by the congresses. Its election, consultation, decision-making and oversight mechanisms operate the chain. The system also turns Party proposals into state will through legal procedure. Wang cites the 2021 revision of the NPC Organic Law and the 2022 revision of the Local Organic Law, which wrote whole-process democracy into law.

Wang calls for upholding the organic unity of Party leadership, the people's position as masters of the country and law-based governance. Further proposals include improving the socialist legal system with Chinese characteristics centred on the Constitution, and strengthening congress oversight of the executive, supervisory, judicial and procuratorial organs. Wang also urges supporting deputies in performing their duties under Party leadership, with grassroots legislative liaison points and better contact with constituents, and building up the congresses and their standing committees themselves. Read the original if you want a compact statement of the official Party-school account of how the people's congress system is tied to whole-process people's democracy, including the specific institutional measures it recommends.
quoteEn: The people's congress system is the fundamental avenue and highest form through which the people exercise mastery of the country; all major state matters are decided by the people's congresses and their standing committees, which also supervise implementation by other state organs.
quoteZh: 人民代表大会制度是人民当家作主的根本途径和最高实现形式，国家一切重大事项都由人民代表大会及其常委会作出决定，并监督其他国家机关实施。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2019 and the Party now uses to describe China's socialist democracy. It stresses that democratic practice spans elections, consultation, decision-making, management and oversight, not only voting.

China's fundamental political system under the Constitution. Congresses at each level are elected and in turn create the executive, supervisory, judicial and procuratorial organs, with the National People's Congress at the top.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: Achieving positive interaction between high-quality development and high-standard security
zh: 实现高质量发展和高水平安全良性互动
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in April 2025, Tang Junfeng takes up the Party's call, repeated at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), to coordinate development and security. Tang argues that high-quality development and high-level security support each other and form a dialectical unity. National security is presented as the foundation on which Chinese modernization can proceed steadily.

The short commentary has three parts. The first explains why national security underpins Chinese modernization, citing China's historical experience of foreign bullying and war and a present international environment the author describes as marked by unilateralism, protectionism and uncertainty. The second sets out how high-quality development and high-level security relate to each other. The third turns to practical measures for the new journey.

In the central section, Tang describes development as the Party's first priority, to be pursued through the new development philosophy, with innovation, coordination, green, open and shared development each answering a particular problem. Security, in turn, is both a condition for development and a yardstick of its results. The author holds that higher-quality development changes what security requires. Protection must move from single fields to systemic, multi-dimensional coverage: economic security stresses industrial resilience and autonomy, data and network security face contests between attack and defence, and military security faces intelligent technologies. Security boundaries must therefore be adjusted dynamically to find the best balance between efficiency and stability, openness and self-reliance, and innovation and risk. Neither side should be stressed at the other's expense.

Tang proposes three lines of action: resolutely applying the holistic approach to national security, including absolute Party leadership and the "ten adherences"; modernizing the national security system and capacity, with the aim of a higher-level "Peaceful China" and a new security architecture to safeguard the new development pattern; and treating security as a shared responsibility of the whole of society. The last includes breaking down departmental and local barriers, clarifying chains of responsibility, and expanding national security education. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party-state commentary links the development–security agenda to Chinese modernization and the holistic approach to national security.
quoteEn: High-quality development requires dynamic adjustment of security boundaries in order to find the optimal solution between efficiency and stability, openness and autonomy, and innovation and risk.
quoteZh: 高质量发展需要通过安全边界的动态调整，在效率与稳定、开放与自主、创新与风险之间寻求最优解。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, elaborated by Xi Jinping since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

A security doctrine put forward by Xi Jinping in 2014. It treats security as spanning politics, economy, military, culture, society, technology and other fields, with the people's security as its aim.
The official framework of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, adopted in 2015.
The official goal of shifting from fast growth to growth that is more efficient, innovative and sustainable, a central theme of Party economic policy since 2017.
An official concept, promoted since 2020, centred on the domestic economic cycle with domestic and international cycles reinforcing each other.
An official initiative aimed at public safety and social stability, referred to in Party documents as a goal for national security and social governance.

t: Mastering the lifelong task of the Communist: Xi Jinping on Party spirit cultivation
st: Xi Jinping's emphasis on "Party spirit cultivation"
zh: 修好共产党人的终身课题
zhSub: 习近平总书记强调的“党性修养”
paras: This commentary, published in Study Times in April 2025, sets out what General Secretary Xi Jinping has said about Party spirit cultivation (dangxing xiuyang) since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Ma defines the practice as Party members' self-education, self-reform and self-improvement, and presents Xi's statements as the fundamental guide for training the "study of the heart" of Communists in the new era.

The piece proceeds chronologically through six Xi texts or speeches: on the Party Constitution (2012), the national organisation work conference (2013), the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection plenary (2016), an inspection in Tibet (2021), the closing session of the 20th Party Congress (2022), and the Politburo democratic life meeting (December 2024).

Ma's reading is that Xi treats Party spirit as something never finished: it is not innate, does not grow automatically with seniority or rank, and requires lifelong effort, like a room that must be cleaned regularly. The Party Constitution is the basic standard, and leading cadres must set the example. Xi also draws on fine traditional Chinese culture and the Two Integrations, and on the founding spirit of the Party. Ma reports that the later texts put political cultivation first, tie it to the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, and require that Party spirit keep pace with theoretical innovation.

Ma concludes that Party members should study and observe the Party Constitution, draw on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and keep loyalty to the Party Central Committee as their basic political responsibility. Read the original if you want a compact, dated chronology of Xi's main statements on Party member self-cultivation as the official press presents them.
quoteEn: Party spirit cultivation is not innate, is not achieved at one stroke and is not settled once and for all; strengthening it is a lifelong task that Party member cadres must handle well to establish themselves.
quoteZh: 党性修养不是与生俱来的，既不是一蹴而就的，也不是一劳永逸的，加强党性修养是党员干部安身立命必须解决好的终身课题。

glossary.explanation: The process by which Party members train themselves to internalise the Party's essential character and principles. The term is also rendered as Party spirit training or tempering.
Xi Jinping's formula for combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture.
A formula adopted in 2021–22 that affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and the whole Party, and the guiding role of his thought.
The requirement that Party members uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.
An official formulation, set out in 2021, of the ideals and character attributed to the Party's founders, used as a resource for Party education.

t: Problems of work style are essentially problems of Party spirit
zh: 作风问题本质上是党性问题
source: China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News, 22 April 2025, p. 8
paras: This commentary, published in the Party's discipline-inspection newspaper in April 2025, takes up Xi Jinping's formula that problems of work style are essentially problems of Party spirit. Hong and Zhang argue that Party spirit is the inner foundation of work style and work style its outward expression: a pure Party spirit yields correct conduct, an impure one does not.

The piece is organised in four short sections. It treats cadres' conduct as a barometer of public judgement of the Party, political life within the Party as a purifier, firm ideals and convictions as the root of good work style, and the cultivation of Party spirit as a lifelong task. It draws on Yan'an-era and revolutionary examples and on conduct since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

The authors contend that cadres' attitudes and conduct directly shape popular trust, and that neglecting work style erects an invisible wall between Party and people. They describe serious, rigorous inner-Party political life as a means of filtering out harmful elements and as the soil in which good style grows. Conviction, in their account, is the root: they cite Jinggangshan frugality, the Huaihai campaign, Huang Wenxiu and Zhang Fuqing as cases where ideals became practical conduct, with loyalty to the Party as the key test.

Hong and Zhang call on Party members to place political training first, draw on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, treat Party rules as a constant mirror, and strengthen inner-Party supervision. Work style building, they say, is never finished. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party-building commentary links discipline, ideology and public trust.
quoteEn: Conviction is the root and work style is the form; when the root is sound the form holds together, and when the root is not sound the form must fall apart.
quoteZh: 信念是本，作风是形，本正而形聚，本不正则形必散。

glossary.explanation: The qualities of political loyalty, discipline and principle expected of a Communist Party member. It is treated as something to be cultivated through study and self-discipline.
The manner of conduct of Party members and cadres in work and daily life, including their relationship with ordinary people. Work style building is a long-standing Party campaign theme.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Party, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The Party's internal practices of meetings, criticism and self-criticism, study and discipline, regulated by norms such as the 2016 guidelines mentioned in the article.

t: Promoting a new type of relationship between the Communist Party of China and political parties of the world
zh: 推动构建新型的中国共产党与世界政党关系
paras: Writing in Qiushi in 2025, Liu Jianchao, identified as head of the CPC's International Department, asks how the Communist Party of China (CPC) should build a new type of relationship with political parties worldwide. Liu argues that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the CPC has moved from friendly exchanges to a leading role among the world's parties. The task now, Liu says, is to consolidate a global network of party partnerships under the guidance of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind.

The piece has three parts. The first describes four ways in which the CPC has become a pioneer, leader, promoter and supporter among world parties. The second sets out the new situation, tasks and opportunities. The third lists four lines of work for the Party's external work. Liu cites figures such as contacts with more than 700 parties and political organisations in over 170 countries by the end of 2024, and a June 2024 briefing in Xiong'an attended by representatives of about 40 countries.

In Liu's account, the CPC explores the laws of governing for ruling parties, shares governance experience, widens exchanges without ideological dividing lines, and supplies global public goods such as the community with a shared future for mankind, the three global initiatives and the Belt and Road Initiative. Liu reports that foreign party figures value this experience and that some parties wish to build their own versions of "socialism with distinctive features". Liu presents three drivers for a new relationship: parties' heavier responsibility in a turbulent world, governance challenges from social change and artificial intelligence, and global divisions and realignments that no party can handle alone.

Liu proposes four tasks: strengthen the global party partnership network through political dialogue, the high-level dialogue between the CPC and world political parties, and BRICS and Shanghai Cooperation Organisation channels; promote mutual learning on governance; deepen development cooperation, including a "party plus" platform and support for each ruling party's own path to modernization; and bring peoples closer through cultural exchange, Belt and Road livelihood projects and think-tank alliances. Liu says this will create a favourable external environment for national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want an official statement from the Party's foreign-liaison leadership on how the CPC frames its inter-party diplomacy in 2025.
quoteEn: It does not draw lines by ideology, does not judge closeness by size or strength, does not export its model or preach, and does not impose on others.
quoteZh: 不以意识形态划界，不以大小强弱论亲疏，不搞输出和说教，不强加于人

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.literal: community of common destiny for humankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2013. It calls for cooperative global governance and has been written into UN documents, according to the article.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
A Chinese initiative launched in 2013 to build infrastructure and economic links across Asia, Africa, Europe and beyond.

t: The historical-analytical method of the Communist Manifesto
zh: 《共产党宣言》的历史分析方法
paras: Shan Chuanyou asks by what method Marx and Engels reached the Communist Manifesto's two central conclusions: the inevitable downfall of capitalism and the inevitable victory of the proletariat. The article answers that this was the historical analysis method. Applied from the standpoint of world history and through the basic laws of historical development, it underlies the Manifesto's account of capitalism, the proletariat and rival socialisms.

This short commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Journal in April 2025, is organised in five parts. These cover the world-historical perspective, the historical position of capitalism, the mission of the proletariat and its party, the historical errors of competing socialist currents, and the dependence of revolutionary practice on concrete historical conditions. Shan draws mainly on the Manifesto, with a reference to The German Ideology and to the prefaces of 1872 and 1882.

Shan makes three main moves. First, capitalism and world history form one process: the bourgeoisie opened the world market and subordinated backward nations and the East to the West, which also extends class antagonism worldwide and creates the conditions for international proletarian unity. Second, capitalism is assessed dialectically. It brought formal personal freedom and an unprecedented growth of productive forces, but private appropriation, periodic crises and overproduction mean it will be sublated, and it produces its own gravediggers in the proletariat. Third, the author reads the Manifesto's critique of reactionary, conservative and utopian socialisms as a charge of historical error. In Shan's reading, these currents try to turn back history, to stay fixed in the present, or to leap beyond history.

Shan stresses that the Manifesto's guidance for Communists in France, Switzerland, Poland and Germany varies with national circumstances. The 1872 and 1882 prefaces likewise hold that the basic principles are correct but their application depends on concrete conditions. The author concludes that, under new historical conditions, researchers should still use a world-historical perspective and the basic laws of history to study the new features of capitalism and to develop Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese-academic reading of the Manifesto's method, framed for current work on Marxist theory in China.
quoteEn: The historical analysis method is the basic method by which Marx and Engels arrived at the "two inevitabilities".
quoteZh: 历史分析方法是马克思、恩格斯得出“两个必然”的基本方法。

glossary.explanation: The Chinese rendering of Aufhebung: to overcome something while preserving and carrying forward its valuable elements.

t: Winning the historical initiative through the Party's self-purification of its conduct
zh: 在党风的自我净化中赢得历史主动
paras: Li Zhongjie, a Party historian, takes up Xi Jinping's warning that the Party's conduct (zuofeng) bears on its image, public support and ultimate survival. He argues that, across more than a century, improving conduct has been a continuous process of self-purification through which the Party has won the historical initiative. In his account, this process must continue if the Party is to escape the "historical cycle" of rise and decline.

The piece, published in Qiushi in 2025, is a Party-historical commentary in two parts. The first surveys conduct-building from the founding through the revolutionary years, the early People's Republic, reform and opening up, and the period after the 18th Party Congress (2012), including the eight-point rule. The second draws five reflections from this record.

Li's historical narrative links conduct to survival at each stage: the Rectification Movement in Yan'an, the Two Musts before the Party took power, and the successive anti-corruption measures under reform. For the present era he presents the eight-point rule against the "four undesirable work styles" (formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance) as the entry point of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. His five reflections hold that conduct expresses the Party's nature and vitality, that it must always be viewed as a matter of life and death, and that it is never finished. He also says the Party's two answers to the historical cycle are Mao Zedong's "new path of democracy" and Xi's self-reform. Finally, he says the Party must be purified yet remain full of vitality.

Li concludes that, in a more complex international and domestic setting, only thorough self-reform and a sound system of full and rigorous self-governance can keep the Party self-purifying and self-improving. He says this should not produce a lifeless organisation but a healthy political ecology in which cadres take initiative and society stays dynamic as well as orderly. Read the original if you want an example of how the Party presents the history of its conduct-building and the reasoning behind the eight-point rule and the self-reform campaign.
quoteEn: The Party's conduct is the Party's image.
quoteZh: 党的作风，就是党的形象。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The slogan for the Party-discipline and anti-corruption drive that Xi Jinping has promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It covers political, ideological, organisational, conduct, disciplinary and institutional building.
Official term for the Party's efforts to correct its own failings and resist corruption. The 20th Party Congress (2022) presented it as the Party's answer to the historical cycle of rise and decline.
A set of rules adopted by the Politburo on 4 December 2012 to improve Party work style and curb waste, extravagance and bureaucratic habits. It became a symbol of conduct-building in the Xi era.
The official label for formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, which the Party campaigns against as the main faults in cadre conduct.
The idea, raised in the 1945 Yan'an conversation between Mao Zedong and Huang Yanpei, that regimes rise and then decline. Party writers use it to describe the danger of losing popular support.
Mao Zedong's 1949 call, at the Second Plenum of the 7th Central Committee, for comrades to stay modest and prudent and to keep up hard struggle as the Party prepared to govern the country.

t: The basic logic and strategic paths for raising the Party's leadership level in comprehensively deepening reform
zh: 提高党对全面深化改革领导水平的基本逻辑与战略路径
source: Scientific Socialism (科学社会主义), 2025 no. 1
