glossary.explanation: Shorthand for new economic organisations, new social organisations and new employment groups, such as private firms, non-governmental bodies and platform or gig workers. Party documents treat them as priority areas for Party building.
The work of establishing and strengthening Communist Party organisations, membership and activities within a given sector or locality.

glossary.en: blow the whistle and report in
glossary.literal: blow the whistle, report for duty
glossary.explanation: A governance mechanism in which grassroots units raise a problem ("blow the whistle") and higher-level departments must send staff to help resolve it.
A system that divides communities into small grids, each with a designated worker who collects information and handles local issues. The article proposes embedding Party organisations in it.

t: Deepening the joint investigation and joint treatment of unhealthy work styles and corruption
zh: 深入推进风腐同查同治
source: China Party and Government Cadres Forum, 2025 no. 2
paras: Tang Huangfeng takes up a problem he describes as prominent in current Party discipline work: unhealthy work styles (the "four undesirable work styles") and corruption are increasingly intertwined. The article argues that investigating and treating the two together ("fengfu tongcha tongzhi") is a necessary strategic response. Tang links it to the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and to Xi Jinping's call at the Fourth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection.

The article, published in 2025 in a Party cadre journal, has three parts. The first sets out the basis for joint treatment. The second describes how the fusion of work-style and corruption problems appears in practice and why it arises. The third lists practical requirements for deepening the approach, grouped under joint investigation, joint treatment, and institutional and mechanism innovation.

Tang's central claim is that the two problems share one root, the alienation of power. Small lapses such as accepting gifts or banquets are said to erode a cadre's defences until quantitative change becomes qualitative change, while uncorrected corruption in turn encourages bad styles. Tang identifies three forms of fusion: improper banquets masking benefit transfers, formalism and bureaucratism shielding graft, and personal enrichment alongside extravagant living. Four causes are named: wavering ideals, weak checks on power, poor enforcement of rules and unhealthy social attitudes. For remedies Tang proposes severe punishment for intertwined cases, better clue-handling, and cross-border asset recovery. The article also calls for tighter supervision of top officials, big-data supervision platforms, ideological and integrity education, and a "one case, four examinations" mechanism covering work style, institutional loopholes, responsibility gaps and the political ecosystem.

Tang concludes that joint investigation and treatment is a long and arduous political task that safeguards the Party's vanguard character and its ties with the people. Its operating principle is that every work-style investigation should dig for corruption, and every corruption case should examine work style. Tang presents this as protection for Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how Party discipline inspection bodies are asked to link work-style rectification and anti-corruption enforcement, including its typology of cases and proposed mechanisms.
quoteEn: That unhealthy work styles and corruption are two sides of one coin, sharing a common root, is the logical starting point for insisting on joint investigation and treatment.
quoteZh: 不正之风与腐败问题互为表里、同根同源是坚持风腐同查同治的逻辑起点。

glossary.explanation: Formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, the targets of the Party's work-style campaign launched after the 18th Party Congress (2012).
The official term for China's development path, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: An official goal of national revival, tied by the Party to the mid-twenty-first century.

t: Giving full play to the role of grassroots Party organisations in government organs as fighting bastions: providing solid support for Jiangsu's new practice of Chinese modernization
zh: 充分发挥机关基层党组织战斗堡垒作用 为推进中国式现代化江苏新实践提供坚实支撑
source: Party Building Research in Government Organs (Jiguan dangjian yanjiu), 2025 no. 3
paras: Writing in 2025, Chu Yonghong, who heads the Working Committee of Jiangsu's provincial government organs, asks how Party building in government organs can support high-quality development in the province. The article is a practical, official-style statement that takes Xi Jinping's July 2024 instruction on Party building in central and state organs as its starting point. Chu's thesis is that the quality of organ-level Party building depends on the quality of its grassroots organisations, and that their role as "fighting bastions" should be strengthened to serve Chinese modernization in Jiangsu.

The article is organised in four parts, each opening with a claim that one outcome depends on grassroots organisations: the quality of Party building, service to high-quality development, the work style and image of provincial organs, and the implementation of Party-building responsibility. Each part pairs a summary of what Jiangsu has done in recent years with a list of tasks for the future. Chu draws on named local programmes, regulations and mechanisms, such as the model-organ upgrading plan, "four-strong" Party branches and the "service for high-quality development vanguard teams".

Chu's first argument concerns capacity. Political guidance, the selection and training of branch secretaries, and the enforcement of standardised rules are meant to strengthen the political and organisational functions of branches. Chu also calls for monitoring the thinking of younger officials and for stronger practical training for officials born in the 1980s and 1990s, whom Chu describes as well educated but short of experience. The second argument concerns output and conduct. Party organisations are to act on key provincial tasks, keep their platforms effective rather than showy, and encourage officials to take responsibility by dealing with reluctance and lack of skill. Discipline education following the 2024 Party discipline campaign is to continue, and measures against formalism should begin with provincial organs. Chu holds that formalism is often visible at the grassroots but rooted higher up.

Chu argues that responsibility must be carried down the chain, from Party committees and groups in each department, through their organ Party committees, to the Working Committee itself. Proposals include at least one Party committee meeting every half-year on organ Party building, contact points for leading cadres, coordination mechanisms, and regular reviews of branch secretaries' reports. These are meant to close the "last mile" of accountability. Read the original if you want a concrete example of how a provincial Party working committee presents its organ Party-building agenda, its named mechanisms and its responsibility system.
quoteEn: Discipline education has only a continuous tense, never a completed one.
quoteZh: 纪律教育只有进行时，没有完成时。

glossary.explanation: The official formulation of China's development path, promoted by the Party leadership since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models of modernization.
An official goal, in place since about 2017, that stresses the quality and efficiency of growth over speed alone.

A standard Party phrase for grassroots Party organisations as strongholds that lead and mobilise people and carry out tasks. It is often paired with the "vanguard and exemplary role" of individual members.

t: Using high-quality investigation and research to generate strong momentum for comprehensively deepening reform
zh: 以高质量调研形成全面深化改革的强大动力
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in March 2025, asks how Party members and cadres can use investigation and research, which the author calls the Party's "family heirloom", to support the further deepening of reform. Zhan argues that research must be "deep, solid, meticulous, accurate and effective" if it is to locate the starting points, focal points and breakthrough points of reform and strengthen its systematic and coordinated character.

The article draws on Xi Jinping's remarks since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is organised under five headings: cultivating a people-centred outlook, upholding a pragmatic work style, focusing on development practice, facing difficulties and challenges, and moving from points to the whole.

Zhan's core claims are that research must follow the mass line and seek out critical voices from the grassroots, and that it must rest on seeking truth from facts, with no staged or showcase visits. It must be problem-oriented, meaning problems are faced, analysed and solved rather than shelved, and cadres should visit difficult places rather than only successful ones. Drawing on Xi's endorsement of "dissecting the sparrow", the author also ties research to a systems approach that balances the macro and micro, the whole and the part, and the particular and the general.

Zhan concludes that cadres should study and apply Xi's statements on research, and treat research as practice of the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, as a way of changing work style, and as a way to resolve reform problems and drive Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-school and university leaders present investigation and research as a method of governance and Party building in the current reform agenda.
quoteEn: Investigation and research cannot tolerate the slightest carelessness; it must uphold the principle of seeking truth from facts, foster a truth-seeking and pragmatic work style, and show the courage to pursue truth and correct errors.
quoteZh: 调查研究容不得半点马虎，必须坚持实事求是的原则，树立求真务实的作风，具有追求真理、修正错误的勇气。

glossary.explanation: A formula adopted in the 2021 Party history resolution and stressed afterwards. It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the Party's core and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.

A political requirement that Party members uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Party Central Committee and in the whole Party, and uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.
The official formulation of China's development path, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A Party working method, associated with Mao Zedong, of gathering views from the people, distilling them, and returning them as policy. It is treated as a basic principle of Party work.
A principle of basing policy on actual conditions rather than on doctrine or on instructions from above. It was revived in the Party's ideological line under Deng Xiaoping.

t: The epistemological essence of investigation and research in the Communist Party of China
zh: 中国共产党调查研究的认识论本质
paras: Yang Ruwei examines investigation and research (diaocha yanjiu), which Xi Jinping calls a family heirloom of the Party, from the standpoint of Marxist epistemology. The short commentary argues that its essence lies in uniting a value orientation with cognition of objective laws. Yang links this to the current drive to advance Chinese modernization and to implement the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).

The piece has three parts: the essence of investigation and research, its process, and its features. It draws on Mao Zedong's On Practice, a passage from Marx on research, and Mao's rural surveys of 1928–1933, including the Xunwu and Mukou village investigations.

Yang holds that the Party's value orientation is goal-directed, revolutionary and people-centred, while its cognition of laws is objective, systematic and developmental. Without a correct value orientation, in Yang's reading, rational knowledge and sound policy cannot be reached. The process has two steps: moving from the concrete to the abstract by gathering material, then from the abstract to the "ideal concrete" by reconstructing it in thought to produce policies. Mao's eleven rural surveys serve as the example.

Yang identifies four features: objectivity, dynamism, purposefulness and timeliness. Methods must change as tasks, investigators and conditions change, and older cadres' experience cannot replace that of new ones. Read the original if you want a brief Party-building account that frames investigation and research as an epistemological process, with Mao's rural surveys as illustration.
quoteEn: Without a correct value orientation, rational knowledge cannot be obtained, and of course correct theories, plans and schemes cannot be produced.
quoteZh: 没有正确的价值导向就不能获得理性认识，当然也不能作出正确的理论、计划、方案等。

glossary.explanation: The Party's practice of fact-finding through field surveys, interviews and meetings before making policy. It is closely associated with Mao Zedong's rural surveys and is regularly stressed by Xi Jinping.
The official term for China's path of modernization, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.pinyin: dǎng de èrshí jiè sān zhōngquánhuì
glossary.en: Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
glossary.explanation: A Party meeting held in July 2024 that adopted a decision on further deepening reform comprehensively.
Mao Zedong's 1937 essay on the relation between knowledge and practice, a core text of Chinese Marxist epistemology.

t: Overseas research on the Communist Party of China's anti-corruption campaign in the new era: an analysis
zh: 新时代中国共产党反腐败问题海外研究论析
source: Foreign Theoretical Trends (国外理论动态), 2024 no. 6
paras: This literature review surveys how scholars outside China have studied the Communist Party of China's anti-corruption campaign since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Liu and Gao argue that overseas scholarship has increasingly taken the campaign seriously and in places revised older explanatory paradigms. They also contend that some of this work remains marked by biases that Chinese researchers should answer, while its sound points deserve critical absorption.

The review first sets out overseas views that the campaign opened a new stage of corruption governance, citing its resilience, institutionalisation and shift from campaign-style control to routine prevention. It then organises the literature by perspective: motives, effects (political, economic, international), institutional reforms (discipline inspection, the supervision system, inspection tours) and policy proposals. Authors discussed include Andrew Wedeman, Melanie Manion, Andrew Walder, Kerry Brown, Yuen Yuen Ang and Jamie P. Horsley.

On motives, Liu and Gao report a "multi-layered dynamic system": removing the threat corruption poses to Party rule, reshaping political culture and morality, and breaking vested interests that block reform. On effects, the review finds that most studies see gains in public trust, though some judge the effect limited. Other studies report officials' passivity and a weakened pipeline of young talent. Firm-level evidence is mixed, and some sectors, such as luxury goods and hospitality, were hit. Overseas scholars also suggest more legalisation, wider social participation, and moral and cultural cultivation. The authors then criticise four tendencies: a functionalist reading that overlooks the principle of "putting the people first"; Western-centrism that takes Western experience as the benchmark; a theory-driven approach that produces a "China paradox"; and weaknesses in sources and methods, including reliance on secondary materials and fragmentary case data.

Liu and Gao conclude that overseas research offers a useful international perspective for developing a distinctively Chinese path against corruption and for shaping China's clean image abroad. They call for a problem-consciousness rooted in practice rather than imported frameworks. Read the original if you want a structured map of English-language and other foreign scholarship on the campaign, together with a Chinese academic response to it.
quoteEn: Only by adhering to a practice-based problem consciousness can one break free from the unreasonable constraints of existing Western theory and pose Chinese questions that combine the particular and the general.
quoteZh: 唯有坚持实践的问题意识，方能破除西方既有理论的无理规制，进而提出兼备特殊与一般的中国问题。

t: The logic and path of the great founding spirit of the Party in leading the "two great revolutions"
zh: 伟大建党精神引领“两个伟大革命”的逻辑理据与路径选择
paras: Xu Fengzhen asks how the great founding spirit of the Party can lead and sustain what official texts call the "two great revolutions": the Party's great self-reform, which Xu describes as remaking the subjective world and answering "what the Party is", and the great social revolution, which remakes the objective world and answers "what the Party does". The article argues that this spirit is the spiritual source of the "high degree of consciousness" in "leading social revolution through the Party's self-reform", a requirement set out in the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). It is written in the language of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

The article proceeds through five grounds: discursive, historical, practical, value-based, and a final section on choice of path. It opens with the genesis of three expressions, "founding spirit", "self-revolution" and "social revolution", and then sets out five relations between the founding spirit and the two revolutions. It then reads the four components of the founding spirit against the question of where Chinese modernization comes from, where it is going, how it proceeds and for whom. Its sources run from the 1921 first Party programme and Mao Zedong to Xi Jinping's speeches.

Xu's first move is conceptual. In Xu's account, "social revolution" fell out of regular use during the socialist-construction and reform eras, and Xi's 2018 speech reconnected it, so its usage traces a "V" shape. Xu also finds a "hidden" social-revolution spirit inside the "spirit of reform and innovation", alongside the explicit "self-revolution spirit". The second move is historical: the founding spirit and the two revolutions appeared together, overlap in roles, advance in step, complement each other and share traits. Without the spirit the revolutions are "blind", and without the revolutions the spirit is "empty". Third, each of the four components is tied to a question about Chinese modernization. Seeking truth and ideals concern direction and the unity of the maximum, minimum and basic programmes. Original aspiration and mission concern the starting point and national rejuvenation. Fearlessness in sacrifice concerns method. Loyalty to the Party and the people concerns purpose, as a dialectical unity of Party spirit and the people's character.

Xu concludes that the spirit must be inherited (the "source") and developed (the "stream"). It is to be turned into theoretical, political, behavioural and value strengths by studying Marxism, taking the people's standpoint, cultivating revolutionary character and putting Party and people first. Xu holds that only then can Party members keep a "thoroughly revolutionary spirit" and carry Chinese modernization and national rejuvenation forward. Read the original if you want to see how Party-history scholarship ties the Party's spiritual lineage to the current formula of self-reform leading social revolution, including its account of how these terms developed.
quoteEn: The "two great revolutions" without the guidance and support of the great founding spirit are blind; the great founding spirit without the nurturing and continuation of the "two great revolutions" is empty.
quoteZh: 没有伟大建党精神引领和支撑的“两个伟大革命”是盲目的，没有“两个伟大革命”抚育和赓续的伟大建党精神是空洞的。

glossary.en: great founding spirit of the Party
glossary.explanation: A formulation first put forward by Xi Jinping in 2021 for the Party's centenary. It sums up the Party's founders' ethos as upholding truth and ideals, staying true to the original aspiration, being fearless in struggle, and loyalty to the Party and the people.

Official shorthand for the great social revolution led by the Party and the Party's own great self-reform. Since the 20th Party Congress (2022) the stated requirement is that the second should lead the first.
The Party's drive to discipline, correct and renew itself, now a core theme of Party-building. Xi Jinping first set out the idea systematically in 2015.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, a central concept in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: The cultural logic of Communists keeping the "Three Musts" in mind in the new era
zh: 新时代共产党人牢记“三个务必”的文化理路
paras: Wang Cheng takes up the "Three Musts" announced in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): all Party members must remain true to the original aspiration and founding mission, must remain modest, prudent and hardworking, and must dare to fight and be good at fighting. The article treats them as an innovative development of Mao Zedong's "Two Musts" of 1949. Wang notes that existing research clusters around their significance, historical background, meaning and practical requirements, and argues that their cultural logic has been little studied. The thesis is that the Three Musts draw on three layers of culture and that Communists can keep them in mind through the Second Integration.

The article has three parts. The first traces the cultural sources of the Three Musts in excellent traditional Chinese culture, in revolutionary culture from the new-democratic and socialist revolution and construction periods, and in advanced socialist culture from reform and opening up and the new era. The second sets out their cultural significance in four respects. The third proposes three paths for putting them into practice.

In Wang's account, each of the three Musts matches a strand of tradition. The first corresponds to the ideas of putting the people first, of governing the world and relieving the people's hardship, and of a world of great harmony. The second corresponds to the Book of Changes' "modesty" hexagram and to the classical stress on self-strengthening and frugality. The third corresponds to the Confucian value of courage and to the unity of knowing and doing. Revolutionary culture then carries these into Party practice, through Mao's warnings in 1949, the spirit of the Party and the Long March, and the Yan'an-era study of the fall of Li Zicheng. Wang argues that the Three Musts help to firm up Communists' ideals and convictions, to solve the problems unique to a large party, to improve Party conduct, government conduct and popular customs, and to advance the goal of building a modern socialist country.

Wang proposes three paths. The first is theoretical innovation, meaning study of the Party's innovative theory, the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, and ideological education. The second is stronger Party spirit and moral cultivation, backed by the Eight-point Regulation and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. The third is a fighting spirit that builds the capacity to meet complex situations. Wang concludes that the Three Musts safeguard the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-theory scholar links a current Party slogan to classical Chinese texts, revolutionary history and the Second Integration.
quoteEn: The "Three Musts" express the Party's fundamental stance and are a safeguard for the Party's comprehensive advancement of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization in the new era.
quoteZh: “三个务必”表明了党的根本立场，是党在新时代以中国式现代化全面推进中华民族伟大复兴的保障。

glossary.explanation: A formula in Xi Jinping's report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It requires Party members to keep the original aspiration and mission, to stay modest and hardworking, and to dare and be good at struggle.
Mao Zedong's 1949 call, at the Second Plenum of the 7th Central Committee, for Party members to stay modest and prudent and to keep up the style of hard struggle.
The Second Integration is the second of the Two Integrations: combining the basic tenets of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture. It is an official formula of the Xi Jinping era.
An official formula, from 2021–22, affirming Xi Jinping's core position in the Party and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.

An official requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and to uphold the Party Central Committee's authority and its centralised, unified leadership.
The official name for China's path of modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party-discipline and anti-corruption campaign pursued since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

t: Seen through the history of theoretical innovation, the "Second Integration" is another emancipation of the mind
zh: 从理论创新史看“第二个结合”是又一次的思想解放
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in March 2025, Feng Jun argues that each step in the Chinese Communist Party's theoretical innovation has been the product of an emancipation of the mind (jiefang sixiang). The article's thesis is that the Two Integrations, in particular the "Second Integration" of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture, mark the latest such emancipation.

The piece is a short commentary organised in three historical stages. It first treats the revolutionary period, from the fight against dogmatism to the Yan'an rectification and the Seventh Party Congress. It then covers socialist construction and the reform era, from the 1956 exploration after the Soviet model through the truth-criterion debate and the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978). Finally it turns to the Second Integration under Xi Jinping.

Feng's central move is to separate two lines. The "First Integration", of Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities, is said to have required breaking with book-worship and Soviet copying. It produced Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents and the Scientific Outlook on Development. The Second Integration, in Feng's account, had been practised implicitly but was first stated explicitly in the new era, giving socialism with Chinese characteristics deeper historical roots. Feng lists five ways it frees thinking: it rejects both historical nihilism and cultural conservatism; it strengthens cultural confidence and cultural subjectivity; it deepens understanding of Chinese modernization as the continuation of an ancient civilization; it widens the space for innovation by joining Marxism as the "soul" to traditional culture as the "root"; and it points the way to a culturally strong country.

Feng concludes that adhering to the Two Integrations is the necessary path for developing socialism with Chinese characteristics. He calls for creative transformation of traditional culture under Marxist guidance, guided by core socialist values. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Party theorists place the Second Integration within the Party's own history of theoretical innovation.
quoteEn: The "Second Integration" is another emancipation of the mind, allowing us to draw fully on the precious resources of fine traditional Chinese culture in a broader cultural space and to explore theoretical and institutional innovation oriented to the future.
quoteZh: “第二个结合”是又一次的思想解放,让我们能够在更广阔的文化空间中,充分运用中华优秀传统文化的宝贵资源,探索面向未来的理论和制度创新。

glossary.explanation: The formula of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities (First Integration) and with fine traditional Chinese culture (Second Integration). The second was stated explicitly under Xi Jinping in the new era.
A Party slogan for breaking free of rigid doctrine and outdated ideas. It is especially associated with Deng Xiaoping and the late-1970s shift to reform.
The official name for China's path of modernization, presented by the Party as distinct from Western models and as rooted in Chinese conditions and civilization.
The guiding concept associated with Hu Jintao, stressing people-centred, comprehensive and sustainable development.
A theory associated with Jiang Zemin, holding that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the people.

t: Systems integration and the creative construction of an autonomous knowledge system
st: How the Third Plenum Decision's systems integration of Chinese modernization elevates a "systematised economic theory" with Chinese characteristics
zh: 系统集成对自主知识体系的创造性构建
paras: Gu Hailiang takes up the Decision adopted at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform and advancing Chinese modernization. He asks what its stress on "systems integration" and a "systems perspective" means for building China's autonomous knowledge system. Gu argues that this integration is both a key to the Decision's spirit and a step that lifts China's "systematised economic theory" to a new level.

The short piece, published in Beijing Daily in March 2025, sets out six features of systems integration as an autonomous knowledge system. It relies mainly on Xi Jinping's speeches on philosophy and social sciences, on the 20th Party Congress (2022) report and on the Decision itself. It also draws on Engels's remark on a "revolution in terminology", on postcolonial critiques of dependent knowledge, and on Peter Burke's history of knowledge.

Gu's core claim is that the integration rests on Chinese conditions and a problem-oriented method, and that it is marked by a "revolution in terminology". He lists new concepts such as the new development philosophy, high-quality development and new quality productive forces, and presents them as signs of intellectual autonomy. He adds that the system is politically and intellectually committed to the Four-sphere Confidence while also being academic, and that it counters a "dependent" knowledge tradition tied to Western-centrism. Drawing on Burke's examples of conflict between "practical" and "theoretical" knowledge, Gu says Chinese modernization's integration joins theory-driven and practice-driven knowledge into one type. He ties this to Xi's call for a "systematised economic theory" that answers real problems and is rooted in Chinese practice.

Gu concludes that systems integration offers a systematic exploration of how to build a knowledge system that combines theoretical and practical orientations. He says it has important implications for the innovative development of China's autonomous knowledge system. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese academics link the Third Plenum Decision to the project of an autonomous knowledge system in economics and the social sciences.
quoteEn: The autonomous knowledge system presented by the systems integration of Chinese modernization integrates both knowledge driven by a scholarly, theoretical problem orientation and knowledge driven by an applied, practical one.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化系统集成所呈现的自主知识体系，既有学理性和学术性问题取向驱动的知识的集成，也有根据应用性和实践性问题取向驱动的知识的集成

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formula for China's path to modernity, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A principle stressed in drafting the Third Plenum Decision. It means planning reform as a whole so that its parts work together efficiently.
An official goal for Chinese philosophy and social sciences: concepts and theories built on Chinese practice rather than imported frameworks.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023. It stresses innovation-driven, technology-intensive development.
The official development goal that replaces a focus on growth speed with quality, efficiency and sustainability.
The Party's guideline of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, announced in 2015.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

t: The people's congress system has a distinctive advantage in safeguarding the rule of law
zh: 人民代表大会制度具有法治保障的显著优势
paras: Taking Xi Jinping's speech marking the 70th anniversary of the National People's Congress as its starting point, this article by Lü Zhongmei, a senior NPC and legal-association official, takes up one of the system's stated advantages: that it safeguards law-based governance in all fields. Lü argues that the people's congress system is the institutional cornerstone of comprehensive law-based governance and that this advantage should be turned more fully into governance effectiveness.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the constitutional and institutional foundations, tracing the system from the 1949 Common Program through the 1954 and 1982 constitutions and describing the legislative and supervisory powers of people's congresses. The second discusses the essential character of the Chinese path of rule of law. The third sets out tasks for the new journey, including legislation, the democratic work of congresses and supervision.

Lü's central claim is that the system joins three things: Party leadership, the people as masters of the country, and law-based governance. In this account the Party turns its proposals into state will through statutory procedures, and the 2018 constitutional amendment writing Party leadership into Article 1 reinforces this. The article says the system pairs formal and substantive justice, draws on world legal civilisation without copying Western models, and keeps law responsive to change, citing foreign investment law, digital economy regulation and ecological legislation. Lü adds that the rule-of-law advantage supports the system's other advantages: Party leadership, whole-process people's democracy, democratic centralism, and national unity and long-term stability.

For the new era, Lü calls for higher-quality legislation under a pattern of Party leadership, congress primacy, government support and broad participation. Lü also calls for better congress procedures, deputy liaison stations and grassroots legislative contact points, and for supervision that is correct, effective and lawful. The article concludes that the system's rule-of-law capacity is a benchmark of modernised state governance and a contribution to political civilisation. Read the original if you want an official-insider account of how Party-state legal scholarship presents the NPC system's constitutional, legislative and supervisory functions in the Xi era.
quoteEn: The people's congress system and the constitution are closely linked and develop in step, each the inside and outside of the other, each enhancing the other.
quoteZh: 人民代表大会制度与宪法紧密相连、同频发展，互为表里、相得益彰。

glossary.explanation: China's fundamental political system under the constitution, in which people's congresses at each level are the organs of state power. The National People's Congress is the highest of these.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2019. It holds that democracy runs through every stage of governance, including elections, consultation, decision-making, management and oversight.
A Leninist organisational principle combining democratic discussion with centralised decision-making. The Party applies it to its own organisation and to state organs.

t: How further deepening reform comprehensively reshapes five relationships
zh: 论进一步全面深化改革对五大关系的重塑
paras: Chen Yongsheng examines how the Decision adopted at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization seeks to "reshape" five relationships. These are centre–locality, regional development, grassroots society, humanity and nature, and urban–rural relations. The author argues that this strand of the Decision has real cognitive and practical value and deserves systematic study.

The article is built as five parallel sections. Each one first records achievements since reform and opening up (or since 1949), then lists new problems, then explains how the Decision responds and what further steps Chen proposes. It draws on official statistics, such as regional GDP figures, Gini coefficients, urbanisation rates and urban–rural income ratios, and on quotations from Xi Jinping. It closes with a note that the work is a stage result of a national social science fund project on whole-process people's democracy.

On centre–local relations, Chen identifies a fiscal gap, oversized transfer payments that reduce efficiency, and uncertainty in the allocation of fiscal powers and spending responsibilities. The Decision's answer is to raise local autonomous revenue, reform transfers and move spending responsibilities upward, so that "the top orders and the bottom pays" becomes less common. On regions, the author cites a widening north–south gap and the polarising pull of megacities, and calls for complementary regional advantages and locally tailored new quality productive forces. For grassroots society, Chen points to a Gini coefficient persistently above 0.4, diversifying interests and rising risks, and endorses income-distribution reform, stronger township and street capacity and a firmer national security system.

For humanity and nature, Chen notes progress in air and water quality but problems of low-quality growth, cadres fixated on growth rates, and weak ecological-product valuation. Chen urges property-rights, compensation, governance and green-finance reforms. For urban and rural areas, relative income gaps are narrowing while absolute gaps are widening, and the household-registration urbanisation rate lags the resident rate by nearly 18 points. Chen calls for supporting agriculture, enabling migrants to receive public services where they live, and integrated planning. Read the original if you want a detailed, statistics-backed Chinese official-academic reading of the Third Plenum Decision's institutional agenda across fiscal, regional, social, ecological and rural–urban fields.
quoteEn: Advancing ecological civilization and achieving modernization in which humanity and nature coexist harmoniously is an inherent requirement of building a strong country and the great cause of national rejuvenation, and a hurdle the Party must clear in governing the country.
quoteZh: 推进生态文明建设，实现人与自然和谐共生的现代化是推进强国建设，民族复兴伟业的内在要求，是我们党治国理政必须要过的一道关卡。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept, elaborated since the 20th Party Congress (2022), of a modernization path said to be specific to China's conditions. It is the framework for the Third Plenum Decision discussed here.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced, technology-driven productive capacity underpinning high-quality development.
The theme of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (July 2024), which adopted a Decision setting reform tasks and a timetable.

t: Deepening the Party's institutions of Party building to advance the Party's self-reform
zh: 深化党的建设制度推进党的自我革命
paras: Bao Xinjian, in a commentary published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in February 2025, argues that institution-building is the core and key element of Party building. The article holds that, in the new era, reform of the Party's institutions must be deepened to meet the internal requirements of the Party's self-reform. It asks that attention go first to three systems: the Party's leadership system, the cadre and personnel system, and the system of power supervision.

The piece is organised around these three areas. Each is treated in its own section: the leadership system and democratic centralism, the selection and appointment of cadres, and the combination of intra-Party supervision with supervision by the people. Bao draws on Marx and Engels's Communist Manifesto and on Marxist theories of the state to ground the discussion, and refers to the Party's existing body of internal regulations.

Bao's central claim is that strict governance of the Party through institutions rests on a basic political logic: developing people's democracy and intra-Party democracy. Without the former, the Party's governing position is hard to consolidate; without the latter, institution-building cannot go deep. Democratic centralism must guard against both excessive dispersal and excessive centralisation, with tighter checks on the top leader ("yibashou") of each unit. On cadres, Bao argues that power is "granted by the people", so selection must unite Party management of cadres with democratic mechanisms, avoiding both pure vote-counting and neglect of public opinion. On supervision, Bao holds that public power always risks monopolisation and corruption. The article therefore proposes a system with intra-Party supervision at its core and supervision by the people as its driving force, drawing on the people's congresses, the CPPCC, social organisations and the media.

Bao concludes that combining the two forms of supervision gives a lasting mechanism for escaping the historical cycle of rise and decline, relying on supervision by the people and the Party's self-reform as the "two magic weapons". The article credits the Party's recent discipline and anti-corruption efforts with changing a past situation of lax and soft Party governance. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Party theorists link democratic centralism, cadre selection and supervision to the Party's self-reform in the Xi Jinping era.
quoteEn: Without people's democracy, the Party's governing position and core leading role can hardly be durably consolidated; without intra-Party democracy, the Party's institution-building and strict institutional governance of the Party can hardly be advanced in depth.
quoteZh: 没有人民民主，党的执政地位和核心领导作用很难持久巩固；没有党内民主，党的制度建设和严格制度治党很难深入推进。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed under Xi Jinping: the Party's capacity to correct its own errors and purge its own problems, presented as the answer to how a long-ruling party avoids decline.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Communist Party, combining democratic discussion with centralised, binding decisions and unified discipline.
Colloquial term for the principal leader of a Party or government unit, regarded in Party discourse as a "key few" requiring special supervision.

t: The threefold global impact of Chinese modernization
zh: 论中国式现代化的三重世界影响
paras: Ji Qiwei and Tian Zhijian ask what influence Chinese modernization has on the world, and answer that its impact is threefold. In their account it changes the global map of modernization, contributes Chinese wisdom to building a better world, and offers experience to developing countries. They frame it as a modernization that is not self-interested but seeks happiness for the Chinese people, rejuvenation of the nation, and progress for humanity. The framing draws on the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and its Decision on deepening reform.

The article has three main sections. The first treats Chinese modernization as redrawing the world map of modernization in terms of population, shared benefits and the place of socialist states. The second covers its contribution to economic recovery, to the questions of the times, and to opportunities for other countries. The third draws lessons for developing countries. It relies on Xi Jinping's statements, official economic figures, and examples such as high-speed rail exports and the Beidou navigation system.

The authors argue that only some twenty countries with about one billion people have modernized, all of them capitalist, so that the existing modernization is a partial and 'private' one. Bringing more than 1.4 billion Chinese into modernity would, in their view, more than double the modernized population and break the equation of 'modernization = Westernization', including Fukuyama's end-of-history thesis. They also cite the Global Development, Security and Civilization Initiatives and a community with a shared future for mankind as Chinese contributions. For developing countries, they draw three lessons: build a strong leadership core, with the Party's full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and self-reform as the model; promote all-round development rather than one-sided growth; and rely on independence and self-reliance while learning selectively from others.

The authors conclude that Chinese modernization is socialist modernization, enriches Marxist modernization theory and raises the global influence of scientific socialism. They stress that China does not export a 'China model' but offers developing countries options for independent paths. Read the original if you want a representative statement of how Chinese academic writing presents the international significance of Chinese modernization, including its claims about leadership, development and the Global South.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is a parallel rather than sequential modernization, a comprehensive rather than one-sided modernization, continually displaying the multidimensional character that modernization should have.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化是并联式的现代化而不是串联式的现代化，是全面现代化而不是片面现代化，持续彰显现代化应有的多维特质。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's path to modernization, set out by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as socialist, with features such as huge population scale, common prosperity and peaceful development.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012–13. It calls for joint development, security and cooperation among countries.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's drive since 2012 to tighten discipline, fight corruption and strengthen internal supervision.
An official term for the Party's capacity to correct its own errors and purify itself. It is a central theme of recent Party-building discourse.
A term for developing countries, used in Chinese diplomacy and scholarship to describe China's partners in the developing world.

t: The philosophical implications of the Party's self-reform in the new era
zh: 新时代党的自我革命的哲学意蕴
source: China Theory Network (中国理论网), 27 February 2025
paras: Yin Tieyan asks what philosophical foundations underlie the Communist Party of China's self-reform in the new era. The article argues that the Party's self-reform rests on the Marxist worldview and methodology, namely the basic positions of historical materialism and dialectical materialism, and that it should be understood through three sets of philosophical perspectives.

The article is organised in three sections. The first deals with a holistic view and a view of tortuous development; the second with the views of connection and practice; the third with the views of contradiction and development. Yin draws on the Party's history from the New Democratic Revolution to the present, on Xi Jinping's statements, and on quotations from other Chinese scholars.

First, Yin holds that self-reform must be treated as a continuous historical whole, set within world socialist revolution and the Party's century-plus history. Because new things develop along a winding, spiral path, risks and challenges are to be resolved within self-reform itself. Second, Yin presents self-reform and social revolution as a dialectical unity: social revolution is the practical basis and direction of self-reform, while self-reform is the driving force that leads social revolution. Self-reform is also tied to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, a community with a shared future for mankind, and the Party's response to crises of political parties worldwide. Third, Yin argues that self-reform arises from contradictions within the Party and society, and that the "two-point theory" and the "emphasis on the key point" must be combined to grasp the principal contradiction and its principal aspect. Yin cites the 19th Party Congress (2017) judgement that the principal contradiction is now between the people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced and inadequate development.

Yin concludes that self-reform in the new era should adhere to seeking truth from facts, investigation and research, and a scientific method for resolving contradictions. In the article's account, this strengthens the Party's long-term governing capacity and reflects its responsibility as the world's largest Marxist governing party. Read the original if you want a short example of how Chinese Party-building scholarship maps Marxist dialectics onto the doctrine of the Party's self-reform.
quoteEn: Realising the Chinese Dream of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is the social development goal of the Party's self-reform.
quoteZh: 实现中华民族伟大复兴的中国梦是党的自我革命的社会发展目标。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed in Party discourse under Xi Jinping, referring to the Party's efforts to correct its own problems and strengthen discipline. It is often paired with leading "social revolution".

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term national goal of the Party, associated with the Chinese Dream and the "two centenary goals".

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–13, describing a vision of international cooperation and shared interests.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The inner mechanism and realisation path of the Communist Party of China's leadership in building the Chinese national community
zh: 中国共产党领导中华民族共同体建设的内在机理与实现路径
paras: Why, and how, does the Communist Party of China lead the building of the Chinese national community (Zhonghua minzu gongtongti)? Wang Chuanfa argues that existing scholarship describes the history, discourse and achievements of this project but gives only a weak theoretical answer to the question of why the Party leads it. The article's thesis is that Party leadership results from a coupling between the project's internal needs and the Party's accumulated "political potential energy".

The article was published in the journal Tansuo in 2025 and opens with a short review of work on the history, discourse and experience of Party-led community building. It then proceeds in three steps: demand (why leadership is necessary), supply (why it is possible) and mechanisms (how it is realised). It draws on Tönnies, Rousseau and Marx for general theories of community and interest, and on Xi Jinping's statements on ethnic work. It also cites Party documents, constitutional and legal changes, and Party membership statistics.

On the demand side, Wang holds that community-building needs emotional bonding, shared values, continuing common interests, and collective action toward shared goals. In each case, the author argues, differences of region, resources and development create tensions that only Party organisation, ideological guidance, integration and its founding mission can resolve. On the supply side, borrowing the concept of "political potential energy" from He Donghang and Kong Fanbin, Wang identifies four kinds: value-based, institutional, organisational and identity-based. Examples include the central ethnic work conferences from 1992, the addition of the phrase "forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation" to the Party Constitution (2017), the insertion of "Chinese nation" into the state constitution (2018), and a Party base of 5.065 million grassroots organisations at the end of 2022. The author names four realisation mechanisms: shaping ideas, embedding organisation, integrating resources and delivering public services.

Wang concludes that the Party's "presence of leadership" (dang de lingdao zaichang) in ethnic work is both an internal requirement of community building and a necessary choice for staying on the correct path of resolving ethnic issues with Chinese characteristics. Strengthening the Party's overall leadership is described as the fundamental political guarantee of ethnic work in the new era and of Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese scholar builds a theoretical case, drawing on the idea of political potential energy, for Party leadership in ethnic affairs and in the building of national identity.
quoteEn: The \"presence of Party leadership\" in ethnic work comes from the coupling of the internal needs of building the Chinese national community with the possibilities supplied by the political potential energy embodied in the Communist Party of China.
quoteZh: 民族工作中“党的领导在场”是由中华民族共同体建设的内在需求和中国共产党蕴含的政治势能供给的可能性耦合而成的。

glossary.explanation: A concept central to the Party's ethnic theory under Xi Jinping. It presents the 56 ethnic groups as one community of shared destiny, and its building is described as the core task of ethnic work in the new era.
A concept borrowed from physics and used by Chinese political scientists. It refers to the stored authority of the Party that can be converted into governance effectiveness.

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: forging a firm consciousness of the Chinese national community
glossary.explanation: The official guiding principle of ethnic work, made its main thread at the 2021 central ethnic work conference. It was written into the Party Constitution in 2017.
The Party's official formulation of China's own path to modernisation, used since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
High-level Party meetings that set the principles and policies for ethnic affairs. The first was held in 1992, and later ones were held in 2014 and 2021.

t: The principled meaning of "promoting a better fit between state governance and social development"
zh: “推动国家治理和社会发展更好相适应”的原理性内涵
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 14 March 2025, studies a formula from the decision adopted by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform and advancing Chinese modernization: promoting a better fit between state governance and social development. Xi Ge and Fu Tianrui argue that this formula, added to the established pairs of productive forces and relations of production and of economic base and superstructure, is a contemporary development of the basic principles of historical materialism. They present it as a worldview and methodological guide for implementing the new development philosophy.

The article has four parts. It first defines state governance and social development and the unity between them. It then links the governance–development contradiction to the basic contradictions of society, takes up the word "better" as a sign of dynamic change, and ends by reading the formula through the Two Integrations.

The authors define both terms broadly. State governance is the whole system of institutions and the capacity to run them, spanning all five spheres of the overall plan. Social development is the development of society as an organic whole, so it already contains state governance as its active, leading element. On this basis Xi and Fu hold that the two are internally unified, and they say this overcomes the Western "dualism" of state versus society. They also argue that the relationship is mediated by the basic social contradictions: social development determines the governance system and policy direction, while governance acts back on the superstructure, then on the economic base, then on the productive forces.

The authors treat the degree of fit as an indicator of Chinese modernization that moves through exploration and uneven progress, tied to the Party's century-long record. In their reading, the Two Integrations appear twice: in practice, such as building a high-standard socialist market economy and developing new quality productive forces, and in roots in socialism with Chinese characteristics and traditional Chinese political culture. They contend that, unlike in the West, neither state nor society has been alienated by capital expansion in China. They conclude that the formula scientifically sums up the driving force and institutional guarantee of Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want to see how Party theorists place governance within the historical-materialist scheme of basic contradictions.
quoteEn: The fit between state governance and social development involves a dynamic process of continual exploration and winding ascent.
quoteZh: 国家治理和社会发展之间的适应存在着一个不断探索、曲折上升的动态发展过程。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, set out in the 20th Party Congress (2022) and presented as distinct from Western models.
Formula for combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture, promoted under Xi Jinping.
Official guiding concept of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, put forward in 2015.
A concept promoted since 2023 for productivity growth driven by technological innovation and emerging industries.
Official term for the system of state institutions and the capacity to run them. It was foregrounded in the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013).

glossary.en: the five spheres of the overall plan
glossary.explanation: The Party's overall plan for economic, political, cultural, social and ecological advancement.

t: Party Leadership Group of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences conveys and studies the spirit of the national Two Sessions
zh: 中共中国社会科学院党组传达学习全国两会精神
paras: This is a short news report from Chinese Social Sciences Net on an enlarged meeting of the Party Leadership Group of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (CASS), held on 12 March 2025. The meeting conveyed and studied General Secretary Xi Jinping's speeches during the national Two Sessions and the spirit of the sessions, and planned how to put them into practice.

The meeting was chaired by CASS President and Party Leadership Group Secretary Gao Xiang, who also spoke. Vice-presidents Peng Jinhui, Zhen Zhanmin and Zhao Rui, discipline inspection team head Hang Yuanxiang and Secretary-General Zhao Zhimin attended, along with the deputy secretary-general and heads of CASS units.

According to the report, the meeting judged this year's Two Sessions especially significant because they fall at the end of the 14th Five-Year Plan and the start of planning for the 15th. It said they bear on implementing the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), deepening reform and advancing Chinese modernization. Gao stressed that CASS is a political organ centred on research. He called for deeper understanding of the Two Establishes, support for the Two Upholds and the Four-sphere Confidence, and a lead role in studying Xi's speeches. He also asked for better research on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, reform of institutions, training of talent, and stronger conversion of research results into practice.

The meeting concluded that studying the Two Sessions is a major political task for CASS now and for some time ahead. It called for consolidating the Academy's political-development framework of "three consensuses, three commitments and three measures", and for a wave of study and publicity, so as to drive high-quality development at CASS. Read the original if you want a brief record of how CASS leadership formally frames its political tasks and institutional priorities after the 2025 Two Sessions.
quoteEn: The Chinese Academy of Social Sciences is a political organ whose central work is scientific research.
quoteZh: 中国社会科学院是以科研为中心工作的政治机关

glossary.explanation: The annual plenary sessions of the National People's Congress and the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, held together each March.
A Party formula, adopted in 2022, affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party formula requiring members to uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the Central Committee's authority and unified leadership.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official development goal emphasising quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.

t: Advancing the Party's self-reform through the building of intra-Party regulations
zh: 以党内法规制度建设推进党的自我革命
paras: Jiang Xueyi and Chen Jinzhao, writing in a Chinese Social Sciences Today commentary of March 2025, ask what role intra-Party regulations play in the Communist Party's self-reform. They argue that building such regulations is both a support and a guarantee for deepening the Party's self-reform. They treat it as an important measure for achieving that goal.

The piece has two parts. The first sets out why regulation-building is a key link. The second sets out specific measures. It draws on the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), the 20th Party Congress report, and recent documents such as the 2023–2027 planning outline for central Party regulations.

On the first part, the authors say intra-Party regulations form the core of the institutional system for self-reform. They contend that these regulations underpin full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and anti-corruption work, and that they improve the quality and effectiveness of the Party's self-supervision. As evidence they cite the revised disciplinary punishment regulations (January 2024), the Party discipline study campaign (April–July 2024) and the revised inspection regulations (February 2024). On measures, they call for continuous improvement of the regulatory system, better quality in rule-making, abolition of outdated rules, and fewer declaratory or merely guiding rules. They also want regulations to make Party leadership more scientific and standardised. Finally, they urge linking correction of the "four undesirable work styles" with discipline and anti-corruption, since corruption often hides in such problems and early-stage work relies on Party rules rather than state law.

The authors conclude that self-reform has run through the Party's history and is the basis of its historical initiative. They call for governing the Party by institutions and regulations, and for a virtuous cycle in which the Party uses its own strength to find problems, correct deviations and raise governing capacity. Read the original if you want a short, official-line account of how Chinese legal scholars link intra-Party regulations to self-reform and anti-corruption.
quoteEn: Building the system of intra-Party regulations is a support and guarantee for deepening the Party's self-reform, and an important measure for achieving it.
quoteZh: 党内法规制度建设，是深入推进党的自我革命的支撑与保障，是实现党的自我革命的重要举措。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed under Xi Jinping: the Party's capacity to purge, correct and improve itself without outside pressure. It is presented as the Party's answer to the question of how to escape the historical cycle of rise and decline.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party-discipline and anti-corruption drive launched after the 18th Party Congress (2012).
Formal rules made by the Party's central bodies to govern Party organisations and members. They are distinct from state law.
Formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance. They were targeted by the 2012 Eight-point Regulation and later campaigns.

t: Understanding the two dimensions of the anti-corruption struggle
st: Historical vision and strategic height
zh: 认识反腐败斗争的双重维度
paras: Zhu Jie's commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today newspaper in March 2025, asks how the significance of the anti-corruption struggle should be understood as the Party pursues further comprehensively deepening reform and Chinese modernization. Taking its cue from Xi Jinping's remarks at the Fourth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection (2025), Zhu argues that the struggle must be viewed with a "historical vision" and from a "strategic height", tied to the Party's mission and tasks. On this reading, such a view strengthens the Party's resolve to see the struggle through to the end.

The article has three parts. The first treats historical vision and strategic height as two methods for judging the "time" and the "trend" of the struggle. The second examines Xi's formulation of the "two historical initiatives" won through full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. The third sets out the dialectical relationship between anti-corruption work and further comprehensively deepening reform, and ends with practical implications.

Zhu says that questions have arisen about how long the struggle will last and whether it will cool down, and that these call for a scientific method. A historical vision places the struggle within the history of the Party, the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and the rise and fall of socialist states. The "two historical initiatives" are, in Xi's words, keeping the Party from changing in nature, colour or flavour, and uniting the people behind national rejuvenation. Zhu links them to lessons from the ruling parties of some socialist states, citing Marx and Lenin on discipline and corruption. A strategic height, in turn, treats anti-corruption work and reform as aligned in goals and coherent in logic: stricter standards empower reform, while reform spirit and institution-building raise governance capacity. Zhu stresses that the two are not in a zero-sum or opposing relationship.

Zhu concludes that the struggle is neither temporary nor static, and must be upgraded as reform proceeds. The article calls for clearing existing corruption while curbing new cases, removing the soil in which corruption grows, making political supervision concrete and routine, reducing formalism at the grassroots, improving Party regulations and national anti-corruption legislation, and building a disciplined and law-governed discipline inspection and supervision force. Read the original if you want an example of how a legal scholar in the Party-building field presents the official rationale for continuing the anti-corruption campaign alongside the reform agenda.
quoteEn: The logical coherence between the anti-corruption struggle and further comprehensively deepening reform reflects the necessity of governing the Party with a reform spirit and strict standards, and shows that the two are not in a zero-sum relationship, still less in opposition.
quoteZh: 反腐败斗争和进一步全面深化改革在逻辑上的融贯性，体现了坚持以改革精神和严的标准管党治党的必要性和必然性，表明反腐败斗争同进一步全面深化改革不是此消彼长的关系，更不是对立关系

glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: A Party-building policy line promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012), stressing strict discipline, supervision and anti-corruption work within the Party.
The official name for the Party's development path and goals, presented as distinct from Western modernization.

glossary.literal: two historical initiatives (seizing the initiative of history)
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's 2025 formulation of what anti-corruption work has secured: keeping the Party from changing in nature, and the Party's ability to unite the people for national rejuvenation.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central goal of the Party's national narrative since the early 2010s, referring to restoring China's strength and international standing by mid-century.

t: On the determination and attribution of Party discipline responsibility
zh: 论党纪责任的认定与归结
paras: Between a disciplinary violation and a punishment lies the question of responsibility. Zhu Linfang argues that, as Party disciplinary practice has matured, "Party discipline responsibility" has separated out from "violation" and "sanction" to become an independent normative element, which makes its determination and attribution the key step in handling disciplinary cases. The article notes that no systematic theory yet exists on this, and that arbitrary enforcement and over-broad accountability are linked to the lack of a unified mechanism for attributing responsibility.

Working from a normative-science perspective, Zhu traces the revisions of the Regulations on Disciplinary Actions of the Communist Party of China (1997 trial version, 2003, 2015, 2018 and the current text) and draws on enforcement experience. The article has three parts: the place of responsibility within the constitution of a violation; the basic elements by which responsibility is determined; and proposals for improving the mechanism.

Zhu's central move is to show that the older "four-element theory", modelled on criminal law, has given way to a "two-tier system" of "objective rule-breaking plus subjective culpability", in which culpability is judged only after a violation is found. The Regulations now contain four elements: capacity for responsibility as the basis, subjective fault (intent or negligence, via Article 19) as the content, force majeure and similar grounds as exclusions, and proportionality between fault and punishment. Zhu reads this as Party discipline's acceptance of the "principle of responsibility" already found in criminal and administrative sanctions. Zhu then proposes presuming fault, so that a Party member whose conduct caused loss must show absence of fault. Zhu also calls for defined standards and types of duty of care, set through guiding cases. Proportionality should be applied systematically, citing cases of over-punishment of trivial conduct and a drink-driving inconsistency. The "etc." in "force majeure and other causes" should be read as open-ended, with caution. "No Party discipline responsibility" should be read narrowly as excluding formal sanctions but not non-sanction measures such as warning education or organisational adjustment.

Zhu concludes that the Regulations have established the basic elements of responsibility, but that how fault is determined, how duty of care is set, how proportionality is applied, what other exclusions exist and what the exemption clause covers all remain without settled rules. Zhu calls for further clarification through interpretation, guiding cases and typology, so as to build a more scientific mechanism. Read the original if you study Party discipline regulation, or the borrowing of criminal-law doctrines such as culpability and duty of care into intra-Party rules, and want the detailed argument and cited cases.
quoteEn: Party discipline responsibility is an indispensable element of a disciplinary violation; only when its existence has been confirmed through determination and attribution does a Party disciplinary sanction have a legitimate basis.
quoteZh: 党纪责任是违纪构成的必备要素，只有经党纪责任的认定与归结之后确认存在党纪责任，党纪处分才具有正当性依据。

glossary.explanation: The responsibility a Party organisation or member bears for a violation of Party discipline. The article treats it as a distinct element between the violation and the sanction.

glossary.zh: 中国共产党纪律处分条例
glossary.en: Regulations on Disciplinary Actions of the Communist Party of China
glossary.explanation: The core intra-Party regulation setting out disciplinary violations and sanctions. It was first issued in trial form in 1997 and revised in 2003, 2015, 2018 and later.

A theory of what constitutes a violation, requiring first objective rule-breaking and then subjective culpability. It was proposed in a 2020 research project of the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and National Supervisory Commission.
A legal concept for events that cannot be foreseen, avoided or overcome. Article 19 of the Regulations uses it as a ground for not pursuing disciplinary responsibility.
The principle that the severity of a sanction should match the fault. The article notes it appears in both the Regulations and the Accountability Regulations.
Measures such as criticism, talks, public notification, suspension or job adjustment. The article says they are not primarily punitive and sit alongside formal Party sanctions.

t: General Secretary Xi Jinping's important thinking on Party building: current state of research and outlook
zh: “习近平总书记关于党的建设的重要思想”研究现状分析与展望
paras: This article is a literature review of Chinese scholarship on "General Secretary Xi Jinping's important thinking on Party building". The concept was formally put forward at the National Organization Work Conference in Beijing in June 2023, which summarised its core content in the "thirteen upholds". Chen Jinlong surveys the research produced since then and argues that it has advanced considerably but still has substantial room to grow.

The review covers five clusters of work: the grounds on which the thinking took shape, its content system, its theoretical characteristics, its value and significance, and its practical requirements. It then identifies three features of the scholarship and closes with three directions for future research. The article appeared in the journal Party Building in 2025.

On the grounds of formation, Chen reports that scholars point to four dimensions: history (traditional Chinese culture and the Party's tradition of strict self-governance), reality, theory (the inheritance and development of Marxist Party-building theory) and practice. Some add a subjective condition, namely Xi's own experience and abilities. On content, researchers describe an organic whole built around full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, with its methodology and original contributions. Its characteristics are said to be originality, systematic coherence, scientific character, a people-centred orientation and practicality. Practical requirements discussed include upholding the Party's overall leadership, using the Party's self-reform to guide social revolution, and building a high-quality cadre force.

Chen finds the scholarship marked by a union of political and scholarly approaches, of historical and contemporary study, and of theoretical exposition and practical pathways. The author nonetheless sees gaps: research mostly elaborates the "thirteen upholds" and pays too little attention to the underlying texts, uses fairly traditional methods, and has not linked the thinking enough to other parts of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Chen calls for a return to the texts, multidisciplinary work including big-data methods, and a wider global view of the thinking's meaning for building a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a brief map of how Chinese academics currently frame and study Xi's Party-building thought, and of where the author thinks research should go next.
quoteEn: Academic research on General Secretary Xi Jinping's important thinking on Party building combines the political with the scholarly, historical with contemporary study, and the exposition of its theoretical system with the exploration of practical pathways.
quoteZh: 学术界对习近平总书记关于党的建设的重要思想的研究，具有政治性与学理性相结合、历史研究与现实研究相结合、理论体系阐释与实践路径探索相结合的特点。

Official concept that the Party must continually rectify itself. It is presented as the "second answer" to the historical cycle of rise and decline.
The list of thirteen principles adopted at the 2023 National Organization Work Conference to summarise the core content of Xi's thinking on Party building.

glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng

t: Two key focal points for improving the Party's institutions and mechanisms of Party building
zh: 深刻把握完善党的建设制度机制的两个着力点
source: Qianxian (Frontline), 2025 no. 3, excerpt from 'Deepening reform of the Party-building system'
paras: This short commentary, excerpted from a longer piece in Qianxian (2025, no. 3), asks how the Party should deepen reform of its Party-building system. Kang and Tang argue that the decisive focal point is mobilising the enthusiasm, initiative and creativity of the whole Party to drive reform and development. They present this as the basic purpose of institutional reform: upholding and strengthening Party leadership.

The authors start from the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization. They read its Party-building provisions as continuous with the general requirements for Party building in the new era. The article then develops the point in two directions: the morale of Party members and cadres, and the social environment for reform.

First, Kang and Tang hold that, with the world undergoing changes unseen in a century and reform in a critical stage, cadres must show courage and reject passivity, evasion and slackness. Second, they argue that mobilising the Party's more than 99 million members will let the Party unite over 1.4 billion people, so reform must rely on the people. In their account, this requires respecting the people's principal position and creativity, listening to the public, and collecting and summing up fresh popular experience.

The authors conclude that cadres and the public should understand the complexity and difficulty of reform and handle adjustments of interests correctly, creating an atmosphere of understanding, support and participation. They describe Party building as a way to keep the Party vital, with the Party's self-reform leading social revolution. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party School scholars explain the Third Plenum's Party-building provisions.
quoteEn: When the enthusiasm, initiative and creativity of more than 99 million Party members are fully mobilised, our Party can unite over 1.4 billion Chinese people and forge an invincible Chinese strength.
quoteZh: 当9900多万党员的积极性、主动性、创造性充分调动起来，我们党就能团结起14亿多中国人民，锻造无坚不摧、无往不胜的中国力量。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's account of China's development path, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official concept for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself, often presented as the way to prevent loss of vitality in long-term rule.

t: Using "investing in people" to unblock the circulation of the national economy
zh: 以“投资于人”畅通国民经济循环
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in March 2025, Wang Zanxin takes up "investing in people", a phrase that drew wide attention during that year's National People's Congress and Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference sessions. Wang argues that the main macroeconomic problem is poor circulation of the national economy, and that investment in people should become the strategic fulcrum for unblocking it. This is to be done by combining it closely with "investing in things", not by replacing the latter.
