Read the original if you want a detailed, document-by-document chronology of how this Party term was built, or if you study Xi Jinping Thought on Culture and Chinese foreign-policy discourse.
quoteEn: The developmental history of the concept of "exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations" concentrates the Party's wisdom in answering the questions of the times, responding to changes unseen in a century, and advancing the development of civilization.
quoteZh: “文明交流互鉴”概念的发展史，集中彰显了中国共产党破解时代之问、回应百年变局、推动文明发展的政党智慧。

glossary.en: exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations
glossary.explanation: A Party formula for Chinese civilizational outlook, stressing that civilizations should interact and learn from one another on an equal footing. It is often used in diplomacy and cultural policy.
A body of ideas on culture, ideology and civilization attributed to Xi Jinping and promoted as a component of Xi Jinping Thought since 2023.
The Party's term for China's own path of modernization, presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012–13, calling for shared global governance and common interests.
An initiative proposed by Xi Jinping in 2023 promoting respect for civilizational diversity, common values and cultural exchange.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China in 1978.

t: The threefold logic of the Communist Party of China's self-reform
zh: 中国共产党自我革命的三重逻辑
paras: Why does the Communist Party of China show a distinctive capacity for self-reform? Writing after Xi Jinping's speech at the Third Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection, which set out "nine requirements" for advancing the Party's self-reform, He argues that this capacity rests on three mutually supporting logics: theoretical, historical and practical.

The short commentary takes each logic in turn. The theoretical section looks to Marxist doctrine on party building, the historical section to episodes from 1921 onwards, and the practical section to the challenges and measures of the new era since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

On theory, He holds that although the Marxist classics never used the term, the idea is embedded in their work. The author points to Marx's call for ruthless criticism of everything existing, to the Communist Manifesto's account of communists as having no interests apart from the proletariat as a whole, and to communism as a long revolutionary movement needing successive generations. On history, He cites the August 7th Meeting of 1927, the Zunyi Meeting of 1935, the Yan'an-era rectification campaign and the 1978 debate on practice as the criterion of truth as moments of self-correction. On practice, the author names problems of unbalanced development, state governance and impurities within the Party, and credits the eight-point rules, intra-Party education campaigns, revised Party regulations and the "three no-corruptions" approach.

He concludes that self-reform is an internally grounded and conscious choice, and that the demands of building a strong country and national rejuvenation require the Party to continue it in the spirit of serving the people. Read the original if you want a compact statement of how Party theorists present the roots of self-reform in Marxist theory, Party history and current practice.
quoteEn: Only by persisting in self-reform, tempering its character and holding firm revolutionary will and belief can a proletarian party avoid losing its convictions, fighting spirit and revolutionary spirit on the long road to this goal.
quoteZh: 无产阶级政党只有坚持自我革命，砥砺品格，具备坚定的革命意志和革命信仰，才不会在实现这一目标的漫长道路中迷失信念，丧失革命斗志和革命精神

glossary.explanation: A term Xi Jinping first used in 2015 for the Party's capacity to criticise, correct and renew itself. It is presented as a defining trait of the CPC.
Rules issued by the Party Central Committee in December 2012 to curb formalism, bureaucracy and extravagance among officials.
An anti-corruption formula: officials should be unable, unwilling and unable to dare to be corrupt, combining deterrence, institutional constraint and ideological education.

glossary.literal: rectifying the style of work movement
glossary.explanation: A Party-wide campaign launched in Yan'an in the 1940s to correct subjectivism, sectarianism and formulaic writing, under the principle of learning from past mistakes to avoid future ones.

t: The innovative role of the Third Party Congress in the development of the National Congress system of the Communist Party of China
zh: 党的三大对全国党代会制度发展的创新作用
source: Journal of China Jinggangshan Cadre Institute, 2024 no. 2
paras: Yang Kai asks what the Third National Congress of the Communist Party of China (1923, held in Guangzhou) contributed to the development of the Party's national congress system. The author argues that, although scholarship has mostly stressed the Third Congress's role in the united front, its institutional innovations were equally significant. Yang identifies three: a transition in delegate selection from appointment to democratic election, the practice of unifying thinking before the congress, and new features of the agenda.

The article places the Third Congress within the sequence of congresses from the First to the Seventh. It opens with a survey showing that research on the Third Congress is thin. By the author's account, a search of the National Social Science Fund database found no funded project on it, and a CNKI search returned only 186, 3 and 1 results for different keyword formulations. The three main sections draw on delegates' memoirs (Luo Zhanglong, Xu Meikun, Zhang Guotao, Liu Renjing and others), Maring's reports and the text of the Party constitution.

On delegates, Yang shows that the First and Second Congresses relied on regional dispatch or designation. For the Third Congress, regional committees held nomination and discussion procedures, although practice varied. Some delegates were elected and others designated, so Yang calls it a transitional case. On preparation, the Third Congress was the first to hold a preparatory meeting and to draft its main resolutions and reports beforehand after consulting Party organisations. Yang says later congresses continued both practices. On the agenda, it was the first to amend the Party constitution, adding provisions on probationary membership, two sponsors for each applicant and lower-level approval of admissions. It also elected a new Central Executive Committee after canvassing delegates. Yang cites the earliest surviving vote tally, a younger leadership and the first industrial workers among its members.

Yang concludes that the Third Congress set precedents that later congresses inherited. The author argues that research should look at causes and at process, and at both larger and smaller processes. Larger processes would place a single congress in the whole sequence leading to the Seventh Congress, the most mature by Yang's account. Smaller ones would examine how a single congress was convened, drafted and decided. Read the original if you study early Party institutions and want a source-based account of delegate selection, pre-congress preparation and constitutional revision in 1923.
quoteEn: The Third Congress's innovation in elections lay in comprehensively strengthening the consideration given to members of the new leading body, so that the leadership as a whole would be more representative and more capable of leading.
quoteZh: 党的三大对于选举方面的创新在于全面加强对新的领导机构成员的考量，使领导机构整体更有代表性更有领导力量。

glossary.explanation: The Party's highest organ under its constitution, which is convened periodically to set the line, amend the constitution and elect the Central Committee. The article treats the rules governing it as a basic Party institution.
The 1923 Congress held in Guangzhou, which endorsed cooperation between the Communist Party and the Kuomintang. It also revised the Party constitution for the first time.
The Party's policy of building alliances with other political forces. In 1923 it meant cooperation with the Kuomintang.
The central leading body elected by the Second to Fourth Congresses. Its name later changed to the Central Committee.
A meeting held before a congress opens to exchange views, settle delegates and discuss draft documents. The article says the Third Congress began this practice.

t: The generative logic of the Communist Party of China's conception of civilization
zh: 中国共产党文明观的生成逻辑
source: Social Sciences in China (Zhongguo shehui kexue), 2024 no. 10
paras: Zhang Bo asks how the Communist Party of China's conception of civilization came about and what it consists of. The article argues that this conception, guided by Marxism and rooted in Chinese tradition, goes beyond Western theories of civilizational superiority and of a clash of civilizations. In Zhang's account, it offers a theoretical guide for building a modern Chinese civilization and a new form of human civilization.

The article is organised in three parts. The first sets out the conception's core meaning in six features: it is people-centred, socialist, scientific, constantly innovating, "harmony in diversity", and world-minded. The second identifies four formative conditions: Marxist theory, traditional Chinese thought, over a century of Party practice from the new-democratic revolution to the new era, and the Party's sense of cultural mission. The third describes the system's four dimensions: civilizational critique, values, construction and governance.

Zhang's central move is to trace the conception to two sources. From Marx and Engels it draws theories of the nature, forms, structure, driving forces and subjects of civilization. From Chinese tradition it draws harmony between humanity and nature, the idea of "all under heaven", "harmony in diversity" and a benevolent moral outlook. Zhang then argues that the Party fused these in practice. It criticised both wholesale Westernisation and wholesale restoration of the past, and it developed the "five-sphere" model of material, political, spiritual, social and ecological civilization. It also asserts that civilizations are equal in value and puts the people before capital.

Zhang concludes that the conception is theoretically deep, practically grounded and marked by the Party's initiative, and that it benefits the world as well as China. It is presented as a response to the question of where human civilization is heading. It is said to point towards inclusive thinking, dialogue between civilizations and a vision of "each appreciating the beauty of others". Read the original if you want a systematic, Party-theoretical account of how Chinese official discourse on civilization is derived from Marxism, tradition and Party history, with extensive references to Xi Jinping's statements.
quoteEn: That civilizations are equal in value is the concentrated expression of the Communist Party of China's conception of civilization in the dimension of civilizational values.
quoteZh: 文明在价值上是平等的，这是中国共产党文明观在文明价值向度上的集中表达。

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: A phrase used in Party discourse for the civilization said to be created through Chinese modernization, which is presented as socialist and as an alternative to the Western capitalist model.

glossary.literal: modern civilization of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A goal set out in Xi Jinping's 2023 remarks on culture. It refers to a modern civilization that combines Marxism with the best of traditional Chinese culture.
The Party's overall framework of economic, political, cultural, social and ecological development. The article renders it as material, political, spiritual, social and ecological civilization.
A classical Chinese maxim meaning to live in harmony while respecting differences. The Party uses it to express its stance on relations between civilizations.

t: The three historical dimensions of the normativity of intra-Party regulations
zh: 党内法规规范性历史渊源的三重维度
paras: Where does the normativity of intra-Party regulations come from? Li Jinheng takes up what the article calls one of the "meta-questions" of research on these rules: why they can legitimately guide, evaluate, constrain and even discipline Party members. Li argues that existing work, which approaches the question through legal studies and political party research, does not cover the whole field. The article proposes three historical dimensions: the history of ideas, the history of practice and the history of civilization.

This short commentary appeared in the China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao) on 27 February 2025. It places intra-Party regulations within the Marxist theory of the political party, the Chinese Communist Party's own record of institution-building across revolution, construction and reform, and the long Chinese tradition of good law and good governance. Each dimension has its own section, followed by a brief closing paragraph.

On the history of ideas, Li holds that intra-Party regulations are the product of a stage in the development of Marxist party theory and of the proletarian revolution. This explains why they exist relatively independently of state law: a revolutionary organisation needs no state "permission" for its internal rules. It also explains why they are stricter than state law, since members carry higher duties than ordinary citizens and need binding external discipline as well as self-conscious Party spirit. On the history of practice, Li says that regulations, whether imported through the Comintern or originating in China, must pass through a process of "canonisation" that turns responses to specific problems into lasting norms. Since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the Party's self-reform has driven the systematic construction of the regulations. On the history of civilization, Li draws four lessons from traditional governance: the blending of ritual and law, "clear virtue and cautious punishment", "inner sageliness and outer kingliness", and "the people as the root of the state".

Li concludes that the normativity of intra-Party regulations must be explained historically, by showing how the rules were generated and standardised in the Party's own construction and practice. Li also locates their foundation in the transition of Chinese political civilization from tradition to modernity. The article adds that the Party's self-reform in the new era requires understanding the complex changes affecting full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Read the original if you want a compact statement of how Chinese Party-law scholars frame the sources of intra-Party regulations beyond a purely legal analysis.
quoteEn: The normativity of intra-Party regulations derives from the Chinese Communist Party's contemporary innovation upon traditional experience of good law and good governance.
quoteZh: 党内法规规范性来源于中国共产党对传统良法善治经验进行的时代创新。

glossary.explanation: The body of formal rules the Chinese Communist Party issues to govern its own organisation and members. They are treated as part of the Party's system of rule-based self-governance and as linked to, but distinct from, state law.
An official term for the Party's efforts to correct itself and maintain discipline without external pressure. It is used prominently since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official slogan for the strict, comprehensive approach to Party discipline and construction promoted since 2012.
A phrase combining just laws with effective governance. It is used in contemporary Chinese legal discourse and traced by the author to classical Chinese political thought.

t: Fully grasping the requirements of our times for Party discipline building
zh: 全面把握党的纪律建设时代要求
paras: This commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in February 2025, asks how Party discipline building should keep pace with the tasks set by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called for further deepening reform and advancing Chinese modernization. Wang argues that keeping discipline abreast of the times is a requirement for deepening institutional reform of Party building and keeping reform on the right political course.

The article describes discipline building as a prominent feature of the overall plan for Party building in the new era. It then sets out four areas of emphasis: political discipline, the Party's central tasks,主体 responsibility for Party governance, and consolidating the results of the Party discipline study and education campaign.

Wang contends that political discipline is the core of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and the mark distinguishing Marxist parties from others. Its core content is the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, and it should lead the other disciplines: organisational, integrity, mass, work and lifestyle. The author presents the new Central Committee implementing measures on the "four forms" of supervision and discipline as an institutional achievement. Wang also says some officials still misjudge the long-term nature of the task. In the author's account, "key minority" corruption and the "four undesirable work styles" persist, so Party committees and their secretaries must carry primary responsibility.

Wang calls for stronger supervision of leading cadres, especially top officials, with no privileges or exceptions in applying discipline. The author also proposes turning the results of the discipline education campaign into regular, lasting study mechanisms, and into officials' everyday habits. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line statement of current priorities in Party discipline building.
quoteEn: Keeping Party discipline building abreast of the times means always strengthening it around the Party's historical mission and central tasks, and working to enhance the scientific soundness, rationality and authority of the system.
quoteZh: 党的纪律建设的与时俱进,就是要始终紧紧围绕党的历史使命和中心任务加强党的纪律建设,着力增强制度的科学性、合理性、权威性。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Official slogan since 2014 for a campaign of tighter Party discipline, anti-corruption work and internal regulation under Xi Jinping.
Formula from the 2022 Party resolution affirming Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
Official requirement that Party members uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the Central Committee's authority and unified leadership.
Official term for China's development path, presented by the Party as distinct from Western models of modernization.
Party discipline framework graded by severity: criticism and warnings as the norm, then light and heavy sanctions, then serious violations referred for investigation.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Using Party building to lead the protection and transmission of rural intangible cultural heritage
zh: 以党建引领乡村非物质文化遗产保护传承工作
paras: This short commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Journal in February 2025, asks how rural intangible cultural heritage can be protected and passed on under present conditions. Han argues that Party building should lead the work, with Party organisations at county, township and village levels providing motivation, organisation and a means of action.

Han first defines rural intangible heritage as cultural forms handed down by villagers over generations, together with related tools, objects and sites. The author names two features: strong regional markers and a reflection of peasants' aesthetic tastes. Han then lists the pressures it faces, including urbanisation, the outflow of young labour, weak awareness, a gap in successors and falling peasant participation. The remainder is organised around three kinds of leadership: ideological, organisational and action-based.

On ideology, Han calls for Party organisations to study Xi Jinping's thought on culture, treat heritage as a political responsibility, and train cadres and members to act as exemplars. On organisation, Han proposes cultivating successors, including returning graduates and outside specialists, and building village cultural councils and associations based on new-era civilisation practice stations. On action, Han suggests converting heritage into products and brands to form cultural new quality productive forces, integrating it with rural tourism and cultural IP, and buying heritage performances as free public cultural services.

Han concludes that Party-building leadership is the engine of high-quality development for rural heritage. The author presents the process as the Party putting the people at the centre, upholding its cultural leadership and promoting common prosperity in peasants' spiritual life. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-building language is applied to rural cultural policy.
quoteEn: Party-building leadership is the engine driving the high-quality development of rural intangible cultural heritage, injecting momentum into its protection and transmission, providing carriers for it and exploring new paths.
quoteZh: 党建引领是推动乡村非遗文化高质量发展的引擎，能为其保护传承注入动能、提供载体并探索新路径。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for growth driven by innovation and technology rather than resource-intensive input. Here the author applies it to the commercial use of cultural heritage.
An official goal, prominent since 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to growth stressing quality, efficiency and innovation.
An official goal of prosperity shared across society. Here the author extends it to the "spiritual life" of peasants.

t: Centralised and unified leadership of the Party Central Committee as the fundamental guarantee for doing economic work well
zh: 党中央集中统一领导是做好经济工作的根本保证
paras: This commentary takes its starting point from Xi Jinping's speech at the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference, which called centralised and unified leadership by the Party Central Committee "the fundamental guarantee for doing economic work well". Yang Ming argues that this is a law-like insight drawn from economic practice since the 18th Party Congress (2012), and that it points the way to completing the targets of the 14th Five-Year Plan and making a good start on the 15th.

The article has three parts. The first explains why the principle holds, drawing on the experience of the new era, the need to secure the right direction of economic development, and the role of the Party in resisting risks and challenges. The second sets out how the Party's capacity to lead economic work can be strengthened. The third turns to practical requirements for the coming year.

Yang's core argument is that the Party leads economic work as its central task, so the Central Committee must bear overall responsibility. In the author's account, the 2019 to 2023 economic work conferences repeatedly reaffirmed this principle. Yang describes the economy as a huge ship that needs steering as it grows, and says the authority of the Central Committee is what lets the whole country act as "one chessboard" and follow one blueprint. The second part urges leading cadres to work with political awareness, scientific method, rule-of-law thinking and professional skill. It also presents the five "must balance" relationships from the 2024 conference: an efficient market and a capable government, aggregate supply and demand, nurturing new and updating old growth drivers, improving the incremental and revitalising the existing, and raising quality while expanding quantity. The author also points to institutional arrangements such as the Politburo Standing Committee, the Central Financial and Economic Affairs Commission and the Central Commission for Deepening Overall Reform.

For the year ahead, Yang calls for keeping to the general principle of seeking progress while maintaining stability, concentrating on key tasks (placing boosting consumption and expanding domestic demand first), and uniting efforts for high-quality development. Yang also calls for guarding against Central Committee decisions being emptied out through documents and meetings, and for judging officials by real results. Read the original if you want to see how Party-theoretical commentary links Xi Jinping's economic thought, the 2024 economic work conference and the Party's leadership system into one argument for centralised leadership.
quoteEn: To strengthen the Party's overall leadership of economic work and bring its core leadership role into full play, the most crucial point is to uphold the authority of the Party Central Committee and its centralised, unified leadership.
quoteZh: 加强党对经济工作的全面领导，发挥好党的领导核心作用，最关键的一条就是要维护党中央权威和集中统一领导。

glossary.explanation: An official formulation since about 2017 that replaces a focus on growth speed with quality, efficiency and sustainability. It is now described as the primary task of economic work.
The Party and state leadership's annual meeting, usually held in December, which assesses the economy and sets the economic tasks for the next year.
The official general principle for economic work since 2012. It combines stable macroeconomic conditions with reform and structural adjustment.

t: The centralised and unified leadership of the Party Central Committee is the fundamental guarantee for doing economic work well
zh: 党中央集中统一领导是做好经济工作的根本保证
source: New Xiang Review (Xin Xiang Pinglun), 2025 no. 1
paras: Taking its cue from the Central Economic Work Conference of 11–12 December 2024, this commentary examines Xi Jinping's statement that the centralised and unified leadership of the Party Central Committee is the fundamental guarantee for doing economic work well. Zhu Ying and Gong Yun argue that this is the first of the thirteen basic components of Xi Jinping's economic thought and has a guiding role within it. Their thesis is that Party leadership over economic work is both a historical lesson and a theoretical necessity.

The article has two analytical parts and a practical one. The first sets out why centralised leadership matters, through a survey of the Party's record from the New Democratic Revolution to the new era, and through the claims that it keeps the economy on a socialist course and is the main defence against major risks. The second explains the theoretical meaning of the principle by drawing on historical materialism, Lenin and the Communist Manifesto. The third lists concrete paths for implementation.

The authors' central move is to derive Party leadership from the dialectic of economic base and superstructure. Citing Lenin, they hold that classes are led by parties and can act with a unified will only under their own party. The Communist Party, as a proletarian vanguard representing the great majority, must therefore lead the economy to serve its economic base. They add that public ownership as the mainstay and common prosperity define the socialist market economy, and that only Party leadership keeps it on course. They present the external setting as a world undergoing great changes unseen in a century, with domestic demand weak and protectionism, unilateralism and de-globalisation rising.

For practice, the authors call for three things. Party members must uphold the Central Committee's authority through the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds. Cadres must raise their capacity by studying Marxist political economy and Xi Jinping's economic thought, by investigating conditions, by punishing corruption and formalism, and by making decisions scientific and law-based. Institutions must also be improved, including the Central Financial and Economic Affairs Commission, the annual economic work conference, local implementation of central policy, and the Third Plenum's reforms. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official rationale linking Party leadership to economic governance in the Xi era.
quoteEn: The emergence of the proletarian party is a product of the contradictory movement between politics and economics. Only by leading the economy can a party better serve its economic base.
quoteZh: 无产阶级政党的产生是政治与经济矛盾运动的产物。政党只有领导经济才能更好地服务于它的经济基础。

glossary.explanation: An annual closed-door meeting of the top Party and state leadership, usually held in December. It reviews the year's economy and sets priorities for the next.
A formula adopted in 2022 affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and the whole Party, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.
A goal of shared affluence for all, presented in official discourse as an essential requirement of socialism and prominent under Xi Jinping.

glossary.zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.explanation: The system adopted in the early 1990s, combining market mechanisms with public ownership as the mainstay and Party leadership.

t: Holding great assemblies in the Yan'an period
zh: 延安时期开大会
paras: This short commentary, published in Jiefang Daily, looks at the large assemblies held in the Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia Border Region during the Yan'an period. The authors argue that these meetings, each focused on a distinct theme, fixed work priorities, allowed policy to be made soundly, mobilised people and resources, unified thinking and advanced the revolution.

The article covers three kinds of gathering: the border region's councils and its production-mobilisation meetings; the 1944 culture and education conference; and the 1942 Yan'an Forum on Literature and Art. It ends with a short statement of what these assemblies offer later revolution and construction.

On the councils, the authors describe the three-tier system of border region, county and township and the powers set out in the 1939 organisational regulations. They note that the 1941 revision added powers, such as removing senior officials, and enlarged the county council's powers from eight items to eleven. They present production mobilisation as Mao Zedong's answer to fiscal strain after 1939: 'starve, disband, or do it ourselves?' On culture and education, they summarise the 1944 resolution on wall newspapers, literacy for ancillary staff and mass entertainment. For the Yan'an Forum, they set out Mao's three points: literature and art are part of the revolutionary cause, writers must take the standpoint of the people, and popularisation guides the direction of art.

The authors conclude that the assemblies yield lessons for later practice. These include uniting Party leadership with a people-centred approach, consulting the people, protecting democratic rights through institutions and law, and embedding consultative democracy in elections, decision-making, management and oversight. Read the original if you want a concise, officially framed overview of Yan'an-era councils, conferences and the Yan'an Forum and how they are used in current Party history writing.
quoteEn: To continue the War of Resistance, the manpower and material resources of all China must be mobilised.
quoteZh: 要继续抗战,就需要动员全中国的人力物力。

glossary.explanation: Elected representative bodies at border region, county and township level in the Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia Border Region, set up under the united front against Japan.

keywords: Yan'an Forum on Literature and Art

t: The historical contribution of the Fourth Party Congress of the CPC to Party organisational building
zh: 中共四大对党的组织建设的历史贡献
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in February 2025, Li Chuanbing asks what the Fourth National Congress of the Communist Party of China, held in Shanghai on 11–22 January 1925, contributed to the Party's organisational building. Li's answer is that the congress, besides raising the questions of proletarian leadership in the democratic revolution and the worker-peasant alliance, revised the Party constitution and adopted a resolution on organisational questions. In Li's account, these steps made organisational work more institutionalised and standardised and supported the continuing advance of the Great Revolution (1924–27).

The article first sets the background: after the First United Front of 1924, Party membership rose from 420 at the Third Congress to 994 at the Fourth, yet Li says the size and the organisational and leadership standards of Party bodies lagged behind the rising revolution. It then examines the Resolution on the Organisational Question and the Second Revised Party Constitution under three headings: improving the organisational system, improving the leadership system and upholding central authority, and refining organisational procedures.

On the organisational system, Li highlights the establishment of the branch (zhibu) as the basic unit, formed wherever three or more members were present, with set meeting schedules and duties beyond recruitment, such as running clubs, labour schools and mutual-aid societies. Committees and Party fractions in the Kuomintang and other bodies, including Whampoa Military Academy, extended Party influence. On leadership, the congress elected a new Central Executive Committee with Chen Duxiu as general secretary, created a Central Organisation Department and cut the structure from five levels to four. Li also reads its call for "democratic centralism" as an early form of democratic centralism. On procedures, admission was simplified from three approval stages to two, withdrawal decisions were moved to the local committee, probationary members gained the right to attend branch meetings, and rules for transferring organisational affiliation were added.

Li concludes that the congress holds an important place in Party-building history. He cites the Central Committee's contemporary judgment that recognising the importance of organisation was one of its major advances, and Cai Hesen's view that organisational work began to take the right path afterwards. Li notes that membership reached 3,470 ten months later and 57,967 by the Fifth Congress in April 1927. Read the original if you want a concise, document-based account of how the 1925 congress shaped Party branches, admission rules and central leadership structures, as presented in official Party historiography.
quoteEn: The Fourth Congress established a correct view of the masses, giving clear direction to the "mass party" proposed at the Second Congress, and the improvement and strengthening of organisational work provided a strong organisational guarantee for advancing all of the Party's work.
quoteZh: 党的四大确立了正确的群众观，使党的二大提出的“群众党”有了明确指向，而党的组织工作的改善和加强，为推进党的各项工作提供了强有力的组织保证。

glossary.explanation: The organisational principle of Leninist parties, combining discussion and election within the Party with strict obedience of lower to higher bodies. The article treats the Fourth Congress's wording as its early form, before formal adoption at the Fifth Congress.
The basic-level Party organisation, such as in a factory, village or school. The article says the Fourth Congress fixed this name and form, which is still used today.
The Chinese term for the 1924–27 revolutionary upsurge during the Kuomintang–Communist cooperation, ending in 1927.
Groups of Communist members organised inside other bodies, such as the Kuomintang or strike committees, to coordinate the Party's line within them.

t: The CPC's practice of reforming rural bad customs in the Yan'an period
zh: 延安时期中国共产党治理乡村陋习的实践
paras: Zhao and Chen ask how the Communist Party, during the Yan'an period, could reform customs that villagers had followed for generations without damaging popular enthusiasm or weakening the revolution. Their answer is that the Party adjusted its reform policies and used traditional art forms creatively. In their account, this removed popular resistance, rebuilt rural order, strengthened the revolutionary base and advanced cultural change in the countryside.

This short newspaper piece first sets out why the authors regard "bad customs" as obstacles, then draws out the lessons of reform. It draws on examples from the Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region: spirit-medium superstition, opium use and the oppression of women.

The authors argue that these customs held back revolutionary consciousness, limited the growth of revolutionary forces and harmed the government's image, citing corrupt anti-opium officials. Early coercive measures, such as the 1939 ban on foot-binding and prison sentences for spirit mediums, are said to have provoked resistance and rumours. The Party then adapted. It tolerated old customs to some degree, shifted its approach to religion towards education, and tied reform to production by giving mediums, idlers and opium users land, tools and grain. It also recast folk forms such as yangge, drama and "Western pictures" as vehicles for science, hygiene and free marriage, following Mao Zedong's call to transform old forms.

Zhao and Chen conclude that this reform loosened the hold of inherited habits and renewed the social foundations of the countryside, changing rural attitudes and creating a new rural order. Read the original if you want a brief overview of Chinese official-academic framing of Yan'an-era social policy, with examples from the Border Region.
quoteEn: The Communist Party's reform of bad customs in the Yan'an period was both an untying of the nested layers of traditional consciousness and habit, and, even more, a regeneration of society's underlying foundations.
quoteZh: 延安时期中国共产党的陋习改造过程既是对传统意识、习惯嵌套的解绑，更是对社会底蕴的再生成。

t: Valuable experience of deepening institutional reform of Party building in the new era
zh: 新时代深化党的建设制度改革的宝贵经验
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in February 2025, asks what lessons can be drawn from the institutional reform of Party building since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Liu Qiang argues that the reform, first proposed at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) and given a prominent place at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), has produced a body of experience that matters for full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and for Chinese modernization.

The article sets out five principles in turn, each presented as a requirement of the reform, and closes with a brief summary. It draws examples from Party regulations, cadre management and the Party's leadership system.

Liu argues that guidance by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is the fundamental guide, and that the Party's overall leadership is the fundamental guarantee. A problem-oriented approach is the focus: Liu names cadres who act improperly or fail to act, weakened Party members' vanguard role, and weak grassroots organisations. Keeping to fundamental principles while innovating is the essential requirement, illustrated by new regulations and a revised disciplinary code. A systems approach is the methodology, as Party leadership reform is said to lead reform in other fields, supported by the 2023–2027 plan for central Party regulations.

Liu concludes that these five principles together form the experience of more than ten years, reflecting shared ideological understanding within the Party and offering direction for broader and deeper reform that keeps Chinese modernization on course. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style statement of how Party theorists summarise the logic of Party-building institutional reform.
quoteEn: Adhering to fundamental principles while innovating is the essential requirement for deepening institutional reform of Party building.
quoteZh: 坚持守正创新，是深化党的建设制度改革的本质要求。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: A policy line associated with Xi Jinping since 2012, covering discipline, anti-corruption, ideological work and institutional regulation inside the Communist Party.
The official name for China's development path, set out by Xi Jinping at the 20th Party Congress (2022) and presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018 and described as Marxism of the twenty-first century.
Formal rules issued by the Communist Party to govern its own organisation and members, such as disciplinary codes. They are distinct from state law.

glossary.en: keeping to fundamental principles while innovating
glossary.explanation: A slogan stressing that new approaches must preserve the Party's core principles, emphasised in the report to the 20th Party Congress.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Upholding and strengthening the Party's overall leadership over publicity, ideological and cultural work
zh: 坚持和加强党对宣传思想文化工作的全面领导
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in February 2025, takes up how the Communist Party of China should secure its cultural leadership. Zhang Shihai argues that upholding and strengthening the Party's overall leadership over publicity, ideological and cultural work is a defining trait and fine tradition of Marxist parties. In the author's view it is also the fundamental requirement for the flourishing of socialist culture with Chinese characteristics in the new era.

The article has three parts. The first traces the tradition from Marx and Engels through Lenin, the collapse of the Soviet Communist Party, and the CPC's own history under Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping. The second sets out why such leadership is fundamentally required on the new journey. The third proposes four ways to raise the Party's capacity to lead this field.

Zhang's central argument is that Party leadership determines the nature, tone and direction of ideological work. He reads the Soviet case as a lesson: Gorbachev and others gave up control over the media and ideological education, and the loss of cultural leadership was, in the author's words, an important cause of the fall of the Party and state. For China, Zhang describes a complex ideological struggle, with hostile international forces and erroneous domestic trends said to be challenging Marxism's guiding role. Party leadership, the article claims, answers this by providing strategic planning beyond departmental interests and by pooling the efforts of all sectors, so that the propaganda departments do not work alone.

To raise leadership capacity, Zhang calls for taking a clear political stance (the Party managing propaganda, ideology and the media, and "politicians running newspapers"). He also calls for unifying Party spirit with the people's character, upholding Marxism's guiding position in ideology together with Xi Jinping's thought on culture, and building a strong cadre and talent corps. Party spirit, he writes, resides within the people's character, and the two must never be set against each other. Read the original if you want a concise statement, in official Party-media language, of how the Party justifies its leadership of ideology and culture and what practical measures it prescribes.
quoteEn: Party spirit resides within the people's character; there is no Party spirit apart from the people's character, and no people's character apart from Party spirit.
quoteZh: 党性寓于人民性之中，没有脱离人民性的党性，也没有脱离党性的人民性。

glossary.explanation: The Party's portfolio covering propaganda, ideology, the media, culture and the arts. It is overseen by the Party's propaganda departments at every level.

glossary.en: Party spirit with the people's character
glossary.explanation: A principle in Party media doctrine holding that loyalty to the Party and service to the people are identical. It is used to justify Party control over the media and cultural output.
The Party's authority over ideology and culture, often discussed with reference to Gramsci's hegemony. In Party discourse it means control over the direction of ideology, media and culture.
A body of Xi Jinping's statements on culture, formally presented in 2023 as part of Xi Jinping Thought. It is now the official guide for cultural and ideological work.

t: Theoretical and practical explorations of Party discipline building in the New Democratic Revolution period
zh: 新民主主义革命时期党的纪律建设的理论与实践探索
paras: Huang asks how the Communist Party of China developed its discipline in theory and practice between its founding and 1949, and what that record offers today. The article argues that the Party kept adjusting its disciplinary rules to the revolutionary situation, its organisational growth and its internal needs. In Huang's account, this adjustment gave the Party the cohesion and fighting capacity to win the New Democratic Revolution.

The article follows five stages in chronological order. It begins with the founding period, covering early Marxists' debate on "iron discipline" and the programme and constitution of the First and Second Congresses. It then treats the Great Revolution (1923–27), the Agrarian Revolutionary War, the full-scale War of Resistance against Japan, and the War of Liberation. A short conclusion draws lessons for the present.

Huang's central claim is that discipline expanded in content and became more specific at each stage. The Second Congress constitution (1922) set out democratic centralism and expulsion as a penalty. The Fifth Congress (1927) first named "political discipline", issued the first anti-corruption notice (1926) and created a Central Supervisory Commission. After 1927 the Party refined rules on secrecy, organisation and relations with the masses, and rebuilt inspection bodies. Mao Zedong's wartime formulations are central: discipline is compulsory but must rest on members' consciousness, and the "four subordinations" were set out in 1938. In the late 1940s, Huang says, the Party used request-and-report systems, discipline education and strict enforcement to end indiscipline and "anarchism" and prepare to govern nationally. The article also notes that mechanical or excessively harsh enforcement under mistaken lines in the 1930s drew correction, which it describes as a combination of persuasion and strict enforcement.

Huang concludes that the Party always treated iron discipline as a basis of survival and adapted it to changing conditions. The author attributes this to the Party's willingness to face problems and to turn the blade inward. For the "new era", Huang calls for drawing on this history to perfect full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, strengthen conduct and discipline, and advance the Party's self-reform. Read the original if you want a detailed, document-based chronology of how Party discipline rules, bodies and enforcement practices developed from 1920 to 1949, as Party historiography presents it.
quoteEn: The Party has always regarded iron discipline as an important guarantee of its very existence.
quoteZh: 党始终将铁的纪律视为安身立命的重要保障

glossary.explanation: A phrase borrowed from the Bolshevik tradition for strict, binding Party discipline. In the article it appears in Cai Hesen's 1920 letter as a condition of membership of a communist party.
The Leninist organisational principle under which Party members debate and then submit to collective decisions, with lower bodies obeying higher ones.
The requirement that members and organisations follow the Party's political line and stay in line with the central leadership. The article says the term first appeared in 1927.
Mao Zedong's 1938 formulation: the individual to the organisation, the minority to the majority, the lower level to the higher level, and the whole Party to the Central Committee.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's drive since 2012 to tighten discipline, supervision and anti-corruption work within its own ranks.
An official formulation for the Party's continuing effort to correct its own faults and renew itself.

t: Upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground: a defining trait of contemporary Chinese Communists' attitude to Marxism
zh: 守正创新：当代中国共产党人对待马克思主义的鲜明品格
source: Research on Ideological and Political Education (思想教育研究), 2023 no. 2
paras: Taking its cue from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), which lists "upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground" among the "six musts", this article asks what the formula says about how Chinese Communists treat Marxism. Yang and Dang argue that it expresses a scientific attitude towards theoretical innovation. In their account, "upholding fundamental principles" is the precondition and "breaking new ground" the source of vitality, and the two are dialectically unified.

The article has three parts. The first shows how the Party has upheld Marxism's basic principles in four respects: historical materialism, materialist dialectics, the people-centred character of Marxism, and the unity of knowing and doing. The second explains how this foundation supports the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context through the Two Integrations. The third presents Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as the latest result of the approach.

Yang and Dang read the Party's "big history" outlook as a Chinese form of historical materialism, and problem orientation as an application of dialectics. They treat "putting the people first" as the practical expression of Marxism's people-centred stance. They argue that the Two Integrations, combining Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional culture, are not a simple extension of the earlier single integration. They describe a reciprocal relationship: the first integration supplies the practical basis for the second, and the second widens the theoretical space for the first. The authors claim that the Marxist-compatible ideas in traditional culture include people-as-root thinking, dialectical thought and the ideal of "all under heaven for the common good". They also contend that this combination is a historical necessity rather than Max Weber's "elective affinity".

The authors conclude that the "six musts" condense the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought and carry forward the nineteenth-century Marxist worldview. They hold that Xi Jinping Thought both defends the truth of Marxism and develops it in political economy, scientific socialism and philosophy. Upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground today means adhering firmly to this body of thought, applying its stance, viewpoint and method, and maintaining the Two Upholds. Read the original if you want a representative statement of how Party-affiliated theorists link the Two Integrations, the "six musts" and the idea of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context.
quoteEn: The scientific character of a theory is the precondition for upholding fundamental principles, and its vitality lies in innovation.
quoteZh: 理论的科学性是守正的前提，理论的生命力在于创新。

glossary.en: upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground
glossary.explanation: A formula in the 20th Party Congress report (2022), listed among the "six musts". It means holding to Marxism's basic principles while innovating in theory and practice.
Formula associated with Xi Jinping: integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. Xi first put it in this form in 2021.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position on the Party Central Committee and in the Party as a whole, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.

keywords: upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground

t: On the historical experience of the Communist Party of China's century of struggle
zh: 论中国共产党百年奋斗的历史经验
source: Journal of Guangxi University (Philosophy and Social Sciences Edition), 2022 no. 2
paras: Yuwen and Xi take up the historical experience that the Communist Party of China draws from its century of struggle, as set out in the 2021 Party resolution on major achievements and historical experience (the Resolution). They argue that summing up experience is a defining trait of the Party and one reason it can remain in power, correct its mistakes and manage risks. In their view, the Resolution's "ten upholds" explain why the Party succeeded in the past and how it can keep succeeding.

The article has three parts. The first shows how the Party has valued experience-summing from the 1945 and 1981 historical resolutions to the successive theoretical innovations of Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The second analyses the ideas and logic of the "ten upholds". The third sets out requirements for applying this experience in the new era.

The central argument is that the ten upholds form a coherent whole in three senses. They revolve around three laws: those governing Communist Party rule, socialist construction and the development of human society. They continue earlier summaries, from the first two resolutions through the "nine musts" of Xi Jinping's 2021 speech, and they form a closed loop in which upholding Party leadership and the Party's self-reform stand at the head and tail. They also verify the "three logics" of history, theory and practice, which the authors say are consistent from Mao Zedong to Xi Jinping.

For applying the experience, the authors propose three requirements: uphold Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and the core position of Xi Jinping in the Central Committee and the whole Party; uphold the people's position as the subject of history; and exercise historical consciousness and initiative in facing great struggles. They distinguish spontaneity from consciousness in history. They hold that grasping historical laws lets the Party seize the initiative on the road to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a systematic, officially aligned account of how Chinese Party theorists interpret the Resolution's ten upholds and their theoretical logic.
quoteEn: By attending to experience from both success and failure, the Communist Party of China can be clearer-headed, more self-aware and more systematic in planning.
quoteZh: 注重总结正反两方面经验，中国共产党才能更清醒、更自觉、更有计划

glossary.explanation: The ten items of historical experience listed in the November 2021 Party resolution, including upholding Party leadership, putting the people first, theoretical innovation, self-reform and the united front.
Nine points of historical experience set out by Xi Jinping in his speech at the Party's centenary on 1 July 2021, which the ten upholds build on.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
An official term for the Party's efforts to purify, improve and discipline itself, emphasised since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official national goal of restoring China's strength and standing, tied to the 'two centenary goals'.

t: The Communist Party of China's understanding and re-understanding of the essence of socialism
zh: 中国共产党对社会主义本质的认识和再认识
source: Journal of Peking University (Philosophy and Social Sciences), 2023 no. 1
paras: Wang Huaichao asks how the Communist Party of China has come to define the "essence of socialism", understood as the fundamental attribute that distinguishes a socialist society from all others. The article argues that the Party's understanding has deepened in stages through practice, moving from the abstract to the concrete and from the general to the particular. It ends by proposing its own new formulation of that essence.

The article moves chronologically. It begins with Marx, Engels and Lenin, noting that Marx and Engels never used the term itself, and then turns to Stalin's "traditional" view of socialism. It then covers Deng Xiaoping's 1992 formulation and later additions under Jiang Zemin, Hu Jintao and Xi Jinping. A closing section sets this development against the Marxist theory of knowledge, citing Lenin and Mao Zedong on practice.

Wang reads Deng's 1992 definition (liberating and developing the productive forces, eliminating exploitation and polarization, and finally achieving common prosperity) as an original contribution to scientific socialism. In Wang's account it unites productive forces with relations of production, purpose with means, and efficiency with fairness. Later leaders added to it: the all-round development of the human being (Jiang), social fairness and justice and social harmony (Hu), and, under Xi Jinping, Party leadership as the most essential feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics, with sharing as an essential requirement. Wang treats the Party's progress as a cycle running from practice to understanding and back to practice, and from the particular to the general and back. Mao's account of knowledge frames this cycle.

Wang proposes that socialism is essentially a new type of social system, led by a proletarian party, with the people as the principal body. Through liberating and developing the productive forces, it gradually achieves common prosperity, realizes social justice and promotes the free and all-round development of the human being. The article lists six elements: Party leadership, the people's principal position, productive forces, common prosperity, social justice and all-round human development. Wang says this formulation rests on the historical experience of socialism with Chinese characteristics and that understanding will keep rising to new levels. Read the original if you want a compact, Party-school account of how official definitions of socialism's essence have developed from Deng to Xi.
quoteEn: Socialism is essentially a new type of social system. Its defining features are leadership by a proletarian party, the people as the principal body, gradual progress towards common prosperity through liberating and developing the productive forces, continual realization of social justice, and promotion of the free and all-round development of the human being.
quoteZh: 社会主义本质上是一种新型的社会制度，这一新型社会制度的本质特征是：以无产阶级政党为领导核心，以人民为主体，通过解放和发展生产力，逐步达到共同富裕，不断实现社会公正，促进人的自由全面发展。

glossary.explanation: The fundamental attribute that distinguishes socialism from other social systems. Deng Xiaoping gave it an explicit definition in 1992, and it has since become a standard theme of Party theory.
The goal that all people share in affluence rather than a minority growing rich. Deng presented it as socialism's greatest advantage, and it has been emphasised again under Xi Jinping.
The official name for the Party's path of socialist development since reform and opening up. It combines Marxist principles with China's conditions.

t: The Lei Feng spirit never goes out of date
zh: 雷锋精神永不过时
paras: Marking the 60th anniversary of Mao Zedong and other revolutionary leaders' inscriptions for Lei Feng, and following a recent instruction from Xi Jinping, the authors argue that the Lei Feng spirit remains valid however the times change. Their commentary, published in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2023, presents sixty years of the nationwide 'learn from Lei Feng' campaign as proof.

The article first recounts the campaign's history. It begins with local activities in Shenyang and Fushun in 1960, passes through the People's Daily coverage of February 1963 and the publication of Mao's inscription on 5 March 1963, and ends with Xi Jinping's recent directive. It then traces how the concept of the Lei Feng spirit was formed.

The authors' central move is to describe a shift from learning from Lei Feng's deeds to learning from a spirit. They report that Mao defined its essence as good thinking, work style and character, and wholehearted service to the people. Zhou Enlai's inscription, they say, set out its content, and Hu Qiaomu in 1983 called it a 'crystallization' and 'symbol' of a collective spiritual core, not an individual's qualities. They also contend that it combines traditional Chinese culture, red revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture, and keeps developing with the times.

The authors conclude that its enduring vitality drives the campaign. In their account it supplies values for individuals and a spiritual force for social progress. Following Xi Jinping, they call for Party members and cadres to set an example, for stronger support for volunteer service, and for learning from Lei Feng to become everyday practice, especially among young people, so as to build a modern socialist country and achieve the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise official account of how the Lei Feng spirit has been defined and promoted since 1963.
quoteEn: The Lei Feng spirit is a theoretical generalisation named after the communist soldier Lei Feng and built on the substance of his words and deeds, which keeps being enriched and developed in socialist practice.
quoteZh: 雷锋精神是以共产主义战士雷锋的名字命名、以雷锋的言行实质为基本内容，在社会主义实践中不断丰富和发展的理论概括。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central goal of Party discourse, associated especially with Xi Jinping, of restoring China's national strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.

A nationwide campaign launched in 1963 urging people to emulate Lei Feng, a soldier who died on duty in 1962 and was presented as a model of selfless service. It is still promoted each March, often through volunteer service.

t: The historical logic of the Communist Party of China's exploration of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国共产党探索中国式现代化的历史逻辑
paras: Writing in 2023, soon after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Guo Guangyin asks how Chinese modernization came to be, and answers that it is the product of the Communist Party of China's long exploration, one the author describes as logically connected across four historical periods. Guo argues that this path, won at great cost, is the only correct road to building a strong socialist country and achieving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article is a short commentary organised chronologically. It covers the failed early attempts at modernization in modern China, the New Democratic Revolution, the period of socialist revolution and construction, the period of reform and opening up, and the decade since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Each section identifies what that stage contributed to the present path.

Guo's central claim is that each stage supplied a necessary condition. Earlier efforts to copy Western models failed, in the author's account, because they neither avoided dependence nor secured national independence, liberation and freedom for the people. The New Democratic Revolution removed these political obstacles. Socialist revolution and construction then established the basic system, an independent industrial system and the concept of the 'four modernizations'. Reform and opening up, beginning with Deng Xiaoping's 1979 formulation of 'Chinese-style modernization', added a mixed ownership structure, a socialist market economy and openness, and developed the goals from 'three-in-one' to 'four-in-one'. Since 2012, Guo says, Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era has widened the goals to 'five-in-one' and begun to build a theoretical system.

Guo concludes that Party leadership and socialism with Chinese characteristics are what distinguish Chinese modernization from Western modernization. The author claims it has regional and national value and also world-historical significance, offering a reference for late-developing countries and helping to overcome the problems of Western-style modernization. Guo adds that the achievements of the new era have strengthened institutions, material foundations and spiritual drive. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars in 2023 presented a continuous historical narrative of Chinese modernization from the Opium War to the new era.
quoteEn: No country or nation can complete modernization by relying on another country or by copying others' experience; achieving national independence and political liberation is the precondition for advancing modernization.
quoteZh: 任何一个国家和民族都不可能以依附他国方式、照搬他人经验完成现代化，实现民族独立和政治解放是推进现代化的前提条件。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for its own path of modernization. Deng Xiaoping used the phrase in 1979, and it became a central slogan after the 20th Party Congress in 2022.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A long-term national goal in official discourse, referring to restoring China's strength and international standing, often tied to the centenary targets of 2049.
The goal of modernizing agriculture, industry, national defence, and science and technology, set out in the 1960s and revived under Deng Xiaoping.

t: The centennial development and historical logic of Chinese Communists' view of communism
zh: 中国共产党人共产主义观的百年发展与历史逻辑
source: Social Sciences Journal (Shehui kexue jikan), 2023 no. 2
paras: Geng Renjie asks how Chinese Communists' understanding of communism (what it is, what it will be like, how it is to be realised) has developed since the Party's founding in 1921, and what logic runs through that development. Writing in 2023, Geng argues that the Party built a scientific view of communism through the combination of Marxist principles with Chinese realities, and that this development has four mutually supporting dimensions.

The article follows these dimensions in turn: practice, understanding of the concept's content, the path to realisation, and the construction of the ideal. It draws on figures from Li Dazhao, Chen Duxiu, Qu Qiubai and Li Da in the early years, through Mao Zedong, Liu Shaoqi and Chen Yun in the revolutionary period, to Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Xi Jinping. Sources include early lectures and essays, Mao's writings, Deng's talks of the 1980s and Party congress documents.

Geng's central claim is that each dimension moves along a distinct trajectory. In practice, the Party shifted from "following the Russians' road" to "taking our own road", a stance Geng credits with helping it withstand the crises of 1956 and 1989–91. In content, understanding deepened from a preliminary acceptance of historical materialism to full command of Marxist philosophy; Mao's 1940 definition of communism as a proletarian ideology and a new social system marks, in Geng's account, the maturing of this view. On the path, early emphasis on proletarian dictatorship gave way, after the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978), to liberating and developing the productive forces with economic construction at the centre, a shift Geng traces to Deng and sets against the radical transition attempts of the Great Leap Forward. On the ideal, early vague longing for a "Great Harmony" society became the Party's "political soul", and the Party consistently opposes both empty talk of the ideal and abandoning it as remote.

Geng concludes that communism is, in turn, a unity of class character and revolutionary character, of necessity and long-term process, of science and justice, and of idealism and realism. The author holds that Chinese Communists must keep developing this scientific view as they pursue the second centenary goal and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization, especially amid intense ideological competition between China and the West. Read the original if you want a periodised, source-rich account of how the CPC's official line on communism is traced from the early 1920s to the 20th Party Congress (2022).
quoteEn: The process by which Chinese Communists have steadily deepened their grasp of the scientific content of communism closely matches the developmental logic of their move from preliminary acceptance to full command of Marxist philosophy.
quoteZh: 中国共产党人不断深化认识共产主义科学内涵的过程，同对马克思主义哲学由初步接受到全面掌握的发展逻辑高度契合。

glossary.explanation: The Party's basic line adopted after the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978, shifting priority from class struggle to developing the economy.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal of the Party, associated especially with Xi Jinping's leadership, referring to restoring China's national strength and international standing.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The goal of building a modern socialist country by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic; the first goal was building a moderately prosperous society by 2021.

t: On the generative mechanism of the Chinese Communist Party's historical confidence
zh: 论中国共产党历史自信的生成机制
source: Journal of Peking University (Philosophy and Social Sciences), 2023 no. 1
paras: Chen Jinlong asks where the Chinese Communist Party's "historical confidence" comes from. The concept was first put forward by Xi Jinping at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021), and the 20th Party Congress (2022) repeated the call to "stand firm in historical confidence and strengthen historical initiative". Chen argues that the Party's historical confidence is produced by four linked elements: historical accumulation, historical consciousness, the grand historical view and historical initiative.

The article is a conceptual and interpretive study, built on Xi Jinping's speeches, the third historical resolution (2021) and the report to the 20th Party Congress. Its four main sections take the four elements in turn, and a short conclusion sets out how they relate to one another and to cultural confidence, civilizational confidence and the Four-sphere Confidence.

Chen holds that historical accumulation is the objective basis. It consists of the history of the Chinese nation and its civilization, the Party's revolutionary, construction and reform achievements and its spiritual lineage, and the record of Chinese modernization since 1949. Historical consciousness, meaning a clear grasp of historical position, experience and laws, supplies the cognitive basis. Examples are the "ten adherences" of the resolution, laws governing Communist Party rule and socialist construction, and the idea of a new form of human civilization. The grand historical view supplies the methodological basis. It judges Chinese history over a long span and within world history, citing Marx on gunpowder, the compass and printing, and the influence of Chinese culture on the European Enlightenment. Historical initiative turns confidence into practice, and Chen says it is also accompanied by a sense of historical concern.

Chen concludes that accumulation, consciousness, confidence and initiative form an organic whole, in which confidence turns into initiative and initiative in turn strengthens confidence. In the author's account, historical confidence is the starting point, cultural and civilizational confidence are embedded in it, and the Four-sphere Confidence and historical confidence contain each other. Respect and reverence for history, Chen says, mark a mature party. Read the original if you want a systematic account of how Party theorists explain the sources of historical confidence and its link to the Four-sphere Confidence.
quoteEn: Historical accumulation, historical consciousness, historical confidence and historical initiative form an organic whole with internal connections.
quoteZh: 历史积累、历史自觉、历史自信、历史主动是一个具有内在联系的有机整体

glossary.explanation: A concept first put forward by Xi Jinping in 2021. It refers to the Party's confidence in the history of the nation, the state and the Party, and is treated as a basis for holding to ideals and convictions.
A term in recent Party discourse covering both an active spirit and the practical seizing of the initiative in historical development. Chen presents it as the practical form of historical confidence.
A method promoted in Party discourse that examines history across long time spans, broad space and holistic thinking. In the article it is the methodological basis of historical confidence.
The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, stressed in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from the Western model.
The official formula of confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2021. It describes the civilizational outcome claimed for Chinese modernization.

t: The Nanniwan spirit: a bright banner of "doing it ourselves for ample food and clothing"
zh: 南泥湾精神：自己动手、丰衣足食的光辉旗帜
paras: Writing in 2023, shortly after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Bi Yuanning asks what the "Nanniwan spirit" is, how it arose and why it still matters. The article argues that this spirit, born in the Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia Border Region's production campaign, embodies revolutionary heroism, the nature and purpose of the people's army, and a tradition that remains relevant today. Bi opens by noting that Xi Jinping led the Politburo Standing Committee to Yan'an soon after the Congress and urged the promotion of the Yan'an spirit.

The piece is a Party-journal commentary in three parts: the formation of the Nanniwan spirit, its content, and its value for the present. The historical section covers the Anti-Japanese War's stalemate phase after 1938, the blockade of the border region, and the Eighth Route Army's 359th Brigade, which began reclaiming wasteland at Nanniwan in March 1941. It credits Mao Zedong's call to \"do it ourselves\" (1939) and Zhu De's survey work as the leadership guidance behind it.

Bi defines the spirit's core as self-reliance and hard struggle, and breaks it into themes: obeying the Party, overcoming difficulties by one's own hands, serving the people, frugality, officers sharing hardship, and innovation. The evidence includes the brigade's claimed self-sufficiency in grain and funds by 1943 and, citing a 1945 Liberation Daily report, about 354,000 mu cultivated and 37,000 shi of grain harvested, with 10,000 shi paid to the government. Bi also lists organisational innovations such as soldiers' cooperatives, a mixed farming–industry–transport–commerce economy, and labour competitions. Bi cites Mao's praise of this as a \"miracle\" and a \"material basis\" that could not be conquered.

Bi concludes that promoting the Nanniwan spirit serves three present needs. It sustains the Party on its \"new road to the examination\", through the \"Three Musts\", the Party's self-reform and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. It is also required for advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization, in the face of risks and challenges. Finally, it unites the people through a people-centred approach and whole-process people's democracy. Read the original if you want an example of how Party media present wartime Yan'an traditions as resources for current Party-building and ideological work.
quoteEn: The Nanniwan spirit is the powerful spiritual force with which the Communist Party of China led the anti-Japanese army and people to rise in adversity and develop amid hardship; its core and distinctive quality is self-reliance and hard struggle, and its main content is doing it ourselves, having ample food and clothing, struggling hard and winning victory.
quoteZh: 南泥湾精神是中国共产党领导抗日军民在困境中奋起、在艰苦中发展的强大精神力量，其核心和特质是自力更生、艰苦奋斗，主要内容是自己动手、丰衣足食、艰苦斗争、夺取胜利。

glossary.explanation: A Party-defined set of values drawn from the 359th Brigade's land reclamation at Nanniwan near Yan'an in the early 1940s. It stresses self-reliance and hard work and is part of the Yan'an spirit tradition.

A campaign launched by the Party from about 1939 in the Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia Border Region. It mobilised troops, officials and civilians in farming and manufacturing to overcome blockade and shortages.
The official term for China's path of modernization, set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) as the route to national rejuvenation.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's drive since 2012 to tighten discipline and combat corruption within its ranks.
An official concept, advanced by Xi Jinping, describing China's democracy as covering every stage of decision-making and not only elections.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, tied to making China a modern, strong, prosperous country by mid-century.
A formula of Xi Jinping at the 20th Party Congress. It urges the Party to stay modest, prudent and hard-working, and to keep fighting.

t: How to keep a clean and healthy political ecosystem at all times
zh: 如何始终保持风清气正的政治生态
source: Party and Government Cadres Forum (中国党政干部论坛), 2023 no. 2
paras: Writing in 2023, Jiang Laiyong takes up one of the "unique problems" that the Party says a century-old governing party must solve: how to keep a clean and upright political ecosystem at all times. Jiang defines the political ecosystem as the conditions and environment in which political actors operate, made up of political relations, customs, tendencies and character. The article argues that this goal is both essential and very hard to achieve, and that it requires Marxist dialectical thinking and effective measures.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why a healthy political ecosystem matters; the second explains why it is arduous and complex to sustain; the third proposes measures under three headings: putting the people first, daring and knowing how to struggle, and a systems approach.

On importance, Jiang contends that the political ecosystem shapes the cadres who live in it, so it is key to producing good cadres. It also underpins the solution of the Party's other unique problems and supports Chinese modernization. On difficulty, Jiang says good and bad ecosystems always coexist as contradictory aspects, and the bad one corrupts faster than the good one forms. Causes are complex, including a historical culture of official-centred thinking and reliance on personal connections, uneven development, and gaps in full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Jiang adds that corruption tends to rebound once pressure eases, so the work is long-term.
