Jiang's proposals include greater transparency and supervision of power, and lifelong accountability for livelihood projects. They also include tackling formalism, bureaucratism and officials' inaction, partly through exit rules for underperforming public employees. Jiang further calls for criticism and self-criticism, and for advancing the three-pronged approach of making officials not dare, not be able and not want to be corrupt. Other proposals are strict cadre-selection standards, supervision of top leaders ("first in command"), rule-of-law methods, assessment indicators for the political ecosystem, and heavier penalties for bribe-givers. Read the original if you want a Party-affiliated scholar's account of how political ecology is framed in anti-corruption and cadre-management policy around 2023.
quoteEn: Building a political ecosystem is a long-term systemic project that is always under way, and it demands firm resolve and lasting perseverance.
quoteZh: 政治生态的建设是一项永远在路上的长期系统工程，必须决心意志坚定，始终保持恒心韧劲。

glossary.explanation: A metaphor from ecology, widely used in Party discourse, for the overall environment of political life, including norms, relationships and conduct among officials. A 'clean and upright' ecosystem is a stated Party goal.
Six problems the Party leadership has said only a long-governing Marxist party faces, such as staying true to its founding mission and spotting and fixing its own faults.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's disciplinary and anti-corruption drive and Party-building efforts since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
Official term for China's own path of modernization, stressing a huge population, common prosperity and balanced material and cultural progress.

glossary.pinyin: bù gǎn fǔ, bù néng fǔ, bù xiǎng fǔ
glossary.en: not dare, not be able and not want to be corrupt
glossary.explanation: An official formula for anti-corruption work that combines deterrence, institutional constraints and ideological education.
Colloquial term for the top leader of a unit or locality, such as the Party secretary, who is seen as responsible for its political climate.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Arming young people with the Party's scientific theory
zh: 用党的科学理论武装青年
paras: Following the 20th Party Congress (2022), which told the whole Party to treat youth work as strategic work, Han Xiping asks why young people must be armed with the Party's scientific theory and how this should be done. Han argues that this theoretical arming is a distinctive strength of the Communist Party of China and that it matters more in the new era. The piece is a commentary in Red Flag Manuscripts.

The article has three parts. The first presents theoretical arming as the Party's advantage. The second explains why the new era makes it more urgent. The third sets out three ways to carry it out. Han draws throughout on Xi Jinping's remarks on youth work, and also cites Marx and Lenin.

Han's first claim is that Marxism is scientific and open to development, so the Party can answer the questions of China, the world, the people and the times. In this account the Party has won over young people because Marxist parties, unlike bourgeois parties, treat youth as friends and successors rather than as tools. The second claim is that today's young people will be the main force of modernization up to mid-century, and that hostile forces are trying to Westernize and divide them. Han describes this as a struggle the Party cannot afford to lose, and calls for Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era to follow each theoretical innovation. Third, Han proposes three ways to deliver this arming. It should be systematic, with staged and differentiated programmes coordinated by Party organizations, the Communist Youth League, Party schools and universities. It should be practical, showing young people the results of the past decade and building lasting mechanisms for social practice. It should be modern, using the internet and platforms such as Study Xi Strong Nation (Xuexi Qiangguo) in language that young people find accessible.

Han concludes that the quality of youth education will shape China's future. Arming young people with the Party's theory is described as a proven path that sets the Party apart from other parties. The goal is to raise qualified successors who can take on building a modern socialist country and advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party theorists justify ideological work among youth and what institutional measures they propose.
quoteEn: Theoretical arming is, in the end, work with people, and to do it well one must start from people themselves and work on making it targeted.
quoteZh: 理论武装工作归根到底是做人的工作，做好这项工作必须从人本身出发，在针对性上下功夫。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party constitution in 2017.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party slogan for restoring China's strength and international standing, closely tied to the Chinese Dream.
The Party's term for systematic education that equips members and the public with its official theory.

t: The internal logic, scientific connotation and fundamental guidelines for establishing a correct view of Party history
zh: 树立正确党史观的内在逻辑、科学内涵与根本遵循
paras: Taking its cue from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), which calls for sustained education in the histories of the Party, New China, reform and opening up, and socialism, this article asks how a correct view of Party history should be established. The authors define such a view as people's overall understanding of the history of the Communist Party of China. They argue that it rests on historical materialism, materialist dialectics and seeking truth from facts, and that it is a political question bearing on the fate of the Party and the state, not merely an academic topic.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the internal logic behind a correct view: historical materialism as its theoretical base, the "big history" outlook as its method, the Party's hundred-year achievements as its practical foundation, and the educational and advisory functions of Party history as its inner driving force. The second sets out the scientific connotation of the view through five components: political, popular, spatio-temporal, mission-related and learning-related. The third turns to the fundamental guidelines, drawn mainly from Xi Jinping's statements on Party history since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

The authors hold that a correct view starts from social being determining social consciousness, and that it must place the Party's century within 5,000 years of Chinese civilisation, 500 years of world socialism and 180 years of modern Chinese history. Each component carries a principle: Party history "belongs to the Party", Party spirit and the people's character are united, the Party's historical position is fixed in time and space, the Party is a mission-driven party, and study follows seeking truth from facts. The guidelines they list include grasping the theme running through Party history, namely the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. They also include studying the "three historical resolutions" and evaluating major problems without letting achievements hide mistakes or mistakes cancel achievements.

The authors name historical nihilism as the main present threat. They describe it as rooted in idealist history, exaggerating Party errors, slandering leaders and heroes, and using fragments to deny the whole. To counter it they propose theoretical education, grasping the significance of the Two Establishes, strengthening the Four-sphere Confidence and the Two Upholds, tightening ideological work and legal measures against defaming history, and promoting core socialist values. Read the original if you want a representative statement of how Chinese Party-history scholars frame the "correct view of Party history" and the campaign against historical nihilism.
quoteEn: Establishing a correct view of Party history is not merely an academic topic urgently requiring a theoretical response, but a political question bearing on the future and fate of the Party and the state.
quoteZh: 树立正确党史观不仅仅是理论上亟待回应的学术论题，更是关乎党和国家前途命运的政治问题。

glossary.explanation: Formula from the Party's 2021 historical resolution and the 20th Party Congress: establishing Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and of the whole Party, and establishing the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The requirement to uphold General Secretary Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Party Central Committee.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics, a formula promoted since the 18th Party Congress.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, presented in Party discourse as the Party's founding mission and the theme of its history.
In official Chinese usage, a label for views seen as denying or distorting the Party's history and revolutionary leaders. The term is polemical and is used mainly in Party ideological campaigns.
A Xi Jinping-era methodological term urging that history be viewed over long spans and as a whole rather than through single episodes.
The Party's three resolutions on history, from 1945, 1981 and 2021, which assess its past and set an authoritative line on major events and figures.

t: The course and experience of Party political building in the new era
zh: 新时代党的政治建设历程及经验
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2022 no. 10
paras: Li Zhenghua and Gu Xunbao ask how the Communist Party of China has developed its "political building" (political construction) since the 18th Party Congress (2012), and what lessons follow for the new journey ahead. They argue that the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core has raised political building to the leading position within Party building, advancing it in both theory and practice, and that this is significant for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article is organised chronologically and then thematically. The first section covers the five years after 2012, when new concepts and measures appeared. The second covers the period from the 19th Party Congress (2017), when political building was placed first among the Party's tasks. The third draws four basic lessons. The authors define political building as work on political conviction, political leadership, political capability and a clean political ecosystem, aimed at unity and consistent action across the Party.

In the authors' account, the first phase introduced the Two Upholds, the "four consciousnesses", "political ecology" and "intra-Party political culture", and "political capability". It also brought measures such as political inspection tours, stricter intra-Party political life, the anti-corruption campaign and a people-centred stance. After 2017, they say, a conceptual system took shape, with over 70 concepts grouped under four headings. Political building was defined as the "fundamental" building that guides all others, and the Two Establishes were put forward. In practice it was made to guide ideological, organisational, conduct, discipline and institutional work, while the Party's basic line was updated and its overall leadership reinforced.

Li and Gu draw four lessons: strengthen Party regulations (they cite 3,615 currently valid by 2021); focus on the "critical few" leading cadres to bring along the "vast majority"; raise political awareness and capability through Party-spirit education and training; and keep the fundamental aim of serving the people and meeting their aspirations for a better life. They present each as guidance for the new journey. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned chronology of Party political building, with the key documents and dates, for study of Party-building discourse.
quoteEn: Among all aspects of Party building, political building is the most important: it is the guide and the core, and the focus and ultimate goal of the other aspects.
quoteZh: 党的政治建设在党的各项建设中是最重要的，是统领和核心，是其他建设的着眼点和落脚点。

glossary.explanation: The requirement to resolutely uphold Xi Jinping's core position on the Party Central Committee and in the Party as a whole, and to uphold the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee. It emerged around the 6th Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2016).

A formulation in the 2021 Party resolution on history: establishing Xi Jinping's core status on the Central Committee and in the Party, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.
Political awareness, awareness of the big picture, awareness of the core, and awareness of keeping in line. It was set as a basic requirement for Party members and organisations from 2016.
A strand of Party building focused on political conviction, leadership, capability and ecosystem, so as to secure Party unity. The 19th Party Congress (2017) put it first among Party-building tasks.
A term for leading cadres, especially senior ones, whose conduct is held to set an example for the wider Party membership.

t: Zhou Enlai and the second large-scale import of complete sets of technology and equipment in New China
zh: 周恩来与新中国第二次大规模引进成套技术设备
source: Documents of the Party (Dang de wenxian), 2022 no. 4
paras: Chi Aiping takes up a gap in the existing scholarship: the background and outline of the 1972–1975 import of complete sets of technology and equipment from Western countries have been studied, but Zhou Enlai's role in deciding and carrying it out has not. The article argues that, with Mao Zedong's support, Zhou led the State Council's working group in launching and steering what it calls the "second large-scale import", which followed the Soviet-aided 156 projects of 1954. It presents the programme as a major spur to later economic and technological progress and as a showcase of Zhou's strategic judgement.

The article has three parts. The first traces how the decision was made and started, from the international and domestic situation of the late 1960s and early 1970s to the State Planning Commission's January 1972 report on chemical-fibre and fertiliser plants, and then to the "4.3 Plan" of 1973. The second examines Zhou's organisational and strategic guidance during implementation. The third assesses the programme's significance and the thinking behind it. Chi draws on leaders' marginal notes, commission reports and Zhou's talks with foreign guests.

Chi's central claim is that Zhou made the key choices at each stage. He set the working line of "learn, use, adapt, create", picked negotiators, accepted a price concession to secure the French fibre contract, and told the commission to merge scattered departmental requests into one larger plan. The 4.3 Plan finally covered 26 projects worth about 4.3 billion US dollars, later raised by 880 million. In implementation, Chi says, Zhou strengthened the working group by bringing in Chen Yun and then Deng Xiaoping, backed the use of bank deposits and deferred payment for foreign exchange, and promoted export earnings through the Guangzhou trade fair and processing of imported materials. Chi adds that Zhou's remarks on bank ties, foreign capital and cheap labour anticipated later opening-up practice, and that he worked against the "Gang of Four" and ultra-leftist interference.

Chi concludes that the programme brought advanced technology, management ideas and market information, and trained cadres and specialists who later supported reform and opening up. In the article's account, the 18 fertiliser, fibre and alkylbenzene projects, 63.84 per cent of investment, laid the material base for solving China's food and clothing problems. Chi holds that the six principles of the plan, including self-reliance and combining learning with original creation, remain a useful reference. Read the original if you want a documented, Party-history account of how Zhou Enlai's role in the early 1970s opening to Western technology is presented in official Chinese scholarship.
quoteEn: The important results achieved by the \"second import\" cannot be separated from Zhou Enlai's strategic guidance.
quoteZh: “二次引进”能取得这些重要成果，与周恩来的战略指导是分不开的。

glossary.explanation: The 1973 programme to import 26 large projects of complete plant and equipment from Western countries and Japan, worth about 4.3 billion US dollars. It is named after the total sum.
The central state body responsible for drafting economic plans and approving major investment projects.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China from 1978.
Official term for four Party leaders, including Jiang Qing, blamed for ultra-leftist policies in the Cultural Revolution and arrested in 1976.

t: The Lei Feng spirit as a spiritual summit of faithfully carrying forward the Party's original aspiration and mission
zh: 雷锋精神是忠实传承党的初心使命的精神高地
paras: Marking the 60th anniversary of Mao Zedong and other senior leaders' inscriptions for Lei Feng, this commentary (first published in People's Daily, 5 March 2023) asks how Lei Feng should be understood on the new journey after the 20th Party Congress (2022). Yan Xiaofeng argues that the Lei Feng spirit should be grasped from the standpoint of the great founding spirit of the Party, and that its core is the Party's original aspiration and mission, which runs through the whole spiritual genealogy of Chinese Communists.

The article has three parts. The first places the Lei Feng spirit within the spiritual genealogy of Chinese Communists, whose source is the founding spirit. The second presents Lei Feng as a model of putting the original aspiration and mission into practice. The third links the spirit to what Yan calls the problems unique to a large party, and to the Party's tasks in advancing Chinese modernization.

Yan contends that the Lei Feng spirit grew out of the founding spirit and became part of the genealogy in its own right. In Yan's account it belongs to the period of socialist revolution and construction, arose among ordinary grassroots Party members, and was formed by the People's Army in peacetime. Yan defines it as lofty ideals and faith, a spirit of service, dedication to one's work, innovation and hard struggle. Yan reads it as the continuation of the Zhang Side spirit under socialism, and cites Lei Feng's diary and conduct as examples of unity of word and deed. The central move is to treat remembering the original aspiration and mission as the first of the Party's unique problems. Learning from Lei Feng is said to help Party members withstand the "four tests" and overcome the "four dangers": the tests of long-term governance, of reform and opening up, of the market economy and of the external environment. Yan says it also helps against spiritual slackening and corruption.

Yan concludes that Party members and officials must lead by example so that learning from Lei Feng becomes everyday practice, especially among young people. Doing so would strengthen the Party's bond with the people and its commitment to full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Every step towards the second centenary goal is described as putting the original aspiration and mission into practice. Read the original if you want an example of how Party-affiliated scholarship ties the Lei Feng model to the spiritual genealogy and to Party-building themes after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: The Lei Feng spirit has become one of the great spirits in the spiritual genealogy of Chinese Communists, and has remained admired by Party members and the public for 60 years, because it set a shining example of putting the Party's original aspiration and mission into practice.
quoteZh: 雷锋精神之所以能够成为中国共产党人精神谱系的伟大精神，之所以能够历经60年仍然在广大党员和群众中成为景仰的对象，是由于雷锋精神树立了践行党的初心使命的光辉典范。

glossary.zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系
glossary.explanation: A set of named "great spirits" (for example the Long March spirit, the Lei Feng spirit) said to have emerged over the Party's history. Since 2021 it has been traced to the great founding spirit as its source.
The Party's stated founding purpose of seeking well-being for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation. It was the theme of a Party-wide education campaign launched in 2019.

glossary.en: problems unique to a large party
glossary.literal: difficult problems unique to a big party
glossary.explanation: A phrase used by Xi Jinping from 2022 for the challenges facing a very large, long-governing party, such as keeping its original aspiration and its ties with the people.
The official name for China's path of modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022) as the Party's central task.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party-discipline and anti-corruption drive pursued since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

t: Party members' reading activities in the early years of the Party and the Great Revolution period
zh: 建党之初和大革命时期党员读书活动的开展
paras: Organising Party members to read in a planned way is described by Yi Fenglin as a fine tradition of the Communist Party of China and a basis for its later study system. The article asks how the Party, in the years after its founding in 1921 and during the Great Revolution (1924–27), set about organising reading among its members. Yi argues that these early efforts laid the groundwork for later systems of Party study.

Using the approaches of reading history and organisational history, and combining macro and micro perspectives, the article draws on Party and Communist Youth League reports, letters, memoirs and resolutions from Hankou, Shanghai, Nanjing, Beijing, Guangdong, Jiangxi and elsewhere. Because Party and League work overlapped heavily at the time, Yi also includes League members. The article is organised in five parts: the background, the planned content of reading, the methods, the material conditions provided, and the results.

Yi argues that reading became a key route for training members because weak theoretical grounding and discipline were widely reported, while teachers, funds and time made large training schools hard to run. The Party therefore planned reading lists (for example Yun Daiying's 1927 list and the Guangdong League's 1926 list) that stressed Marxist theory, Party documents and periodicals such as Xiangdao. Reading combined individual study with branch-level group discussion, supported by guidance, tests of understanding, supervision and links to practical work. The Party guaranteed supply through translation and editorial committees, its own publishing bodies, Party and League periodicals, and libraries. According to the article, the results were firmer communist conviction, better revolutionary skills such as judging political disputes, and organisational growth, as members recommended readings to others and local Party founders in Jiangxi used reading to recruit.

Yi concludes that organised reading strengthened members' ideological level and working ability and increased the cohesion and fighting capacity of the Party organisation. The article presents this early practice as part of the Party's tradition of self-building. Read the original if you are interested in the early history of Party education, reading practices and local Party organisation, and want archival examples of specific reading lists and methods.
quoteEn: The Party carefully planned the main content of members' reading, encouraging wide reading while stressing mastery of revolutionary theory and Party policy as the focus.
quoteZh: 我们党对党员阅读的主要内容进行了精心规划，既鼓励广泛阅读，又强调要以掌握革命理论和党的方针政策为重点。

glossary.explanation: The term used in Chinese historiography for the 1924–27 national revolution, in which the Communist Party and the Kuomintang cooperated against warlords and imperialism before the split in 1927.
The Party's central weekly organ, founded in 1922, which explained Party policy and was treated as required reading for members.

t: Sixty years of the "Learn from Lei Feng" campaign: development and lessons
zh: 学雷锋活动六十年来的发展历程及启示
paras: Marking the 60th anniversary of Mao Zedong and other senior revolutionaries' inscriptions for Lei Feng, this commentary (published in Guangming Daily, 1 March 2023) asks how the campaign to learn from Lei Feng has developed and what it teaches. Ouyang argues that Lei Feng has grown from an individual model into a social culture, a moral marker and spiritual benchmark of socialist China, and that the Lei Feng spirit "never goes out of date". The piece draws on Xi Jinping's recent instruction on the campaign.

The article is organised chronologically in four stages. It begins with the campaign's rise in 1960–63, moves to its place in socialist spiritual civilization building after 1977 and in the early reform years, then to its role as a vehicle of the socialist core value system from 1989 onward, and ends with the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Each stage is illustrated with documents, commemorative events, publications and model figures.

Ouyang describes how the campaign spread from the army to the whole country after Mao's 1963 inscription, which set 5 March as Learn from Lei Feng Day. In the reform era it was tied to civility campaigns and, from the 1990s, to volunteer service and the slogan of learning from Lei Feng at one's post. In the new era, the author reports, it was given top-level design: institutionalised volunteering (2014), annual national model selections from 2015, a 2019 outline on civic morality, and the inclusion of the Lei Feng spirit in the spiritual genealogy of Chinese Communists in 2021.

Ouyang concludes that the campaign has endured because the Lei Feng spirit emerged from socialist construction, accords with the Party's purpose of serving the people wholeheartedly, and inherits traditional national virtues. Its vitality lies, in this view, in keeping pace with the needs of each era and in serving as a vehicle for moral standards and civic ethics. Read the original if you want a concise official-line chronology of the Lei Feng campaign, with its key documents and dates, up to 2023.
quoteEn: The campaign to learn from Lei Feng has flourished and deepened, and the Lei Feng spirit has been passed on and ever renewed, fundamentally because it keeps pace with the needs of the times, solves the problems of the times and promotes the development of the times.
quoteZh: 学雷锋活动蓬勃开展、持续深入，雷锋精神赓续传承，历久弥新，根本就在于能够紧随时代需要、解决时代问题、促进时代发展

glossary.explanation: A set of virtues attributed to Lei Feng (1940–1962), a People's Liberation Army soldier presented as a model of selfless service to the people. It has been promoted since 1963 as a moral ideal.

glossary.zh: 社会主义精神文明建设
glossary.explanation: A Party policy line, prominent since the early 1980s, to cultivate morality, ideals and culture alongside material development.

glossary.zh: 社会主义核心价值体系
glossary.explanation: The Party's formulation of the central values that society is expected to uphold, later condensed into the socialist core values.

glossary.zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系
glossary.explanation: An official list of exemplary spirits from the Party's history, such as the Long March spirit, compiled and expanded from 2021.
The Communist Party congress of 2012, at which Xi Jinping became General Secretary; "since the 18th Party Congress" marks the "new era" in official usage.

t: Telling the story of the Communist Party of China well
zh: 讲好中国共产党的故事
paras: Marking the publication of the English edition of The Centenary of the Communist Party of China (Zhongguo Gongchandang de yibai nian), Qu Qingshan, head of the Party's central institute for Party history and literature, argues that the book gives a basis for presenting the Party to foreign readers. This is a commentary rather than a research article. Qu presents the English edition as a major event for Party history work, theoretical education and external publicity. He ties it to the call in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) to build Chinese discourse and narrative systems and to present a credible, lovable and respectable image of China.

The piece has three parts. The first describes the book as an authoritative official history and says the English edition is faithful to the Chinese original. The second sets out what readers can find in the four-volume work. The third explains how to use it to tell the Party's story, organised around the Party's image as seen through its members, its internal character and its international role.

Qu characterises the book as a standard history marked by authority, scientific rigour, accuracy, completeness, systematic treatment and responsiveness to current questions, including rebuttal of historical nihilism. He says it does three things: it recounts the Party's struggles and achievements through documented facts; it shows the Party's spirit and the lineage of Communist spirit that begins with the founding spirit; and it explains why the Party has succeeded and how it can continue to do so. Qu holds that this can correct what he calls foreign, especially Western, bias and distortion, and shift the Party's image from one shaped mainly by others to one shaped mainly by itself. On storytelling, he calls for explaining the Party's purpose of serving the people, its ties with the people, its scientific theory and policy continuity, its discipline and self-correction, its rigorous self-governance and its contributions to world peace and a community with a shared future for mankind.

Qu concludes that the English edition gives China a new platform for telling the Party's story. He describes it as an outward declaration of the Party's historical self-confidence, and a means of spreading the Party's history, theory and voice. He expects it to help more foreign readers understand China and to support exchange with other countries. Read the original if you want to see how a senior Party historian presents the aims and intended international use of the official centenary history.
quoteEn: The history of the Communist Party of China is the richest soil and foundation for the Party's story.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的历史是中国共产党故事最为雄厚的土壤和底蕴。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s. It describes a vision of international relations based on shared interests and cooperation.
In Party usage, a label for views that question or denigrate the official account of the Party's history and the revolution. Official texts present combating it as a task of Party history education.

glossary.literal: great spirit of founding the Party
glossary.explanation: A formulation announced in 2021 for the values attributed to the Party's founders. It is treated as the source of the Party's spiritual lineage (精神谱系).

keywords: Centenary of the Communist Party of China

t: Firmly grasping the key guide for historical research in China in the new era
zh: 牢牢把握新时代中国史学研究的重要指针
paras: This commentary, originally published in the People's Daily on 8 November 2021, asks how Chinese historians should study and apply Xi Jinping's statements on the science of history. Yu Xinhua argues that these statements are an integral part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and serve as the key guide and basic principle for historical research in the new era. Historians are urged to study them closely and put them into practice.

The piece is organised under three headings: innovating and developing the Marxist theory of history; strengthening research on major historical questions centred on the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation; and promoting the integration of disciplines. It begins by noting that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) Xi has addressed studying, writing and using history across Party history, national history, the history of the Chinese nation and world history.

On theory, Yu calls for work on the history of Marxist historiography in China, from the early spread of historical materialism, through the debates on Chinese social history and the "five golden flowers" discussions, to the rise of social, environmental, cultural, medical and women's history after the 1980s. Yu also wants Marxist historical theory tied to contemporary conditions such as artificial intelligence and shifting international patterns. On major questions, Yu lists the origins and development of Chinese civilization, the contemporary value of fine traditional culture, academic support for forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation, and historical wisdom for building a community with a shared future for mankind. Historians should draw on China's historical record of peace-seeking values and on the Silk Roads to show the logic of a peaceful development path.

Yu holds that these questions cannot be answered with traditional methods alone, and urges closer ties between Chinese and world history, archaeology and textual studies, and with other humanities, the natural sciences, big data and AI. The article concludes that historians should grasp the core meaning of Xi's statements and the Marxist standpoint, viewpoint and method running through them. They should build a discipline, academic and discourse system for history with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a concise official statement of the research priorities set for Chinese historians in 2021.
quoteEn: To study and apply General Secretary Xi Jinping's important statements on the science of history in depth means continually innovating and developing the Marxist theory of history in the new era.
quoteZh: 深入学习贯彻习近平总书记关于历史科学的重要论述，就要在新时代不断创新发展马克思主义历史理论。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. Official sources present it as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's "Chinese Dream".

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept, promoted since 2012–2013, which calls for joint international development and cooperation.

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: firmly cast the consciousness of the Chinese nation community
glossary.explanation: A Party formulation, prominent since 2017, that stresses a shared national identity among China's ethnic groups. Official texts treat it as the guiding line of ethnic affairs work.

t: Strengthening the Party's overall leadership of Chinese modernization from a political height
zh: 从政治的高度切实加强党对中国式现代化的全面领导
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily shortly after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Bao Xinjian argues that the Party's political leadership is the most fundamental element of its overall leadership, and that it decides the direction and fate of Chinese modernization. In the article's account, whether Party organisations and leading cadres can raise their political judgement, political understanding and political execution bears directly on whether modernization succeeds.

The commentary has three parts. The first sets out the distinctive features and inner logic of Chinese modernization. The second discusses the major principles and correct direction needed on the new journey. The third treats the promotion of whole-process people's democracy as a key link in strengthening Party leadership. It relies heavily on the 20th Party Congress report and on speeches by Xi Jinping.

Bao's central move is to contrast two modernization logics. Chinese modernization follows a "people-centred logic" aimed at all-round human development, while Western modernization, in this reading, follows a "capital logic" that produces one-sided social development and a loss of human subjectivity. The author adds that the people-centred approach does not reject capital: in the primary stage of socialism, capital must be used while its negative effects are curbed, through an "effective market" and a "capable government". Bao then ties leadership to the "five adherences" of the Congress report, to seizing historical initiative amid global upheaval, and to relying on the people. Whole-process people's democracy is presented as a measure of the Party's leadership capacity, to be developed in three ways: people-centred, problem-oriented and institution-based. Bao names the people's congress system, multiparty cooperation, regional ethnic autonomy and grassroots self-governance as its institutional chain.

Bao concludes that Party organisations and cadres at every level must stand firmly with the people, hold to the political principles and direction set by the Central Committee, and raise the institutionalisation, standardisation and proceduralisation of democracy. Doing so is presented as a precondition for Chinese modernization to avoid deviating from its course. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party theory in early 2023 linked Party leadership, the critique of capital logic and whole-process people's democracy.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is people-centred, takes all-round human development and comprehensive social progress as its core value and follows a "people-centred logic"; Western modernization takes capital as its logical starting point and inner driving force and follows a "capital logic".
quoteZh: 中国式现代化坚持以人民为中心，以实现人的全面发展和社会全面进步为核心价值，遵循的是“人本逻辑”；西方式现代化则是以资本为逻辑起点和内在驱动力，遵循的是“资本逻辑”。

glossary.explanation: The official concept, elaborated at the 20th Party Congress (2022), of a distinctive path to modernization with five stated features, presented as an alternative to Western models.
A term used by Xi Jinping and the Party to describe China's democratic system as covering election, consultation, decision-making, management and oversight, not only voting.
The official judgement that China remains in an early phase of socialism, which justifies a market economy and a mixed ownership structure.

The five major principles listed in the 20th Party Congress report: Party leadership, the socialist path with Chinese characteristics, a people-centred approach, deepening reform and opening up, and a spirit of struggle.

t: Implementing Party leadership comprehensively, systematically and holistically
st: Further advancing the great new project of Party building in the new era
zh: 《人民日报》评论部：全面、系统、整体落实党的领导
zhSub: 深入推进新时代党的建设新的伟大工程
paras: This commentary from the People's Daily commentary department (2 February 2023) takes up the question of how the Party should uphold its leadership. It argues that, to govern a large Party and a large country, Party unity, centralised and unified leadership, and the authority of the Central Committee are of paramount importance. Party leadership, in the words it quotes from the 20th Party Congress report (2022), must be implemented comprehensively, systematically and holistically.

The piece opens with Xi Jinping's 2021 visit to the Yangjiagou revolutionary site in Shaanxi, where the Central Committee was based during the civil war. It then moves through the achievements of the past decade, the practical meaning of upholding Central Committee authority, and the 20th Party Congress's plans for improving Party leadership.

The commentary presents centralised and unified leadership as the main political guarantee of the period's successes, citing poverty alleviation and the response to COVID-19. For the latter it gives figures such as more than 4.6 million grassroots Party organisations. It calls the Two Establishes the decisive factor behind these changes. Upholding leadership is described as concrete: it means the Four Consciousnesses, the Four-sphere Confidence and the Two Upholds, plus following the Central Committee in all circumstances and absolute loyalty to the Party. It adds that leadership must also be improved, through stronger political discipline, democratic centralism and better decision-making bodies.

The commentary concludes that speaking out clearly on politics and ensuring Party unity are the Party's lifeblood. Deeper understanding of the Two Establishes and higher political judgement, understanding and execution, it says, will make the Party more united. Read the original if you want an example of official 2023 Party-press language on leadership, loyalty and centralisation after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Upholding Party leadership means, first of all, upholding the authority of the Party Central Committee and its centralised and unified leadership.
quoteZh: 坚持党的领导，首先是坚持党中央权威和集中统一领导。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the 2021 Party resolution on history, affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of his thought. It is presented officially as decisive for the Party's achievements.
The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.
Party requirements for political awareness, big-picture awareness, core awareness and alignment awareness, promoted since 2016.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Communist Party, combining discussion with binding unity of action under central leadership.

t: Deepening research on the history of New China to encourage firm historical confidence
zh: 深化新中国史研究 激励人们坚定历史自信
paras: Writing in early 2023, Yang Shengqun takes up Xi Jinping's congratulatory letter to the History Society of the People's Republic of China on its 30th anniversary. The letter asked researchers of national history to help people "firmly establish historical confidence" and strengthen historical initiative. Yang argues that this task combines political and scientific requirements and that research on the history of New China should be deepened so that it can educate people through history.

The article is a commentary organised under four headings. They are: the historical logic and inevitability of socialism with Chinese characteristics; the major achievements and historical experience of socialist construction since 1949; the intellectual, theoretical, institutional and cultural legacies of earlier generations; and the scholarly transmission of the history of the Chinese nation's progress since modern times. Yang draws on Mao Zedong's Yan'an-era writings, Deng Xiaoping, and the Party's two historical resolutions of 1981 and 2021.

Yang's central claim is that historical confidence must rest on a grasp of historical logic and inevitability. In this account, socialism with Chinese characteristics is the conclusion of more than 180 years of modern Chinese history, over 500 years of world socialism and more than 5,000 years of Chinese civilisation. Yang holds that summing up achievements and experience is both a political and Party-spirit requirement and a scientific one, since good history highlights the "essence and mainstream" of events. Yang also calls for more study of the thought and institutional legacies of Mao Zedong, Zhou Enlai, Liu Shaoqi, Zhu De, Deng Xiaoping and Chen Yun, within a people-centred view of history that still credits leading figures.

Yang concludes that New China history, the "soul" of which is Party history, is the composite vehicle for what the article calls the "four histories". Yang admits it began late and has not yet fully formed the features of an independent discipline. Yang urges researchers to organise the field around the theme of national rejuvenation and the three leaps of standing up, becoming prosperous and becoming strong, so as to strengthen the Four-sphere Confidence. Read the original if you want to see how a senior Party historian links the discipline's tasks to official guidance on historical confidence in 2023.
quoteEn: Summing up historical achievements and historical experience is a distinct political and Party-spirit requirement of research on Party history and the history of New China.
quoteZh: 总结历史成就和历史经验，是党史研究和新中国史研究鲜明的政治性要求与党性要求。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed by Xi Jinping, especially in the context of the Party's 2021 history resolution. It means confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics, grounded in knowledge of Party and national history.

The study of the People's Republic of China since 1949. It is treated in China as a distinct field alongside Party history, reform and opening-up history, socialist development history and national history.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The formula is associated with Xi Jinping's leadership.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism, associated with Deng Xiaoping and the reform era.

t: The distinctive strengths of the Communist Party of China as a century-old large party
zh: 中国共产党百年大党的独特优势
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2023 no. 1
paras: Writing after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Liu Honglin takes up the Congress report's call to stay clear-headed and resolute about solving the "unique problems of a large party". Liu argues that to meet this demand the Party must draw on lessons from its hundred years of struggle and understand the distinctive strengths it has as a century-old large party. The article identifies five: political, theoretical, institutional, organisational and spiritual, together with Party building as a "magic weapon".

Liu begins by reading the Congress wording closely: the emphasis falls on "clear-headedness and resolve", and the unique problems are specific to the world's largest Marxist governing party remaining in power for the long term. Liu links them to supervising power, opposing corruption, self-reform and escaping the historical cycle of rise and fall. Each of the five sections then traces one strength from the Party's early congresses and revolutionary bases through the reform era to the period after the 18th Party Congress (2012), quoting Mao Zedong, Xi Jinping and the 2021 Party history resolution.

The core argument is a ranking of the five strengths. Putting the people first is the political strength and the "red thread" running through all the others. Theoretical innovation that keeps pace with the times, through adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, gives guidance. Centralised and unified Party leadership is the key institutional strength. A tight organisational system, which Liu says has at least ten levels, 96.712 million members and 4.936 million primary organisations at the end of 2021, and strict discipline supply support. The spirit of self-reform, shown in anti-corruption campaigns from the 1920s to the present, supplies drive. Liu contends that no other party in the world pursues Party building and self-reform so consistently.

Liu concludes that these advantages become decisive only if they are turned into a winning position through full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and continued work on the new great project of Party building. Party building is therefore presented as the means of preserving existing strengths and creating new ones. The article answers the Party's historical-cycle question with Xi Jinping's "second answer", the Party's self-reform, alongside Mao's earlier answer of popular supervision. Read the original if you want a detailed account of how Party scholarship frames the Party's strengths, and how it uses the 20th Party Congress concept of the "unique problems of a large party".
quoteEn: Upholding the people's standpoint and putting the people first is the "red thread" that runs through all of the Party's strengths.
quoteZh: 坚持人民立场、人民至上是贯穿党的所有优势的“一条红线”

glossary.en: unique problems of a large party
glossary.literal: problems unique to a large party
glossary.explanation: A phrase introduced in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It refers to the difficulties facing a very large Marxist party in long-term rule, such as supervising power, corruption and keeping the Party's character unchanged.

Xi Jinping's term for the Party's efforts to discipline, purify and renew itself. It is presented officially as the "second answer" to the question of how to escape the historical cycle of rise and decline.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The policy of strict Party discipline and anti-corruption work pursued since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for developing Marxist theory in line with China's conditions and each historical period.

glossary.en: the historical cycle of rise and fall
glossary.explanation: The pattern of dynasties and regimes flourishing and then collapsing. Huang Yanpei raised it with Mao Zedong in 1945, in the exchange known as the "cave dialogue" (窑洞对), and Party leaders cite it when discussing long-term rule.

t: Ren Bishi and the Northwest Bureau senior cadres conference
zh: 任弼时与西北局高干会
paras: This article, from the journal Party Literature (2022, no. 3), examines the senior cadres conference of the CPC Central Committee's Northwest Bureau, held from 19 October 1942 to 14 January 1943. Mao Zedong called it an "examination" in the Rectification campaign. Wang Guangxin argues that Ren Bishi, entrusted by the Central Committee, guided the conference from start to finish and contributed decisively to its success and to the implementation of its decisions. The author also presents the conference as significant for the Party-wide Rectification campaign.

The article follows three stages. The first covers the preparation: Ren's promotion of rectification study in the Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region, and his investigations into Party–government–army–people relations, the border region economy and Party history. The second covers the conference itself, under three headings: Party centralised and unified leadership, shifting the focus of work to production, and resolving historical problems of the Northern Shaanxi Party. The third covers the aftermath in the border region and other base areas.

Wang's central claim is that Ren's guidance combined theory with fieldwork. Ren traced disunity, such as disputes over salt transport and over the garrison corps' relation to the Northwest Bureau, to weak Party spirit among some cadres. At the conference he argued that the Party is the highest form of proletarian organisation and that democratic centralism is not to be shaken. He told cadres that production was now the "central link" and that wartime mobilisation habits had to change. He also proposed using familiar labour-exchange teams rather than a new name for labour mutual-aid.

On historical problems, Wang describes Ren's long investigation of the mistaken 1930s purges in Northern Shaanxi. It led to the Central Committee's December 1942 re-examination decision, which the article says Mao endorsed. Wang concludes that the conference strengthened centralised leadership, drove the production campaign (the article cites 1943 figures for land reclaimed and self-sufficiency), clarified Party history and strengthened unity. Wang presents this as a good result in the "examination" and as a model for other base areas. Read the original if you study the Yan'an Rectification campaign, Ren Bishi's role, or the Party's wartime handling of leadership, economy and history.
quoteEn: Developing production is the central link in all of our work today.
quoteZh: 发展生产是我们今天全部工作的中心一环

glossary.explanation: The Yan'an-period campaign (from 1942) to correct subjectivism, sectarianism and formulaic writing, the "three work styles", through study of documents and criticism and self-criticism.
The Communist-led base area with Yan'an as its centre, covering parts of Shaanxi, Gansu and Ningxia, during the War of Resistance against Japan.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Party, in which the individual obeys the organisation, the minority the majority, and lower levels higher levels.
The campaign of the early 1940s in which Party, army and government organs in the base areas engaged in farming and handicrafts to become self-sufficient under blockade.

t: The spiritual quality of "perseverance" in the historical experience of the Communist Party of China's century of struggle
zh: 中国共产党百年奋斗历史经验中“坚持”的精神品质
source: Teaching and Research (Jiaoxue yu yanjiu), 2022 no. 9
paras: The 2021 Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee, uses the word "persevere" (jianchi) 160 times. Shen and Jin ask what this recurring verb reveals about the Communist Party of China (CPC). They argue that the spirit of perseverance, steadfastness and tenacity running through the "ten adherences" is the volitional guarantee and source of strength that made the Party's whole historical experience possible.

The article is organised around three questions: why the Party perseveres, what it perseveres in, and how it does so. The first part traces the origins of the "persevering" struggle in the four historical periods of the century and in the Party's ideals and sense of foreboding. The second sorts the ten adherences into three levels: the subject, the object and the path of development. The third sets out the mechanisms that sustain the quality.

Shen and Jin contend that perseverance was forced by the hard road of national rejuvenation and grew from lofty ideals and a collective consciousness of hardship, expressed as concern for the nation, the people and the Party itself. On the subject level, they place leadership by the Party, self-reform, the united front and daring to struggle. On the object level, they place putting the people first and having the world in mind. On the path level, they place an independent Chinese road, now Chinese modernization, together with theoretical and practical innovation. They then identify three sustaining mechanisms. The first is an inner drive: founding the Party for the public good and governing for the people. The second is an external corrective: summing up experience, learning from setbacks and holding a correct view of Party history. The third is the logical unfolding of perseverance through a consistent guiding ideology (Marxism), a continuous genealogy of Party spirit traced to the great founding spirit, and stable policies since the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978).

The authors conclude that the Party's perseverance appears concretely as perseverance in guiding thought, in spiritual genealogy and in institutions and policy. In their account, guiding thought fixes its nature, the spiritual genealogy gives it character and policy expresses it in action. Only when the abstract and the concrete are united, they argue, can the quality be passed on and developed. Read the original if you want a close reading of how a Party-affiliated academic account derives a psychological and moral "quality" from the 2021 Resolution's historical summary and ties it to the Party's account of its own legitimacy.
quoteEn: The greatness of the Communist Party of China lies not in avoiding mistakes but in being good at summing up experience and reflecting on lessons, always upholding truth and correcting errors, so that the idea of "perseverance" keeps advancing in the right direction.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的伟大不在于不犯错误，而在于善于总结经验和反思教训，始终坚持真理，修正错误，保证“坚持”思想始终朝着正确的方向不断前进。

glossary.explanation: The ten items of historical experience summarised in the 2021 Resolution on the Party's century of struggle, such as upholding Party leadership, putting the people first and self-reform.
The Party's capacity to examine and correct its own problems, a theme emphasised in official discourse under Xi Jinping.
The official term for China's path of modernization, presented as distinct from Western models.
The official term for the chain of named Party 'spirits' (such as the Long March spirit), traced to the great founding spirit.

t: The documentary value of Zhou Enlai's "The Current Situation and Tasks of the War of Resistance" in elaborating "protracted resistance"
zh: 周恩来《目前抗战形势及任务》阐发“长期抗战”的文献价值
paras: This article examines a little-noticed report outline by Zhou Enlai, "The Current Situation and Tasks of the War of Resistance" (Mudian kangzhan xingshi ji renwu), which the authors present as an important early statement of the idea of "protracted resistance" against Japan. The text survives in Bai Shui's book Zhou Enlai and Deng Yingchao, first published in Hankou in April 1938 and reissued in 2014. The authors argue that the outline shows Zhou applying Marxist standpoint and method to China's concrete conditions, and that it is a valuable source for studies of Zhou's thought and of the War of Resistance.

The article has three parts. The first traces the document's publication history: Li and Wu compare it with entries in Zhou's chronology and with four pre-1949 versions under slightly different titles, and conclude that it is the outline of Zhou's report of 17 December 1937 to representatives of Xi'an organisations. The second summarises the content in three sections: lessons from four months of full-scale war, the crisis of resistance and the way out, and the tasks of sustaining a long war. The third assesses the document's value.

On the first section, the authors report Zhou's view that the war had raised national self-confidence and begun to create a unified political authority through Kuomintang–Communist cooperation. Early military setbacks, in his analysis, came from Japan's greater strength and long preparation, from collaborators and pro-Japanese elements, and from weak mobilisation. The article reads Zhou as locating the real crisis not in lost territory but in wavering inside the anti-Japanese camp and the rise of capitulationism. His remedy was to consolidate and expand the anti-Japanese national united front on the basis of Kuomintang–Communist cooperation, build a unified national defence government and army, and mobilise and organise millions of people. The authors also cite Zhou's refusal in February 1938 of Chiang Kai-shek's proposal that the Communist Party dissolve into the Kuomintang, as evidence of both independence and flexibility in the united front.

The authors conclude that the document enriches research on Zhou's military thought. They place it in a sequence of his statements from July to December 1937 in which his understanding of a protracted war deepened as the situation changed. They also hold that it offers further angles for the history of the War of Resistance, notably its treatment of protracted resistance through the united front. Read the original if you are a historian of the Chinese Communist Party, of Zhou Enlai or of the anti-Japanese war and want the source-tracing of this outline and its place among Zhou's wartime texts.
quoteEn: Zhou Enlai was one of the earlier leaders among Chinese Communists to foresee that the War of Resistance against Japan would be a long, protracted war.
quoteZh: 周恩来是中国共产党人中较早预见抗日战争是长期战、持久战的领导人之一。

glossary.explanation: The strategic line, advanced by Communist leaders from 1937, that China should prepare for a long war against Japan instead of seeking a quick decisive battle or a negotiated peace.
The alliance of the Communist Party, the Kuomintang and other forces against Japanese invasion, formed in 1937 on the basis of Kuomintang–Communist cooperation.
The second period of cooperation between the Kuomintang and the Communist Party, announced in September 1937 after the full-scale Japanese invasion.
Zhou's term for a government based on national unity and focused on resisting Japan, which he proposed building on the existing Nationalist government.

t: Accelerating the construction of the "three major systems" of historical theory research in the new era
st: Preface to a five-volume series and an account of the founding of the Institute of Historical Theory
zh: 加快构建新时代历史理论研究“三大体系”
source: Historiography Theory Studies (Shixue lilun yanjiu), 2023 no. 1
paras: Xia Chuntao, writing in early 2023, introduces a five-volume series, Frontier Series of Historical Theory Research in the New Era, and uses it to explain why the Institute of Historical Theory was founded and what it should do. The series collects articles from the institute's journal, and it is the institute's first collective publication. Xia's thesis is that historical theory research must be built up quickly into the "three major systems" (discipline, academic and discourse systems), with historical materialism as its guide.

The piece has three parts. The first reads the institute's name and gives three reasons for its creation. The second goes through its nine research offices and their projects. The third reviews the journal's transformation since 2019, the contents of the five volumes, and what Xia calls the "founding spirit" of unity, pragmatism and perseverance.

Xia argues that the name "historical theory", rather than "historiographical theory", signals the primacy of historical materialism, and that the concept of historical theory takes priority over that of historiographical theory. The three reasons are these. First, a correct view of history is needed against historical nihilism. Second, history should serve contemporary China, and Xia criticises scholarship that is detached from reality, "fragmented" and heavy on textual criticism but light on theory. Third, Chinese historiography has a weaker international voice than the country's standing warrants. Xia urges selective, critical engagement with Western currents such as postmodern historiography, global history, the "New Qing History" and the history of emotions. The nine offices, Xia says, link ancient and modern, Chinese and foreign. Xia stresses that upholding historical materialism and developing it go together, citing the Party's treatment of the five-social-formations theory as a guide rather than a dogma. Success, Xia says, is measured by producing results and talent, because people are the core element of the three systems.

Xia concludes that the new era offers historical theory unprecedented opportunity, and calls on the institute to combine basic theory with applied policy research, and historical with contemporary research. Xia also acknowledges that the four newer offices started late and lack accumulated scholarship, and that traditional strengths in historiographical studies have weakened. The text is an institutional self-presentation as well as a programme. Read the original if you want to understand how a leading Chinese institute defines its mission, structure and priorities in historical theory under the current political guidance.
quoteEn: The key to measuring the effectiveness of building the "three major systems" is whether they produce results and produce talent.
quoteZh: 衡量“三大体系”建设之成效，关键看是否出成果、出人才。

glossary.explanation: In official Chinese discourse, a label for interpretations seen as denying or distorting the main course of Chinese history, especially Communist Party history and the socialist path. The author treats it as a harmful trend of thought.

A policy formula calling for China's own discipline system, academic system and discourse system in philosophy and the social sciences. It was promoted by Xi Jinping from 2016 and restated in the 20th Party Congress report (2022).
The Marxist theory of history that explains social development through material production and class relations. In China it is the officially mandated guiding framework for historical research.

t: The Communist Party of China's war behind enemy lines through Norman Bethune's eyes, 1938–1939
st: Based on the Bethune archives held overseas
zh: 白求恩眼中的中国共产党敌后抗战（1938-1939）
zhSub: 以海外藏白求恩档案为中心
source: Documents of the Party (Dang de wenxian), 2022 no. 2
paras: The article asks how Norman Bethune, the Canadian Communist surgeon who came to China in 1938 and died in Hebei in November 1939, saw the Communist Party of China and the resistance war it led behind Japanese lines. Guo and Zhu argue that Bethune was not merely an observer but a participant. In their account he recorded conditions faithfully, judged the Party's line highly and publicised its war effort abroad.

The source base is the newly digitised Norman Bethune Papers at the Osler Library of the History of Medicine, McGill University, which hold more than 300 items in five collections. The authors first survey the archive in three groups: material from before China, Bethune's letters, reports, diaries, writings and photographs from his time in China, and later Sino-Canadian commemorative records. They then analyse his China-period documents under two headings: his record of the battlefield, and his evaluation and promotion of the Party's resistance.

On the first heading, the authors cite Bethune's reports and letters on Japanese bombing and atrocities, and on severe shortages of trained medical staff, drugs, instruments and food for the wounded in the base areas. They also cite his diary impressions of Yan'an and the Anti-Japanese Military and Political University, where he noted egalitarian practice and high morale. On the second, they say Bethune called the Party the best national Communist party he had seen. He endorsed its protracted-war strategy, united front policy and guerrilla warfare, and held that mass mobilisation was the key to survival and growth.

The authors describe Bethune's propaganda work as four-fold: a 1938 dispatch for the Manchester Guardian, the story 'The Dud Shell' and the essay 'Wounds' for North American publications, a Jin-Cha-Ji branch of a foreign-publicity association, and the use of treated Japanese prisoners as material. They conclude that his writings show the Party leading the war in the right direction and sustaining national hope, and that he brought this to international audiences. Read the original if you want a source-based account of foreign perceptions of the Communist-led resistance, or a guide to the Bethune materials at McGill.
quoteEn: Bethune was not only a witness to and participant in the Chinese nation's War of Resistance against Japan, but also an important propagandist.
quoteZh: 白求恩不仅是中华民族抗日战争的亲历者和参与者，还是一个重要的宣传者。

t: Meeting challenges with a fighting spirit, opening up the future through striving
zh: 以斗争精神迎接挑战 以奋进拼搏开辟未来
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) in early 2023, Zhou Junjie takes up the question of why the Communist Party of China must keep and develop a "fighting spirit" (douzheng jingshen) on the new journey after the 20th Party Congress (2022). The article contends that the Party has reached its present position through struggle and must rely on struggle to win the future. It places this within Xi Jinping's call for full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and the Party's self-reform.

The piece has three parts. The first presents daring and skilful struggle as the "spiritual code" behind the Party's achievements, drawing on Marxist dialectics and the Party's history. The second sets out why struggle is especially needed now, looking in turn at the international situation, domestic conditions and the state of the Party. The third sets out how to carry out struggle on the new journey.

Zhou argues that contradiction is universal and that new things grow only through hardship, citing Mao Zedong and Engels. The article describes the world as undergoing changes unseen in a century, with technological competition, geopolitical tension, supply-chain disruption and what it calls hegemonic bullying. At home it lists unbalanced development, dependence on imported key components and Western pressure over trade, technology, finance, Taiwan and the South China Sea. Within the Party it identifies slackness, official inaction and the persistence of corruption risks. Its prescription has three strands: keep historical initiative and the correct political direction, including the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds; build confidence and take the initiative in struggle, with leading cadres setting an example; and raise capabilities and a sense of responsibility. It adds that struggle is an art: seize the principal contradiction, hold firm on principle, stay flexible on tactics, and unite all forces that can be united.

Zhou concludes that, with the first centenary goal achieved, the Party must meet the second with a strong sense of responsibility and a willingness to fight, and must solve the "unique problems of a large party". The article is a Party-theoretical commentary that conveys how the official line links struggle, Party discipline and national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want to see how a military-academy Party theorist presents the fighting spirit in official discourse after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Precisely because it is arduous it is great; precisely because it is arduous, struggle is all the more needed.
quoteZh: 惟其艰巨，所以伟大；惟其艰巨，更需斗争。

glossary.explanation: A Party term for readiness to confront risks and opponents. Since the 18th Party Congress (2012) Xi Jinping has stressed it, and the 20th Party Congress (2022) listed it among principles to uphold.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's disciplinary and anti-corruption campaign and wider Party-building drive under Xi Jinping.
A formulation in Xi Jinping-era discourse that describes the Party as correcting its own problems without outside pressure.
A formula adopted in 2021–22 that affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and the guiding role of his thought.
The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised leadership of the Central Committee.

t: Dare to struggle and be good at struggle
zh: 敢于斗争 善于斗争
authors: Guangdong Research Center for Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily and written by a Guangdong provincial research centre on Xi Jinping Thought (drafted by Zhang Hao), takes up the call in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) that all Party members must be willing and able to struggle. It argues that the Party was born amid domestic and foreign troubles and has grown through hardship. In the authors' account, a spirit of struggle runs through every period of its history and must now be carried into the new journey.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out why the 'great struggle' with 'many new historical features' is long-term, complex and arduous. The second explains where confidence for that struggle comes from. The third lists what the Party must do to win new victories: sharpen awareness of danger, strengthen will and skills, and keep strategic confidence and resolve.

On long-term, complex and arduous, the authors point to the changing world, China's continued position in the primary stage of socialism, and the Party's lasting tests and dangers, such as self-complacency, corruption and detachment from the masses. They add that 'black swan' and 'grey rhino' events may occur at any time, and that the nearer the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation comes, the greater the risks. Confidence is said to rest on four sources: the Party's firm leadership, with the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds; the guidance of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era; the advantages of the socialist system with Chinese characteristics; and the united effort of the people.

The authors conclude that the Party, having reached today through struggle, will win the future the same way. They call for awareness of potential danger and bottom-line thinking, for cadres to build fighting will and capability and take the lead in crises, and for strategic confidence combined with tactical flexibility. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated research centres present the 20th Congress's language on struggle and risk to cadres.
quoteEn: Our Party has come this far by relying on struggle, and it will inevitably have to rely on struggle to win the future.
quoteZh: 我们党依靠斗争走到今天，也必然要依靠斗争赢得未来。

glossary.explanation: A formulation from the 2022 Party resolution and the 20th Party Congress affirming Xi Jinping's position as the Party's core and the guiding role of his thought.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.
The official characterisation of China's present level of development, in which it is said to remain for a long time.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central national goal in Party discourse, associated with the Chinese Dream and the 'second centenary goal' of building a modern socialist country by 2049.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.

t: Qiushi commentator: advancing full and rigorous self-governance of the Party without pause
zh: 《求是》杂志评论员：一刻不停推进全面从严治党
paras: This commentary, issued under the label of a Qiushi magazine commentator in early 2023, responds to Xi Jinping's 9 January speech at the Second Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection. It presents the speech as a strategic deployment for continuing full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, and argues that the Party must advance it "without pause" and carry the Party's great self-reform through to the end.

The piece first frames the issue historically, then turns to the speech's main themes. It recalls Mao Zedong's Yan'an-era answer to escaping the historical cycle of rise and decline (popular supervision of government) and presents self-reform as the second answer. It then covers the "unique problems of a large party", the building of a governance system, and seven practical tasks for the new journey.

The commentary's core claim is that a decade of rigorous Party governance has produced results, which it supports with a 2022 opinion survey by the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the National Bureau of Statistics. According to the survey, 97.4 per cent of respondents considered the effort effective, 22.4 points higher than in 2012. It then lists the "six how-to-always" challenges Xi set out, such as keeping the original aspiration, unifying thought and will, and spotting and solving the Party's own problems. The tasks it derives are political supervision, the eight-point regulations and the "four forms of decadence", discipline building, anti-corruption work, a stronger supervision system and a loyal inspection corps. Anti-corruption is to advance through making officials unwilling, unable and afraid to be corrupt, with zero tolerance.

The commentary concludes that Party organisations and members should study the speech, grasp the Two Establishes, and strengthen the Four Consciousnesses, the Four-sphere Confidence and the Two Upholds. It says political supervision should guarantee that the 20th Party Congress (2022) decisions are carried out and give a firm start to building a modern socialist country. Read the original if you want an authoritative example of how Party media presented the 2023 anti-corruption and discipline agenda, with its official vocabulary and survey figures.
quoteEn: The system of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party should be a dynamic system with rich content, complete functions, scientific standards and efficient operation.
quoteZh: 全面从严治党体系应是一个内涵丰富、功能完备、科学规范、运行高效的动态系统。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: Official slogan for the campaign, associated with Xi Jinping since 2012, to tighten Party discipline, conduct and anti-corruption enforcement.
Official formula, adopted in 2021–22, affirming Xi Jinping's position as core of the Party and the guiding role of his thought.
Official requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the Central Committee's authority and centralised leadership.
Official formula of confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
Rules on official conduct issued by the Central Committee in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism among officials.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Promoting the spiritual lineage of Chinese Communists, with the great founding spirit of the Party as its source
zh: 弘扬以伟大建党精神为源头的中国共产党人精神谱系
authors: Theoretical Study Centre Group of the Party Affairs Meeting, Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee
paras: This Qiushi article, written collectively by the theoretical study group of the Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee, responds to the 20th Party Congress (2022). The Congress put promoting the great founding spirit of the Party into its theme and wrote that spirit into the Party Constitution. The authors argue that the spiritual lineage of Chinese Communists, which has the founding spirit as its source, is a core strength of the Party and should be turned into spiritual support for building a modern socialist country and achieving national rejuvenation.

The piece has three sections. The first reads the Party's century of history as a unity of a history of struggle and a history of spirit. The second explains why the lineage is the Party's "genetic code". The third sets out how to apply it on the new journey. The first section goes through four periods: the new-democratic revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era. For each it names the main task and a list of "spirits", from the Jinggangshan and Yan'an spirits to the poverty-alleviation, anti-epidemic and scientists' spirits.

The authors' central claim is that great undertakings give rise to great spirit, and great spirit leads great undertakings.
