They attribute the Party's vitality to four traits that the lineage embodies: advanced thought and firm belief in Marxism and communism; an unchanged original aspiration to seek happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the nation; tenacity and fine conduct, illustrated by casualty and sacrifice figures; and loyalty to the Party and to the people. For the present, they call for drawing four kinds of strength from the lineage: the power of truth, of practice and struggle, of personal character, and of wisdom (historical initiative). Each is tied to a task, such as studying Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, sustaining a fighting spirit, standing with the people, and taking a long historical view.

The article concludes by calling on the whole Party to rally around the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core and to promote the lineage as it sets out toward new goals. It cites Xi's visit to Yan'an after the Congress as a sign of the leadership's intent to carry on the Party's red heritage. Read the original if you want an authoritative statement of how Party theorists framed the "spiritual lineage" and the founding spirit after the 20th Party Congress, including its periodisation and its list of named spirits.
quoteEn: Great undertakings give birth to great spirit, and great spirit leads great undertakings.
quoteZh: 伟大事业孕育伟大精神，伟大精神引领伟大事业。

glossary.en: great founding spirit of the Party
glossary.explanation: A formulation Xi Jinping presented at the 2021 centenary of the Party. It names the spirit of the Party's founders as upholding truth and ideals, practising the original aspiration and mission, fearless struggle, and loyalty to the Party and the people.

glossary.zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系
glossary.explanation: The official term for a series of named "spirits" (such as the Long March spirit and the Yan'an spirit) that the Party says arose in successive periods of its history. The founding spirit is presented as their common source.
A term used in Party discourse for consciously grasping historical laws and trends in order to shape events rather than be shaped by them.
The official name for the Party's path of socialist development since reform and opening up.

t: Carrying the Party's great self-reform in the new era through to the end
zh: 把新时代党的伟大自我革命进行到底
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in early 2023, Yang Fei, a Guangzhou Party discipline official, takes up Xi Jinping's call of December 2022 to see the Party's "great self-reform" through to the end. The article argues that full and rigorous self-governance of the Party has produced an "overwhelming victory" against corruption, but that the struggle is far from finished and must be sustained with firm political resolve.

The piece is a study-and-implementation essay on Xi's Politburo speech and the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It has three parts: why self-reform is the Party's "second answer" to the historical cycle of rise and fall; what full and rigorous self-governance has achieved over the past decade; and what discipline inspection and supervision organs must now do. It closes with a note on Guangzhou's own tasks.

Yang's central claim is that willingness to undertake the Party's self-reform follows from the Party's nature and purpose: it has no interests of its own and represents none of the interest groups or privileged strata. Self-reform and social revolution, in this account, reinforce each other, and a Party of over 96 million members must watch for problems peculiar to large parties, as the Soviet collapse is said to show. For the decade since 2012, Yang credits the Eight-point Regulations, the anti-corruption campaign and the Two Establishes with strengthening Party unity. Yang cites a poll in which 97.4 per cent of respondents rated the campaign effective, 22.4 points above 2012. The practical agenda covers political supervision, a stronger system of Party regulations, continued correction of the "four undesirable work styles", and zero tolerance of corruption, including "new-type" and hidden forms.

Yang concludes that discipline organs must keep a tough tone and uphold the centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee as the basis of self-reform. Yang also calls for tighter oversight of top leaders and of corruption involving officials' relatives, and for joint punishment of bribe-givers. Guangzhou, described as at the "two frontlines", is urged to pioneer measures against cross-border and new corruption. Read the original if you want an example of how a local discipline-inspection chief translates the 20th Party Congress line on Party self-reform into concrete anti-corruption tasks.
quoteEn: Having the courage to undertake self-reform is the Party's most distinctive political character and also its greatest strength.
quoteZh: 勇于自我革命，是我们党最鲜明的政治品格，也是我们党最大的优势。

glossary.explanation: Official term for the Party's efforts to purify, improve and renew itself through discipline, anti-corruption work and institutional rules. Xi Jinping presents it as the Party's answer to the problem of how a ruling party avoids decline.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Slogan for the Party-building and anti-corruption drive launched after the 18th Party Congress (2012), stressing strict discipline, ideological education and supervision.
Formula adopted in 2021–22 affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the whole Party, and the guiding status of his thought.
Rules issued in December 2012 to curb official extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism, regarded as the starting point of the post-2012 discipline campaign.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Chen Yun's explorations in advancing the Party's political building in the Yan'an period
zh: 延安时期陈云推进党的政治建设的探索
source: Documents of the Party (Dang de wenxian), 2022 no. 6
paras: Writing after the 20th Party Congress (2022), which stressed strengthening the Party's political building, Liu Dong asks what Chen Yun contributed to this task during the Yan'an period. Liu argues that Chen, then head of the Central Organization Department, worked out a substantial body of ideas on political building through practice and summing up experience. These ideas, the article holds, still offer guidance for the new great project of Party building in the new era.

The article is organised around four themes that mirror the 2019 Central Committee opinions on strengthening the Party's political building: firm political belief, upholding the authority of the Central Committee and centralised, unified leadership, building political capacity, and carrying measures through in organisation and implementation. Liu draws on Chen's speeches and writings from 1935 to 1947, including 'How to Be a Communist Party Member' (1939), his writings on branch work, and his drafting of Organization Department decisions on cadres. The material is set against the Party's rapid expansion and the mixed class background of its new members.

Liu's central claim is that Chen tied belief, discipline and practice together. On belief, Chen required members to study Marxist theory, led a study group in the Organization Department, and insisted that the interests of the people and the Party are identical. On authority, he backed Mao Zedong as the leading core, demanded the 'four subordinations' (individual to organisation, minority to majority, lower level to higher, whole Party to the Central Committee) and held that a core leadership forms only through strict democratic centralism. On capacity and implementation, Liu reports Chen's four tasks for Party branches, his insistence on mass work led by the Party, his view that theory must be combined with practical experience, his emphasis on criticism and self-criticism, and his rule that cadres be selected with politics first and ability second, 'with virtue primary'.

Liu concludes that Chen's Yan'an ideas are a valuable asset of the Party and should be studied and drawn on today, so that the Party's political building can play its leading role and the Party remains the firm leadership core of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The article is largely expository, presenting Chen's views through extended quotation. Read the original if you want a detailed, source-based account of Chen Yun's Yan'an-era thinking on Party discipline, cadre selection and branch work, as it is presented in current Party-history scholarship.
quoteEn: Chen Yun saw the raising of Party members' and cadres' political capacity as an organic and unified process in which theory and practice interact and complement each other.
quoteZh: 陈云将党员干部政治能力的提高看作是一个理论和实践相互作用、相辅相成的有机统一过程。

glossary.explanation: A strand of Party building concerned with political orientation, loyalty to the Central Committee, discipline and political ecology. The 20th Party Congress report said it should guide all other Party-building work.
The Party's fundamental organisational principle, combining internal discussion with binding central decisions and subordination of lower bodies to higher ones.
A summary of Party discipline: individual to organisation, minority to majority, lower level to higher level, and the whole Party to the Central Committee.
A Party method of resolving internal contradictions and correcting errors through open critique of others and of oneself, widely practised from the Yan'an period.

t: Basic experience of the Communist Party of China's century-long construction of political identification
zh: 中国共产党百年政治认同建设的基本经验
paras: Wang and Li ask how the Communist Party of China has built and kept the political identification of the people over its first hundred years. Political identification, they define, is members of society's psychological belonging, emotional attachment and behavioural support towards their political system. The authors argue that the Party worked along four dimensions: interests as the foundation, institutions as the safeguard, emotion as the key link, and values as the point of belonging. Together, they say, these formed a unified force behind what they call the two miracles of rapid economic growth and long-term social stability.

The article takes each dimension in turn and traces it through four periods: the New Democratic Revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics. It draws on Marx, Engels, Lenin, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping, and also cites Aristotle, Rawls and Freud. It closes with a short conclusion on how the four dimensions fit together.

In the authors' account, interest identification comes first: land reform, the consolidation of people's status as masters of the country, the end of hunger and poverty, and a better life for all. Because interests are changeable, institutional identification is needed, and it rests on fair and just institutions such as the 1954 Constitution, the basic economic system and whole-process people's democracy. Emotional identification is built through the Party's moral conduct in office: rectification campaigns, discipline, anti-corruption work and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Value identification, the most stable and highest level, comes from ideological work, from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and from core socialist values.

Wang and Li conclude that the four dimensions follow a logical progression and priority order, and that stable identification requires all four to be fused. They hold that, in a period of great global change and national rejuvenation, the Party must keep its close ties to the people if it is to preserve its legitimacy as a long-term ruling party. Read the original if you want a structured, officially aligned account of how Party theorists explain popular support for the CPC across its history.
quoteEn: Interests as the foundation, institutions as the safeguard, emotion as the bond and values as the point of belonging: these are the four dimensions of the Party's construction of political identification, and they stand in a logical progression and an order of priority.
quoteZh: 以利益认同为基础、以制度认同为保障、以情感认同为纽带、以价值认同为归属，这是党政治认同建构的四重维度，存在逻辑递进关系和发展优先次序

glossary.explanation: A concept in Chinese political science and Party-building writing for citizens' sense of belonging to, and support for, a political system or ruling party. The article treats it as a source of the Party's legitimacy.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A strategy stressed since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering ideological education, discipline and anti-corruption within the Party.
Official term for China's democratic model, promoted under Xi Jinping. It claims to cover every stage of political and policy processes, not just elections.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions.

t: Problems unique to a large party: what is "unique" and where lies the "difficulty"
zh: 大党独有难题：“何为独有”又“难在何处”
paras: Xu Yanling takes up a formulation from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): that the Communist Party of China, as the world's largest Marxist governing party, must stay clear-headed and firm in solving "problems unique to a large party". Writing in the People's Forum, Xu reads the phrase as a deepening of Xi Jinping's earlier remark that a large party has "large difficulties". The article argues that these problems are best understood at three levels: governing the Party, governing a large country, and global governance.

The article is organised into three sections, one for each level. The first concerns Party governance and the "historical cycle" of rise and decline. The second concerns the governance of a vast and complex country in the course of Chinese modernization. The third concerns the Party's role in reforming global governance and building a community with a shared future for mankind. Each section ends with a short summary of why the difficulty is distinctive.

On Party governance, Xu cites official figures of 96.712 million members and 4.936 million primary organisations at the end of 2021. The author argues that growth in size brings new problems: diverse membership, "detached" members, weakened organisation in some places, and a wider age range. Xu sets "four tests" (governing, reform and opening up, the market economy, the external environment) as external causes against "four dangers" (slackening of spirit, insufficient capacity, detachment from the masses, corruption) as internal causes. Their combination is said to catalyse the historical cycle, and self-reform is presented as the second answer to it. On governing the country, Xu identifies a basic difficulty in a huge and uneven society, a process difficulty in pursuing Chinese modernization as a late developer under Western pressure, and a goal difficulty in the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, where haste and complacency must both be avoided. On the global level, Xu describes an objective difficulty (deficits in peace, development, security and governance), a difficulty of agency (reduced willingness among states, with the United States and its allies accused of abandoning treaties and organisations), and a practical difficulty (value consensus and public goods). The author attributes resistance to Western ideology and to "Thucydides trap" and "Kindleberger trap" thinking.

Xu concludes that the Party faces both difficulties specific to the era and difficulties of its own in promoting a community with a shared future for mankind. In the author's account, it is meeting them as a responsible century-old party, joining its own development to that of the world. Read the original if you want a structured Chinese-language account of how Party theorists frame the "unique problems" formula, and of how they link Party building, domestic governance and foreign policy.
quoteEn: In sum, judging from the historical position and governing environment of our Party, the "four tests" are the external factors and the "four dangers" are the internal factors.
quoteZh: 综上，从我们党所处的历史方位和执政环境来看，“四大考验”是外因，“四大危险”是内因

glossary.en: problems unique to a large party
glossary.literal: difficulties unique to a big party
glossary.explanation: A formulation in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), developed from Xi Jinping's earlier remark that a large party has large difficulties. It refers to the challenges of governing a very large ruling party in a very large country.

The idea, raised in the 1945 Yan'an "cave dwelling conversation" between Huang Yanpei and Mao Zedong, that regimes tend to rise and then decline. Party writers present supervision by the people and the Party's self-reform as ways to escape it.

The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is distinguished from Western modernization by features such as huge population scale and common prosperity.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, tied to the two centenary goals for 2021 and 2049. It is framed as restoring China's historical standing.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for China's approach to international relations and global governance, stressing interdependence and shared values.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: We must always remain clear-headed and resolute in tackling the problems unique to a large party
zh: 必须时刻保持解决大党独有难题的清醒和坚定
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in early 2023, Zhan Chengfu takes up a formula from Xi Jinping's report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): to keep the people's support and consolidate its long-term governing position, the Communist Party must stay clear-headed and resolute about the problems unique to a large party. Zhan presents this as a deepening of Xi's argument that the Party escapes the historical cycle of rise and fall through the Party's self-reform. The article is an interpretive commentary that treats confronting such problems as a mark of the Party's vanguard character.

The piece has three parts. The first explains why the Party is distinctive and lists the difficulties that follow, citing figures of 96.712 million members and 4.936 million primary organizations at the end of 2021. The second reviews a decade of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third sets out eight tasks for continuing it.

Zhan names three distinctive features: the Party's heavy historical mission, its long-term single-party rule, and its unmatched size. From these Zhan derives three problems. The first is keeping unity of thought, will and action under a firm leadership core, illustrated by the Zunyi Conference, Zhang Guotao, Wang Ming and the Yan'an rectification campaign. The second is keeping the original aspiration and spotting its own faults, with the Soviet Communist Party cited as a party that became a privileged bureaucratic group. The third is keeping up drive and a clean political climate against the "four dangers". Zhan argues that the past decade's measures covered ideology, responsibility, discipline, cadres, work style and anti-corruption. In Zhan's account these produced a system of self-purification and showed that self-supervision, a worldwide puzzle, can be solved under one-party rule.

Zhan concludes that the Party must keep pursuing full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and the Party's self-reform to the end. Zhan lists eight measures. They include strengthening the Central Committee's centralized and unified leadership, arming the Party with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and improving the rules governing self-reform. They also cover building a high-calibre cadre corps, strengthening Party organizations, correcting work style, and fighting corruption as a protracted campaign. Read the original if you want an official-line account, from a senior government official, of how the Party frames its own organizational problems and the anti-corruption agenda after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Self-supervision is a worldwide problem; over the past decade the Communist Party of China has tackled this problem through concrete action and handed in an outstanding answer that commands fresh respect.
quoteZh: 自我监督是世界性难题，十年来，中国共产党用实际行动攻克这一“难题”，交出了令人刮目相看的优异答卷。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: Slogan for the Party's drive to tighten discipline, supervision and anti-corruption, associated with Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It was later made part of the Four Comprehensives strategy.

Xi Jinping's term for the Party's capacity to correct itself without external checks. Official texts present it as the second answer to the question of how to escape the historical cycle of rise and fall.

glossary.en: historical cycle of rise and fall
glossary.explanation: The idea, raised by Huang Yanpei in conversation with Mao Zedong in 1945, that regimes flourish and then decline. Official discourse treats avoiding it as a central task of the Party.

glossary.en: problems unique to a large party
glossary.literal: difficult problems unique to a big party
glossary.explanation: A phrase introduced in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It refers to difficulties the leadership attributes to the Party's size, long period in power and heavy responsibilities.

Official list of dangers facing the Party: mental laxity, inadequate capacity, detachment from the people, and passive corruption. It is paired with the "four tests" of long-term rule, reform and opening up, the market economy and the external environment.

t: Full and rigorous self-governance of the Party depends on improving the system
zh: 全面从严治党重在健全体系
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in early 2023, Zhao Xusheng takes up a new task set by the 20th Party Congress (2022): improving the system of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. The commentary argues that this system-building is the key to carrying the governance effort forward. In Zhao's reading, it is a comprehensive and pioneering part of Party building in the new era.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out why such a system is necessary, the second defines its content and place, and the third proposes ways to improve it. Zhao draws throughout on Xi Jinping's speeches, the Party Congress report and plenary session documents, including the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee and the Second Plenum of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection.

Zhao gives three grounds for the system. First, building a Marxist party follows a basic law that combines ideological work with governance through institutions and Party regulations. Second, the achievements of the past decade have laid a foundation: Zhao says lax and soft Party management has been fundamentally reversed, and cites Xi's six experiences. Third, the "unique problems of a large party", summarised as "six how's", can be solved fundamentally only through institution-based governance. Zhao defines the system as a dynamic whole of five subsystems: core (the Party's overall leadership), elements (organisations, members and cadres, with leading cadres as the "critical few"), structure (the overall layout of Party building), standards (strictness) and responsibility. To improve it, Zhao calls for top-level design with systems thinking, closer linkage between governance by Party regulations and the rule of law, and coordinated integration with full coverage of content, targets, responsibility chains and institutions.

Zhao concludes that building out this system is how the Party can address the problems peculiar to a large party through self-reform. The author calls for fragmented, piecemeal efforts to be avoided. Responsibility should be placed on Party committees, with secretaries treating Party building as their first responsibility and discipline commissions carrying out supervision. Read the original if you want a concise, Party School-style account of how the 20th Party Congress framed Party discipline and institution-building as a system.
quoteEn: The system of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party should be a dynamic system with rich content, complete functions, scientific norms and efficient operation.
quoteZh: 全面从严治党体系应是一个内涵丰富、功能完备、科学规范、运行高效的动态系统。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: Official slogan, part of the "Four Comprehensives" strategy since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It covers strict discipline, anti-corruption and institutional rules for Party members and organisations.

glossary.en: unique problems of a large party
glossary.literal: difficulties unique to a big party
glossary.explanation: A phrase introduced in the 20th Party Congress report. It refers to the problems of governing a very large, long-ruling party, summarised by Xi as "six how's".
Official term for leading cadres, who are held to bear the main responsibility for Party conduct and are the focus of governance efforts.

glossary.literal: governing the Party according to rules
glossary.explanation: The practice of managing the Party through intra-Party regulations, which the Party treats as part of the socialist legal system with Chinese characteristics.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: The governance advantages of a century-old Party
zh: 百年大党的治理优势
paras: Writing after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Chen Zhongkui asks why the Communist Party of China governs so well and why China has developed so quickly. The article's answer is that the Party holds three governance advantages: its leadership as the core governing agent, a clear people-centred value orientation, and a strong capacity for organisation and mobilisation. Chen presents these as strengths that should be upheld, consolidated and improved.

The piece is a Party-theory commentary built on three headed sections: the advantage of the governing subject, the advantage of values, and the advantage of effectiveness. It draws on Xi Jinping's statements, episodes from Party history from the 1927 repression to the Huaihai Campaign and poverty alleviation, and repeated contrasts with Western parties and political systems. Chen also cites Edgar Snow on Mao Zedong and Francis Fukuyama's revised view of the 'end of history'.

On the first advantage, Chen argues that any party that is to be a strong governing agent needs three conditions: lofty belief, severe trials and organisational self-renewal. In Chen's account the Party meets all three, citing the sacrifices of revolutionaries, the failure of repeated Western predictions of China's collapse, and the Party's record of self-reform from the Gutian and Zunyi meetings to full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. On values, Chen contends that the Party represents the fundamental interests of all the people, whereas Western parties represent segments of voters and so fall into endless partisan conflict. The article points to the elimination of absolute poverty as evidence. On effectiveness, Chen says the Party's tight organisation, the unity of Party spirit and the people's will, and its roots among the people let it mobilise society when needed.

Chen concludes that Party leadership is the root of the socialist system with Chinese characteristics and that without it the 'China model' would not have succeeded. The article ends with a call for all Party members to remember the Party's founding mission, stay close to the people and work toward the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want an example of how a Chinese Party-school style commentary frames the case for Party leadership as a governance advantage and contrasts it with Western party politics.
quoteEn: Party leadership is the root and source of the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the 'heart' and 'engine' of modernizing the national governance system and capacity. It governs what is fundamental, the whole and the long term, and plays an irreplaceable, guiding role.
quoteZh: 党的领导是中国特色社会主义制度体系的根和源，是国家治理体系和治理能力现代化的“心脏”和“引擎”，管根本、管全局、管长远，发挥着提纲挈领、无可替代的作用。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's discipline and anti-corruption drive since the 18th Party Congress (2012), stressing stricter internal supervision and rules.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central goal of Party discourse, referring to restoring China's national strength and international standing, with 2049 as its target date.

t: From the "Two Musts" to the "Three Musts": new vistas, new requirements and new expectations on the road of the Party's "examination"
zh: “两个务必”到“三个务必”：赶考路上的新图景、新要求、新期待
source: Journal of Xinjiang Normal University (Philosophy and Social Sciences), 2023 no. 3
paras: Zhao Maosheng and Fan Mingyang start from the image of the Communist Party as a "mission-driven party" that is always sitting an "examination" (gan…kao). They ask what situation the "Three Musts" face, what they demand and what they expect, compared with Mao Zedong's "Two Musts" of 1949. The "Three Musts" are Xi Jinping's call, made after the first centenary goal had been met, that Party members must never forget the original aspiration and keep the mission in mind, must stay modest, prudent and hard-working, and must dare and know how to struggle. The authors argue that the two formulations are continuous but that the later one is more comprehensive and systematic.

The article has three parts. The first compares the historical settings: the Second Plenary Session of the Seventh Central Committee at Xibaipo (1949), when the Party was about to become the governing party, and the present stage of national rejuvenation, with what the authors call great changes unseen in a century. The second compares the requirements each slogan places on Party members. The third compares the expectations attached to each. The authors draw on Mao's speeches and letters, Xi's statements and a few passages from Marx.

In the authors' reading, Mao's "Two Musts" (modesty and prudence, plus hard struggle) drew on the Party's earlier style of work. They were meant to guard against complacency and corruption after victory, and to help the Party escape the "historical cycle" of dynastic rise and fall. The "Three Musts" are set out as answers to three questions. "For what" is the value goal of serving the people and national rejuvenation. "Why able" is the work-style guarantee of modesty and hard work. "How" is the practical call to struggle with both courage and skill. The authors present the three as an organic whole: the first supplies the premise and goal, the second the safeguard, and the third the capacity and method.

The authors conclude that the "Three Musts" are expected to sustain firm conviction in building a modern socialist country. They are also expected to secure the path to national rejuvenation and to supply the character needed for the Party's self-reform, so that it can solve the problems unique to a large party and avoid the historical cycle. They call on Party members to keep close ties with the people and to cultivate struggle skills. They also call on them to resist hostile external forces and to correct internal weaknesses in responsibility and practical ability. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how Party theorists link Mao's 1949 warning to Xi Jinping's Party-building discourse after the 20th Party Congress (2022).
quoteEn: The "Three Musts" complement each other and form an internally coherent organic whole.
quoteZh: “三个务必”相辅相成，构成内在融贯的有机整体。

glossary.explanation: Mao Zedong's 1949 call, at the Second Plenum of the Seventh Central Committee, that comrades must keep up a modest, prudent, non-arrogant, non-rash style and a style of hard struggle.
Xi Jinping's call at the 20th Party Congress (2022): never forget the original aspiration and keep the mission in mind, remain modest, prudent and hard-working, and dare and know how to struggle.
Mao's image of 1949, when the Party moved to Beijing, of the Party sitting an examination whose judges are the people. Later leaders use it to frame ongoing governance tasks.
The pattern of dynasties flourishing and then collapsing, raised by Huang Yanpei in a 1945 conversation with Mao. Party writers present the Party's work style and self-reform as ways to escape it.
A self-description of the Communist Party as a party defined by its mission of seeking happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation.
Xi Jinping's term for the Party's continuous internal cleansing and discipline. It is presented as a second answer to the historical cycle, alongside popular supervision.

t: Improving the institutional and normative system for the Party's self-reform
zh: 完善党的自我革命制度规范体系
paras: This commentary in Guangming Daily (February 2023) takes up the call in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) to improve the institutional and normative system for the Party's self-reform. Liu Chang, a professor at Jilin University, argues that three components are central: the system of intra-Party regulations, the Party and state supervision system, and the integrated pursuit of the "three no-corruptions".

The piece opens by presenting self-reform as the second answer the Party has found to escaping the historical cycle of rise and fall. It then has three sections, each treating one component as a precondition, an institutional environment or a driving force for the system.

On regulations, Liu holds that the intra-Party regulatory system is the Party's code of conduct, rooted in full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and defined by its political character. It needs better enforcement, links with law enforcement and the judiciary, and a case-guidance system. On supervision, Liu says intra-Party supervision must lead and other forms of supervision must work in coordination. Discipline, supervisory, dispatched-office and inspection supervision are to form a "trunk" force backed by clear lists of responsibilities. On the "three no-corruptions", Liu argues for pursuing them together under the lead of Party political building. This would use mechanisms that combine early warning with punishment and accountability with tolerance of error, and would be supported by a culture of integrity.

Liu concludes that these measures turn self-reform into a lasting, stable and effective institutional system, which in turn lets it guide social revolution and modernize state governance. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Party-affiliated scholars framed the institutional agenda for self-reform after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: The Party's position as the governing party means that intra-Party supervision is the most basic and primary element in the Party and state supervision system; only when it is strong and effective can other forms of supervision play their proper role.
quoteZh: 党的执政地位决定了党内监督在党和国家监督体系中是最基本的、第一位的，党内监督有力有效，其他监督才能发挥应有作用。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering discipline, anti-corruption and Party-building measures.
The idea that the Communist Party corrects and renews itself through its own efforts. Xi Jinping presents it as the answer to the problem of how a ruling party avoids decline.
Formal rules issued by Party bodies to govern Party organisations and members. They are distinct from state law.

glossary.pinyin: bù gǎn fǔ, bù néng fǔ, bù xiǎng fǔ
glossary.literal: dare not, unable to, do not want to be corrupt
glossary.explanation: An official anti-corruption formula combining deterrence by punishment, institutional constraints and ideological or cultural prevention.

t: Holding firmly to the "ruler" of discipline in governing the Party in the new era
zh: 抓牢新时代管党治党的“戒尺”
paras: This newspaper commentary, originally published in Guangming Daily in February 2023, takes up Xi Jinping's statement at the second plenary session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection that discipline is the "ruler" (jièchǐ) for governing the Party. Liu Xiaochuan argues that discipline-building must be given greater prominence in the new era so that rules have "teeth" and officials come to respect them, take warning and know their limits.

The piece has three parts. It first presents strict discipline as a glorious tradition and distinctive strength of the Party. It then explains why discipline-building is the fundamental measure of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. It closes with practical requirements for holding on to the "ruler".

In the first part, Liu cites Marx, Engels and Lenin on the need for Party discipline, along with early Chinese communists and later Party documents, to portray a continuous tradition up to the 18th Party Congress (2012). In the second, Liu contends that some ruling parties around the world lost power because they weakened discipline, and that the Party's "four tests" and "four dangers" will persist. Liu adds that discipline secures the unity the Party needs to govern a large developing country. In the third, Liu sets out three tasks: put political discipline first as the most fundamental kind; focus on leading cadres as the "critical minority", who should set an example in observing the Party constitution and the law; and enforce discipline so that it does not become a "scarecrow". Enforcement means equality of all members before Party discipline, no exceptions, and linking discipline enforcement with law enforcement under governing the country by law and the Party by rules.

Liu concludes that gripping the "ruler" of discipline is necessary for raising the standard of Party governance, keeping the Party vital and passing the new "examination" of the new era. The text is a short, official-style exposition of current Party-building doctrine rather than an empirical study. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-school commentary presents discipline-building under Xi Jinping, including its citations of the Marxist classics.
quoteEn: The vitality of discipline lies in its enforcement.
quoteZh: 纪律的生命力在于执行。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A policy slogan prominent since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering ideological, organisational, disciplinary and anti-corruption work to tighten control over Party members and organisations.
A traditional teacher's ruler used to discipline pupils. Xi Jinping uses it as a metaphor for Party discipline as a standard that restrains and corrects members.
A phrase Xi Jinping applies to leading cadres, who are said to set the example for the whole Party and society.
In Party rules, the most basic category of discipline, centred on upholding the authority and decisions of the Central Committee.

Official formulation of the long-term challenges facing the Party: governing, reform and opening up, the market economy, and the external environment. It is paired with the "four dangers": lack of drive, lack of ability, detachment from the people, and corruption.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Developing a positive and healthy intra-Party political culture
zh: 发展积极健康的党内政治文化
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily shortly after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Sang Xuecheng asks how intra-Party political culture can be developed so that it helps purify the Party's political ecology. The author argues that a positive and healthy culture is an important basis for keeping the Party advanced and pure. Its ideals, beliefs, values and conduct are meant to shift Party building from "treating pollution" to "clearing the source", and from treating symptoms to treating root causes.

The short commentary follows the Congress's call to persevere with full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. It sets out four components of intra-Party political culture: a culture of belief, an organisational culture, a culture of conduct and an institutional culture. Each is paired with a means of building it: Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, democratic centralism, thoroughgoing self-reform, and a complete system of intra-Party regulations.

In Sang's account, belief is the spiritual core of the culture. It is built through Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and through firm confidence in socialism with Chinese characteristics, and it must resist ideas that distort or negate Marxism. Organisational culture rests on democratic centralism and on the Two Upholds. It should combine unity of thought, will and action with initiative from all quarters, and it rejects individualism, cliques and similar negative habits. Conduct culture depends on the Party's self-reform, which Sang calls the second answer to the historical cycle of rise and fall. Rigorous Party life, criticism and self-criticism, and the "Four Work Styles" campaign are the means. Institutional culture is carried by intra-Party regulations, and the author cites 221 central, 170 departmental and 3,327 local regulations as of June 2022.

Sang concludes that the regulatory system must keep developing, tighten its "institutional cage", and fix the Party's cultural values in rules. The author points to personnel selection and intra-Party supervision as priority areas. The text presents these steps as ways to keep the Party from degenerating and to make a healthy political ecology permanent. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars frame political culture, the Party's self-reform and the role of regulations in Party building after 2022.
quoteEn: The effectiveness of building intra-Party political culture ultimately depends on whether an advanced and pure culture of conduct can be built, and whether Party principles can be turned into members' conscious action and gathered into a healthy political ecology.
quoteZh: 党内政治文化建设的成效，最终取决于能否建设先进纯洁的党内行为文化，能否将党性原则转化为党员的自觉行动，进而聚合为风清气正的良好政治生态。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: The Party's official name for its campaign of discipline, anti-corruption and internal management, stressed since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
The shared beliefs, values, norms and habits of conduct within the Communist Party, which official texts treat as shaping its political ecology.
The Leninist organisational principle by which the Party combines discussion with binding unity of action. Official texts treat it as the basis of Party structure and discipline.
The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position on the Party Central Committee and in the whole Party, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.
An official concept for the Party's capacity to correct itself and fight corruption and misconduct without outside pressure. It is presented as the answer to the historical cycle of rise and fall.

t: Continuing to promote the flourishing development of research on the history of the People's Republic
zh: 不断推动国史研究繁荣发展
paras: Song Yuehong, writing in the People's Daily in February 2023, asks how research on the history of the People's Republic (guoshi, 'national history') should develop. Prompted by Xi Jinping's congratulatory letter to the Chinese Society for the History of the People's Republic on its 30th anniversary, the article argues that this field must hold to the main theme, main thread and mainstream essence of the country's history. It presents the field's growth as a story of steady progress under correct political guidance.

The commentary has three parts. The first traces how national-history research began inside Party history research, then grew through the Mao-era compilation of local gazetteers and five-, seven- and ten-year histories, and became a discipline after the 1981 resolution on Party history. The second summarises results of the decade since the 18th Party Congress (2012) in content, forms and publications. The third sets out four tasks for the new journey.

Song contends that the 1981 resolution, which divided the period to 1981 into four stages, spurred the writing of national history. Two works are called pioneering: the multi-volume Contemporary China series and the Draft History of the People's Republic of China. For the new era, Song cites research on the dialectical unity of the periods before and after reform and opening up, the 'Recording a Moderately Prosperous Society' database project, and short histories used in Party history study and education. For the future, Song calls for stress on research into the new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and for study of Chinese modernization's theoretical system and practice. Song also urges comprehensive general histories of the People's Republic and a wider international perspective, including new concepts that foreign audiences can understand. The author insists that historical nihilism must be firmly opposed.

Song concludes that national-history research should contribute to building a modern socialist country in all respects and to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The article is an official-style programmatic overview, not a detailed historiographical study. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how the Party-state frames the development, achievements and priorities of People's Republic history research as of early 2023.
quoteEn: Research on national history should be grounded in the overall strategy of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and in the world's once-in-a-century changes, and should study in depth the influence and contribution of New China's construction and development on the world.
quoteZh: 国史研究要立足中华民族伟大复兴战略全局和世界百年未有之大变局，深入研究新中国建设和发展对世界的影响和贡献

glossary.explanation: In this usage, the history of the People's Republic of China since 1949, treated as a discipline that grew out of Party history research.
Official concept for China's own path to modernization, given a fuller theoretical statement at the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: Central official goal associated with Xi Jinping, meaning China's restoration to national strength and international standing.
Official label for views that question or negate the Party's official account of history, especially of the revolution and the socialist period.
The policy of economic reform and openness to the outside world launched in 1978.

t: Historiographical criticism as the foundation of the historiography of CPC history
zh: 史评是中共党史学史之基础
paras: Zhou Liangshu argues that criticism of historical writing (shiping) is the foundation of the historiography of Chinese Communist Party history, the field that studies how Party history has itself been written. The short commentary draws mainly on the thinking of the Party historian Zhang Jingru.

Zhou begins with the long tradition of historiographical criticism in China and the West, citing Confucius, Liu Zhiji, Zhang Xuecheng and Herodotus. The commentary then notes Li Dazhao's early theoretical work and the revival of research on the subject from the 1980s. The remainder follows Zhang's reflections on the status, function, object, principle and method of criticism in Party history studies.

Zhou reports that Zhang planned a history of Party historiography from 1980 and needed ten years to finish it. Zhang blamed weak criticism in the field, where book reviews mostly summarised content or offered praise. On Zhang's view, criticism drives the field's development, because it links historical scholarship with society. Its main objects are historians and their works. Its fundamental principle is seeking truth from facts, with all authors treated equally whatever their status. Its basic method is "knowing the person and the age", which Zhou sets against abusive polemic.

Zhou concludes that criticism helps and guides later scholars and should rest on reasoned argument and sound sources, not on labelling opponents. Zhang's own verdict on his book was that it lacked a base in criticism. Read the original if you want a brief account of how one leading Party historian saw the role and ethics of scholarly criticism in the discipline.
quoteEn: Historiographical criticism is the foundation of the historiography of CPC history.
quoteZh: 史评是中共党史学史之基础。

glossary.explanation: A principle associated with Mao Zedong and later Deng Xiaoping, who stressed judging matters by practice and evidence. Here it is the basic principle of historical criticism.

glossary.en: knowing the person and the age
glossary.literal: know the person, discuss the age
glossary.explanation: A classical Chinese critical method that calls for understanding an author's life and historical setting before judging a work.

t: Arming young people with the Party's scientific theory
zh: 用党的科学理论武装青年
paras: Following the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), which called on the whole Party to treat youth work as strategic work and to arm young people with the Party's scientific theory, Han Xiping asks why this task matters and how it should be carried out. Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) in early 2023, Han argues that arming youth with Party theory is an advantage of the Party, that it is especially necessary in the new era, and that it needs systematic, practice-oriented and internet-aware methods.

The article has three parts. The first presents theoretical arming of youth as a Party strength and a reason the Party has won young people. The second explains why the new era makes it more urgent. The third sets out three approaches to the work: systematism, practicality and responsiveness to the times.

Han contends that Marxism, as a science and not a fixed dogma, lets the Party keep answering the questions of China, the world, the people and the age. In the author's account, bourgeois parties treat young people as instruments and so cannot win their lasting allegiance, whereas Marxist parties rely on the mass line and guide youth to understand their own interests. The author describes the next dozen or so years to basic modernization, and about thirty to a strong modernized country, as a period in which today's youth are the main force. Han claims that hostile forces try to Westernize and divide Chinese youth, so winning them is a struggle the Party cannot afford to lose. Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is named as the content to be taught.

On method, Han calls for a system run under the principle of Party leadership over youth work. It would coordinate Party organizations, the Communist Youth League, Party schools and universities, vary teaching by age and occupation, and institutionalize proven schemes such as the Young Marxists training project. It would also tie theory to practice, citing Lenin's warning against book knowledge cut off from work, by presenting the achievements of the past decade and creating lasting mechanisms for social practice. Finally, it would use online platforms such as Xuexi Qiangguo with plainer language. Han concludes that this is the Party's distinctive path for producing qualified successors. Read the original if you want to see how a university Party official presents the rationale and methods of youth ideological work after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Theoretical arming is, in the final analysis, work with people; to do it well one must start from the people themselves and work at making it targeted.
quoteZh: 理论武装工作归根到底是做人的工作，做好这项工作必须从人本身出发，在针对性上下功夫。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party constitution in 2017. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
The Party's term for systematic education that equips members and the public with the Party's official theory, treated as a way to turn theory into practical force.

glossary.en: principle of Party leadership over youth work
glossary.literal: principle of the Party managing youth
glossary.explanation: The principle that Party committees at every level bear direct leadership responsibility for youth work and the Communist Youth League.
The Party-led mass organization for young people, which serves as a reserve force for Party membership.

t: Deeply grasping the decisive significance of the "Two Establishes" and continuously strengthening the Party's political development on the diplomatic front
zh: 深刻领悟“两个确立”的决定性意义 不断加强外交战线党的政治建设
source: Organ Party Building Research (Jiguan dangjian yanjiu), 2023 no. 1
paras: This article, published in early 2023 and written by a research group of the Foreign Ministry's Party organisation, asks how the diplomatic front should strengthen the Party's political development in light of the Two Establishes. Tang and Sun argue that grasping the decisive significance of the Two Establishes and carrying out the Two Upholds is the political guarantee for what they call major-country diplomacy with Chinese characteristics in the new era.

The article has three parts. It first sets out why political development matters for diplomacy, then describes the main practices adopted in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the missions abroad, and finally draws lessons from them. The authors draw on ministry measures, survey results and research visits, and the work won a 2022 national award for Party-building research in central Party and government organs.

The authors give three reasons for the task: diplomacy is by nature political work and must be led by the Party; a world of rapid change requires the diplomatic corps to be politically sound; and loyalty to the Party is a long tradition, which they trace to Mao Zedong's appointment of generals as ambassadors and Zhou Enlai's sixteen-character guideline for diplomats. Their account of practice has four strands. These are treating the ministry as a political organ and putting head-of-state diplomacy at the centre; arming officials with Xi Jinping Thought, including study of Xi's diplomatic thought; reinforcing a people-centred stance through education on the original aspiration and mission, consular protection and countering what the authors describe as US and Western attacks over Xinjiang, Hong Kong and human rights; and cultivating a clean political environment through discipline, cadre selection and anti-corruption work.

From these practices the authors draw five lessons: keep the correct political direction, hold to a people-centred position, raise political capability, guard against political risks, and preserve the Party's political essence while pressing responsibility down the chain. They cite a questionnaire in which over 80 per cent of respondents said leaders increasingly treat Party building as their main achievement and 98.1 per cent rated the work as good or fairly good. The authors conclude that political development must remain the first task of the diplomatic front. Read the original if you want a detailed, insider account of how Party-building measures are organised in China's foreign ministry and of the official rationale behind them.
quoteEn: Diplomatic work is in essence political work; it is necessary to deeply grasp the decisive significance of the "Two Establishes" and to carry the Party's leadership through every stage and aspect of diplomacy.
quoteZh: 外交工作本质上是政治工作，必须深刻领悟“两个确立”的决定性意义，把党的领导贯彻到外交工作的全过程和各方面。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the 20th Party Congress period (2022) affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and of the whole Party, and the guiding status of Xi Jinping Thought. Official texts describe it as decisive for the Party and country.

The requirement that Party members uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.
A strand of Party building, stressed in official documents since 2017, focused on political direction, loyalty to the Central Committee and discipline.

t: The interaction between modernization and modernity in the Party's century of exploration
zh: 党的百年探索视阈下现代化与现代性的互动关系
paras: Ma Yunzhi and Zhao Rongfeng ask how the Communist Party of China's century-long pursuit of modernization has related to the construction of a distinctively Chinese modernity. They argue that socialist modernization has been closely tied to the model of modernity it produces. In their account, modernization conforms to the basic features of modernity while, as it advances, building a Chinese modernity that differs from the Western one.

The article follows the Party's history in three stages, which it labels the emergence, presence and future logic of Chinese modernity. It begins with the early exploration from the founding of the Party through the first decades of the People's Republic, then turns to modernization under socialism with Chinese characteristics, from Deng Xiaoping Theory through the Three Represents and the Scientific Outlook on Development to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. It ends with the goal of building a modern socialist country in all respects.

The authors first define the two concepts, treating modernization as the outward form of modernity's inner values. They hold that Marx located modernity's pillars in the logic of capital and metaphysical rationality, and that China's modernity began logically with the Party's founding, which linked modernization to Marxism. They then argue that each theoretical stage added a dimension: Deng Xiaoping Theory set the tone of Chinese characteristics, the Three Represents added the twin aims of liberating productive forces and liberating people, and the Scientific Outlook on Development moved from putting things first to putting people first. For the future, they say China is crossing three "traps" (middle-income, Thucydides and Kindleberger), advancing economic, political, cultural, social, ecological and Party modernization together, and keeping a people-centred orientation that they say surpasses the capital-centred modernity of the West.

The authors conclude that building modernity in China is still unfinished, but that the Party's path has produced a modernity fundamentally different from Western models. They contend that this offers other countries a Chinese approach to modernization and a new form of human civilization. They add that the process advances the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and twenty-first-century Marxism. Read the original if you want a Party-history account that reads the post-1921 modernization story through the concept of modernity and its official theoretical milestones.
quoteEn: The Chinese path to modernization is people-centred, and has achieved an essential transcendence of capitalist modernity, whose core is the logic of capital.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化道路以人民为中心，实现了对以资本逻辑为核心的资本主义现代性的本质性超越。

glossary.explanation: The mode of production, life and thought that took shape with capitalist modernization since the European Renaissance. The authors use it to ask what kind of modern order China's modernization builds.
Guiding concept associated with Hu Jintao, stressing people-centred, comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable development.
Theory associated with Jiang Zemin, holding that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the overwhelming majority.

t: Correctly understanding the importance of Xi Jinping's statements on bottom-line thinking and preventing and defusing major risks
zh: 正确认识关于坚持底线思维着力防范化解重大风险论述的重要性
paras: Writing shortly after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Cai and Liu take up Xi Jinping's repeated call to uphold "bottom-line thinking" and to focus on preventing and defusing major risks. They argue that this body of statements is a new judgement and requirement for Party building in the new era, grounded in theory, history and practice.

The short commentary is organised in three parts: the theoretical source in basic Marxist principles, the historical evidence drawn from positive and negative experience, and the practical need to build a modern socialist country in an all-round way.

On theory, the authors contend that bottom-line thinking embodies the unity of subjective initiative and objective laws, a systemic outlook that treats risks in politics, ideology, the economy, technology and other fields as one whole, and the dialectic of contradiction. On history, they cite Mao Zedong's "two musts" in 1949, the decision to enter the Korean War, and the "three musts" in the 20th Party Congress report. On practice, they present four needs: consolidating the socialist system amid external pressure, building the new development pattern and high-quality development, modernising national security, and maintaining the Party's advanced and pure character through full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

The authors conclude that the path of Chinese modernization is long and difficult, so the Party must hold to bottom-line thinking to prepare for the second centenary goal. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-school commentary links Xi's risk discourse to Marxist theory, Party history and current policy priorities.
quoteEn: Bottom-line thinking is a method of thought that starts from the lowest point and strives for the greatest expected result.
quoteZh: 底线思维是立足最低点争取最大期望值的思维方法

glossary.explanation: A mode of thought stressed by Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012): identify the worst-case scenario and the limit that must not be crossed, then plan to secure the best possible outcome.
The official term for China's path to modernization, set out in the 20th Party Congress report (2022) as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's drive since 2012 to tighten discipline, fight corruption and strengthen internal oversight.
The official goal for China's economy since 2017, stressing quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.
Mao Zedong's 1949 injunction that Party members must remain modest, prudent and free from arrogance, and must keep up the style of hard struggle.

t: Firmly grasping the theme, main thread and mainstream essence of the history of New China
zh: 牢牢把握新中国史的主题主线、主流本质
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in February 2023, Song Yuehong takes up the congratulatory letter that Xi Jinping sent for the 30th anniversary of the Chinese Society for the History of the People's Republic. The letter calls on historians to hold firmly to the "theme, main thread and mainstream essence" of the history of New China. Song argues that studying and teaching that history requires an objective, comprehensive and accurate grasp of its course, achievements and experience, and that these three concepts supply the basic framework for doing so.

The piece is a short commentary in three parts. The first sets out the theme and main thread of New China's history, tracing the Party's changing goals and its reading of the principal social contradiction across the socialist revolution and construction period, the reform era and the new era. The second defines the mainstream and essence of that history. The third turns to practical directions for research.

Song defines the theme as the continuous adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, together with the founding and development of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Its purpose is to build a modern socialist country and achieve the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Four main threads follow: safeguarding sovereignty and promoting a community with a shared future for mankind; upholding Marxism and the Party's self-reform; advancing Chinese modernization and common prosperity; and promoting national reunification. The mainstream is described as founding, enriching and strengthening the country, taking its own path and benefiting the people. Song acknowledges serious setbacks, above all in the socialist revolution and construction period. In the article's account, however, these were part of exploration, and the period's achievements and lessons prepared the ground for the reform era.

Song concludes that research should clarify the history, necessity and regularities of the socialist path with Chinese characteristics, and should study Chinese modernization as a process running through New China's history. The article also calls for building the discipline, academic and discourse systems of New China history, combining theory with the collection of sources, and openly opposing historical nihilism. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of how Party historians are told to frame the history of the People's Republic and what research agenda follows from it.
quoteEn: The mainstream of the history of New China can be stated as founding, enriching and strengthening the country, taking its own path, bringing benefit to the people and promoting a better world, with brilliant achievements and broad prospects.
quoteZh: 新中国史的主流可表述为，立国兴国强国，走自己的路，为民造福，推动建设美好世界，成就辉煌、前景广阔。

glossary.en: theme, main thread and mainstream essence
glossary.explanation: A framework from Xi Jinping's letter for interpreting the history of the People's Republic. It is meant to direct historians to the dominant direction of that history rather than to its setbacks.
The Party's official term for its own path of modernization, which it describes as sharing features with other countries while having distinct Chinese characteristics.
A goal of shared wealth for all the people, presented in official discourse as a defining feature of socialism.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept of a world order based on shared interests and cooperation.
An official term for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself, which is said to drive broader social transformation.
In Party usage, a label for views that deny or belittle the Party's revolutionary and socialist history, especially its achievements.

t: On the relationship between the discipline of CPC history and Party building and the construction of ideological and political theory courses
zh: 中共党史党建学科与思想政治理论课建设关系刍议
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2022 no. 12
paras: In September 2022 the Academic Degrees Committee of the State Council and the Ministry of Education added "CPC history and Party building" as a first-level discipline under law. Song Xueqin and Yang Zongru ask how this new discipline relates to the compulsory ideological and political theory courses taught in Chinese universities. They argue that the two are mutually dependent and inseparable, and that building the discipline well requires treating them together.

The article has three parts. The first argues that the discipline needs the courses; the second that the courses supply momentum for the discipline's "three systems" (disciplinary, academic and discourse systems); the third that building an autonomous body of knowledge in the discipline can raise the quality of the courses. The authors draw on Xi Jinping's statements, central Party documents from 2019 and 2022, and a historical review of how Party history was taught from the 1950s onward.

In the first part, the authors say courses largely decide a discipline's standing. They trace Party history's strong periods (the 1950s–60s and the 1980s) to its close tie with required political theory courses, and its weakening to later course reforms in 1998, 2005 and 2008 that separated them. They set out two current proposals: replace or merge existing courses into one on CPC history and theory, or keep the present course structure and have several disciplines jointly support three named courses. Both are called feasible, but the authors favour a dedicated course platform. In the second part, they argue that the courses' principle of unity of political and academic quality guides the disciplinary system. Student questions raised in teaching become research problems for the academic system, and the courses bring different discourse resources together for the discourse system.

In the third part, the authors say the autonomous knowledge system should enrich course content through the Sinicization of Marxism and the spiritual lineage of Chinese Communists. It should also supply research methods, including the 2021 historical resolution's guidance on a correct view of Party history and opposition to historical nihilism, and strengthen problem orientation in teaching. They cite weak problem awareness, for example in teaching modern Chinese history, as a current shortcoming. They conclude that the discipline and the courses should interact in a virtuous circle. Read the original if you want a Chinese academic account of how the new first-level discipline is meant to connect to compulsory political theory teaching, including the course-reform options under discussion.
quoteEn: Practice has shown that avoiding a disconnect between building the CPC history and Party building discipline and the provision of ideological and political theory courses is the key to a virtuous circle between the two.
quoteZh: 实践证明，避免中共党史党建学科建设与思想政治理论课设置相脱节的现象，是实现二者良性循环的关键。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses on Marxism, Party theory and modern Chinese history taught to all university students in China. They are often called "sizheng" courses for short and are treated as the main channel of ideological education.

glossary.literal: Study of CPC history and Party building
glossary.explanation: A first-level discipline added under law in China's 2022 graduate education catalogue. It covers the history of the Communist Party of China and the Party's own organisational development.
A formula from Xi Jinping's call to build Chinese philosophy and social sciences: the disciplinary system, the academic system and the discourse system.
In official usage, a label for interpretations that question or deny the Party's historical narrative and achievements. Party documents call for opposing it.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.literal: Sinicization and adaptation of Marxism to the times
glossary.explanation: The official idea that Marxism is adapted to Chinese conditions and to the needs of the era. It is presented as a sequence running from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought.

t: The Party's investigation and research work during the full-scale War of Resistance
st: Methods, results and lessons of the Yan'an-era campaign
zh: 全面抗战时期党的调查研究工作
source: Documents of the Party (Dang de wenxian), 2022 no. 1
paras: He Lei and Liu Shuru examine how the Chinese Communist Party carried out investigation and research (diaocha yanjiu) between 1937 and 1945, a period they call the full-scale War of Resistance against Japan. They argue that the campaign, promoted above all by Mao Zedong, was a high point in the Party's history of fact-finding. In their view it offers lessons for improving the investigative skills of Party members and cadres today.

The article has three parts. The first explains why such work was necessary. The second describes four methods used in the anti-Japanese base areas: comprehensive survey, typical-case survey, survey by conference, and pilot-point survey. The third reviews the results and draws four lessons. The authors illustrate each method with a case: Li Zhuoran's Gulin survey, surveys of village Party branches in the Taihang area, Zhang Wentian's Yan'an rural investigation, and Xi Zhongxun's Haojiaqiao survey.

On necessity, the authors argue that the Party's rapid growth and the lingering subjectivism and dogmatism after the Zunyi Conference called for investigation. They present it as a bridge between the universal truths of Marxism and China's concrete conditions, and therefore as a means of adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions (Marxism's Sinicization) and unifying Party thinking. They also treat it as a way of practising the mass line, since measures cut off from local needs had strained Party–people relations. The four lessons are: give the work high priority in thinking; build and improve investigation institutions, as the 1941 Central Committee decision did by creating a Central Investigation and Research Bureau and local research offices; adhere to seeking truth from facts; and keep to the principle of going 'from the masses, to the masses'.

The authors conclude that when the Party emphasised investigation its policies fitted reality, and that neglect led to losses. They hold that the wartime experience can help today's cadres improve their investigative ability, apply theory to practice and keep close ties with the people. Read the original if you want a historical account of Yan'an-era survey methods, with named cases and Mao's remarks on them, framed as guidance for present-day Party work.
quoteEn: The Party's history shows that whenever the whole Party, from top to bottom, has valued and strengthened investigation and research, the policies, line and guidelines it formulates have conformed better to objective reality, and the cause of the Party and the people has advanced smoothly.
quoteZh: 党的历史表明，什么时候全党上下重视并加强调查研究，党制定的政策、路线、方针就会更加符合客观实际，党和人民的事业就会顺利发展

glossary.explanation: The Party's practice of fact-finding through field surveys and interviews before making policy. It is closely associated with Mao Zedong's 1930s–40s writings and is often called a 'family heirloom' of the Party.
A Party method of leadership that gathers the views of the people, turns them into policy and tests them in practice. Mao Zedong formulated it as 'from the masses, to the masses'.

An ideological principle that policy should start from objective reality rather than from texts or preconceptions. Mao Zedong gave it a Marxist interpretation in 1941, and it later became a core slogan of the Party.
In Party usage, a way of working that proceeds from preconceptions or book knowledge instead of investigation. Mao Zedong criticised it together with dogmatism.

t: The theoretical implications of the idea of "serving the people" in the new era
zh: 新时代“为人民服务”思想的理论意蕴
source: Research on Ideological Education (Sixiang jiaoyu yanjiu), 2023 no. 1
paras: Feng Gang examines the idea of "serving the people" (wei renmin fuwu) in the new era. The article presents it as the fundamental purpose of the Communist Party of China, a moral demand placed on the people, a proposition within the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context, and a body of thought and culture. Feng argues that deepening its theoretical implications is needed to consolidate the Party's governing foundation and to meet the "four tests" and "four risks".

The article has three parts. The first identifies the Marxist theoretical core of the idea. The second traces its cultural roots in traditional Chinese culture, revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture. The third shows how the idea is carried forward in governance practice since the 18th Party Congress (2012), in the rule of law, in the building of ethics and cultural-ethical progress, and in Party building. The text draws on classic texts and on Xi Jinping's speeches and Party documents.

Feng grounds the idea in three Marxist pillars. The conception of history centred on the masses explains why one serves the people, because they create material and spiritual wealth and drive social change. Marxist views of interest explain how: they respect objective interests and aim at the interests of the great majority. The labour theory of value, read through Marx's account of species-being and alienated labour, explains how it is possible, since everyone is both a subject and an object of such service. On the cultural side, Feng points to the people-as-foundation thought of Confucius, Xunzi and Mencius and to benevolent government, which the idea is said to have dialectically sublated. Revolutionary ideals, the Party's spirit and revolutionary values then shaped it, and advanced socialist culture is said to sustain it through cultural consciousness, confidence and strength.

In governance, Feng reads the principle of the people's principal position in comprehensive rule of law and in judicial reform as the idea's contemporary expression. In ethical-cultural progress, it calls for attention to people's real social relations, to their needs given the shift in the principal contradiction, and to their active participation. In Party building, it is embedded in the mass line, in full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and in the "original aspiration and founding mission". Feng concludes that the Party should distil its century of experience, strengthen its sense of purpose, and raise the level of modernising national governance. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-school-style account links Marxist theory, Confucian people-centred thought and current Party-building language around a single core slogan.
quoteEn: The idea of "serving the people" reflects the most thoroughgoing view of the masses and of the people's interests, and is clearly distinct from serving a false "community".
quoteZh: “为人民服务”思想反映的是最彻底的群众观和人民利益观，同为虚假“共同体”服务具有明显的区别

glossary.explanation: A Party principle associated with Mao Zedong's 1944 speech. The Party's constitution and official texts describe it as its fundamental purpose.
The Party's method of work, which stresses drawing on the masses' views and staying close to them. It is a long-standing principle of Party work.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the campaign of tighter Party discipline and Party building since 2012.

glossary.literal: never forget the original intention, keep the mission firmly in mind
glossary.explanation: An official slogan for Party members' commitment to the Party's founding purpose of seeking the people's wellbeing. It was promoted in a Party-wide campaign from 2019.

t: The Communist Party of China's self-reform in the perspective of the Marxist view of revolution
zh: 马克思主义革命观视域下中国共产党自我革命研究
source: Journal of Northeastern University (Social Science Edition), 2023 no. 1
paras: Zeng Wei asks where the Communist Party of China's "self-revolution" (rendered here as the Party's self-reform) comes from in Marxist theory, and why it arises.
