The political foundation is the system's combination of Party leadership, the people as masters of the country and law-based governance; Feng contrasts what is called Chinese order with Western disorder, citing economic crises and unrest in the West. The material guarantee is rapid growth, the elimination of absolute poverty and the building of a moderately prosperous society in 2020. The driving force is the Party's self-reform, including anti-corruption work and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

Feng concludes that the Party must keep to Marxism, particularly Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and keep combining it with China's fine traditional culture, so as to contribute more to human civilisation. Self-reform is presented as what keeps the Party from degenerating while it serves both the Chinese people and global progress. Read the original if you want a representative example of official Party-theory commentary on the Party's international significance around the centenary in 2021.
quoteEn: China's successful practice shows that there is no single, fixed model of modernization in the world, no standard of modernization valid everywhere, and that every country has the right to explore its own path of development.
quoteZh: 中国的成功实践表明，世界上根本不存在定于一尊的现代化模式，也不存在放之四海而皆准的现代化标准，每个国家都有探索自身发展道路的权利。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's own path to modernization under Party leadership, presented as an alternative to Western models. It was elaborated especially after the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept advanced by Xi Jinping from around 2013. It calls for a world of mutual respect, fairness and win-win cooperation.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and described as the Marxism of contemporary China.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan for the Party's drive since 2012 to tighten discipline, fight corruption and strengthen internal oversight.
A long-standing Chinese goal of general, modest prosperity. The Party declared it fully achieved in 2020.

t: Giving full play to the political function of primary-level Party organizations
zh: 充分发挥基层党组织的政治功能
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in September 2022, Wang Binglin asks how the Communist Party of China's grassroots organizations can better perform their political function. Wang argues that the Party is a Marxist party whose basic attribute is political and whose basic function is political, so primary-level organizations must remain "fortresses" and not turn into mere service bodies. The article opens with the Party's size, citing 96.712 million members and 4.936 million primary-level organizations at the end of 2021.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out why the political function matters; the second reviews what has been achieved since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and the weaknesses that remain; the third offers four lines of work for Party building in the new era.

Wang gives five reasons why the political function is necessary. It is required by the Party's overall leadership, by the people-centred approach, by the consolidation of the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and by full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Wang credits primary-level organizations with firmer political direction, with the Two Upholds, with "Party member shock teams" in the Covid-19 response and disaster relief, and with poverty alleviation work. Wang also lists problems: some organizations apply Party policy half-heartedly, chase economic targets while neglecting people's demands, leave gaps in coverage (especially in emerging sectors), have an ageing Party-affairs workforce, stress service over politics, and fall into formalism such as paperwork and record-keeping.

Wang proposes four remedies. Primary-level organizations should be secured as the leading core of grassroots governance. They should meet the people's needs for a better life, with management and service combined. Their organizational strength should be raised through full coverage, better-chosen leaders, and more resources and authority. Full and rigorous self-governance of the Party should extend downward through study of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, criticism and self-criticism, and checks on petty power. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how Party theorists in 2022 framed the political role of grassroots Party branches and the weaknesses they acknowledged.
quoteEn: Primary-level Party organizations are fortresses and must not become mere service organizations; their political function must be given full play.
quoteZh: 基层党组织是战斗堡垒，不能变成单纯的服务组织，其政治功能要充分发挥。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since 2014. It covers stricter discipline, anti-corruption work and ideological education within the Party.
The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralized, unified leadership.
The official name for China's governing ideology and system since the reform era, describing a socialist path adapted to Chinese conditions.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
A traditional Party metaphor for primary-level organizations as strongholds that carry out the Party's line and mobilize the masses. It is used here in contrast to being only service providers.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: A century of change in the Party Constitution
zh: 党章的百年演变
source: China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News, 15 December 2022, p. 5
paras: Published in the Party discipline newspaper on 15 December 2022, shortly after the 20th Party Congress (2022), this commentary traces how the Constitution of the Communist Party of China has developed since the first formal text of 1922. Yao and Chen argue that, over a hundred years, the Party Constitution has become more complete in structure and content, and that it records the evolution of the Party's theory, political positions, line and institutions.

The article follows the Constitution through four periods: the New Democratic Revolution, the exploration of the socialist road, reform and opening up and modernization, and the new era since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It runs from the 1921 first Programme and the 1922 Second Congress text (six chapters, 29 articles) through the 1927 revision, the 7th Congress text, the 8th Congress text, the texts of the Cultural Revolution years, and the revisions of the 12th to 19th Congresses.

Yao and Chen present each revision as a response to the Party's circumstances. The 1927 text fixed the basic framework later used. The 7th Congress text added a general programme and established Mao Zedong Thought as the guiding ideology. The 12th Congress text, in their account, removed the 'Left' errors and became the model for the new period. The authors then list what each later congress wrote in: Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development, and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. For the 20th Congress they report 50 amendments (37 in the general programme, 13 in articles). These concern the Thought's positioning and the Two Integrations, the Party's century of experience, common prosperity and security, whole-process people's democracy, the Party's overall leadership, and the Party's self-reform.

The authors conclude that the 20th Congress amendments reflect theoretical, practical and institutional innovation since the 19th Congress (2017), and that revising the Constitution to keep pace with the times is a Party convention. They call on all Party organisations and members to study, observe, implement and uphold it. Read the original if you want a compact, officially framed chronology of each Party Constitution from 1922 to 2022 and a summary of the 20th Congress amendments.
quoteEn: It is a convention of our Party that the National Congress revises the Party Constitution in line with the needs of theoretical and practical innovation.
quoteZh: 党的全国代表大会根据理论创新和实践创新的需要对党章进行修改，是我们党的一个惯例。

glossary.explanation: The Communist Party of China's basic internal rulebook, covering its guiding ideology, aims, membership, organisation and discipline. It is revised at National Party Congresses.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping. It was written into the Party Constitution at the 19th Congress in 2017.
The formula of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. The 20th Congress added it to the Party Constitution.
An official term for China's democratic model, which the Party says involves popular participation at every stage of governance, not only at elections.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, which the Party stresses in its socialist objectives.
An official term for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself, linked to the anti-corruption campaign and strict Party governance.
A guiding concept associated with Hu Jintao, stressing people-centred, coordinated and sustainable development. It was written into the Party Constitution in 2007.

t: From awareness of hardship to bottom-line thinking: continuity and development across generations of Party leaders
zh: 从忧患意识到底线思维：党的几代领导人的坚持和发展
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2022 no. 7
paras: Yang Yucheng asks how the traditional Chinese consciousness of hardship and danger (youhuan yishi) has been carried forward by successive generations of Chinese Communists and turned into the method of "bottom-line thinking" associated with Xi Jinping. The article argues that Communists combined the basic tenets of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture, creatively transforming the old ideal of being prepared for danger in times of peace. Mao Zedong's generation first turned it into the method of "thinking from the worst possibility", and Xi Jinping's generation refined it into bottom-line thinking for preventing major risks.

The article first traces the tradition from pre-Qin Confucian, Daoist and Mohist texts through later historians and officials such as Sima Qian, Wei Zheng, Ouyang Xiu and Wei Yuan. It then follows Mao Zedong, Liu Shaoqi, Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao, and Xi Jinping's speeches from the 18th Party Congress (2012) to the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). A central section defines what a "bottom line" is and what bottom-line thinking involves, and a final section assesses its innovation over the tradition.

Yang defines a bottom line as the lower limit of the "measure" within which a thing keeps its present qualitative state, a critical point beyond which it degrades. Bottom-line thinking has three linked elements: looking from the worst case, preparing most fully, and striving for the best result. Yang reads this as an application of materialist dialectics, including the law of the mutual transformation of quantity and quality. Holding the bottom line is presented as a precondition for achieving more, not an end in itself. Yang says traditional awareness of hardship was a kind of cautionary warning with little operability, and that bottom-line thinking supplies identifiable lines, contingency plans and concrete steps.

Yang contends that bottom-line thinking also bears on the question of "escaping the historical cycle of rise and fall", which Mao raised in his cave-dwelling talk with Huang Yanpei. In Yang's account the answer has two parts: modernizing the system and capacity of national governance through comprehensive deepening of reform, and the Party's self-reform through full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, which Yang says leads the first. Yang concludes that bottom-line thinking gives the old wisdom new vitality in the new era. Read the original if you want a Party School scholar's account of how Xi Jinping's risk-prevention doctrine is placed in a lineage from Mao to the present and in Chinese tradition.
quoteEn: Bottom-line thinking is a method of thinking that \"objectively sets a minimum goal, stands on the lowest point, and strives for the greatest expected value\".
quoteZh: 底线思维就是“客观地设定最低目标，立足最低点，争取最大期望值”的思维方法。

glossary.explanation: A method Xi Jinping has urged cadres to use: identify the worst-case outcomes and limits that must not be crossed, prepare fully, and then strive for the best result. It is central to the Party's current discourse on preventing major risks.

glossary.en: the historical cycle of rise and fall
glossary.explanation: The pattern of dynasties flourishing and then collapsing, raised in the 1945 cave-dwelling talk between Huang Yanpei and Mao Zedong. Party discourse treats "escaping" it as a core question of long-term rule.
A formulation stressing that the Party must purify, improve and renew itself under long-term rule, mainly through discipline and anti-corruption work.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's strict internal discipline and anti-corruption drive since 2012.

glossary.zh: 国家治理体系和治理能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā zhìlǐ tǐxì hé zhìlǐ nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.en: modernizing the system and capacity of national governance
glossary.explanation: A reform goal set out at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) and elaborated at the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019). It refers to improving institutions and their effective operation.

t: The centenary evolution and basic experience of the Communist Party of China's propaganda work
zh: 中国共产党宣传工作的百年演进与基本经验
paras: Zhong Xiaowu takes up the history of the Communist Party of China's propaganda work over its first hundred years. The article starts from the formula that propaganda is an "extremely important" task of the Party and a fine tradition and political advantage in winning victories in revolution, construction and reform. Zhong argues that tracing this history and distilling its experience offers a historical reference for keeping to fundamental principles while innovating (守正创新) in propaganda and ideological work in the new era.

The article has three parts. The first divides the century into four periods, each with a defining trait: the New Democratic Revolution (revolutionary), socialist revolution and construction (rebuilding), reform and opening up (innovative), and the new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics (transformative). The second lists six achievements. The third draws nine "basic experiences", each tied to a feature of propaganda work.

In Zhong's account, early propaganda joined the "gun" to the "pen", mobilised workers and peasants, and used Marxist education to build the Party and army. After 1949 it reshaped socialist ideology and culture, and from 1978 it was institutionalised through guidelines and regulations. Since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Xi Jinping's statements on propaganda and ideological work and the Regulations on Propaganda Work of the CPC are presented as bringing the work to "high maturity". The nine experiences are Party leadership (political character), propaganda as an extremely important task, Marxism's guiding position (ideological character), a people-centred approach (mass character), serving the central tasks (service), coordinated material and spiritual civilization (constructive), promoting correct and resisting erroneous ideas (struggle), a "big propaganda" pattern involving the whole Party (systemic), and innovation (artistic).

Zhong concludes that propaganda history is also a history of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and that it has shaped a distinctive Party theory of propaganda. The author calls for continued Party leadership, a combative stance against "left" and right deviations, and innovation such as county-level media convergence centres and the Xuexi Qiangguo platform. Read the original if you want a systematic, officially aligned periodisation of Party propaganda work and its guiding principles, as presented by a provincial academy scholar.
quoteEn: The century-long history of the Party's propaganda work is a history of the sinicization of Marxism, and also a history of propaganda and mobilisation through which the Communist Party of China drew the broad masses into revolution, construction and reform.
quoteZh: 党的宣传工作百年发展史，就是一部马克思主义中国化史，也是一部中国共产党发动广大群众积极投身革命、建设和改革的宣传动员史

glossary.en: keeping to fundamental principles while innovating
glossary.literal: uphold what is correct and innovate
glossary.explanation: A formula in recent Party discourse meaning to hold to core principles and political direction while introducing new methods and ideas.
The Party's term for its work on theory, media, culture and ideology. The article notes it replaced the narrower phrase "propaganda work" in official usage from the 1990s.
Official term for moral, cultural and ideological development, paired with material civilization. Promoted from the early reform era under the 'grasp with both hands' principle.

glossary.zh: 中国共产党宣传工作条例
glossary.en: Regulations on Propaganda Work of the CPC
glossary.explanation: Intra-Party regulations on propaganda, which the article calls the first basic and principal regulation of its kind.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for applying Marxist principles to China's conditions and producing new theoretical results.

t: The China best suited to "China": the historical evolution and inner meaning of the CPC's visions of state-building
zh: 最适合“中国”的中国：中国共产党建国构想的历史演进与内在意蕴
paras: Li Chaoqun asks how the Communist Party of China has understood and led the building of a modern Chinese state, and what its successive state-building blueprints reveal. The article argues that these blueprints, adjusted to each period's revolutionary situation, national conditions and the logic of modernization, together show the Party exploring a path of national construction that Li calls the "China best suited to 'China'".

The first part traces six stages. These run from the early communists' idea of a "state of the labourers" (Li Dazhao, Chen Duxiu, Mao Zedong) through the Second Congress (1922) plan for a democratic republic and federation, then the workers' and peasants' democratic dictatorship of the Soviet period and the wartime adjustments. They continue to the New Democratic republic and the people's democratic dictatorship, consolidated in the 1949 Common Programme and the 1954 Constitution. The last two stages are socialist industrialization and the "four modernizations", and the post-1978 goals of a modern socialist country, from "three-in-one" through "four-in-one" to "five-in-one" and the strategy of the 19th Party Congress (2017). The second part draws out three implications.

Li's core claim is that the sequence shows the Party's lofty founding mission, its theoretical creativity and the people's agency in its path. Li contrasts the Guomindang's one-party rule with a Party that Li says consistently served the people's fundamental interests. On theory, Li argues that the Party adapted the Marxist theory of proletarian dictatorship and developed New Democratic theory, in line with the Two Integrations. It also dropped the early federalism and national self-determination borrowed from Soviet Russia and the Comintern, for a unitary multi-ethnic state with regional ethnic autonomy, which Li attributes to China's tradition of political unity. Third, Li holds that the blueprints tied people's democracy to state-building, and treats whole-process people's democracy as the latest form of this. Li contrasts this with what the article describes as capital-driven "Western-style democracy".

Li concludes that the Party, as the core of state-building, has led the country through saving, founding, reviving, enriching and strengthening the nation. In Li's account this unified the Party's growth with that of the modern state and produced a distinctive Chinese logic of state-building. The experience is presented as lasting support for building a modern socialist great power. Read the original if you want a periodised, document-based survey of the Party's changing state-building formulas from the 1920s to the 2010s, as presented in mainstream Party-history scholarship.
quoteEn: As the leading core and central pillar of state-building, the Communist Party of China has shouldered the historical mission of building the modern Chinese state since its birth.
quoteZh: 中国共产党作为国家建设的领导核心和中心支柱，其自诞生伊始就承担起中国现代国家建设的历史使命

glossary.explanation: Formula associated with Xi Jinping: combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
Mao Zedong's 1949 formula for the new state, led by the working class and based on the worker-peasant alliance. It remains in the Chinese constitution as the state's nature.
Concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2019, describing Chinese democracy as covering all stages of decision-making rather than only elections.
The goal, set out by Zhou Enlai in 1964 and revived under Deng Xiaoping, of modernizing agriculture, industry, national defence, and science and technology.
The official system of autonomous areas for ethnic minorities within a unitary state, adopted in place of the federal model the Party first proposed.

t: "Defending the country means defending the people's hearts"
st: The Communist Party of China's feeling for the people
zh: “守江山，守的是人民的心”
zhSub: 中国共产党的人民情怀
paras: This short commentary, written after the 20th Party Congress (2022), takes up Xi Jinping's statement in the congress report that the country is the people and the people are the country, and that the Party, having won the country with the people, defends it by defending their hearts. Zhang argues that the phrase expresses the Party's working-class vanguard character, its fundamental purpose of serving the people wholeheartedly, and its original aspiration and mission.

The article is organised around three claims about the phrase, followed by two practical requirements. It runs through the Party's history from its founding to the post-2012 period, using the sequence of stages "stood up, grew rich, became strong".

Zhang first presents the phrase as the clearest expression of the Marxist view of the people as creators of history, and as the Party's decisive explanation for its successes in revolution, construction and reform. Zhang then calls it a necessity for the "new road to the test" and the second centenary goal, since the Party's tests and dangers will persist and, in Xi's words, the greatest danger after taking power is losing touch with the masses. Zhang cites the Party's record, from land reform and industrialisation to poverty alleviation and a moderately prosperous society, as evidence of its commitment.

Zhang concludes that the Party must take the people's standpoint, put the people first in its heart, and work for their wellbeing. The article contends that if Communists keep their founding mission, the people will keep following the Party and the socialist state will endure. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-building commentary after the 20th Party Congress presents the Party's relationship with the people.
quoteEn: The Party was born for the people and has flourished because of the people, always staying with the people and striving for their interests.
quoteZh: 党为人民而生，因人民而兴，始终同人民在一起，为人民利益而奋斗

glossary.literal: new road of sitting an examination
glossary.explanation: An image drawn from Mao Zedong's remark in 1949 that the Party was going to Beijing to "take the exam". It is now used to describe the Party's governing challenges, with the people as examiners.

The goal of building a modern socialist country by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic. It follows the first centenary goal of a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021.
A Chinese development goal of basic material comfort for all. The Party declared it "fully built" in 2021.
A Party slogan for its founding purpose: seeking the people's wellbeing and the rejuvenation of the nation. It was heavily promoted from 2019.

t: Maintaining a distinctive political character and bringing strong political advantages into play
zh: 保持鲜明政治品格 发挥强大政治优势
paras: Writing shortly before the 20th Party Congress (2022), Liu Jianhui elaborates Xi Jinping's statement that being guided by Marxist scientific theory is the Communist Party of China's distinctive political character and strong political advantage. Liu reads Xi's conclusion that Marxism is ultimately the reason why the Party "can" and socialism with Chinese characteristics is "good" as the fundamental explanation of past success and the condition of future success. The piece is a Party-theory commentary rather than an empirical study.

The article has three parts. The first argues that Marxism has profoundly changed the course of Chinese history. The second reviews how the Party has used Marxism to observe, interpret and lead its era across four historical periods. The third turns to the tasks of the new journey, namely study of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and continued theoretical innovation.

Liu's central claim is that Marxism works in China because it has been adapted to Chinese conditions and to the needs of the times. Liu cites the Party's growth from about 50 members at its First Congress to over 96 million today as evidence of this political advantage. Liu then traces successive theoretical leaps: Mao Zedong Thought in the revolutionary and socialist-construction periods, the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics after reform and opening up, and Xi Jinping Thought since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Each is presented as an answer to the problems of its period and as proof that the Party adheres to Marxism while developing it.

Liu concludes that adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times has no end point, especially amid what the article calls great changes unseen in a century. Liu calls on the whole Party, and leading cadres in particular, to study Xi Jinping Thought as the primary political task. The thought is to be linked with the Marxist classics and Party history, and is to be combined with Chinese realities and traditional culture. Read the original if you want a representative example of how Party theorists in late 2022 presented Marxism as the Party's political advantage and described the sequence of theoretical "leaps".
quoteEn: Marxism \"works\" because the Party proceeds from reality in everything, promptly answers the questions of China, the world, the people and the times, and keeps adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times and using it to guide practice.
quoteZh: 马克思主义之所以行，就在于党坚持一切从实际出发，及时回答中国之问、世界之问、人民之问、时代之问，不断推进马克思主义中国化时代化并用以指导实践。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxist theory to Chinese conditions and contemporary developments. The "needs of our times" element was added to the older formula of Sinification in recent Party documents.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. The Party presents it as the latest stage of Marxism adapted to China.
The official name for the Party's path, theory and system since reform and opening up, associated with Deng Xiaoping.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978.

t: Staying clear-headed and resolute about the problems unique to a large party
zh: 时刻保持解决大党独有难题的清醒和坚定
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 28 October 2022, takes up a line from Xi Jinping's report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): to win popular support and consolidate its long-term governing position, the Party must stay clear-headed and resolute about the problems unique to a large party. Han Bing argues that grasping why the Party has succeeded in the past, and how it can keep succeeding, matters for the new journey of building a modern socialist country.

The piece is organised around four such problems, each introduced as one the century-old Party must solve. They concern holding to the original aspiration, maintaining unity, staying alert to danger, and carrying out self-reform. Each section quotes Xi Jinping, adds a short historical reference, and ends with what the Party must do on the new journey.

On the original aspiration, Han holds that the Party represents the fundamental interests of the people and has no special interests of its own. Forgetting this, the author warns, would change the Party's nature. On unity, Han presents the Party's ideological, political and organisational building as the basis of its cohesion, and describes the Two Establishes as a judgement reflecting the shared will of the whole Party. On vigilance, Han recalls Mao Zedong's "cave dialogue" with Huang Yanpei and the Second Plenum of the 7th Central Committee, and stresses avoiding the historical cycle of rise and fall.

Han concludes that the Party must keep to a people-centred stance, strengthen the Four Consciousnesses, the Four-sphere Confidence and the Two Upholds, and apply bottom-line thinking to risks. It must also continue full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, which Han says is never finished, so that it can purify, improve and renew itself. Read the original if you want a concise, official-register statement of how Party commentary frames the Party's governing challenges after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: An advanced Marxist party is not born that way but is tempered through continuous self-reform, and the spirit of self-reform is a powerful support for the Party's enduring youthful vitality.
quoteZh: 先进的马克思主义政党不是天生的，而是在不断自我革命中淬炼而成的，自我革命精神是党永葆青春活力的强大支撑。

glossary.explanation: A formula adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the Party's core and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold the authority of Xi Jinping as the core of the Central Committee and the Party's centralised, unified leadership.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the campaign, intensified since 2012, to tighten Party discipline, conduct and anti-corruption work.
Party members' consciousness of political integrity, the big picture, the leadership core and alignment with the central leadership.

t: Self-reform as the Party's second answer to escaping the historical cycle of rise and fall
zh: 自我革命是党跳出历史周期率的第二个答案
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily in October 2022, takes up a question raised in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): how a long-ruling Marxist party can escape the historical cycle of order, disorder, rise and decline. Dong argues that the Party's self-reform is the "second answer" to this problem, and that it keeps the Party from degenerating in nature, colour or flavour.

The piece first recalls the 1945 "cave dwelling conversation" between Huang Yanpei and Mao Zedong, in which Mao named democracy as the first answer. It then traces Xi Jinping's statements on the cycle from 2013 to 2021, and reviews the work done since the 18th Party Congress (2012), before turning to the tasks set by the 20th Congress.

Dong's central claim is that self-reform is what distinguishes the Communist Party from other parties. In the author's account, the Party has applied full and rigorous self-governance of the Party through a "combination of punches": a system of rules for self-purification, self-improvement, self-renewal and self-elevation, tighter supervision and accountability, and a focus on the "critical few". The author also describes the campaigns against "tigers", "flies" and "foxes" as having removed serious hidden dangers in the Party, state and army.

Dong concludes that the Party must keep its Marxist character by carrying out the "three musts" and staying alert to corruption. The author calls for self-reform to lead social revolution and social revolution to promote self-reform, so that the Party can lead the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Party's self-reform is presented in official commentary after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Self-reform is the most salient mark distinguishing our Party from other parties, the second answer to escaping the historical cycle of order, disorder, rise and decline, and the key to our Party moving from one victory to another.
quoteZh: 自我革命，是我们党区别于其他政党最显著的标志，是跳出治乱兴衰历史周期率的第二个答案，也是我们党不断从胜利走向新的胜利的关键所在。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed under Xi Jinping: the Party's continuous effort to purify, improve and discipline itself without external pressure. Official texts present it as a distinguishing feature of the CPC.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The policy, pursued since 2012, of strict discipline, anti-corruption work and institution-building inside the Party.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, closely tied to the Chinese Dream.
A formula in the 20th Congress report: the whole Party must keep its original aspiration and mission, remain modest and hardworking, and dare and know how to struggle.

t: What underpins our Party's firm convictions and its grasp of historical initiative
zh: 我们党坚定信仰信念、把握历史主动的根本所在
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 21 October 2022 during the 20th Party Congress, asks why the Communist Party of China holds firm to its convictions and keeps the historical initiative. Chen Shuguang answers that the decisive factor is guidance by Marxism, and specifically by Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Chen builds on the Congress report's statement that the Party's success ultimately rests on Marxism "working".

The piece has two sections. The first explains why Marxism is said to work and traces the Party's record of adapting it. The second looks ahead to the Party's responsibility to keep writing new chapters of this adaptation on the new journey.

In the first section, Chen presents Marxism as revealing universal laws of nature, society and thought, as standing for people's liberation and free, all-round human development, and as both interpreting and changing the world. Chen argues that Marxism's effectiveness comes from the Party's continual adaptation of it, citing Mao Zedong's 1938 statement and Deng Xiaoping's 1982 opening speech. Since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Chen says, this effort has produced Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, which Chen calls twenty-first-century Marxism and a new leap in adaptation. In the second section, Chen says Marxism is a guide to action, not dogma, and that theory must develop with practice. Chen lists principles to uphold, including putting the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, and a global outlook.

Chen calls on Party members to keep Marxism's guiding status, deepen theoretical innovation and answer the questions of China, the world, the people and the times. Chen also urges them to study Xi Jinping Thought thoroughly and turn that study into practical results. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Party's official line at the 20th Congress presented Marxism's adaptation as the source of its historical initiative.
quoteEn: Marxist theory is not dogma but a guide to action, and it must develop as practice changes.
quoteZh: 马克思主义理论不是教条，而是行动指南，必须随着实践的变化而发展。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
The official name for China's path of socialist development since reform and opening up, associated with Deng Xiaoping's formulation.

t: The dialectical relationship between the two answers of the Communist Party of China to escaping the historical cycle
zh: 中国共产党跳出历史周期率两个答案的辩证关系
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊); posted on marxism.cass.cn 2022-11-03
paras: Ding Zhongyi takes up the question of how the Communist Party of China can escape the 'historical cycle' of rise and fall, and how its two official answers relate to each other. The first answer is Mao Zedong's 1945 reply of 'people's supervision'. The second is the Party's self-reform, which Xi Jinping named in 2021. Ding argues that the two are distinct in emphasis but internally unified, and that they restrain and reinforce each other.

The article has three parts. The first sets out how the two answers differ. The second, the longest, identifies three shared features: a commitment to 'putting the people first', public-power supervision as a method, and the security of the Party's governing position as a goal. It then examines how the answers condition each other. The third part draws out practical implications for the Party's present 'examination road'. Ding draws on Marx, Engels, Deng Xiaoping and Xi, and on recent Chinese scholarship on the topic.

In Ding's reading, the first answer stresses external constraint, heteronomy and external momentum, while the second stresses introspection, self-discipline and internal momentum. Ding applies the Marxist theory of internal and external causes: external factors work through internal ones. People's supervision supplies social momentum and helps the Party see its own problems. Self-reform in turn improves the quality of people's democracy and moves the Party from passively accepting supervision to seeking it. Ding grounds the shared method in an account of public power as prone to expansion and misuse, so that supervision, both inside and outside the Party, is needed to prevent abuses of power.

Ding proposes that each answer be used for its particular strengths and that their mutual reinforcement be encouraged. Whole-process people's democracy is presented as raising Mao's answer to a new level. Ding also calls for turning institutional advantages into governance effectiveness. This means making democracy effective as well as participatory, and resolving the tension between regulating power and keeping officials active, for example through mechanisms that tolerate errors. Read the original if you want a detailed Party-theory account of how people's supervision and self-reform are meant to work together, with its Marxist and Chinese-source references.)
quoteEn: The Party's self-reform mainly stresses how the Party, through its own building, consolidates the subjective foundation for escaping the historical cycle and strengthens internal momentum.
quoteZh: 党的自我革命侧重强调的是党如何通过自身建设来夯实党跳出历史周期率的主体基础、强化内部动能。

glossary.explanation: The pattern of dynasties and regimes rising quickly and collapsing, raised by Huang Yanpei in his 1945 conversation with Mao Zedong in Yan'an. Party theorists use it to ask how the CPC can stay in power long-term.
The Party's practice of treating itself as the object of reform through criticism, discipline and self-purification. Xi Jinping presented it in 2021 as the second answer to the historical cycle.
An official concept introduced under Xi Jinping describing Chinese socialist democracy as covering every stage of decision-making and governance, not only elections.
An official value stance in Xi-era Party discourse, holding that the Party's work should serve the people's fundamental interests.

t: A vivid narrative of the Communist Party's firm ideals and convictions: what revolutionary cultural relics "say"
zh: 中国共产党坚定理想信念的生动叙事：革命文物的“言说”
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2022 no. 6
paras: Han Ling and Tang Song ask how revolutionary cultural relics can convey the firm ideals and convictions of the Communist Party of China and pass them on to today's young people. They argue that relics "speak" (yanshuo, rendered as narrative): they tell the story of the revolution and turn abstract belief into something that can be seen, heard and touched. In the authors' view this makes them an indispensable tool for the ideological education of youth.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the logic of this "narrative" function and the formula "relic + scene + story + spirit". The second reads particular relics as expressions of the spiritual qualities of the Party's convictions. The third draws out the present-day value of this narrative for educating young people.

The authors claim that relics reconstruct historical scenes and, through "embodied cognition", place visitors inside them. This moves them from the material object to revolutionary spirit, such as the Jinggangshan and Long March spirits. Examples include Li Dazhao's gallows, Fang Zhimin's manuscript, a peasant Party member's handwritten oath, and a mortar at Jinggangshan that visitors may touch. Relics are then linked to three qualities. Mao Zedong's 1929 letter, "A Single Spark Can Start a Prairie Fire", stands for innovative optimism. The Xunwu investigation, Red Army slogans and the "Three Main Rules and Six Points of Attention" stand for a people-centred outlook. The "branch built on the company" and the Ruijin complaint box stand for the Party's self-reform. The authors cite the fall of the Soviet Communist Party to argue that firm conviction and self-reform depend on each other.

The authors propose that educators pair classroom teaching with visits to relics and sites, and to red family letters. Young people's ideals should rest on rational acceptance of scientific theory (Marxism), on a correct grasp of historical laws, and on an accurate assessment of revolutionary figures. Such experience is also meant to help them resist historical nihilism, which the authors say spreads through online media and distorts the image of revolutionary fighters. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Party-history and ideological-education study uses specific relics and anecdotes from Jinggangshan and Ruijin to argue for experiential teaching of ideals and convictions.
quoteEn: Breaking through historical nihilism and returning to historical authenticity is where the value of the "narrative" function of revolutionary cultural relics lies.
quoteZh: 击破历史虚无，回归历史本真，是革命文物“言说”功能的价值所在。

glossary.explanation: Material objects and sites linked to the struggle for national independence and to the Party-led revolution and socialist construction since 1840. They are protected and used in Party-history and patriotic education.
The authors' term, glossed with the English word Narrative, for the function by which relics tell stories and convey values in political education.
A psychological idea, used here to mean that visitors learn by physically placing themselves in reconstructed historical scenes and immersive settings.
Official term for the Party's efforts to correct itself, through criticism and self-criticism and anti-corruption work. The authors trace it back to the Sanwan reorganisation of 1927.
In Party discourse, a label for views seen as denying or distorting the history of the revolution and the Party's record.

t: A good tradition of our Party: studying and applying philosophy in practice
zh: 我们党的一个好传统在实践中学哲学用哲学
paras: This short commentary, published in the People's Daily on 24 October 2022, takes up the Party's tradition of studying and applying philosophy. Tan Qunyu argues that this tradition rests on the Marxist principle that practice is the basis of knowledge, and that it must continue to guide the Party in its new journey.

The piece first sets out four propositions about practice drawn from Marx, Engels, Mao Zedong and Xi Jinping: practice is the source of knowledge, the driving force of its development, and the sole criterion of truth, and it has the character of direct actuality. It then turns to the Party's history over more than a century and to the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Tan contends that knowledge, including indirect knowledge, ultimately derives from direct experience, and that cognition advances through repeated cycles of practice and understanding. A theory counts as true only after testing across many fields and regions, and it then becomes a material force. In Tan's account, the Party has built theory on the practice of the people. Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, the judgement that the principal contradiction in Chinese society has changed, high-quality development, targeted poverty alleviation and ecological civilization are all presented as results of the practice–cognition–practice process.

Tan concludes that the aim of studying philosophy is to improve understanding and guide practice, in pursuit of the second centenary goal. Party members should master the principle that matter determines consciousness, the analysis of contradictions, materialist dialectics, the analysis of society's basic contradictions, and the view that the people create history. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party commentary links Marxist epistemology to the legitimation of current policy.
quoteEn: The fundamental purpose of studying and applying philosophy is to improve understanding and guide practice.
quoteZh: 学哲学用哲学，根本目的在于提高认识、指导实践。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
An official economic policy goal, prominent since 2017, that emphasises quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.
The official aim of building China into a modern socialist country by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic.

t: The generative logic of the experience of putting the people first in the Communist Party of China's century of struggle
zh: 中国共产党百年奋斗中坚持人民至上经验的生成逻辑
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), reposted on marxism.cass.cn, 3 November 2022
paras: Following the Party's 2021 historical resolution, which lists 'putting the people first' among the lessons of its century of struggle, Wan Guangxia asks how that experience came into being. The article argues that it rests on three interlocking logics: a theoretical logic, a historical logic and a practical (contemporary) logic. Together, in Wan's account, they explain why the principle is both a product of the Party's history and a requirement for the present.

The article is organised in three parts that follow this scheme. The first traces theoretical sources: the classical Marxist view of the people as the subject of history, its adaptation in China from Mao Zedong to Xi Jinping, and the people-based (minben) thought of traditional Chinese culture. The second part covers the historical path from the nation 'standing up' to 'becoming prosperous' and 'becoming strong', together with lessons drawn from the ruling experience of proletarian parties, especially the Soviet Union. The third part addresses present-day requirements.

In the theoretical part, Wan identifies three elements in Marx and Engels: the 'real individual' as premise, the people as makers of history, and all-round human development as the goal. Wan then links successive Party leaderships to formulations such as serving the people wholeheartedly, raising living standards as a test of socialism, representing the fundamental interests of the overwhelming majority, putting people first, and the people-centred development philosophy. Traditional ideas of respecting, loving, pacifying and benefiting the people are presented as the cultural root. In the historical part, Wan reads the Soviet case as a warning: a rigid planned economy that neglected livelihoods, weak intra-Party democracy, and a Party that lost its vanguard character and its mass ties through privilege and corruption.

On the practical side, Wan argues that putting the people first is an inherent requirement of upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics: its path, theory, system and culture. It is also required for the new journey of building a modern socialist country that is prosperous, democratic, civilised, harmonious and beautiful. Wan sets out what this means for the material, political, cultural, social and ecological spheres, including whole-process people's democracy, improved livelihoods and green development. Read the original if you want a systematic account, in the Party-theory idiom, of how Chinese scholars derive the principle of putting the people first from Marxist, traditional and Soviet-historical sources.
quoteEn: The experience of putting the people first is an inheritance, innovation and development of the classical Marxist writers' thought on the people as the subject.
quoteZh: 坚持人民至上经验是对马克思主义经典作家人民主体思想的继承创新发展。

glossary.explanation: A principle stressed in Xi Jinping-era Party documents, including the 2021 historical resolution, which lists it among the lessons of the Party's century of struggle. It presents the Party's work as serving the people's interests.
The Party's fundamental purpose, associated with Mao Zedong and written into the Party constitution at the 7th Party Congress (1945).

glossary.zh: 以人民为中心的发展思想
glossary.pinyin: yǐ rénmín wéi zhōngxīn de fāzhǎn sīxiǎng
glossary.literal: development thinking with the people at the centre
glossary.explanation: A formulation associated with Xi Jinping that treats development as being for, reliant on and shared by the people.
An official term for China's democratic model, which stresses people's participation across the full cycle of elections, consultation, decision-making, management and oversight.
The official name for the Party's path of socialist development since reform and opening up.

t: Staying clear-headed and resolute about the problems unique to a large Party through self-reform
zh: 以自我革命保持解决大党独有难题的清醒和坚定
paras: Writing shortly after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Zhang Zhiming asks how the Communist Party of China can keep its character under what the author calls the problems unique to a large Party. The central one, in Zhang's account, is how to govern the Party well and keep it from changing in nature, colour or flavour under opening up, a market economy and long-term rule. Zhang argues that the Party has always faced this problem soberly and that its answer is the Party's self-reform, as Xi Jinping presents it.

The commentary moves through Party history. It begins with the overseas Chinese leader Tan Kah Kee's 1940 visit to Yan'an and his worry, recorded in his memoirs, about whether the Communists could stay clean if they controlled wealthy regions. It then covers the new-democratic revolution, with Mao Zedong's reply to Huang Yanpei, the "two musts" of 1949, the early anti-corruption struggle, and the later turn to mass campaigns and then to rule by institutions after reform and opening up. Finally it sets out four features of the path opened since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Zhang's core argument is that Xi identifies two answers to the "Yan'an cave question": Mao's answer that the people must supervise the government, and the second answer, self-reform. The article treats Mao's "new road of democracy" as consistent in substance with self-reform, since it depended on a Party made strong through its own building, on Party leadership, and on the rule of law. On the post-2012 path, Zhang lists four features. The first is full and rigorous self-governance of the Party driven from within. The second is governing the Party through institutions and Party regulations, combined with ideological education. The third is treating intra-Party supervision as the most fundamental form of supervision, with a system of inspections, supervisory commissions and a National Supervision Law. The fourth is leading the people in developing whole-process people's democracy.

Zhang concludes that self-reform is the Party's innovative, distinctively Chinese way to break out of the historical cycle of rise and fall, and that its institutional rules must keep being refined, with gaps filled and enforcement strengthened. Zhang presents the Party's leadership and the people's mastery of the country as mutually reinforcing. Read the original if you want a Party School scholar's account of how self-reform is linked to earlier Party history and to Xi Jinping's formulations on Party governance.
quoteEn: The success of the new road of democracy depended on the success of the Communist Party of China in strengthening Party leadership and Party building in the spirit of self-reform.
quoteZh: 民主新路的成功取决于中国共产党以自我革命精神加强党的领导和党的建设的成功。

glossary.explanation: The Party's term, emphasised under Xi Jinping, for its capacity to correct and renew itself from within. It is presented as the second answer to the question of how a ruling party can avoid decay.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party-discipline and anti-corruption drive launched after the 18th Party Congress in 2012.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2019. It describes the Chinese democratic model as covering every stage of political life, not only elections.

Refers to the 1945 exchange in Yan'an in which Huang Yanpei asked Mao Zedong how the Party could escape the historical cycle of rise and fall. Mao answered that democracy and the people's supervision of government would do so.

glossary.en: historical cycle of rise and fall
glossary.explanation: The idea that regimes tend to flourish and then decay. Huang Yanpei raised it in 1945, and the Party now says it has escaped it.
Mao Zedong's 1949 call for Party members to remain modest, prudent and free of arrogance, and to keep up their plain style of hard struggle, as the Party prepared to take national power.

t: The Party's century of struggle has fundamentally changed the future and destiny of the Chinese people
zh: 党的百年奋斗从根本上改变了中国人民的前途命运
paras: This commentary, first published in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) in 2021, explains a claim made in the Resolution on the Major Achievements and Historical Experience of the Party's Centenary Struggle, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021): that the Party's hundred years of struggle fundamentally changed the future and destiny of the Chinese people. Yang Fengcheng argues that the change is visible in three areas: China's international standing, the people's political status, and the country's economic condition and living standards.

The article is organised as three historical arcs, each running from the pre-1921 situation to the present. The first goes from the insult of being called the "sick man of East Asia" to "standing up" and approaching "the centre of the world stage". The second goes from feudal autocracy to the people becoming masters of the country and then to whole-process people's democracy. The third goes from poverty and a weak industrial base to economic independence and finally to a moderately prosperous society in all respects.

Yang's core argument is that each shift was brought about by the Party's leadership at successive stages. On national dignity, Yang points to the anti-imperialist struggles of the 1920s, the war of resistance against Japan, the abolition of unequal treaties in 1949 and the Korean War, then to reform-era diplomacy and the Belt and Road Initiative. On democracy, the article credits the Party with politically educating and organising the peasantry, and with building the people's congress system, multiparty cooperation, regional ethnic autonomy and grassroots democracy. It also warns that Western "constitutionalism", multiparty rotation and the separation of powers must be guarded against. On the economy, Yang describes China as having avoided the dependent development of some former colonies, and cites figures such as GDP above 100 trillion yuan in 2020, per capita GDP above US$10,000, and a middle-income group of more than 400 million.

Yang concludes that a century earlier China appeared to the world as a picture of decline, whereas it now shows vigour, and that the founding of the Party was an epoch-making event that changed the direction of the Chinese nation. The author presents the achievement of the first centenary goal as a milestone and sees the country moving towards the second, a modern socialist power. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how Party historiography frames the Party's century in terms of national independence, democracy and prosperity.
quoteEn: The founding of the Communist Party of China was an epoch-making event that profoundly changed the direction and course of the Chinese nation's development in modern times, and profoundly changed the future and destiny of the Chinese people and nation.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的成立是开天辟地的大事，深刻改变了近代以后中华民族发展的方向和进程，深刻改变了中国人民和中华民族的前途和命运。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2019 that describes China's democracy as covering every stage of political life, from elections to consultation, decision-making, management and oversight. Official sources present it as a distinct form of democracy.
A Chinese international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched in 2013.

glossary.en: a moderately prosperous society in all respects
glossary.explanation: A Party development goal, announced at the 16th Party Congress in 2002 and declared achieved in 2021. It is the first of the "Two Centenary Goals".

t: Embedding the requirement of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party in the Party's leadership of economic work
zh: 把全面从严治党要求体现在党领导经济工作之中
paras: Writing in Economic Daily on 24 October 2022, just after the 20th Party Congress, Ye Xiaowen takes up how the Party's comprehensive leadership of economic work can be secured. Ye argues that full and rigorous self-governance of the Party must be built into that leadership, linking discipline and anti-corruption work with deepening reform, improving institutions and promoting development.

The commentary opens from the first of the thirteen components of Xi Jinping's economic thought, the Party's overall leadership of economic work. It then proceeds under three headings: restraining power through institutions, strengthening ideological foundations, and ensuring the Party does not 'change in quality, colour or flavour'. Ye draws throughout on the 20th Party Congress report and on Xi Jinping's remarks.

Ye contends that the Party faces lasting tests, including that of the market economy, which makes self-reform especially urgent. In Ye's account, a socialist market economy brings the risk of corruption from collusion between power and capital. Ye credits the post-2012 anti-corruption system with an 'overwhelming victory' but says residual corruption remains and has taken new forms. The remedy has two sides: institutional checks that make officials unwilling, unable and afraid to be corrupt, and ideological education through Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, ideals and convictions, and traditional Chinese virtues.

Ye concludes that the high-pressure stance against corruption must be kept up, while mechanisms are also built to motivate officials to act. These aim to make cadres willing and able to get things done as well as loyal, clean and responsible. This, Ye says, would let the Party lead economic work better and advance towards common prosperity. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-building discourse after the 20th Party Congress ties anti-corruption to economic governance.
quoteEn: To build the requirement of full and rigorous self-governance into the Party's leadership of economic work, we must strengthen the ideological foundation, raise Party-spirit awareness and improve the ability to resist corruption and degeneration.
quoteZh: 把全面从严治党要求体现在党领导经济工作之中，必须从思想上固本培元，提高党性觉悟，增强拒腐防变能力

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since 2014, covering Party discipline, ideology, organisation and anti-corruption work.
A stated goal of socialism with Chinese characteristics, meaning prosperity shared by all, which has been emphasised in Party documents since 2021.
The official name for China's economic system, which combines market allocation of resources with Party leadership and a major role for the public sector.

glossary.pinyin: bù gǎn fǔ, bù néng fǔ, bù xiǎng fǔ
glossary.en: unwilling, unable and afraid to be corrupt
glossary.literal: dare not, cannot, do not want to be corrupt
glossary.explanation: An official formula for a three-part anti-corruption system, combining deterrence, institutional constraint and ideological education.

t: The three national conferences held in the history of the Communist Party of China
zh: 党史上召开过的三次全国代表会议
paras: Published in Study Times shortly before the 20th Party Congress (2022), this short historical commentary explains a lesser-known Party institution: the national conference, which differs by one character from the national congress. Wu notes that the Party Constitution allows committees to convene delegate conferences when necessary to decide major issues that need prompt resolution. Wu presents the national conference as an important organisational system and a useful supplement to the congress.

The article reviews the three national conferences in Party history: the 1937 Soviet Areas Delegates' Conference in Yan'an, the 1955 national conference in Beijing, and the 1985 national conference. For each, Wu gives the dates, the participants, the agenda and the speeches and resolutions.

Wu describes the 1937 conference, with over 200 delegates representing more than 40,000 members, as the only such conference of the new-democratic revolution period. It endorsed the Central Committee's line since the Zunyi Meeting and prepared the Party for the War of Resistance. The 1955 conference approved the First Five-Year Plan outline and set up supervisory commissions; Wu quotes Mao Zedong calling it another rectification meeting. The 1985 conference adopted the proposals for the Seventh Five-Year Plan and adjusted the central leadership to speed generational turnover.

Wu concludes that all three conferences were convened urgently, at key historical junctures, and resolved major problems. The latest revised Party Constitution specifies the conference's powers: discussing and deciding major issues, and adjusting or adding members of the Central Committee and the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection. In Wu's account, the conference is therefore retained as a regular organisational system. Read the original if you want a concise factual overview of an obscure Party institution and its three precedents.
quoteEn: The three national conferences in our Party's history were convened to meet urgent needs, arose from their times and acted in step with circumstances, and each resolved major historical problems at an important historical juncture.
quoteZh: 我党历史上的三次全国代表会议应急而开、因时而生、顺势而为，都是在重要历史节点解决了重大历史问题。

glossary.explanation: A Party meeting of delegates convened between congresses when necessary to decide major issues promptly. It is provided for in the Party Constitution and is smaller in standing than the national congress.
A Politburo enlarged meeting held in January 1935 during the Long March. Party histories treat it as the point at which Mao Zedong's leadership was established.
A Party campaign of criticism, self-criticism and ideological education, first launched in Yan'an in the early 1940s.

t: Adhering to full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and advancing Party building
st: Officials of the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection, the Organization Department and the Central Policy Research Office brief the press
zh: 坚持全面从严治党 深入推进党的建设
zhSub: 中纪委、中组部、中央政策研究室负责人介绍坚定不移全面从严治党有关情况
paras: This is a report, compiled by Guangming Daily journalist Gong Liang, on the second press conference of the 20th Party Congress press centre, held on the afternoon of 17 October 2022. Three officials spoke: Xiao Pei of the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the National Supervisory Commission, Xu Qifang of the Central Organization Department, and Tian Peiyan of the Central Policy Research Office. The theme was unwavering full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and the new great project of Party building in the new era.

The report arranges the officials' answers under short thematic headings. These cover full and rigorous self-governance of the Party as the defining theme of Party building, the implementation of the Party's organizational line, theoretical innovation, the Two Establishes, rule-based governance of the Party, strict management of cadres, and the comprehensive nature of Party leadership. Four sidebar items give figures from opinion surveys, inspections, Party regulations and poverty-alleviation work.

Xiao Pei describes the past decade's anti-corruption struggle as unprecedented and says it reversed lax and soft Party governance and kept the Party from degenerating or being infiltrated by interest groups. Xu Qifang lists six strands of organizational work, from strengthening Party leadership to talent strategy, and stresses strict supervision of officials, including reporting of personal matters and rules on the business activities of officials' relatives. Tian Peiyan presents Xi Jinping's ideas on Party building as an original contribution to Marxist theory. He calls the Two Establishes the major political achievement of the new era and says rules-based governance is the fundamental remedy. He adds that Party leadership must be implemented comprehensively, systematically and as an integral whole. The sidebars cite a survey in which 97.4 per cent of respondents considered the effort effective, and say that nearly 4,000 Party regulations are in force, over 70 per cent of them newly made or revised in the past decade.

The speakers say the 20th Party Congress (2022) set out a strategic plan to deepen Party building, and they promise further work on strengthening centralized leadership, improving the Party's self-reform, and winning the long-term anti-corruption campaign. They present this as a guarantee for building a modern socialist country. Read the original if you want a compact official statement of how Party leaders framed Party discipline, cadre management and regulation at the start of the 20th Party Congress, together with the figures they cited.
quoteEn: Governing the Party through institutions and Party regulations is the fundamental remedy in the Party's full and rigorous self-governance, and the basic means of managing and governing the Party.
quoteZh: 制度治党、依规治党是我们党全面从严治党的治本之策，是管党治党的基本方式

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan of the Xi Jinping era, used since 2014, for a sustained drive for Party discipline, anti-corruption work and stricter management of members and cadres.
A formula from the 2021 Party history resolution. It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and the whole Party, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
An official term for the Party's claimed capacity to correct itself and clean up its own ranks, in the context of anti-corruption and discipline.
Rules issued by the Party for its own organizations and members, separate from state law. They govern discipline, organization and internal political life.

t: Clearly and firmly strengthening the Party's political development
zh: 旗帜鲜明加强党的政治建设
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 13 October 2022, takes up Mao Zedong's 1944 dictum that "the key to all problems lies in politics", which Xi Jinping cited in January 2021. Xiao Guiqing argues that politics is as decisive in the new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics as it was in the New Democratic revolution, and that strengthening the Party's political development is therefore the "golden key" to the Party's tasks.

The piece is short and built around a repeated formula: the more complex the situation and the heavier the tasks, the more the Party must act in four areas. These are political direction and political leadership, the people as the political foundation, political capability, and political discipline.

Xiao argues that political direction is the first question for the Party's survival and development, and that upholding it means upholding the Party's leadership and the central leadership's centralised, unified authority. Citing Mao's follow-on remark that the key of all politics is the masses, the author ties the people-centred approach to the Party's original aspiration. The author also stresses political capability as the first of the abilities cadres need, especially senior cadres, who must understand "matters of national importance" and see problems politically. On discipline, Xiao presents the Party's self-reform and the anti-corruption campaign since the 18th Party Congress (2012) as a second answer to the "historical cycle" question.

Xiao concludes that Mao's dictum has been confirmed by more than 70 years of practice. Communists now face a "new test" and a "fresh departure" at the junction of the two centenary goals, and the author calls on the Party to use political development to address the major questions of the new era. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party theorists framed political development in the run-up to the 20th Party Congress (2022).
quoteEn: An important part of raising political capability is being good at analysing and solving problems from a political standpoint.
quoteZh: 提高政治能力，很重要的一条就是要善于从政治上分析问题、解决问题。

glossary.explanation: A strand of Party-building stressed since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It covers political direction, loyalty to the central leadership, political ability and discipline.
A formula used by Xi Jinping for the Party's continuous efforts to purify itself, including through anti-corruption and discipline.
Official goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary (2021) and a modern socialist country by the PRC's centenary (2049).
The idea, raised by Huang Yanpei to Mao in 1945, that regimes rise and then decline. Party discourse offers supervision by the people as the first answer and self-reform as the second.

t: Major historic achievements in the Party's political building in the new era
zh: 新时代党的政治建设取得重大历史性成就
paras: Published in Guangming Daily on 12 October 2022, shortly before the 20th Party Congress, this commentary takes up the Party's "political building" (dang de zhengzhi jianshe) since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Fan and Yang argue that the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core placed political building first among the Party's fundamental tasks, and that original ideas and transformative practice have produced major historic achievements. These, they say, give a firm political guarantee for the "great new project" of Party building.

The piece has three parts. The first presents Xi Jinping's statements on political building as an original contribution to Marxist theory of Party building. The second sets out the achievements and basic experience of the new era under five headings. The third treats political building as a permanent task and lists four directions for further work.

In the first part the authors identify four claims: that taking a clear political stand is the Party's political advantage; that the first task is ensuring the whole Party obeys the Central Committee and upholds its authority and centralised, unified leadership; that political building is the fundamental form of Party building, deciding its direction and effect; and that the Party must consolidate its governing base, nurture a healthy political ecology, guard against political risks and raise political capability. The second part reviews the record: arming the Party with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, institutional rules on Party leadership, the people-centred approach (including poverty eradication and the eight-point regulations), training leading cadres, and anti-corruption work, which the authors say has achieved an overwhelming victory.

Fan and Yang conclude that, because the Party's political advanced character cannot be secured once and for all, political building is a permanent task and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party must continue. They propose strengthening ideological guidance, implementing the Two Upholds, improving political capability and purifying political life inside the Party. Read the original if you want an official-line account of how Party-history researchers frame political building on the eve of the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Strengthening the Party's political building is not a stopgap measure but the fundamental way to make the Party stronger and consistently sound, and it must be pursued with perseverance and without relaxation.
quoteZh: 加强党的政治建设不是一时之计，而是把党建设得更加坚强有力、使自身始终过硬的根本途径，必须持之以恒、常抓不懈。

glossary.explanation: A concept placed by the Party leadership after 2012 at the head of its Party-building agenda. It centres on political stance, loyalty to the Central Committee, political discipline and a healthy political ecology.
A formula from the 6th Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021) affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the whole Party, and the guiding role of his thought.
The requirement that Party members firmly uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and the state constitution in 2018.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the campaign since 2012 to tighten Party discipline, conduct and anti-corruption enforcement.

t: The Yan'an Rectification Movement and strengthening the Party's centralised and unified leadership
zh: 延安整风与加强党的集中统一领导
paras: Published in Guangming Daily in October 2022, this short historical commentary asks how the Yan'an Rectification Movement (1941–45) helped the Chinese Communist Party build centralised and unified leadership. Opening with Xi Jinping's 2021 remark that rectification brought the Party 'unprecedented unity', Tan Huwa argues that the movement was an ideological education campaign. In Tan's account it taught the whole Party to apply Marxism-Leninism to China's practical problems and to understand Marxist Party-building principles, and so it strengthened centralised leadership.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why strengthening centralised and unified leadership reached the historical agenda during the War of Resistance. The second follows the central documents and institutional steps of 1941–43. The third takes the Northwest Bureau and the Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region as a model case of implementation, using speeches by Chen Yun, Ren Bishi and Mao Zedong and local directives of 1943.

Tan gives four reasons for the need: the survival of sectarianism and 'mountain-top' tendencies from the Land Revolution period and the influence of Wang Ming's dogmatism; harsher conditions behind enemy lines, which demanded unified command; mistaken ideas arising from the 'three-thirds' system, such as the view that Party organisation hardly mattered in government; and the new burden of local governance. The key document, the 'September 1' decision of 1942, is presented as affirming that the Party leads all other organisations. It required lower levels to obey higher ones and the whole Party to obey the Centre. It also limited Party leadership of government to principles and policy, not substitution for it. Tan then links this to the formation of a leadership core, including the 1943 decision making Mao Zedong chairman of the Politburo and Secretariat. In the Northwest Bureau, the Party committee was made the centre of unified leadership over mass organisations, propaganda broadcasts, army relations and economic bodies such as the salt industry. Tan also notes shortcomings that remained by late 1943, especially weak Party control over the army and finance.

Tan concludes that rectification further cleared away subjectivism and sectarianism, raised the standards of Party building and comprehensively strengthened centralised leadership. In Tan's view, this laid an important ideological and political basis for victory in the War of Resistance and in the democratic revolution. Read the original if you want a compact, officially framed account of the documents and Northwest Bureau practice through which Yan'an-era Party unity is presented today.
quoteEn: The advance of the Yan'an Rectification further cleared away subjectivism and sectarianism within the Party, set higher requirements for Party building, and comprehensively strengthened the Party's centralised and unified leadership.
quoteZh: 延安整风的推进对党内主观主义、宗派主义进行了进一步清理，对党的建设也提出了更高要求，全面加强了党的集中统一领导
