glossary.explanation: A Party-wide ideological campaign launched in 1941 and lasting to about 1945, aimed at subjectivism, sectarianism and Party formalism. It consolidated Mao Zedong's leadership and shaped later Party-building practice.
The principle that the whole Party and all other organisations act under the unified direction of the Party Centre. It is a core concept in the Party's account of its own authority.
A 1940 principle for anti-Japanese base-area governments: Communists were to hold no more than one third of seats, with the rest for non-Party left-progressives and middle-of-the-road figures.

t: Providing a firm guarantee for advancing the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics
st: Reading Xi Jinping's "Implement the Party's organizational line for the new era and keep making the Party stronger and more powerful"
zh: 为推进中国特色社会主义事业提供坚强保证
zhSub: 读习近平总书记《贯彻落实新时代党的组织路线，不断把党建设得更加坚强有力》
paras: This commentary, first published in Study Times and posted in October 2022, reads Xi Jinping's speech of 29 June 2020 at a Politburo study session of the 19th Central Committee. Feng presents the speech as a guide to action for carrying out the Party's organizational line for the new era. The article argues that this line gives the Party a firm organizational guarantee for upholding and strengthening its overall leadership and for advancing socialism with Chinese characteristics.

The piece has three parts. It first sets out the scientific content of the organizational line, which Xi first formulated in full at the 2018 national organization work conference. It then reviews achievements in Party organization since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Finally, it lists measures for implementing the line.

Feng reports four points on content: arming the whole Party with scientific theory, focusing on the organizational system, choosing and using the right people, and subordinating the organizational line to the political line. On achievements, the author cites 96.712 million Party members and 4.936 million primary-level organizations at the end of 2021. Feng also cites the "five systems" for cadre training and selection, and a series of regulations on primary-level organizations. The implementation measures include Party leadership over organizational work, the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, a tight organizational system, putting the people at the centre, and improving organizational rules.

Feng concludes that a tightly organized Party can unite its members, gather talent and mobilize the public to meet major risks and challenges. Together, these measures are meant to raise the Party's creativity, cohesion and combat effectiveness. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party media present the organizational line for the new era and its claimed results.
quoteEn: A tight organizational system is where a Marxist party's strength and advantage lie.
quoteZh: 严密的组织体系是马克思主义政党的优势所在、力量所在

glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding principles for organizational work, including Party building, cadre selection and talent policy. It is said to serve the Party's political line.
A formula from the 6th Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the Party's core and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralized leadership of the Central Committee.
The five systems for building a high-quality cadre corps: training, judging people, selection and appointment, strict management, and positive incentives.

t: How to overcome the "fear of lacking skills" when facing online public opinion
zh: 面对网络舆情如何克服“本领恐慌”
paras: This short commentary, first published in Study Times (Xuexi Shibao), asks how Party leading cadres can overcome the "fear of lacking skills" (benling konghuang) when dealing with online public opinion. The authors observe that, in recent hot-button online incidents, some cadres at first ignored the issue or treated it lightly, then panicked or avoided it, so that incidents escalated and rebounded on them. They argue that the remedy lies in correct views of news and public opinion, institutional and organisational capacity, and practical analytical tools.

The piece sets out three steps in turn. It begins with ideological orientation, then moves to systems and organisation, and ends with concrete methods for judging public opinion. It draws on Xi Jinping's call to become expert in using new media and on Mao Zedong's remarks on running newspapers.

First, the authors call for a Marxist view of news that combines Party spirit with the people's character, and a view of public opinion that relies on the masses. Cadres should not trust a few influential online "big Vs", since the "silent majority" matters more. Second, they propose a routine system of monitoring, early warning, response and review, a streamlined organisation for rapid "discover–decide–execute" action, legal and disciplinary oversight, and a young, media-literate team backed by outside experts. Third, they recommend four tools: monitoring notes, emotion-volume charts, communication-path maps and process-analysis charts. Each helps cadres track a case's platforms, emotions, key accounts and life-cycle stages.

The authors conclude that these measures can raise cadres' sensitivity to online opinion and their ability to anticipate its course. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party media commentary frames cadre training in online public-opinion work, including its practical tools.
quoteEn: Good work on online public opinion is built up in ordinary times; without day-to-day accumulation it is hard to achieve anything in a moment of need.
quoteZh: 做好网络舆情工作功在平时，无平日之积累难有一时之作为

glossary.explanation: A phrase associated with Mao Zedong and repeatedly used by Xi Jinping. It refers to cadres' anxiety that their abilities do not meet the demands of new tasks, and it is used to urge continuous learning.

t: Grasping the characteristics of young people to teach ideological and political courses well
zh: 把握青少年特点上好思政课
paras: This short commentary, published in the People's Daily and reposted in October 2022, asks how ideological and political theory courses in schools can be taught more effectively. Han Liying argues that they must be designed around the characteristics of young people, in line with Xi Jinping's remark that ideological and political education is a continuous process that should target each stage of growth. The aim, in the author's account, is to cultivate a new generation able to take on the task of national rejuvenation.

The article is organised under three headings: building a firm ideological foundation, following the laws of young people's development, and enriching the forms of teaching. Each is presented as a requirement for fulfilling the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education.

On content, Han calls for sustained education in Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, in the histories of the Party, New China, reform and opening up and socialism, and in patriotism, collectivism and socialist core values. On developmental stages, the author distinguishes early adolescence, with vivid, image-based thinking suited to experiential learning, middle adolescence, with emerging abstract thinking suited to commonsense learning, and late adolescence, with more complex thinking suited to inquiry-based learning. On method, Han urges teachers to answer students' real questions through case-based, experiential and interactive teaching, turning 'big principles' into 'small stories', respecting students' central position and using modern information technology.

Han concludes that tiered course content, matched to the stages of growth and delivered in lively forms, will gradually raise young people's ideological and political awareness and strengthen the appeal of the courses. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese education scholar sets out the official rationale and teaching approach for school ideological and political courses.
quoteEn: Young people's growth is a unity of continuity and stages: a process with distinct features at each stage, yet with each stage linked to the one before.
quoteZh: 青少年的成长是连续性和阶段性的统一，是具有不同阶段特点又前后关联的过程。

glossary.explanation: Compulsory courses (often shortened to 思政课) in Chinese schools and universities that teach Marxism, Party history and official ideology. They are a central channel of political education.
A slogan defining the fundamental task of education in China: moral and political character formation alongside knowledge.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
A set of twelve official values promoted since 2012, covering the national, social and individual levels.
The policy of economic reform and engagement with the outside world launched in China in 1978.

t: Providing the people with more reliable and fuller social security
zh: 为人民提供更可靠更充分的保障
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily in October 2022, asks how China can give its people "more reliable and fuller" social security. Jiang Wenling, a regional civil affairs official, argues that meeting people's needs for a better life and steadily advancing common prosperity require a social security system with full coverage that is sustainable.

Opening with a statement by Xi Jinping on social security as a basic institutional safeguard, the piece is organised around four principles: Party leadership, putting the people first, reform and innovation, and service first.

Jiang first claims that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Party Central Committee has given social security top-level design, producing a functionally complete system built around social insurance, with social assistance, welfare and special care for veterans and their families. Jiang then presents the people-first principle as the starting point of the system, tied to common prosperity and to improving livelihoods from childcare to elderly care. The author says reform must respond to population ageing, urbanisation and more varied forms of employment, and must target the people's most pressing concerns.

Jiang calls for multi-tier, multi-pillar pension insurance, provincial-level pooling of basic medical, unemployment and work-injury insurance, better urban–rural social assistance, and more accurate identification of beneficiaries. The author also urges a unified online–offline service platform, digital transformation of social insurance administration, and an emergency response mechanism for major risks, drawing on experience from routine epidemic control. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style statement of the policy priorities for social security after the 18th Party Congress.
quoteEn: To provide the broad masses with more reliable and fuller security, we must put the people first and uphold common prosperity, take improving people's wellbeing and promoting social fairness as the fundamental starting point and goal of social security work, and let the fruits of reform and development benefit all the people more widely and more fairly.
quoteZh: 为广大人民群众提供更可靠更充分的保障，必须坚持人民至上，坚持共同富裕，把增进民生福祉、促进社会公平作为发展社会保障事业的根本出发点和落脚点，使改革发展成果更多更公平惠及全体人民。

glossary.explanation: A goal of shared wealth for all, long associated with socialism in Chinese official discourse and given renewed emphasis under Xi Jinping.
An official principle under Xi Jinping holding that the people's interests rank highest in Party and government work.
The set of institutions covering social insurance, social assistance, social welfare and special care for veterans and their families.

t: Gathering great strength through unity: setting the banner and direction for united front work
zh: 以团结汇聚伟力为统战举旗定向
paras: Writing in 2022, a hundred years after the Communist Party first formally put forward a united front policy, Liu Jiaqiang offers a study-and-implementation reading of Xi Jinping's speech at the Central United Front Work Conference. Liu presents the speech as a programmatic document that gives fundamental guidance for strengthening the patriotic united front in the new era. The article is a commentary by a senior figure from one of China's non-communist parties.

The piece is organised in five sections. They cover the importance of developing the patriotic united front, the guiding thought for united front work, the Party's leadership as its basic principle, the historical responsibility of unity, and the task of making multi-party cooperation more standardised and vigorous. Liu draws heavily on Xi's own formulations and on the Party's 2021 resolution on its history.

Liu's central claim is that the united front is a key instrument for the Party in winning struggles and governing, and for uniting Chinese people at home and abroad behind the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Liu reports Xi's "three more important" roles: defending sovereignty, security and development interests; serving the central tasks of national development; and broadening the Party's class and mass base amid social change. The article lists the "twelve musts" that summarise Xi's important thinking on united front work and says this thinking draws on Marxist united front theory, the Party's century of practice, socialism with Chinese characteristics and traditional Chinese culture. Liu argues that Party leadership is the first political principle, pointing to the Central United Front Work Leading Group and the revised united front work regulations. Liu also stresses unity as a historical responsibility, to be pursued through the "unity–criticism–unity" tradition and by seeking common ground while respecting diversity.

Liu concludes that the democratic parties should treat studying Xi's speech as a political task. Liu calls on them to uphold Party leadership, strengthen their own theoretical education and organisation, and serve the central tasks of the country, in preparation for the 20th Party Congress (2022). Liu describes the multi-party cooperation system as a new type of party system grown from Chinese soil. Read the original if you want to see how a leader of a non-communist party presents the official reading of the 2022 united front conference and the role assigned to the democratic parties.
quoteEn: United front work is work with people; the purpose of the united front is to strengthen the forces that strive together.
quoteZh: 统一战线是做人的工作，搞统一战线就是为了壮大共同奋斗的力量。

glossary.explanation: A Party strategy of building alliances with non-Party groups and forces, including the democratic parties, ethnic and religious groups, entrepreneurs and overseas Chinese. It is overseen by the Party's United Front Work Department.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.
The eight non-communist parties in China, such as the RCCK, which take part in political consultation under the leadership of the Communist Party.

t: Dare to struggle, dare to win
zh: 敢于斗争 敢于胜利
paras: This short commentary, first published in People's Daily and dated October 2022, argues that a willingness to struggle and to win is the Chinese Communist Party's invincible spiritual strength. Qiu Xin takes as a starting point Xi Jinping's call to the whole Party to heighten awareness of danger, hold to bottom-line thinking and strengthen the will and ability to struggle.

The piece moves from the Party's history to the present and then to what is required of its members. It describes the Party's first century as one long history of great struggle, reviews the risks of the past ten years, and sets out why struggle will continue.

Qiu argues that society advances through contradictions, so struggle is unavoidable. In the author's account, the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation will not be easy, and the world is undergoing changes unseen in a century, which means more risks. The author lists achievements of the new era as results of struggle, among them the victory in poverty alleviation, the results of balancing economic development with epidemic control, and changes in ecological protection. Qiu holds that struggle will accompany the whole process of reaching the second centenary goal, and that complacency or avoiding contradictions is wrong. The author names tasks that demand struggle, including full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, high-quality development, rural revitalisation and national security.

Qiu concludes that the ability to struggle is not innate. It must be built through ideological tempering, political experience, practice and professional training, so that Party members and cadres can stand firm on principle and take responsibility in a crisis. Read the original if you want a brief example of how the official press framed the theme of struggle shortly before the 20th Party Congress (2022).
quoteEn: The various struggles we face are not short-term but long-term, and will accompany at least the whole process of achieving the second centenary goal.
quoteZh: 我们面临的各种斗争不是短期的而是长期的，至少要伴随我们实现第二个百年奋斗目标全过程。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's "Chinese Dream".

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The slogan for a campaign, prominent since 2012, to strengthen discipline, combat corruption and tighten Party organisation.
An official economic goal, stressed since 2017, that favours innovation, efficiency and sustainability over speed of growth alone.
The goal of building China into a modern socialist country by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic.

t: Carrying forward the spirit of historical initiative to create new great undertakings
zh: 发扬历史主动精神开创新伟业
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscript in October 2022, Sun Cunliang takes up Xi Jinping's repeated call, since the 18th Party Congress (2012), to grasp the general trend of history and seize the historical initiative. Sun defines this as exercising human subjective initiative on the basis of historical laws, so as to analyse the trend of history scientifically and overcome obstacles. The article argues that the Party's mastery of historical initiative rests on historical materialism, has deep roots in Party tradition, and answers present needs.

The piece has three parts. The first explains historical materialism as the ideological basis of the spirit of historical initiative. The second treats the Party's consistent hold on the initiative as a historical tradition and political strength. The third sets out how to walk the "new road to the examination" (the new journey towards the second centenary goal) while keeping the initiative.

In Sun's account, historical laws are objective, but people are not passive before them. The Party must unite conformity with law and conformity with purpose, combining respect for objective laws with creative practice. Sun reads the Party's whole history, from its founding through new-democratic revolution, socialist revolution, reform and opening up, and the new era, as a history of seizing the initiative. Three reasons are given for continuing to do so: it is a lesson of a century of Party history, an element of strategic thinking, and a requirement for meeting major risks as national rejuvenation draws nearer. Sun contends that risks must be anticipated rather than met passively.

For the new journey, Sun proposes six tasks: studying historical laws and summing up experience; strengthening historical confidence through a correct view of Party history under historical materialism; heightening awareness of opportunity, risk and bottom-line thinking while keeping strategic resolve; carrying forward the fighting spirit; and daring to undertake self-reform. Self-reform is tied to full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, anti-corruption work and reliance on the people. Sun's aim is a Marxist governing party that remains in the forefront of the times and enjoys the people's support. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholarship in 2022 linked historical materialism to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and the Party's self-reform.
quoteEn: Carrying forward the spirit of historical initiative requires always upholding a high degree of unity between conformity with law and conformity with purpose, which is a basic requirement for a Marxist party.
quoteZh: 发扬历史主动精神，必须始终坚持合规律性与合目的性的高度统一，这是对马克思主义政党的一个基本要求。

glossary.literal: historical initiative / taking the lead in history
glossary.explanation: A phrase used in Party discourse for consciously grasping historical trends and acting proactively rather than reacting. Xi Jinping stressed it repeatedly, notably in the 2021 Party centenary resolution.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central national goal in Party discourse, referring to restoring China's strength and international standing, with 2049 as the target date for the main stage.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The slogan for the Party-building and anti-corruption drive launched after the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering political, ideological, organisational, conduct and discipline building.

A formulation stressing that the Party must correct its own problems through internal discipline and rectification, presented as the answer to the question of how to escape the historical cycle of rise and fall.

glossary.literal: new road of going to sit the exam
glossary.explanation: An image from Mao Zedong in 1949, who likened the march to Beijing to going to take an examination. Xi has applied it to the journey towards the second centenary goal of building a modern socialist country.

t: Promoting the great unity of all Chinese sons and daughters
zh: 促进中华儿女大团结
authors: Theoretical Study Group of the Party Leadership Group of the Central Institute of Socialism
paras: Published in the People's Daily in 2022, this commentary by the Party leadership group's theoretical study group at the Central Institute of Socialism takes up Xi Jinping's statement that promoting the great unity of all Chinese sons and daughters is the historical responsibility of the patriotic united front in the new era. The authors argue that unity guarantees the Chinese people's ability to overcome risks and challenges, and that the united front must keep consolidating unity among all ethnic groups, all the people and all Chinese at home and abroad in order to support the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article has four parts. It first traces the united front from the Second Party Congress of 1922 through the revolutionary periods, the founding of the People's Republic, the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978) and the new era. It then reviews achievements in united front work since the 18th Party Congress (2012), grouped as theoretical, institutional and practical results. The final and longest part sets out five tasks for the Central Institute of Socialism, which the authors describe as a higher political college of a united front character.

The authors argue that unity is the essence and permanent theme of the united front, which "arose from unity and prospers through unity". In their account the new-era front is the Party's broadest alliance and has been embedded in the system of national governance. They credit Xi Jinping's important thinking on united front work as theory, new regulations and leading groups as institutions, and results in multiparty cooperation, ethnic work, religious work, non-public-sector figures and outreach to Hong Kong, Macao, Taiwan and overseas Chinese as practice. The five tasks they list are upholding Party leadership as the "centre of the circle", teaching the Party's innovative theory, anchoring unity in the goal of national rejuvenation, promoting patriotism, and strengthening cultural identity.

The authors conclude that the Institute should train united front personnel and build a shared ideological and political foundation. This means bringing Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era "into textbooks, classrooms and minds", and fostering the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds among students. It also means promoting Chinese modernization, patriotic education and the overseas spread of Chinese culture. Read the original if you want a concise official statement of how the united front's history, achievements and training tasks are presented in 2022 for a Party-school audience.
quoteEn: The united front arose from unity and prospers through unity.
quoteZh: 统一战线因团结而生，靠团结而兴。

glossary.explanation: The Communist Party's strategy of building alliances with non-Party groups and social forces. Its work is led by the United Front Work Department.
A Party-run college that trains non-Communist Party members, including members of the democratic parties and non-Party figures, for united front work.
A formula adopted in 2021–22 affirming Xi Jinping's position as the Party's core and the guiding role of his thought.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party Central Committee's authority and centralised leadership.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central goal of Party rhetoric under Xi Jinping, linked to the Chinese Dream and the second centenary goal for 2049.

t: Giving full play to the political function of primary-level Party organisations
zh: 充分发挥基层党组织的政治功能
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 30 September 2022, Wang Binglin asks how the Communist Party's primary-level organisations can be strengthened so that they carry out the Party's line effectively. Wang's answer is that these organisations must give full play to their political function. The author starts from the claim that a Marxist party's basic attribute is political and its basic function is political. The article cites official figures of 96.712 million Party members and 4.936 million primary-level organisations at the end of 2021.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why the political function is necessary. The second reviews what primary-level organisations have achieved since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and the weaknesses that remain. The third proposes four areas of work for Party building in the new era.

Wang gives four reasons why the political function is necessary: it is required by the Party's overall leadership, by the people-centred approach to development, by upholding and developing the socialist system with Chinese characteristics, and by full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. The author insists that primary-level organisations are a "fighting fortress" and must not become mere service bodies, even though service is one of their functions. Achievements cited include the Two Upholds, the extension of branches into villages, communities and research teams, the work of Party members in the Covid-19 response and disasters, and poverty alleviation. Wang also lists shortcomings. These include weak implementation of policy, an emphasis on economic targets at the expense of responding to people's demands, gaps in coverage (especially in emerging sectors), an ageing cadre pool, and formalism such as time spent on forms and records.

Wang calls for work in four areas. The first is to secure the leading position of primary-level organisations in grassroots governance. The second is to meet people's growing needs for a better life by combining management with service. The third is to raise organisational capacity: set up organisations in step with social change, choose and strengthen leaders, promote capable Party workers, and give primary-level organisations more resources and powers. The fourth is to extend full and rigorous self-governance of the Party downwards through theoretical education, criticism and self-criticism, and checks on petty powers. Read the original if you want a concise official-academic statement of how Party-building scholars justify and prescribe the political role of grassroots Party branches after 2012.
quoteEn: Primary-level Party organisations are fighting fortresses and must not become mere service organisations; their political function must be given full play.
quoteZh: 基层党组织是战斗堡垒，不能变成单纯的服务组织，其政治功能要充分发挥。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A Party-building policy line promoted since 2012 that stresses discipline, anti-corruption and the Party's responsibility for managing its own members.
A formula requiring Party members to uphold General Secretary Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised leadership of the Central Committee.
A standard Party description of primary-level organisations as strong, disciplined bases that carry out the Party's tasks and mobilise the masses.

glossary.zh: 以人民为中心的发展思想
glossary.pinyin: yǐ rénmín wéi zhōngxīn de fāzhǎn sīxiǎng
glossary.explanation: A principle in Xi Jinping-era Party theory that development should serve the people's interests and aspirations.

t: Building firm faith on a theoretical foundation
zh: 以理论之基筑牢信仰根基
paras: Writing as a young cadre working in theory and publicity, Lü Hongbo takes up Xi Jinping's 2021 call for young cadres to be firm in conviction and loyal to the Party. Lü argues that firm ideals and convictions come from firm theory, and that only a solid theoretical foundation can anchor faith.

This short commentary in Study Times is organised around three linked claims: theoretical clarity gives firm conviction, theoretical confidence gives steadfast faith, and theoretical consciousness gives political consciousness. It ends with a note on the author's own work in Fujian.

Lü contends that ideals rest on a rational acceptance of scientific theory, of historical laws and of national conditions. In Lü's account, Marxism has guided the Party through a century of ordeals, and studying Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is a required course for young cadres. Lü contrasts the delegates to the First Party Congress who abandoned the cause with those, such as Mao Zedong, who kept their faith. Lü also holds that the depth of one's grasp of Marxism determines political sensitivity and breadth of vision, and that Marxism should serve as a compass for new problems.

Lü calls for continuous, in-depth study of the Thought and for deeper work on tracing its origins, drawing on Xi Jinping's 17 and a half years in Fujian. The aim is stronger political, intellectual, theoretical and emotional identification with the Two Establishes. Read the original if you want an example of how Party theory cadres present ideological study as the basis of conviction.
quoteEn: Firmness of ideals and convictions comes from firmness in ideological theory.
quoteZh: 理想信念的坚定，来自思想理论的坚定。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
A formula from the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the Party's core and the guiding role of his Thought.

t: Making Party history study and education in universities regular and long-term
zh: 推进高校党史学习教育常态化长效化
paras: This short commentary, published on Guangming Net in 2022, asks how universities can turn Party history study and education into a regular, long-term practice. Han Yun argues that, following Xi Jinping's repeated requirements since the 18th Party Congress (2012), universities must consolidate the results of the Party history campaign, especially among young people.
The piece has two parts. The first sets out why such education matters; the second proposes practical paths for universities.

On value, Han claims that Party history education strengthens students' ideals and beliefs, helps them build a correct view of history and resist what the author calls erroneous social trends, and trains 'new-era people' who can serve as builders and successors of socialism. On practice, Han makes three proposals. First, build a systematic body of content, with top-level planning that presents the Party's theoretical exploration, revolutionary struggle and self-development, combining macro narrative with vivid detail, answering student concerns and adding recent achievements. Second, innovate teaching methods beyond lectures: themed talks on exemplary Party members such as Jiao Yulu, quizzes, role-play, visits to red heritage sites and new media. Third, guide and persuade rather than preach, letting students understand how knowledge developed, and linking past, present and future.

Han concludes that this approach should lead students to value present-day well-being, recognise what the article describes as the distinct advantages of socialism with Chinese characteristics through comparison with the West, and take up their responsibilities. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party history education in higher education is framed and what teaching methods are recommended.
quoteEn: Party history study and education has a powerful function of setting the record straight: it can expose, in academic terms, the nature of erroneous social trends and build students' ability to discern and resist them.
quoteZh: 党史学习教育具有强大的正本清源功能，既能从学理上揭露错误社会思潮的本质，培养和提升学生辨析和抵制错误社会思潮的能力

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism, developed since the reform era.
A nationwide campaign in 2021, the centenary year of the CPC, requiring Party members and students to study the Party's history.

t: Three dimensions for understanding "leading social revolution through the Party's self-reform"
zh: 三个维度理解“以党的自我革命引领社会革命”
paras: Published in Guangming Daily in September 2022, shortly before the 20th Party Congress, this commentary takes up Xi Jinping's call to "lead social revolution through the Party's self-reform". Li Xiaodong argues that the Communist Party of China's ability to carry out great self-reform is what has allowed it to lead great social revolution. The author presents the two as an organic unity, with self-reform as the driving force.

The piece is organised around three "dimensions". The first treats the principle as an inherent requirement for a Marxist party to fulfil its historic mission. The second treats it as valuable experience from the Party's revolution, construction and reform. The third presents it as the key to meeting changes in the world, in the times and in history. Throughout, Li draws on Xi's speeches, with citations from Engels and Lenin on internal struggle and on a party's attitude to its own mistakes.

In the first dimension, Li defines a Marxist party's self-reform as continuous self-purification, self-improvement, self-renewal and self-elevation. Li argues that the Party's historical height in self-reform determines the depth of social revolution, and that new revolutionary tasks in turn set new demands for self-reform. Old parties and dynasties, in this reading, failed because they lacked the courage to resolve their own serious problems. For the second dimension, Li traces the Gutian, Zunyi and Yan'an rectification episodes, the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978), and the campaign of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Li credits these with helping the Party escape the "historical cycle" of rise and fall. In the third dimension, Li stresses the unprecedented breadth, sharpness and difficulty of today's social revolution and the "four dangers" and "four tests" the Party still faces.

Li concludes that self-reform is never finished and that full and rigorous self-governance of the Party is "always on the road". Li calls on the Party to strengthen its mechanisms for self-reform, to guard against any loss of its advanced and pure character, and to raise cadres' capacity to carry out modernization. Li expresses confidence that the Party will keep winning victories on the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-building theory was presented to a general readership on the eve of the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: The historical height reached by the Party's self-reform determines the practical depth of the great social revolution.
quoteZh: 党的自我革命所达到的历史高度，决定着伟大社会革命的实践深度

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A Party-building policy emphasised since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It combines discipline, anti-corruption campaigns and internal supervision.
A concept stressed by Xi Jinping. It refers to the Party's continuous self-purification, self-improvement, self-renewal and self-elevation, so as to correct its own problems.

In the article, this covers both the overthrow of the old order and the ongoing work of building socialism. Here the term is applied to the current project of upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's path of socialist development since reform and opening up.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: The Party's distinctive political character and formidable political strength
zh: 党的鲜明政治品格和强大政治优势
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily in September 2022, takes up Xi Jinping's statement at a seminar for provincial and ministerial-level leading cadres that being guided by Marxist scientific theory is the Party's distinctive political character and formidable political strength. Wang Xinsheng reads the statement as explaining why the Party has kept its vanguard character and purity, and why it has won victory after victory.

The piece moves from the Party's history to the present. It first recalls the Party's century-long adherence to Marxism, then discusses how theory underpins political maturity, then turns to the way Marxism is applied in China, and ends with a call to keep to Marxism's guiding position.

Wang argues that Marxism gave the Party a scientific worldview and methodology, which in the author's account freed it from the self-interested limits of earlier political forces. This is said to have let it correct errors, keep the historical initiative and complete tasks no other Chinese political force could. Marxism, however, is treated as a guide to action rather than dogma: its effect depends on combining its basic principles with Chinese realities and fine traditional Chinese culture, which the author calls adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Wang presents Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as a new leap in this process and cites the past decade's achievements as proof.

Wang concludes that the guiding position of Marxism must never be shaken, since it is the foundation of the Party and the state and the source of confidence in meeting turbulence. The author calls on the whole Party to study the worldview, methodology, standpoint and method of Xi Jinping Thought. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary in 2022 framed Marxism as the Party's core political asset.
quoteEn: Theoretical maturity is the basis of political maturity, and political firmness stems from theoretical clarity.
quoteZh: 理论上的成熟是政治上成熟的基础，政治上的坚定源于理论上的清醒。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for combining Marxism's basic principles with China's specific conditions, culture and the demands of the current era. It extends the earlier idea of the 'sinification of Marxism'.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
The official name for China's path, system and theory since reform and opening up, which the Party presents as Marxism applied to Chinese conditions.

t: Consciously putting Communists' values into practice
zh: 自觉践行共产党人价值观
paras: Wang Peizhou, in a commentary originally published in Study Times, asks what values Chinese Communists should concretely follow today. The author argues that Communist values are both an old and a new subject: old because the Party's political nature fixes their basic orientation, new because the present era demands specific value norms.

The piece first distinguishes three layers: the lofty goal of communism, understood as the free and all-round development of every person; the core orientation of serving the people wholeheartedly; and concrete norms shaped by the times. It then cites Xi Jinping's statements from the 18th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection plenary session, the 19th Party Congress report and a Politburo study session.

Wang reads Xi's wording as shifting from "uphold" to "promote" to "promote and put into practice", which signals unity of knowing and doing. The trailing "etc." suggests the list will expand as full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and the Party's self-reform advance. Four norms are examined in turn: loyalty and honesty, fairness and decency, seeking truth from facts, and integrity and incorruptibility. Wang links each to a present problem: officials who are politically two-faced, distorted views of power, formalism and bureaucracy, and the intrusion of commodity-exchange logic into inner-Party life.

Wang concludes that these four norms are basic requirements of the Party's self-governance and self-reform, and that officials with greater power should hold greater reverence for it. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-press commentary presents the values expected of cadres and links them to Xi Jinping's formulations.
quoteEn: Communists' values are both an old subject and a new one.
quoteZh: 共产党人价值观既是一个老课题，又是一个新课题。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A policy line stressing strict discipline and anti-corruption work within the Communist Party, prominent since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
Official phrase for the Party's claimed capacity to correct its own faults and purify itself, emphasised under Xi Jinping.

t: Jiangxi: the birth and continuation of the Red statistics enterprise
zh: 江西：红色统计事业的发祥与发扬
authors: Theoretical Study Centre Group of the CPC Jiangxi Provincial Committee
paras: Marking the 70th anniversary of the founding of the PRC government's statistical agency, this commentary by the Jiangxi Provincial Party Committee's theoretical study group asks where Party-led statistics began and what lessons it holds today. The authors argue that the "Red statistics enterprise" originated and took root in Jiangxi during the Land Revolution period, and that its spirit should be carried forward in present-day statistical work.

The piece has three parts. The first traces the institutional history from the Jinggangshan base area to the Central Soviet Area. The second distils the "spiritual connotation" of Red statistics into five principles. The third describes how Jiangxi applies these principles in what the authors call high-quality development of statistics in the new era. It is written in the authoritative, programmatic style of a provincial Party document.

In the authors' account, a specialised statistical system took shape step by step. An investigation section was set up under the Party's Organisation Bureau from 1927. In 1931 the provisional central Soviet government in Ruijin placed statistical units in several ministries. In April 1933 a National Economy Department with its own Investigation and Statistics Bureau was created, with matching offices at provincial and county level. The authors present this as the prototype of the PRC's statistical organs. They treat Mao Zedong's Xunwu investigation as the source of its guiding ideas, "going deep, being practical, seeking truth". The five principles are Party leadership as the fundamental principle, the mass line as the core requirement, seeking truth from facts as the essential feature, rule by law and regulation as the safeguard, and efficiency with integrity as the hallmark. The authors illustrate the last with Mao's surveys done during military pauses and with the "knapsack government".

For the present, the authors report that Jiangxi acts on Xi Jinping's directives on statistics by upholding the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds. They describe a shift towards giving social statistics equal weight with economic statistics, a drive against statistical falsification, and a modernised survey system with data-sharing platforms. They also cite the Jiangxi Statistics Management Regulations, a "data responsibility system", and training of cadres at sites such as the Central Soviet Area investigation and statistics history museum. Read the original if you want an example of how a provincial Party body uses revolutionary-era history to frame current statistical governance and anti-falsification policy.
quoteEn: Adhering to seeking truth from facts is the essential feature of Red statistical work.
quoteZh: 坚持实事求是是红色统计工作的本质特征。

glossary.explanation: A label for the investigation and statistics work led by the Communist Party in the revolutionary base areas, especially the Central Soviet Area in the 1930s. Present-day official writing presents it as the root of the PRC's statistical system.
The main Communist-held base area in southern Jiangxi and western Fujian in the early 1930s. The Chinese Soviet Republic was proclaimed there in 1931, with Ruijin as its capital.
A Party working method associated with Mao Zedong: gathering the views of the people and returning them as policy ("from the masses, to the masses").
A principle of basing policy on actual conditions, promoted by Mao Zedong and later by Deng Xiaoping. It is treated as a core ideological line of the Party.
A formula adopted in 2021–22 that affirms Xi Jinping's position as core of the Party and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A political requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the Party Central Committee's authority and centralised leadership.
An official policy goal, prominent since 2017, that stresses the quality and efficiency of growth rather than speed alone.

t: The Two Establishes as the source of the strong cohesion and guiding power of ideological discourse in the new era
zh: “两个确立”是新时代意识形态话语强大凝聚力和引领力的力量之源
paras: Writing in 2022, Wu Xueqin takes up the call in the Party's third historical resolution, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021), to build a socialist ideology with strong cohesion and guiding power. The article argues that the Two Establishes (establishing Xi Jinping's core position and the guiding status of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era) are the source of that power. Wu presents them as grounded in theory, history, practice and institutions.

The article first defines cohesion and guiding power and proposes four tests of whether an ideology has them. It then devotes four sections to the theoretical, historical, practical and institutional strength of the Two Establishes. The historical section runs from the Zunyi Meeting through the Deng Xiaoping era to the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

On theory, Wu answers critics at home and abroad who equate establishing a leader's authority with personal despotism or a personality cult. The author draws on Marxist accounts of the relation between outstanding individuals and the masses, and of social being and social consciousness, to argue that a leader's authority arises from historical conditions and cannot be reduced to worship. Wu adds that the relationship between the leading core and the guiding ideology is dialectical, as with Marx, Lenin, Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping. On history, Wu holds that the Party gained cohesion each time it established a core and a guiding thought, and that each period produced its own ideological discourse: revolution, construction, reform and now rejuvenation. On institutions, Wu contrasts China's merit-based cadre selection and intra-Party democracy with Western electoral democracy, which the author describes as money-driven. Wu also cites Party regulations that embed the Two Establishes in the system of Party leadership.

Wu concludes that the Two Establishes strengthen the Party's leadership over ideological work, give the whole Party and people a firmer backbone, improve safeguards against ideological risk in new media, and consolidate Party unity. Wu says they also help China answer Western discursive dominance and strengthen national identity. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how Party theorists justify the Two Establishes and rebut the charge of personality cult, or if you want to see how ideology, history and Party-building are linked in this literature.
quoteEn: Establishing the Party's leading core and guiding thought arises from practical need and is determined by the real social conditions in which people live, so great figures too must be assessed within objective social and historical conditions, neither deified and worshipped nor wantonly vilified.
quoteZh: 确立党的领导核心和指导思想正是由于现实的需要，是由生活其中的现实社会条件所决定的，因而对伟大人物的评价也要将其置于客观社会历史条件中，既不神话膜拜也不肆意诋毁。

glossary.explanation: A formulation from the Party's 2021 third historical resolution. It affirms Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party, and the guiding status of Xi Jinping Thought.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and the state constitution in 2018.

t: Advancing as one the efforts to make officials dare not, be unable to and not want to be corrupt
zh: 一体推进不敢腐不能腐不想腐
paras: This short commentary, originally published in the People's Daily in September 2022, takes up the Party's anti-corruption approach of making officials dare not, be unable to and not want to be corrupt. Song Wei argues that advancing these three aims as one is an important experience of the new era. In the author's account it has become the basic anti-corruption policy and a key strategy of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

The piece begins from Xi Jinping's recent speech to a seminar for provincial and ministerial-level leading cadres, which reviewed the previous five years. Song then explains the logic of the three aims, describes how enforcement and institution-building have been carried out, and closes by linking the campaign to the Party's long-term position.

Song contends that corruption results from long-accumulated factors, personal, environmental and institutional, so no single measure can cure it. Not daring to be corrupt is the precondition and rests on punishment and deterrence. Being unable is the key and rests on institutional constraint. Not wanting to is the foundation and rests on education. The three are an organic whole, not three stages, and must work together. The author describes a policy of "no forbidden zones, full coverage, zero tolerance" and the pursuit of "tigers", "flies" and "foxes", alongside oversight reform and ideological education. Song also presents learning from cases, reforming and governing on the basis of cases as a working method that reduces existing corruption and curbs new cases.

Song concludes that the anti-corruption struggle is a protracted battle of the Party's self-reform. The author holds that the Party must win it to escape the historical cycle of rise and fall and keep the people's trust. Song calls for greater ability to advance the three aims together. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line statement of the rationale behind the Party's anti-corruption method.
quoteEn: The three are not a division into three stages, nor a severing into three links, but an organic whole.
quoteZh: 三者不是三个阶段的划分，也不是三个环节的割裂，而是有机的整体。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A Party-building policy promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering discipline, anti-corruption and organisational rules for Party members.
An official formulation describing the Party's efforts to correct its own problems through internal discipline and rectification.

glossary.pinyin: bù gǎn fǔ, bù néng fǔ, bù xiǎng fǔ
glossary.en: dare not, be unable to and not want to be corrupt
glossary.literal: not dare to be corrupt, not able to be corrupt, not want to be corrupt
glossary.explanation: The official three-part anti-corruption formula combining deterrence by punishment, institutional constraint and ideological education.

t: Historical materialism and the historical summing-up of the Communist Party of China's century of struggle
zh: 唯物史观与中国共产党百年奋斗的历史总结
source: Journal of Wuhan University (Philosophy and Social Sciences Edition), 2022 no. 5
paras: Li Weiwu asks how the Party's 2021 Resolution on the major achievements and historical experience of the Party's centennial struggle, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee, uses historical materialism to sum up the Party's history. Writing in 2022, the author argues that the Resolution is a model of researching and writing Party history on a historical-materialist basis, and that it works as a "mirror of history" showing where the Party has come from and where it is heading, and why this course is historically reasonable.

The article rests on the long Chinese tradition of drawing lessons from history and on Mao Zedong's Yan'an-era call to study the Party's own history. It organises the Resolution's approach under five headings: its guiding principle (a correct view of Party history), its method (seeking truth from facts), its logic (examining the process and giving an overall assessment), its focal point (establishing the new era), and the lines of thought that follow for Party-history writing. Li draws on Feng Youlan's distinction between history as it happened and history as written, on Cai Hesen's early Party-history writings, and on Mao's and Xi Jinping's statements.

Li's central claim is that correct Party history requires combining historical objectivity with the discovery of historical regularity. Merely listing facts, the author says, blurs the distinction between essence and surface, mainstream and tributary, and invites historical nihilism. The Resolution's division of the century into four periods and its account of three leaps in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context are presented as expressions of this method, as are its five-fold historical significance and ten lessons. Li also argues that the weight given to the new era under Xi Jinping rests on an objective change in the principal contradiction in society and in the Party's tasks. In this account, the Two Establishes follow from the historical reading.

Li concludes that studying Party history from a historical-materialist standpoint means holding together three linked elements: historical objectivity, historical regularity and historical initiative, the last being the conscious activity of people acting within objective laws. Li treats the Resolution as having unified these elements, and as therefore giving the Party's "yesterday, today and tomorrow" a coherent reading. Read the original if you want a detailed account of how the official Party-history narrative is justified methodologically, or of how the 2021 Resolution is read within Chinese Marxist philosophy.
quoteEn: In researching and writing Party history, one must attend not only to the "facts" of Party history but also to discover and grasp the "truth" within those facts; one must uphold historical objectivity and also strive to reveal historical regularity from within it.
quoteZh: 在党史研究和书写中，不仅要重视党史上的“实事”，而且还要从“实事”中发现和把握党史中的“是”；不仅要坚持历史客观性，而且要力求从历史客观性中揭示历史规律性。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the 2021 Resolution affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and of the whole Party, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought. It has since become a standard reference point in Party documents.

A principle associated with Mao Zedong and later Deng Xiaoping, taken as the core of the Party's ideological line. Li reads it as combining attention to facts with the search for their underlying regularities.
In Party usage, a label for readings of history that stress failures, errors or detours in a way that is said to deny the mainstream of the Party's or socialism's historical course.

glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context
glossary.explanation: The official idea that Marxism must be combined with China's specific realities and culture. The Resolution identifies three major "leaps" in this process: Mao Zedong Thought, socialism with Chinese characteristics theory, and Xi Jinping Thought.

t: Accurately grasping the logic and path of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party in the new era
zh: 准确把握新时代全面从严治党逻辑路径
paras: This commentary, published in Economic Daily in September 2022, asks how the Party's strategic policy of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party should be understood in the new era. Ni Bangwen takes as a starting point the 2021 Sixth Plenum resolution on the Party's century of struggle. The author argues that the policy has a clear logic, with a starting point, a destination and a point of leverage, all tied to the Party's founding mission of seeking happiness for the people and rejuvenation for the nation.

The piece is built in three sections. The first, "everything for the people, everything relying on the people", deals with the Party's class basis and with democracy. The second concerns ensuring that the Party remains the strong leadership core, and the third concerns persisting in self-reform. Ni draws on Mao Zedong and Xi Jinping, and on the Marxist idea that a proletarian party has no interests separate from those of the proletariat as a whole.

Ni's central move is to link Party discipline to popular legitimacy. The Party, in this account, has no special interests of its own, so it can examine its own faults honestly. Whole-process people's democracy, with its rights to information, participation, expression and supervision, is said to let the people supervise power and to keep it in a "cage" of institutions. The author then ties the Party's leadership to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and to the risks the Party faces, listing four tests (holding power, reform and opening up, the market economy, the external environment) and four dangers (slackness, insufficient capacity, detachment from the masses, corruption). Self-reform is presented as three paired efforts: ideological education alongside rule-based governance, a healthy political culture and ecology, and campaigns against misconduct together with anti-corruption work.

Ni concludes that full and rigorous self-governance of the Party must cover every area and stage and be sustained, so that the Party does not change in character. Specific proposals include continued centralised study campaigns, making the Party constitution the basic reference, upholding democratic centralism and the Two Upholds, strictly enforcing the eight-point regulations, and following a "zero tolerance" approach to corruption. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Party-building and anti-corruption policy were justified in the run-up to the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Boldness in self-reform is the distinguishing mark that sets the Communist Party of China apart from other political parties.
quoteZh: 勇于自我革命是中国共产党区别于其他政党的显著标志。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A strategic policy associated with Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering Party discipline, conduct and anti-corruption work.
A concept promoted since the 2010s, describing the Party's model of democracy as covering election, consultation, decision-making, management and supervision.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term national goal, often described as the Party's central mission.

The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and its centralised, unified leadership.
The policy launched in 1978 of economic reform and opening to the outside world.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Firmly establishing a correct view of Party history
zh: 牢固树立正确党史观
paras: Writing in 2022, as the Party marked its first centenary, Wang Guang argues that the study of Party history depends on the right view of history. In the author's account, a correct view of Party history, grounded in historical materialism, determines the attitude and method of historical research and whether lessons can be drawn from it. The commentary rests heavily on Xi Jinping's statements and on the communiqué of the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021).

The piece is a short essay built around three claims about why a correct view of Party history is needed. It is needed for understanding the Party's hundred years of struggle, for uncovering historical laws that guide the Party and state, and for resisting historical nihilism. Wang closes with a note on the present task, at the junction of the "two centenary goals".

On the first point, Wang sketches modern Chinese history as a passage from national humiliation under feudal rule and foreign aggression, through failed earlier attempts at salvation, to success under the Party's leadership. The author attributes that success to combining Marxism with Chinese realities and traditional culture and to treating the people as creators of history. On the second, Wang treats recognition of historical laws as the dividing line between historical materialism and idealism, and calls the Party's history one of exploring and applying such laws. Wang presents Xi Jinping's ideas as a new advance in understanding the laws of Communist Party governance, socialist construction and human social development. On the third, Wang lists forms of historical nihilism: exaggerating errors, linking Party history to current problems, and trivialising it with rumour and unofficial accounts. The author cites Xi's explanation of the Soviet collapse as the cost of totally negating Soviet and Soviet Party history.

Wang reports that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the correct view has brought clarification of Party history and curbed nihilism, especially online. The author adds that more research and more popular forms of communication are still needed so that the official account becomes a consensus across the Party and society. Wang calls on readers to take Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as guidance and to draw spiritual strength for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation from history. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars in 2022 framed the official view of Party history and the campaign against historical nihilism.
quoteEn: The view of history one holds determines the understanding of history one arrives at.
quoteZh: 有什么样的历史观，就会有什么样的历史认知。

glossary.explanation: In official Chinese usage, a label for interpretations that stress errors or negate the Party's and socialism's history. The Party treats it as an ideological threat.

glossary.en: a correct view of Party history
glossary.explanation: A phrase Xi Jinping promoted during the 2021 Party history study campaign. It means interpreting Party history through historical materialism and the Party's official assessments.
Marx's theory that material conditions and social relations shape historical development. Chinese official texts present it as the basic method for understanding history.
Official goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021 and a modern socialist country by the People's Republic's centenary in 2049.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal, closely associated with Xi Jinping, of restoring China's national strength and international standing.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and the state constitution in 2018.

t: Cultivating the Communist's "philosophy of the mind"
zh: 修炼共产党人的“心学”
paras: Zhong Jun's commentary takes up Xi Jinping's call to "cultivate the Communist's 'xinxue'" (literally 'learning of the mind', a term borrowed from Ming-dynasty Neo-Confucian thought). It reads the phrase as a demand that Party members, especially leading cadres, firm up their ideals and convictions and strengthen Party spirit. Zhong's thesis is that this inner cultivation rests on three lifelong tasks: steadfast ideals and convictions, remembering the original aspiration and founding mission, and the spirit of self-reform.

Written in 2022, the piece is organised around these three tasks and draws heavily on Xi's speeches, notably his remarks at the opening of the Central Party School's training courses for young and middle-aged cadres in autumn 2021 and spring 2022. It also cites Lenin on a serious party's open admission of errors, Xi's 2020 visit to Hunan and the 'half a quilt' story, and the lessons Xi draws from the collapse of the Soviet Union.

On ideals, Zhong argues that belief works as a 'master switch'. In the author's account, the loss of conviction explains why the Soviet party fell without resistance, while Chinese Communists' conviction rests on a rational understanding of Marxism and historical laws, not on emotion. Zhong calls for reading Marxist classics closely and for theoretical grounding. On the original aspiration, the author says that the Party's purity does not persist naturally and that members need regular ideological check-ups. Zhong also stresses that a correct view of performance means judging achievements by the people's real experience. On self-reform, Zhong holds that it distinguishes the Party from other parties. Full and rigorous self-governance of the Party has achieved results since the 18th Party Congress (2012), but Zhong still points to cadres who are complacent, evade criticism or breach discipline and the central eight-point regulations.

Zhong concludes that the 'thief in the heart' is harder to defeat than external enemies, so cadres must guard their inner selves, resist greed and keep to Party discipline from small matters upward. The piece offers a compact guide to how Party theorists present moral and ideological self-cultivation as part of Party building. Read the original if you want to see how a provincial academy head restates Xi Jinping's language on belief, discipline and cadre self-discipline in a Party-building journal.
quoteEn: Establishing ideals and convictions is not a momentary impulse or naive sentiment but a rational choice, supported by a deep theoretical faith.
quoteZh: 理想信念的确立，不是一时的冲动和朴素的感情，而是一种理性的选择，有深厚的理论信仰作支撑。

glossary.explanation: A school of Neo-Confucian thought associated with Wang Yangming that stresses moral cultivation of the mind. Xi Jinping uses the phrase 'Communist's xinxue' for inner cultivation of belief and Party spirit.
A Party formulation, stressed in the 2019 campaign, that the Party's aim is to seek happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name of the Party's discipline and anti-corruption drive promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
Official term for the Party's claimed capacity to correct its own errors and purge corruption, presented as the way to escape the 'historical cycle' of dynastic rise and fall.
Rules adopted in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism among Party officials.

t: Upholding and strengthening the Party's centralised and unified leadership over economic work
zh: 坚持和加强党对经济工作的集中统一领导
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscript in 2022, Ding Xiaoqin takes up why and how the Communist Party of China should uphold and strengthen its centralised and unified leadership over economic work. Ding presents this as an important component of Xi Jinping's economic thought and as a necessary consequence of the Party's overall leadership. The central claim is that the authority of the Party Central Committee is the highest principle of Party leadership and the key guarantee that economic work stays on the right course.

The article has four parts. It first places economic leadership within the principle of the Party's overall leadership, drawing on the 2021 Resolution on the Party's century of struggle and on Xi Jinping's statements. It then discusses the role of the Central Committee, followed by the institutions through which leadership is exercised at the central, local and state-owned enterprise levels. The last part sets out what is needed to raise the Party's capacity to lead economic work.

Ding argues that the Central Committee sets direction, formulates strategy and policy, and bears overall responsibility for economic work. The article traces how the annual Central Economic Work Conferences from 2018 to 2021 increasingly named centralised and unified leadership as a core lesson, and in 2021 as the first priority. In Ding's account, this authority allows the concentration of resources on major undertakings and strengthens the reaction of the superstructure on the economic base. Institutionally, Ding points to the 2018 conversion of the leading small groups on finance and on deepening reform into commissions, the Central Financial and Economic Affairs Commission's quarterly reviews, local Party committees' collective decisions, and Party committees in state-owned enterprises that discuss major matters before boards and managers decide.

Ding proposes three ways to raise the Party's capacity. Leaders should acquire professional expertise through study of Marxist political economy, fieldwork, use of think tanks and better selection and training of cadres. They should also govern the economy by law, and apply the method of seeking progress while maintaining stability, with stability focused on growth, employment, prices and financial risk, and progress on structural adjustment and reform. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Party leadership over the economy is justified and institutionalised in the Xi Jinping era.
quoteEn: Only when the Party Central Committee has authority can the whole Party be firmly united, and in turn the people of all ethnic groups be closely bound together, forming an irresistible force of one heart and mind.
quoteZh: 只有党中央有权威，才能把全党牢固凝聚起来，进而把全国各族紧密团结起来，形成万众一心，无坚不摧的磅礴力量。

glossary.explanation: A Party principle that the Central Committee holds final authority over major decisions, with the whole Party and state apparatus following its direction. It is emphasised in Xi Jinping-era statements on Party leadership.
Annual closed-door meetings, usually in December, where the Party and government leadership review the year's economy and set priorities for the next.
The general keynote of Chinese economic policy since the early 2010s, balancing stable macroeconomic conditions with reform and structural change.

glossary.en: Central Financial and Economic Affairs Commission
glossary.explanation: A Party body set up in 2018 from the earlier leading small group. It coordinates and decides major economic and financial policy at the top level.

t: On ideological security in the new era
zh: 论新时代意识形态安全
source: Studies on Marxism (马克思主义研究), 2022 no. 6
paras: Writing in Studies on Marxism in 2022, Tang Aijun asks how China should conceive and safeguard ideological security amid what official discourse calls profound changes unseen in a century and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The article argues that the task requires a new concept, a "holistic view of ideological security" derived from the holistic view of national security, and that ideological struggle today is above all a competition for identification, or "winning hearts and minds".

The article has four parts. It first defines ideological security and sets out the holistic view, tracing earlier Party strategic thinking from Mao Zedong to Hu Jintao. It then assesses the situation since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and the main risks. A third part analyses the means of ideological contest, and a fourth proposes an ideological security system at the international and domestic levels.

Tang defines ideological security as a state in which the mainstream ideology is relatively free of danger and external or internal threat, together with the capacity to sustain that state. Because ideology is both political and cultural, the author places it in the categories of both political security and cultural security. The holistic view is said to be comprehensive (a "big security" covering culture, values and online opinion), systematic and sustainable. Tang identifies four challenges: diverse social trends (the "6+1", including constitutional democracy, universal values and historical nihilism), market profit-seeking, infiltration and containment by hostile Western forces, and new media and technology. Tang says these contests are fought through three ideological functions: value orientation, social control and integration, and political legitimacy.

Tang calls for a more actively combative international system: strategic confidence, stronger international communication, institutional discourse power, exposing the double standards behind "universal values", and confronting issues the West attacks. Domestically, the author proposes a system built on "hearts and minds", with an early-warning view that popular support equals security, and "six identifications": political, ideological, value, historical, practical and emotional. Read the original if you want a detailed account of how a Party School scholar frames ideological security as a competition for identification and what institutional measures follow.
quoteEn: Today's ideological struggle is mainly a competition for identification, and this competition mainly takes the form of contests between different ideologies over the functions of value orientation, social control and integration, and political legitimation.
quoteZh: 当前意识形态斗争主要是一种认同竞争，而认同竞争主要表现为不同意识形态在价值导向、社会控制与整合、政治合法化等功能维度上的较量。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping first put forward on 15 April 2014 at the first meeting of the Central National Security Commission. It treats security as covering many fields, including politics, culture and ideology, and as requiring coordinated management.

The author's own formulation, derived from the holistic view of national security. It treats ideological security as a broad, systemic and long-term matter that combines the state of security with the capacity to maintain it.
The author's term for the contest between mainstream and non-mainstream ideologies to win people's acceptance and allegiance. It is described as the essence of "winning hearts and minds".
The ability of a state to shape international institutions and global governance by setting agendas, making rules and spreading institutional ideas. The term appears in Party documents from 2015.
In Chinese official discourse the term usually refers to Western-style democracy, freedom and human rights promoted as universal. The article treats it as a vehicle of ideological infiltration.

t: Upholding the Party's leadership over ideological work in the new era: basis, value and paths of realisation
zh: 新时代坚持党对意识形态工作的领导权：基本依据、价值意蕴和实现路径
source: Ideological and Political Education Research (思想教育研究), 2022 no. 7
paras: Xiao Guangwen and Li Xiaotong take up the call in the historical resolution of the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021) to "firmly grasp the leadership over ideological work" and build a socialist ideology with strong cohesion and guiding power. They argue that upholding the Party's leadership over ideological work in the new era rests on historical, theoretical and practical grounds. In their account it serves the Party's ruling base, mainstream values, political security and spiritual unity, and it can be realised through four concrete paths.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the basis for the leadership: the Party's century of ideological work, from the 1921 First Congress through Yan'an, the post-1949 period, the Cultural Revolution, reform and opening up, and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012); the Marxist theory of ideology; and the demands of the "two overall situations". The second discusses its value in four respects. The third proposes ways to put it into practice.

On theory, the authors draw on Marx and Engels on the ruling ideas of an age, Lenin's doctrine of "inculcation" and "scientific ideology", and Gramsci's concept of ideological hegemony. They read these as showing that a proletarian party must hold ideological leadership to prevent the dissolution of mainstream ideology and to defend its political legitimacy. On value, they hold that such leadership unites Party spirit and the people's character, fosters the core socialist values, and counters what they call erroneous trends of thought promoted from the West, including neoliberalism, "universal values" and historical nihilism. They also say it strengthens discursive power, which they break down into the rights to pose questions, to judge, to interpret and to criticise.

For realisation, the authors propose four paths. The first is to be guided by Xi Jinping's statements on ideological leadership, including building Chinese philosophy and social sciences and governing online ideology.
