The second is to enforce the primary responsibility of Party committees under the 2015 and 2016 responsibility-system measures. The third is to raise the ideological capacity and fighting spirit of Party members and cadres. The fourth is to improve institutions, namely the fundamental system of Marxism's guiding role, Party management of ideology, and supervision, assessment and accountability. They conclude that only a sound institutional system and stronger execution can secure comprehensive Party leadership in this field. Read the original if you want a representative account of how Party-affiliated scholars justify and operationalise ideological leadership in the Xi Jinping era.
quoteEn: Upholding the Party's leadership over ideological work is the fundamental guarantee of the Party's ideological work in the new era.
quoteZh: 坚持党对意识形态工作的领导权是新时代党的意识形态工作的根本保证。

glossary.explanation: The Party's authority to direct propaganda, theory, education, culture and media. The Party has stressed it since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and reaffirmed it in the 2021 historical resolution.
Xi Jinping's formula for the strategic context of the new era: the overall strategy of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and the world's "great changes unseen in a century".
A set of 24 characters in 12 values, promoted officially since the 18th Party Congress (2012), including prosperity, democracy, freedom, equality, patriotism and integrity.
The capacity to set agendas, interpret events and have one's narrative accepted. Chinese scholars use it for competition over meaning and values at home and abroad.

t: The contemporary value and transmission of the spiritual genealogy of Chinese Communists
zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系的时代价值与传承路径
paras: This commentary in Guangming Daily (September 2022) asks why the spiritual genealogy of Chinese Communists matters now and how it should be passed on. Xu and Peng argue that this genealogy, rooted in the great founding spirit of the Party, is a lasting resource for the new journey towards the second centenary goal. They hold that it supports socialism with Chinese characteristics, full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, and the Party's original aspiration and mission.

The article first traces how the genealogy took shape over a century. It lists clusters of spirits from each period: the Jinggangshan, Long March and Yan'an spirits in the revolutionary years; the "Two Bombs, One Satellite" and Lei Feng spirits in socialist construction; and the special economic zone and flood-fighting spirits in reform and opening up. For the new era it names poverty alleviation, anti-epidemic, lunar exploration and Beidou spirits. It then sets out four contemporary values and four ways of transmitting the genealogy.

On value, the authors present the genealogy as a spiritual support for opening new prospects, an ideological weapon for Party building, and a source of strength for the Party's mission. They add that it combines Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture and carries wider appeal. On transmission, they call for more rigorous scholarly research and interpretation, including rebutting views that distort Party history. They also call for effective publicity using new media, coordinated protection and use of "red resources" such as sites and museums, and mass cultural activities that link the genealogy to core socialist values.

Xu and Peng conclude that the genealogy should be built into the Party's "blood and genes" and supply spiritual momentum for building a modern socialist country. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-school scholars frame the official "spiritual genealogy" and its practical dissemination.
quoteEn: The spiritual genealogy of Chinese Communists is the spiritual expression of their original aspiration and mission.
quoteZh: 中国共产党人精神谱系是中国共产党人初心和使命的精神表达

glossary.zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系
glossary.explanation: An official term for the series of named "spirits" (such as the Long March spirit) said to have arisen in the Party's history. It was formally presented in 2021 around the Party's centenary, with the founding spirit as its source.
A formulation announced by Xi Jinping in 2021: upholding truth and ideals, staying true to the original aspiration and mission, fearless struggle, and loyalty to the Party and the people.
A Party slogan summarising its purpose as seeking happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's campaign, intensified since 2012, to tighten discipline and internal management.
Sites, relics, memorials and stories linked to the Communist revolution, used for Party education and tourism.

t: The contest over discursive power between the Guomindang and the Communist Party in the New Democratic Revolution period
st: A reading from the field of philosophy and social sciences
zh: 新民主主义革命时期国共两党的话语权博弈
zhSub: 以哲学社会科学领域为视角的解读
paras: Wang Dong asks how the Guomindang (Kuomintang) and the Communist Party contended for discursive power in philosophy and the social sciences between the 1920s and 1940s. The article argues that, besides its military campaigns, the Guomindang waged a reactionary 'cultural encirclement' to build a discourse guided by the Three People's Principles. In Wang's account, the Party met it with effective counter-measures that weakened that campaign, raised the influence of Marxist philosophy and social science, and strengthened popular identification with the revolution.

Wang says existing scholarship on discursive power is mostly present-oriented and has not examined this period systematically. Drawing on archival and published historical sources, the article looks at three arenas: the publication and distribution of books and periodicals, academic controversy (using the debate on the nature of Chinese society as the case), and attitudes towards traditional culture. It closes by linking the history to present-day ideological work.

On publishing, Wang documents Guomindang censorship laws and standards, the persecution of writers, raids on bookshops and postal inspection. The Party answered with disguised titles, nominal bookshops, use of legal periodicals and publishers, and a cultural united front calling for academic freedom. In the debate on Chinese society, Wang argues that Tao Xisheng's 'New Life' group and the Reorganization faction denied that China was semi-colonial and semi-feudal in order to undercut the Party's revolutionary discourse. Communist writers such as Pan Dongzhou, Wu Liangping and Jian Bozan countered with economic analysis, which the article says confirmed the scientific character of Marxism. On tradition, Wang describes the Guomindang drawing on Confucian ethics, the New Life Movement and Chiang Kai-shek's 'philosophy of vigorous action' to bolster authoritarian rule. The Party, in Wang's reading, criticised this revivalism through the New Enlightenment movement while practising sublation of tradition, which also advanced the adaptation of Marxism to Chinese conditions.

Wang concludes that Marxist philosophy and social science rose from an emerging academic discourse to the mainstream, contributing to the revolution's victory. Today, Wang notes, historical nihilism, neoliberalism and democratic socialism challenge socialist ideology. The article calls on the Party to carry forward its revolutionary-era traditions and consolidate Marxism's discursive power in these fields in the new era, in support of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a source-rich, Party-historiographical account of Guomindang censorship and Communist counter-strategies in the Republican-era publishing and intellectual world.
quoteEn: The Communist Party's attitude of sublation towards traditional culture both repelled the revivalist undercurrent of Japanese imperialism and the Guomindang, and let its revolutionary theory draw nourishment from fine traditional culture, while speeding up the Sinicization of Marxist philosophical and social-scientific discourse and effectively raising its own discursive power.
quoteZh: 中国共产党对传统文化的扬弃态度，既反击了日本帝国主义以及国民党的复古逆流，又使自身革命理论从优秀传统文化中汲取养分，同时加快了马克思主义哲学社会科学话语中国化的步伐，有效提升了自身话语权。

glossary.explanation: The capacity to shape the dominant ideas, terms and narratives in a field. In Chinese ideological discussion it is closely tied to control over ideology.
A Communist-side term for the Guomindang's suppression of left-wing publications and writers in the 1930s, modelled on the 'encirclement campaigns' against the Red Army.
Sun Yat-sen's doctrine of nationalism, democracy (people's rights) and people's livelihood, the official ideology of the Guomindang.
A mid-1930s intellectual movement led by Communist-aligned intellectuals, which continued the May Fourth spirit of 'science and democracy' and opposed cultural revivalism.
The Hegelian-Marxist idea of simultaneously negating and preserving, used here for a critical approach that keeps the valuable parts of traditional culture.

keywords: debate on the nature of Chinese society

t: Strengthening education for Party members and cadres on the essential nature of money
zh: 加强对党员干部金钱本质教育
paras: This short commentary, first published in Study Times (Xuexi Shibao) in 2022, asks how to make Party members and cadres genuinely unwilling to be corrupt. Xu Baojian argues that, besides ideals-and-convictions education and education in discipline and the legal system, education about the essential nature of money is an overlooked but necessary addition.

The piece begins from the framework of making officials unwilling, unable and afraid to be corrupt, in which Xu treats unwillingness as fundamental. It then cites recent prosecutions of senior officials accused of taking bribes of hundreds of millions of yuan, and the case of Lai Xiaomin, who kept more than 200 million yuan in cash in a flat.

Xu's central claim is that money is by origin a tool of exchange whose value lies in use and circulation, so hoarded cash is merely a number or a pile of waste paper. Officials who amass it, in Xu's reading, end up as custodians of property that must finally be returned to the people or the state. People load money with symbolic meanings and overlook its essence, which Xu links to Marx's critique of money fetishism and the alienation of people by things. The author compares excessive greed to Jia Rui and the mirror in Dream of the Red Chamber.

Xu concludes that education should dispel illusions about money and teach that it is for sharing, not monopolising. Linking this to the Communist goal of common prosperity, Xu calls on cadres to be masters of money rather than its slaves and to use it for the people's benefit. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party press commentary frames anti-corruption education in moral and Marxist terms.
quoteEn: Strengthening education on the essential nature of money for Party members and cadres means breaking the myths and illusions about money, and recognising that everything attached to the essence of money is untrue and illusory.
quoteZh: 加强对党员干部金钱本质教育就是要打破对金钱的迷思和幻象，认清一切附着在金钱本质之上的东西都是不真实的、都是虚幻的。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal in Chinese Party discourse, stressed again under Xi Jinping, of wealth shared by all rather than concentrated in a few.

glossary.pinyin: bù gǎn fǔ, bù néng fǔ, bù xiǎng fǔ
glossary.en: unwilling, unable and afraid to be corrupt
glossary.literal: dare not be corrupt, cannot be corrupt, do not want to be corrupt
glossary.explanation: The Party's three-part anti-corruption approach combining deterrence, institutional constraints and ideological education. Official texts call the three 'mutually dependent and mutually reinforcing'.

t: The fundamental guidelines for the Party's youth work
st: A study of Xi Jinping's "On the Party's Youth Work"
zh: 党的青年工作的根本遵循
paras: This study essay, first published in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) and posted in September 2022, reads Xi Jinping's collection On the Party's Youth Work as the basic guide for youth work in the new era. Liu argues that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Central Committee with Xi at its core has raised the Party's understanding of how youth work operates. In Liu's account, the book says what youth work is, why it matters and how to do it.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why youth work bears on the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, the continuity of the Party's cause and the international outlook of Chinese youth. The second turns to the book's answers to the major questions of the new era, the path to follow and the theme of the youth movement. The third looks at the importance of youth work and what it requires of the Communist Youth League. Liu relies throughout on quotations from Xi's speeches and talks.

Liu's central claim is that youth work is a strategic task and not a sectoral one. The article presents Xi's formulations: youth work is "extremely important" and "bears on the future and destiny of the Party and the country", and the Party must represent, win over and rely on young people. Liu reports the guiding questions as what kind of young people to cultivate, how to cultivate them, and what kind of Youth League to build and how. The answer is the path of mass organizations with Chinese characteristics, under unified Party leadership. The Youth League's fundamental task is to train socialist builders and successors, its political responsibility is to consolidate and expand the Party's support among young people, and its main line of work is to focus on the Party's central tasks and serve the overall interest. Liu also lists the demands for strict self-governance of the League and for staying close to young people. The League is to avoid becoming bureaucratic, administrative, aristocratic or entertainment-oriented, and its cadres are to be "friends of the young, not officials".

Liu concludes that the book offers a rich body of ideas and working methods on the theoretical and practical questions of youth work. The author calls for careful study and thorough implementation, so that young people can be united, organized and mobilized for the second centenary goal and the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise, Party-school view of how Xi's youth-work ideas are organized and presented for study within the Communist Youth League system.
quoteEn: On the Party's Youth Work is full of General Secretary Xi Jinping's deep concern and earnest hopes for young people of the new era, and it gives profound answers to the major theoretical and practical questions of what the Party's youth work is, why it matters and how to carry it out.
quoteZh: 《论党的青年工作》饱含着习近平总书记对新时代青年的深切关怀和殷切期望，深刻回答了新时代党的青年工作是什么、为什么、怎么办等重大理论和实践问题

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, popularised under Xi Jinping as the Chinese Dream, of restoring China's national strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.
A slogan Xi Jinping introduced in 2012 and equated with the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
The Party's mass organization for young people, roughly ages 14 to 28, which serves as a feeder to Party membership.
Work with Party-led mass organizations such as the Youth League, trade unions and women's federations, which link the Party to specific social groups.
The goal of building China into a great modern socialist country by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic.

t: Forging a long-ruling Marxist party through full and rigorous self-governance and self-reform
zh: 在全面从严治党与自我革命中锻造长期执政的马克思主义政党
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), posted 2022-09-01
paras: Liu Honglin takes up a question that the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021) placed among the core propositions of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era: what kind of long-ruling Marxist party should be built, and how. Liu argues that the question can only be understood through the practical, theoretical and institutional innovations in Party governance since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and through Xi Jinping's related speeches. The article's thesis is that full and rigorous self-governance of the Party is the effective route to the Party's self-reform, which Liu presents as the way to escape the historical cycle of rise and fall.

Liu organises the argument around six key terms: the Party's overall leadership, long-term rule, full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, supervision and restraint of power, self-reform, and escaping the historical cycle. These are handled in three sections. The first defines the long-ruling Marxist party and its relation to Party leadership. The second examines Xi's judgement that self-reform is the "second answer" to the historical cycle. The third links self-reform to full and rigorous self-governance. Liu draws on comparisons with the Soviet Communist Party, Mexico's Institutional Revolutionary Party and other long-serving parties.

In the first section Liu distinguishes the Chinese Communist Party from Western parties by six features: guiding ideology, nature, purpose, founding mission, essence of rule and standards of work. Liu holds that upholding overall leadership is the basic political precondition for long-term rule, and that this does not mean the planned-economy practice of the Party managing everything. In the second section, Liu reads Mao Zedong's 1945 Yan'an answer (supervision of government by the people) and Xi's answer (self-reform) as continuity and development. The "blade" moves from the government to the ruling Party itself, and the target widens from power corruption to power corruption plus political corruption. Liu treats political corruption as systemic and especially dangerous to a ruling party.

Liu concludes that the two are mutually reinforcing: self-reform advances through full and rigorous self-governance, and the political awareness behind self-reform sustains it. Liu credits the decade since 2012 with turning Party governance from lax to strict and with an overwhelming victory in the anti-corruption struggle. Liu calls for continued strictness, strengthened Party-building, the Two Upholds, a cadre corps willing to reform itself and a more complete system of intra-Party regulations. Read the original if you want a representative account of how Party scholars link long-term rule, self-reform and Party discipline within Xi-era theory.
quoteEn: Full and rigorous self-governance of the Party is the Party's self-reform in the new era, and an effective route for self-purification under long-term rule and for escaping the historical cycle.
quoteZh: 全面从严治党就是新时代党的自我革命，就是一条党长期执政条件下实现自我净化、跳出历史周期率的有效途径

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: A Party-building policy since the 18th Party Congress (2012) that stresses strict discipline, anti-corruption work and intra-Party regulation across all aspects of Party life.
Xi Jinping's term for the Party correcting its own problems through its own efforts. The official English rendering is the Party's self-reform.

glossary.en: historical cycle of rise and fall
glossary.explanation: The idea, associated with the 1945 Yan'an cave-dwelling conversation between Mao Zedong and Huang Yanpei, that regimes flourish and then collapse. Party texts present escaping it as a central task.
The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position on the Party Central Committee and in the Party as a whole, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.

The Party's prolonged position as ruling party, a term first explicitly used by Jiang Zemin in 2001. Party theory treats it as bringing particular risks such as corruption and detachment from the people.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Full and rigorous self-governance of the Party as the only path to lasting vitality and a successful "new road to the exam"
zh: 全面从严治党是党永葆生机活力、走好新的赶考之路的必由之路
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2022, Guo Guangyin takes up a remark by Xi Jinping to the Inner Mongolia delegation at the National People's Congress session: that full and rigorous self-governance of the Party is the only way for the Party to keep its vitality and to pass the "new exam". Guo argues that this is a considered statement of how a long-ruling Marxist party must be built, and that it should run through every area of Party building.

The article has three parts. The first sets out what full and rigorous self-governance means (comprehensive in scope, strict in practice, effective in governance) and goes through the areas of Party building one by one. The second claims that this self-governance is the route to the Party's lasting vitality. The third claims it is the route to meeting the demands of the "new road to the exam" of the new era.

In the first part, Guo gives political building priority as the "foundation and soul" of the rest, tied to the Two Upholds. Ideological building comes next, then organisational building, work style (including the central Eight-point Regulation), discipline and rule-based Party governance through internal Party regulations. In the second part Guo lists the means: firm ideals and convictions, holding to the original aspiration and mission, and the courage for self-reform. Guo calls self-reform the mark that sets the Party apart from other parties and the way it escapes the "historical cycle of rise and fall". The Party must also grasp the laws of governing, which Guo says means better governing capacity and a more scientific level of Party building, backed by ideology and by institutions.

Guo concludes that, since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the campaign has reversed lax and soft Party governance, secured an overwhelming victory against corruption and strengthened the Party's capacity for self-purification and self-improvement. The Party still faces long-term "four tests" and severe "four dangers". It should therefore keep a strict tone and treat Party building as the decisive "great new project" alongside the great struggle, the great cause and the great dream. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official rationale for Party discipline and Party building in the new era, as presented in a Red Flag Manuscripts commentary.
quoteEn: Courage for self-reform is the distinguishing mark that sets our Party apart from other parties, and the secret of its success in escaping the historical cycle of order and chaos, rise and fall, and growing more vital after a century of vicissitudes.
quoteZh: 勇于自我革命是我们党区别于其他政党的显著标志，是党跳出治乱兴衰历史周期率、历经百年沧桑更加充满活力的成功秘诀。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A strategy announced after the 18th Party Congress (2012) and later folded into the "Four Comprehensives". It covers Party discipline, ideological education, organisation, work style and the anti-corruption campaign.
The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Party Central Committee and in the Party as a whole, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.
Rules adopted by the Politburo in December 2012 to curb bureaucratic formalism, extravagance and waste among officials. They are treated as the starting point of the work-style campaign.

A metaphor from Mao Zedong's remark in 1949, as the Party moved to Beijing, that it was going to take an exam. It is used to present the Party's governing record as a continuing test judged by the people.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Upholding and strengthening the Party's centralised and unified leadership over economic work
zh: 坚持和加强党对经济工作的集中统一领导
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao), Ding Xiaoqin takes up how the Communist Party of China should lead economic work. Ding presents upholding and strengthening the Party's centralised and unified leadership over economic work as an important component of Xi Jinping's economic thought and as a necessary consequence of the Party's overall leadership. The central claim is that the authority of the Party Central Committee is the key guarantee of this leadership, and that it requires both better institutions and stronger leadership capacity.

The article is organised in four parts. It first places economic leadership within the Party's overall leadership, citing the 2021 historical resolution (adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee) and Xi Jinping's statements. It then explains why the Central Committee's role is decisive, followed by a survey of institutional mechanisms at the central, local and state-owned enterprise levels. The last part sets out three requirements for improving the Party's capacity to lead economic work.

Ding's core argument draws on the Central Economic Work Conferences of 2018 to 2021, which the author says increasingly named centralised and unified Party leadership as a lesson of successful economic work, and finally placed it first. In this reading, the Central Committee sets direction, strategy and policy, which unifies thought and action and allows the nation to concentrate resources on major undertakings. On institutions, Ding points to the replacement of the central leading small groups by commissions, including the Central Financial and Economic Affairs Commission, to quarterly economic analysis and to annual work conferences. Ding also describes local Party committees collectively deciding development plans, and state-owned enterprise Party committees discussing major matters before boards and managers decide.

On capacity, Ding calls for three things. Cadres should acquire professional competence, through studying Marxist political economy, doing fieldwork, drawing on think tanks and improving selection and training. Economic leadership should be conducted according to law and in line with objective economic, social and natural laws. The method of seeking progress while maintaining stability should be applied, with "stability" meaning steady growth, employment, prices and financial security, and "progress" meaning structural adjustment and deeper reform and opening up. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official rationale and institutional channels for Party leadership over the economy in the period after the 19th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Only by upholding and strengthening the Party Central Committee's centralised and unified leadership over economic work can it better play its core leadership role of overseeing the whole situation and coordinating all parties, which helps concentrate efforts on major undertakings and lets the superstructure better react upon the economic base.
quoteZh: 只有坚持和加强党中央对经济工作的集中统一领导才能更好发挥党中央总揽全局、协调各方的领导核心作用，从而有利于集中力量办大事，更好地发挥上层建筑对经济基础的反作用。

glossary.explanation: A principle in Party documents that the Central Committee holds ultimate decision-making authority and that all Party organisations and levels of government carry out its line. Under Xi Jinping it is stressed as the highest principle of Party leadership.
An annual meeting, usually held in December, at which the Party leadership reviews the year's economy and sets the tasks and policy tone for the next year.
The general guiding principle for economic work in the Xi Jinping era. It combines keeping the economy stable with pursuing structural adjustment and reform.

glossary.en: Central Financial and Economic Affairs Commission
glossary.explanation: A decision-making body of the Party Central Committee for major economic work. It was formed in 2018 by upgrading the earlier Central Financial and Economic Leading Small Group.
The official term for the body of ideas on economic work attributed to Xi Jinping, presented as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

t: Strengthening Party building to lead the high-quality development of state-owned enterprises
zh: 加强党的建设引领国有企业高质量发展
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) in 2022, Deng Weihua, a senior Party and corporate official at a state-owned construction firm, takes up how Party building can guide the development of state-owned enterprises (SOEs). The author's thesis is that Party leadership is the "root and soul" of SOEs, and that high-quality Party building is the fundamental guarantee of their high-quality development. SOEs, in this account, must keep Party leadership unwavering and fuse Party work with production and management.

The article opens by citing the Central Committee's trial regulations on strengthening Party leadership in corporate governance and on Party grassroots organisations in SOEs, together with Xi Jinping's remarks on SOE Party building. It then proceeds through five headings: Party building as direction-setting, as part of management, as a means of rallying people, as a source of work style, and as a source of vitality. Deng draws on examples from corporate practice and on the Covid-19 response.

Deng's central claim is that the Party's political advantage must be converted into development advantage and governance effectiveness. This is to be done through overall strategy, organisational structure, grassroots leadership arrangements and cadre training. Party organisations are to be embedded in governance through the management system, decision-making (major matters going first to the Party committee for prior review before the board's standing committee), work deployment and performance appraisal that links business results and Party-building targets. Deng also stresses the "people-centred" aim of SOEs: employment, income, benefit-sharing and care for employees. The article further urges SOEs to preserve their "red gene" and to distil a replicable "wartime Party building" model. It argues that Party members' conduct in the Covid-19 response showed the political advantages of the system.

Deng concludes that, amid what the article calls changes unseen in a century and global competition, the Party must strengthen its governing capacity in the economic sphere. Its leadership should be built into every link of corporate governance, and Party work should adapt to a younger workforce born in the 1990s and 2000s. The stated goal is to raise the Party's organisational strength, cohesion and combat effectiveness. Read the original if you want an insider's view, from a practising SOE leader, of how Party committees are being built into corporate governance, appraisal and employee work in China's state sector.
quoteEn: Upholding and strengthening Party leadership is the glorious tradition of China's state-owned enterprises, and their root and soul.
quoteZh: 坚持党的领导、加强党的领导，是我国国有企业的光荣传统，是国有企业的根和魂。

glossary.explanation: An official slogan, prominent since 2017, that stresses quality, efficiency and innovation of growth rather than speed alone.
A term in the article for a Party-building mechanism that mobilises SOEs quickly for extraordinary national tasks, such as the Covid-19 response.

t: The distinctive political character and powerful political strengths of the Communist Party of China
zh: 中国共产党鲜明的政治品格和强大的政治优势
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2022, no. 16), Feng Pengzhi takes up Xi Jinping's July 2022 statement, made at a seminar for provincial and ministerial leading cadres ahead of the 20th Party Congress. Xi said that being guided by Marxist scientific theory is the Party's distinctive political character and powerful political strength. Feng argues that this explains why the Party succeeds and why socialism with Chinese characteristics works: in the end, "Marxism works".

The article has three parts. The first treats Marxism as the soul and banner of the Party. The second presents the continuous adaptation of Marxism to Chinese conditions as the Party's key historical experience. The third sets out how to grasp and apply Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, including its worldview and methodology. Feng relies heavily on Xi's statements and on the 2021 Party resolution on history.

Feng's central claim is that Marxism has proved effective in China because the Party has kept "adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times" and has not treated it as dogma. Feng traces three historic leaps: Mao Zedong Thought, the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and Xi Jinping Thought. Each is tied to an era of Party work, from the New Democratic Revolution to the new era after the 18th Party Congress (2012). Feng attributes the Party's strength to several habits: drawing on Chinese practice and traditional culture, keeping pace with the times, and absorbing the achievements of other civilizations.

Feng then turns to practice. The Party must rely on the people, benefit the people and stay rooted among them, with whole-process people's democracy, common prosperity, and opposition to corruption, formalism and bureaucratism. Cadres should also master the materialist-dialectical principles in Xi Jinping Thought, such as the unity of the material world, contradiction, and the people as makers of history. They should apply its methods too: systemic thinking, strategic, historical, dialectical and bottom-line thinking, and a spirit of struggle. Feng presents these as the way to keep opening up new realms of Marxism in China. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party theorists in 2022 tied the Party's "Marxism works" formula to the three leaps and to study of Xi Jinping Thought.
quoteEn: Marxism is not dogma but a guide to action, and it must develop as practice changes.
quoteZh: 马克思主义不是教条，而是行动指南，必须随着实践的变化而发展。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for combining Marxist principles with China's concrete conditions, its traditional culture and contemporary developments. It was stressed in Party documents after the 19th Party Congress.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage of the adaptation of Marxism to China.
An official concept, promoted by Xi Jinping since 2019, describing China's democracy as covering every stage of political life and not only elections.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, emphasised by the Party leadership as a feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The official name for China's path and theoretical system since reform and opening up, combining Marxist principles with Chinese conditions.

t: Embracing the world: the historical evolution of the Communist Party of China's international outlook
zh: 胸怀天下：中国共产党国际观的历史沿革
paras: Taking up the Sixth Plenum's 2021 Resolution on the Party's century of struggle, which names "embracing the world" as a historical lesson, Zhang asks how the Communist Party of China (CPC) has understood its relationship to the outside world. The article argues that the Party's international outlook is distinct from its theory of international relations or diplomacy. It covers the Party's views on world history, on other parties, on Chinese and world revolution, and on civilizations. Zhang holds that this outlook grew out of Marxist internationalism, Chinese traditional culture and changing conditions, and that it should be read within the history of the world socialist movement.

The article traces four periods. These are the New Democratic Revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics. For each, Zhang identifies the central problem the Party faced and the answers it gave. Zhang closes by drawing four lessons from the century as a whole.

In the first period, Zhang argues, the young Party, then a section of the Communist International, absorbed Lenin's theory of world revolution. It copied Soviet urban-insurrection strategy and went through detours until Mao Zedong's Sinification of Marxism. Zhang points to the thesis that the Chinese revolution is part of the world revolution, to the strategy of encircling the cities from the countryside, and to the principle of independence and self-reliance. In the second period, the Party first took the Soviet Union as its teacher, then urged critical learning and a "second integration". After the Sino-Soviet split it developed the "intermediate zone" and "three worlds" ideas. In the reform era, Zhang says, "peace and development" became the theme of the age, and self-reliance was combined with opening up. This led to the idea of a harmonious world. Since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Zhang describes an outlook framed by the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and "changes unseen in a century", and expressed in a community with a shared future for mankind and Chinese modernization.

Zhang concludes that the Party has "embraced the world" by following four principles. It upholds Marxist internationalism while taking its own road. It analyses situations realistically and sides with human progress. It maintains independence and self-reliance while learning from abroad. It pursues peace and mutual benefit while being ready to struggle against hegemonism and imperialism. The article presents these as the basis of the Party's current global role and of its claim to lead a revival of world socialism. Read the original if you want a periodised, officially framed account of how Party theorists link China's revolution, construction and reform to its view of world order.
quoteEn: The CPC's international outlook differs from its theories of international relations and diplomacy. The latter mainly set out the relations and activities among nation-states and other international actors, whereas the outlook aims to understand the Party's own relationship with the outside world from a global perspective.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的国际观区别于其国际关系理论和外交理论，后两者主要致力于阐述民族国家等国际行为主体之间的关系与活动，而其国际观则旨在以世界眼光认识自身同外部世界的关系

glossary.literal: to hold the world in one's heart
glossary.explanation: A phrase the 2021 Party Resolution on the century of struggle lists as one of the Party's historical lessons. It stresses concern for humanity's future alongside national goals.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept, promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012), of a world order based on cooperation, shared security and common development.
The official term for China's path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models and as an option for developing countries.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central goal of Party discourse in the Xi era, referring to restoring China's national strength and international standing.

glossary.zh: 世界百年未有之大变局
glossary.literal: great changes in the world not seen in a hundred years
glossary.explanation: A phrase Xi Jinping uses to describe a shifting global balance of power and a turbulent international environment.
Mao Zedong's 1946 notion of a belt of countries lying between the United States and the Soviet Union, later developed into the three worlds theory.
Deng Xiaoping's assessment that peace and development, not war and revolution, are the main themes of the age. It underpins reform-era foreign policy.

t: Deeply understanding the "Two Establishes" and consciously achieving the "Two Upholds"
zh: 深刻理解“两个确立” 自觉做到“两个维护”
paras: Writing in Qiushi (2022, no. 2), Chen Li takes up the Party's 2021 historical resolution, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee, which declared that establishing Xi Jinping as the core of the Central Committee and the whole Party, and establishing the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, are of decisive significance. This is a theoretical commentary on the Party's line. It argues that the Two Establishes rest on theoretical, historical and practical grounds, and that understanding them should strengthen the Party's consciousness in carrying out the Two Upholds.

The article has four parts. Three sections set out the theoretical, historical and practical bases of the Two Establishes. A final section describes how Party members and cadres should achieve the Two Upholds. Chen draws on Marx, Engels and Lenin, on Party history from the First Congress through the Zunyi Meeting, Yan'an and Deng Xiaoping, and on developments since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

On theory, Chen holds that upholding the authority of the Party centre and centralised, unified leadership is a principle of the Marxist doctrine of party-building. The article cites Engels on the Paris Commune and on authority, and Lenin on political leaders and revolutionary theory. It attributes the collapse of the Soviet Communist Party partly to its abandonment of centralised leadership. On history, Chen argues that the Party suffered repeated setbacks before the Zunyi Meeting because it lacked a mature leadership core. After Zunyi, a core around Mao Zedong formed, a point Chen reinforces with Mao's and Deng's remarks on the leadership core. On practice, Chen says the Party centre with Xi as its core has since 2012 strengthened Party leadership, handled major risks and achieved historic changes. Xi's core status and his Thought were then written into the Party constitution and the state constitution.

Chen concludes that the Two Establishes reflect the will of the Party, army and people and provide a stronger political guarantee for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Chen calls for turning support for them into the Two Upholds through five steps: firm belief in and faithful practice of Xi Jinping Thought, stronger Party political building, concrete action rather than slogans, loyalty to the Party, and better political capacity. Read the original if you want an authoritative statement of how the Party's theorists justify the Two Establishes and what they require of cadres.
quoteEn: Achieving the "Two Upholds" is a concrete matter, not an abstract one, and must be put into action.
quoteZh: 做到“两个维护”，是具体的不是抽象的，要落实到行动上。

glossary.explanation: A formulation from the 2021 historical resolution: establishing Xi Jinping as the core of the Central Committee and the whole Party, and establishing the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought. The Party describes it as decisive for the cause of the Party and state.

The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Party Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee. It was introduced in 2018 and is presented as a core political duty of Party members.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and the state constitution in 2018.
An official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, central to Party discourse since the 18th Party Congress.
A category of Party-building work stressing political stance, direction and discipline, and obedience to the Central Committee. It is ranked first among the Party's building tasks.

t: The Communist Party of China and the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
zh: 中国共产党与中华民族伟大复兴
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 29 June 2022, Ren Lixuan argues that only the Communist Party of China could take on the historic mission of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and that this rejuvenation is the single theme running through the Party's century of struggle. The piece is an authoritative-style commentary that builds on Xi Jinping's statement that without the Party there would be no new China and no national rejuvenation, and on the 2021 Party resolution on its history.

The article has three parts. The first explains why the Party was the only force able to carry the mission, citing four factors: scientific theory, its founding aspiration, reliance on the people, and self-reform. The second says that all the Party's struggles, sacrifices and creations since 1921 have served rejuvenation. The third looks ahead and sets out how to advance the cause by taking in hand the "four greats": great struggle, great project, great cause and great dream.

In Ren's account, earlier political forces failed to save the nation because they lacked a lasting mass movement and did not recognise the strength of the people. The Party, by contrast, adapted Marxism to China, culminating in Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and it pursues no special interests of its own. It also escaped the "historical cycle" of rise and fall through self-reform, which Ren presents as the second answer after Mao Zedong's answer of supervision by the people. The article cites more than 3.7 million identifiable martyrs between 1921 and 1949 as evidence of sacrifice, and it points to the building of a moderately prosperous society, Chinese modernization and institutional innovation as evidence of creation.

Ren concludes that the country is closer than ever to rejuvenation but must expect harder struggle, including against a long-term external containment campaign that the author attributes to the United States. The author calls for implementing the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, continuing full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, and pursuing high-quality development and common prosperity along socialism with Chinese characteristics. The piece also presents rejuvenation as contributing to a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a representative statement of the official Party narrative of rejuvenation in the run-up to the 20th Party Congress (2022).
quoteEn: Our Party has come this far by relying on struggle, and it will inevitably have to rely on struggle to win the future.
quoteZh: 我们党依靠斗争走到今天，也必然要依靠斗争赢得未来。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal. It presents China's modern history as a path from humiliation to renewed strength, with milestones set for 2021 and 2049.
A formula adopted in 2021 that affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the whole Party, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold the authority of Xi Jinping as core and the centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The name of the Party's discipline and anti-corruption drive since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering political, ideological and organisational discipline.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into its constitution in 2017 and presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
A socialist goal that the Party has emphasised since the 2010s, meaning prosperity shared by all rather than by some.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept of international relations, promoted since 2013 as a framework of cooperation and common interests among states.

t: Opening up a historic undertaking by upholding and strengthening the Party's overall leadership
zh: 在坚持和加强党的全面领导中开创历史伟业
paras: Published in Guangming Daily on 1 July 2022, the centenary of the Party's founding, this commentary asks why the Communist Party of China's overall leadership must be upheld and how it should be strengthened. Liu Tongfang takes as the starting point the Resolution on the major achievements and historical experience of the Party's century of struggle, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). Liu argues that leadership by the Party is the first lesson of the century and that it must be maintained steadfastly and without wavering.

The piece has three parts. The first grounds the principle in scientific socialism and the classical texts. The second sets out how Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era places Party leadership first among its core contents. The third gives practical measures for the Party's leading role in the new era, and a short closing passage restates the main points.

Liu's central claim is that leadership by a proletarian party is a basic principle of scientific socialism. The author gives four reasons: it realises the people's interests, it fulfils the proletariat's historical mission, it is needed for victory in struggle, and it is the precondition for moving socialism from theory to practice. Liu draws on Marx, Engels and Lenin for support. Liu then presents three formulations from Xi Jinping as an original contribution to scientific socialism in the twenty-first century. In them, Party leadership is the most essential feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics, the greatest strength of its system, and the supreme political leadership force. Liu says the Party's leading position is confirmed by history, set by the nature of the state and written into the constitution. Liu also contrasts China's peaceful development and stable economy with what the author describes as continuing local wars and weak growth in the West.

For practice, Liu calls for three things. The first is to uphold the authority of the Party Central Committee and its centralised, unified leadership, with the Two Upholds as the basic political requirement. The second is to build an institutional system that carries Party leadership into state organs, the rule of law and grass-roots organisations, and to improve democratic centralism. The third is to pursue the Party's self-reform so as to keep it advanced and pure, including through anti-corruption work and better governing capacity. Liu concludes that Party leadership is the anchor for the new journey towards a modern socialist country and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of the official line on Party leadership as presented in a major Party newspaper at the 2022 centenary.
quoteEn: Upholding the leadership of the Communist Party of China is, in essence, to establish and consolidate the people's position as masters of the country, and fundamentally to safeguard, realise and develop the vital interests of the Chinese people and the Chinese nation.
quoteZh: 坚持中国共产党的领导，本质上是确立与巩固人民群众作为国家主人翁的地位，是从根本上维护、实现和发展中国人民和中华民族的切身利益。

glossary.explanation: A political requirement, formulated in 2018, to uphold Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and the state constitution in 2018.
The official name for China's path of socialist development since reform and opening up, which the Party presents as combining Marxist principles with Chinese conditions.
An official term for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself, including anti-corruption work and strengthening Party building.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Party, combining internal discussion with binding, centralised decisions and subordination of lower bodies to higher ones.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream, of restoring China to a position of strength and prosperity.

t: Summing up historical experience: the scientific method behind the Communist Party of China's major achievements
zh: 总结历史经验：中国共产党取得重大成就的科学方法
paras: Han Zhenfeng and Mi Ting ask how the Communist Party of China (CPC) has used the summing-up of historical experience as a working method, and why it counts as a decisive factor in the Party's achievements. They define the method as a scientific application of Marxist methodology, an expression of dialectical-materialist epistemology in practice. It turns knowledge gained in practice into rational conclusions and theory that then guide new practice. Drawing on the Party's third historical resolution (2021), the authors present it as a tradition of more than a century.

The article proceeds chronologically through four periods: the New Democratic Revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics. For each period it identifies characteristic practices, from the 1927 August 7 Meeting and the Zunyi Meeting to Mao Zedong's rural investigations, the 1945 and 1981 historical resolutions, and Xi Jinping's call for a 'grand historical view' and the 2021 Party history study campaign. A final section draws out the method's basic dimensions and lessons.

The authors identify three constant principles: integrating Marxist fundamentals with China's concrete conditions, using dialectical thinking to weigh positive and negative experience, and combining continuity with development. They argue that the Party sums up experience in several ways: through investigation and the mass line, through domestic and foreign experience, and through routine summing-up at congresses and anniversaries. They also stress raising experience into new theory. Their main analytical move is to distinguish fundamental, basic and specific experience. Fundamental experience, such as upholding the Party's overall leadership, Marxism and the socialist path, governs the other two; specific cases such as the 'Fengqiao experience' or 'Jinjiang experience' supplement and refine it.

The authors conclude that summing-up must keep to the people's standpoint and respond to the demands of the times, guided by a problem-oriented approach. They call for the Party to draw lessons from mistakes while opposing exaggeration of errors or negation of Party history. They also urge it to treat foreign experience as reference, not as a model to copy, with its own experience primary. They add that experience should be promptly turned into theory and used on new problems, since summing-up serves present needs and is not an end in itself. Read the original if you want a systematic, Party-official account of how the CPC describes its own method of historical self-assessment, from Mao to Xi.
quoteEn: We do not sum up experience for the sake of summing up experience, but in order to resolve the problems and contradictions that arise on the path of development; the fundamental starting point is to serve practical needs.
quoteZh: 我们不是为了总结经验而总结经验，而是为了解决发展道路上出现的问题和矛盾而总结经验，是以服务现实需要为根本出发点的。

glossary.explanation: A formal Central Committee resolution that gives an authoritative verdict on the Party's history. The CPC has adopted three: in 1945, 1981 and 2021.
A concept Xi Jinping promoted in the early 2020s. It calls for viewing the Party and country in long historical time and in global context.
A Party working method that gathers the views and experience of ordinary people and turns them into policy, then returns to the people to put policy into practice.

keywords: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context

t: The great changes of the new era's ten years show the strong resilience and vitality of China's economy
zh: 新时代十年的伟大变革彰显中国经济强大韧性和活力
paras: Published in Guangming Daily on 31 August 2022, shortly before the 20th Party Congress, this commentary takes Xi Jinping's speech to a seminar of provincial and ministerial leaders as its starting point. Ye and Huang argue that the decade since the 18th Party Congress (2012) brought historic changes that show the strength, resilience and vitality of China's economy. They present these changes as the basis for Chinese modernization and for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article has three parts. The first reviews economic achievements across six areas: economic strength, scientific and technological innovation, coordinated regional development, green development, opening up, and people's livelihoods. The second describes what the authors call a new outlook in the economy, covering resilience, strategic resolve, released vitality and China's contribution to the world economy. The third sets out the sources of this performance and the direction ahead.

The authors rely on figures to make the case. They cite GDP of 114 trillion yuan in 2021, a global share rising from 11.4% to above 18%, per capita GDP of 12,500 US dollars, and R&D spending 2.7 times the 2012 level. They also cite a fall in the urban–rural income ratio from 2.88 to 2.50 and the poverty alleviation of 98.99 million rural people. They attribute resilience to a complete industrial system, a supply chain with strong supporting capacity, a flexible macroeconomic policy toolkit and a very large domestic market. They name Xi Jinping Thought on the economy, the Party's overall leadership of economic work, the people-centred approach, the new development philosophy, problem-oriented reform and integration into the world economy as the guiding factors. Leadership, in their account, supplies the capacity to concentrate resources on major undertakings and is the core advantage against risks.

Ye and Huang conclude that the decade's changes give the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation a stronger institutional, material and spiritual footing and set a course for high-quality development. They contend that China followed an independent path rather than the old Western road to modernization. They also hold that China has acted as a builder of world peace and a contributor to global development. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official-aligned scholars summarised the economic record of 2012–2022 on the eve of the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Leadership by the Communist Party of China is the defining feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the greatest strength of the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 中国共产党领导是中国特色社会主义最本质特征，是中国特色社会主义制度最大优势。

glossary.explanation: Official term for China's own path to modernization, stressed in Party discourse especially from the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China to national strength and prosperity, closely associated with Xi Jinping's leadership.
A framework of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, put forward in 2015 as a guide to economic policy.
Official term for a shift from speed-oriented growth to growth that stresses efficiency, innovation, sustainability and fairness.

glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on the economy
glossary.explanation: The economic component of Xi Jinping's thought, presented by the Party as a guide to economic work in the new era.

keywords: Xi Jinping Thought on the economy

t: On the Marxist shaping of "Chinese governance" by the Communist Party of China
zh: 论中国共产党关于“中国之治”的马克思主义塑造
paras: Scholars have read "Chinese governance" (zhongguo zhi zhi) through traditional culture, through comparison with the West, and through the Fourth Plenum document of 2019. He Changyu and Wang Guiquan argue that this literature lacks a Marxist account of the concept's scientific content. Their thesis is that "Chinese governance" is the result of the Communist Party of China applying Marxism to Chinese conditions, and that it has four linked dimensions: historic achievement, "Chinese wisdom", "Chinese institutions" and "Chinese capacity".

The article first traces the term from the Song writer Su Shi through Lu Xun, Kang Youwei and Liang Qichao. In the authors' account, these earlier models failed to deliver order and prosperity. It then devotes one section to each dimension and ties each to a principle of historical materialism. It closes with practical measures for turning institutional strengths into governance effectiveness.

The authors map the four dimensions onto Marxist categories. "Chinese wisdom" is social consciousness actively reflecting social being, and they place Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era in this line. "Chinese institutions" are a superstructure resting on a particular economic base. The authors set out the fundamental, basic and important institutions of socialism with Chinese characteristics as three tiers, comparing them to a worldview, a methodology and concrete methods. "Chinese capacity" rests on Marx's view of practice. Here they argue that an institution is judged by the governance results it produces, citing GDP growth from 1952 to 2019 and long-term social stability as the "two miracles".

To keep institutional advantages and convert them into effectiveness, the authors propose three measures. The first is to uphold and improve Party leadership. The second is to give full play to the people's role through people's congresses, multiparty cooperation and grassroots self-governance. The third is to improve government decision-making and implementation, with accountability for failures. They conclude that the Party's century of history is one in which "Chinese wisdom" guides, "Chinese institutions" are established and "Chinese capacity" is applied. Read the original if you want to see how Party theorists fit the official concept of governance into the base–superstructure and practice framework of historical materialism.
quoteEn: "Chinese governance" is by no means a flight of fancy; it truly turns astute "Chinese wisdom" into operable, programmable "Chinese institutions".
quoteZh: “中国之治”绝非凭空想象，而是真正使聪慧的“中国之智”，转化为可操作可程序化的“中国之制”。

glossary.explanation: A phrase popularised by the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) for China's system of order and governance. The article reads it through Marxism and the Party's history.
The authors' term for the Party's guiding ideas, which they present as social consciousness reflecting China's social being.
The authors' term for the state institutions and legal system built by the Party, which they treat as a superstructure.
The authors' term for the practical effectiveness with which institutional strengths are turned into governance results.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
Hu Jintao-era guiding concept, adopted in 2007, stressing people-centred, comprehensive and sustainable development.
Jiang Zemin's theory, introduced around 2000. It holds that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the majority.

t: A century of relations between Chinese youth and the Communist Party of China: review and reflections
zh: 中国青年与中国共产党关系百年发展的回顾与思考
source: Research on Ideological Education (Sixiang jiaoyu yanjiu), 2022 no. 7
paras: Writing in 2022, after the Party's centenary, Peng Qinghong and Tian Shan ask how young people and the Communist Party of China (CPC) have related over more than a hundred years, and how that relationship should be handled in future. They argue that the two are "interconnected and mutually thriving" (xiangtong gongrong): the Party's growth has depended on youth, and young people's development has depended on Party guidance. The authors treat this as a main reason for past success and a condition of future success.

The article has three parts. The first traces the role of youth across five periods: founding of the Party, national liberation, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era. The second analyses the internal factors behind the relationship. The third proposes how to develop it going forward. The authors support their account with quotations from Lenin, Stalin, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin, Hu Jintao and Xi Jinping, and with Party membership statistics from 2022.

In the authors' analysis, the relationship rests on three things. The first is affinity: young people's pursuit of truth, novelty, change and practicality is said to match the Party's righteousness, revolutionary character, creativity and practical orientation. The Party's "people-oriented" character and its collective organisation are said to supply young people with a foundation for growth and with socialisation. The second is shared prosperity: the Party offers a broad stage for young people, who give it vitality in return. The third is the Communist Youth League, which the authors describe as the bridge and link that gathers young people around the Party and addresses their practical problems. As evidence of structural closeness, they cite the 2022 Party statistical bulletin: 24.159 million members aged 35 or under, 25 per cent of the 96.712 million total, and 80.8 per cent of those recruited in 2021.

For the future the authors propose a strategy of "four lines advancing together". The ideological line calls for strengthening ideals and convictions and for combating historical nihilism, money worship, hedonism and extreme individualism. The organisational line calls for extending Party and League organisation to young people in new occupations and for innovating forms of activity. The development line calls for supporting young people's growth, innovation and entrepreneurship. The problem-solving line calls for easing difficulties in employment, housing and education and for protecting young people's rights. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist-institute scholarly article presents the Party–youth relationship historically and sets out the youth-work agenda of the new era.
quoteEn: Young people's development relies on the Party's correct guidance, and the Party's lasting vitality relies on the boundless vitality of youth.
quoteZh: 青年的发展依托于党的正确引领，党永葆活力依靠青年的无限活力。

glossary.explanation: The authors' term for the relationship between youth and the Party, in which the two share common features and flourish together. It is used by the authors as an analytical frame rather than as an official slogan.
The CPC-led mass organisation for young people, founded in 1922. It is officially described as the Party's assistant and reserve force, and as a channel for recruiting and educating young people.
The period since the 18th Party Congress (2012), described in official discourse as a new stage of socialism with Chinese characteristics under Xi Jinping.

glossary.zh: 社会主义革命和建设时期
glossary.pinyin: shèhuì zhǔyì gémìng hé jiànshè shíqī
glossary.explanation: The official periodisation label for the years from 1949 to 1978, before reform and opening up.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world begun at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978.

t: The Communist Party of China's practice and experience in opposing historical nihilism
zh: 中国共产党反对历史虚无主义的实践与经验
source: People's Tribune (Renmin Luntan), July 2022 (second half-month issue)
paras: Writing in mid-2022, Yang Jun asks how the Communist Party of China has responded to historical nihilism and how that struggle should continue as the phenomenon changes form. Yang treats historical nihilism as a political current fundamentally opposed to Marxism, not as the value-neutral 'academic discussion' it claims to be. The article argues that the Party's approach combines affirmative 'building' with 'refuting', that nihilism has taken a 'soft', harder-to-detect form, and that opposing it requires long-term persistence.

The article has four parts. It first reviews the Party's measures since 2021, then describes five features of present-day historical nihilism. It next examines how nihilism interacts with other social currents, and finally gives three reasons why criticism must be sustained and what tasks follow. Yang's examples include the Party history study campaign, online rumour-refutation lists, legal punishment of insults to heroes and martyrs, and online controversies of 2021.

On the Party's response, Yang points to the campaign launched in February 2021 and the 'four histories' publicity drive, backed by films and television series. On the 'refuting' side, Yang cites rumour-refutation lists and prosecutions under the Law on the Protection of Heroes and Martyrs. Yang says these measures raised public awareness of the concept and shrank nihilism's room for spread. Nihilism, in Yang's account, now focuses on Party history and the history of the People's Republic and reform era, and uses concealed rhetoric, recycled old online content, online disputes and 'fan circle' culture. It also draws on consumerism, pan-entertainment and online populism, which Yang says clothe a political aim in an 'invisibility cloak'.

Yang concludes that the struggle must be long-term, for three reasons: Marxism has always developed through contending with hostile currents; nihilism threatens ideological security on the road to the second centenary goal; and global changes are sharpening the contest between socialism and capitalism. Yang calls for better analysis of nihilism's theory and trends, clear criteria separating scholarship from political agitation, and work on institutions, rule of law, education, internet governance and communication. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-affiliated scholar describes the current forms of historical nihilism and the state's strategy against it.
quoteEn: Criticising and curbing historical nihilism cannot be expected to succeed in one stroke, nor should it stall because of nihilism's concealment, the complexity of the ideological environment or the challenge of changing internet technology; one should keep up an attitude and conviction of persistent effort.
quoteZh: 批判、遏制历史虚无主义，既不能幻想在短时间内一蹴而就，也不能因历史虚无主义的隐蔽性、社会思想环境的复杂性、网络技术迭代更新的挑战性而止步不前，应保持久久为功的态度和信念。

glossary.explanation: In official Chinese usage, a political current that denies or distorts the Party's history, the revolution and socialism. Critics of the term say it can be used to label dissenting historical views.
The history of the Party, of the People's Republic, of reform and opening up, and of socialist development. They are the core of the 2021 publicity and education drive.
A nationwide campaign launched in February 2021, ahead of the Party's centenary, to study the Party's history.
The organised online fan communities around celebrities, known for defending idols collectively.
The official aim of building a modern socialist country by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic.

t: Bringing the Party's political advantage of overall leadership into play on the new journey
zh: 新征程上发挥党的全面领导的政治优势
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in August 2022, asks how the Party's overall leadership can be used as a political advantage on the new journey of building a modern socialist country. Wu Jiaqing, drawing on volume four of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China, argues that the Party now faces conditions and tasks of rare complexity and difficulty. In Wu's view, making full use of this advantage will be the key to success on what the text calls a new "examination road".

The piece is organised under two headings. The first concerns the authority of the Party Central Committee and its centralised, unified leadership. The second concerns the Party's capacity to set direction, take the overall view, formulate policy and promote reform.

On the first, Wu argues that the Central Committee's authority is the basic support in times of difficulty. Wu credits the achievements since the 18th Party Congress (2012) to the leadership of the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core, and cites the Two Establishes as confirming this. Wu calls on Party members to practise the Two Upholds and to strengthen the institutional safeguards, citing intra-Party regulations, reporting requirements and a tightly linked organisational system. On the second, Wu treats each of the four capacities as a matter of ability and resolve for leading cadres: correct political direction, a focus on the "matters of national importance", policy grounded in investigation and a people-centred approach, and deepening reform.

Wu concludes that leading cadres at every level must raise these capacities so that modernization stays on course. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars presented the Party's overall leadership as a source of strength shortly before the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: The most important thing in upholding and strengthening the Party's overall leadership is to resolutely safeguard the authority of the Party Central Committee and its centralised, unified leadership.
quoteZh: 坚持和加强党的全面领导，最重要的是坚决维护党中央权威和集中统一领导。

glossary.explanation: A formulation from the sixth plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the whole Party, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.

glossary.literal: the great matters of the country
glossary.explanation: A phrase used by Xi Jinping for the fundamental, major issues bearing on the fate of the Party and country. Cadres are urged to keep them in mind.

t: Seeking the code of why a century-old Party has succeeded
zh: 探寻百年大党为什么能够成功的密码
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in August 2022, Sang Donghua asks why the Communist Party of China has stayed vigorous, remained at the forefront of its era and continued to serve as the core of leadership after a hundred years. Drawing on the Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021), Sang answers that five things have never changed: the Party's lofty ideals, its founding mission, its fundamental purpose of serving the people, its commitment to developing Marxism, and its political courage for self-reform.

The commentary is organised into four sections, each describing the Party as a particular kind of political force: a mission-driven party, a party of the people, a party armed with scientific theory, and a party of revolutionaries. Each section runs through the revolutionary, socialist construction, reform and opening up, and post-18th Party Congress (2012) periods. It draws on speeches by Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping, early Party documents and episodes from the Long March and the Yan'an years.

Sang argues first that the Party has held to socialism and communism since 1921, and cites the more than 3.7 million named revolutionary martyrs of 1921–1949 as proof of its commitment. Second, Sang holds that the Party's strength comes from its bond with the people, from the 1945 inclusion of serving the people in the Party constitution to the poverty-alleviation campaign, which the article says lifted 98.99 million rural poor out of poverty. Third, adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, is presented as the Party's ongoing theoretical innovation. Fourth, Sang stresses self-reform: the Party's greatness lies not in avoiding errors but in confronting its own problems, now through full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

Sang concludes that the Party's century of history is one of striving for lofty social ideals, of sharing the people's fate, of continually adapting Marxism, and of leading a great social revolution through a great self-revolution. The piece is a concise statement of the official account of Party success. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-affiliated historians present the sources of the Party's longevity, with the standard quotations and episodes used in that account.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China is great not because it never makes mistakes, but because it never shies away from treating its own ailments, faces its own problems squarely and has the courage to carry out self-reform.
quoteZh: 中国共产党之所以伟大，不在于不犯错误，而在于从不讳疾忌医，直面自身存在的问题，勇于进行自我革命

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering discipline, anti-corruption and the improvement of Party conduct.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxist principles to Chinese conditions and producing new theory. The article dates its first formal statement to Mao Zedong's 1938 report.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.
A phrase central to Xi Jinping-era Party discourse: to seek happiness for the Chinese people and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

t: Leading social revolution through the Party's self-reform
zh: 以党的自我革命引领社会革命
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in August 2022, shortly before the 20th Party Congress, Li Xiaodong argues that the Communist Party of China has been able to lead what the article calls a great social revolution because it has repeatedly carried out a great revolution on itself. The piece takes its cue from Xi Jinping's recent remarks to provincial and ministerial leaders, which call for the Party's self-reform to lead social revolution. Li presents this as essential to the Party's long-term rule.

The commentary is organised in three numbered sections. The first treats self-reform as an inherent requirement of a Marxist party's historical mission. The second reads it as a lesson drawn from the Party's revolution, construction and reform. The third presents it as the key to coping with changes in the world, the era and history.

Li defines social revolution as resting on the contradiction between productive forces and relations of production, covering both the violent overthrow of old political structures and the building of new society. Self-reform, in this account, means continual self-purification, self-improvement, self-renewal and self-elevation.
