Li cites Engels and Lenin on internal struggle and on a party's attitude to its own mistakes. Li argues that the two revolutions form an organic unity, in which the height reached by self-reform determines the depth of social revolution. The historical record is traced through the Gutian, Zunyi and Yan'an rectification meetings, the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978), and the anti-corruption campaign and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party since 2012. Li contrasts this with dynasties and large parties elsewhere that, the article says, failed to resolve their own serious problems and fell into the pattern of rising quickly and collapsing quickly.

Li concludes that the Party faces lasting "four dangers" and "four tests" and that impurities in ideology, politics, organisation and work style remain unresolved. Self-reform therefore has no end point, and the Party must strengthen its urgency, initiative and foresight to ensure it does not degenerate. Li ties this to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and to building a modern socialist country. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-building discourse in 2022 justified full and rigorous self-governance of the Party as the precondition of the Party's leadership of social change.
quoteEn: The historical height reached by the Party's self-reform determines the practical depth of the great social revolution.
quoteZh: 党的自我革命所达到的历史高度，决定着伟大社会革命的实践深度

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering discipline, anti-corruption and Party-building measures.
The idea that the Party must continually purify and renew itself, stressed in Xi Jinping's speeches as the Party's way to avoid decline in long-term rule.
Official formulation of the Party's main risks: lack of drive, inadequate capacity, detachment from the people, and passivity, along with corruption.
Official formulation of challenges to the Party: the tests of governance, reform and opening up, the market economy, and the external environment.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term national goal, stressed since 2012, of restoring China's strength and international standing.

t: The "small organisation" problem in the early Chinese Communist Party
zh: 中共创建初期的“小组织”问题研究
source: Research and Teaching of Party History (Dangshi yanjiu yu jiaoxue), 2022 no. 3
paras: Between the First and Third Congresses (1921–1923), the young Chinese Communist Party faced what later Party reports called the "small organisation problem" (xiao zuzhi wenti): a group of activists around Zhang Guotao that threatened central leadership and unity. Yang Yang argues that earlier accounts reduced the episode to Zhang's ambition against Chen Duxiu and drew mainly on memoirs. Drawing on Chinese and foreign archives, Yang contends that the group was internally diverse and was driven by a shared wish to tighten Party discipline. Yang also argues that resolving it strengthened the Party's organisational system.

The article has four parts. It first traces how the term changed from a generic label for small groups into a specific name for factional activity after the Second Congress (1922). It then reconstructs the group's membership, its two sources of recruits (the China Labour Union Secretariat and returnees from Russia and France) and its effect on the central leadership. Next it covers the 1922 West Lake meeting, where the Comintern representative Maring (Henk Sneevliet) intervened. It ends with the group's dissolution at the Third Congress and the institutional changes that followed.

Yang makes three main moves. First, the group is measured against Lenin's criteria for factionalism, a separate platform and separate group discipline. Yang finds neither: the members demanded stricter discipline and regular meetings, and criticised Chen Duxiu and the intellectual founders, such as Chen Wangdao and Li Hanjun, as lax. They are therefore described as an "organisation within the organisation" rather than a true faction. Second, Yang shows how the group marginalised Chen and the founding cadres while Zhang's rivalry for Party power, and his abrasive style, fuelled conflict in Wuhan and the Youth League. Third, Maring first sought to cultivate Zhang but backed Chen as the only capable leader. The group collapsed when Zhang lost Comintern support, was discredited after the 1923 Beijing–Hankou railway strike, and failed to be re-elected to the Central Committee at the Third Congress.

Yang concludes that the episode left lasting distrust in the Party. It was also later used as a negative example, and the 1945 Party constitution banned small-organisation activity. The Third Congress produced the Party's first organisational regulation, which defined the chairman's powers, added a secretary's countersignature and fixed meeting schedules. Yang sees this as meeting the group's own demands, and says the case gave experience for applying democratic centralism. Read the original if you study early CPC organisational history, the Comintern's role in China, or the origins of Party discipline, and want an archive-based reassessment of Zhang Guotao's group.
quoteEn: Subjectively, the members of the small organisation had no intention of undermining Party discipline or setting up an independent organisation against central decisions; on the contrary, they demanded that Party discipline be strengthened and strictly enforced.
quoteZh: 小组织成员在主观上没有破坏党的纪律、建立独立组织对抗中央决策的意图，相反他们要求强化和严格执行党的纪律。

glossary.explanation: A term used in early Party documents for the group of activists around Zhang Guotao after the Second Congress (1922). It had a factional sense, unlike the earlier generic meaning of "small group".
The Leninist organisational principle of the Party: free discussion, then binding unity of action and subordination of lower bodies to higher ones.
A special meeting of the Party Central Committee in Hangzhou in August 1922, held at Maring's urging. It discussed Communists joining the Guomindang and the small organisation issue.
The Party's body for leading the labour movement, founded in 1921. It was the organisational base of Zhang Guotao's activist group.

t: The development path, defining categories and innovative value of the CPC's thought on building a moderately prosperous society
zh: 中国共产党小康社会建设思想的发展进路、标识范畴及拓新价值
paras: Following Xi Jinping's 2021 announcement that a moderately prosperous society (xiaokang) had been fully built, Huang Rongsheng asks how the Communist Party of China's thinking on building such a society developed, what its core categories are, and what it adds to theory and practice. The article argues that this thought answers the questions of how xiaokang is built and completed, and that it is a distinctive part of Chinese modernization that will continue to matter in the second centenary goal.

The article has three parts. The first traces the development path through traditional Chinese culture, the Party's century of struggle, and the people's rising living standards. The second sets out five defining categories. The third assesses the innovative value of the thought for the Chinese nation, the modernization project, global poverty governance and Marxist theory.

In Huang's account, the idea runs from the Book of Songs and the Confucian Book of Rites, through the late-Qing reformer Kang Youwei and Sun Yat-sen, to Deng Xiaoping's adoption of xiaokang in 1979 to explain a Chinese-style modernization. The five categories are a people-centred philosophy; social civilizational progress and all-round human development as the essence; poverty alleviation as the focus; Chinese modernization as the direction; and the Party's overall leadership as the key. Huang presents these as applications of historical materialism and of Marx's idea of free and all-round human development. The innovative value is said to lie in delivering the first centenary goal, laying material, institutional and popular foundations for a modernized socialist country, offering a Chinese sample for global poverty reduction, opening the path to common prosperity and a community with a shared future for mankind, and enriching contemporary Chinese Marxism. Huang also draws a favourable comparison between China and the West.

Huang concludes that xiaokang thought fuses traditional culture, the Party's struggle and popular aspiration, and that it is a scientifically tested understanding with an original place in the Party's theoretical innovation. The author treats full xiaokang as a starting point rather than an endpoint, and calls for inheriting the thought in building a modernized socialist country and pursuing common prosperity. Read the original if you want a detailed Party-theory account of how xiaokang is framed historically and conceptually, including its link to poverty alleviation and common prosperity.
quoteEn: Fully building a moderately prosperous society and fully building a great modern socialist country are two key goals of Chinese modernization that are consistent, mutually connected and inseparable.
quoteZh: 全面建成小康社会与全面建成社会主义现代化强国是一以贯之、彼此承接、不可分割的中国式现代化的两个关键目标

glossary.explanation: A term from the Book of Rites, revived by Deng Xiaoping in 1979 to describe a modest level of prosperity as the goal of modernization. 'Fully building' it by 2021 was the Party's first centenary goal.
The official name for China's path to modernization. Deng Xiaoping used a related phrase in 1979. It has been a central slogan since the 2010s and especially after the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The campaign launched in 2015 to eliminate absolute rural poverty by 2020. It was officially declared successful in 2021.
The official goal of shared wealth for all, stressed in the new era. The article treats it as the next stage after xiaokang, with relative poverty as the next challenge.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations and global governance.

t: Persistently advancing full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
zh: 持之以恒推进全面从严治党
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in August 2022, shortly before the 20th Party Congress, Sang Xuecheng, Shi Wei and Xu Jiang take up a speech by Xi Jinping to provincial and ministerial leaders. In it Xi said that building a modern socialist country depends above all on the Party. The authors' thesis is that this requires persistent full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and the continued advance of the "new great project" of Party building in the new era. They say the task rests on five pairings that must be handled together.

The piece is a theoretical commentary built around those five pairings, each introduced with a statement by Xi. They are: Party leadership and rigorous self-governance; ideological and institutional Party building; popular supervision and the Party's self-reform; comprehensive advance and a focus on key points; and treating symptoms and root causes. The authors draw on the experience accumulated since the 18th Party Congress (2012). They present the pairings as a method that the Party's central leadership summed up from the Party's history.

The first argument is that the two halves of each pairing reinforce one another. The more the Party stresses its overall leadership, the more it must govern itself rigorously, because the quality of Party governance determines whether its leading role can be exercised. The authors describe ideological education and institutional rules as the soft and the hard side of Party building. In their view, ideals and convictions give rules their force, and rules give ideological work its backing. Second, the authors present popular supervision, together with whole-process people's democracy, and the Party's self-reform as two answers to the question of how to escape the historical cycle of rise and decline. Third, they present rigorous governance as covering all areas, all Party bodies and the whole process, while giving priority to leading cadres as the "critical minority". They also call for tackling corruption at once through deterrence and for the longer term through institutions and a clean political culture, so that officials "dare not, cannot and do not want to" be corrupt.

The authors conclude that self-governance of the Party is "always on the road" and must never slacken. They hold that only persistence will keep the Party a strong leadership core in upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era. The text is mainly an authoritative restatement of Xi's thinking on Party building, with little new evidence. Read the original if you want a concise, officially framed account of the Party's own rationale for its anti-corruption and Party-discipline policy on the eve of the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Ideological Party building and institutional Party governance combine firmness with flexibility; they complement and reinforce each other.
quoteZh: 思想建党与制度治党二者刚柔并济、互为补充、相辅相成。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan of the Xi Jinping era, used since about 2014, for a campaign of tighter Party discipline, anti-corruption work and internal rules covering all Party organisations and members.

glossary.zh: 新时代党的建设新的伟大工程
glossary.pinyin: xīnshídài dǎng de jiànshè xīn de wěidà gōngchéng
glossary.en: new great project of Party building
glossary.literal: the new great undertaking of Party building in the new era
glossary.explanation: A phrase used by Xi Jinping and the Party leadership for the effort to strengthen the Party's organisation, ideology and discipline in the new era. It builds on the earlier label "great new undertaking" of Party building.

A term for the Party's efforts to correct its own problems and purge corruption without outside pressure. Xi Jinping presents it as the Party's second answer to the question of escaping the historical cycle of rise and decline.

Xi Jinping's term for China's democratic model, which stresses participation at every stage, including election, consultation, decision-making, management and supervision, rather than only at the ballot box.

glossary.pinyin: bù gǎn fǔ, bù néng fǔ, bù xiǎng fǔ
glossary.en: dare not, cannot and do not want to be corrupt
glossary.literal: not dare to be corrupt, not able to be corrupt, not want to be corrupt
glossary.explanation: A three-part formula for anti-corruption work. It combines deterrence by punishment, institutional constraints and ideological education.
A term for leading officials, especially those in senior posts or holding public resources. Party discipline campaigns treat them as the main target of supervision.

t: The Chinese Communist Party's century-long view of Marxism, as seen through the three historical resolutions
zh: 从三个历史决议看中国共产党的百年马克思主义观
paras: Ouyang Qi asks what view of Marxism the Chinese Communist Party has built up over a century, and argues that the three historical resolutions (1945, 1981 and 2021) are the best place to read it. Writing in 2022, Ouyang holds that although each resolution was drafted in a different era, together they answer three questions: what Marxism is, how to treat it, and how to evaluate it.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the basic content of the Party's view of Marxism under three headings: ontology (the nature of Marxism), practice (how to study and apply it) and value (its contemporary worth). The second discusses the significance of this view for the nation, for socialism and for human civilization. The third draws out the experience behind the view's formation, using examples from each resolution.

On ontology, Ouyang reads the resolutions as presenting Marxism as a rigorous guide to action and a scientific truth that keeps pace with the times, in contrast to dogmatism and empiricism. On practice, they call for systematic study of the classics, for research and innovation, and for the leading role of Party leaders in theoretical creation. On value, Marxism appears as guiding ideology, scientific belief and a conception of civilization. The author argues that this view guided the choice of banner and path, helped revive socialism in the twenty-first century, and supported a community with a shared future for mankind. Its formation rests on three things: combining Marxism with China's concrete conditions, joining a sense of the times with a world outlook, and uniting Party leadership with putting the people first.

Ouyang concludes that the Party's view of Marxism runs like a golden thread through adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and explains why "Marxism works". The author presents it as an innovation in Marxist theory and also in the theory and practice of human civilization. Read the original if you want a close reading of the three resolutions as statements on Marxism itself, and a view of how Party theorists present the continuity between them.
quoteEn: The Party's view of Marxism is a golden thread running through the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and through the related practice.
quoteZh: 党的马克思主义观是贯穿在马克思主义中国化时代化及相关实践中的一条金线。

glossary.explanation: Three Central Committee resolutions on Party history, adopted in 1945, 1981 and 2021. Each assesses the Party's past and sets an authoritative line for the future.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxism to China's conditions and updating it for each era. Its latest version adds "of our times" to the older "Sinification of Marxism".

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, centred on shared interests, mutual benefit and common development.

t: Upholding and strengthening the Party's overall leadership and the centralised, unified leadership of the Party Central Committee
zh: 坚持加强党的全面领导和党中央集中统一领导
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 3 August 2022, in the run-up to the 20th Party Congress, Liu Jingbei argues that upholding and strengthening the Party's overall leadership and the centralised, unified leadership of the Party Central Committee has been a fundamental political guarantee of the achievements of the past decade. The commentary takes its cue from Xi Jinping's speech at a seminar for provincial and ministerial-level leading cadres, which described the previous five years and the changes of the new era. Liu's thesis is that, since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core has produced original ideas, institutional arrangements and practical results that have unified the Party in thought, politics and action.

The piece is organised in three parts: a set of original new concepts, thoughts and strategies; a series of important institutional arrangements; and a series of major practical results. The practical results are divided into strengthening leadership over the Party's own building and strengthening the Party's leadership over the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era. The article ends with a short call for the Party to rally around the Central Committee.

On ideas, Liu summarises Xi's statements: the Party's leadership is the defining feature and greatest strength of socialism with Chinese characteristics, the Party leads everything "in east, west, south, north and centre", and it must be "comprehensive, systematic and holistic". Liu holds that these formulations raised understanding of Party leadership to a new level. On institutions, Liu stresses the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, then lists mechanisms: the Political Bureau Standing Committee hears annual work reports from the legislature, State Council and judicial bodies, Political Bureau members submit annual written reports, and systems of task allocation, supervision, review and accountability ensure that central decisions are carried out. On results, Liu cites full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, the eight-point regulation, anti-corruption work described as having achieved an overwhelming victory, and Party leadership across the economy, politics, culture, society, ecological civilisation, diplomacy and defence.

Liu concludes that the Central Committee's authority and unified leadership have been firmly secured, the Party's leadership system has been steadily improved, and its methods of leadership have become more scientific. Liu calls on Party members to understand the decisive significance of the Two Establishes, strengthen the "four consciousnesses" and practise the Two Upholds. Read the original if you want a compact example of how an official Party-school commentary of 2022 summarises the case for Party centralisation before the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: In sum, in the new era, upholding and strengthening the Party's overall leadership and the centralised, unified leadership of the Party Central Committee has been carried through and reflected in every field: reform, development and stability; domestic affairs, foreign affairs and defence; and governing the Party, the country and the armed forces.
quoteZh: 总之，新时代，坚持加强党的全面领导和党中央集中统一领导贯彻和体现到改革发展稳定、内政外交国防、治党治国治军各个领域各个方面。

glossary.explanation: A formula adopted in the 2021 Party history resolution. It refers to establishing Xi Jinping's status as the core of the Central Committee and the whole Party, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.

The requirement that Party members uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the whole Party, and uphold the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A strategic policy since the 18th Party Congress covering Party discipline, anti-corruption, ideological education and organisational building.
The official name for the Party's path, theory and system since the reform era.
Rules adopted by the Central Committee in December 2012 to curb extravagance, bureaucratism and formalism among officials.

t: Keeping the Party forever young and vital through self-reform
zh: 在自我革命中永葆党的青春与活力
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on the eve of the 20th Party Congress (2022), Yang Yang asks why the Communist Party of China has stayed vital after more than a century, and answers that persistent self-reform (自我革命) is the reason. The commentary takes its cue from the 2021 historical resolution adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee, which lists adherence to self-reform among the Party's valuable historical experiences. Yang also draws on Xi Jinping's recent address to provincial and ministerial leaders. Yang calls self-reform the Party's distinguishing mark, the "code" of its youthfulness and a guarantee of its leading role.

The piece is organised under three headings. The first treats self-reform as what separates the Party from every other party, and traces its theoretical lineage from Marx, Engels and Lenin through Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping to Xi Jinping. The second presents self-reform as the source of the Party's vitality, with an account of the campaigns since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third reviews the Party's history as a series of self-corrections and links self-reform to national rejuvenation.

Yang defines self-reform as a conscious process of self-sublation by the Party as subject: upholding truth, correcting errors, renewing itself and turning the blade inward. In Yang's account, an advanced Marxist party is not born but is forged through this process. Yang argues that a party able to lead a great social revolution must keep its own advanced character and purity, which means removing whatever corrodes its body. Yang credits the post-2012 measures with solving long-standing problems: theoretical education, work-style rectification, stricter discipline, tighter cadre selection and the anti-corruption drive of "tigers, flies and foxes". The article says these produced an overwhelming victory against corruption, a healthier political ecology within the Party and closer Party–people ties. It also lists earlier milestones, from the 1927 August 7 Meeting and the Zunyi Meeting to the Yan'an rectification and the "Three Stresses" campaign.

Yang concludes that the Party faces more numerous and complex risks as it enters a critical period for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, so it must never relax. Yang holds that without a Party armed with the spirit of self-reform, national rejuvenation would remain a fantasy. The author calls on readers to rally around the Central Committee with Xi at its core, apply Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and continue the new great project of Party building. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official commentary on the eve of the 20th Party Congress framed self-reform and its lineage from the Marxist classics.
quoteEn: Put plainly, self-reform means making revolution against oneself and operating with a knife on one's own problems; this is clearly hard and painful, and so above all demands courage.
quoteZh: 自我革命，通俗地讲就是“革”自己的命，对自身存在的问题“动刀”，这显然是艰难和痛苦的，所以最需要勇气。

glossary.explanation: A concept in Party discourse for the Party's own rectification, self-criticism and purification. It is often rendered officially as the Party's self-reform and became prominent under Xi Jinping.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, restoring China's strength and international standing, usually dated to the mid-twenty-first century.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.
A Hegelian-Marxist term (Aufhebung) for negating something while preserving and transcending its valuable elements. Here Yang applies it to the Party's treatment of itself.

t: Advancing under the Party's banner towards the centenary goal of the army's founding
zh: 在党的旗帜下向着建军一百年奋斗目标前进
paras: Marking the 95th anniversary of the founding of the People's Liberation Army on 1 August 2022, this commentary in the People's Daily argues that a strong country requires a strong military and that the army, under the Party's leadership, is now advancing along the path of building a strong military with Chinese characteristics. Zhao Zhouxian, a researcher at the National Defence University, presents the army's history and current agenda as guided by Xi Jinping's thought on strengthening the military and aimed at the centenary goal of 2027.

The piece has three parts. The first reviews the army's record in the revolutionary period, the early decades of the People's Republic and the era of reform and opening up. The second sets out what the author calls the historic achievements and transformations in building the military since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third turns to the tasks that Zhao says must be carried out between now and 2027.

On the historical record, Zhao credits the army with winning the revolutionary wars, building up defence science and industry (including the \"two bombs and one satellite\" programme), and providing security for reform and development. For the new era, the author identifies three levers. The first is ideological guidance, including the absolute leadership of the Party, the chairman responsibility system of the Central Military Commission and a political clean-up in which Guo Boxiong, Xu Caihou, Fang Fenghui and Zhang Yang are named. The second is top-level design: the broadest defence and military reform since 1949, a 300,000 cut in personnel, a new command structure, and the integrated development of mechanisation, informatisation and intelligentisation. The third is strategic guidance that focuses on combat readiness, legal governance of the military and the handling of external challenges, which the author says include deterring \"Taiwan independence\" separatism.

For the period to 2027, Zhao calls for upholding the Party's absolute leadership, equipping the whole army with the Party's innovative theory, and carrying out the tasks in the 14th Five-Year Plan for military building. Zhao also calls for continuing the reforms, self-reliance in science and technology, and civil–military integration, with wider national defence education and the tradition of army–people unity. The author presents these as the means to build a world-class military and to support national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want an example of the official People's Daily framing of the PLA's history and its 2027 centenary goal on the eve of the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: The 95 years of history prove beyond dispute that without a strong army there can be no strong country.
quoteZh: 95年的历史无可辩驳地证明，没有一支强大的军队，就不可能有强大的祖国。

glossary.en: Xi Jinping's thought on strengthening the military
glossary.explanation: The official body of ideas on military building associated with Xi Jinping, formulated after the 18th Party Congress (2012) and stressing the Party's absolute leadership over the armed forces and combat readiness.

glossary.pinyin: dǎng duì jūnduì de juéduì lǐngdǎo
glossary.literal: the Party's absolute leadership over the army
glossary.explanation: The principle that the armed forces are under the direct command of the Communist Party rather than the state, a long-standing principle in the official account of the PLA.

glossary.en: chairman responsibility system of the Central Military Commission
glossary.explanation: The arrangement under which the Chairman of the Central Military Commission bears overall responsibility for the armed forces; the article says it was written into the Party Constitution.

t: The "Two Establishes" in the perspective of democratic centralism
zh: 论民主集中制视阈中的“两个确立”
source: Marxist Theory Discipline Studies (马克思主义理论学科研究), 2022 no. 4
paras: Li Haiqing takes up the formula, set out in the Sixth Plenum resolution of 2021, that the Party established Xi Jinping as the core of the Central Committee and of the whole Party and established the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The article argues that the Two Establishes cannot be understood only through the circumstances and achievements of the new era. In Li's view they must be read through democratic centralism, the Party's fundamental organisational principle, and reading them otherwise invites misinterpretation.

The article has three parts. It first explains democratic centralism as a principle governing relations inside the Party. It then asks how each of the Two Establishes rests on a democratic basis. Finally it describes the organisational advantages of correct centralisation in Party governance, state governance and global governance, and closes with a short conclusion.

Li holds that democratic centralism combines centralisation on a democratic basis with democracy under centralised guidance, and that centralisation is the pivot, comparable to the brain. Because power and responsibility are concentrated level by level, the leadership core is the highest bearer of centralisation, and its theoretical output becomes the Party's guiding thought. Li describes the top level as in effect a "committee plus core" system. The first Establish is said to rest on step-by-step intra-Party election and testing, and the second on the way the thought gathers views from below and then refines them in the centralising stage, where the core's ability is decisive. Li says the Two Establishes show the system's strength in several fields. In Party governance, Li cites full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, the Party's self-reform and the 2021 document on supervising top leaders. In state governance, Li points to the "Two Centenary Goals" and systematic reform. In global governance, Li points to Chinese modernization and a community with a shared future for mankind.

Li concludes that the Two Establishes are the necessary result of centralisation on a democratic basis, resting on modern democratic politics and communist democratic values. Li also argues that a strong core and a guiding thought that is both orthodox and innovative produce institutional advantages. Further improvement of democratic centralism and effective implementation of the Two Establishes are said to help the Party meet opportunities and challenges on the new journey. Read the original if you want an example of how a Party School scholar justifies the Two Establishes in organisational and institutional terms rather than through historical achievements alone.
quoteEn: Only within the perspective of democratic centralism can the "Two Establishes" be understood fully, accurately and properly.
quoteZh: 只有在民主集中制的视阈中，“两个确立”才会得到完整、准确、到位的理解。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the Sixth Plenum resolution of 2021. It affirms Xi Jinping's position as core of the Central Committee and of the whole Party, and the guiding status of Xi Jinping Thought.
The organisational principle of the Communist Party. It combines democratic participation and election with centralised discipline and obedience to higher bodies.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Official slogan, prominent since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering discipline, anti-corruption and Party-building.
An official concept that the Party must keep correcting itself through its own internal supervision and discipline.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, presented as an alternative to Western models.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's slogan for China's vision of international relations and global governance.

t: Upholding the Communist Party of China's commitment to taking the whole world in view
zh: 坚持胸怀天下的中国共产党
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in July 2022, examines one of the historical experiences listed in the resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021): "upholding a worldwide vision" (胸怀天下). Mu argues that the resolution's formulation of this experience is an original contribution. In Mu's reading, it is at once a sense of mission, a mode of strategic thinking and a political and spiritual quality. It helps explain why the Party's century of struggle has influenced the course of world history.

The article has three parts. The first traces the sources of the commitment to Marxism and to traditional Chinese culture. The second surveys the Party's history from its founding to the present, in four stages: the revolutionary period, the early People's Republic, reform and opening up, and the years since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third sets out what the commitment requires on the "new journey".

Mu's core argument is that the Party's worldwide vision follows from the Two Integrations, that is, from combining Marxism's basic principles with excellent traditional culture. Marxism supplies the aim of human liberation, while ideas such as "all under heaven as one family" and "harmony in diversity" supply cultural roots. Mu then reads the Party's record as handling China's development and the world's progress together. Examples include the Second Congress's 1922 resolution on the world situation, the anti-fascist war, the Korean War, reform and opening up, and recent Chinese modernization, the Belt and Road Initiative and a community with a shared future for mankind. In Mu's account these have given the world Chinese wisdom, solutions and strength.

Mu concludes with three requirements for the future. The Party must study Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and keep a firm grasp of historical laws. It must take its own path, with independence and self-reliance, while learning from other countries. It must pursue peaceful development and major-country diplomacy with Chinese characteristics, building a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise official-line account of how Party historians present the Party's international outlook within its century-long narrative.
quoteEn: This also determines that the Communist Party of China is not only a party that seeks happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation, but also a party that seeks progress for humanity and universal harmony for the world.
quoteZh: 这也决定了中国共产党不仅是为中国人民谋幸福、为中华民族谋复兴的党，也是为人类谋进步、为世界谋大同的党。

glossary.explanation: A formula stressing the integration of Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. It is associated with Xi Jinping's leadership.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models. It has been prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since about 2012. It calls for shared security, development and governance.
An infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017.

glossary.literal: carrying all under heaven in one's heart
glossary.explanation: A phrase from the 2021 resolution on the Party's historical experience. It describes a commitment to humanity's progress alongside China's own development.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The Chinese Communist Party's understanding and practice of the eight-hour working day in the New Democratic Revolution period
zh: 新民主主义革命时期中国共产党对八小时工作制的认识与实践
paras: How did the Chinese Communist Party handle the eight-hour working day, a demand of the international labour movement, under Chinese revolutionary conditions? Zhang Longping argues that the Party never applied the principle mechanically. Over several decades it combined firm principle with flexibility and arrived at an eight-to-ten-hour flexible system, which Zhang reads as a concrete case of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The article follows four periods. It begins with the Party's founding and the First Revolutionary Civil War, when the eight-hour day entered Party programmes and labour congresses. It then covers the Soviet areas of the Agrarian Revolution period, the full War of Resistance against Japan, and the War of Liberation. Zhang draws on labour laws, Party directives, congress resolutions and statements by Mao Zedong, Chen Yun, Zhang Wentian, Liu Shaoqi and others. The account ends with the 1949 Common Program.

Zhang's central claim is that each adjustment answered a practical constraint without abandoning the principle. Early petitions to the Beiyang government gave way, after the failures of the early 1920s, to the view that economic struggle must become political struggle. In the Soviet areas, laws first fixed the eight-hour day rigidly. Zhang Wentian and Chen Yun criticised this as detached from reality, and the 1933 revision added exceptions for overtime and for employers of auxiliary labour. During the War of Resistance, central directives from 1940 treated stressing the eight-hour day as an excessive demand. Mao Zedong then allowed a ten-hour day, which the March 1942 Outline of Labour Policy described as a stopgap given backward, dispersed industry and wartime needs. In 1947–48 the centre criticised excessive labour conditions in newly liberated cities, including the draft Harbin labour law, as a repeat of the 'Left' errors of 1931–34.

Zhang concludes that Mao Zedong's 1945 formula of an eight-to-ten-hour day was adopted by the All-China Federation of Trade Unions in 1949 and confirmed by the Common Program, and that it continued into the early People's Republic. In Zhang's view this shows a Party that proceeds from the overall, long-term and fundamental interests of the people and links theory with practice. Read the original if you want a source-based account of Chinese labour-time policy and its Party-history justification from 1920 to 1949.
quoteEn: The Chinese Communist Party did not mechanically adhere to the basic principle of the eight-hour day, but adjusted it in good time as historical conditions changed in different periods and stages.
quoteZh: 中国共产党并不是机械地坚持八小时工作制的基本原则，而是根据不同时期、不同阶段历史条件的变化适时作出调整

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxist theory to Chinese conditions and to current tasks. The article uses the shorter phrase 'Sinification of Marxism', which has been Party language since the 1930s.
Rural revolutionary base areas where the Party set up Soviet governments in the 1930s, notably the Chinese Soviet Republic in Jiangxi from 1931.

t: The basic connotation of the international discourse power of China's new-type party system and paths to enhance it
zh: 中国新型政党制度国际话语权的基本内涵与提升路径
paras: Zang Xiuling takes up the question of how China's new-type party system can gain an international voice that matches its institutional performance. The author argues that the system has begun to break the discourse hegemony of "Western centrism" in party politics, but that its international discourse power remains weak. Zang contends that it can be raised by building on theory, culture, practice and a global mission, and through concrete changes in how the system is communicated abroad.

The article opens with a short review of existing research, which Zang groups into party theory, party-system discourse and party diplomacy. It then defines international discourse power and analyses it in four dimensions: supply, competitiveness, attractiveness and influence. After that it sets out the opportunities and challenges, the principles for improvement, and four practical paths. Zang draws on Marx, Engels, Lenin, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, Zhou Enlai and Xi Jinping.

Zang reads international discourse power as having a dual nature, a right to speak and a power to affect others, and as resting on national strength. In the author's account, Western party systems are caught in a "institutional bottleneck" of vetoing party politics, procedural democracy and social division. The new-type party system is credited with unifying leadership and cooperation, supplying an institutional carrier for whole-process people's democracy and keeping policy continuous. The main obstacles named are Western labels such as "authoritarian" and "flower vase", an official-dominated and stiff propaganda style, and academic discourse that lags behind political discourse and leans on Western concepts. Zang therefore ties each dimension of discourse power to a foundation: the Sinicization of Marxism, traditional Chinese culture, the achievements of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and a community with a shared future for mankind.

Zang proposes that the Communist Party lead with strategy and trained personnel, that the democratic parties and non-party figures speak actively, and that ordinary people and scholars take part. The author also calls for less lecturing, more languages and media, stronger online presence, and a shift from rule-follower to rule-maker in international discourse. Party diplomacy and the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference are to widen channels, with the aim of an international united front of parties friendly to China. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese scholar frames discourse strategy for the party system, and how the argument ties culture, theory and diplomacy together.
quoteEn: To solve the problem of being \"criticised\", China's new-type party system cannot be measured by the value system and evaluation standards of Western capitalism.
quoteZh: 要解决“挨骂”的问题，就不能按照西方资本主义的价值体系和评价标准来衡量中国新型政党制度

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's system of multiparty cooperation and political consultation under Communist Party leadership. It is presented as distinct from one-party, two-party and multiparty systems.
The capacity to set concepts, standards and narratives in international debate. Chinese scholars use it to describe who defines and judges political systems.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2019. It describes China's democracy as covering every stage of decision-making, not only elections.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's slogan for China's vision of international relations built on cooperation and shared interests.
The eight non-Communist parties that take part in China's political consultation under Communist Party leadership.
A consultative body that brings together the Communist Party, the democratic parties, non-party figures and other groups.

t: Drawing on the Party's history of struggle as a source of strength for keeping the original aspiration and mission in mind
zh: 从党的奋斗史中汲取牢记初心使命的力量源泉
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in July 2022, asks why the Communist Party of China has been able to keep its original aspiration and mission over a century, and how it can do so more firmly and consciously in future. Guo and Chu argue that the Party's history of struggle is a history of generations of Communists faithfully carrying out that mission, and that four sources of strength can be drawn from it.

The piece is organised as four short sections, each naming one "constant" of the Party's conduct: lofty ideals and convictions, a value orientation that puts the people first, a theoretical consciousness that keeps pace with the times, and the continuation of the Party's spiritual lineage. Each section combines historical illustration, citations of Engels, Mao Zedong and Xi Jinping, and a closing call on present-day Party members and cadres.

On ideals, the authors cite the Xiang River battle, the martyrdom of the divisional commander Chen Shuxiang and the rural teacher Zhang Guimei as examples of belief turned into action. On the people, they trace a line through the New Democratic Revolution, socialist construction, reform and opening up, and the new era, which they describe as moving from national liberation to a moderately prosperous society and now common prosperity. On theory, they hold that the Party's strength lies in continual theoretical innovation and education, from Mao through Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao to the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). On spirit, they list the Jinggangshan, Long March, Yan'an, Daqing, special-economic-zone, poverty-alleviation and anti-epidemic spirits as a lineage that began with the great founding spirit.

The authors conclude that a Party of more than 96 million members governing a country of over 1.4 billion needs a high degree of theoretical consciousness. They call for advancing the Two Integrations, arming the whole Party with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, deepening reform, promoting common prosperity, and extending the Party's spiritual lineage amid what they call great changes unseen in a century. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official Party-history commentary links the centenary narrative to current ideological education.
quoteEn: The history of the Party's struggle is a history of constantly strengthening theoretical consciousness, advancing theoretical innovation and carrying out theoretical armament.
quoteZh: 党的奋斗史，就是一部不断增强理论自觉，推进理论创新，进行理论武装的历史。

glossary.explanation: A Party slogan, stressed from 2019, referring to the Communist Party's founding aim of seeking happiness for the Chinese people and the rejuvenation of the nation.
The formula of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture, promoted in Party theory since 2021–2023.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all, emphasised in Party policy especially since 2021.
The official series of named "spirits" (such as the Long March spirit and Yan'an spirit) said to originate in the great founding spirit and to guide the Party.
A Party term for deliberate, continuous attention to theory and its innovation as a guide to practice.

t: Better grasping and applying the historical experience of the Party's century of struggle
zh: 更好把握和运用党的百年奋斗历史经验
paras: This is a speech by Xi Jinping delivered on 11 January 2022 to a special study session for principal provincial and ministerial-level leaders on implementing the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). Xi says the session aims to study the plenum's resolution on the Party's century of struggle, help cadres grasp and apply its historical experience, promote the spirit of the Party's founding, and mobilise the Party and people toward the Party's second centenary goal.

Xi organises the talk around five questions: advancing the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times; correctly grasping the principal contradiction in society and the central task; attending to strategy and tactics; keeping the Party's character as a Marxist party; and making Party-history study and education routine and long-term. Each of the first four sections begins by summarising how the plenum resolution treats the theme across successive historical periods, from the new-democratic revolution to the new era.

On theory, Xi argues that Marxism works because the Party keeps adapting it to Chinese conditions, and that it must not be treated dogmatically or pragmatically. Specific theses and policies cannot stay fixed, and one cannot mechanically apply what Marx, Engels, Lenin or earlier Party documents said. He holds that misjudging the principal contradiction can be ruinous, citing the Cultural Revolution, and that strategic errors, such as those in the fifth anti-encirclement campaign, cost far more than local ones. Strategic firmness must be joined with tactical flexibility, and local departments must carry out central decisions unconditionally while devising suitable tactics. On Party building, he gives self-reform as the second answer to escaping the historical cycle of rise and fall, after Mao's answer of supervision by the people. He says the Party represents no interest group or privileged stratum, and that anti-corruption must continue without slackening.

Xi also lists new formulations in the third historical resolution, including a revised periodisation of the new-democratic revolution, the 14-year War of Resistance dated from 1931, and the expansion of the "eight clarifications" to ten. He calls for Party-history education to be built into everyday routine through study groups, Party schools, school courses and red resources. Read the original if you want the authoritative statement of how the leadership framed the 2021 resolution and its lessons for cadres in early 2022.
quoteEn: Times are developing and the cause is advancing; we cannot simply apply what Marx, Engels and Lenin said back then to China's reality today, nor simply apply some of the specific theoretical views the Party put forward in the past, and the specific policies derived from them, to today's work.
quoteZh: 时代在发展，事业在前进，我们不能简单拿马克思、恩格斯、列宁当年所说的话来套今天的中国实际，也不能简单拿党过去提出的一些具体理论观点和由此产生的具体政策举措来套今天的工作。

glossary.explanation: A concept from Mao's "On Contradiction": the central social tension that determines the Party's central task in each period. Since the 19th Party Congress (2017) it has been defined as that between the people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development.
The official term for the Party's capacity to correct itself and purge its own problems, presented by Xi as the Party's answer to the historical cycle of rise and decline.
A resolution on Party history adopted by the Central Committee to set an authoritative assessment. The third was adopted in November 2021, after those of 1945 and 1981.

t: Moving beyond the "discourse trap"
st: How the Communist Party of China has responded to US and Western "discourse traps" over its first century, and lessons for today
zh: 超越“话语陷阱”
zhSub: 建党百年来中国共产党对美西方“话语陷阱”的应对及启示
paras: Writing in 2022, Zhang Chaoying asks how China and the Communist Party of China (CPC) can get beyond the \"discourse traps\" that the United States and the West have built around them. The article argues that these traps are systematic, ideologically driven political narratives tied to US domestic agendas and foreign strategy, not isolated remarks. In Zhang's account, the Party has answered them in three stages over its century, and today needs to renew its discourse system rather than merely rebut Western claims.

The article opens with a theoretical section on discourse, discourse power and discourse hegemony. It draws on Marx and Engels on ruling ideas, Foucault on power and discourse, and Joseph Nye on hegemony as monopoly over rules. Zhang illustrates the point with the March 2021 \"Xinjiang cotton incident\". A historical survey of Western traps follows: the \"communist red menace\" and \"collapse of China\" theories, the \"end of history\" thesis after the Soviet collapse, the comprehensive \"China threat\" theory, and, since the 2008 financial crisis, \"trap\" theories such as the \"Thucydides trap\". The third section covers the CPC's responses, and the fourth section sets out proposals.

Zhang describes the Party's response as three stages. In \"1.0\" came the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence at Bandung (1955) and Mao Zedong's \"three worlds\" theory (1974). In \"2.0\" came the mutually beneficial opening-up strategy and the path of peaceful development, which the 11th Five-Year Plan (2005) first formally set out. In \"3.0\" came the community with a shared future for mankind, written into a Party Congress report in 2012. In this reading the community with a shared future is a historic move beyond \"jungle law\" and zero-sum thinking. Zhang also draws on Engels's remark that economically backward countries can \"play first fiddle\" in philosophy, to argue that China's experience shows a less developed country can win discourse power without seeking hegemony.

Zhang concludes that passive denial reinforces the claims it rejects, so China should move from reactive to proactive speech. The article proposes three directions. The first is to build a locally rooted discourse system and an autonomous body of Chinese knowledge. The second is to strengthen professional, academic discourse and tell precise, individualised stories, citing targeted poverty alleviation and pandemic control. The third is to criticise Western-centrism and promote civilisational dialogue with the non-Western world. Read the original if you want to see how a PLA-affiliated Party-theory researcher frames the history of Western narratives about China and the CPC's discourse strategy in response.
quoteEn: Turning passive, responsive language into proactive, narrative language is the primary direction of work in renewing our discourse system.
quoteZh: 变被动的回应性语言为主动的诉说式语言是我们革新话语体系首要的工作方向。

glossary.explanation: The author's term for narratives about China and the CPC that the US and the West are said to construct deliberately to stigmatise it and build a hostile consensus.
The capacity to define, interpret and shape the terms of debate, especially in international affairs. Chinese scholarship links it to Foucault's work on discourse and power.

Principles of mutual respect for sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference, equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful coexistence. China promoted them in the 1950s, notably at the 1955 Bandung Conference.
Mao Zedong's 1974 division of the world into the superpowers, the other developed countries, and the developing countries of the Third World, which China placed itself among.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–2013, calling for shared security, common development and civilisational exchange.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Transcending the "discourse traps"
st: How the Communist Party of China has responded to US and Western "discourse traps" over the century since its founding, and what follows from it
zh: 超越“话语陷阱”
zhSub: 建党百年来中国共产党对美西方“话语陷阱”的应对及启示
paras: Zhang Chaoying asks how the Communist Party of China (CPC) has dealt, and should deal, with what the article calls the "discourse traps" set by the United States and the West. These are narratives that, in the author's account, stigmatise the Party and China to build a false "consensus" and to display Western ideological dominance. The article argues that the Party has answered such traps for a century through a series of innovative international positions, and that today China should move from reactive denial to actively building its own discourse system.

The article opens with a theoretical section on discourse, discourse power and discourse hegemony, drawing on Marx and Engels's account of ideology, Foucault and Joseph Nye. It then traces four historical "traps": the "communist red menace" and "collapse of China" theories from the Party's founding to the early People's Republic; the "end of history" thesis after the Soviet collapse; the comprehensive "China threat" theories of the 1990s and 2000s; and the "Thucydides Trap" and similar "trap" theories after the 2008 financial crisis. The 2021 "Xinjiang cotton incident" serves as the author's contemporary example of how a hegemonic narrative is manufactured.

Zhang sets out the Party's responses in three stages. Version 1.0 is the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence (1955) and Mao Zedong's "three worlds" theory. Version 2.0 is the opening-up strategy of mutual benefit and win-win results and the path of peaceful development. Version 3.0 is the call for a community with a shared future for mankind, which the author presents as a historic move beyond Western "jungle law" and zero-sum thinking. Citing Engels's remark that economically backward countries can still "play first fiddle" in philosophy, Zhang argues that China's record shows that a rising economy need not produce hegemonic ambition.

For the present, Zhang proposes three directions for renewing China's discourse system. The first is to replace passive rebuttal with proactive, positive self-expression and new concepts that connect China with other countries. The second is to build professional, academic discourse and describe China accurately and in its own terms, using stories such as targeted poverty alleviation and epidemic control. The third is to engage with a multipolar world, criticise Western-centrism and foster dialogue among civilizations. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese military-affiliated scholar periodises the Party's international discourse strategy and frames Western narratives about China as deliberate "traps".
quoteEn: Turning passive, responsive language into active, declarative language is the primary direction for renewing our discourse system.
quoteZh: 变被动的回应性语言为主动的诉说式语言是我们革新话语体系首要的工作方向。
keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Grasping the logic of strengthening Party spirit cultivation
zh: 把握加强党性修养的逻辑
paras: Why should Party members and cadres keep working on their Party spirit (dangxing)? In this commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 19 July 2022, Cao Jiangqiu argues that strengthening dangxing xiuyang, the cultivation of Party spirit, is a lifelong obligation for Communists. The author grounds this in three "logics": theoretical, historical and practical.

The piece opens with a statement by Xi Jinping that leading cadres must exercise self-discipline and check their conduct against the Party Constitution. It then takes the three logics in turn. The first draws on Marx, Engels, Lenin, Mao Zedong and Xi to define what a Marxist party is. The second surveys Party history from the Second Congress to the period after the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third looks at the international, domestic and Party situation of the early 2020s.

Cao's theoretical claim is that advancedness and purity are the essential attributes of a Marxist party, and that Party spirit and the people's character are unified: upholding one means upholding the other. The historical section lists milestones as evidence that attention to Party spirit explains the Party's endurance. These include the 1941 decision on strengthening Party spirit, the 1942 Yan'an rectification movement, and the intra-Party regulations issued since 2012. On practice, the author cites the Party's size (96.712 million members at the end of 2021) and says many young members lack experience of intra-Party political life. Cao adds that Party spirit does not rise automatically with seniority or rank, and that problems of impure thinking, politics, organization and work style persist.

Cao concludes that the more complex the domestic and international environment, the more Party spirit must be cultivated. Members are urged to treat Party education as a discipline of the heart, to understand the decisive significance of the Two Establishes, and to carry out the Two Upholds. The author presents this as the way to advance the Party's self-reform and keep the Party from degenerating. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-school scholars present Party-building doctrine, with its standard historical milestones, in mid-2022.
quoteEn: The advancedness and purity of a Marxist party are not maintained naturally as time passes. Communists' Party spirit does not rise naturally with years of membership or with promotion, and must be strengthened constantly through rigorous intra-Party life.
quoteZh: 马克思主义政党的先进性和纯洁性不是随着时间推移而自然保持下去的，共产党员的党性不是随着党龄增长而自然提高，也不会随着职务的升迁而自然提升，必须在严格的党内生活锻炼中不断增强。

glossary.explanation: The essential character of a political party, which in Chinese Communist usage covers members' ideals, loyalty, discipline and political stance. Cadres are expected to cultivate it throughout their careers.

A formula from the 6th Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and of the whole Party, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Party Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralized, unified leadership.
Official term for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself, linked to full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

t: The Communist Party of China is the most reliable backbone for achieving great undertakings
zh: 中国共产党是成就伟业最可靠的主心骨
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily in July 2022, takes its title from a statement by Xi Jinping: that the Communist Party of China is the most reliable backbone (zhuxingu) for achieving great undertakings. Yan and Wang read this as both a summary of past practice and a basic requirement for the future. They argue that, on the new journey of building a modern socialist country in all respects, the Party's centralised and unified leadership must be upheld and carried through every sphere of Party and state work.

The piece has three sections. The first presents the Party as the author of a historic achievement for the Chinese nation and for the world. The second explains why Party leadership is the 'sea-stabilising needle' of the cause. The third turns to the present and asks how to win new victories in socialist modernization under that leadership. The authors support their points with Xi's statements, one quotation from Marx on the proletariat organising as a party, and remarks by the American writers Ted Fishman and Kenneth Lieberthal.

The central argument is that Party leadership determines the nature, direction and destiny of socialism with Chinese characteristics, as well as its outlook and its capacity to meet major risks. The authors say the Party led the Chinese people through four great achievements, from the new-democratic revolution to the new era. In their account it also produced Chinese modernization, which they say broke the 'myth' that modernization means Westernization, and it revitalised world socialism after the Soviet and East European collapse. They cite China's GDP of 114 trillion yuan in 2021, about 18% of the world total, and the country's lead in contributing to global growth since 2006. They hold that the Party's leadership has been decisive in crises ranging from foreign aggression and natural disasters to the Covid-19 pandemic and pressure from the United States and the West. They also contend that some developing countries stall in modernization for lack of a strong party.

Yan and Wang conclude that the Party's comprehensive leadership of modernization must be strengthened and made to cover every area. They call on leading cadres at all levels to raise their political capacity, strategic vision and professional competence, so as to meet a more complex 'great changes unseen in a century' than earlier modernizers faced. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official commentary in 2022 tied Party leadership to modernization, global influence and crisis management.
quoteEn: Party leadership determines the nature, direction and destiny of the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 党的领导决定了中国特色社会主义事业的性质、方向和命运。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path of development under Party leadership. It is presented as an alternative to Western models of modernization.
The official designation of China's current system and path, associated with reform and opening up since 1978.
An image from the novel Journey to the West (the Monkey King's staff). It is used here to mean a steadying anchor of the whole enterprise.

t: A major work on the theory of the Party's self-reform
st: On "Self-Revolution: The Second Answer to Escaping the Historical Cycle"
zh: 研究阐释党的自我革命理论的一部力作
zhSub: 读《自我革命：跳出历史周期率的第二个答案》
paras: This is a book review, published in Guangming Daily in July 2022, of Self-Revolution: The Second Answer to Escaping the Historical Cycle, written by Zhen Zhanmin and others and published by People's Publishing House. Reviewer Shen Chuanbao presents the book as a first-rate study of Xi Jinping's statements on the Party's self-reform. In Shen's view it explores how self-reform relates to escaping the "historical cycle" of rise and decline.

The book treats the theory of self-reform in eight parts: its scientific meaning, theoretical basis, successful practice, historical experience, main challenges, ethical consciousness, systemic framework and strategic guidelines. Shen organises the review around four qualities the book is said to have: it is systematic, scholarly, practical and innovative.

On the first two points, Shen argues that earlier scholarship mostly analysed individual assertions, whereas this book builds a fairly complete analytical framework. It also starts from concepts and compares existing definitions. It then defines self-reform in four dimensions: spirit, practice, theory and politics. Its theoretical grounds are drawn from philosophy, political science and cultural studies. On practice, Shen notes the book's chapter on the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It covers Party building and the anti-corruption struggle, and the role of intra-Party regulations. It holds that theoretical, action-based and institutional consciousness must work together, which in Shen's account yields the second answer to the historical cycle.

Shen credits the book with a fresh topic, new formulations such as six \"unities\" of experience, and up-to-date data from the 2022 plenary session of the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection. It also proposes a four-dimension system of goal, motivation, conduct and evaluation, and stresses ethical self-awareness. Shen's assessment is wholly favourable. Read the original if you want a brief, Party-affiliated reading of how this book frames self-reform theory in the 2022 discussion.
quoteEn: Taking self-reform as its theme and aiming to answer how to escape the historical cycle, the book has a topic rich in novelty.
quoteZh: 该书以自我革命为主题，着眼于回答如何跳出历史周期率，选题富有新意。

glossary.explanation: A concept that Xi Jinping has stressed since 2012. It refers to the Communist Party's capacity to purify, improve and renew itself through rigorous internal discipline and anti-corruption work.

glossary.literal: jumping out of the historical cycle rate
glossary.explanation: Refers to the pattern of dynastic rise and decline. Huang Yanpei raised it with Mao Zedong in 1945, and Mao answered that democracy was the way out. Party texts now add self-reform as a 'second answer'.

t: The Party's overall leadership profoundly shapes the political advantages of whole-process people's democracy
zh: 党的全面领导深刻塑造全过程人民民主政治优势
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily in July 2022, asks why Chinese democracy can be described as covering the "whole process". Chai and Li argue that the Party's overall leadership is the deep driving force behind the political advantages of whole-process people's democracy. They say it supplies the fundamental political guarantee and the direction for building a broader and more effective operating system of democracy.

The article is organised in five sections. Four of them examine how Party leadership works: it keeps the people's will present in every link of the process, turns institutional strengths into governance effectiveness, provides the political foundation for implementation, and strengthens the supervision and restraint of power. The last section places the model in the wider context of human political civilisation. Throughout, the authors contrast the Chinese practice with Western capitalist democracy, which they describe as limited to voting.

In the authors' account, Western democracy replaces broad participation with episodic voting, and its checks and balances produce money politics, elite politics and a "veto politics" of reflexive opposition. Whole-process people's democracy instead builds the Party's people-centred stance into a full chain of democratic election, consultation, decision-making, management and oversight. The authors say this chain is supported by the Party's leadership system and the mass line. They draw on Engels's essay "On Authority" to argue that modern society requires political authority, and that the Party's leadership combines democracy with authority. In their view, this lowers the costs of democratic procedures, helps manage social disagreement and brings the separate mechanisms together. They add that the Party shapes the oversight system, so that Party supervision drives supervision in other fields.

Chai and Li conclude that Party leadership gives whole-process people's democracy a supreme moral basis, scientific theoretical guidance, a deep mass base and a tight organisational structure. They present it as a new form of democratic civilisation distinct from the West, one that offers "Chinese wisdom" and a "Chinese approach" to political civilisation and strengthens China's international democratic discourse power. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Chinese commentary in 2022 tied the Party's leadership to the claimed superiority of Chinese democracy over Western models.
quoteEn: The Party's overall leadership is itself the product of an organic combination of democracy and authority.
quoteZh: 党的全面领导本身即为民主与权威有机结合的产物

glossary.explanation: A concept presented by Xi Jinping in 2019 and later made central to official accounts of Chinese democracy. It holds that democracy extends beyond voting to cover election, consultation, decision-making, management and oversight.

The principle that the Communist Party leads all fields of work, including state, society, the economy and the military. It is treated in official discourse as the most essential feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
A Party method of work associated with Mao Zedong. It calls for gathering the views of the people, refining them and returning them as policy.

t: Integrating Party history study and education into daily life and making it routine
zh: 把党史学习教育融入日常、抓在经常
paras: This short commentary in Guangming Daily (July 2022) takes up Xi Jinping's January 2022 instruction that a single campaign is not enough to make the whole Party study and use Party history well. Yuwen argues that Party history education must be made routine and long-term, and that this is important for consolidating the Party's leadership and strengthening Party building in the new era.
The article first explains the purpose of studying Party history, then sets out the institutional mechanisms needed to make the study permanent, and ends with the wider attitudes required.

Yuwen holds that studying history is meant to clarify principles, strengthen confidence and raise political awareness, so that Party members do not forget the Party's founding mission. The article puts study and implementation of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era first. It lists five mechanisms: the study system of Party committee theory study groups; cadre education and training, with Party history as a compulsory and regular course in Party schools; ideological and political courses in schools; education using red resources; and the practice of 'doing practical things for the people'.

Yuwen concludes that institutional rules are the key to removing obstacles to regular study. The author also calls for a lasting, lifelong and whole-course concept of learning, so that results show in Party members' and cadres' practical work toward building a modern socialist country. Read the original if you want a brief, official-line account of how Party history education is meant to be institutionalised after the 2021 campaign.
quoteEn: The key to making Party history study and education routine and long-term is to make full use of institutions and mechanisms to set standards and establish norms to be followed.
quoteZh: 推进党史学习教育常态化长效化，关键是要充分运用体制机制的力量加强规范、形成遵循

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sixiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.en: doing practical things for the people
glossary.literal: I do practical things for the masses
glossary.explanation: A practice campaign linked to the 2021 Party history education, in which Party members and cadres were asked to address concrete problems of ordinary people.
Revolutionary sites, relics and cultural materials associated with the Party's history, used for patriotic and political education.

t: Keeping the clarity and purity proper to young cadres
zh: 永葆年轻干部应有的清澈和纯粹
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in July 2022, takes up Xi Jinping's call at the centenary of the Communist Youth League for young cadres to show "clarity and purity" (qingche and chuncui). Xu Huixia argues that these qualities are a long-standing Chinese and communist ideal, and that they now have a concrete content and a practical route of cultivation for young cadres.

The article has two parts. The first traces the meaning of the two words through classical Chinese texts and through remarks by Marx, Lenin and Mao Zedong on the purity of the Party and of communists. It then sets out what Xi Jinping has required of young cadres since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second part proposes four ways of cultivating these qualities under the heading of the "new journey".

Xu identifies five elements of clarity and purity: firm ideals and convictions as their soul; loyalty to the Party as their foundation; a work style of taking responsibility and striving; integrity and self-discipline as their bottom line; and the original aspiration of serving the people as their essence. For cultivation, Xu calls for study of the Party's theory and the "four histories" to replenish the "spiritual calcium". Xu also calls for loyalty grounded in the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, for pioneering and courage to take on responsibility, and for caution in the use of power. Finally, Xu stresses the mass line and fieldwork at the grassroots.

Xu concludes that only by keeping clarity and purity can young cadres contribute to the second centenary goal and to a better China. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party-building discourse in 2022 frames the qualities expected of young cadres.
quoteEn: Its soul lies in unshakeable ideals and convictions.
quoteZh: 其灵魂在于坚定不移的理想信念。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the 2021 Party resolution on history. It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and of the whole Party, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised leadership of the Party Central Committee.
A Party principle of working "from the masses, to the masses", associated with Mao Zedong. It requires cadres to consult ordinary people and serve their interests.
A study programme covering the history of the Communist Party, of the People's Republic, of reform and opening up, and of the development of socialism.

t: Advancing full and rigorous self-governance of the Party in depth with the spirit of self-reform
zh: 以自我革命精神把全面从严治党向纵深推进
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in July 2022, Yang Jinwei takes up how the Communist Party of China should sustain its vitality as it pursues the second centenary goal. The commentary argues that full and rigorous self-governance of the Party is the Party's great practice of self-reform in the new era. In Yang's account, it must be pushed further in depth through a firm spirit of self-reform.
