The piece is organised in three parts. The first presents self-governance as the practice of self-reform since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second claims it has opened a new realm of self-reform for a century-old Party. The third sets out how to advance it in depth. Yang draws throughout on statements by Xi Jinping and on the 2021 Party resolution on its century of struggle.

Yang treats the willingness to carry out self-reform as the Party's most distinctive trait and greatest strength. The article cites a historical sequence from the 1927 Emergency Meeting, the Gutian and Zunyi meetings and the Yan'an rectification to the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978). In this reading, repeated corrections let the Party turn crises around. Since 2012, Yang says, the Central Committee has confronted the "four tests", the "four dangers" and the "four impurities", starting with the eight-point regulations. Yang credits it with a decisive victory in the anti-corruption struggle and a stronger oversight system, and reads this as the "second answer" to the historical cycle of rise and fall. Yang also stresses that the Party has no special interests of its own and represents the fundamental interests of the people.

Yang calls for upholding the Party's overall leadership and for treating loyalty to the Central Committee as the first task of political building. Party members are to grasp the Two Establishes, strengthen the four consciousnesses and carry out the Two Upholds. Yang further proposes keeping strictness as the long-term keynote, with thought, oversight, discipline, cadre management, conduct and anti-corruption work all kept strict, and pursuing the aim that officials dare not, cannot and do not want to be corrupt. Read the original if you want a compact example of how the Party's official press framed self-reform and Party discipline in mid-2022.
quoteEn: Only by turning the blade inward and carrying out self-reform, always insisting that the Party must govern itself and do so fully and rigorously, and by continually forging the Party in a revolutionary way with a high degree of political, theoretical, ideological and practical consciousness, can the Party's long-term rule be secured and the great social revolution kept moving forward.
quoteZh: 只有刀刃向内、自我革命，始终坚持党要管党、全面从严治党，以高度的政治自觉、理论自觉、思想自觉、行动自觉不断对党进行革命性锻造，才能确保和实现党长期执政，才能推动伟大社会革命不断向前。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: The slogan for the Party-building drive launched under Xi Jinping after 2012. It combines discipline, ideological education, institution-building and the anti-corruption campaign.
A formula from the 2021 Party resolution. It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.

t: The people are the Party's greatest source of confidence in governing and building the country
zh: 人民是党执政兴国的最大底气
paras: This short commentary, published in the People's Daily in July 2022, takes up the principle of 'putting the people first', one of the ten historical lessons in the Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience adopted by the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). Yang argues that the people are the Party's root, lifeblood and strength, and hence its greatest source of confidence in governing and building the country.

The piece moves from the Party's founding mission to its history and then to the role of the people in making history. It draws on Xi Jinping's statements and on the Communist Manifesto, and it surveys the Party's record from its founding through the founding of the People's Republic and reform and opening up to the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Yang contends that the people's standpoint is the Party's fundamental political position and what distinguishes a Marxist party from others. Quoting the Manifesto's contrast between minority movements and the proletarian movement of the immense majority, Yang says the Party has escaped the pursuit of narrow interests and set itself the original aspiration and mission of securing the people's wellbeing and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Yang names close ties with the masses as the Party's greatest political strength and estrangement from them as its greatest danger once in power. The mass line is described as the Party's lifeline. Yang cites the achievement of a moderately prosperous society for over 1.4 billion people and the development of whole-process people's democracy as evidence.

Yang concludes that on the new journey the Party will keep to the people's standpoint, respect their initiative and draw on their creativity to achieve new accomplishments. Yang presents this as following from the historical-materialist view that the people drive history. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party commentary presents the people-centred principle in the 2021 historical resolution.
quoteEn: The Party's greatest political strength is close ties with the masses; its greatest danger after taking power is becoming divorced from them.
quoteZh: 党的最大政治优势是密切联系群众，党执政后的最大危险是脱离群众。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2019 and used to describe China's political system as involving popular participation at every stage, not only at elections.

A Party working method associated with Mao Zedong, summarised as 'from the masses, to the masses'. The Party gathers popular views, turns them into policy and then carries the policy back to the people.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: An official goal of national revival, in which the Party presents its mission as restoring China's strength and standing.

Official phrase for the Party's founding purpose, stated as seeking the wellbeing of the Chinese people and the rejuvenation of the nation. It was emphasised in the 2019 campaign on staying true to it.
An official goal of a moderate level of prosperity for all. The Party declared it achieved nationwide in 2021.

t: The Communist Party of China's persistent self-reform: historical course and lessons
zh: 中国共产党坚持自我革命的历史进程及经验启示
source: Marxist Theory Discipline Research (《马克思主义理论学科研究》), 2022 no. 6
paras: Taking its cue from the 2021 Party resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience over the past century, which lists "adhering to self-reform" among the Party's valuable experiences, Duan Yan examines how the Communist Party of China has practised the Party's self-reform since its founding. The article argues that courage to uphold truth and correct errors, self-criticism, purging its own ranks and building institutions have together made self-reform the Party's most distinctive political quality and advantage.

The article is a chronological survey in four periods: the New Democratic Revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics. A final section draws four lessons for the present. Duan cites Party resolutions, campaigns and meetings as evidence, from the August 7 Meeting and the Zunyi Meeting to the 1981 historical resolution and the Party's regulations since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

For the revolutionary years, Duan stresses struggle against Right and "Left" deviations, the Gutian Conference, the Yan'an rectification movement and the establishment of Party schools. After 1949 the focus is on rectification campaigns, the "Three-Antis" movement and criticism and self-criticism, including Mao Zedong's self-criticism at the 1962 enlarged work conference. In the reform era Duan highlights the restoration of discipline inspection bodies, anti-corruption work under Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao, and the 1978 truth-criterion debate. Since 2012, Duan points to new forms of Party-wide education campaigns and a growing body of Party regulations, together with a "zero tolerance" approach to enforcement.

Duan draws four lessons: put the people first and accept their supervision; strengthen ideals and convictions through Marxist theoretical education, including Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era; push anti-corruption work deeper, building mechanisms so that officials do not dare, are unable and do not want to be corrupt; and rely on institutions and Party regulations to make self-reform lasting. In Duan's view, this path of using self-reform to drive social revolution will sustain full and rigorous self-governance of the Party on the road to the second centenary goal. Read the original if you want a chronological, officially aligned account of how Party historiography presents self-reform from the 1920s to the 2020s.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China has forged a successful path of using self-reform to drive social revolution.
quoteZh: 中国共产党走出了一条以自我革命推动社会革命的成功路径。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed in Party discourse, especially under Xi Jinping, for the Party's capacity to correct its own errors, discipline members and purify its ranks without external pressure.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan of the Xi Jinping era covering anti-corruption, discipline, ideological education and the building of Party regulations.

glossary.literal: rectifying the style of work campaign
glossary.explanation: Party-wide campaigns of study, criticism and self-criticism to correct ideological and work-style errors. The best known is the Yan'an rectification movement of 1941–1945.
A long-standing Party practice in which members openly criticise others and examine their own faults, presented as a means of unity and improvement.
Formal rules issued by the Party for its own organisation and members, such as the disciplinary regulations and the supervision regulations.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Correctly distinguishing socialism with Chinese characteristics in the CPC's century of history
st: A rebuttal of several "equation theories" about socialism with Chinese characteristics
zh: 正确辨析中国共产党百年史上的中国特色社会主义
zhSub: 中国特色社会主义若干“等式论”驳议
paras: Wang Gang takes up a set of claims, at home and abroad, that socialism with Chinese characteristics has fundamentally 'changed colour' and is really something else. The article calls these 'equation theories' and argues that they stem from ideological bias, neoliberalism and historical nihilism. Its thesis is that socialism with Chinese characteristics equals none of the four things it is said to be, and that it is, first of all, socialism.

The article is organised in four sections, each rebutting one alleged equation: with capitalism with Chinese characteristics, with state capitalism, with democratic socialism, and with Confucian socialism. It draws on Marx, Engels, Lenin, Stalin, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping. It also traces the history of the concepts involved, including state capitalism in Soviet Russia and early People's Republic China, and the shift in names from social democracy to democratic socialism and back.

On capitalism, Wang argues that equating planned economy with socialism and market economy with capitalism originated with Stalin and was later absorbed in China. After the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978), Deng treated plan and market as instruments rather than system categories. Wang adds that public ownership remains dominant and the state economy holds key sectors. On state capitalism, Wang follows Lenin's distinction: under proletarian power it is a restricted, instrumental form serving the transition to socialism, so Western use of the label confuses appearance with essence. On democratic socialism, Wang finds three basic differences from socialism with Chinese characteristics: guiding ideology (pluralism versus Marxism), the view of democracy (rejecting versus upholding the people's democratic dictatorship), and ownership (private ownership tolerated versus public ownership). On Confucian socialism, Wang holds that Marxism spread in China because it was scientific truth and met practical need, not because of Confucianism. Traditional terms such as 'moderately prosperous society' have been given new meanings, and the Party's promotion of traditional culture is selective, not a restoration of Confucianism.

Wang concludes that socialism with Chinese characteristics upholds the basic principles of scientific socialism while giving them Chinese features. In this reading, the 'Chinese characteristics' must not erase the socialist character, and the 'equation theories' ultimately aim to remove the leadership of the Communist Party. Wang also warns against overstating its universality, since it is neither a template from the classics nor a copy of other countries' practice. Read the original if you want a detailed Party-theory rebuttal of the claims that China is state-capitalist, social-democratic or Confucian-socialist, with its use of Lenin and Deng.
quoteEn: Here, we must not let the "Chinese characteristics" obliterate the "socialist" nature of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 在这里，我们不能因为“中国特色”而抹杀中国特色社会主义的“社会主义”属性

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's theory and system of socialism, associated with Deng Xiaoping's reform era. The Party presents it as Marxism applied to China's conditions.

The official definition of China's state system: democracy for the people and dictatorship over hostile forces. Mao Zedong formulated it, and it is presented as the Chinese form of the dictatorship of the proletariat.
A term from the classic Book of Rites, adopted by Deng Xiaoping as a development goal. The Party uses it for a society with basic material comfort.

t: A century of grassroots Party building by the Communist Party of China and its lessons
zh: 中国共产党基层党建的百年实践与启示
paras: Jia Gangtao and Gao Hongbo, writing in Guangming Daily in July 2022, ask what a century of work at the grassroots of the Communist Party of China offers for Party building today. Their thesis is that attention to the grassroots has been a 'glorious tradition' of the Party and a precondition of its growth. In their account, it ensures that central decisions reach 'the last mile' and strengthens the Party's base for governing. The newspaper commentary draws on Xi Jinping's statements on grassroots organisations.

The article has two parts. The first surveys grassroots Party building by period: the New Democratic Revolution under Mao Zedong, the early People's Republic and the Eighth Party Congress, the reform era under Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao, and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second turns to the present and sets out requirements for Party building in the new era, with examples of organisational and institutional innovation.

For each period the authors link grassroots work to the Party's guiding ideas of the time. Examples are Bolshevisation and the 'great new project' of Party building, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development, and, after 2012, the mass line campaign, the 'Three Stricts and Three Honests' and the 'Two Studies, One Doing' education drives. For today they name four requirements: arming Party members with theory, including the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds; full and rigorous self-governance of the Party; raising 'organisational strength' (zuzhili); and institution-building. They cite Party regulations for rural areas, state-owned enterprises and universities. They also cite innovations such as branches 'built on the industrial chain' or 'on the front line of epidemic prevention', 'Internet Plus Party building' and 'Party building plus grids'.

The authors conclude that grassroots organisations are the Party's 'nerve endings' and the 'foundation' of its governing edifice. They hold that the Party should draw on its historical experience, innovate in methods, let Party building lead social governance, and never relax its grassroots work. They present this as a basis for building a modern socialist country. Read the original if you want a concise official-style periodisation of grassroots Party building and the main lines of its current policy priorities.
quoteEn: Grassroots Party organisations are the 'nerve endings' of the Party's body and also the 'foundation' of the edifice of its rule.
quoteZh: 基层党组织是党的肌体的“神经末梢”，也是党执政大厦的“地基”。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan prominent since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering discipline, anti-corruption and Party-building measures. It is presented as one of the 'Four Comprehensives'.
A formula from the 2021 Party resolution on history. It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the 'core' of the Party and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold the authority of General Secretary Xi Jinping as core of the Party and the centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.

A term used since around 2017 for the capacity of Party organisations to mobilise members and the public and carry out tasks. Official texts treat raising it as the focus of grassroots Party building.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Understanding the great founding spirit of the Party as the "wellspring" of the Party's spirit
zh: 深入理解伟大建党精神是党的“精神之源”
paras: Published in Guangming Daily on the eve of the Party's 101st anniversary, this commentary takes up Xi Jinping's description of the great founding spirit of the Party as the "wellspring" of the Party's spirit. Qi Biao argues that the formulation explains both the Party's century of achievement and the source from which its other great spirits flow. The author holds that studying this source in the light of how the Party's spirit formed and developed helps to carry on the "red bloodline" and supplies spiritual momentum for building a modern socialist country and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article has three sections. The first examines how the founding spirit took shape, the second its relation to the Party's spiritual lineage, and the third what the Party should do to preserve its roots. Qi draws on Xi's remarks at sites such as the Peking University Red Building, Fengze Garden, the venue of the First Party Congress and the South Lake in Jiaxing. The text ends with a quotation from Li Dazhao on the revival of "Young China".

Qi's core argument is that the founding spirit gathers several tributaries: Marxism and its revolutionary spirit, the great national spirit built up over millennia, and the experience of modern revolutionary pioneers. It was present when the Party was founded, even though it was systematically summarised only in 2021. The author then identifies five features in how the Party's spiritual lineage is passed on: multiple bearers, from early pioneers to Party organisations and the masses; varied forms, from the Jinggangshan spirit to the anti-epidemic spirit; richer and more innovative content, as in the Soviet Area spirit or the poverty-alleviation spirit; era-specific themes in each historical period; and a highly stable "gene" of original aspiration and mission. In this account the founding spirit is the red thread running through all of them.

Qi concludes that confidence in the Party's future rests on its character as a vanguard with no interests of its own, on its historical mission, and on its attention to history and tradition. The author calls for keeping up the spirit of "revolution plus desperate effort" and for not abandoning frugality, struggle and caution, and presents Party history study and the "four histories" education as means to this end. Qi presents carrying on the Party's spirit as essential both to the Party's vitality and to national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want an official-academic account of how the Party's spiritual lineage is framed in the run-up to the 20th Party Congress year.
quoteEn: In a certain sense, the construction of the Party's spiritual lineage is a continuous inheritance and development of the great founding spirit of the Party.
quoteZh: 从一定意义上说，党的精神谱系构筑就是对伟大建党精神不断进行的继承和发展。

glossary.en: great founding spirit of the Party
glossary.explanation: A formula set out by Xi Jinping in his speech on the Party's centenary on 1 July 2021: upholding truth and ideals, staying true to the original aspiration and mission, fearing no sacrifice and fighting bravely, and being loyal to the Party and the people. It is presented as the source of the Party's other spirits.

The official term for the series of named 'spirits' (Jinggangshan, Long March, Yan'an and others) that the Party says it has built up since its founding. It is used to present Party history as a continuous moral tradition.

A phrase in Party discourse for seeking happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation. It was prominent in the 2019 campaign 'Staying true to the original aspiration and keeping the mission in mind'.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central goal of Party narrative since the early 2010s, referring to restoring China to national strength and prosperity after the 'century of humiliation'.
Party history, the history of New China, the history of reform and opening up, and the history of the development of socialism. They are the subjects of an education campaign launched in 2020–21.

keywords: great founding spirit of the Party

t: "Opening, continuation, turn, conclusion": one way to understand the great founding spirit of the Party
zh: “起承转合”：理解伟大建党精神的一个视角
paras: This newspaper commentary, published on the Party's anniversary in 2022, asks how the official formulation of the great founding spirit of the Party can be read as a coherent whole. Jiang Youfu argues that its eight phrases and 32 characters form four tiers that follow the classical Chinese compositional pattern of qi-cheng-zhuan-he (opening, continuation, turn, conclusion).

The article takes the four tiers in turn. Each is paired with one couplet of the formulation: upholding truth and ideals; putting the original aspiration into practice and shouldering the mission; fearing no sacrifice and fighting bravely; and being loyal to the Party and true to the people.

Jiang reads the first couplet as the historical and logical starting point: Marxist truth and the communist ideal are the ideological precondition of the Party, and truth and ideal are two sides of one thing. The second couplet makes them concrete as the original aspiration and mission, which the author describes as seeking happiness for the Chinese people and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, realised through successive historical paths. The third extends this into courage in struggle, which Jiang says matters in the new era because upholding socialism with Chinese characteristics is a hard social revolution. The fourth gathers the rest: loyalty to the Party, which the author ties to upholding the Central Committee's centralised leadership, is presented as consistent with the Party's people-centred stance.

Jiang concludes that this structure shows the founding spirit to be the source of the Party's spirit and foundational to its century of struggle. The author adds that it also serves as a practical guide for building a modern socialist country and achieving national rejuvenation, and calls for full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Read the original if you want a short example of how official Party-history discourse explains the logic of the founding spirit.
quoteEn: Truth without ideals is empty; ideals without truth are blind.
quoteZh: 真理离开理想则空，理想离开真理则盲。

glossary.en: great founding spirit of the Party
glossary.explanation: A formulation stated by Xi Jinping in 2021, around the Party's centenary, summarising the spirit of the Party's founding period in 32 characters. It is treated as the source of the Party's later revolutionary spirit.
A Party slogan for its founding purpose: to seek happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, central to Party discourse since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party-discipline and anti-corruption drive promoted since 2012, aimed at keeping the Party disciplined and cohesive.
The official name for China's path of socialist development since reform and opening up.

t: On the contemporary construction of the correct view of Party history
zh: 论正确党史观的当代建构
source: Marxist Studies (《马克思主义研究》), 2022 no. 3
paras: Writing in 2022, on the eve of the 20th Party Congress, Xu Chengfang asks why and how a "correct view of Party history" should be built. The term was first put forward by Xi Jinping in February 2021 and repeated in the explanation of the third historical resolution that November. Xu argues that building this view is a continuing process with three linked parts: a theoretical core, a political subject and a social foundation. It is needed to counter historical nihilism and to anchor socialist ideology.

The article opens with the necessity and significance of the project. It cites four reasons: opposing historical nihilism, giving the ideology a base, strengthening historical consciousness and confidence, and the project's domestic and international significance. Three sections then follow. The first sets out the content of the view, the second the groups who must hold it (leading cadres, all Party members and the people), and the third the social supports: the internet, exhibition venues and theme parks, organisational systems and the economic base.

Xu's central claim is that the view's theoretical core rests on Marxist philosophy, above all historical materialism, and takes its authoritative form in the three historical resolutions (1945, 1981, 2021). The third resolution is described as having five components. These are an affirmative overall judgement, the theoretical leaps of Marxism's adaptation to Chinese conditions, a summary of the four great achievements, and ten lessons. It also includes the evaluation of past errors, such as the Cultural Revolution, and a forward-looking section, with the Two Establishes as a highlight. Xu draws on Mao's critique of Dean Acheson's idealist history and on the Soviet case. In Xu's reading, the Soviet Party's split over its history, after the distortions of the Short Course, contributed to its collapse.

Xu concludes that the correct view of Party history assesses the past, confirms the present and opens the future. It lays a political and ideological basis for the 20th Party Congress and reflects the Party's maturity. The author calls for lasting study of Party history among senior cadres, "cultivation" of the view in all members, and its popularisation through new media and the economy. Read the original if you want a detailed account of how Party theorists in 2022 framed the third historical resolution and the fight against historical nihilism as a programme of ideological construction.
quoteEn: The correct view of Party history is not the product of pure speculative deduction or logical reasoning, but a system of ideas built on the achievements and lessons of the Party's hundred years of struggle in practice.
quoteZh: 正确党史观不是纯粹思想推演、逻辑思辨的产物，而是建立在党的百年奋斗实践的成就和经验教训基础上的观念体系。

glossary.explanation: A term Xi Jinping put forward in 2021 for the approved way of understanding the history of the Communist Party. It stresses the mainstream and essence of that history and opposes what officials call historical nihilism.
In official usage, a label for interpretations that deny or belittle the Party's history, its leaders and its achievements. The Party treats it as an ideological threat.
Three Central Committee resolutions (1945, 1981, 2021) that give the Party's authoritative assessment of its own history and of key events and figures.

A formula from the 2021 resolution. It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and the whole Party, and the guiding status of Xi Jinping Thought, as of decisive significance.

t: On the new journey we must uphold the Party's overall leadership
zh: 新征程上必须坚持党的全面领导
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Economic Daily on 30 June 2022 shortly before the 20th Party Congress, argues that the Party's overall leadership must be upheld on the new journey towards national rejuvenation. Wang's thesis is that this leadership is the decisive factor behind China's historical achievements and institutional strengths.

The piece has four sections. It reviews a century of Party struggle, presents Party leadership as the key to the advantages of China's system, explains why the authority of the Party Central Committee and its centralized, unified leadership must be defended, and ends on the Two Upholds.

Wang contends that since the Opium War the goal of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation has organised all Party struggle, and that without the Party there would be no new China. Party leadership is called the greatest advantage of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and the condition for the other advantages, including the basic economic system, the Two Unwaverings and common prosperity. The Central Committee is likened to the commanding piece in a game of chess, and obedience to it is to be unconditional. Wang adds that this authority is concrete, and starts with upholding Xi Jinping's core position.

Wang concludes that the Two Establishes were the choice of history, the times and the people. Cadres should strengthen the Four Consciousnesses, hold to the Four-sphere Confidence and practise the Two Upholds. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars framed the case for centralized leadership just before the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Party leadership is the greatest advantage of the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 党的领导是中国特色社会主义制度的最大优势。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central goal of Party discourse: restoring China to national strength and prosperity after the 'century of humiliation' that began in 1840.
Formula from the 2021 Party resolution on history: establishing Xi Jinping's core position on the Central Committee and in the Party, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralized, unified leadership of the Party Central Committee.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The policy of unwaveringly consolidating the public sector and unwaveringly supporting the non-public sector.
A goal of prosperity shared by all, which Party discourse treats as a defining feature of socialism.
Political consciousness, awareness of the overall situation, awareness of the core, and alignment with the Party's line, required of Party members.

t: Research on the Party's governing discourse and the construction of philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics
zh: 党的执政话语研究与中国特色哲学社会科学建构
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in June 2022, Qi Weiping argues that studying the Communist Party of China's governing discourse (zhizheng huayu) is an important task in building philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics. Qi presents it as a duty of Chinese scholars to condense the Party's governing narrative into Chinese concepts and to "tell the story" of the Party's rule well. The piece takes its cue from Xi Jinping's speech at the centenary of the Party's founding and his call to build Chinese discourse and narrative systems.

The article is organised in four parts. It first calls for greater theoretical rigour in research on governing discourse, then examines how that discourse was formed, from the revolutionary period to the present. It then lists a series of innovations in governing discourse since the 18th Party Congress (2012), and ends with the need to strengthen the discourse's communication at home and abroad.

Qi's central claim is that governing discourse is both a political and a cultural phenomenon, resting on identifiable concepts, categories and logic, and should be studied with linguistics, political science, communication studies and organisational behaviour. In Qi's account, it took shape from the local governing experience of the Jiangxi-based Soviet regime and the Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region, through the People's Republic's "serve the people" formulations, to new expressions under Xi. Qi identifies six areas of new-era innovation: upholding Party leadership, the original aspiration and mission, preserving the Party's vanguard character and purity, modernization of the system and capacity of national governance, goals of national development such as the Chinese Dream and Chinese modernization, and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

Qi concludes that scholars must also raise the communicative power of this discourse, since discourse gains vitality only through effective dissemination. Qi calls for research on communication mechanisms, media platforms, responsible actors, innovation in methods and platforms for international communication, linking this to the claim that China's economic growth and long-term stability demonstrate the effectiveness of Party rule. Read the original if you want an example of how a Party-affiliated scholar frames governing discourse as a research field and a task for Chinese social science.
quoteEn: Discourse gains vitality through wide dissemination and gains persuasive force through effective dissemination.
quoteZh: 话语以广泛传播而获得生命力，以有效传播而产生感染力。

glossary.explanation: The language and concepts through which the ruling Party expresses why it governs, what it aims to do and how. The article treats it as a distinct object of academic study.

glossary.zh: 中国特色哲学社会科学
glossary.en: philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics
glossary.explanation: A project, stressed by Xi Jinping since 2012, to build Chinese-style guiding thought and disciplinary, academic and discourse systems in the humanities and social sciences.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's disciplinary and organisational campaign to strengthen itself, prominent since 2012.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, presented as distinct from Western models.
A slogan Xi Jinping introduced in 2012 for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

keywords: philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics

t: The practical path for the Communist Party of China to meet risks and tests through self-reform in the new era
zh: 新时代中国共产党以自我革命应对风险考验的现实路径
paras: How should the Communist Party of China deal with the risks and tests it faces in the new era? Writing in 2022, Duan Yan answers that the Party must rely on self-reform, which the article calls its most distinctive quality and greatest strength. Following Xi Jinping, Duan presents self-reform as the Party's second answer to the question of how to escape the historical cycle of rise and fall, and as the key to moving from victory to victory.

The article is organised around the four long-term tests named in Xi Jinping's formulation: the test of holding power, the test of reform and opening up, the test of the market economy, and the test of the external environment. Each test is matched to a field of Party building: ideological and organisational purity, institutions and the constraint of power, leadership of the socialist market economy, and theoretical armament and innovation. Each section first describes the problems Duan sees and then sets out measures.

Duan's argument has three main strands. On long-term rule, the author lists weak ideals, lax organisational life and formalism, and calls for stricter admission and exit of members, stricter organisational routines and cadres selected by political standards. On reform and opening up, Duan stresses Party regulations built around the Party Constitution, democratic centralism, criticism and self-criticism, combined internal and mass supervision, and continued anti-corruption work. On the market, the author argues that Party leadership should use, regulate and steer capital, set "traffic lights" for it, uphold the basic economic system, extend supervision to all public officials, and build a "close and clean" relationship between government and business.

On the fourth test, Duan holds that the basic path is to study Marxism and its Sinicised theoretical achievements, including Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, through regular education campaigns. The author also calls for the Two Integrations, joining Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The article concludes that this self-reform keeps the Party advanced and capable amid great changes at home and abroad. Read the original if you want a systematic statement of how official Party-building discourse links self-reform to specific institutional and ideological measures.
quoteEn: Self-reform is the second answer the Communist Party of China has given in the new era to the question of how to escape the historical cycle, and it provides the winning weapon for the Party to overcome risks and challenges and move from victory to victory.
quoteZh: 自我革命是新时代中国共产党对探索如何跳出历史周期率给出的第二个答案，为党战胜风险挑战、从胜利不断走向新胜利提供了制胜法宝。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed by Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012): the Party's capacity to identify and correct its own problems without outside pressure. It is usually rendered officially as the Party's self-reform.

glossary.en: the historical cycle of rise and fall
glossary.literal: jumping out of the historical cycle
glossary.explanation: A reference to a 1945 conversation in which Huang Yanpei warned Mao Zedong of the cycle of dynastic rise and decline. Mao's answer was democracy; Xi Jinping's is self-reform.
The principle of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current official guiding ideology, written into the Party Constitution in 2017.

t: The "Two Betters" as the Communist Party of China's solemn commitment and historical mission
zh: “两个更好”是中国共产党的庄严承诺和历史使命
paras: This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily in June 2022, interprets Xi Jinping's instruction, given during an inspection tour in Henan, to build the revolutionary old areas better and let their people live better lives, known as the "Two Betters". Mao argues that the instruction expresses Xi's concern for old-area residents, reflects the Party's political responsibility to carry out its founding mission, and gives a basic guide for revitalising these areas.

The piece has three parts. The first recalls the old areas' role in the revolution and the Party's later poverty-relief record there. The second sets out how development should proceed in the new stage and cites local examples from Jiangxi, Xinyang and Yan'an. The third links the instruction to common prosperity.

In Mao's account, the old areas were the root of the Party, the army and the People's Republic, and their people made great sacrifices. The Party has repaid this through successive poverty-alleviation models and the victory over poverty. Today, the author says, the areas must follow the new development philosophy, build on local resources, use Party building to serve the masses, and pursue high-quality development. Mao cites the end of 2020 figures of 98.99 million rural people lifted out of poverty, 832 counties removed from the poverty list and 128,000 villages. The author adds that Xi has visited old areas more than thirty times and that central policy support has been refined from "1258" to "1+N+X".

Mao concludes that, with people-centred development and consolidated poverty-alleviation gains, the old areas will be built better and common prosperity will be realised. The article presents the old areas as a "special revitalisation zone" for that goal. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary ties the Party's revolutionary history, rural revitalisation and common prosperity together.
quoteEn: In advancing common prosperity, the key lies in the countryside and the difficulty lies in the old revolutionary areas.
quoteZh: 推进共同富裕，关键在农村，难点在老区。

glossary.explanation: Shorthand for Xi Jinping's 2021 instruction to build the revolutionary old areas better and enable their people to live better lives. It is used as a guideline for old-area development policy.
Former base areas set up by the Communist Party during the Agrarian Revolutionary War and the War of Resistance against Japan. They are now treated as a category for special development support.
A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, associated with Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping and given new emphasis under Xi Jinping.
The official guideline of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, put forward in 2015.
The official goal of shifting from fast growth to growth that is efficient, innovative and sustainable.

t: "Telling the story of the Communist Party of China well to the world"
st: The multiple narratives of the CPC's external discourse system in the Yan'an period
zh: “向世界讲好中国共产党的故事”
zhSub: 延安时期中共构建对外话语体系的多重叙事
paras: How did the Communist Party of China (CPC) make its voice heard abroad during the Yan'an period, when the Kuomintang (KMT) imposed a tight news blockade? Wang argues that the Party built an external discourse system that conveyed a core revolutionary message of political democracy, economic self-reliance, press freedom and active resistance to Japan. In Wang's account, this let the international community form an accurate picture of the Party and its place in the War of Resistance. The author notes that existing domestic scholarship on the contest over discourse power between the two parties is thin.

Drawing on archival material and combining Party history with communication studies, the article is organised in four parts: why the system was built, how, what it said, and with what effect. The causes include KMT smear propaganda, the search for foreign aid, KMT cultural controls (over 200 decrees in 1938–1945, as cited), and the Party's own emphasis on external publicity. The article ends with lessons for present-day international communication.

The core of the argument is the set of narrative strategies. The Party created dedicated bodies such as the Yan'an reception office and the Southern Bureau's publicity group, and published foreign-language periodicals at home and abroad. It also invited foreign journalists, including Edgar Snow, Agnes Smedley and Israel Epstein, to speak on its behalf, and it used film, photography and radio, notably Xinhua's English-language broadcasts from 1944. It also drew on united-front allies and overseas Chinese. Wang says these channels presented the CPC as firmly Marxist, the mainstay of resistance, led by approachable and honest leaders, backed by a disciplined army, serving the people's welfare and practising democracy. Wang contends that this contrasted with the KMT's image of corruption.

Wang concludes that the effort broke the KMT blockade, disillusioned Western observers about the KMT government, and raised foreign recognition of the CPC. Over a hundred foreign visitors came to Yan'an, and 25 Chinese translations of their works appeared in 1938–1946, according to the article. For today, Wang calls for an open and proactive stance, for inviting foreign media to report, and for telling China's story in a rounded way that also admits shortcomings. Read the original if you study CPC history, wartime propaganda or the roots of present-day debates on international communication, and want a source-based account of foreign journalists' role.
quoteEn: We should make full use of foreign media: while taking our own voice abroad, we must also learn to bring people in, actively inviting foreign media to interview and report, and asking them to speak for us.
quoteZh: 要充分利用国外媒体发声，在自身发声“走出去”的同时，还要学会“引进来”，主动邀请国外媒体采访和报道，请他们替我们发声。

glossary.explanation: The years (roughly 1935–1947) when the CPC leadership was based at Yan'an in northern Shaanxi, during the War of Resistance against Japan and the struggle with the KMT.

t: The sources of strength behind the Communist Party of China's century of achievement
zh: 中国共产党铸就百年辉煌的力量源泉
paras: Zhao Xiaohu and Mao Junji ask why the Communist Party of China was able to achieve what it did over its first hundred years. In this newspaper commentary, they answer that four forces acted together: the power of faith, of theoretical innovation, of bold practice and of self-reform. In their account, these forces kept the Party at the forefront of its age and let it advance through setbacks.

The piece takes each force in turn under its own heading. It draws on Xi Jinping's 2021 speech marking the Party's centenary, on the 2021 Party resolution on its history, and on statements by Mao Zedong. It ends with a short look ahead to the Party's second centenary goal.

On faith, the authors say the Party's ideals rest on Marxism, on the family-and-country sentiment of traditional Chinese culture and on the aim of national independence. They tie these to the founding spirit. On theoretical innovation, they stress a practical, seek-truth-from-facts style of thought. They also stress that each theoretical advance has been followed by Party-wide study, so that theory becomes material force. On practice, they trace a line from the revolution through construction and reform and opening up to national rejuvenation. On self-reform, they argue that the Party has no special interests of its own. They present Mao's call for popular supervision and Xi's idea of self-reform as two answers to the problem of keeping the Party from degenerating.

The authors conclude that if the Party keeps and develops these four forces, it will find a successful path for building and strengthening itself under long-term rule. They write as the Party begins its "new journey" towards the second centenary goal, amid what they call changes unseen in a century. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-school scholars present the sources of the Party's success in official discourse.
quoteEn: An advanced Marxist party is not born that way; it is tempered through continuous self-reform.
quoteZh: 先进的马克思主义政党不是天生的，而是在不断自我革命中淬炼而成的。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed under Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It refers to the Party's efforts to correct its own errors and combat corruption and degeneration from within.

A phrase Xi Jinping first set out in his speech of 1 July 2021. It names the values of the Party's founders: upholding truth and ideals, staying true to the original aspiration, fearless struggle, and loyalty to the Party and the people.
The policy of domestic economic reform and opening to the outside world, launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

glossary.literal: great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China's strength and standing, usually tied to the two centenary goals of 2021 and 2049.

t: The logic behind the formation of Party-building discourse
zh: 党建话语的生成逻辑
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in June 2022, Sun Zhaohong takes up Xi Jinping's instruction to improve the discipline, academic and discourse systems of Party building. The commentary asks how the Communist Party of China's distinctive Party-building discourse came into being. Sun argues that it rests on three logics: historical, theoretical and practical.

The piece is short and organised under three headings. It moves from the discourse's origins in the early Party and the Comintern's influence, through the Mao Zedong era, to the vocabulary of the new era since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

On the historical logic, Sun argues that the discourse grows out of the Party's experience and changes with it. The slogan "branches built on companies" emerged from the lessons of the failed Autumn Harvest Uprising and is now applied online, in villages and along industrial chains. Mao's and Xi Jinping's answers to the "cave dialogue" question, popular supervision and the Party's self-reform, are said to show continuity and development together. On the theoretical logic, Sun presents the discourse as a product of the Two Integrations: Marxism combined with China's realities and with fine traditional culture. Sun cites Mao's "seeking truth from facts" and Xi's use of classical sayings to educate officials. On the practical logic, discourse arises from practice and answers the questions of the times and of the people.

Sun concludes that the Party's capacity to respond to changing conditions explains its growth from a handful of members to over 95 million, and that its evolving discourse carries this capacity. Sun calls for new concepts, categories and formulations in Party building to strengthen Marxism's explanatory power. Read the original if you want a concise official-academic account of how Party-building terminology is framed and justified.
quoteEn: Party-building discourse is the voice of the times and the voice of the people.
quoteZh: 党建话语是时代的声音、人民的声音。

glossary.explanation: Formula stressing the combination of Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. It is used in Party theory to describe adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.literal: branches built at the company level
glossary.explanation: Principle that Party branches be established at the level of army companies, associated with Mao Zedong's army-building after 1927. It was later extended to civilian organisations.
Reference to a 1945 conversation in Yan'an between Mao Zedong and Huang Yanpei about how a ruling power can escape the historical cycle of rise and decline.
Official term for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself, named by Xi Jinping as a second answer to the cave dialogue question.

t: An advanced organisation that keeps close to the Party and stays at the forefront of the times
st: Self-reform and the Communist Youth League
zh: 紧跟党走在时代前列的先进组织
paras: Writing in 2022, Dong Yuyi, secretary of the Qinghai Provincial Committee of the Communist Youth League, takes up Xi Jinping's speech at the League's centenary. In it Xi said the League can keep pace with the times, youth development and practical innovation only if it dares to undertake self-reform. Dong argues that the League, as the Party's assistant and reserve force, should follow the Party's own practice of self-reform. The aim is a League that reassures the Party, satisfies young people, meets the needs of social development and stays at the forefront of the times.

The commentary is organised under three headings: keeping to the correct political direction, deepening reform of the League's own work, and advancing full and rigorous self-governance of the League. It draws on the Party's hundred-year experience and on Xi's remarks on youth work. It is a programmatic essay for League cadres rather than a study of historical cases.

On direction, Dong holds that the League's political positioning, original aspiration, functions and line must not change. This requires absolute Party leadership, the Two Upholds and the Two Establishes, and the path of mass organisations with Chinese characteristics. It also requires the League to keep its political character, advanced nature and mass character. On reform, Dong proposes extending services to emerging, disadvantaged and marginal youth groups, and restructuring work so that objects, content, forces and platforms become more social. Further proposals are to strengthen county-level and branch organisations, recruit talent beyond formal League and institutional boundaries, build internet-based work, and widen coverage into non-public enterprises and new social organisations.

On self-governance, Dong calls for raising political standing, grasping the laws of youth growth, creating a supportive atmosphere and promoting overall planning under the Implementation Outline for Full and Rigorous Self-Governance of the League in the New Era. This would be done while learning from, but not mechanically copying, full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. League cadres are urged to be friends of youth rather than 'youth officials', to stay close to the grassroots and to be ready for great struggle. Read the original if you want a practitioner's account of how Party discourse on self-reform is translated into working guidance for the Communist Youth League.
quoteEn: Political character is the soul of mass organisations, advanced nature is the source of strength of their work, and mass character is their fundamental feature.
quoteZh: 政治性是群团组织的灵魂，先进性是群团工作的力量之源，群众性是群团组织的根本特点。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan of the Xi Jinping era for strict discipline and management within the Communist Party, including anti-corruption work. The article extends it by analogy to the Youth League.
A Party formula, prominent since 2018, calling for upholding Xi Jinping's position as core of the Party Central Committee and the Party's centralised, unified leadership.
A formula from the 2021 Party resolution on history, affirming Xi Jinping's core position and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The Communist Youth League of China, the Party's youth organisation for people roughly aged 14 to 28, founded in 1922. It is described officially as the Party's assistant and reserve force.

t: The Communist Party of China's valuable experience in seizing the historical initiative
zh: 中国共产党把握历史主动的宝贵经验
source: Studies on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics, 2022 no. 2
paras: Hou Yanshe and Lü Mingyang ask how the Communist Party of China (CPC) has managed to "seize the historical initiative" (bawo lishi zhudong), a phrase Xi Jinping used repeatedly in speeches around the Party's centenary in 2021. Writing in 2022, they treat it as an epistemological, practical and methodological question tied to the fate of the Chinese nation. Their thesis is that the Party's century of achievement rests on six interlocking sources of experience, which they present as an organic system.

The article is organised in six sections, each naming one element of seizing the initiative and its role. These are following historical laws (the precondition), firm historical confidence (the foundation), respecting the historical subject, meaning the people (the driving force), strengthening historical responsibility (the focal point), grasping historical opportunities (the key), and daring to carry out self-reform (the essence). The authors draw on Marx and Engels, Xi Jinping's speeches, Deng Xiaoping, and the 2021 Party resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience. They illustrate the points with episodes from Party history, from the Zunyi Meeting to the post-2012 anti-corruption campaign.

In the authors' account, historical materialism allows the Party to treat history as law-governed while still stressing the active choices of historical agents. Historical confidence comes from summing up successes and failures and from Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and it is bound up with the Four-sphere Confidence. They argue that the Party seizes the initiative by relying on the masses, in line with the mass line, and by carrying the responsibilities of national rejuvenation and of a community with a shared future for mankind. Past opportunities, from the Soviet October Revolution through reform and opening up to the \"two overall situations\", were exploited by correctly reading the era. The authors present self-reform as the decisive element, an answer to the \"historical cycle\" of rise and decline, and contrast it with other parties that, they say, lacked scientific theory and represented narrow interests.

Hou and Lü conclude that the six aspects form one system, grounded in the fact that the Party has no special interests of its own. They call for updating the Party's leadership methods and mass line, organising and educating the people, widening channels for popular views, and strengthening the Party's institutions of self-reform so that it does not change in character. They also stress political initiative as part of historical initiative. Read the original if you want a systematic, officially aligned account of how Party theorists frame \"historical initiative\" in terms of laws, confidence, the people, responsibility, opportunity and self-reform.
quoteEn: The essence of the CPC's seizing the historical initiative lies in daring to carry out self-reform, consciously and proactively adjusting and repairing itself as circumstances, times and trends require, and so pressing forward through revolutionary forging and tempering.
quoteZh: 中国共产党把握历史主动的精髓就在于勇于自我革命，自觉主动地随机、随时、随势自我调适和自我修复，从而在革命性的锻造与锤炼中奋勇前行。

glossary.explanation: Official term for the Party's continuous effort to correct its own errors and combat corruption. It is presented as the Party's answer to the "historical cycle" of rise and decline.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Xi Jinping promoted it as a core Party formula.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept of a world of shared interests and responsibilities, promoted since about 2013.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and presented officially as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.

t: Historical lessons from a century of building the intra-Party political ecology of the Communist Party of China
zh: 中国共产党百年党内政治生态建设的历史经验
paras: Writing in 2022, Lin Ting asks what the Communist Party of China's hundred years of efforts to build a healthy intra-Party political ecology can teach the Party today. Starting from Xi Jinping's statements since the 18th Party Congress (2012) that a clean political ecology is the soil of good Party conduct, Lin argues that the Party's experience yields four lasting principles and four tasks for the future.

The article has three parts. The first applies historical materialism to define the political ecology as the overall environment, atmosphere and habits of Party organisations and members. It traces its changing emphasis through the new-democratic revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era. The second part draws out four basic lessons. The third identifies remaining problems and four directions for further work.

Lin's four lessons are these. First, political development must take the lead, uniting Party spirit and the people's character, securing unity of thought, politics and action, and upholding the authority of the Central Committee. Second, ideological, theoretical, institutional and spiritual work must be combined: ideological work as the foundation, theory as the core, rule-based governance as the safeguard and the Party's spiritual lineage as the driving force. Third, organisational structure must be matched by political culture. Fourth, internal construction must be matched by outward influence, which Lin links to combining the Party's self-reform with social revolution. Lin holds that a good political ecology depends on the Party's leadership, and that the leadership role rests on these combined efforts.

Looking ahead, Lin notes continuing problems: a political base that needs consolidating, uneven initiative in self-reform, a gap between current anti-corruption work and a systematic institutional framework, and limited influence on wider social norms. Lin calls for upholding Party leadership against internal and external risks, sustaining the spirit of great struggle and self-reform, building long-term mechanisms to remove the conditions for corruption, and using "Party governance" to advance "state governance". Read the original if you want a detailed account of how Party-theoretical writing frames the Party's century of internal discipline and organisation, and its justification for continued strengthening of Party leadership.
quoteEn: Building the intra-Party political ecology is not a temporary expedient but a continuing state of the Communist Party of China's self-reform amid constantly changing historical conditions.
quoteZh: 党内政治生态建设不是一时的权宜之计，而是中国共产党在历史条件不断变化中进行自我革命的持续性状态

glossary.explanation: A term popularised under Xi Jinping for the overall environment, atmosphere, habits and conduct within the Party. It is used to discuss Party discipline, culture and anti-corruption work.
Official term for the Party's claim to correct its own errors and purify itself, increasingly stressed in Xi-era discourse.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Historical lessons from a century of building the Communist Party of China's intra-Party political ecology
zh: 中国共产党百年党内政治生态建设的历史经验
paras: Written in the year after the Party's centenary, this article asks what a hundred years of effort to build a healthy "intra-Party political ecology" can teach the Communist Party of China. Lin Ting defines the concept as the overall environment, atmosphere and habits in which Party organisations and members live and work. The author argues that this ecology has existed since the Party's founding, that it has developed in step with the Party's historical missions, and that sustaining it is essential to the Party's vanguard character and purity.

The article has three parts. The first applies historical materialism to the topic, treating the political ecology as an objective, composite product of many forces and as the result of the Party actively taking up its mission in four periods: the New Democratic Revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era. The second part draws four basic lessons from the century. The third turns to current problems and to how the work should continue.

In the core of the argument, Lin holds that political development must lead the whole effort, because it secures the unity of Party spirit and the people's character, a unified will across the Party, and the authority of the Party Central Committee. Lin then names four mutually reinforcing means: ideological, theoretical, institutional and spiritual Party-building. Organisational structure and political culture are said to need parallel development. Building inside the Party is said to be inseparable from its outward influence on government conduct and social norms, which the author links to the Party's "self-reform" and to social revolution.

Lin finds that, despite results since the 18th Party Congress (2012), problems remain: the political base of governance needs consolidating, the Party's drive for self-reform is not yet sufficiently self-motivated, the anti-corruption institutional system is incomplete, and the Party's role in shaping social attitudes needs strengthening. The author calls for upholding Party leadership, keeping up the spirit of struggle and self-reform, establishing long-term mechanisms against corruption, and using "Party governance" to advance "state governance". Read the original if you want a detailed example of how Party-building scholarship in China frames the Party's history, institutions and tasks through the idea of a political ecology.
quoteEn: Building the intra-Party political ecology is not a stopgap measure but a continuing state in which the Communist Party of China carries out self-reform amid constantly changing historical conditions.
quoteZh: 党内政治生态建设不是一时的权宜之计，而是中国共产党在历史条件不断变化中进行自我革命的持续性状态

glossary.explanation: A term popularised in Party discourse after the 18th Party Congress. It refers to the overall environment, culture, norms and practices within the Party that shape the conduct of members and officials.
A term in Party discourse for the Party's capacity to correct itself and purge its own shortcomings. It is often paired with "social revolution".

A strand of Party-building that stresses political direction, loyalty to the Central Committee and political discipline. Since the 19th Party Congress (2017) official texts have placed it first among the Party's various forms of building.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: The formation, characteristics and practical value of the spiritual lineage of Chinese Communists
zh: 中国共产党人的精神谱系的形成原因、特征表现及现实价值
paras: Writing in 2022, Liu Haifei takes up the concept of the "spiritual lineage of Chinese Communists", which Xi Jinping used in 2021 and which the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021) described as having the great founding spirit of the Party as its source. Liu notes that scholarly work on the concept is still thin on its causes, features and value, and sets out to address all three. The article argues that the lineage arose from several converging historical, ideological and organisational conditions, that it has identifiable external and internal characteristics, and that it retains concrete value for Party building today.

The article is organised in three parts. The first gives six reasons for the lineage's formation. The second describes its features at three levels: outward form, inner substance and value choices. The third sets out six areas of practical value. Examples are drawn from the Party's revolutionary, socialist construction, reform and new-era periods, including the Jinggangshan, Long March, Yan'an, Daqing, Lei Feng, Special Economic Zone and anti-epidemic spirits.

On causes, Liu points to traditional Chinese spirit and cultural "genes"; Marxist belief as a "catalyst"; the national longing for rejuvenation after modern humiliation; the Party's tradition of ideological and political education and cadre training; the exemplary role of martyrs, heroes and models as carriers of each spirit; and the Party leadership's formal articulation of the concept since the 18th Party Congress (2012). On characteristics, Liu describes the lineage as systematic, successive across four historical periods, and broad in field, trade, region and naming. Its inner substance is summarised as loyalty, firm conviction, hard struggle, dedication, seeking truth from facts, service to the people and innovation. Its value choices are said to be sacrificing life, favouring righteousness over profit, and putting the collective before the family.

Liu argues that the lineage has six practical functions: unifying thought and rallying strength in a Party of over 95 million members; maintaining the Party's vanguard character; purifying the political ecosystem, with Yan'an spirit as an example; training revolutionary successors; fostering a healthy social ethos; and stimulating economic production, since spiritual force can become material force. Liu calls for continued propagation of these spirits through education, media and the example of Party members. Read the original if you want a systematic Chinese-language account of how the Party's "spiritual lineage" is classified and justified, with many named examples of individual spirits.
quoteEn: It can be said that if this spirit endures in Party members, the Party's vanguard character endures; if the spirit is lost, the vanguard character is lost.
quoteZh: 可以说，党员身上这种精神存，则党的先进性存；党员身上这种精神失，则党的先进性失。

glossary.zh: 中国共产党人的精神谱系
glossary.explanation: A concept referring to the series of named "spirits" (such as the Jinggangshan or Yan'an spirit) that the Party says it developed over its history. It was used by Xi Jinping in 2021 and endorsed in the Party's official documents.

glossary.en: great founding spirit of the Party
glossary.explanation: A formulation put forward by Xi Jinping on the Party's centenary in 2021. It is officially described as the source of the Party's later spirits.
The Party's system of teaching political beliefs and values to members, soldiers and students, including through Party schools and study campaigns.

t: Grasping the historical significance of the Party's centenary struggle as a whole
zh: 从整体上把握党百年奋斗的历史意义
source: Research on Ideological and Political Education (Sixiang jiaoyu yanjiu), 2022 no. 5
paras: The 2021 Party resolution on the major achievements and historical experience of the Party's century of struggle sums up the significance of that struggle in five dimensions: the people's fate, the choice of path, theoretical innovation, world influence and the Party's self-reform. Wang and Shi, writing from the perspective of teaching the course Outline of Modern and Contemporary Chinese History, argue that the five should not only be explained one by one but grasped as a whole. They hold that this requires joining the historical, theoretical and practical logics, a grand view of history and systems thinking, so as to strengthen students' historical confidence and emotional identification with the Party.

The article is organised in three parts, each tied to one methodological requirement. The first sets the Party's struggle in a long vertical sweep of Chinese civilisation and modern history and in comparison with the West. The second applies systems thinking to the link between theory and practice across the five significances. The third asks for historical confidence that connects past, present and future, drawing on the resolution's "ten upholds" of historical experience.

In the first part, the authors recount the capture of Beijing and Nanjing by foreign invaders and the failure of earlier national salvation schemes. They present the Party's centenary as a unified pursuit of national rejuvenation through liberating productive forces while standing with the people, and as the exploration of Chinese modernization. In their account, this has broken the Western monopoly on development models, civilisational forms and democratic forms, and has refuted the "end of history" and "China collapse" theses. The second part argues that Party leadership is the most essential feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics and that each stage of Marxism's adaptation produced a leap in theory and practice. It also claims that the Party's work has shaped world history, from the anti-fascist war to the survival of socialism after the Soviet collapse. The third part calls for a correct view of Party history that opposes historical nihilism, and for linking the significances with the three great relationships of Party and people, theory and practice, and China and the world. It also attributes the Soviet failure partly to a clash between Marxism and Russian Orthodox culture, in contrast with the affinity the authors see between Marxism and Chinese traditional culture.

The authors conclude that historical confidence rests on the Two Integrations, on honestly facing the Party's past errors, and on full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. They present self-reform as the second answer to the historical cycle of rise and decline, after the people's supervision. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-school-style teaching approach frames the 2021 resolution as a unified whole for classroom use.
quoteEn: The Party's hundred-year history is a history of seeking the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, in which, while exploring the path of Chinese modernization, it has united the liberation and development of the productive forces with a people-centred stand.
quoteZh: 党的百年历史就是一部为了实现中华民族伟大复兴，在探索中国式现代化道路中坚持解放和发展社会生产力与坚持人民立场相统一的历史。

glossary.explanation: Official term for China's own path to modernization, which the Party says differs from Western models. It is usually described by features such as a huge population and common prosperity.
Formula for combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Official slogan, prominent since 2012, for strict discipline, anti-corruption work and Party-building.
Official label for views seen as distorting or denying the Party's history and achievements.

t: The Communist Party of China's century of struggle has fundamentally changed the future and fate of the Chinese people
zh: 中国共产党百年奋斗从根本上改变了中国人民的前途命运
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2022 no. 5
paras: Han Xiping elaborates a key judgement of the Party's 2021 Resolution on the major achievements and historical experience of the Party's century of struggle: that the Communist Party of China's century of struggle has fundamentally changed the future and fate of the Chinese people. The article argues that the Party has consistently taken the people's standpoint as its basic political stance, and that this has produced an irreversible change in the people's condition, from a survival crisis to the pursuit of a better life.

The article has three parts. The first examines how the Party worked to change the people's fate, through its goals, its assessment of the principal contradiction in society, and its lines, principles and policies. The second sets out the results: better living standards, a changed political status for the people, and a growing sense of happiness. The third looks ahead to the strength accumulated in the century of struggle and to the tasks of the new era.

Han's central move is to treat the people's happiness, needs and interests as the basis of Party practice. On this reading, the Party defines itself as the one answering the exam paper and the people as the examiners. It also judges shifts in the principal contradiction by the changing needs of the people, from survival in the New Democratic revolution, to material and cultural needs after 1949, to the present contradiction between the people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced and inadequate development. For the results, Han contrasts pre-1949 China (80 per cent of people said to be hungry or half-starved, life expectancy of 35) with a moderately prosperous society for over 1.4 billion people and a life expectancy of 77.3. Han credits whole-process people's democracy with making the people masters of their own fate. The article also compares China with a world marked, in its account, by inequality and extreme poverty.

Han concludes that moderate prosperity is a new starting point. China's material strength (GDP above 100 trillion yuan, per capita GDP above US$10,000), institutional strength and spiritual strength, in Han's account, now underpin further progress. Han describes four directions for the new era: resolving the principal contradiction through the new development philosophy and high-quality development, advancing common prosperity in stages towards 2035 and mid-century, and promoting the all-round development of the person, which Han presents as the highest Marxist goal. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-school style commentary on the 2021 Resolution presents the people-centred logic of the Party's history and its stated goals for the new era.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China has carried the people's standpoint through every judgement about the principal contradiction in society and its transformation, ensuring that the direction of struggle never departs from realising the people's happiness.
quoteZh: 中国共产党把人民立场贯穿判断社会主要矛盾及其转化始终，确保奋斗方向始终朝向实现人民幸福不偏离。

glossary.explanation: A Party concept for the central tension in society at a given stage, which determines the Party's strategic priorities. The 19th Party Congress (2017) redefined it as the contradiction between the people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced and inadequate development.
A term popularised by Xi Jinping from 2019 for China's democratic model, which the Party presents as covering every stage of governance rather than only elections.
A goal of shared wealth for all the people, associated with socialism in Party theory and given renewed emphasis under Xi Jinping, with staged targets to 2035 and mid-century.
The five principles of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, put forward in 2015 as guidance for economic and social policy.
An official formulation, prominent since 2017, for shifting from rapid growth to growth stressing quality, efficiency and balance.
Mao Zedong's term for the stage of China's revolution before socialism. It was led by the proletariat and directed against imperialism, feudalism and bureaucrat-capitalism.

t: The great founding spirit of the Party: generative logic, connotations and ways of promoting it
zh: 伟大建党精神：生成逻辑、内涵意蕴与弘扬路径
paras: Writing in Studies on Marxism (2022, no. 2), Zhang Shihai takes up the "great founding spirit" of the Communist Party of China, which Xi Jinping first formulated in his speech at the Party's centenary on 1 July 2021 and called the "source of the Party's spirit". The article asks how this spirit came into being, what it contains and how it should be carried forward. Zhang argues that it arose from the national project of rejuvenation, Marxism and traditional Chinese culture, and that it must now be turned into practice through four paths.

The article has three parts. The first reconstructs the spirit's generative logic in four strands: the goal of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, the scientific and truth-bearing character of Marxism, the nourishment of fine traditional Chinese culture, and the early Party-founding activities from 1920 to the Second Party Congress in 1922. The second part analyses the four phrases of Xi's formulation. The third sets out how to promote the spirit in the new era.

In Zhang's core argument, each pair of phrases expresses a dialectical unity. Upholding truth and ideals joins truth and value; putting the original aspiration into practice and shouldering the mission joins theory and practice; fearing no sacrifice and fighting bravely joins the revolutionary and the political; and loyalty to the Party and not failing the people joins Party spirit and the people's character. The Party's mission is said to have taken concrete form in the stages of \"standing up\", \"becoming prosperous\" and \"becoming strong\".
