For promotion, Zhang proposes deeper theoretical elaboration, institutional mechanisms for publicity, supervision and feedback, a objective and respectful treatment of traditional culture, and the integration of the spirit into the \"four greats\": great struggle, great project of Party building, great cause and great dream.

Zhang concludes that promoting the spirit is a major historical task of the new era and that it must move from theory to practice. The author notes that existing research has said little about its practical functions and paths, and calls for work on the relation between the founding spirit and the Party's broader spiritual lineage. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how Chinese Party scholars interpret the founding spirit and propose to institutionalise it.
quoteEn: The great founding spirit is not only a major theoretical proposition but, even more, a major practical one.
quoteZh: 伟大建党精神不仅是一个重大的理论命题，更是一个重大的实践命题。

glossary.explanation: A formulation Xi Jinping first set out on 1 July 2021: upholding truth and ideals, practising the original aspiration and shouldering the mission, fearing no sacrifice and fighting bravely, and being loyal to the Party and not failing the people. It is presented as the source of the Party's later spiritual traditions.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: An official goal of national revival after the 'century of humiliation' that began in 1840. It is treated as the unifying theme of the Party's history.
The official term for the series of named 'spirits' (such as the Jinggangshan spirit or the Yan'an spirit) formed in the Party's history. The founding spirit is described as their origin.
Xi Jinping's formula of great struggle, great project (Party building), great cause (socialism with Chinese characteristics) and great dream (national rejuvenation).

The official term for the parts of China's cultural heritage that the Party endorses as sources of values and legitimacy. It is paired with calls for 'creative transformation and innovative development'.

t: The Communist Party of China's century of struggle has fundamentally changed the future and destiny of the Chinese people
zh: 中国共产党百年奋斗从根本上改变了中国人民的前途命运
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2022 no. 5
paras: This article expounds a sentence from the 2021 Party resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience of the past century: that the CPC's century of struggle fundamentally changed the future and destiny of the Chinese people. Han Xiping argues that the Party's founding mission of seeking happiness for the people and rejuvenation for the nation has produced an irreversible change, from a crisis of survival to the pursuit of a better life.

The text is organised in three parts. The first examines how the Party has worked to change the people's fate, through its goals, its judgements about the principal contradiction in society, and its lines and policies. The second sets out the results in three dimensions: quality of life, the people's status, and their sense of happiness. The third looks to the future, with four themes: accumulated strength, resolving the principal contradiction of the new era, common prosperity, and all-round human development.

Han's central move is to treat the people's standpoint as the thread running through all Party activity. The author holds that the Party defines its goal by the people's wish for a better life, and that at each stage it has used the people's changing needs to identify the principal contradiction and set its direction. The article traces this from the New Democratic Revolution, through the post-1956 and reform-era formulations, to the contradiction between growing needs for a better life and unbalanced and inadequate development. The second move is a double comparison. Han contrasts old China, citing figures of 80 per cent of people hungry and average life expectancy of 35, with present life expectancy of 77.3 and a moderately prosperous society for over 1.4 billion people. The author also contrasts China with a world described as marked by inequality and extreme poverty, and presents whole-process people's democracy as the institutional form of the people's mastery of their own destiny.

Han concludes that a moderately prosperous society is a new starting point. The author points to material strength (GDP above 100 trillion yuan, per capita GDP above US$10,000), institutional strength and spiritual awakening as the basis for further progress. Han expects the new development philosophy, high-quality development and staged steps towards common prosperity by 2035 and mid-century to lead to more equal and freer lives, in line with Marx's goal of free and all-round individual development. Read the original if you want a representative example of how Party-affiliated scholars in 2022 interpreted the century-of-struggle resolution through the idea of the people's standpoint.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China has carried the people's standpoint through its judgement of the principal contradiction in society and its transformation, ensuring that the direction of struggle never deviates from realising the people's happiness.
quoteZh: 中国共产党把人民立场贯穿判断社会主要矛盾及其转化始终，确保奋斗方向始终朝向实现人民幸福不偏离。

glossary.explanation: A Party formulation of the central tension in society at a given stage, used to set strategic priorities. The 19th Party Congress (2017) restated it as the contradiction between people's growing needs for a better life and unbalanced and inadequate development.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2019 to describe China's political system as democracy running through every stage of governance, not only elections.
A long-standing socialist goal of shared wealth for all, given renewed emphasis under Xi Jinping, with staged targets for 2035 and mid-century.
The official framework of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, put forward in 2015.
The official term for a shift from speed of growth to quality and efficiency of development, prominent since 2017.

t: Upholding a correct view of Party history
zh: 坚持正确党史观
paras: This short commentary, published in the People's Daily in June 2022, asks how the Communist Party's history should be viewed. Han argues that a correct view of Party history rests on the methods of dialectical and historical materialism. In Han's account, this view consolidates the results of Party history study and education and helps the Party grasp the theme, main thread and mainstream essence of its history.

Han builds the piece around Xi Jinping's explanation of the 2021 Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee. Three requirements structure the text: Party history should be viewed in concrete historical terms, objectively and comprehensively, and in terms of connection and development. Each is illustrated with passages from the Resolution.

On the first point, Han cites Lenin on considering the objective content of historical processes in specific conditions, and notes that the Resolution divides the century into four periods with distinct tasks and achievements. On the second, Han points to the Resolution's treatment of the periods before and after reform and opening up as connected, so that the achievements of the earlier period prepared the later one despite serious setbacks. On the third, Han presents the three historical resolutions as consistent with one another, with the latest focusing on the achievements of the new era.

Han concludes that this method brings out the Party's founding mission of seeking happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the nation. In Han's reading, it shows why the Party, Marxism and socialism with Chinese characteristics succeed, builds consensus and strengthens historical confidence. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary frames the methodology of Party history writing after the 2021 Resolution.
quoteEn: A systematic presentation of the theme, main thread and mainstream essence of the Party's historical development lets people understand deeply that the red political power, New China and socialism with Chinese characteristics were all hard won.
quoteZh: 党的历史发展的主题主线、主流本质的系统呈现，让人们深刻认识到红色政权来之不易、新中国来之不易、中国特色社会主义来之不易

glossary.explanation: The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping, which the Resolution treats as a new historical period.
The official name for the Party's model of socialism, developed since reform and opening up.
The three Central Committee resolutions on Party history, adopted in 1945, 1981 and 2021, which set the official assessment of the Party's past.

t: Unwaveringly upholding and strengthening the Party's overall leadership
zh: 毫不动摇坚持和加强党的全面领导
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in 2022, argues that the Party's overall leadership must be upheld and strengthened without wavering in the new era. Sang begins from the first of the "Ten Clarifications" that summarise Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. That clarification names Communist Party leadership as the most essential feature and greatest strength of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Sang holds that only such leadership can let the country manage both the strategic overall situation of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and the world's "changes unseen in a century".

The piece is organised under four headings. It first sets out what upholding the Party's overall leadership means. It then turns to the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, to arming the whole Party with Xi Jinping Thought, and to full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Sang draws on Xi's statements and on the 2021 Party resolution on the Party's history.

On the first point, Sang says the Party's leadership should be understood through historical, theoretical and practical logic. In this account it is the choice of history and the people, and it rests on the Marxist theory of the party. Sang adds that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) Xi's statements have enriched Marxist ruling-party theory. Because the Party is "the leading force in everything", its leadership must be comprehensive and systematic, covering economic, political, cultural, social and ecological work. On the second point, Sang attributes the historic achievements of the new era to Xi's position as the core of the Central Committee and the Party, and to the guidance of his thought. Sang calls for stronger political, ideological, theoretical and emotional identification with the Two Establishes, to be turned into action. Sang also presents the Party's "self-reform" as the way to overcome the Party's own problems. The piece warns that corruption is still a serious challenge despite the "overwhelming victory" of the anti-corruption campaign.

Sang concludes that, on this "road of the exam", the Party must treat studying Xi Jinping Thought as its first political task. It must keep adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and must keep up strict Party discipline. The aim is to keep the Party from losing its character and to ensure it remains the strong leadership core of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party commentary in 2022 tied the Party's overall leadership to the Two Establishes, theoretical study and the Party's self-reform.
quoteEn: Full and rigorous self-governance of the Party is the great practice of the Party's self-reform in the new era.
quoteZh: 全面从严治党是新时代党的自我革命的伟大实践。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the 2021 Party resolution on history. It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the whole Party, and the guiding status of Xi Jinping Thought.
The requirement that Party members resolutely uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's leadership.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The slogan for Party-building and discipline policy since 2012. It includes the anti-corruption campaign and stricter internal supervision.
The official idea that the Party can purify and renew itself without external checks. It is presented as the answer to the problem of the historical cycle of rise and decline.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's ongoing effort to combine Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete conditions and traditional culture.

t: The new era as a new field for research on Party history and the history of New China
zh: 新时代是党史新中国史研究的新领域
source: Studies on the History of the Communist Party of China (Zhonggong dangshi yanjiu), 2019 no. 11
paras: Writing in 2019, on the 70th anniversary of the People's Republic, Qu Qingshan asks what the "new era" that began with the 18th Party Congress (2012) means for the history of the Communist Party and the history of New China, and what it demands of historians. Qu holds that the two histories largely overlap, with Party history as the core of New China's history. The article's answer is that the new era is an integral part of both, a new epochal coordinate and a new milestone, and therefore a new and important field of research.

The article is organised in four parts, each taking a different vantage point on the new era: the two historical tasks the Party has carried since 1921, the Party's "historical position", the realisation of the great national dream, and finally the implications for historical scholarship. It divides the record into four periods, each tied to a keyword: revolution (1921–1949), construction (1949–1978), reform (1978–2012) and rejuvenation (2012 to mid-century). It draws on Xi Jinping's statements and on official figures, such as GDP rising from 51.94 trillion to 90.03 trillion yuan between 2012 and 2018.

Qu's central move is to present the four periods as one continuous struggle: saving the nation, building it, enriching it and, in the new era, making it strong. The new era is both a continuation of the reform period and a qualitative leap, justified by three factors: a world undergoing "changes unseen in a century", China's strongest development conditions in modern times, and a shift in the principal contradiction in Chinese society. Qu also stresses that the new era links the "two centenary goals" and the two-step plan to 2035 and mid-century. Counting to 2049, the new era would take up 38 per cent of New China's history and 29.7 per cent of the Party's, which Qu takes as reason enough to study it.

Qu rejects the saying that contemporaries should not write contemporary history, arguing that history and reality have no sharp boundary. The article names the field's difficulties: events still unfolding, the need for specialist knowledge across many sectors, and the task of sifting abundant public information. Qu calls the field under-studied, since existing work is mostly about current problems and not about history, experience or laws of development. Qu calls on historians to follow Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, combine Party spirit with scientific method and serve the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want an authoritative statement of how Party historiography is told to periodise the PRC era and fold the Xi period into Party history.
quoteEn: Whether in terms of time span or of content, research on the new era should become a new yet extremely important field of study in the history of the Party and of New China.
quoteZh: 无论是从时段上讲，还是从内容上讲，关于新时代的研究，都应当成为党史新中国史研究一个新的却又极其重要的领域。

glossary.explanation: The label for the period beginning with the 18th Party Congress in 2012 under Xi Jinping, formally proclaimed at the 19th Party Congress (2017). Official texts treat it as both a continuation of and a step beyond the reform period.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A long-standing nationalist goal that Xi Jinping made central to Party discourse, linked to the Chinese Dream. It denotes restoring China to a strong, prosperous position after the "century of humiliation".
Goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary (2021) and a modern socialist country by the PRC's centenary (2049).

A Maoist category identifying the central tension in society at a given stage. The 19th Party Congress restated it as one between people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

t: Upholding the Party's overall leadership is the choice of history and the people
zh: 坚持党的全面领导是历史和人民的选择
source: People's Daily (Renmin Ribao); posted on marxism.cass.cn 27 May 2022
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily, takes up the sixth plenary session of the 19th Central Committee's 2021 Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience. Wang notes that the Resolution puts Party leadership first among the "ten affirmations" of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The article's thesis is that upholding the Party's overall leadership is the choice of history and of the people, and the only route for upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics.

The piece has three parts. The first reviews the Party's history from its founding through the revolution, socialist construction, reform and opening up, and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second turns to the Two Establishes and the role of a leadership core. The third deals with maintaining and improving the institutional system of Party leadership.

Wang argues from historical experience that when overall leadership is upheld thoroughly, the cause of the Party and the people advances smoothly, and when it is weakened, the cause takes detours or suffers setbacks. Examples include the lessons of the failed Great Revolution, the leading role in the anti-Japanese united front, and the Party's answers at each turning point after the Cultural Revolution. The author holds that a strong leadership core has always been decisive in critical moments, citing the Zunyi Meeting and the 1945 Resolution on historical questions. On that basis Wang presents the Two Establishes as the most important political outcome since 2012, and describes Xi Jinping as a core tested by history and practice and as the principal founder of the thought that bears his name.

Wang concludes that, amid what the article calls a century of change in the world and a once-in-a-century pandemic, the Party must grasp the decisive significance of the Two Establishes and carry out the Two Upholds. The author calls for the leadership system to be improved: mechanisms for keeping the founding mission in mind, institutions defending the authority of the Central Committee, systems for governing for and by the people, and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official Party narrative justifies overall leadership and the leadership core on historical grounds.
quoteEn: History and practice have both fully shown that when the Party's overall leadership is upheld thoroughly, the cause of the Party and the people advances smoothly; when it is weakened, the cause takes detours or even suffers setbacks.
quoteZh: 历史和实践都充分表明，当党的全面领导坚持得彻底时，党和人民事业就会顺利推进；当党的全面领导被削弱时，党和人民事业就会走弯路甚至遭受挫折。

glossary.explanation: Formula from the 2021 Resolution on Party history: establishing Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and establishing the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought. Official texts call it the most important political outcome since 2012.
The requirement that Party members firmly uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralized, unified leadership of the Central Committee.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. The 2021 Resolution summarises its core content in ten affirmations.
The official name for the Party's path, system and theory of socialism since reform and opening up.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Official term for the Party-building and anti-corruption campaign pursued since 2012, covering discipline, supervision and institutional rules.

t: The Party's system of leadership institutions continues to improve
zh: 党的领导制度体系不断完善
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily, takes up the statement in the Resolution adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021) that the system of Party leadership institutions has been continuously improved. Li Zhenghua argues that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core has made perfecting this system a priority, with notable results.

The article describes three strands of work: top-level design around the principle that Party leadership is China's fundamental leadership system; institutions that safeguard the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee; and measures to extend Party leadership to every type of organisation.

Li reports that the 19th Party Congress (2017) wrote into the Party Constitution the principle that the Party leads everything, and that the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) defined Party leadership as the fundamental leadership system. The author lists intra-Party regulations on Central Committee work, local committees, Party groups and reporting of major matters, and describes stronger decision-making and coordinating bodies, democratic centralism and political supervision tied to the Two Upholds. Li adds that Politburo members now submit annual written reports, and that the Party's leadership of the legislature, government, judiciary, armed forces, enterprises and grassroots bodies has been regularised.

Li concludes that these arrangements have built a system of Party leadership running from the centre to the grassroots, making Party leadership more mature and settled. In Li's account, this has strengthened the Party's consistency with the Central Committee and its role in coordinating all sides. Read the original if you want a concise official-line summary of the institutional measures taken to consolidate Party leadership after 2012.
quoteEn: The Party's leadership system is our country's fundamental leadership system.
quoteZh: 党的领导制度是我国的根本领导制度。

glossary.explanation: A formula requiring Party members to uphold General Secretary Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee. It became prominent after 2018.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Party, combining discussion and election with obedience of lower levels to higher levels and of the minority to the majority.
Formal rules issued by the Party's organs to govern Party organisation, conduct and work, distinct from state law.

t: The history of the Communist Party of China is a history of self-reform
zh: 一部中国共产党史就是一部自我革命史
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in May 2022, takes up the claim in the Party's 2021 historical resolution that courage in self-reform is what distinguishes the Communist Party of China from other parties. Zhang argues that the Party's hundred-year history is itself a history of self-reform, and that this capacity explains how it has survived and grown while many other communist parties collapsed.

The piece is organised in three parts. The first traces the sources and record of the Party's self-reform; the second identifies criticism and self-criticism as the means by which it is achieved; the third turns to full and rigorous self-governance of the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Zhang draws heavily on Xi Jinping, Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping, along with the 2021 resolution.

Zhang holds that self-reform as the Party's most distinctive trait comes from two sources: the nature of a Marxist party, which must keep adapting to new struggles, and Chinese traditional culture, whose self-renewing spirit the Party inherits. In this account, every major turning point, from the first United Front to the shift from a planned to a market economy, was achieved through self-reform, and the Party repeatedly recognised and corrected its own errors. Criticism and self-criticism is described as the indispensable weapon: without it, self-reform is impossible. Zhang adds that the Party must accept supervision by the people and not carry out self-reform behind closed doors.

Zhang concludes that self-reform is bound up with the Party's leadership of social revolution, and that its strength comes from the objective needs of that revolution. Since 2012, the author says, the Party has acted decisively against entrenched ills. Zhang calls on the whole Party to keep up the political awareness that full and rigorous self-governance of the Party is always a work in progress, even after the anti-corruption campaign's overwhelming victory. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-school scholars present self-reform as the key to the Party's historical continuity and its Marxist character.
quoteEn: For the Communist Party's lofty ideals and noble mission to be carried through in concrete work and struggle, it must keep carrying out self-reform as circumstances change.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的远大理想和崇高使命要落实到具体的实际的工作和斗争中去，就要根据形势的变化而不断地实现自我革命。

glossary.explanation: Official term, stressed by Xi Jinping, for the Party's capacity to correct its own errors and purify itself. Official English texts render it as 'self-reform' (or sometimes 'self-revolution').

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Policy line associated with Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering Party discipline, anti-corruption and ideological and organisational rectification.
A long-standing Party practice of airing shortcomings in meetings and correcting them, which Mao Zedong described as a Marxist-Leninist weapon.

t: The Communist Party of China's contributions to world socialism over the past century
zh: 百年来中国共产党对世界社会主义的贡献
source: Contemporary World and Socialism (Dangdai shijie yu shehuizhuyi)
paras: Taking its cue from the Resolution on the Party's century of struggle adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021), this article asks how the Communist Party of China (CPC) has contributed to world socialism. Yan argues that over its first hundred years the Party made major contributions in four areas: practical paths, theory, institutions and culture. The article presents these as part of the Resolution's claim that the Party's struggle displayed the vitality of Marxism and shaped world history.

The article is organised into four sections. The first traces three paths: the New Democratic revolution, socialist transformation and construction, and socialism with Chinese characteristics. The second covers the three theoretical achievements of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times: Mao Zedong Thought, the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The third sets out the institutional system of fundamental, basic and important institutions, and the fourth the Party's socialist culture.

Yan contends that each stage extended Marxism and the international communist movement. The Chinese revolution is described as the first case of proletarian dictatorship achieved by encircling the cities from the countryside. Reform and opening up is said to have carried China through the low ebb after the Soviet collapse and to have given developing countries a new option, which the article links to Chinese modernization. On institutions, Yan treats Party leadership as the most essential feature and attributes the Soviet collapse to weakened Party leadership and the abandonment of Marxism's guiding role in ideology. The article says the institutional system underpins what it calls "Chinese governance" against "Western chaos" amid rivalry with the United States and the West. On culture, Yan combines excellent traditional Chinese culture, revolutionary culture (the spirit of more than 90 revolutionary spirits) and advanced socialist culture.

Yan concludes that the Party has answered the historic question of what socialism is and how to build it, and that it has made the Marxist theory it developed available to other countries. The article states that the Party has grown from about fifty members to over 95 million and is the world's largest governing party. It expects the Party to contribute more to world socialism as it builds a modern socialist country in all respects. Read the original if you want a representative, official-line account of how Party scholars frame the CPC's centenary role in the history of world socialism.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China has successfully solved the historic problem of "what socialism is and how to build it".
quoteZh: 中国共产党成功破解了“什么是社会主义、怎样建设社会主义”的历史性难题。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxism to China's conditions and updating it for the present. Mao Zedong first raised "Sinification of Marxism" in 1938.
The official name for the path and system pursued in China since the reform era began in 1978. It is presented as socialism adapted to China's national conditions.
The policy launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978. It shifted the Party's focus to economic development, market-oriented reform and engagement with the world economy.
The official term for China's own path to modernization. It is presented as an alternative to Western models, especially for developing countries.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions from 2017–2018. It is described officially as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.

t: Party leadership as the fundamental guarantee for running socialist universities with Chinese characteristics well
zh: 党的领导是办好中国特色社会主义大学的根本保证
paras: Taking its cue from Xi Jinping's remarks during a visit to Renmin University of China, this commentary in Guangming Daily argues that Party leadership is the fundamental guarantee for running socialist universities with Chinese characteristics well. Sun treats Xi's call to uphold Party leadership and Marxism's guiding position, and to forge a new path to world-class universities with Chinese characteristics, as the framework for the discussion.

The piece first traces Party leadership of higher education through four periods: the new-democratic revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the years since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It then sets out four ways in which, in the author's view, Party leadership shapes universities.

Sun describes leadership as giving universities their soul of conviction, their institutional foundation, their driving force and their path of development. Conviction means passing on Marxist belief, including Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The institutional foundation is the president responsibility system under the leadership of the Party committee, together with democratic centralism and Party control over direction, cadres, talent and ideology. Leadership is also said to keep universities united and to rule out simply copying foreign models.

Sun concludes that the president responsibility system under Party committee leadership must be upheld and improved. The author also calls for stronger grassroots Party organisations and for ideological and political work to run through all teaching, so that universities remain a front line for training socialist builders and successors. Read the original if you want a short example of how official commentary justifies Party leadership in higher education.
quoteEn: Party leadership is the most essential feature and the most notable advantage of socialist universities with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 党的领导是中国特色社会主义大学最本质的特征和最显著的优势。

glossary.zh: 党委领导下的校长负责制
glossary.pinyin: dǎngwěi lǐngdǎo xià de xiàozhǎng fùzé zhì
glossary.en: the president responsibility system under the leadership of the Party committee
glossary.explanation: The governance arrangement in Chinese public universities. The Party committee leads the institution as a whole, and the president handles administration and teaching under that leadership.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Communist Party. Decisions are made collectively after discussion, and lower bodies are bound by higher ones.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

t: Three dimensions of upholding the authority of the Party Central Committee
zh: 维护党中央权威的三个维度
paras: Yuan Yinchuan and Zhang Xiaohui ask why the authority of the Party Central Committee must be upheld, and answer from three angles: theoretical, historical and contemporary. They open by rejecting what they call a Western-centric discourse that presents capitalist liberal democracy as a universal model and denies the diversity of political civilisations. Deconstructing that discourse, they argue, helps explain the Communist Party of China's century of struggle and strengthens practical commitment to the Two Upholds.

The article has three main sections. The theoretical section traces the Marxist theory of authority from Marx and Engels through Lenin. The historical section reviews the Party's revolutionary, construction and reform periods. The contemporary section links the issue to national rejuvenation, to what the authors call great changes unseen in a century, and to the Party's self-governance.

The authors argue that, for Marx and Engels, authority arises from cooperative production and takes on a class character in class society. In their account, the proletarian party needs authority to unify will against anarchists such as Bakunin, and Lenin defended the necessity of party and leader authority. The historical section treats the Zunyi Conference, the struggles against Zhang Guotao and Wang Ming, the Yan'an rectification, and Deng Xiaoping's call that the centre must have authority as lessons that the Party succeeded because its Central Committee had a core. The authors present democratic centralism as the organisational principle that joins authority with intra-Party democracy. They also hold that leaders arise from the masses and should not be exaggerated into something separate from them.

For the present, the authors contend that the Party's leading core is indispensable to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. They describe Western politics as in disorder and Chinese governance as ordered, and maintain that upholding the Centre's authority represents the people's fundamental interests rather than personal power. They stress full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, citing intra-Party regulations issued since 2012, as the means of institutionalising the Two Upholds, and call for ideological, political and practical self-awareness among Party members. Read the original if you want a representative example of how Party-school scholars ground the Two Upholds in Marxist authority theory and Party history.
quoteEn: In essence, the Two Upholds are not meant to secure personal power or protect personal interests, but to coordinate the people's collective will and realise their overall, fundamental and long-term interests.
quoteZh: “两个维护”在本质上不是为了保证个人权力和维护个人私利的需要，而是为了统筹人民整体意志实现人民群众的整体利益、根本利益和长远利益的需要。

glossary.explanation: A political requirement, formulated in 2018, to resolutely uphold General Secretary Xi Jinping's core position in the Party Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Communist Party of China, combining democratic discussion with centralised decision-making and subordination of lower levels to higher ones.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A campaign since the 18th Party Congress (2012) to tighten Party discipline, supervision and anti-corruption work, expressed in intra-Party regulations.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, associated with the Chinese Dream and the two centenary goals.

t: Ensuring that the Party always exercises overall leadership and coordinates all sides
zh: 确保党始终总揽全局协调各方
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily and posted in May 2022, takes up the Party's principle of "taking overall responsibility and coordinating the efforts of all sides". Qin and Ji argue that the Party's leadership is the fundamental guarantee for managing China's affairs and for national rejuvenation. Ensuring that the Party always plays this role is, in their view, both the key experience behind past success and the basic guarantee of future success.

The piece is written as an interpretation of the Resolution adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021) and quotes it repeatedly. It first reviews the record since the 18th Party Congress (2012), then explains why the principle remains essential in the new journey, and finally names two ways to uphold it.

The authors contend that, under the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core, the Party's leadership has been applied to all fields, and that this explains the historic achievements and changes of the new era. They present these as proof that the Party's overall leadership is the only path for sustaining and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics. Although conditions for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation are now stronger, they warn of foreseeable and unforeseeable risks. The first measure is to grasp the decisive significance of the Two Establishes and strengthen the Two Upholds. The second is to improve the institutional system of Party leadership, described as the "four beams and eight pillars", so that the Party's leadership is comprehensive, systematic and holistic.

Qin and Ji conclude that without the Communist Party there would be no national rejuvenation, and that there must be no wavering or ambiguity on this principle. They call for stronger institution-building at every level and in every area, together with more scientific, democratic and law-based governance. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary in 2022 framed the Party's overall leadership after the Sixth Plenum Resolution.
quoteEn: Ensuring that the Party always takes overall responsibility and coordinates all sides is the most precious experience behind our past success and victory, and also the most fundamental guarantee of continued success and victory in the future.
quoteZh: 确保党始终总揽全局、协调各方，这是我们过去能够成功和胜利最为宝贵的经验，也是未来继续成功和胜利最为根本的保证。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the 2021 Resolution on the Party's history, affirming Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the whole Party, and the guiding role of his thought.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream, of restoring China's national strength and international standing.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism since reform and opening up.

t: The Communist Party of China is the most reliable backbone of united struggle
zh: 中国共产党是团结奋斗最可靠的主心骨
paras: Taking its cue from Xi Jinping's statement that united struggle is the only way for the Chinese people to create great historic achievements, this newspaper commentary argues that the Communist Party of China is the Chinese people's backbone and the most reliable backbone of united struggle. Xu presents the Party's leadership as the key to both past successes and future ones.

The piece is organised under three headings: the unity of Party spirit and the people's character, a mission and goals that unite popular consensus, and institutions and mechanisms for great unity and solidarity. It runs through the Party's history from the New Democratic Revolution to the new era.

Xu first contends that the Party has no interests of its own, which makes it, in the author's account, the one force able to unify the people. Late Qing and republican-era reformers, by contrast, lacked the political vision and selflessness for lasting unity. Second, Xu reviews how the united front changed with each period's tasks, from the anti-Japanese national united front to the current drive for common prosperity. Third, Xu lists six institutional arrangements under Xi Jinping: the new type of party system, work with non-Party intellectuals, forging a strong sense of community among the Chinese nation, the sinicization of religion, guiding non-public-sector entrepreneurs, and mobilising compatriots in Hong Kong, Macao, Taiwan and overseas.

Xu concludes that Party leadership, shared goals and institutional guarantees together turn unity into a lasting capacity for struggle. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary in 2022 framed the united front and the Party's leading role in national unity.
quoteEn: This high degree of unity between Party spirit and the people's character gives rise to, and consolidates, the firmest and most reliable united struggle.
quoteZh: 这种党性与人民性的高度统一，孕育和凝结着最为坚强和可靠的团结奋斗

glossary.explanation: A Party strategy of building alliances with non-Party groups and social forces, including other parties, ethnic and religious groups, and entrepreneurs, to support its goals.
The official description of China's system of multi-party cooperation under Communist Party leadership, which it presents as distinct from Western party systems.

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: forging a strong sense of community among the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: forge a firm consciousness of the Chinese nation as a community
glossary.explanation: A line of ethnic policy emphasised under Xi Jinping that stresses a shared national identity across China's ethnic groups.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, given greater emphasis in Party policy in the new era.

t: Keeping the destiny of China's development and progress firmly in our own hands
zh: 把中国发展进步的命运牢牢掌握在自己手中
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily in May 2022, argues that China must keep the destiny of its development and progress firmly in its own hands. Sun Laibin presents "walking our own path" as a historical conclusion drawn from a century of Party struggle and as a requirement for the new journey towards the second centenary goal. The author holds that, whatever risks arise, the Party will lead the people along the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, upholding independence and self-reliance.

The article has three parts. The first reviews the Party's century through four stages: the new-democratic revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era. It relies on the resolution adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). The second part explains why control over China's fate is necessary, and the third sets out what steady progress towards the second centenary goal requires.

Sun's central claim is that every achievement of the Party and people came through struggle, not as a gift from others. The author gives three reasons for self-reliance now. Chinese modernization has no ready-made model, since modernization takes more than one form and China's culture, history and national conditions require its own path. Rising risks near the goal of national rejuvenation, in a world undergoing great changes unseen in a century, call for strategic composure. Finally, Sun contends that no nation has become strong by depending on outside forces or copying foreign models, and that the new development pattern, whose essence is high-level self-reliance, secures the initiative in development. The article says China welcomes useful suggestions and learning from others but rejects lecturing from self-appointed "schoolmasters".

Sun calls for three commitments: unwavering adherence to Party leadership, described as the defining feature and greatest strength of the system; firm adherence to socialism with Chinese characteristics, avoiding both the "old closed and rigid path" and the "evil path of changing banners"; and strategic composure, including pursuing reform and opening up at a higher level. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official line on independence, self-reliance and the Party's historical experience was presented to a general readership in 2022.
quoteEn: In human history, no nation or country has become strong and rejuvenated by relying on external forces, copying foreign models, or trailing step by step behind others.
quoteZh: 人类历史上没有一个民族、一个国家可以通过依赖外部力量、照搬外国模式、跟在他人后面亦步亦趋实现强大和振兴。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's own path to modernization, stressed from the 20th Party Congress (2022) on. Its stated features include a huge population, common prosperity, material and cultural-ethical advancement, harmony between humanity and nature, and peaceful development.
The official name for the Party's theory, path and system since the reform era, presented as Marxism adapted to Chinese conditions.
The goal of building a modern socialist country that is prosperous, strong, democratic, culturally advanced and harmonious by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic.

An economic strategy announced in 2020 that takes the domestic cycle as the mainstay, with domestic and international cycles reinforcing each other. It stresses self-reliance in technology and supply chains.

glossary.literal: great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's overarching goal of restoring China to a position of wealth, strength and international standing after the "century of humiliation".
The policy launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping, introducing market-oriented reforms and engagement with the global economy.

t: Firmly establishing a correct view of Party history
zh: 牢固树立正确党史观
paras: Writing in 2022, after the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021) adopted its resolution on the Party's history, Wang Guang takes up the question of what outlook should guide the study of the Communist Party's past. The author argues that one's view of history largely determines one's attitude and method towards it. On this basis Wang contends that the Party must firmly establish a "correct view of Party history" grounded in historical materialism, as Xi Jinping has repeatedly stressed.

The commentary rests on three arguments for why this matters: a correct view is needed to understand the Party's hundred-year struggle, to reveal historical laws that guide the Party and the country, and to oppose historical nihilism. It draws throughout on Xi Jinping's statements and the plenum communiqué. It places the Party's centenary at the meeting point of the "two centenary goals", linking modern China's suffering with the goal of national rejuvenation.

Wang's first claim is that earlier struggles, from the Taiping movement to the 1911 Revolution, failed for lack of scientific theory and an advanced class force, whereas the Party succeeded by integrating Marxism with Chinese realities and traditional culture. The second is that recognising historical law is, in Marxist terms, the dividing line between materialist and idealist history. The author presents the Party's century as a history of exploring and applying such laws, and says Xi's innovations deepened understanding of the laws of Communist Party governance, socialist construction and human social development. Third, Wang describes historical nihilism as exaggerating errors, sensationalising Party history or reading it as gossip, and cites Xi's view that Soviet collapse followed the wholesale negation of Soviet history.

Wang reports that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Party has set the record straight, neither hiding mistakes because of achievements nor denying achievements because of mistakes, and that nihilism has been firmly curbed. The author adds that more research and more popular forms of communication are needed so that the orthodox history becomes a shared consensus. The piece closes by calling on the Party to follow Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and draw spiritual strength for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars in 2022 framed the official view of Party history and the campaign against historical nihilism.
quoteEn: The kind of view of history one holds determines the kind of understanding of history one arrives at.
quoteZh: 有什么样的历史观,就会有什么样的历史认知。

glossary.explanation: In official Chinese usage, a label for views seen as distorting or negating the Party's and the PRC's history, including its mistakes and setbacks. The term is used in Party discourse to criticise such interpretations.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, presented as overcoming the 'century of humiliation' and restoring China's strength and standing.

A concept stressed by Xi Jinping, meaning an approach to the Party's history based on historical materialism that affirms its mainstream and essence. It was emphasised during the 2021 Party history study campaign.
Official goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021 and a modern socialist country by the PRC's centenary in 2049.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official name for Xi Jinping's body of ideas, written into the Party and state constitutions as a guiding ideology.

t: The core meaning, formation logic and contemporary call of the great founding spirit of the Party
zh: 伟大建党精神的核心要义、生成逻辑及时代呼唤
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (Sixiang lilun jiaoyu daokan), 2022 no. 4
paras: Writing in 2022, shortly after Xi Jinping's speech at the centenary of the Communist Party of China (2021), Zhang Guozuo and Liu Xinwei take up the "great founding spirit" of the Party that Xi summarised in four pairs of phrases. The article asks what this spirit means, why it arose and why the new era needs it. Its thesis is that the spirit has four inseparable dimensions, arises necessarily from theory, history and practice, and must be upheld today.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the core meaning of the four dimensions: adhering to truth and ideals, putting the original aspiration into practice and shouldering the mission, fearing no sacrifice and fighting bravely, and being loyal to the Party and not failing the people. The second explains how the spirit was formed. The third turns to the present and shows what each dimension requires in the new era. Examples include revolutionary, Korean War, construction-era and new-era heroes, and model Communists such as Wang Jinxi, Jiao Yulu and Lei Feng.

Zhang and Liu identify "truth" with Marxism and "ideals" with communism and, for China, socialism with Chinese characteristics. They read the Party's original aspiration and mission as seeking happiness for the Chinese people and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Loyalty to the Party and the people expresses the unity of Party spirit and the people's character. The authors stress that the four dimensions form one whole: without practice, loyalty and sacrifice, "adhering to truth" becomes empty talk. The spirit's formation is explained in three logics. Theoretically, Marxism is scientific, practical, revolutionary and people-centred. Historically, earlier attempts at national salvation failed for lack of scientific theory, firm ideals, devotion and roots among the people. Practically, great revolutionary, construction and reform practice necessarily produces a great spirit, and the later spirits in the Party's "spiritual lineage", such as the Jinggangshan, Long March and Yan'an spirits, derive from it.

For the present, the authors argue that adhering to truth and ideals lets the Party resist erroneous trends they name, including historical nihilism, "universal values", neoliberalism and Western constitutional democracy. Putting the original aspiration into practice is needed for the long relay toward national rejuvenation. The fighting spirit is needed for the long, complex struggles that Xi has warned of. Loyalty to the Party and the people is presented as what preserves the Party's advanced nature and purity. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned exposition of how Chinese Party theorists structure and justify the founding spirit, in the framework Xi set out in 2021.
quoteEn: Great practice will inevitably give birth to a great spirit.
quoteZh: 伟大的实践必然会孕育出伟大的精神。

glossary.explanation: A formula Xi Jinping presented on 1 July 2021: upholding truth and ideals, practising the original aspiration and mission, fearing no sacrifice, and being loyal to the Party and the people. Official discourse treats it as the source of the Party's later "spiritual lineage".
The Party's officially stated founding purpose: seeking happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation. It was made a central slogan in Party-building campaigns from 2019.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official name for the national goal of restoring China's strength and standing after the "century of humiliation". It is the central theme of Party narratives of its own history.
The official name for the path, theory and system developed since reform and opening up began in 1978. It is presented as Marxism applied to Chinese conditions.
The official term for the series of named "spirits" (Jinggangshan, Long March, Yan'an and others) said to have arisen in the Party's history. It is used in Party education.
In official Chinese usage, a label for views that question or negate the Party's revolutionary history and the socialist path. Authors who use it typically treat it as an ideological threat.

t: The resolute leadership of the Communist Party of China
zh: 中国共产党的坚强领导
paras: Song Yuehong takes up the question of why the Communist Party of China's leadership is, in Xi Jinping's words, the fundamental political guarantee for calmly meeting major risks and challenges. The article argues that Party leadership is a historical necessity and the choice of the people. In Song's account it is the foundation and lifeblood of the Party and state, and it is tied to the interests and fate of all ethnic groups in China.

This is a short commentary published in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2022, after the Party's centenary and the 19th Party Congress period. It is organised as five "always" principles: putting the people first, remembering the original aspiration and mission, playing the role of leadership core that oversees the overall situation and coordinates all parties, daring to struggle and being good at winning, and carrying out self-reform. Each section links the Party's historical record, especially since the 18th Party Congress (2012), to its present role.

Song contends that the Party's roots, strength and legitimacy lie in the people. In this reading, the people were liberated from oppression through the founding of the new China, and the Party's "people-centred" approach has since produced a moderately prosperous society and a rise in the people's sense of fulfilment and security. The article holds that Party leadership is comprehensive and systematic, covers economic, political, cultural, social, ecological, military, diplomatic and Party-building work, and has been strengthened by improving the institutions of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the system of national governance. Song cites the poverty-alleviation campaign and the response to COVID-19 as proof of the Party's organising capacity. The author presents full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, including the anti-corruption campaign, as the means by which the Party escapes the "historical cycle" and keeps its vanguard character.

Song concludes that only by upholding Party leadership can the people be given a better life and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation be achieved. The author maintains that the Party's leadership, its institutions and its self-reform must be sustained over the long term, and that these have enabled the nation's leap from "standing up" to "becoming prosperous" to "becoming strong". Read the original if you want a compact example of how the official case for Party leadership was framed in 2022, in the vocabulary of the new era.
quoteEn: Party leadership is the most essential feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the greatest strength of the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 党的领导是中国特色社会主义最本质的特征，是中国特色社会主义制度的最大优势。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012) covering Party discipline, supervision and the anti-corruption campaign.
The official name for China's path, theory and system since the reform era. Official texts treat it as Marxism applied to Chinese conditions.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream and with achieving a strong modern socialist country.
An official concept for the Party's continuous internal purification and improvement, presented as the way the Party avoids degeneration.
A long-standing development goal. Officials declared it fully built in 2021.

t: The six shifts in the Communist Party of China's theory of inter-party relations in the new era
zh: 论新时代中国共产党党际关系理论的六大转换
paras: How has the Communist Party of China's thinking on its relations with foreign parties changed since the 18th Party Congress (2012)? Yang and Yu argue that the four principles of inter-party relations (independence, complete equality, mutual respect, non-interference in internal affairs), set out at the 12th Party Congress in 1982, have entered a stage of "sublimation". They hold that Xi Jinping's call for a "new type of party relations" inherits and develops those principles, and they identify six shifts in the theory.

The article first reviews existing research, which stresses four "new" features of the new-era guiding thinking: its theoretical basis, the way it defines party functions, its focus and its value goal. The authors say this work is mostly single-angle and propose a comprehensive reading. They then examine six dimensions: strategic guideline, strategic thinking, premise and foundation, strategic focus, partners and scope, and external communication. A further section analyses the forces driving the changes, and a closing section looks ahead.

In the authors' account, each shift moves from a reform-era position to a new-era one. The guideline moves from stressing economic development to stressing political support; thinking moves from integrating into the world to shaping it; the foundation moves from the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence to a "new type of international relations"; the focus moves from non-interference to mutual learning; and the scope moves from bilateral to multilateral ties. External communication moves from "connecting China and the world" to "bridging" them. Three drivers are named: the global governance deficit, the changing world party landscape (the decline of established parties and the rise of populist ones after the 2008 crisis), and the need to turn China's strength into international discourse power. The authors add that the shift in premise is "not absolute", since the Five Principles still matter.

Yang and Yu propose three directions. Parties should promote global governance through international party cooperation, rejecting unilateral dominance and building institutional platforms. They should advance the new type of party relations through exchange of governance experience, especially on Party building. And they should use home-hosted platforms organised by the Party to convert national strength into international discourse power. Read the original if you want a detailed Chinese-language account of how Party scholars frame the continuity and change in the Party's foreign-party work since 2012, with the main speeches and summits cited.
quoteEn: The shift from integrating into the world to shaping the world is a change of thinking made by the Communist Party of China as it adjusts the goals of its external engagement.
quoteZh: 从融入世界到塑造世界的转换，是中国共产党在调适对外交往目标中进行的思维性转变。

glossary.explanation: Independence, complete equality, mutual respect and non-interference in each other's internal affairs. They were formally set out in the report to the 12th Party Congress in 1982 as the basis for the Party's relations with foreign parties.

A formulation associated with Xi Jinping after 2012, calling for party ties built on seeking common ground while reserving differences, mutual respect and mutual learning. It is presented as resting on a "new type of international relations".

Principles of mutual respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, non-aggression, non-interference, equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful coexistence. China put them forward in the 1950s as the basis of its foreign relations.

t: Party leadership as the fundamental guarantee for running universities with socialist characteristics well
zh: 党的领导是办好中国特色社会主义大学的根本保证
paras: This short commentary in Guangming Daily (May 2022) responds to Xi Jinping's inspection visit to Renmin University of China. Sun Liang argues that Party leadership is the fundamental guarantee for building universities with Chinese characteristics and a world-class standing. Sun treats it as the most essential feature and most distinctive strength of such universities.

The piece first sketches the Party's leadership of higher education across four periods: the new-democratic revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the years since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It then sets out four ways in which Party leadership supports universities, and closes with practical requirements.

In Sun's account, Party leadership provides a soul of conviction, since it secures the transmission of Marxist belief and the study of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. It also provides an institutional foundation, chiefly the presidential responsibility system under the leadership of the Party committee, together with democratic centralism and Party control over direction, cadres, talent and ideology. It supplies a driving force, keeping thought, action and strength unified. And it charts a development path, because Sun, citing Xi, holds that Chinese universities should not copy foreign models.

Sun concludes that the Party committee-led presidential responsibility system must be upheld and improved. Sun also calls for stronger grassroots Party organisations, fostering virtue through education as the central task, and ideological and political work throughout teaching. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary frames Party leadership in higher education after Xi's 2022 visit to Renmin University.
quoteEn: Party leadership is the most essential feature and the most notable strength of universities with socialist characteristics.
quoteZh: 党的领导是中国特色社会主义大学最本质的特征和最显著的优势。

glossary.zh: 党委领导下的校长负责制
glossary.pinyin: dǎngwěi lǐngdǎo xià de xiàozhǎng fùzé zhì
glossary.en: presidential responsibility system under the leadership of the Party committee
glossary.literal: president responsibility system under Party committee leadership
glossary.explanation: The governance system in Chinese public universities in which the Party committee takes overall leadership and the president manages daily academic and administrative work. It was reaffirmed in a 2014 Party document and a further implementation opinion.
An educational aim stressed in Party documents: schools should shape students' moral and political character as well as impart knowledge. It is called the fundamental task of education.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Communist Party, combining discussion with binding, unified decisions. The article applies it to university Party committees.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented officially as the Marxism of contemporary China and of the twenty-first century.

t: The history of the Communist Party of China is a history of self-reform
zh: 一部中国共产党史就是一部自我革命史
paras: This newspaper commentary, written after the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021), asks why the Communist Party of China has endured and grown over a century. Zhang Taiyuan answers that the Party's willingness to carry out self-reform is its most distinctive trait and its greatest strength. On this reading, the history of the Party's cause and the history of its own growth are one and the same: a history of self-reform.

The piece opens with Xi Jinping's remarks and the Party's 2021 historical resolution, then proceeds in three steps. It first shows how the Party has demonstrated self-reform in practice. It then turns to criticism and self-criticism as the means by which self-reform is achieved. Finally it takes up the Party's present drive for full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, drawing throughout on Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi.

Zhang argues that the trait comes from two sources: the nature of a Marxist party, which must keep adapting to new struggles in pursuit of communism, and Chinese traditional culture, which the author says gives the Party something no other party or political force possesses. The Party's strength is said to have formed in revolutionary history, since every major turning point, from the First United Front to the shift from a planned to a market economy, was achieved through self-reform. A typical form is correcting its own mistakes, and reform and opening up is presented as having drawn its impetus from reflection on earlier errors. Criticism and self-criticism are called both the typical expression of self-reform and the only route to it, and Zhang stresses that the Party must accept supervision by the people rather than reform behind closed doors.

Zhang concludes that the Party's self-reform is bound up with its social revolution and decides its rise or fall. The author points to the campaign since the 18th Party Congress (2012) against entrenched ills and corruption, and quotes Xi that the work remains "always on the road" and that weariness must not set in. If the Party keeps up self-reform and preserves its advanced and pure character, the author holds, it will keep its Marxist character and remain invincible. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how Party scholars present self-reform as the key to the CPC's historical success.
quoteEn: Every major turning point and every major change in the cause of the Communist Party of China was achieved by persisting in self-reform.
quoteZh: 中国共产党事业的每一次重大转折，每一次重大变化，都是在坚持自我革命中实现的。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed under Xi Jinping: the Party's capacity to correct its own errors and purify itself. The 2021 historical resolution calls it a mark distinguishing the CPC from other parties.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party-discipline and anti-corruption drive that has been pursued since the 18th Party Congress in 2012.
A long-standing Party practice of mutual and personal critique within the Party, described in Marxist-Leninist tradition as a means of correcting mistakes.

glossary.zh: 中共中央关于党的百年奋斗重大成就和历史经验的决议
glossary.pinyin: Zhōnggòng Zhōngyāng guānyú dǎng de bǎinián fèndòu zhòngdà chéngjiù hé lìshǐ jīngyàn de juéyì
glossary.literal: Resolution of the CPC Central Committee on the Major Achievements and Historical Experience of the Party over the Past Century
glossary.explanation: A document adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee in November 2021, giving the Party's authoritative assessment of its first hundred years.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: "To achieve the complete liberation and independence of the Chinese nation"
st: The Party's accounts of and responses to the September 18 Incident, and their historical significance for national rejuvenation
zh: “以求中华民族彻底的解放和独立”
zhSub: 我们党对九一八事变的论述与应对及其对民族复兴的历史意义
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in May 2022, Zhang Hao asks how the Chinese Communist Party understood and answered the September 18 Incident of 1931, the Japanese seizure of north-east China, and what that meant for national rejuvenation. Starting from Xi Jinping's description of the incident as the starting point of China's War of Resistance and the prologue to the world anti-fascist war, Zhang argues that the Party saw early on that the incident was historically inevitable. Zhang holds that its statements and policies pointed the way from national crisis towards the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article draws on Party declarations, resolutions, newspaper editorials and writings by leaders including Mao Zedong, Zhou Enlai, Zhang Wentian, Wang Jiaxiang, Dong Biwu and Qin Bangxian, from 1931 to 1946. It is divided into two parts. The first covers the Party's analysis of why the incident occurred and what it signified. The second covers how Party policy shifted in response.

In the first part, Zhang reports the Party's argument that the incident followed from Japan's long-planned continental policy. The sources Zhang cites name several causes: economic crisis in Japan, hostility towards the Soviet Union, the Guomindang's non-resistance, and support from other imperialist powers. Zhang also reports that Party statements, from the 1931 declaration through Zhou Enlai's later essays, treated the incident as the beginning of a second world war and of fascist aggression in Asia. In the second part, Zhang traces a turn from domestic revolutionary war to a national war of liberation. The Party criticised non-resistance and reliance on the League of Nations, moved towards the anti-Japanese national united front, and began a new stage of armed struggle. It also developed the view that patriotism is internationalism applied in a national revolutionary war, and tied this to a world anti-fascist united front. Zhang presents this as the Party's renewed exploration of the path of new-democratic revolution.

Zhang concludes that the incident, though the first step of a war that brought great suffering, also gave the Chinese nation the chance to stand up. After fourteen years of resistance, which Zhang calls the first complete victory over foreign invasion in modern times, the Party's persistence in fighting to the end is said to have ended a century of humiliation and nurtured new hope of rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a source-based Chinese Communist Party account of how its wartime leaders interpreted 1931 and linked it to national independence and rejuvenation.
quoteEn: The September 18 Incident inspired in our Party a great spirit of advancing courageously for national independence and national rejuvenation.
quoteZh: 九一八事变，激发了我们党为民族独立和民族复兴而勇往直前的伟大精神。

glossary.explanation: The 1931 Japanese military action at Shenyang that led to the occupation of north-east China (Manchuria). Chinese official history treats it as the start of the War of Resistance against Japan.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal of the Communist Party, referring to restoring China's strength and international standing after the 'century of humiliation'.
The Party's policy of uniting classes and parties against Japanese aggression. It took shape in the mid-1930s and involved cooperation with the Guomindang.
Mao Zedong's concept of the stage of Chinese revolution led by the proletariat against imperialism, feudalism and bureaucrat-capitalism, preceding socialism.
The Marxist principle of solidarity among workers and nations across borders. Here the article cites Mao's claim that it is consistent with revolutionary patriotism.

t: The Party's system of leadership institutions continues to be improved
zh: 党的领导制度体系不断完善
paras: This short commentary, published in the People's Daily in May 2022, takes up a line from the Resolution adopted by the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021): that the system of Party leadership institutions has been continuously improved. Li Zhenghua argues that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core has given priority to building this system, with many new rules and notable results.

The piece is organised in three parts: top-level design around the idea that the Party's leadership system is the country's fundamental leadership system; institutions for upholding the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee; and measures to consolidate foundations, build on strengths and address weaknesses.

Li reports that the 19th Party Congress (2017) wrote into the Party constitution the principle that the Party leads everything, and that the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) defined the Party's leadership system as the fundamental one. The author lists Party regulations on Central Committee work, local committees, Party groups and reporting of major matters, together with stronger decision-making and coordinating bodies, democratic centralism, Party political building and political oversight centred on the Two Upholds. Li also cites the Party's leadership over the legislature, government, courts, armed forces, enterprises and grassroots organisations, and annual work reports to the Central Committee.

Li concludes that these arrangements form a leadership system running from the centre to the grassroots, ensuring the Party's leading role in all kinds of organisations. In Li's account, this has strengthened consistency with the Central Committee and the Party's capacity to govern. Read the original if you want a compact, official-line overview of the Party regulations and institutional measures presented as consolidating Party leadership after 2012.
quoteEn: This series of major institutional arrangements has established and improved a system of Party leadership institutions running from the centre to the grassroots, and has effectively ensured that the Party plays its leading role in organisations of every level and type.
quoteZh: 这一系列重大制度性安排，建立健全了从中央到基层的党的领导制度体系，有力保证了党在各级各类组织中领导作用的发挥。

glossary.explanation: A formula requiring Party members to uphold Xi Jinping's core position on the Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee. It became prominent after 2018.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Communist Party, combining discussion and election with strict subordination of lower levels to higher ones and of the minority to the majority.
Formal rules issued by the Party that govern its organisation and members' conduct, distinct from state law.
Party bodies set up inside non-Party state or social institutions, such as government departments, to ensure the Party's leadership there.

t: Providing a fundamental political guarantee for the development of the Party and the state
zh: 为党和国家事业发展提供根本政治保证
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in May 2022, Xu Weixin takes up the first of the 13 areas in which the Party's 2021 historical resolution (adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee) records achievements of the new era: upholding the Party's overall leadership. Xu argues that this has been one of the most important achievements since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and is the fundamental political guarantee for the continued opening of new prospects for socialism with Chinese characteristics.

The commentary has three parts. It first presents theoretical innovations in Xi Jinping's thinking on Party leadership. It then reviews practical results under three headings: a more complete system of institutions, a tighter organisational system, and more sound mechanisms and methods.
