It ends with three requirements for ensuring that the Party remains a strong leadership core.

On theory, Xu presents Xi's claims that Party leadership is the defining feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics and that it must be comprehensive, systematic and holistic, covering every sphere from the economy and culture to national defence, foreign affairs and Party building. Xu singles out the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee as the highest principle of that leadership. On practice, the author cites writing the Party's leadership into the Constitution, new Party regulations on propaganda, united front, political-legal and national security work, and reforms creating or upgrading central commissions and leading groups. Xu also lists the strengthening of grassroots organisations, a cadre selection and management system, and requirements for reporting to the centre, political supervision and inspection.

Looking ahead, Xu calls for a firm grasp of the decisive significance of the Two Establishes and for the Two Upholds to be put into practice. Xu also calls for keeping a people-centred position, with the Party representing no special interests and working towards common prosperity, and for the Party to play its role of overseeing the whole situation and coordinating all parties. The aim is to mobilise society for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how Party leadership is presented in Party media after the 2021 resolution, including the institutional measures it cites.
quoteEn: Upholding the Party's overall leadership is one of the most important achievements since the 18th Party Congress, and the fundamental political guarantee for socialism with Chinese characteristics continually opening up new prospects.
quoteZh: 坚持党的全面领导，是党的十八大以来取得的最重要的成就之一，是中国特色社会主义事业不断开创新局面的根本政治保证。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the 2021 historical resolution: establishing Xi Jinping's position as core of the Central Committee and of the whole Party, and establishing the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought. It is presented as decisive for the Party's future.
The requirement that Party members firmly uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.
A long-standing socialist goal, emphasised under Xi Jinping, of prosperity shared by all the people rather than a few.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, presented as restoring China to national strength and prosperity by the mid-twenty-first century.
The principle that the Communist Party leads all sectors of state and society, including government, military, economy and culture.

t: The forms, course and lessons of the evolution of the Communist Party of China's discourse on long-term governance
zh: 中国共产党长期执政话语演进的形态、历程与启示
paras: Yang Binbin asks how the Communist Party of China (CPC) has talked about its own long-term governance (长期执政) over the past century, and what that vocabulary reveals. The article argues that the discourse is a key part of Party political language and records a historical change in the Party's view of governance: its grasp of the laws of ruling, its summing-up of experience and its growing capacity. Yang notes that the 6th Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021) listed how to build a Marxist party in long-term power as one of the major questions answered by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the discourse's basic forms: long-term governance as a concept, as a body of propositions and judgements, and as a mission. The second traces its history through three periods: socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era. The third draws lessons for how Party discourse should be used and built. Yang draws on speeches and Party documents from Jiang Zemin to Xi Jinping.

Yang argues that the concept moved from a descriptive account of a Party already long in office to a normative demand that it stay in power. It first appeared in a Jiang Zemin speech on corruption and bureaucratism and was later developed into terms such as the 'long-term governing party'. Propositions such as long-term governance as a 'test', rule by law and the 'historical cycle' problem are said to show deepening understanding, as are judgements such as 'corruption is the greatest threat' and 'divorce from the masses is the greatest danger'. Yang then presents long-term governance as a political mission with three aspects: awareness, resolve and capacity. The article contrasts the CPC with Western bourgeois parties, for which office is said to serve particular interests. Across the periods, Yang describes a shift from theoretical proposition to practical task, then to system-building, and finally to the Party's self-reform and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

Yang draws three lessons. Long-term governance discourse should guide the Party's political leadership, ideological influence and organisational strength, in part by raising the political ability of the 'key minority' of officials. It should also be built into a coherent system of concepts, discourse and theory that explains the strengths of China's institutions, and Yang recommends standardising the phrase 'long-term governing Marxist party'. Finally, it should win popular recognition through education in Party history and by presenting the Party's rule as people-centred, scientific and modern. Read the original if you want a close, Party-internal account of how the vocabulary of long-term rule was formed and how Chinese scholars propose to use it.
quoteEn: Long-term governance, as a political principle, should be turned into the inner identification and conscious action of the people.
quoteZh: 长期执政作为一种政治原则应当转化为人民群众的内在认同和自觉行动。

glossary.explanation: The Party's term for its continuing rule as the governing party. It came into wide use after Jiang Zemin, and the article treats it as a concept, a set of propositions and a mission.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping-era policy of strict Party discipline, anti-corruption work and Party-building, presented as the basis for staying in power.
Official idea that the Party can purify and renew itself without outside checks. It is offered as the answer to the 'historical cycle' of rise and decline.
The pattern of dynasties rising and falling. Huang Yanpei raised it with Mao Zedong in the 1945 'cave dwelling conversation', and Mao answered that democracy and supervision would avoid it.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.

t: The significance for our times of upholding the Party's overall leadership
zh: 坚持党的全面领导的时代意蕴
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in May 2022, Guo Qingsong takes up Xi Jinping's formulation at that year's Two Sessions of "five musts" (five paths that must be followed) and "five favourable conditions" for China's development. Guo notes that upholding Party leadership comes first in both lists. The article's thesis is that in the new era, sustaining socialism with Chinese characteristics and the cause of the Party and state requires upholding the Party's overall leadership.

The commentary is organised in six numbered sections. Each presents Party leadership as the necessary basis for one goal: building a Marxist party in long-term power; upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics; building a modern socialist country in all respects; achieving common prosperity; realising the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation; and promoting a community with a shared future for mankind. Guo draws mainly on Xi Jinping's statements, the 19th Party Congress (2017) and the 2021 Party resolution on history.

Guo argues that the Party has written "the Party leads everything" into its constitution and Party leadership into the state constitution, giving overall leadership an institutional form. In Guo's account, the Party has given two answers to the historical cycle of rise and decline: popular supervision, as Mao Zedong said at Yan'an, and now the Party's self-reform. Guo holds that institutions are fundamental and long-term, so strengthening the system of Party leadership lets the country meet risks by keeping direction, balancing interests and pursuing reform. On common prosperity, Guo says it is a political as well as an economic matter. It requires Party-led work on regional, urban–rural and income gaps, stronger redistribution, "traffic lights" for capital, and regulation that harnesses its positive role while curbing its negative effects. For the Chinese Dream, Guo says the Party secures the Chinese path, spirit and strength.

Guo concludes that, amid what the Party calls great changes unseen in a century, Party leadership ensures that China pursues its own rejuvenation within humanity's shared development. In Guo's account, the Party advances a globally shared approach to governance and a more just world order. The piece is a representative statement of the official case for Party leadership as a precondition for each national goal. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-school commentary in 2022 linked Party leadership to modernization, common prosperity and foreign policy.
quoteEn: Common prosperity is linked not only to the productive forces, involving the possession of wealth and income distribution, but also to the relations of production, involving social fairness and justice and the institutions and mechanisms of political and economic operation.
quoteZh: 共同富裕不仅同生产力相关联，涉及财富占有、收入分配等内容，而且同生产关系相关联，涉及社会公平正义、政治经济运行体制机制等内容。

glossary.explanation: The principle, stressed since the 18th Party Congress (2012), that the Communist Party leads all fields of work, summed up in the formula that the Party leads everything. It was written into the Party constitution and the state constitution.

A term in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse for the Party's continuing effort to address its own problems through discipline and anti-corruption. It is presented as the second answer to the historical cycle of rise and decline.
A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all. It was given new policy prominence under Xi Jinping, with emphasis on narrowing regional, urban–rural and income gaps.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official national goal of restoring China's strength and standing, closely associated with the Chinese Dream proposed by Xi Jinping in 2012.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept, put forward from 2012–13, of a world of interdependent states pursuing common development and security.

t: Leading the great social revolution through the great self-reform
zh: 以伟大自我革命引领伟大社会革命
paras: This short commentary in the People's Daily takes up the tenth of the "ten clarifications" in the resolution on the Party's century of struggle adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021): leading the great social revolution through the Party's great self-reform. Liu argues that the formula has a Marxist theoretical basis, rests on the Party's historical experience and marks a defining feature of governance in the new era, and calls for study and implementation of Xi Jinping's strategic thinking on the Party's self-reform.

The article is organised in three parts, each beginning with the same phrase: the theoretical logic in Marx and Engels, the lessons of the Party's hundred years, and the practice since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It closes with a short call to action for the road to the second centenary goal.

Liu reasons that Marx and Engels described the abolition of class exploitation as the deepest social revolution, one that does not occur spontaneously and needs a real social force. An advanced party can play that role only if it arms itself with theory, stays close to the people, clears away negative phenomena and keeps discipline, so a Marxist party must carry out self-reform as well as social revolution. In Liu's account, the Party's history shows the two reinforcing each other. Since 2012, full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, covering political, ideological, organisational, conduct, discipline and institutional building, is said to have removed serious hidden dangers and found a way to escape the historical cycle of rise and fall.

Liu concludes that on the "new road to the test" towards the second centenary goal, the Party must keep up its self-reform and improve its capacity for self-purification, self-improvement, self-renewal and self-advancement, so that it does not change in character. Read the original if you want a concise, officially framed statement of how Party-building discourse links self-reform to the wider revolutionary project.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China's hundred-year history is both a magnificent history of social revolution and a history of self-reform that cleanses the foul and promotes the good.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的百年历史，既是一部波澜壮阔的社会革命史，也是一部激浊扬清的自我革命史。

glossary.explanation: Official term for the Party's efforts to discipline, purify and renew itself, stressed in Xi Jinping-era Party-building. It is presented as the counterpart of the Party's leadership of social revolution.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A strategy since 2012 that combines anti-corruption work, discipline and Party-building across political, ideological, organisational, conduct and institutional fields.
A ten-point summary of the core content of Xi Jinping Thought, set out in the 2021 Party resolution on the century of struggle.

glossary.en: historical cycle of rise and fall
glossary.literal: jumping out of the historical cycle rate
glossary.explanation: A phrase tied to a 1945 exchange between Mao Zedong and Huang Yanpei about regimes that flourish and then decline. Party discourse uses it to claim that the Party can avoid such a fate.

glossary.literal: new road to sit the examination
glossary.explanation: A metaphor, drawn from Mao's 1949 remark about going to the capital to "take the exam", for the Party's current tasks and its need to prove itself.

t: Full and rigorous self-governance of the Party as a great practice of the Party's self-reform in the new era
zh: 全面从严治党是新时代党的自我革命伟大实践
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in May 2022, Li Zhiyong takes up the question of how the Communist Party of China can stay vital as a long-ruling Marxist party. Li's answer is that full and rigorous self-governance of the Party is the necessary path. In the article's account, it is the Party's self-reform in practice, and it allows the "great self-reform" to lead the "great social revolution".

The commentary opens with Xi Jinping's formulations and has three sections. The first assesses what the policy has done since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second sets out the lessons Li draws from the experience. The third lists tasks for the new journey towards the second centenary goal. It is a Party-building piece, not a scholarly study, and it relies on official wording throughout.

Li makes three main moves. First, Xi's statements on the subject are said to have enriched Marxist Party-building doctrine by answering what kind of long-ruling party to build and how. Li says the results include a reversal of earlier laxity, an "overwhelming victory" in the anti-corruption struggle, a stronger Party organisation and a fuller system of Party regulations. Second, Li calls this the "second answer" to the "cave question" of escaping the historical cycle of rise and fall. Mao Zedong's first answer was to let the people supervise the government. Third, Li draws lessons: uphold the Party's overall leadership; let political development lead; treat ideological work as foundational; implement the Party's organisational line; keep up work on conduct, discipline and anti-corruption; and govern the Party through institutions and regulations.

Looking ahead, Li calls for planning self-governance within the overall cause of the Party and the state, with political development in the lead. Li also urges resolving problems that people complain about most, such as those in education, healthcare, pensions, the environment and food and drug safety, and keeping a strict tone for the long term with responsibility firmly placed. Read the original if you want a compact example of the official line on Party self-governance, as stated by a senior Party-building official shortly before the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: The facts fully show that full and rigorous self-governance of the Party is not only a strategic policy the Party must long uphold in advancing its self-reform, but also a strategic choice that must be long upheld to unite the people, drive development and achieve rejuvenation.
quoteZh: 事实充分说明，全面从严治党不仅是党推进自我革命必须长期坚持的战略方针，而且是凝聚人民、推动发展、实现复兴必须长期坚持的战略抉择。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: Party-building policy emphasised since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It covers discipline, anti-corruption, ideological education and the strengthening of Party regulations.
Official term for the Party's efforts to purify, improve and renew itself without external pressure. Xi Jinping presents it as the Party's answer to the risks of long-term rule.
Refers to a 1945 exchange in Yan'an in which Huang Yanpei raised the problem of the historical cycle of rise and fall. Mao Zedong replied that popular supervision of government was the answer.

t: Gaining a deep grasp of the intrinsic laws of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
zh: 深入把握全面从严治党的自身规律
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in May 2022, asks how the Communist Party of China should understand and follow the laws that govern its own strict self-governance. Zhou Jingqing starts from Xi Jinping's statement that strict governance has its own laws, and that this holds all the more for a large, long-established party. The author's thesis is that, since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the Party has advanced full and rigorous self-governance of the Party by following these laws, and that it must keep doing so in the new great project of Party building.

The article is organised around six paired principles, each presented as one dimension of the governing law. They are: preserving tradition together with innovation; problem orientation together with value orientation; treating symptoms together with root causes; comprehensive advance together with breakthroughs at key points; popular supervision together with the Party's self-reform; and ideological Party building together with institutional governance. Each section pairs a statement of principle with Xi Jinping's formulations and examples of Party practice since 2012.

Zhou makes three main moves. First, the author traces strict governance from the early call for an "iron discipline" Party through the Gutian Conference and the Yan'an rectification to its entry into the Party constitution, to show continuity of thought and line. Second, Zhou ties the problem-oriented method to the aim of winning popular support, and describes anti-corruption work as combining "not daring, not being able and not wanting to be corrupt", with pursuit of "tigers", "flies" and "foxes" alongside institutional reform and ideals. Third, Zhou frames the Party's self-reform and popular supervision as the first and second answers to the "historical cycle" question Huang Yanpei put to Mao Zedong in 1945. Zhou also stresses that ideological education and rule-making need each other, citing 3,615 Party regulations in force as of 1 July 2021.

Zhou concludes that these paired principles together make up the laws of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, and that following them gives strong political guidance and a guarantee for the new journey. The text presents ideological Party building and institutional governance as complementary, with neither effective alone. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how Chinese Party scholars set out the principles behind the post-2012 Party-building and anti-corruption campaign.
quoteEn: Without institutional support, ideological Party building will hang in mid-air and cannot last; without ideological guidance, institutional governance will lose its direction and not know where to apply its force.
quoteZh: 思想建党若缺乏制度支撑，就会悬浮空中、难以持续；制度治党若没有思想引领，就会迷失方向、发力无术。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party-building campaign promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering ideology, organisation, conduct, discipline, institutions and anti-corruption. It was later included in the 'Four-Pronged Comprehensive Strategy'.
Xi Jinping's term for the Party's capacity to correct its own errors and purge its own problems. It is presented as the second answer to the 'historical cycle' question.
The pattern in which regimes flourish and then decline. Huang Yanpei raised it with Mao Zedong in Yan'an in 1945, and Party writers cite it when discussing how the Party can avoid the same fate.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Showing the logic of China through the story of the Communist Party of China
zh: 通过中国共产党的故事彰显中国之理
paras: This short commentary in Guangming Daily (9 May 2022) responds to Xi Jinping's inspection visit to Renmin University of China. Zhang Xiaomeng argues that telling the story of the Communist Party of China well is a key way to show the logic behind China's path, and that philosophers and social scientists should take this up.

The piece offers three reasons, each in its own section. Telling the Party's story supplies China's wisdom and proposals for the questions of the age; it is integral to building a world-class university with Chinese characteristics; and it helps the world decode China.

On the first point, Zhang says the Party's century of experience is a shared spiritual asset of humanity. In the author's account, Chinese modernization is not a copy of earlier paths and has created a new form of human civilization, which can help the international community build consensus at a historic crossroads. On the second, Zhang holds that a university's world-class standing depends on whether it can merge answers to the questions of China, the world, the people and the times, and balance national character with global outlook. On the third, Zhang argues that understanding China requires understanding the Party, and that international communication should draw on Chinese culture as the basis of a new external discourse, seeking consensus through equal dialogue.

Zhang concludes that scholars should use the strengths of philosophy and the social sciences to tell the Party's story in depth and with innovation, and so raise the global influence of the Party. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party-affiliated academics link international communication, university building and Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: To understand China today, one must understand the Communist Party of China.
quoteZh: 读懂今天的中国，必须读懂中国共产党。

glossary.explanation: Official term for China's own path of modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models. It became a central Party slogan after the 20th Party Congress in 2022.

Official phrase, used in the Party's 2021 centenary discourse, for the civilization said to result from Chinese modernization, balancing material, political, spiritual, social and ecological progress.

t: The century-long evolution of the Communist Party of China's slogans guiding the direction of the youth movement
st: A historical study based on May Fourth commemorative texts
zh: 中国共产党引领青年运动方向口号的百年演变
zhSub: 基于五四纪念文本的历史考察
paras: Guo Xiang asks how the slogan that the Communist Party of China (CPC) uses to steer the youth movement has changed over a century, and what those changes show. The author treats the slogan as a compressed "signature symbol" of the Party's discourse and argues that each change reflects the Party's mission and discursive system of the time. The thesis is that the slogan has moved through three discourses, revolutionary, reform and strong-country, while keeping a constant structure of political, social and mission-oriented guidance.

The study draws on speeches by Party leaders at May Fourth anniversaries and on May Fourth editorials in the People's Daily, beginning with Mao Zedong's 1939 speech "The Orientation of the Youth Movement". It is organised by period. The first part covers the new-democratic revolution and the era of socialist revolution and construction. The second covers reform and opening up, and the third covers the new era. The author notes that earlier research on May Fourth commemoration has paid little attention to these slogans.

Guo argues that "integration with the workers and peasants" had a dual meaning before 1949. It mobilised student and intellectual youth, whom Mao classed as petty-bourgeois, to organise the masses. It also required them to learn from workers and peasants and to overcome their own vacillation. After 1949 the signified shifted towards training youth to be both "red and expert", and during the Cultural Revolution the slogan was reduced to ideological remoulding. In the reform era it became "integration with practice and with the people", and from 1999 "two upholds": upholding Party leadership and advancing with the people's great practice. In the new era, Guo says, the slogan centres on struggle for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and a community with a shared future for mankind. "Struggle" replaces "practice" as the key word, which the author reads as expressing the Four-sphere Confidence in plainer, more popular language.

Guo concludes that the slogans always centre on the Party's mission, record the development of its ideological discourse, and express constant commitments to Party leadership and putting the people first. The referents of "youth" and "the masses" have widened, and a world-oriented guidance has been added in the new era. The author argues that identifying these patterns builds historical consciousness and helps Party youth work today. Read the original if you study CPC discourse, youth policy or May Fourth commemoration and want the textual evidence, including word-frequency tables, behind the slogan's changes.
quoteEn: The century-long evolution of the slogan guiding the direction of the youth movement reflects the Communist Party of China's struggle, sacrifice and creation in striving for the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
quoteZh: 引领青年运动方向口号的百年演变，折射中国共产党为中华民族伟大复兴奋斗、牺牲、创造的斗争历程。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central goal of Party discourse, associated especially with Xi Jinping's "Chinese Dream". It refers to restoring China's national strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The formula became prominent under Xi Jinping.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations and global governance, promoted since the early 2010s.
A Maoist ideal of combining correct political consciousness ("red") with technical and professional competence ("expert").
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978. The article treats it as a distinct historical period of Party discourse.

t: Making Party history study and education regular and long-term by following the mass line well
zh: 在走好群众路线中推动党史学习教育常态化长效化
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2022, Liu Tongfang takes up the Central Committee General Office's opinion on making Party history study and education regular and long-term. The article argues that this can be achieved only by following the Party's mass line well in the new era. Liu presents the mass line as both the lesson of the Party's history and the practical route by which study of that history is turned into results.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out why the people are the foundation of the Party's founding, flourishing and strengthening. The second argues that following the mass line is a necessary requirement of regular, long-term history education. The third identifies three areas in which effort should be concentrated in the new era.

In the first part, Liu says the Party's roots, lifeblood and strength all lie in the people. The author points to the growth from a small party of a few dozen members to one of more than 95 million, and treats this as evidence that popular support explains its successes. The second part gives three reasons for the requirement: it expresses the Party's nature and purpose and the character of a Marxist party; it serves the Party's original aspiration and mission and its governing capacity; and it preserves the Party's vanguard character and purity and secures its governing position. Liu warns that advanced status and ruling status are not permanent, and that losing touch with the masses endangers them. The third part calls for work in three areas: firm awareness of the Party's purpose and better work style, including the eight-point regulations; putting the people-centred philosophy of development into practice and consolidating the "Doing practical things for the people" campaign; and strengthening grassroots governance and institutions.

Liu concludes that the unity of knowing and doing is what matters most for regular, long-term history education. Study results must become real action in the service of the people. By taking root among the people and relying on them, the Party can consolidate its governing base and advance towards the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a representative example of how Party-history education is linked to the mass line and to grassroots work-style and governance requirements in 2022.
quoteEn: What matters most in making Party history study and education regular and long-term is the unity of knowing and doing, turning the results of theoretical study into real action in the service of the people.
quoteZh: 推动党史学习教育常态化长效化，贵在知行合一、把理论学习的成果转化为为人民服务的现实行动。

glossary.explanation: The Party's method of work, associated with Mao Zedong, of gathering the views of the people ("from the masses, to the masses") and turning them into policy. It is described in Party documents as the Party's lifeline.
A nationwide campaign launched in 2021, around the Party's centenary, to study the Party's history. The 2022 opinion discussed here calls for making it a regular, lasting practice.

A formula in Party discourse for the founding goals of seeking the happiness of the Chinese people and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. It has been prominent since the 19th Party Congress (2017).

glossary.zh: 以人民为中心的发展思想
glossary.pinyin: yǐ rénmín wéi zhōngxīn de fāzhǎn sīxiǎng
glossary.explanation: A principle associated with Xi Jinping that development should serve the people and its benefits be shared by them. It is part of the new development philosophy.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term national goal, closely linked to the Chinese Dream. It is presented as restoring China's strength and international standing.
Rules on official conduct adopted by the Politburo in December 2012. They aim to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucracy and to keep officials close to the public.

t: A full grasp of the theoretical content and epochal significance of advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization
zh: 全面把握以中国式现代化推进中华民族伟大复兴的理论内涵和时代意义
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2022 no. 4
paras: Writing in 2022, Yan Xiaofeng takes up the second of the "ten clarifications" in the Resolution on the Party's century of struggle, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). That clarification names the general task of upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics as socialist modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, to be pursued through Chinese modernization. Yan argues that the formula is a concise statement of that task and a guide for the new journey towards the second centenary goal.

The article has three parts. The first examines the organic unity of socialist modernization and national rejuvenation, tracing it through the Party's four historical periods. The second presents the Chinese modernization path as the necessary road to rejuvenation. The third sets out the significance of the formula for the adaptation of Marxism to China, for the leap from "standing up" and "becoming prosperous" to "becoming strong", for developing countries, and for socialism worldwide.

Yan's central claim is that modernization and rejuvenation are two descriptions of one process, not two tasks. Modernization is the core content and necessary stage of rejuvenation, while rejuvenation is modernization's fundamental purpose. Chinese modernization is thus the route, driving force and support of rejuvenation, and rejuvenation is its theme and vehicle. Yan holds that the Chinese path is a socialist path, essentially socialism with Chinese characteristics. Following the Resolution and Xi Jinping, the article says this path resolves problems of Western modernization: capital-centred development, polarization, materialism and external expansion. Yan says it creates a "new form of human civilization" with material, political, spiritual, social, ecological and human dimensions, and a community with a shared future for mankind.

Yan concludes that the formula is an important component of the new leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and the basic guide to becoming strong. It also offers developing countries an option other than Westernization or surrendering sovereignty. Yan adds that success in modernization would strengthen the appeal of socialist ideology and the credibility of the socialist system against capitalism, contributing to the "two rejuvenations" of nation and socialism. Read the original if you want a detailed Party-theory account of how Chinese modernization was tied to national rejuvenation in the period just after the 2021 Resolution.
quoteEn: Realizing socialist modernization and the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation are not two tasks within the general task of upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics, but different expressions of one and the same process, stressing different aspects of the same practice.
quoteZh: 实现社会主义现代化和中华民族伟大复兴，不是坚持和发展中国特色社会主义总任务的两个任务，而是同一个过程的不同表述，强调的是同一个实践的不同内涵。

glossary.explanation: Official term for China's own path to modernization, presented as socialist and distinct from the Western model. It became central in Party discourse after the 19th Party Congress and especially after 2021.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's overarching national goal of restoring China's strength and standing after the 'century of humiliation' that began in 1840. It is closely tied to the Chinese Dream.
Phrase in the 2021 Resolution describing what the Chinese modernization path is said to create, as a civilization surpassing capitalist modernity.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for China's vision of international relations, stressing common interests and cooperation.

glossary.zh: 党的十九届六中全会决议
glossary.pinyin: Dǎng de shíjiǔ jiè liù zhōngquánhuì juéyì
glossary.en: the Resolution on the Party's century of struggle
glossary.literal: Resolution on the major achievements and historical experience of the Party's century of struggle
glossary.explanation: The third historical resolution of the Communist Party, adopted in November 2021, which sums up the Party's history and affirms Xi Jinping Thought.

t: The inherent value of the "ten upholds" historical experience
zh: “十个坚持”历史经验的内蕴价值
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in April 2022, takes up the "ten upholds" (ten adherences) of historical experience summarised in the Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience adopted by the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). Huang Rongsheng asks what values are embedded in these ten lessons. The author argues that they form a unified, mutually connected system that helps answer what the Communist Party is, what it is to do, why it has succeeded and how it can keep succeeding.

The piece is a short essay organised under four numbered headings. Each heading names one value or function of the ten lessons: the fundamental guarantee of the success of the cause of the Party and the people; the root of the Party's seizing the historical initiative; the fundamental path by which the Party stays at the forefront of the times; and the source of strength that keeps the Party invincible. Each section draws on episodes from the Party's history, from the revolutionary period to the years after the 18th Party Congress (2012).

In the first section, Huang holds that the Party's leadership is what ultimately explains success at every stage, from overthrowing the "three mountains" to socialist construction, reform and the period since 2012. The second section presents struggle, including the Korean War decision and the response to COVID-19, as the way the Party keeps the initiative. The third treats self-reform as the Party's second answer to the "historical cycle" question, after the "cave dialogue" answer of people's supervision. Huang lists measures since 2012: theoretical education, correcting work styles, discipline, and anti-corruption work. The fourth section holds that independence and self-reliance, grounded in Marxism and traditional culture, produced the path of Chinese modernization.

Huang concludes that history repeatedly shows these lessons to be decisive: only by upholding Party leadership, struggle, self-reform and an independent path can the Party remain the strong leadership core of national rejuvenation. The text is an official-style interpretive commentary, not an analytical study. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-affiliated scholars in 2022 explained the ten historical lessons and linked them to episodes of Party history.
quoteEn: History powerfully shows that only by always upholding the courage for self-reform can the Party's own body remain forever healthy and remain the strong leadership core of the cause of national rejuvenation, standing at the forefront of the times.
quoteZh: 历史有力说明，惟有始终坚持勇于自我革命，方能使党自身肌体永远健康，始终成为走在时代前列的民族复兴伟业的坚强领导核心。

glossary.explanation: The ten lessons of historical experience set out in the 2021 Party resolution on the Party's century of struggle: Party leadership, putting the people first, theoretical innovation, independence, the Chinese path, a broad perspective on the world, innovative breakthroughs, struggle, united front and self-reform.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, promoted under Xi Jinping, presented as distinct from Western models.

A 1945 conversation in Yan'an between Mao Zedong and Huang Yanpei about how to escape the "historical cycle" of rise and decline of regimes; Mao answered that democracy and people's supervision of government would do so.

t: Drawing wisdom and strength from the Party's century of struggle
zh: 从党的百年奋斗历程中汲取智慧和力量
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily in April 2022, asks how the Communist Party of China should draw on its century of struggle as it begins a new journey. Hu Jinyan argues that this requires grasping three interlinked logics of the Party's hundred years, historical, theoretical and practical, in order to understand why the Party has succeeded in the past and how it can keep succeeding. The stated aim is to work towards the second centenary goal and the Chinese Dream of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The piece takes as its basis the Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021), and quotes Xi Jinping throughout. After a short introduction, it has three sections, one for each logic. The historical section runs from the Opium War through the 1911 Revolution to the Party's founding; the theoretical section covers the successive stages of adapting Marxism to China; the practical section reviews achievements from the Party's founding to the present, including 2021 economic figures.

On the historical logic, Hu holds that after the Opium War China became semi-colonial and semi-feudal, earlier struggles failed, and the Party gave the nation new leadership. The conclusion drawn is that without the Party there would be no new China and no national rejuvenation, and that Party leadership is the fundamental guarantee of that goal. On the theoretical logic, Hu stresses the Party's success in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, tracing it from Mao Zedong Thought through Deng Xiaoping Theory to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The article presents the latter as a product of the Two Integrations. On the practical logic, Hu describes the Party's self-reform as leading social revolution, and cites GDP of 114 trillion yuan and per capita GDP above 12,000 US dollars in 2021.

Hu concludes that the Party must pass on and develop its successful experience on the "new road to the examination". For this the article calls for understanding the significance of the Two Establishes, strengthening the Four Consciousnesses, and carrying out the Two Upholds. It also calls for upholding Xi Jinping Thought as guidance. Read the original if you want a compact example of how the official narrative of the Party's centenary was presented to a mass readership in 2022.
quoteEn: The theoretical logic of the Party's century of struggle shows profoundly that whether Marxism can play a role in practice depends on whether its basic principles can be combined with China's realities and the features of the times.
quoteZh: 党百年奋斗的理论逻辑深刻表明，马克思主义能不能在实践中发挥作用，关键在于能否把马克思主义基本原理同中国实际和时代特征结合起来。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the Sixth Plenum resolution (2021) that affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold General Secretary Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.
A Party slogan calling on members to maintain political awareness, a sense of the big picture, a sense of the core, and alignment with the Central Committee.
Formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with China's fine traditional culture.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official description of the Party's continuing effort to adjust Marxist theory to Chinese conditions and to the current era.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central national goal in Party discourse, understood as restoring China's strength and international standing by the middle of the 21st century.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.

t: Grasping the three-fold meaning of the decisive significance of the "Two Establishes"
zh: 准确把握“两个确立”决定性意义的三重意蕴
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in April 2022, takes up the 2021 Party resolution on the Party's century of struggle, which says that establishing Xi Jinping as the core of the Central Committee and of the whole Party, and establishing the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought, are of decisive significance. Niu Jun argues that this judgement has three layers of meaning and should serve as the fundamental political guide for upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era.

The article is organised under three headings. It presents the "Two Establishes" as a requirement of Marxist party-building, as a conclusion drawn from the Party's hundred-year history, and as a necessary guide for the practice of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

On the first point, Niu cites Marx, Engels and Lenin on the need for leaders and authority, and on the role of theory in guiding action, to argue that a mature, stable leadership core and a guiding theory mark a mature Marxist party. On the second, Niu traces the Zunyi Meeting, the Seventh Party Congress and Mao Zedong Thought, the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978) and Deng Xiaoping's stress on a core, and then the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). In Niu's account, upholding the Party's core and the authority of the Central Committee, while advancing the adaptation of Marxism, is a principal reason for the Party's successes.

Niu concludes that, as the world's largest governing party, the Party needs a core with high prestige and a Central Committee with high authority to meet major risks and challenges. Party members and cadres are called on to strengthen the "four consciousnesses", practise the Two Upholds, and strengthen political development, theoretical study and the Party's self-reform. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party commentary justifies the Two Establishes historically and doctrinally.
quoteEn: Practice has proved that resolutely upholding the Party's core and the authority of the Central Committee, and continually advancing the Sinicization, modernization and popularization of Marxism, is an important historical lesson of the Party's century of struggle and the fundamental reason it has gone from victory to victory.
quoteZh: 实践证明，坚决维护党的核心和党中央权威，不断推进马克思主义中国化、时代化、大众化，是中国共产党百年奋斗的重要历史经验，是我们党百年征程从胜利走向胜利的根本原因。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the 2021 Party resolution on history, affirming Xi Jinping's position as core of the Central Committee and the whole Party and the guiding status of Xi Jinping Thought. It has since been presented as a basic political principle.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and to uphold the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.
A Party slogan for members and cadres: political consciousness, consciousness of the overall situation, consciousness of the core, and consciousness of keeping in line.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sixiǎng
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, in full Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.
An official term for the Party's continuing efforts to discipline and improve itself, associated with full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

t: Pathways for converting the institutional strengths of Party leadership into high-quality development effectiveness
zh: 党的领导制度优势转化为高质量发展效能的实现路径
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in 2022, asks how the institutional advantage of leadership by the Communist Party of China can be turned into effective governance that delivers high-quality development. Huang Qisong argues that, in the face of what the article calls changes unseen in a century, the key lies with the Party. Only by converting this institutional advantage into national governance capacity, Huang contends, can high-quality development be achieved at root.

The piece is organised around five lines of action, each with its own sub-heading: Party building as guidance, self-reform, comprehensive deepening of reform, the new development philosophy, and a people-centred approach. It draws throughout on Xi Jinping's statements, the Fifth and Sixth Plenums of the 19th Central Committee (2020 and 2021) and the Party's centenary speech.

Huang's first move is to treat high-quality development as a requirement covering the economy, politics, culture, society and ecology, which in the author's view only the Party's overall leadership can coordinate and unite into a joint force. Second, Huang presents the Party's self-reform as both an essential attribute of a Marxist party and a driving force of development, requiring the removal of conservative attitudes and of institutional obstacles. Third, the article links reform and opening up to the new development philosophy, citing GDP growth from 367.9 billion yuan in 1978 to 114.4 trillion yuan in 2021 as evidence of reform's results. It states that high-quality development is development that applies the philosophy of innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing, and that it requires a new development pattern.

Huang closes by stressing that high-quality development must benefit the people. The author calls for attention to the changing principal contradiction, to improving livelihoods, to coordinated regional development, and to linking poverty-alleviation achievements with rural revitalisation and common prosperity. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars in 2022 framed Party leadership as the institutional basis of the high-quality development agenda.
quoteEn: Only by genuinely converting this institutional advantage into national governance effectiveness can high-quality development truly be achieved at root.
quoteZh: 只有把这种制度优势切实转化为国家治理效能，才能从根本上真正实现高质量发展。

glossary.explanation: An official goal, prominent since the 19th Party Congress (2017), of shifting from fast growth to growth emphasising quality, efficiency and balance across the economy and society.
A formula introduced in 2015 comprising innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing, intended to guide economic and social policy.
An official term for the Party's efforts to correct its own problems and maintain discipline, presented as a hallmark of its character.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
A goal of shared wealth for all, stressed in Party policy and associated with demonstration zones such as in Zhejiang.
A strategy, announced in 2020, that centres on domestic circulation while keeping domestic and international circulation mutually reinforcing.

t: The Communist Party of China's contributions to world socialism over the past century
zh: 百年来中国共产党对世界社会主义的贡献
paras: Writing in 2022, after the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021) adopted its resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience, Yan Rong asks what the Communist Party of China's century of struggle has meant for world socialism. The article takes up one of the resolution's five historical significances, that the Party's struggle has deeply influenced the course of world history. Yan argues that the Party has contributed to world socialism in four areas: practice, theory, institutions and culture.

The article is organised around these four contributions. The first section traces three paths the Party explored: the road of new-democratic revolution, the road of socialist transformation and construction, and the road of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The second covers the theoretical results of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, from Mao Zedong Thought through the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The third examines the institutional system, and the fourth the culture the Party has built.

Yan argues that each contribution rests on independent exploration suited to China's conditions. In practice, the Party's encirclement of the cities from the countryside is presented as a development of Marxism-Leninism. The Party is also said to have survived the collapse of the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe and to have refuted the "end of history" thesis. Institutionally, Yan holds that leadership by the Communist Party, the people's congress system and the guiding position of Marxism in the ideological sphere are fundamental institutions. Citing the Soviet case, Yan contends that weakening Party leadership and Marxist guidance leads to failure. Culturally, Yan describes a fusion of fine traditional Chinese culture, revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture, which gives the Party a distinct spiritual lineage.

Yan concludes that the Party has answered the question of what socialism is and how to build it, and has offered developing countries a new option for modernising while keeping their independence. In this reading, the Party has changed the historical contest between socialism and capitalism in socialism's favour, and will contribute still more as it builds a modern socialist country. Read the original if you want an official-line account of how Chinese scholars frame the Party's centenary significance for the international socialist movement.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China has successfully solved the historic puzzle of "what socialism is and how to build it."
quoteZh: 中国共产党成功破解了“什么是社会主义、怎样建设社会主义”的历史性难题。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.literal: the Sinification and modernisation of Marxism
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of applying Marxism to Chinese conditions and updating it for each era. Mao Zedong first used the idea of the "sinification of Marxism" in 1938.
The official name for China's socialist path since the reform era. Deng Xiaoping popularised it, and the 12th Party Congress (1982) put it forward as a formula.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping. It was written into the Party constitution in 2017.
Mao Zedong's term for the stage of Chinese revolution led by the proletariat, aimed at overthrowing imperialism, feudalism and bureaucrat-capitalism. It was seen as a step towards socialism.

t: A programmatic Marxist document that upholds the methodology of dialectical and historical materialism
st: On the Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience over the past century
zh: 坚持辩证唯物主义和历史唯物主义方法论的马克思主义纲领性文献
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in April 2022, Wang Qiang offers a study-guide commentary on the Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience over the past century, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). Wang argues that the Resolution, by upholding the methodology of dialectical and historical materialism, is a brilliant programmatic Marxist document. In Wang's account it is also a political declaration for Communists in the new era and a guide to action for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article is organised around four pairs of principles that Wang says run through the Resolution: the materialist conception of history together with a correct view of Party history; grasping the laws of historical development together with seizing the historical initiative; the continuity together with the stages of history; and the historical process together with the process of thought. Each section sets out how the Resolution applies the principle, then draws a lesson for readers. The commentary draws on Xi Jinping's remarks and a quotation from Engels.

Wang contends that the Resolution treats Party history in a concrete, comprehensive and developmental way, and that its judgements fit with earlier historical documents. Wang reads the Resolution's "ten upholds" as answering why the Party succeeded in the past and how it can keep succeeding, and as evidence that the Party holds the historical initiative. Wang insists that the Party's different periods are not to be set against one another: continuity must not be denied by stages, nor progress by setbacks. Wang presents the successive "great leaps" from the end of feudal autocracy to the stage of becoming strong as one connected process. On the intellectual side, Wang traces the sinicization of Marxism from Mao Zedong Thought through the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Wang calls the last the latest result of adapting Marxism to China and says it is twenty-first-century Marxism.

Wang concludes that the Party succeeds, and socialism with Chinese characteristics is good, ultimately because Marxism works. Wang calls on readers to study the Resolution's methodology, to see history as a whole that cannot be fragmented, and to avoid subversive errors on fundamental questions. Wang also urges them to strengthen the Four Consciousnesses, the Four-sphere Confidence and the Two Upholds, and to look to the Central Committee. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary in 2022 presented the Resolution's method and its link between Party history and Xi Jinping Thought.
quoteEn: One must not use the stages of history to negate its continuity, nor use its twists and turns to negate its forward progress.
quoteZh: 不能用阶段性否定连续性、用曲折性否定前进性。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party constitution in 2017. Party texts present it as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
The official name for the Party's path, theory and system since reform and opening up. It combines a market economy with Party leadership and public ownership.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China to national strength and prosperity, closely associated with Xi Jinping's slogan of the Chinese Dream.
A Party requirement to uphold the core position of Xi Jinping within the Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.
Official slogan calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
A Party slogan urging cadres to maintain political awareness, a sense of the big picture, a sense of the core, and a sense of alignment with the Central Committee.
The ten summarised lessons of the Party's historical experience in the 2021 Resolution, including upholding Party leadership, putting the people first, theoretical innovation and self-reform.

t: The Communist Party of China's century-long exploration of, and contribution to, the Marxist theory of science, technology and the economy
zh: 中国共产党百年对马克思主义科技经济理论的探索及贡献
paras: Zhang Xinning asks how the Communist Party of China, over its first hundred years, developed the Marxist theory linking science, technology and the economy, and what it added to Marxist political economy. The article argues that the Party advanced this theory systematically in three stages and made four contributions: moving from a mainly philosophical view of technology to a political-economic one; from 'explaining the world' to 'changing the world'; from an auxiliary to a leading role for innovation; and from product-based to innovation-based international competition.

The article follows the Party's history chronologically. It begins with Marx, Engels, Lenin and Stalin on technology, then turns to the revolution and construction period under Mao Zedong. It next covers the reform and opening up period, from Deng Xiaoping to Hu Jintao, and finally the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012) under Xi Jinping. A closing section sets out the significance of the whole development and the functions of innovation.

In Zhang's account, Mao treated natural science as 'a weapon for people's pursuit of freedom' and scientific experiment as a basic form of social practice alongside production struggle and class struggle. He also set a strategy centred on technological revolution, which produced the 'two bombs and one satellite'. Deng's 'primary productive force' thesis made technology the 'gene' of productive forces. This was put into practice through the 863 Programme, the strategy of invigorating China through science and education, and the building of an innovation-oriented country, and Zhang describes a 2003 dispute between self-reliant innovation and technology import that was settled in favour of the former. Under Xi, innovation became the 'primary driving force' of development. Zhang says this extends technology's role beyond the economy into politics, culture, ecology, diplomacy and defence, and ties it to high-quality development and the new development philosophy.

Zhang concludes that this body of theory settled doubts in political economy by bringing productive forces back into the discipline, and that it opened a new realm for political economy with Chinese characteristics. The article lists six functions of innovation: industrial change, economic growth, social stability, people's livelihood, ecological protection and national defence. It calls on economists to keep pace with the new technological revolution and to treat innovation as a core subject of research. Read the original if you want a Party-historical account of how Chinese theorists present continuity from Mao to Xi on technology and political economy.
quoteEn: Scientific and technological innovation is the gene and cell of the modern economy, the cause of its development, and it represents the direction in which the modern economy is moving.
quoteZh: 科技创新是现代经济的基因和细胞，是现代经济发展的动因，代表着现代经济的发展方向。

glossary.explanation: Deng Xiaoping's 1988 formulation that science and technology is the foremost productive force, going beyond Marx's statement that science is a productive force.
A set of five principles (innovation, coordination, green, open and shared development) put forward by the Party leadership in 2015 to guide economic and social policy.
An official goal, stressed since about 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to growth based on quality, efficiency and innovation.

glossary.en: strategy of invigorating China through science and education
glossary.explanation: A national strategy formally adopted in 1995 that made science, technology and education the basis of national development.
A strategic goal announced in 2006 to make China a country driven mainly by its own scientific and technological innovation by 2020.

t: The assertion that "the Party is the highest political leadership force": historical survey, internal logic and practical orientation
zh: “党是最高政治领导力量”论断的历史考察、内在逻辑与现实指向
paras: Yang Binbin examines how the formula "the Party is the highest political leadership force" came into being and what it means for the Chinese political system. The article, published in Party and Government Studies in 2022, argues that the formula is a product of the endogenous evolution of the Party's leadership system. In Yang's account, it carries forward Marxist teaching on the proletarian party and gives it a Chinese discursive form, characterised by principle, timeliness and national character.

The article has three parts. The first traces the formula's roots in Marx, Engels and Lenin, then follows the vocabulary around it in Chinese Communist Party documents: "leadership core", "core force" and "leadership force". It dates these usages from the 1920s and 1940s through Mao Zedong's speeches of 1954 and 1956 and the 14th Party Congress (1992) to the 19th Party Congress (2017), Xi Jinping's 2018 speech and the constitutional revision of that year. The second part sets out the formula's internal logic, and the third turns to practical implications for the present.

Yang's central claim is that the successive wordings differ in expression but share one principle, the authority of Party leadership, while "highest" stresses its supremacy, with political leadership as the most basic form. The formula is tied to four relationships: the people's democratic dictatorship, the new type of state system (including Party–government relations), the new type of party system (relations between the Communist Party and other parties) and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Yang holds that Chinese multi-party cooperation cannot be sorted by Western-centric party theory, and that the Party's self-positioning as a leading, revolutionary and governing party underpins the Party's self-reform.

For the present, Yang calls for three things: firm direction, by upholding Party leadership; a more complete institutional system, to strengthen that leadership; and better governance, to optimise it. In practice this means continuing self-reform, raising the Party's leadership and governing capacity, and building a stronger body of concepts and discourse to "tell the institutional story" of Party leadership, in service of modernising national governance. Read the original if you want a detailed genealogy of the Party's own terms for its leadership role and an official-academic view of how that role links to the state, the party system and Party discipline.
quoteEn: Although "leadership core", "core force" and "leadership force" differ at the level of discursive expression, they reflect a consistent political principle: the authority of Party leadership.
quoteZh: “领导核心”“核心力量”“领导力量”虽然在话语表达层面存在差异性，但反映了一致的政治原则，就是党的领导的权威性。

glossary.zh: 党是最高政治领导力量
glossary.pinyin: dǎng shì zuìgāo zhèngzhì lǐngdǎo lìliàng
glossary.literal: the Party is the highest political leadership force
glossary.explanation: A formulation introduced in the report to the 19th Party Congress (2017). Xi Jinping repeated it in 2018, when Party leadership was also written into the revised constitution.
The official description of China's system of multi-party cooperation under Communist Party leadership. It is presented as distinct from both Western multi-party systems and earlier socialist models.
A concept Xi Jinping formally put forward in September 2019. It refers to the institutional form of China's people's democratic dictatorship, with the people's congress system at its centre.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official term for the Party's drive since 2012 to tighten discipline, internal regulations and Party-building.

The constitutional definition of China's state character, under working-class leadership and based on the worker–peasant alliance. It is treated as the Chinese form of the dictatorship of the proletariat.
An official term for the Party's efforts to correct itself and keep its character, stressed in Party documents since the 2010s.

t: Basic experience of upholding and strengthening the Party's overall leadership in the new era
zh: 新时代坚持和加强党的全面领导的基本经验
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in April 2022, takes up the first of the 13 areas in which the Party's 2021 resolution on its century of struggle summarises historic achievements of the new era: upholding the Party's overall leadership. Zhu Jiamei argues that distilling the basic experience of this work matters theoretically and practically for consolidating the Party's governing position and for the new journey of building a modern socialist country in all respects.

The piece sets out five lessons, each given its own numbered section. They are: clarifying the issue at the level of theory, proceeding from the Party's political line, perfecting the institutional system of overall leadership, providing strong organisational guarantees, and strengthening and improving ideological leadership. The treatment is a summary of policy and leadership practice rather than a historical or comparative study.

Zhu begins from a diagnosis: for a period, some Party members were vague about Party leadership, and its implementation was weakened, hollowed out, diluted and marginalised, with some localities pursuing countermeasures to central policy. In response, the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core restated that the Party leads everything and placed "upholding the Party's leadership over all work" first among the 14 basic principles of the new era. Zhu then describes the mechanisms that make this operational: political discipline and training for cadres, systems of reporting requests and annual work reports to the central leadership, reformed Party and state institutions, and an organisational chain running from the central Party organisation to grassroots branches, extended into new economic and social organisations. Ideological work, in Zhu's account, rests on ideals-and-convictions education, study of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and firm Party control of the ideological sphere through responsibility systems.

Zhu concludes that this system of leadership, extending horizontally to every sector and vertically to the grassroots, has allowed the country to keep developing through risks and challenges while maintaining political stability and balancing vitality with order. Upholding Party leadership is presented as the foundation of the Party and state and of the people's interests. Read the original if you want a concise, official-register statement of how Party leadership is justified and institutionalised in the Xi Jinping era.
quoteEn: Upholding the Party's leadership over all work is the foundation and lifeblood of the Party and state, and the basis of the interests and happiness of the people of all ethnic groups.
quoteZh: 坚持党对一切工作的领导，是党和国家的根本所在、命脉所在，是全国各族人民的利益所在、幸福所在。

glossary.explanation: The principle, emphasised since the 18th Party Congress (2012), that the Communist Party leads all areas of work, summed up in the phrase "the Party leads everything".

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sixiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's guiding ideology under Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
The Party's fundamental guiding direction and tasks, which the article treats as the reference point for all policy and for checking deviations.

t: Using the experience of a century of struggle to increase the Party's wisdom, unity, confidence and fighting spirit
zh: 以百年奋斗成就经验推动全党增长智慧、增进团结、增加信心、增强斗志
paras: This commentary, published in Party Building (Dangjian) in 2022, takes up the Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience over the past century, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). Liu Jie argues, following Xi Jinping's explanation of the draft, that studying this record should strengthen four things across the Party: wisdom, unity, confidence and fighting spirit.

The article is organised in four parts, one for each of these aims. Each part links the Resolution's summary of the four historical periods and its ten items of historical experience to a task for the Party as it begins a new journey towards the second centenary goal.

On wisdom, Liu says the Party's wisdom grew out of a century of practice and the integration of Marxism with China's concrete realities and fine traditional culture, producing successive theoretical innovations from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. On unity, Liu presents ideological unity, the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds as the means of binding the Party together. On confidence and fighting spirit, Liu cites the achievements of the past century as grounds for belief in the Party's path, and holds that the Party's self-reform is the key to keeping its resolve and escaping the historical cycle of rise and fall.

Liu concludes that a century is only a prologue and calls on Party members to rally around the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core, study the Resolution and work towards the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Party official presents the 2021 Resolution to cadres as a tool for study and mobilisation.
quoteEn: The Party's unity and solidarity are its lifeblood and the source of its strength.
quoteZh: 党的团结统一，是党的生命，是党的力量之所在。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the 2021 Resolution affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the whole Party, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought. It is presented in Party documents as decisive for the cause of the Party and state.

A Party requirement to uphold General Secretary Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee. It was first formulated in 2016 and is now an obligation for all Party members.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Party, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central national goal in Party discourse, referring to restoring China's strength and international standing after the 'century of humiliation'. It is associated with the Chinese Dream and the two centenary goals.
Official term for the Party's efforts to correct its own faults and maintain its purity. Xi Jinping presents it as the Party's answer to the historical cycle of dynastic rise and fall.

keywords: Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee

t: Upholding the supremacy of the people is the distinguishing mark separating the Communist Party of China from Western parties
zh: 坚持人民至上是中国共产党区别于西方政党的显著标志
paras: This commentary in Guangming Daily argues that putting the people first (人民至上) is the key lesson of the Communist Party of China's hundred years of struggle and the clearest mark distinguishing a Marxist party from Western parties. Li and Liu present this principle as running through the whole of the Party's governance and expressing its fundamental purpose of serving the people wholeheartedly.

The article is organised in three sections. The first treats the Party's founding mission, tracing it from the Opium War and the October Revolution through the first two Party Congresses to the founding of the People's Republic. The second discusses the Party's goal of meeting the people's aspirations for a better life, including poverty alleviation and common prosperity. The third takes up governance, using the response to Covid-19 as its main example.

In the authors' account, Western parties exist to realise and protect bourgeois interests; two-party and multi-party systems are described as rule by a minority over the majority, with decisions captured by interest groups. The Communist Party, by contrast, is said to have no special interests of its own and to represent the fundamental interests of the broadest masses. Li and Liu cite the elimination of absolute poverty under current standards (98.99 million rural people, 832 counties) as evidence, and contrast Western private ownership and distribution by capital, which they say produce wealth gaps. They also claim that in the pandemic the Party put life first at any cost, which parties that put capital and votes first cannot do.

The authors conclude that the people are the source of the Party's strength and the basis of its victories. They call for policy to rest on the principal contradiction in society and national conditions, and to respond promptly to popular demands. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party commentary in 2022 contrasted the Communist Party with Western parties around the theme of people-centredness.
quoteEn: The most essential difference between the Communist Party of China and Western parties is that we stand on the side of the people, always taking the fundamental interests of the broadest masses as our highest interests, keeping them constantly in mind and holding the people dear.
quoteZh: 中国共产党和西方政党最本质的区别就在于我们是站在人民立场上的，始终将最广大人民群众的根本利益作为自己的最高利益，念兹在兹、心系人民。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, given renewed emphasis under Xi Jinping from 2021 as a task of the new era.

t: Full and rigorous self-governance of the Party is the only way for the Party to keep its vitality and walk the new road of the "examination"
zh: 全面从严治党是党永葆生机活力 走好新的赶考之路的必由之路
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in April 2022, takes up one of the "five musts" (五个必由之路) that Xi Jinping set out at that year's National People's Congress session, when he joined the Inner Mongolia delegation. Li Guojuan explains the claim that full and rigorous self-governance of the Party is the only path by which the Party can keep its vitality and succeed on its new "examination" road. Li treats the claim as having overall and strategic significance for reaching the Second Centenary Goal.

The piece first reviews what has been done since the 18th Party Congress (2012), when full and rigorous self-governance of the Party was placed within the "Four-pronged Comprehensive Strategy" and anti-corruption work was stepped up. It then gives three reasons why this path is necessary, before a brief closing call to action.

Li argues, first, that rigorous governance is needed to preserve the Party's advanced nature and purity, which the author calls the essential attributes of a Marxist party. Second, it strengthens cohesion and fighting capacity: Li says the Party's history shows setbacks whenever belief, organisation and discipline weakened, and lists individualism, factionalism, cliques and double-dealing as risks to be removed. Third, it is the political guarantee that the Party's self-reform can lead a great social revolution. In Li's account, the success of the Chinese nation's move from standing up to becoming prosperous and then strong depended on the Party's willingness to reform itself. Li also warns against complacency, including the view that anti-corruption can pause or that rigour has already been fully achieved.
