Li concludes that the Party should keep its founding mission, deepen full and rigorous self-governance and advance its self-reform. In this way it would provide political security, ideological guidance and leadership for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary in 2022 justified the Party's self-governance campaign and linked it to the Second Centenary Goal.
quoteEn: The reason the Party has been able to lead the people in creating Chinese miracles is, in the final analysis, that it has always adhered to rigorous self-governance and dared to reform itself, constantly strengthening its capacity to govern, winning the people's genuine support and becoming the backbone of the Chinese people and nation.
quoteZh: 党之所以能够带领人民创造中国奇迹，归根结底，就是因为党始终坚持从严治党、勇于自我革命，不断增强了自身的执政能力，始终赢得广大人民的真心拥护，成为中国人民和中华民族的主心骨。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A Party-building policy emphasised since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering discipline, anti-corruption, and ideological and organisational discipline within the Communist Party.

An official concept that the Party can purify, improve and renew itself without external checks. Xi Jinping presents it as the Party's answer to the problem of the "historical cycle" of rise and fall.
The goal of building a modern socialist country that is prosperous, strong, democratic, culturally advanced and harmonious by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China to national strength and international standing, central to Party discourse since the 18th Party Congress.

glossary.literal: new road of taking the exam
glossary.explanation: A metaphor from Mao Zedong's 1949 remark that the Party was going to the capital "to take the exam". It is now used to describe the Party's continuing tests of governance.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: The Party's third historical resolution and the CPC's methods of summing up its own historical experience
zh: 从党的第三个历史决议看中国共产党总结自身历史经验的方法
paras: Zhu Jiamu asks how the Communist Party of China goes about summing up its own historical experience, taking the Resolution on the Major Achievements and Historical Experience of the Party's Century-long Struggle, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021), as his case. This short commentary, published in 2022, argues that the Resolution reflects the basic method set out by Mao Zedong and Xi Jinping, namely historical materialism and seeking truth from facts. It also uses three more specific methods that Zhu says are worth studying and applying.

The article opens by recalling Mao's remarks on experience and Xi's calls since the 18th Party Congress (2012) to link Party history study with summing up experience and to form a correct view of Party history. It then takes the three methods in turn, drawing on the Resolution's treatment of the four historical periods: the new-democratic revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era. Zhu closes by noting that other methods exist and that the Resolution does not limit itself to these three.

The first method is to sum up each period separately while also linking all periods together. Zhu lists the lessons the Resolution draws for each period, then points to problems common to all of them, such as keeping the Party's vanguard character. For this reason the Resolution adds a section on ten lessons from the century, from upholding Party leadership to the Party's self-reform. The second method is to assess experience from today's level of understanding while placing it in its specific historical conditions. Citing Lenin, Zhu says the early move to a public-ownership, highly centralised planned economy must be understood against imperialist threat and scarce capital and talent. The third method is to concentrate on successes without ignoring failures. Zhu says the Resolution treats achievements as the mainstream but openly names problems, such as a period of lax Party governance that allowed corruption to spread.

Zhu concludes that the Party values correct methods of summing up experience as well as the experience itself. Studying the Resolution should therefore include absorbing its methods, so as to distil effective approaches, improve the Party's capacity for struggle and governance, strengthen resistance to corruption and risk, and carry forward socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a brief, officially aligned account of the methodological logic behind the 2021 resolution, as presented by a leading Party-history scholar.
quoteEn: In summing up historical experience, besides summarising the specific experience of each period of the Party's own development, one must also link the periods together and sum up the general experience of the Party's century of leading the people in great struggle.
quoteZh: 总结历史经验，除了要对党自身发展的各个历史时期的具体经验进行总结之外，还要把各个历史时期贯通起来，总结一百年来党带领人民进行伟大斗争的普遍经验。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's theory, path and system since the reform era. It presents China's socialism as adapted to Chinese conditions.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched at the end of 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
A term for the Party's efforts to correct its own problems and keep its discipline and integrity. The Resolution lists it as the tenth lesson of the century.

t: Understanding the scientific connotation of the Party's self-reform
zh: 深入理解把握党的自我革命的科学内涵
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in April 2022, asks what the Communist Party of China's "self-reform" means and why it distinguishes the Party from other parties. Dai Yanjun argues that self-reform is the Party's most distinctive trait and an essential route to keeping it advanced and pure. In his account, full and rigorous self-governance of the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012) is the great practice of self-reform in the new era.

The article has three parts. The first explains where the Party's capacity for self-reform comes from. The second sets out the tasks self-reform has performed historically. The third examines how the campaign for full and rigorous self-governance of the Party under Xi Jinping has enriched the concept, drawing on episodes from the Zunyi Conference to the Yan'an rectification movement.

Dai locates the sources of self-reform in two features: the Party is a Marxist party, and Marxism is an open, developing doctrine; and the Party serves the people wholeheartedly, so whatever harms popular interests is wrong and must be corrected. On this basis he lists four historical functions: correcting errors in decision-making through inner-Party political life (the Zunyi Conference, the Seven Thousand Cadres Conference, the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee); purging politically two-faced people; punishing corrupt elements; and using criticism and self-criticism to achieve unity, with the Yan'an rectification as the model. For the new era he identifies four features: political development as the essential requirement, discipline and conduct as the routinised element, the anti-corruption struggle as the key focus, and the improvement of inner-Party regulations as the move towards rule by law.

Dai concludes that self-reform must adapt its priorities and methods to the problems of each period, and that the policies of the Party leadership centred on Xi Jinping have opened a new stage of it. He credits them with an overwhelming victory in the anti-corruption struggle, now being consolidated. Read the original if you want a concise official-academic statement of how Party theorists justify self-reform and tie it to full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.
quoteEn: The greatness of the Communist Party of China lies not in never making mistakes, but in daring to face reality, not shying away from its own faults, and conscientiously correcting the errors it has made.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的伟大，不是从来不犯错误，而是在于敢于直面现实，不讳疾忌医，认真纠正自己所犯的错误

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed in Party discourse since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It refers to the Party's claimed ability to identify and correct its own errors and purge unhealthy elements without outside pressure.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan and programme of Party-building adopted under Xi Jinping, covering political, ideological, organisational, conduct, discipline and institutional work, including the anti-corruption campaign.
The Party's internal activities, such as meetings, criticism and self-criticism, and decision-making under democratic centralism, through which it handles disputes and discipline.
An inner-Party education and discipline campaign. The best-known is the Yan'an rectification of the early 1940s, aimed at subjectivism, sectarianism and formulaic 'Party-style writing'.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: The Party's centenary: historical theme and spatio-temporal fields of the Communist Party of China
zh: 中国共产党百年的历史主题与时空场域
paras: Marking the Party's centenary in 2021, Liu asks how the usual account of the Communist Party of China's hundred years can be placed within a wider time frame. The article argues that three overlapping "centuries" must be studied together: modern China from 1840 to 1949, the Party's own century from 1921, and the century of New China from 1949 to 2049. In Liu's reading, one historical theme runs through all three, namely the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article has three main sections. The first treats the century of modern national disaster as the setting in which the theme of national rejuvenation arose. The second follows the Party's record from early reformers and the founding congresses to the achievements of each period. The third covers the New China century, looking at the goal of a modern, powerful socialist country, the continuing development of socialism with Chinese characteristics, the Party and the people as the "narrative subject", and the external extension of this field.

Liu's central move is to derive the theme from the principal contradictions of modern society. Citing the formula of imperialism versus the nation and feudalism versus the masses, the author says these produced two linked tasks, "revolution" and "modernization". Peasant movements, self-strengthening, reform and the 1911 Revolution all failed, in the author's account, because they imitated the West. Marxism then supplied the ideological weapon, and the Party took up the task from its first congresses in 1921 and 1922. Liu then traces the Party's step-by-step formulation of the goal: Deng Xiaoping's xiaokang, the three-step strategy, the "two centenary goals" and the modernization of national governance. The author presents foreign policy from Mao Zedong to Xi Jinping as the theme's external side, ending with a community with a shared future for mankind and the Belt and Road Initiative.

Liu concludes that studying the three centuries together lets one grasp the Party's past, present and future, as well as the internal logic of national rejuvenation. The author holds that the Party, united with the people, will lead Chinese modernization through the "great changes unseen in a century" and contribute to human well-being. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Party-history scholar fits the Party's hundred years into a longer sequence from 1840 to 2049 around the theme of national rejuvenation.
quoteEn: The interweaving of the three \"centuries\" as spatio-temporal fields has throughout carried a practical picture whose historical theme is the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
quoteZh: 三个“百年”时空场域的交织叠加，始终贯穿着以中华民族伟大复兴为历史主题的实践图景。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's overarching goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing after the "century of humiliation". Jiang Zemin used the phrase in 1989, and it became central under Xi Jinping.
The official name for China's path to modernization. The article traces it to Deng Xiaoping's idea of a xiaokang-level modernization and presents it as the Party's current course.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s. It calls for cooperative international relations and shared development.
A Chinese-led programme of infrastructure and economic cooperation launched in 2013, linking China with countries in Asia, Africa and Europe.
The goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021 and a modern socialist country by the centenary of the People's Republic in 2049.

t: Upholding the Party's overall leadership is the only way to uphold and develop socialism with Chinese characteristics
zh: 坚持党的全面领导是坚持和发展中国特色社会主义的必由之路
paras: Feng Jun's commentary, published in 2022, explains one of the "five musts" that Xi Jinping set out when joining the Inner Mongolia delegation to the Fifth Session of the 13th National People's Congress. The first of these holds that upholding the Party's overall leadership is the only way to uphold and develop socialism with Chinese characteristics. Feng reads this as a summing-up of why the Party has succeeded in the past and how it can keep succeeding. In Feng's account, it also reflects an understanding of the laws governing Party rule, socialist construction and social development.

The article follows the Party's record in four stages. It begins with the founding programmes and Mao Zedong's writings on New Democracy. It then covers the establishment of the socialist system in the 1950s and the search for a path of socialist construction suited to China. Its last section turns to the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012), with figures on growth, poverty alleviation and the building of a moderately prosperous society.

Feng's central claim is that socialism has been the Party's goal since its founding, and that Party leadership has been the means of reaching it at every stage. Quoting Mao, Feng argues that no revolution could succeed without the Party and that only the Party could lead China to socialism. Feng credits it with the transition of the 1950s, which did not copy the Soviet Union, and with finding a path fitted to Chinese conditions after setbacks, including the Cultural Revolution. Feng also holds that the Party's leadership steered China through the collapse of the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe and so kept world socialism alive.

Feng concludes that history and present reality show there would be no new China and no socialism with Chinese characteristics without the Party, and that national rejuvenation depends on its overall leadership. Feng calls for upholding the authority of the Party Central Committee and its centralized, unified leadership, and for the Party's organization to cover all work. Risks and challenges are said to make this more urgent. Read the original if you want an official-line account of how Party history is used to justify the principle of overall Party leadership in the Xi Jinping era.
quoteEn: Leadership by the Communist Party of China is the defining feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the greatest strength of its system, and the Party is the highest political leadership force.
quoteZh: 中国共产党领导是中国特色社会主义最本质的特征，是中国特色社会主义制度的最大优势，党是最高政治领导力量。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's line of socialist development since reform and opening up, associated with Deng Xiaoping and later elaborated by successive leaders.
A formulation Xi Jinping put forward in March 2022 listing five principles the Party presents as essential for success. The first is upholding the Party's overall leadership.

t: Upholding Party leadership as the primary experience of the Party's century of struggle
zh: 坚持党的领导是百年奋斗首要经验
source: Studies on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics, 2022 no. 1
paras: Why does the Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience, adopted by the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021), list upholding Party leadership as the first lesson of the Party's hundred years? Liu Hanfeng argues that this is the most fundamental reason the Chinese people and nation changed their modern fate. The article sets out to explain how Party leadership should be understood and upheld in the new era, taking the Eighth Party Congress (1956) report's account of the Party's leadership as a basic reference point.

The article is organised in three dimensions: historical, theoretical and practical. The historical section traces China's modern revolution from the Opium War, and compares the bourgeois reformers and revolutionaries with the Communist Party. The theoretical section moves through Marx, Engels and Lenin on the proletarian party, then the Chinese Party's own development of leadership theory and the question of proletarian leadership. The practical section reviews institutional arrangements from the Zunyi Meeting through the reform era to the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Liu's core argument is that China's bourgeoisie, tied to imperialism and feudal forces, could not complete the twin tasks of anti-imperialist and anti-feudal revolution, so only a revolution led by the working class could succeed. Theoretically, the author holds that Party leadership rests on the advanced character of Marxist theory and on Lenin's principles of organisation and democratic centralism, which the Chinese Party extended through its doctrine of unified leadership in the base areas. Liu adds that holding proletarian leadership is a long-term task under long-term governance, and that the Party's leadership has been consolidated by institutions. These include collective leadership, reforms to cadre tenure, and, since 2012, a system of leadership institutions covering the Two Upholds, comprehensive Party leadership and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

Liu concludes that Party leadership is the primary experience because the Party represents the advanced force and the highest political leading force. Upholding it, in the author's account, means continually improving leadership and long-term governing capacity, strengthening the Party's self-reform and its ability to guide social revolution, and improving strategy and tactics. It also means serving the people, pursuing common prosperity, and applying the Two Upholds and democratic centralism. Read the original if you want an official-line account of how Party scholars link history, Leninist theory and institution-building in justifying Party leadership.
quoteEn: The establishment and improvement of the system of Party leadership institutions is a powerful annotation of the theory of socialism with Chinese characteristics and a practical deepening of the basic principles of Marxism.
quoteZh: 党的领导制度体系的建立和完善是对中国特色社会主义理论的有力注释，也是对马克思主义基本原理的实践深化。

glossary.explanation: A political requirement, formalised in 2018, to uphold Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and of the whole Party, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The slogan for the Party-building drive since 2012, covering discipline, anti-corruption, ideological work and institutional rules within the Party.
The official idea that the Party can purge its own errors and corruption by its own efforts, presented as the way to escape the historical cycle of rise and decline.
A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all members of society, given new emphasis in official policy under Xi Jinping.
The Leninist organisational principle by which Party bodies are elected and discuss democratically, but the minority obeys the majority and lower levels obey higher ones.
A Politburo meeting held in January 1935 during the Long March, regarded in Party history as establishing Mao Zedong's leading position in the Central Committee.

t: The historical course of scientific socialism's development in China over the Party's first century, and its lessons
zh: 建党百年科学社会主义在中国发展的历史进程及经验启示
paras: Taking up the call of the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021) to understand why the Party succeeded in the past and how it can keep succeeding, Li Zhengxing asks how scientific socialism has developed in China across the Party's hundred years and what lessons follow. The article argues that the Party answered the defining questions of each period by combining Marxism with Chinese conditions, and that this advanced both Chinese practice and scientific socialism itself.

The article has two parts. The first sets out three guiding threads and then traces four periods: the New Democratic Revolution (1921–1949), socialist revolution and construction (1949–1978), reform and opening up (1978–2012), and the new era since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second part draws five lessons, each tied to a basic task, driving force, value or guarantee of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

Li identifies three threads: the unity of theory and practice, of logic and history, and of truth and value. In this reading, the Party kept scientific socialism's basic principles while drawing on historical experience. Each period yielded original contributions: New Democratic revolutionary theory and the rural-centred revolutionary road; a peaceful transition to socialism and early theories of construction, despite the errors of "class struggle as the key link" and the Cultural Revolution; the path and theory of socialism with Chinese characteristics; and, in the new era, Xi Jinping's ideas on development, governance, ecology, Party building and a community with a shared future for mankind. The five lessons are to integrate scientific socialism with China's actual conditions, including the primary stage of socialism; to centre work on economic development and the productive forces; to deepen reform and opening up; to put the people first and promote people's all-round development; and to uphold Party leadership and Party building.

Li concludes that the Party's century of experience shows these principles must be upheld in order to keep socialism with Chinese characteristics on the right course. The author calls for keeping the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, strengthening the Party's long-term governing capacity and advancing full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. Read the original if you want a compact, officially aligned periodisation of how Chinese Party theory presents its own relationship to scientific socialism.
quoteEn: The development of scientific socialism in China has advanced precisely through the positive interaction of theoretical innovation and practical innovation.
quoteZh: 科学社会主义在中国的发展，正是在理论创新与实践创新的良性互动中向前推进的。

glossary.explanation: The Marxist term for socialism grounded in historical materialism and the analysis of capitalism, as opposed to utopian socialism. In Chinese official discourse it is one of the components of Marxism.
The Party's official name for its path, theory and system since the reform era, introduced by Deng Xiaoping in 1982.
The official judgement, formalised in the 1980s, that China is still at an early and underdeveloped stage of socialism that will last a long time.
A formula from the 2021 Party history resolution affirming Xi Jinping's core position in the Party and the guiding role of his thought.
The Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised leadership of the Central Committee.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The slogan, prominent since 2012, for strict discipline, anti-corruption work and institution-building within the Party.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations and global governance, promoted since 2012–2013.

t: A century of upholding and improving the Party's system of leadership: course and basic experience
zh: 坚持和完善党的领导制度的百年历程和基本经验
paras: Published in a series of written reflections on the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021), this article asks how the Communist Party of China has built and refined its system of leadership over a century. Wang argues that upholding and improving this system is the basic experience behind the Party's long-term rule and the guarantee of its successes. The article treats the system in a narrow sense (intra-Party leadership institutions) and a broad sense (the full set of institutions through which the Party leads state, society and people).

The article has two parts. The first divides the century into four stages: the New Democratic Revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The second draws four lessons from that record. Wang's institutional focus is collective leadership, centralised leadership and the Party's methods of leadership.

In the historical account, Wang traces how democratic centralism, collective leadership, the Party committee system and unified leadership centred on the Party took shape before 1949. After 1949 the Party extended unified leadership over state affairs, with Party groups and central leading small groups. Wang says that after 1957 this drifted into Party–government fusion and personal rule. Reform after 1978 restored collective leadership, replaced the chairman system with a general secretary, formalised the leadership core, and set the principle of scientific, democratic and law-based governance. For the new era, Wang describes a Party leadership system with six institutional dimensions, tied to the Two Upholds, the Two Establishes and democratic centralism. The four lessons are: uphold Party leadership over all work, and cite the Soviet collapse as a warning; keep innovating institutions; safeguard the authority of the Central Committee; and use strategic thinking so that Party leadership institutions guide national governance, through Party groups, institutional reform and organisation down to the grassroots.

Wang concludes that improving the Party's leadership system means combining "upholding fundamental principles" with innovation, using the spirit of self-reform to strengthen what is described as the greatest advantage of the system. Only by bringing the advantages of the "Chinese system" into full play, the author holds, can "Chinese governance" succeed. Read the original if you want an official-line account of how the Party periodises the development of its own leadership institutions, and how it ties them to the modernisation of national governance.
quoteEn: Upholding and improving the Party's leadership system is a unity of \"upholding fundamental principles\" and \"innovation\".
quoteZh: 坚持和完善党的领导制度是“守正”与“创新”的统一。

glossary.explanation: A Party formula, prominent since 2018, calling on members to firmly uphold Xi Jinping's core position on the Central Committee and in the Party as a whole, and the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.

A formula from the 2021 Party history resolution. It affirms the establishment of Xi Jinping's core position on the Central Committee and in the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Party: decisions are taken after internal discussion and then bind all members and lower organisations.
Party bodies placed inside state organs and other non-Party organisations to ensure that Party decisions are carried out there.
Party bodies, first created in 1958, that coordinate policy and decisions in a given field, such as finance, foreign affairs or politics and law.
A goal set out at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) to modernise China's system and capacity of governance.

t: Full and rigorous self-governance of the Party opens a new realm in the self-reform of a century-old Party
zh: 全面从严治党 开辟百年大党自我革命新境界
paras: Zuo Tengfei's commentary in Guangming Daily takes up Xi Jinping's statement at the sixth plenary session of the 19th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection that full and rigorous self-governance of the Party is a great practice of the Party's self-reform in the new era. Zuo argues that this practice opens a new realm of self-reform for a Party now a century old. The article presents the link between self-reform and rigorous Party governance as an answer to how the Party was able to succeed in the past and how it can achieve more in future.

The piece has three parts. The first explains why persistent self-reform and strict Party governance keep the century-old Party vigorous. The second reviews what full and rigorous self-governance of the Party has achieved since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third sets out four pairings of principles for taking it further.

In the first part Zuo argues that self-reform preserves the Party's advanced nature and purity, strengthens its creativity, cohesion and combat effectiveness, and keeps it the backbone of the Chinese people. Zuo cites the collapse of the Soviet Union and the upheavals in Eastern Europe, which the article attributes partly to ruling communist parties losing these qualities. In the second part Zuo says the campaign has carried forward earlier Party-building experience and supplied what Xi calls the "second answer" to the historical cycle of rise and decline, after Mao Zedong's first answer of letting the people supervise the government. Zuo adds that it has deepened understanding of how to build a long-governing Marxist party and has underpinned what the article calls the great social revolution, including reform.

Zuo calls for pressing ahead by combining mission with problem-orientation, spiritual with capacity building, organisational drive with individual initiative, and upholding fundamentals with innovation. Concrete measures include putting Party political building first, strictly applying the Central Committee's eight-point regulations, sustaining the anti-corruption struggle and building a system of institutional rules for self-purification, self-improvement, self-renewal and self-advancement. Zuo holds that the Party's future success depends chiefly on the Party itself. Read the original if you want a compact example of how the official line on Party discipline and self-reform was presented to a general readership in 2022.
quoteEn: Persisting in self-reform and strict Party governance is not meant to weaken the Party but to consolidate its leadership and governing position and strengthen its creativity, cohesion and combat effectiveness.
quoteZh: 坚持自我革命、从严管党治党，不是要削弱自己，而是为了巩固党的领导和执政地位，增强创造力、凝聚力、战斗力。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A Party-building slogan prominent since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It covers discipline, supervision, conduct and the anti-corruption campaign.
Xi Jinping's term for the Party's capacity to correct its own faults and renew itself. The 2021 historical resolution lists it as a lesson of the Party's century of struggle.
Rules adopted in December 2012 to curb bureaucratism, extravagance and formalism among officials. They are a core tool of Party conduct discipline.

glossary.en: the historical cycle of rise and decline
glossary.explanation: A reference to a 1945 exchange between Mao Zedong and Huang Yanpei about how to avoid the repeated rise and fall of dynasties. Mao answered that democratic supervision by the people was the way.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: The Communist Party of China's century-long exploration and development of building a modern socialist great power
zh: 中国共产党百年来对建设社会主义现代化强国的探求和发展
paras: Written as part of a series of study essays on the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021) and its resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience, this article asks how the Communist Party of China has pursued the goal of a modern socialist great power over its first hundred years. Song argues that the goal has deep historical roots, a broad practical basis and a clear logic of development. In the author's account, it runs from the revolutionary struggle for national independence to the present drive towards the second centenary goal.

The article is organised chronologically in three parts. The first covers the New Democratic Revolution and the period of socialist revolution and construction, treated as the fundamental political premise and historical foundation. The second covers reform and opening up from 1978, including the theory of socialism with Chinese characteristics, the primary stage of socialism, the "three-step" strategy and the building of a moderately prosperous society. The third turns to the new era under Xi Jinping and the new stage of development.

Song's central move is to read each period as supplying a precondition for the next. Before 1949, Mao Zedong and the Party linked national independence to a plan for industrialisation and a new state. After 1949, socialist transformation and the construction of an independent industrial system laid the institutional and material base, despite what Song calls serious setbacks. Reform and opening up then solved the question of path and stage. For the new era, Song sets out the sequence from a moderately prosperous society to basic modernization by 2035 and a great power by the mid-century. This is tied to the new development philosophy, high-quality development, the modernization of the system and capacity of national governance, and the "five-sphere" and "four-pronged" strategic layouts.

Song concludes that the Chinese nation has moved from "standing up" and "becoming rich" to "becoming strong", and that this has created a new path of Chinese modernization and a new form of human civilisation. The author adds that building a modern socialist great power will fully test and display the scientific character, people-centred orientation, practicality, openness and timeliness of Marxism in China. Read the original if you want an official-line, resolution-based periodisation of how Party documents link the revolutionary, Maoist, reform-era and Xi-era goals of national strength.
quoteEn: The new stage of development is a new stage in which the Party has united and led the people to a historic leap from standing up and becoming rich to becoming strong.
quoteZh: 新发展阶段是党团结带领人民迎来从站起来、富起来到强起来历史性跨越的新阶段。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's own path of modernization under Party leadership. It is presented as distinct from Western models and is characterised by five features, including a huge population and common prosperity.
An official economic theme since about 2017. It stresses quality and efficiency over speed of growth, and is defined through innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing.
A set of five principles (innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development) put forward by Xi Jinping in 2015 to guide economic and social policy.

The official thesis, set out at the 13th Party Congress in 1987, that China is at an early stage of socialism. It is used to justify the Party's basic line of economic development and reform over a long period.
A goal first put forward by Deng Xiaoping in 1979. The Party declared it fully achieved in 2021, which it presents as the first centenary goal.

The policy course adopted at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in December 1978. It shifted the Party's focus to economic construction and introduced market reform and opening to the outside world.

t: The Party's century of struggle demonstrates the great vitality of Marxism
zh: 党的百年奋斗展示了马克思主义的强大生命力
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育), 2022 no. 2
paras: Taking its cue from the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021) and its Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience, which states that the century of struggle "demonstrated the great vitality of Marxism", the article asks why Marxism has flourished in China. Liu and Fan argue that this vitality comes from Marxism's own theoretical features: scientific character and truth, people-centredness and practicality, openness and development. They hold that it also depends on the Party's century of struggle, which tested, implemented and displayed those features.

The article is organised in five parts. It first presents Marxism as the Party's fundamental guiding ideology, tracing the turn to Marxism after the Opium War and the Russian Revolution. The next three parts take each pair of features in turn and walk through four periods: the New Democratic Revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era. A final part considers the international effect of China's experience.

The central move is to treat each period as a test case. In the authors' account, Mao Zedong's analysis of a semi-colonial, semi-feudal society, the transition to socialism, the shift to economic construction under Deng Xiaoping, and the policies of the Xi Jinping era each applied Marxist principles to Chinese conditions and were confirmed by results. The authors then show people-centredness being put into practice through the mass line, the concept of "the people", and later formulations such as the Three Represents, putting people first, and a people-centred approach to development. Openness is shown through Marx and Engels revising their own formulations, and through successive theoretical innovations from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Together these are said to have produced the Two Integrations' predecessors, the adaptation of Marxism to Chinese conditions, in successive leaps.

Liu and Fan conclude that China's success has shifted the global balance between socialism and capitalism in socialism's favour. They claim it strengthens confidence in socialism, countered talk of socialism's end in the 1990s, and offers other developing countries a model of modernization that preserves independence. They say the Party will keep adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Read the original if you want a detailed example of the official Party-history narrative of Marxism's "vitality", organised by period and theoretical feature.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China and Marxism are bound together as flesh and blood and share a common fate; whether in the past, present or future, Marxism must always be upheld as the fundamental guiding ideology.
quoteZh: 中国共产党与马克思主义血肉交融、休戚与共，无论过去、现在还是未来，都必须始终坚持马克思主义根本指导思想。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the Party's project of applying Marxism to China's conditions and updating it for each era. The phrase 时代化 was added to the older 中国化 in recent Party documents.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
Jiang Zemin's theory, introduced around 2000. It holds that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the overwhelming majority of the people.
The principle of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture. The second integration was added in 2021–2022.

t: The Party stays at the forefront of the times through self-reform
zh: 党在自我革命中坚定走在时代前列
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2022, no. 5), after the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021), Zhou Suya asks how the Communist Party of China can keep itself at the forefront of the times under long-term rule. The article's answer is the Party's self-reform: Zhou presents it as the route the Party has found to solve its own problems and escape the historical cycle of rise and decline. It is described as a necessary result of the Party's adherence to historical materialism and a correct view of Party history.

The article draws on the Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience over the past century and on Xi Jinping's speeches at the plenum and the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection session. It is organised in three parts. The first presents self-reform as the political character of a Marxist party. The second looks at how self-reform has been pushed deeper in the new era. The third addresses the need to advance "two great revolutions" together.

In the first part, Zhou ties self-reform to the revolutionary nature, self-critical spirit, vanguard character and purity of a Marxist party. The Party, Zhou says, has no special interests of its own, and this is the source of its courage to reform itself. In the second part, Zhou says self-reform since the 18th Party Congress (2012) rests on firm ideals, steadfast adherence to the Party's original aspiration and mission, and a campaign against corruption with "no forbidden zones", full coverage and zero tolerance. Zhou calls corruption the greatest threat to long-term rule and says the struggle remains grave and complex. In the third part, Zhou argues that the Party's self-reform guides the great social revolution, while that revolution in turn drives self-reform. The degree and effect of self-reform, Zhou says, determine the historical height and practical depth of the social revolution.

Zhou concludes that, on the new journey, the Party must keep self-reform going and strengthen the Party's political, ideological, organisational, conduct, discipline and institutional building, together with the fight against corruption. It must also uphold Party leadership over both revolutions under Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Zhou holds that only the Party itself can defeat it, and that the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation will follow if the Party keeps its original mission. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-building scholarship in 2022 framed self-reform as both a Marxist principle and a governing method.
quoteEn: The degree and effect of the Party's self-reform directly determine the historical height and practical depth of the great social revolution.
quoteZh: 党的自我革命的程度和效果,直接决定着伟大社会革命的历史高度与实践深度。

glossary.explanation: Official term for the Party's efforts to correct its own errors, discipline members and combat corruption. Xi Jinping has stressed it since the 18th Party Congress as the Party's distinctive strength.

glossary.en: historical cycle of rise and decline
glossary.explanation: The pattern in which dynasties and regimes flourish and then collapse. In Party discourse it is linked to a 1945 exchange between Mao Zedong and Huang Yanpei about how to escape it.
The Party's stated purpose of seeking the happiness of the Chinese people and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. It was the theme of a 2019 Party-wide education campaign.
Xi Jinping's formulation pairing the great social revolution led by the Party with the Party's own great self-reform, said to advance together.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's overarching national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream, of restoring China to national strength and prosperity.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: The Communist Party of China and a new form of human political civilization
zh: 中国共产党与人类政治文明新形态
paras: Taking its cue from Xi Jinping's speech at the centenary of the Communist Party of China (2021), which spoke of a new form of human civilization and Chinese modernization, Xu Junzhong asks what kind of political civilization the People's Republic has created. The article's thesis is that the republic's politics is "people's politics" (renmin zhengzhi), which Xu presents as essentially different from Western party politics and as a new political civilization.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the logic of people's politics, rooted in Mao Zedong's idea of a "great union of the popular masses", and contrasts it with Western liberal democracy. The second identifies four defining features. The third traces the lineage of people's politics, argues that it belongs to the Marxist political tradition, and lists open problems for its further development.

Xu argues that Western party politics is a competition among elites, sustained by money, in which formally equal citizens merely choose periodically between rival groups. People's politics instead rests on "the people", defined historically as everyone except the enemy and therefore internally heterogeneous. Its four features, in Xu's account, are: seeking cooperation among classes rather than contest; balanced planning and proper handling of contradictions among the people; participation by the people themselves, now expressed as whole-process people's democracy; and leadership by the Communist Party. Xu says the Party can play this role because Marxism gives it a people-centred view of history, and because its self-reform keeps it committed to the people.

Xu concludes that people's politics is a self-conscious creation of the Party, distinct from both Euro-American democracy and the Soviet model, and warns against judging it by liberal standards. The article also states that it is not perfect. It asks how deputies can avoid becoming representatives of particular strata or interest groups, how popular participation and oversight can be institutionalised, and how the Party can avoid degeneration. Xu calls on Chinese scholars to close the gap between practice and theory using Marxism. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of how Chinese scholars contrast people's politics with Western electoral democracy, including the problems the author concedes remain.
quoteEn: The most prominent basic feature of people's politics is that it keeps seeking common interests among a people who are not homogeneous, building political consensus, forming common political goals, and establishing a united front in political, economic and cultural terms.
quoteZh: 人民政治最突出的基本特点就是不断在非同质性存在的人民中，寻找共同利益，凝聚政治共识，形成共同的政治目标，结成政治上、经济上和文化上的统一战线。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2019, holding that democracy covers every stage of political life (elections, consultation, decision-making, management, oversight) and not just voting.
The author's term for the political form created by the Communist Party in China, which he contrasts with Western multiparty "party politics".

glossary.en: great union of the popular masses
glossary.explanation: A phrase from Mao Zedong's early writings (1919), calling for broad unity among the popular masses; the author treats it as the starting point of people's politics.
Mao Zedong's 1957 category for non-antagonistic conflicts within the people, as distinct from antagonistic conflicts with enemies. He proposed resolving them by persuasion and consultation.
The official name for China's development path, presented as distinct from Western modernization.

t: The Communist Party of China's historical pursuit of fairness and justice and its responsibilities in the new era
zh: 中国共产党对公平正义的历史追求和时代担当
paras: Published in Marxism and Reality in 2021, the year of the Party's centenary, this article asks how the Communist Party of China (CPC) has pursued fairness and justice (gongping zhengyi) over its hundred years, and what that pursuit requires now. Xia argues that commitment to fairness and justice is a fundamental reason for the Party's leading position, and that a party which keeps the people at heart and upholds fairness and justice will win popular support and move history forward.

The article has three parts. The first traces the Party's exploration of the theme through four periods: the New Democratic Revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era. It cites Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin, Hu Jintao and Xi Jinping, and mentions the setbacks of the Cultural Revolution. The second part sets out four core elements of the Party's view. The third looks at how it is being developed under Xi Jinping.

In the core section, Xia holds that the Party's view combines Marxist theory of justice with Chinese realities, treats justice as historically and class-conditioned, and is secured by institutions. Drawing on Marx and Engels, Xia contends that justice in capitalist societies is formal and procedural, hiding substantive injustice, whereas China's socialist system aims to unite content and form of justice through public ownership, distribution according to labour, and the people's congress system. Xia also says justice should guide both rule by law and rule by virtue, and that efficiency and fairness must be combined, moving beyond the early reform formula of 'efficiency first, with due consideration to fairness'.

For the new era, Xia proposes four routes: institution-building, a people-centred value orientation, deepening reform, and high-level opening up. The article presents the poverty-alleviation campaign and the response to COVID-19 as illustrations, and contrasts them with Western governments, which it accuses of politicising the pandemic and putting capital first. It calls for promoting fairness and justice as shared human values within a community with a shared future for mankind, and for firmly resisting hostile forces that use 'universal values' against China. Read the original if you want an official Party-affiliated account of how fairness and justice are framed in Chinese Party historiography and in the contrast drawn with Western systems.
quoteEn: Fairness and justice are both a driving force of reform and an important criterion for judging its success or failure.
quoteZh: 公平正义既是改革的动力，也是检验改革成败得失的重要标准。

glossary.explanation: A paired value term in Party discourse covering equity in rights, opportunities, rules and distribution. It features prominently in speeches by Hu Jintao and Xi Jinping on social governance.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations and global governance, presented as China's contribution to a more equitable world order.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Deepening understanding of advancing the Party's self-reform in the new era
zh: 深化对推进新时代党的自我革命的认识
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2022, no. 5), Wang Weiguo, a professor at the School of Marxism, Xi'an Jiaotong University, explains how to understand the Party's self-reform in the new era. The article takes as its starting point Xi Jinping's speech at the sixth plenary session of the 19th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection, which says that the Party has found, in self-reform, a path to escape the historical cycle of rise and fall. Wang argues that the "six musts" Xi set out on self-reform form a unified whole that explains past success and shows how it can continue.

The commentary is organised as a series of six sections, each taking one of the "six musts" and arguing for a deeper grasp of it. They cover political development as the guiding principle, ideological development as the foundation, the Central Committee's eight-point regulation on conduct and discipline, the campaign against corruption, the political function and organisational strength of Party organisations, and a system of institutional rules for the Party. Each section opens with a quotation from Xi and ends with practical requirements.

In Wang's account, political development is the Party's fundamental development, and its first task is to ensure the whole Party obeys the Central Committee. Wang attributes the achievements since the 18th Party Congress (2012) chiefly to Xi as the core of the Party and to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and calls for understanding the Two Establishes and practising the Two Upholds. On conduct, Wang says that the eight-point regulation, adopted in December 2012, together with supporting rules, has brought a fundamental turn for the better in Party and government style. On corruption, Wang argues that it takes ever-changing forms and that the struggle will never end while its conditions persist. Wang therefore calls for attacking both "tigers" and "flies", and for pursuing the aim that officials dare not, cannot and do not want to be corrupt. Institutionally, Wang calls for governing the Party by rules and law together, and for stronger oversight of the "key minority", especially top leaders.

Wang concludes that deepening understanding of these six requirements is necessary for the Party to keep its advanced and pure character over time, since this does not persist automatically. Practical proposals include firm ideals and convictions, correct views of performance for officials, and stronger grassroots Party organisations. The text also urges overcoming factionalism, individualism and "circle culture" in the Party, and supervision of leadership transitions. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how the Party's self-reform was framed in early 2022 and of the six requirements Xi laid out.
quoteEn: The anti-corruption struggle is an important part of full and rigorous Party self-governance; only by resolutely fighting all negative and corrupt phenomena can Communists forever preserve their political character.
quoteZh: 反腐败斗争是全面从严治党的重要内容，坚决同一切消极腐败现象作斗争，才能永葆共产党人的政治本色。

glossary.explanation: A formulation in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse for the Party's continuous internal reform, discipline and anti-corruption work, presented as the way to avoid the historical cycle of rise and decline.
A formulation from the 6th plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021) that affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party and the guiding role of his thought.

The requirement that Party members uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official name for Xi Jinping's body of ideas, written into the Party constitution in 2017 as a guiding ideology.
Rules adopted by the Politburo in December 2012 to curb extravagance, bureaucratism and formalism among officials and to improve their links with the public.

t: Governing for the people and relying on the people
zh: 坚持为人民执政、靠人民执政
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in April 2022, takes up one of the historical lessons set out in the resolution on the Party's century of struggle adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021): "governing for the people and relying on the people". Liu Xiaoling argues that the principle sums up the Party's experience of putting the people first, deepens understanding of how communist parties govern, and is the basic guide for the "road to the exam" in the new era.

The article has three parts. The first presents the principle as a defining trait of a Marxist party. The second treats it as the source of the Party's strength in governing and building the country. The third turns to the present and sets out what the Party must do to pass the new "exam" on the way to the second centenary goal.

In the first part, Liu separates two sides of the principle. Governing for the people is described as the essential feature of a Marxist party, citing the Communist Manifesto and Xi Jinping's 2021 centenary speech on the Party having no interests of its own. Relying on the people is described as a requirement of historical materialism, expressed in the mass line. In the second part, Liu says that winning popular support rests on a party's stance and on its record, and that the leap from "standing up" to "becoming prosperous" to "becoming strong" gave the Party moral standing. The author also says the people's practice and spirit drive the Party's achievements, and that a "two-way commitment" between Party and people explains its ability to overcome hardship.

For the new era, Liu proposes three measures. The first is to put the people first and keep the Party's fundamental purpose of serving the people wholeheartedly. The second is to uphold the mass line, fight ideas that sow discord between Party and people, and take the people's well-being as the key measure of political performance. The third is to improve institutions for governing for and relying on the people, by perfecting systems for Party members and cadres to keep in touch with the public, creating online mass-work mechanisms, and strengthening mass organisations. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the 2021 historical resolution's principle of people-centred governance is explained in Party-theory commentary for a general readership.
quoteEn: Governing for the people and relying on the people is the foundation of the Party's rule and the source of its strength, the fundamental guarantee that it can overcome all difficulties and obstacles, and the code to why the Communist Party of China "is able to succeed".
quoteZh: 坚持为人民执政、靠人民执政，是我们党的执政之基、力量之源，是我们党战胜一切艰难险阻的根本保证，是中国共产党“为什么能”的密码。

glossary.literal: the road of going to sit the examination
glossary.explanation: A metaphor drawn from Mao Zedong's remark in 1949, as the Party moved to Beijing, that it was "going to sit an exam". Xi Jinping has revived it to describe the Party's continuing task of proving itself to the people.

The Party's working method of drawing ideas from the people, turning them into policy and returning to the people to carry it out. It is summed up in the formula "from the masses, to the masses" and is treated as a Party lifeline.
A principle named in the 2021 historical resolution as one of the Party's historical lessons. It is used to express the claim that the Party's work serves the people's interests above all.
The goal of building China into a great modern socialist country by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic.

t: Understanding the world-historical significance of the Communist Party of China's century of struggle
zh: 深刻理解中国共产党百年奋斗的世界历史意义
paras: This article, published in early 2022, sets out to explain what the Communist Party of China's hundred years of struggle mean for world history. It takes as its guide the Party's 2021 historical resolution, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee, which places Party history within the history of socialism and of human society. Li argues that the Party's struggle has demonstrated the vitality of Marxism, altered global trends and structures, opened a new path to modernization and offered solutions to problems shared by humanity.

The article is organised in four parts. The first treats Marxism's vitality, tracing the adapting of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times through Mao Zedong Thought, the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The second examines changes in the world economic, political and cultural order. The third sets out five features of Chinese modernization, and the fourth reviews the Party's contributions to world peace, common development and global governance.

Li's central claim is that the Party's achievements have shifted the balance between socialism and capitalism. In the author's account, Western-dominated dependency relations are being loosened. Li cites China's share of world output, rising from 2 per cent in 1978 to over 17 per cent, and its contribution to global growth. The article presents the post-1991 period as showing that the 'end of history' thesis was wrong. Chinese modernization is described as a non-capitalist route to modernity, defined by its socialist character, common prosperity, self-reliance, the coordinated advance of five civilizations (material, political, spiritual, social and ecological) and peaceful development. Li contends that this breaks the 'path dependence' of developing countries on Western models.

The article concludes that the Party has handed history an outstanding answer and that the road ahead is harder still. Li calls for closer unity around the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core, and for building a community with a shared future for mankind. The text is a Party-historical interpretation rather than an empirical study, and it draws heavily on official documents and leaders' statements. Read the original if you want a systematic account of how Party-history scholarship presents the world-historical meaning of the Party's centenary and its resolution.
quoteEn: The path of Chinese modernization belongs both to China and to the world.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化道路既是中国的，也是世界的。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's own path to modernization under Party leadership, described in Party documents as socialist and distinct from Western models. The article lists five features of it drawn from Xi Jinping's formulation.
The official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, presented as a defining aim of socialism and of Chinese modernization.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept, in use since the early 2010s, for China's vision of international relations built on shared interests, peace and common development.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng

glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since the 19th Party Congress (2017), described as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
The official name for the Party's model of socialism since the reform era, combining a socialist political system with market-oriented reforms.

t: The origins and development of the Communist Party of China's commitment to keeping the world in mind
zh: 中国共产党坚持胸怀天下的由来及发展
paras: Chen Li takes up one of the ten historical lessons set out in the Resolution on the Major Achievements and Historical Experience of the Party over the Past Century, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021): keeping the whole world in mind. The article argues that this has been a defining trait of the Communist Party of China since its founding. In Chen's account, the Party has always judged Chinese revolution, construction and reform against the trends of human development and the changing world order.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the theoretical and historical grounds for the commitment: Marxism, the world situation at the Party's birth, and traditional Chinese culture. The second follows its practice through the New Democratic Revolution, the early People's Republic and the reform era. The third turns to the new era, covering the Party's guiding statements, the community with a shared future for mankind, the Belt and Road Initiative, global governance, and cooperation on climate, poverty and the pandemic.

Chen's central claim is that the commitment follows from Marxism's call to emancipate all humanity, from the Party's reading of events such as the October Revolution, the Paris Peace Conference and the Washington Conference, and from the traditional ideals of 'all under heaven as one family' and 'harmony among all nations'. The Party's early links with the Comintern are cited as evidence. Chen then traces a line from Mao Zedong's internationalist duty and the decision to enter the Korean War, through Deng Xiaoping's repeated statements that China should make a greater contribution to humanity, to the new era. The author cites GDP figures to argue that China's growth has changed its position and responsibilities, and presents Chinese modernization as an option for developing countries that want to grow while keeping their independence.

Chen concludes that the Party works both for the Chinese people and for human progress, and calls this the meaning of its 'four for, four seek' formula. The article presents the community with a shared future for mankind, 'genuine multilateralism' and the Belt and Road Initiative as the current form of this commitment, and says China must balance domestic and international priorities. Read the original if you want an official-line account of how Party scholarship ties China's foreign policy and international role to the Party's theory and history.}
quoteEn: From its founding, the Communist Party of China has had a global outlook, viewing and grasping the problems of the Chinese revolution from a broader world perspective, and has established the necessary organisational mechanisms for this purpose.
quoteZh: 中国共产党自成立起，就具有世界眼光，从更宽广的世界视野来看待和把握中国革命问题，并为此建立必要的组织机制。

glossary.literal: carrying all under heaven in one's breast
glossary.explanation: A phrase from the 2021 Party resolution on history, listed as one of the ten historical lessons. It describes a Party outlook that looks beyond China's borders and links national goals to the progress of humanity.

glossary.en: community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept associated with Xi Jinping's foreign policy since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It calls for common development, shared security and cooperation among states.
A Chinese initiative launched in 2013 for infrastructure and economic cooperation with partner countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.
The official name for China's own path to modernization. Party texts present it as an alternative to Western models of development.

t: Adhering to the strategic policy of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
zh: 坚持全面从严治党的战略方针
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2022, no. 1), Guo Yong takes up the question of how the Communist Party of China should continue its strategy of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party in the new era. Guo argues that this strategy is a distinctive theme of Party building since the 18th Party Congress (2012), and that it rests on the Party's willingness to carry out self-reform. The article is framed by the 2021 Party resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience, which Guo cites as setting the direction.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the political leadership and guarantee that full and rigorous self-governance provides. The second describes how it runs through every area of Party building: ideals and convictions, work style, the oversight system, anti-corruption and institution-building. The third lists what is needed to achieve "greater strategic results": political conduct, the eight-point rules, coordinated oversight, and an integrated approach to corruption.

Guo's central claim is that the Party's vanguard character is forged through continual self-reform rather than given at birth. On this reading, the strategy secures the Party's overall leadership and the authority of the Central Committee against weakened or hollow implementation of its decisions. Guo credits it with underpinning poverty alleviation and the response to COVID-19. In the account of practice, Guo points to ideological education campaigns, the campaign against formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, reform of the Party and state oversight system including the National Supervisory Commission, and "zero tolerance" anti-corruption work. Guo describes the result as an overwhelming victory in the anti-corruption struggle that has now been consolidated.

Looking ahead, Guo calls for putting political building first, which means upholding the authority and centralized, unified leadership of the Central Committee. Guo also calls for persistent enforcement of the eight-point rules, since the "four undesirable work styles" persist in disguised forms. Guo further urges better coordination among Party, state, democratic-party, public and media oversight, and an integrated approach in which officials dare not, cannot and do not want to be corrupt. Guo presents this last approach as a theoretical and practical innovation that also supports the modernization of national governance. Read the original if you want a concise official-line account of how Chinese Party scholarship framed Party discipline and anti-corruption policy at the start of 2022.
quoteEn: However, an advanced Marxist party is not born that way; it is tempered through continual self-reform.
quoteZh: 然而，先进的马克思主义政党不是天生的，而是在不断自我革命中淬炼而成的。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party-discipline and anti-corruption drive led by Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It covers political, ideological, organisational, work-style and disciplinary building.
An official term for the Party's capacity to correct its own faults and purify itself. It is presented as a defining trait of the Party.
Rules adopted in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism among officials. They are the starting point of the work-style campaign.

glossary.pinyin: bù gǎn fǔ, bù néng fǔ, bù xiǎng fǔ
glossary.en: dare not, cannot and do not want to be corrupt
glossary.literal: not dare to be corrupt, not able to be corrupt, not want to be corrupt
glossary.explanation: An official anti-corruption formula combining deterrence through punishment, institutional constraints and ideological awareness.
Formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, the four work-style problems that Party campaigns target.
The official framework of Party, supervisory, state, democratic, public and media oversight, in which Party oversight is said to be primary.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Theoretical innovation on Party leadership in the new era
zh: 新时代关于党的领导的理论创新
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2022, no. 2), Shen Chuanliang takes up the first of the "Ten Clarifications" in the 2021 Party resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience. That clarification holds that Communist Party leadership is the defining feature and greatest strength of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Shen argues that it marks a new high point in theoretical innovation on Party leadership since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

The article has three parts. The first treats the innovation as problem-driven and assesses its place within the Party's body of innovative theory. The second explains three claims in the resolution: that Party leadership is the most essential feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics, that it is the system's greatest strength, and that the Party is the highest political leadership force. The third turns to practice, covering the requirements to strengthen the "four consciousnesses", stay firm in the Four-sphere Confidence and achieve the Two Upholds.

Shen contends that the theory answers real problems. These include vague understanding of, and weak action on, Party leadership, the weakening or hollowing out of its implementation, and poor execution of central decisions. Shen argues that Party leadership determines the nature, direction and fate of socialism with Chinese characteristics. In this account, world socialist history shows that without communist party leadership a socialist cause loses its political, organisational and ideological safeguards, and international competition is largely competition between systems. Shen cites the Party's record, from the new-democratic revolution to the elimination of absolute poverty, as evidence that the Party is the "mainstay" of national rejuvenation. Shen also places this theory first among the core contents of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and calls it original, enriching the Marxist doctrine of the Party.

Shen concludes that theory must become practical force, and that the Four Consciousnesses, the Four-sphere Confidence and the Two Upholds are the path for upholding and strengthening the Party's overall leadership. The Two Upholds, in Shen's reading, are essentially one: upholding General Secretary Xi Jinping's core status means upholding the authority of the Central Committee. Shen also calls for opposing formalism and "two-faced" people. Read the original if you want a concise official-line account of how Party leadership is framed in the 2021 resolution and how it is linked to Party discipline and loyalty.
quoteEn: Within the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics, the leadership of the Communist Party of China is the commanding, decisive and creative factor.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的领导在中国特色社会主义制度中是统领性、决定性、创造性的因素。

glossary.explanation: Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics, a formula promoted under Xi Jinping.
The Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position on the Central Committee and in the whole Party, and to uphold the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.
The Party's requirement for political awareness, awareness of the big picture, awareness of the leadership core and awareness to keep in line with the Central Committee.
The official name for the Party's path, theory and system of socialism, developed since reform and opening up.
